items.statement: No slowdown in digital/team investments in wealth/IB despite market volatility

items.quote: this burn phase will continue for the next 2, 2.5 years. And once we cross around INR20,000 crores to INR25,000 crores of equity, we should reach breakeven and build out from that.

items.quote: we don't expect the profitability to scale up in the first couple of years at the same pace at which the revenues wil l scale up because there will be investment in talent and other infrastructure costs and technology

items.quote: Port ones, there are not many players, there is a very unorganized market. It all depends on what kind of port equipments you are buying. items.quote: Our interest-bearing acceptance is about INR 2,500 crores and the total LC is about INR 3,300 crores.

In Q3 it is the first quarter where the entire consolidation has happened and about Rs. 8 crores delta in depreciation that you see is on account of the Renom

items.statement: FY25 guidance: growth higher than 30%, EBITDA 20-22%, PAT 15-16%
items.quote: So, we ha ve guided to a growth higher than 30% and EBITDA betw een 20 -22% and PAT between 15 - 16

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin at 21%, midpoint of guided 20-22% range
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 21%, which is at the midpoint of our guided range of 20% to 22% EBITDA.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 PAT margin at 16%
items.quote: Profit after tax, stood at Rs. 48 Cr for Q3 and PAT margins for the quarter should at 16%.

items.statement: Demand environment exceptionally strong across banking, transit, and data center segments
items.quote: the demand environment remains exceptionally strong as the strongest we have seen in a long whi le for both the segments, right

items.statement: Order book net addition Rs 30-40 Cr per quarter; this quarter exceptional due to strong wins
items.quote: typically, what happens to us from one quarter to the next is we roughly are at a pace of consuming about Rs. 250 Cr to 260 Cr from the order book, and we add, let's say, between Rs. 250 and 300 Cr. So, the net addition ends up being Rs. 30-40 Cr.

items.statement: R&D investment at 8%+ of revenue, expected to continue into next financial year
items.quote: We remain committed to innovation, consistently investing 8% or more of our revenues in R&D, a trend that we expect to continue going into the next financial year.

items.statement: R&D expense currently Rs 110-115 Cr annually
items.quote: We expense every single cent of our R&D which is probably at Rs. 110-115 Cr right now.

items.statement: Fenixys acquisition expected to close in Q4 FY25, will strengthen European presence and delivery capacity
items.quote: A key development in this area is our expected closure of Fenixys acquisitions this quarter. This acquisition will significantly strengthen our presence in the European markets, providing us with a strong foothold and delivery capabilities in the region.

items.statement: US revenue share reached double digits, growing 70-80% this year; channel and partnerships fully built out
items.quote: I think overall, the share of revenue from U.S. clients is now up to double digits. So, I think this year will probably grow between 70% and 80%, I think, from that geography.

items.statement: Revenue split roughly 60% India, 30% Asia ex-India, 10% America
items.quote: So, the split roughly for US is 60% India, 30% Asia Ex-India and 10% America roughly.

items.statement: DSO midpoint around 100 days, range 90-115 days depending on project mix
items.quote: I would say 100 odd days is where the sort of midpoint of the range lies, depending on project values and all. Now, from time to time, it may actually go up to 110, 115, and I think there may be times it drops below 100.

items.statement: Q3 cash flow promising; expect strong collections by March 31
items.quote: So, I believe we will end up in good shape as we finish the year and so far, Q3 has been very promising.

items.statement: Banking & Fintech grew 41% to Rs 474 Cr (9M); Technology Innovation Group grew 23% to Rs 372 Cr (9M)
items.quote: Banking and Fintech segments delivered 41% growth, reaching Rs. 474 Cr, while Technology Innovation Group segments grew by 23% to Rs. 372 Cr.

items.statement: Delivery capacity ramp-up underway in Europe and US; Fenixys acquisition to augment European delivery
items.quote: We are working very hard at that. I think we have got a very, very strong model to build that capacity, but still the constraint remains how fast can you get the project delivered.

items.statement: AI explainability (AryaXAI) enhancing competitiveness of transaction banking and lending stacks
items.quote: We have become one of the most competitive players in the transaction banking space, thanks to being the sort of leading product with a very strong AI offering inside the transaction banking stack.

items.statement: Transaction banking win rate ~60% of decided deals over last 5 quarters
items.quote: We probably have won in the last 4-5 quarters, I would say 60% +of the deals we competed in and I think or 60% of deals tha t we competed in that got decided over the last 5 quarters

items.statement: Europe's strong AI regulatory framework favors AryaXAI explainability platform; engaging with regulators
items.quote: Europe has a very strong regulatory framework around the AI which is very different from let's say a place like US or India and that really sets the market up very nicely for us because we really have the framework in place to see that the models that you build up are fully explainable to make sure there is a compliance to regulations.

items.statement: DeepSeek impact on global data center demand uncertain; India data center demand driven by compute/storage not AI compute
items.quote: I would say the jury is out on that one and you have not completely debunked what you call the scaling hypothesis. What you sort of proven is you can get very close to a frontier mode l using algorithmic techniques instead of blind

items.statement: US risk low due to product/IP model, small size, minimal visa dependence
items.quote: We are a very product oriented, IP oriented business. So, we don't really think there is a lot of impact.

items.statement: Attracting talent from global fintech firms (Finastra, Murex); senior leadership tied to Vision 2030 quantitative objectives
items.quote: It has encouraged, it has attracted a lot of talent from top global firms to come and join us and I think that way we have been a bit lucky that we were a bit unique in terms of our models and we were a bit lucky that we were more ambitious than probably some of the others a nd that helped us to draw in talent from globa l fintech firms, from the Finastra, from Murex

items.statement: Europe expansion led by banking and transit; targeting both regions >10% revenue share by end FY26
items.quote: by the time we get to the close of FY26, I think we are getting to both Europe and U.S. being north of 10% of the revenue share.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 guidance to be given in May with FY25 results
items.quote: For the complete business, I will come back to you in May when we report the full year results and then we will guide.

items.statement: Vision 2030: aim to be top 3 in each product segment; internal quantitative objectives being delivered ahead of plan
items.quote: Our Vision 2030 is fairly clear, it is fairly detailed. Externally, it is a set of qualitative objectives that we published. Internally, it is a set of hardcore quantitative objectives that we are chasing. So, far we are actually delivering ahead of those objectives.

items.statement: Full-year credit cost target maintained at 1.3% to 1.5%
items.quote: our stated goals for the full year is to keep credit cost in the 1.3% to 1.5% range, basis how Q3 has panned out and how we look at executing on Q4, we still hold these targete d ranges of 1.3% to 1.5

items.statement: NIM target for FY25 is 6.5% to 6.7%
items.quote: NIMs, yes, is also in the range that we want to close the year 6.5% to 6.7%.

items.statement: ROA target for FY25 is 1.8% to 2%
items.quote: ROA, we are maintaining that we would like to be in the 1.8% to 2%.

items.statement: Asset growth target for next financial year is mid- to high-teens
items.quote: We'd like to be in the mid- to high teens.

items.statement: Long-term NIM target revised to around 7% from earlier 7.5% aspiration
items.quote: I don't think 7.5% with the kind of choice metrics that we have shared on the profile of incremental customers as well as the kind of product choices that we are making for the future will achieve a 7.5%. So, 7% is more like the long-range target.

items.statement: Long-term ROA aspiration is to climb up to 2.5%
items.quote: For a longer term, yes, the aspiration is to climb up to 2.5%.

items.statement: Q3 NIM at 6.6%, up 10 bps sequentially but down 20 bps year-on-year
items.quote: On the margin front, what you would see that the NIMs are at 6.6% for the quarter. This is a 10 bps sequential gain. It has, of course, been a 20 bps fall from last year same time, Q3.

items.statement: GS3 at 3.9%, up 10 bps sequentially but 4 bps lower year-on-year; INR 216 crore added to GS3 stock in Q3
items.quote: Here, the highlights are that GS3 moved up sequentially by 10 bps. It is still 4 bps lower than quarter 3 of last fiscal. On a sequential standpoint, we have added INR 216 crores.

items.statement: Q3 credit cost only INR 9 crore due to INR 434 crore provision reduction from LGD decline
items.quote: For the quarter, we have added only INR 9 crores in terms of overall credit cost. The big difference here is the provision reduction of INR 434 crores.

items.statement: Management expects PCR to gradually tick up to 51%-54% range but remain range-bound below peak levels
items.quote: I don't thi nk this will definitely go beyond a 54% number. That's why I said, between 51% to 54% number in the near future

items.statement: SME disbursements grew 60% YoY driven by LAP business
items.quote: Our SME business, as I mentioned earlier, has seen a promising growth of 60% Y-o-Y. We do recognize this is from a relatively lower base, but what's really moving here is the LAP business, which now constitutes the majority of the business.

items.statement: Used vehicle disbursements soft in Q3; replacement demand muted and risk factors considered
items.quote: What we have seen the PV continues, the used CV as the main CV business, LCV, SCVs are not growing significantly. Some of the replacement demand in that segment is starting to be muted. And also, we have to factor in what is the risk that is in part of the segment.

items.statement: Secured exclusive lending partnership with M&M for Born Electric vehicles starting bookings from 14th February
items.quote: We have secured an exclusive lending partnership with M&M for the new to Born Electric vehicles, which are slated for bookings from 14th of February.

items.statement: Launched co-branded credit card with RBL Bank; signed up 9 insurance providers via corporate agency license; tied up with IDFC Bank for FASTag issuance; received NPCI in-principle approval for TPAP license
items.quote: In the quarter gone by, we linked a credit card partnership with RBL Bank, post getting the license from RBI for co-branded credit cards. We have also, after getting our corporate agency license signed up 9 insurance providers for distributing life, nonlife and health insurance. Another source of revenue is for the vehicles that we finance. We are looking at getting some amount of revenue from the

items.statement: Added 25 branches in Q3, 34 YTD; plan to add another 15-20 branches in FY25
items.quote: From a distribution standpoint, we have not had too many branch additions, but we have added 25 branches in the last quarter. Overall year-to-date 34 branches. We plan to add another 15, 20 for the year.

items.statement: Tier-1 capital at 15%; actively evaluating Tier-1 augmentation at current leverage levels
items.quote: So, it is clearly on our minds. And we usually, when we come to these levels, we start warming up the engine for Tier-1 augmentation. At the right time, we will have commentary on that.

items.statement: Collection efficiency stable at 95%; formula based on real-time CD and OD collections, not linked to LGD pool
items.quote: Not really because the collection efficiency formula basically stayed constant, and that pool is the LGD pool. But I think what you have to look at collection efficiency is real-time CD and OD collection, right? That's what goes in the numerator divided by the current view collection.

items.statement: Management considered but did not create management overlay on provisions; may evaluate in future if needed
items.quote: We did contemplate it. We just felt we'd be being a bit too cute and trying to basically do artwork on top of the model. At the right time, if we believe that we have got to start creating buffers, we will do it.

items.statement: GNPA-Stage 3 gap (IRACP vs IND-AS) sticky at ~INR 6,200 crore vs INR 4,500 crore; pool carries Stage-2 provisions
items.quote: Jigar, we do carry the same Stage-2 provision on this asset. If they are IRACP. but not IND-AS NPAs, they sit largely in Stage-2, and yes, they would take the Stage-2 provision. This number, you are right. I mean, it's difficult to get 3 EMIs sometimes. So, that's why that pool has remained range bound.

items.statement: Mahindra Rural Housing Finance being rightsized; asset quality improving; adequately capitalized with no immediate growth plans; senior resource from Bajaj Housing Finance now full-time
items.quote: We have already reduced a significant amount of manpower. OPEX will come down. And of course, asset quality, we are starting to see positive changes there. From a capital adequacy, that entity is adequately capitalized. There is no need, we are not growing anyway. We are looking at more rightsizing that organization and making sure the asset quality in that organization reaches a desirable level.

items.statement: Detailed long-range strategy including mortgage business plan, digital AI roadmap, and Investor Analyst Day to be shared at end of Q4
items.quote: End of Q4, we plan to have a very detailed in fact, Investor Analyst Day of sorts, where we will share much more details on the overall growth aspirations, asset category participation, aspirations, digital AI capabilities that we have built.

items.statement: Housing Finance AUM growth guidance of ~20% for FY25 maintained; expects run rate to improve further with RM additions
items.quote: We hold the same guidance of about 20% AUM growth for FY25.

items.statement: Expects continued best-in-class earnings growth and return ratios supported by financialization mega trend and strong balance sheet
items.quote: We expect these mega trends supported by a strong brand, very strong balance sheet will help us deliver continued best-in-class earnings growth and return ratios to our shareholders.

items.statement: Demat accounts grew 33% YoY to 185 mn in Q3FY25; expects growth trajectory to continue given low financial savings penetration
items.quote: the demat account s witnessed addition of ~10 mn accounts during Q3FY25 implied growth of 33% YoY and 6% QoQ basis, taking the total of demat accounts base to 185 mn

items.statement: Jan'25 was second strongest month ever for incremental mutual fund flows; net new flow market share multiple times AUM market share
items.quote: Jan'25 is the second strongest month in terms of incremental flows in our history. The earlier strongest was Dec'24.

items.statement: Wealth Management NII spread improved from 5.9% to 6.8% YoY; cost of funds declined 30 bps sequentially
items.quote: Spread improved from 5.9% in Q3FY24 to 6.8% in Q3FY25.

items.statement: AMC taking steps to grow profitability; 4Q will show full impact of distributor commission rationalization
items.quote: Growing profitability is going to be our endeavor. We have taken some steps. 4Q will show the full impact of those steps.

items.statement: Wealth Management AUA grew 67% YoY to Rs 3,08,000 cr; distribution AUM grew 38% YoY to ~Rs 32,000 cr; net flows quadrupled to ~Rs 3,000 cr
items.quote: Our total assets under advice in the Wealth Management business grew to Rs. 3,08,000 cr, up 67% YoY.

items.statement: Asset Management AUM crossed Rs 1.3 lakh cr, up 100% YoY; mutual fund AUM at ~Rs 98,000 cr, up 128% YoY; SIP AUM ~Rs 21,000 cr
items.quote: Our asset management AUM stands at over ~Rs. 1.3 lakh cr, up 100% YoY.

items.statement: Private Wealth AUM at ~Rs 150,000 cr, up 34% YoY; ARR assets ~Rs 32,000 cr, transaction-bearing assets ~Rs 116,000 cr
items.quote: Our private wealth AUM stands at ~Rs. 150,000 cr as of Dec'24, up 34% YoY.

items.statement: Housing Finance AUM grew 15% YoY to Rs 4,343 cr; disbursements up 93% YoY to ~Rs 1,000 cr in 9MFY25
items.quote: Our AUM for this business grew 15% YoY to Rs. 4,343 cr.

items.statement: Investment Banking completed 35 deals aggregating ~Rs 46,000 cr in 9MFY25; ranked #1 in all India QIP league table
items.quote: We have completed 35 deals, aggregating to ~Rs 46,000 cr in 9MFY25.

items.statement: AMC headcount expanding from 250 to over 600 by year-end; most incremental hires for on-ground city presence and sales team
items.quote: Beginning of the year, the AMC business had 250-odd people. Today, we hope to end the year with over 600.

items.statement: Wealth Management distribution team of 600 people with plans to increase to 1,000 in near future
items.quote: We've created a dedicated distribution team of a strong 600 people with plans to increase this to 1,000 people in the near future.

items.statement: Housing Finance RM count increased 46% YoY to 1,246; doubled in FY24 over FY23 and up another 50% in FY25
items.quote: Our RM count in FY24 was doubled over FY23. Similar in FY25, this base is up by another 50%.

items.statement: Private Wealth RM count increased 27% YoY to 600; only 29% have vintage over 3 years, expects productivity improvement to continue
items.quote: The total relationship manager count increased by 27% YoY to 600. The stronger revenue growth that you saw during the 9MFY25 is clearly an outcome of the improved productivity that we have guided for.

items.statement: F&O per lot pricing increased in line with contract size increase; pricing linear to lot sizes
items.quote: increase in t he per lot pricing based on the contract size increase has been implemented for our customers in line with changes in the lot size

items.statement: Fee-based revenue contribution increased from 30% to 41% YoY; annual recurring revenue at 56% of group revenues
items.quote: Our fee-based revenue contribution to the total revenues increased from 30% in Q3FY24 to 41% in Q3FY25.

items.statement: AMC is completely equity-oriented; ~Rs 27,000 cr passive AUM (NASDAQ/S&P ~Rs 13,000 cr); ETFs small but launching new ETFs
items.quote: We are completely Equity oriented AMC. With respect to offshore, we can't invest in the offshore strategies. We are limit-up in those.

items.statement: Private Wealth targets families with Rs 25 cr+ financial net worth; onboards at Rs 3 cr+ within a year
items.quote: We look at families with a financial net worth of Rs. 25 cr plus in the Private Wealth Management business and we onboard with Rs 3 cr plus.

items.statement: ~60% of DP AUM from clients with >Rs 1 cr balance; cross-sell focus on 4.5 mn client base
items.quote: Around 60% of our DP AUM comprise of clients with more than Rs. 1 cr DP balance, implying serious cross-sell ability to these clients.

items.statement: Expects to be largest full-service broker benefiting from industry consolidation due to rising compliance costs
items.quote: broking industry will also see further consolidation in the hands of the larger players due to many reasons including increasing compl iance costs and norms being few of them , a nd hence , we expect Motilal Oswal to be the largest full-service broker in the country

items.statement: Will not pursue discount broking model; focusing on quality and advisory; digital client acquisition increasing month-on-month
items.quote: We are very clear that we will not be going on the discount side of the business and we are focusing on the quality.

items.statement: Chinese walls maintained across businesses due to different regulators; cross-sell includes third-party products via open architecture
items.quote: Yes, we have Chinese walls across all the businesses. Many of them are regulated by different regulators. So, these businesses operate stand-alone as separate entities.

items.statement: Housing Finance GNPA 140 bps, NNPA 80 bps; negative credit cost due to recoveries from pre-FY20 written-off assets
items.quote: The asset quality continues to be quite good with GNPA of 140 bps and NNPA of 80 bps.

items.statement: Wealth Management lending book resilient with only 5% sequential dip despite sharp market correction; NII up due to spread improvement
items.quote: As far as the lending book is concerned on the both Wealth Management and Private Wealth Management, there is a marginal dip on a sequential basis of about 5%.

items.statement: Group AUA crossed Rs 6 lakh cr, up 62% YoY; operating revenue Rs 1,345 cr up 43% YoY; operating PAT Rs 525 cr up 38% YoY
items.quote: Our assets under advice (AUA) crossed the Rs. 6 lakh cr mark, up 62% YoY.

items.statement: Group net worth Rs 11,569 cr up 40% YoY; annualized ROE 36%; interim dividend Rs 5/share
items.quote: Our net worth as of Dec'24, stood at Rs. 11,569 cr, up 40% YoY.

items.statement: Private Wealth hired senior talent for UHNI/family office proposition; aims to be leading player in 3 years
items.quote: In the past 9 months, we focused on several senior level hiring to strengthen the overall leadership strength of the business. This improves our UHNI and family office proposition, and positions us strongly to be a leading player in the private wealth business in the next 3 years' time.

items.statement: No systemic risk from margin calls due to SEBI margin changes and high client cash balances; minimal overnight impact
items.quote: No. This is because of the changes which SEBI implemented on the margins and after margins, the impact of the fall is very minimal, and we don't see any big impact coming on an overnight basis.

name: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Ltd

items.statement: Overall demand environment remains subdued amid inflationary pressures and muted urban growth; rural demand decent due to good monsoon and rising wages but recovery is gradual and cannot compensate for urban stress.
items.quote: The overall demand environment continues to be subdued amid inflationary pressures and muted growth rates in urban India. However, good monsoon and growing rural wages saw decent rural demand during the quarter.

items.statement: Urban-rural split is 60-40; rural is recovering but growth not great, urban continues to have issues and rural cannot compensate for urban stress.
items.quote: So the ratio is 60-40, 60% urban, 40% rural. And rural has been decent, while urban continues to have issues.

items.statement: Gross margin maintained at 49.8% YoY in Q3, protected by raw material coverage; EBITDA margin fell 110 bps to 16.4% due to 8% volume growth vs 4% value growth and 7-8% opex increase.
items.quote: Our gross margin for the quarter stands at 49.8%, which was maintained at the same level on a year-on-year basis. Our coverage of some of the key raw materials helped us protect the gross margin in Q3.

items.statement: 9-month gross margin improved 150 bps to 50.4%; EBITDA margin improved 10 bps to 17.8%; absolute EBITDA rose to INR387.7 cr from INR371.4 cr.
items.quote: On the gross margin front as well, there is an improvement of 150 bps, that is 50.4% compared to 48.9% of last year. EBITDA in absolute terms improved from INR371.4 crores in the last year to INR387.7 crores in this year. And the EBITDA margin saw an improvement of 10 bps from 17.7 to 17.8.

items.statement: Management aims for double-digit volume growth in FY26 but is cautious and does not guide for it; expects value-volume gap of 2-3% over long term.
items.quote: Our ambition is still there to grow in double-digit volume growth, but we are a little cautious here. We'll try our best to be in the double digits, but I don't want to guide you there.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY26 held at 16-17% band but will be confirmed later; near-term focus is protecting Q4 margin amid volatile input prices.
items.quote: We are still believing that we will -- we should be able to deliver between 16% to 17%. But we'll come back to you in the next earnings call probably what would be the guidance for the next year.

items.statement: Low single-digit price increase taken in body soap end of December; further pricing actions planned in Q4 Personal Care depending on input prices and market conditions.
items.quote: Soap, we have taken towards the end of December is a low single-digit increase that we have taken, but we are planning to take further pricing action in quarter 4 in Personal Care category.

items.statement: Fabric Care near double-digit growth driven by liquid detergents and powders; Post Wash Ujala Supreme leadership reinforced; Dishwash grew 3.6% with Pril liquid, Exo, Scrubbers; Personal Care declined 3.7%; Home Insecticide severely impacte
items.quote: Q3 saw Fabric Care category touching nearly double-digit year-on-year growth. The growth was contributed mainly by liquid detergents and duly supported by detergent powders. Our Post Wash category remained a key priority with Ujala Supreme maintaining its leadership position.

items.statement: Launched Jovia beauty soap (mass segment, ~INR25-26 for 75g) with Vitamin E in two variants; initially select geographies, intended PAN-India; also launched Maxo anti-mosquito racket and Mr. White liquid detergent.
items.quote: To tap growth opportunities in the mass toilet soap category, we have just launched Jovia beauty soap captured with the goodness of Vitamin E and natural ingredients. Jovia comes in 2 variants, Lemon and Aloe Vera and Sandal and Turmeric for clear and glowing skin.

items.statement: Dishwash competition intense and will continue; grammage benefits passed to consumers; HI segment coil degrowth but liquids double-digit; market leader's new technology acknowledged but confident in own formulation.
items.quote: See, stabilized -- see in a scenario where everybody wants volume growth and when consumer is willing to come, there will be this competitive aspect that will continue for quite some time.

items.statement: Strong manufacturing capabilities spread across country cited as competitive advantage; no specific capex numbers or plans disclosed.
items.quote: As mentioned in the past, we are focused on launching innovative products, leveraging our competitive advantage such as strong manufacturing capabilities spread across the country, cost optimization, excellent vendor partnerships, deep distribution network.

items.statement: Freight, transportation and logistics costs increased due to 8% volume growth; other expenses largely in line with prior year.
items.quote: You would have noticed that our volumes have gone up by 8% Y-o-Y. So freight and transportation and logistic cost has actually increased. So that's the only increase. Other than that, most of the expenses are in line with previous year.

items.statement: A&P spend constant at 9% of sales in Q3 YoY; near to mid-term A&P spend to remain range-bound; brand investment strategy to continue.
items.quote: Our advertisement and sales promotion spend remained constant at 9% in Q3 FY 2025 as compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Near-term demand challenging; Q4 initial signs not encouraging; input price and crude volatility create margin uncertainty; HI segment losses INR10 cr in Q3 (INR20 cr 9M) with breakeven dependent on season.
items.quote: No, it looks challenging. The initial signs in quarter 4 are not very encouraging. So I don't think quarter 4 is going to be meaningfully different or superior. So it's going to be tough.

items.statement: No management changes or key hires discussed; focus on building portfolio for future growth across categories.
items.quote: See Prolin, I believe in building for the future, and that's where the launches play. Today, we need to have certain play in these categories. And hence, we are launching, and this will be the future growth.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA per ton guidance retained at INR7,000-10,000; FY26-27 target raised to INR8,000-11,000
items.quote: FY '25, we've already said, 9 months are out. So, 1 quarter is left, we will remain in the range of INR7,000 to INR10,000 EBITDA per ton in the fourth quarter also and '25, '26, we had said we will be INR8,000 to INR11,000.

items.statement: ROCE target of 20-25% EBITDA on capital employed maintained
items.quote: And yes, we stick with the return on a capital employed figures of EBITDA on capital employed of 20% and the target of 25%. We stand by it.

items.statement: Melting capacity tested at 25,000 tons/month (300,000 tpa run rate) in December; rolling capacity to reach 270,000 tpa by end of FY26
items.quote: I'm happy to report that in the month of December, we have tested making 25,000 tons for the whole month, which means that now we have tested albeit only for 1 month but a run rate of 300,000 tons for the full year.

items.statement: INR160-170 crore capex to be capitalized in FY26 for Kocks Block, reheating furnace, cooling beds; NDT line work to start FY26
items.quote: So roughly INR160 crores to INR170 crores worth of capex will be capitalized next year. In addition, we will be starting work on the NDT line, the second non-destructive testing line.

items.statement: New greenfield plant in Punjab (Ludhiana district) under planning; land in final negotiation; Board approval targeted for April meeting
items.quote: We are looking for land in Punjab. So the new plant is going to come up in Punjab, hopefully, in Ludhiana District itself, we are in the last stages of negotiation for some land.

items.statement: Market conditions tough with pricing pressure; auto demand (cars, CVs, tractors) weak; Chinese HRC imports hurting sentiment
items.quote: The market conditions have been pretty tough and there is pricing pressure, and all of us are facing that pressure. There are 2 reasons for that pressure. One is on the demand side, after the very good growth last year. This year, growth in cars have been also much lower.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA/ton INR8,000; 9M FY25 EBITDA/ton INR8,500; within stated INR7,000-10,000 range but lower than anticipated
items.quote: EBITDA per ton is INR8,000 per ton in this quarter. And for the 9 months, our total volume is 162,000 tons which is higher by 13.5%. And in terms of value, it is higher by 9.5%. EBITDA per ton for the 9 months as a whole is INR8,500 well within our stated range.

items.statement: FY25 volume guidance of ~215,000 tons on track despite Q4 shutdown; 9M volume 162,000 tons (+13.5% YoY)
items.quote: Yes, we are in line. When we made the guidance, we knew there was shutdown coming, and we have planned inventories with us. So, which is why if you analyse the balance sheet, you'll see working capital significantly higher than our norms.

items.statement: Power & fuel cost per ton decreased; variable power cost ~INR5.65/unit; solar to cover 40-45% of power needs
items.quote: The variable cost is lower. So the fixed cost will remain what it is, the variable cost only that part will be saved with the solar plants coming in. So you should look at a cost of INR5.65 as a variable cost.

items.statement: Scrap ~80% of raw material mix; tested up to 100% scrap; Punjab location chosen for scrap availability
items.quote: Scarp is roughly 80% in our raw material mix, and we have tested that we can go up to almost 100% of scrap also.

items.statement: Kalyani Group setting up green steel plant (acquired Kamineni Steel); SLR may expand; Tata Steel/JSW profits down sharply
items.quote: Kalyani Group has already come out in public. They're putting up a green steel plant. They have taken over a steel plant in the South, Kamineni Steel.

items.statement: PLI 1 approved; will apply for PLI 3 when announced; carbon trading benefits expected when implemented (current 0.73 CO2/ton vs 2.2 norm)
items.quote: We are approved in the PLI 1 scheme. Angad Katdare: Sir, my second question is on... Sachit Jain: And the new project when it comes up. So first, you have to have a detailed project plan before you apply it. So we will hope that a PLI 3 scheme will come in, and if it comes in, we will

items.statement: Export target of 30,000 tons not met due to weak Thai auto demand and yen depreciation; rupee depreciation now helping; European OEs inquiring due to low carbon footprint
items.quote: We are below our target of 30,000 tons of exports that was planned primarily because Toyota sales in Thailand have -- are not taking off as per their expectation. And the yen depreciated significantly over the last 5 years.

items.statement: Inventory buildup for March/April shutdown; working capital significantly higher than norms; inventory to normalize post-shutdown
items.quote: There is an inventory buildup in the company that is for the shutdown coming in March end. So after that shut down, the finished goods inventory should come down to a reasonable level.

items.statement: Solar plant in SPV; only 26% equity (~INR19 crore) on books; all debt/obligations with operator
items.quote: The power plant is putting up in an SPV. Only our share of the equity, 26% of the equity, which is roughly INR18 crores. I'm sorry, my CFO has corrected me, INR19 crores.

items.statement: Aichi stake increase likely in next 1-2 years alongside new project announcement; promoters to co-invest to limit dilution
items.quote: Talks are going on, have been going on with Aichi for some time. And, it is part of the plan at some stage, they will increase their stake.

items.statement: Forging plans with Aichi (world's 3rd largest forging co) to concretize in 1-2 years; India to serve domestic, Africa, Europe markets
items.quote: I have a strong feeling that within the next year or 2, these plans will get concretized and we should start taking some concrete steps on the forgi ng journey

items.statement: Carbon footprint 0.73 tCO2/ton (target 0.45 by May); well below 2.2 norm; circular economy talks with Maruti, Hero, others
items.quote: We are already at 0.73. And you know further planning to go down to 0.4. I just want to understand the unit economics, how we will be benefited from green steel.

items.statement: Pricing pressure from Chinese imports and weak auto demand; margin compression; shutdown execution risk in March/April
items.quote: The market conditions have been pretty tough and there is pricing pressure, and all of us are facing that pressure. There are 2 reasons for that pressure. One is on the demand side.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; Aichi partnership deepening with potential stake increase
items.quote: One thing about Vardhman is when we partner with somebody, then we go the whole hog with them. And Aichi is the world's third largest forging company and 1 of the best in quality.

items.statement: User industry mix marginally shifted: tractor/CV segment slightly higher, non-auto slightly higher; strategic customers provide volume stability
items.quote: The tractor and commercial vehicle segment would be a bit higher than -- marginally higher and some nonautomotive sales also would be a bit higher. Gargi: Okay, sir. Sir, secondly... Sachit Jain: But these are all marginal differences

items.statement: GST refund available until Sep'26; electricity duty exemption until Sep'29; ~INR24-25 crore annual benefit
items.quote: One is GST refund. And GST refund is available to us up to September '26, and electricity duty exemption is available up to September '29.

items.statement: FY25 volume guidance maintained near 4.4 lakh tonnes; Q4 volume targeted at 1.25-1.35 lakh tonnes
items.quote: We've been maintaining a steady rate of about, say, 1 lakh tonne of volume per quarter. And going forward, we are poised to achieve, say, 1,25,000 tonnes to 1,35,000 tonnes in the 4th Quarter and maintain the guidance, near to the guidance that we had given earlier at the starting of the year.

items.statement: FY26 volume target of 5.5-6 lakh tonnes; EBITDA per tonne target of Rs 5,000
items.quote: So, it's easy to say that we will achieve sales over 5.5 lakhs tonnes, 6 lakhs tonnes in next year.

items.statement: EBITDA per tonne target Rs 5,000 for FY26 after returning to normalcy of Rs 4,500 in Q4 FY25
items.quote: So, last in FY '24, our EBITDA per tonne was averaging out close to Rs. 4,500. In this Financial Year in the nine-months, our EBITDA per tonnes is coming close to Rs. 4,000. And in the next financial year or starting this quarter actually, we come back to normalcy levels of Rs. 4,500 and then 10% to 15 % jump over that in the EBITDA per tonne is evident throughout the next year.

items.statement: Total project cost for 1 million tonne expansion is Rs 1,000 crores; Rs 480 crores received, Rs 300 crores spent so far
items.quote: It's close to Rs. 1,000 crores.

items.statement: Installed capacity to reach 1 million tonnes by end of FY25; next 1 million tonnes expansion in phases over next two years in Maharashtra
items.quote: By the end of this year, we will be reaching 1 million tonnes of capacity by the installation of DFT. At the starting of this year, we stood at 6,86,000 tonnes. In the third quarter, we went live with 1 lakh tonnes of production in our Raipur plant. And the 14,000 tonnes balance in Mandi Gobindgarh will also come by this end year. So, and another 2 lakh tonnes will come by the DFT line in Mangaon.

items.statement: DFT line at Mangaon (2 lakh tonnes) to start in Q4 FY25; will produce value-added structural sections 350x350mm
items.quote: We would be the only one in that area producing it. So, we are next to the port. There is a very good demand from the export market for these products of structural steel, wherein this has already been implemented in abroad for a number of years. See, a section of 350-350, we would essentially be the third one in India after APL Apollo and JSTL to implement this size.

items.statement: Secured Rs 265 crore Jal Jeevan Mission order for 36,000 tonnes galvanized tubes in Jammu as L1 bidder
items.quote: During this quarter, JTL secured a Rs. 265 crores order as a L1 bidder for supplying 36,000 metric tonnes of galvanized mild steel tubes for Jal Jeevan Mission in Jammu.

items.statement: Value-added products at 24% of 9M FY25 sales mix; target 40-45% in FY26 and 55-60% at 2 million tonnes capacity
items.quote: We are at about 24% of value-added products with DFT, which is by inception only a value-added product. So, we are targeting about say 40% to 45% of value addition in the next financial year. As our KT offering and for when we move towards 2 million tonnes of capacity with our other products, we will be targeting value added in a ratio of about 55% to 60%.

items.statement: Primary/secondary mix shifting to 70% primary, 30% secondary at 1 million tonnes capacity (from ~44% primary currently)
items.quote: By the end of the 1 million tonnes we are not expanding in our secondary market, we are only expanding in the primary market since we are increasing our value offering and size offerings. So, by the end of it, it will be I would say 70% of primary and 30% of secondary.

items.statement: EBITDA per tonne fell to Rs 3,800-4,000 in 9M FY25 from Rs 4,500 in FY24 due to price correction and de-stocking; DFT expected to add Rs 200-250/tonne
items.quote: Right now, with these levels at 3,800-4,000 are a subdued level of the year of price correction, I would say.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin 7-8% near term, aiming for double digits with DFT; healthy EBITDA per tonne level ~Rs 4,400-4,500
items.quote: Our target always remains to have a healthy EBITDA level of about 7% to 8%. And with the coming of DFT, we are targeting it to be close to getting to double digits.

items.statement: Safeguard duty on steel imports expected in Budget; would raise domestic prices and reduce cheap import competition
items.quote: See, so the Q4, we have seen a considerable step from the government regarding the safeguard duty, which, when implemented, we are awaiting the decision in the budget or soon after. When implemented, we shall see a considerable rise in the prices of steel, so to say, which will entail that the cheap incoming material will not be available to the Indian market.

items.statement: Export volumes doubled YoY to 26,859 tonnes in 9M FY25 (10% of sales vs 5% prior year); DFT to open new export markets
items.quote: Export volumes doubled year-over-year, reaching 26,859 metric tonnes for nine-months, which now represent 10% of our total sales, compared to 5% in the previous year.

items.statement: Zero long-term debt; funded expansion via QIP (Rs 300 cr) and preferential warrants (Rs 675 cr, Rs 180 cr received); cash Rs 121 cr
items.quote: We are currently at zero debt position and going forward as well, we are well equipped with the recent QIP and the promoter infusion that we have done for the expansion, the capital expansion that we have done and for the working capital that is needed.

items.statement: Nabha Steel (67% stake) being converted to subsidiary; consolidated accounts targeted by end of FY25
items.quote: We are in process of merging it. We shall be completing the merger. It would not be a merger, so to say, so since we have 67% share, we can only right now Nabha is a partnership firm. So, we are converting it into a subsidiary, and it will be a subsidiary -- Vikas Singh: Yes. Basically, the conciliated account-- Dhruv Singla: Yes. So, our target is to get the consolidated accounts by the end of th

items.statement: Good demand outlook in Q4 FY25; prices expected stable to rising from February; infrastructure projects driving volume
items.quote: There is good demand outlook in the 4th Quarter. See everybody is wanting to say revisit their strategies in the 4th Quarter and this new duty implication would mean that the looming problem of price decline from the incoming material from abroad or dumping material from abroad has gone away. So, we are optimistic that from this coming month of February, the prices are going to be a little bit on

items.statement: Working capital needs to be met by bankers; no long-term debt planned; ROCE to normalize as new assets start generating returns
items.quote: We might, going forward, only need certain working capital which our bankers are already behind us to take it forward. But, apart from that, there would be no long-term debts the Company intends to take.

items.statement: DFT 350x350mm structural sections: only 3rd player in India after APL Apollo and JSTL; no local competition in Maharashtra region
items.quote: See, a section of 350-350, we would essentially be the third one in India after APL Apollo and JSTL to implement this size. So, not a lot of competition in this area here.

items.statement: Price correction and channel de-stocking suppressed EBITDA/tonne in 9M FY25; HR coil prices fell from Rs 52-53k to Rs 46k
items.quote: See, in the entire year, we have seen prices going down and the realizations also suffering. That's the reason there's a lot of de-stocking that has happened and also the prices from a level of HR coils at about Rs. 52, Rs. 53. We saw a bottom of about Rs. 46.

items.statement: Completed QIP fundraise with marquee investor interest
items.quote: We are, first of all, pleased to announce the successful completion of our recent fundraise through a QIP process, which generated significant interest and support from marquee investors.

items.statement: Q3 revenue INR121.5 cr, down 2% YoY due to lower turnout in Bhubaneswar and Cochin
items.quote: Revenue for the quarter was INR121.5 crores, a degrowth of 2% compared to the previous year. The dip in revenues were mainly due to lower turnout in some of the key locations like Bhubaneswar and Cochin.

items.statement: Chennai Park slated to open for commercial operations from December 2025; Bengaluru resort extension by beginning of next financial year
items.quote: Our Chennai Park is slated to begin operations towards the end of the next financial year, most likely open -- will be open for commercial operations from December. The extension of our resort at Bengaluru is also proceeding at the right direction, and we expect to launch this by the beginning of next financial year.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA INR42.2 cr, down 30.3% YoY; margin 33.3%; PAT INR20.3 cr, down 45.7% YoY; margin 16.1%
items.quote: Our EBITDA, including other income for the quarter was INR42.2 crores, down by 30.3% on a year-on-year basis. EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 33.3%. Additionally, our profit after tax for the quarter amounted to INR20.3 crores, representing a degrowth of 45.7% compared to the previous year. PAT margins for the quarter stood at 16.1%.

items.statement: 9M EBITDA INR140.9 cr, down 32.8% YoY; margin 37.5%; PAT INR98.3 cr, margin 26.2%
items.quote: EBITDA, including other income for the 9 months stood at INR140.9 crores, down by 32.8% on Y -o-Y basis. EBITDA margin stood at 37.5%. The profit after tax stood at INR98.3 crores and the margins are at 26.2% for the 9 months ended FY '25.

items.statement: Q3 ARPU INR1,272; 9M ARPU INR1,472
items.quote: In terms of our average revenue per user, our Q3 FY '25 stood at INR1,272 and for the 9 months, it stood at INR1,472.

items.statement: Bangalore flood and Cochin meningitis issue caused footfall dip; Bhubaneswar hit by cyclones and seasonal new-market dynamics
items.quote: So what happened in Bengaluru was we had a great Dussehra, but the second half, which is also a critical part in October, there was the sudden unexpected monsoon. In fact, you would have read news about Bangalore being under the flood. So it kind of derailed our entire revenue for 2 weeks, which kind of caused the dip. And in Cochin, we saw good growth in our retail footfall, but this was a big ye

items.statement: Bhubaneswar footfall grew 42% QoQ but cyclones and new-market seasonality limited Q3; expect pickup from March
items.quote: But the issue, I think weather is one of the issues we had. We had 2 cyclone events there. And also, I think because it's the first year. And we don't -- I mean, we are new in the category actually in Bhubaneswar, most of the water parks that are existing in that area, they are operational mostly during summer only. And so the whole idea of going out to an amusement park during a winter season doe

items.statement: Incremental capex in older parks: new Chikku attraction in Cochin rolled out to Bangalore/Hyderabad; virtual attraction in Bangalore; big rides and restaurants planned
items.quote: We are doing a lot of incremental capex, especially in the older parks like Cochin and Bangalore. We are opening a new attraction. We have just opened a new attraction in Cochin at end of December, which is our Adventures of Chikku, right? And that will be rolled out to Bangalore and Hyderabad as well. I think it will be done as we speak. Then we are also launching a large attraction in Bangalore

items.statement: Moving to dynamic pricing model; ATP fluctuates with demand, especially Q2-Q4; online bookings >50% of general footfall
items.quote: So I think, see, the way we look at ticket prices, it's also a function of demand. So whenever we see demand weakening maybe because of weather or other issues and we see intent to visit is low, we play with pricing. So we are slowly going towards a dynamic pricing kind of a model that we use discounts and other methods, mostly for online footfall. So that's why you'll see ATPs will keep fluctuati

items.statement: No formal guidance; expect Q1 FY26 stronger with full Bhubaneswar summer and recovery in Bangalore/Cochin
items.quote: We don't give guidance, but we are hoping that Q1 of FY '26 should be stronger because that's the first time we will have an entire Q1 for Bhubaneswar. And also, I think Bhubaneswar, we are still in the kind of a launch -- semi-launch phase in the last yea r. So I think this is the first time. I think next financial year, we hopefully -- March onwards, we can see Bhubaneswar numbers pick up. Other

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin expectation 35-40%; new park openings temporarily pressure margins
items.quote: So it depends on when we are opening up the park, generally, there will be expenses, which is not corresponding to the revenue what they generate, so which can impact our EBITDA for a temporary purpose -- temporary period. this can be about 35% to 40% if you historically observe the EBITDA margin of the company, so you can see about pre-COVID, it was about some 35% to 40%. And after COVID, after a

items.statement: Non-ticket revenue CAGR ~11% last 4 years; target 9-11% SPH growth going forward
items.quote: If you look at our last 4 years CAGR also, we've been at about 11%. And we continue -- we are bullish on driving our ARPU through our non-ticketing revenue. So we expect moving forward also anywhere between 9% to 11%, we want to build our sales per head.

items.statement: FY26 capex estimated INR400-500 cr including new park and existing park investments; ~10% of revenue for sustaining capex
items.quote: Presently whatever is as per object as per QIP, which is for our Chennai Park and then certain other extension in our existing parks like Bangalore, one ride and then the refurbishment of our resort, all those things are already planned as per the QIP. And apart from that, we generally spend about some 10% of revenue towards the ca pital expenses as a ride expansion or maybe restaurant building an

items.statement: Future projects funded via internal accruals and ~30% debt; no further equity raise needed
items.quote: we will not need any more capital. It will be -- all the future thing will be done through a combination of internal accruals and maybe some debt. Angad Katdare: Okay. And how much debt are we comfortable debt to equity? Saji Louiz: It's about some 30% of the total spend, that is what we are thinking of from

items.statement: Weather remains key unpredictable risk; strategy: geographic diversification and online pre-booking (>55% of general footfall) to lock demand
items.quote: See, I think the business -- any kind of tourism business will always have weather being one of the issues that can create dips in footfalls. And that I don't think we can change. We can do a couple of things. One is to have more geographies where we can -- so we can hedge our -- we can grow in size and also hedge our bet in terms of weather issues. The other thing is we have more tickets sold onl

items.statement: Chennai Park capex INR515 cr, no cost escalation expected; delay due to weather only
items.quote: No, we don't expect any escalation in the course because we already placed the order. There's only a slight delay because of some weather and other conditions. So we are not expecting any increase in the cost of… Arun Chittilappilly: Only inclement weather that is part of the delay. I mean all our costs are [Inaudible 51:45] only. There is not much. Maybe some small change here and there can happe

items.statement: Chennai Park breakeven within first full year of operations
items.quote: Within the first full year of operations, I think we should be able to break even.

items.statement: Plan to open 15-20 new labs in FY25
items.quote: We are accelerating our reach in the underserved markets with the planned opening of 15 to 20 new labs in this financial year.

items.statement: Nine months FY25 capex Rs 30 crore; maintenance capex Rs 60-70 crore per year
items.quote: In nine months roughly we have made a CAPEX of around Rs. 30 crore. As Shankha mentioned, we are planning to open 15-16 labs in this year. Maybe this is coming in the later part of this year, so Q3 and Q4. And going forward, on an ongoing basis, maintenance CAPEX is about Rs. 60 - Rs. 70 crore per year excluding any major investment in any other venture.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin 25.8%; YTD FY25 EBITDA margin 28%
items.quote: EBITDA for Q3 FY25 came in at Rs.154 crore compared to Rs.141 crore in Q3 FY24, registering a growth of 9.6% with the EBITDA margin of 25.8%.

items.statement: Gross margin slightly lower YoY in Q3; management expects gross margins to remain stable at current levels
items.quote: I think just to correct, the gross margin in this quarter compared to last year same quarter has not improved. Basically, this gross margin is slightly lower than last year same quarter.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 revenue grew 10.7% YoY driven by sample volume growth and mix improvement, no price increase
items.quote: We maintained a strong performance trajectory in the third quarter of the fiscal year 2025, delivering 10.7% growth in revenues. The growth is delivered through sample volume growth and mix improvement and does not have any price increase benefit.

items.statement: Sample volume grew 10.3% YoY to 20.6 million; patient volume grew 3.8% YoY to 6.9 million in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Sample volume stood at 20.6 million in Q3, a growth of 10.3% YoY, while patient volumes came in at 6.9 million, an increase of 3.8% over the same period last year.

items.statement: Swasthfit bundle revenue grew 27.2% YoY in Q3 FY25; contribution 23% in Q3 vs 20% YoY
items.quote: Our bundle test program, Swasthfit, continues to contribute favorably to the overall performance with a robust growth of 27.2% in Q3 FY25.

items.statement: Specialized portfolio defined as ~22% of business
items.quote: There is no industry standard definition of specialized, but the way we look at our business, the way we define specialized, that portfolio for us is about 22% right now.

items.statement: No price increase planned for next 6-9 months; holding prices to drive volume growth
items.quote: We will probably review this going forward maybe 6-9 months later, but as of now, we don't plan to take any price increase.

items.statement: Reagent cost pressure from dollar appreciation; consumption cost reduced from 22.5% to ~20.9% via local sourcing
items.quote: If you see last 2-3 years consumption cost, it has reduced substantially because of mix which we are changing from 22.5% to now roughly 20.9% this quarter. That is where wherever we have opportunity, we are doing that, but at the same time there is a inflationary pressure which is coming.

items.statement: Patient service center to lab ratio ~20-21x; management sees higher ratio as better but dynamic
items.quote: I think clearly this particular metric of ratio between lab and collection center is very important. Because a throughput through a collection centre is definitely more efficient than throughput through a lab.

items.statement: Franchisee collection centers contribution ~45%; pickup points ~20-25%; rest walk-in and home collection
items.quote: The contribution from franchisee collection centers now has gone up to nearly 45%.

items.statement: Delhi NCR delivered double-digit revenue growth for second successive quarter after years of single-digit growth
items.quote: I am pleased to share with you that Delhi NCR recorded double-digit revenue growth for the second successive quarter.

items.statement: West region contribution ~15% of revenue, similar to East; South identified as focus area for growth
items.quote: West region contribution is now nearly 15% all put together, which is similar to what we do in East. East and West are now easily sort of balanced now, gone up from 14 to 15 is what I see.

items.statement: Organized competition seen as beneficial for market shift from unorganized; hospital labs not aggressive on pricing
items.quote: Overall I have a feeling that these people will help market to grow on an organized play, shift from unorganized to organized will move further.

items.statement: Industry stabilizing after period of deep discounting; no significant stress in smaller labs
items.quote: Overall, it is stabilizing. I don't see too much of a sort of stress in the smaller labs, but I also don't see too many new labs coming up.

items.statement: Revenue per patient Rs 861 in Q3 FY25, up 6.7% YoY; test per patient 2.97 vs 2.79 YoY
items.quote: Revenue per patient for Q3 FY25 stands at Rs.861, a growth of 6.7% compared to Q3 FY24. This growth in Classification: Confidential revenue per patient is on account of mixed management initiatives on geography, channel and products

items.statement: YTD patient volume growth 4.4%; sample volume growth 9.5%; target to return to 7-8% patient volume CAGR
items.quote: Last year I think we ended the full year at about 2.7% and I think right now YTD we are about 4.4%. Give or take let's say we are in the range of 4.5%-5% is what I think we are expecting patient volume.

items.statement: Net cash Rs 1,123 crore as of 31 Dec 2024
items.quote: Net cash as on 31st December 2024 is Rs.1,123 crore.

items.statement: Third interim dividend of Rs 6 per share approved; total dividend YTD Rs 18 per share
items.quote: At last, I am pleased to share that the Board of Directors of the company have approved a Third Interim Dividend of Rs.6 per share, taking the total dividend for the current year till date to Rs.18 per share.

items.statement: Hired ~100 people in sales and marketing team for future growth
items.quote: we have started investi ng in new infra and we hired about roughly 100 people in our sales and marketing team as well

items.statement: Voluntary liquidation of Suburban to save administrative, legal and compliance costs; not substantial
items.quote: This is administrative and legal and compliance costs primarily, which can be saved because right now there are multiple entities, now it will be one.

items.statement: M&A focused on geographic expansion; capabilities added by buying equipment (e.g., Illumina for genomics) not acquisitions
items.quote: You don't need to go and acquire any company. The effort really needs to be put on the sales and marketing side and then acquiring some of these because these technologies come from outside, available on the shelf and you just go and buy these equipment and you are adding those capabilities.

items.statement: Government committed to increase public health spend to 2.5% of GDP from ~1.8%; NCDs account for 65% of deaths
items.quote: The Government of India has committed to increasing the public health spend to 2.5% of our GDP from the current approximately 1.8%.

items.statement: Dollar appreciation creating reagent cost headwinds for entire industry
items.quote: Most of these regions are imported and dollar becoming expensive, while we are still holding on to this, I don't know what the response of our vendors going forward, but that pressure also is going to come not only for us, but for the entire industry.

items.statement: Suburban Q3 EBITDA margin 12.3% vs 11.5% YoY; full year margin expected 15-16%
items.quote: Q3 FY24 EBITDA margin for Suburban was 11.5%, now it's 12.3%.

items.statement: Pricol expects 13-15% growth over next couple of quarters driven by product mix, new launches and market demand
items.quote: We are expecting to grow at around between 13% and 15% based on our product mix, new product introduction, and market demand.

items.statement: Pricol targets consolidated EBITDA margin around 11-12% with Sundaram acquisition
items.quote: Around 11 to 12 is right, yes.

items.statement: Pricol aims to maintain standalone EBITDA margin around 13% but consolidated margin will be lower due to Sundaram's single-digit margins
items.quote: So I always maintain that we will be on a consolidated basis at around 13%. Now, with Sundaram joining the table, it is going to be a lower average because the plastics business is a lower average.

items.statement: Acquired Sundaram Auto Components (to be renamed Pricol Precision Products) at 3.5x adjusted EBITDA multiple; 50% revenue from TVS group
items.quote: The total business that is expected to be done by this company this year is about 800 crores with an EBITDA of about 70 crores and we have acquired the business at an adjusted EBITDA multiple of 3.5 times EBITDA multiple which is value accretive to our shareholders.

items.statement: Plan to double Sundaram business to 1600-1700 crores over 3 years organically and inorganically; move from component supplier to FSS plastic supplier
items.quote: Our plan is to double the business to about or somewhere in the region of 1700 crores over the next 3 years. Both organically and inorganically.

items.statement: Sundaram acquisition closes 1st February; will become subsidiary of Pricol
items.quote: Tomorrow is the date of closure. So if all goes well from 1st February it becomes a subsidiary of Pricol.

items.statement: Consolidated debt after Sundaram acquisition will be around Rs 80 crores; currently zero debt
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, as we stand today, there is zero de bt. After the closure of Sundaram deal, we will hardly have 80 crores of debt

items.statement: Pricol at far end of 650 crore capex cycle; last 200 crores remaining; maintenance capex ~100-120 crores/year going forward
items.quote: Pricol we are at the far end of a 650 crore CAPEX cycle, which I have been talking about for the last 3 years. We are at the far end of that last 200 crores of that CAPEX cycle.

items.statement: Maintenance capex for Pricol is about 100 to 120 crores a year unless inorganic growth
items.quote: Our maintenance CAPEX is about 100 to 120 crores a year.

items.statement: Q3 demand muted across industry; supply chain issues caused lower sales; 50% mitigation done, rest in Q4, normalization from Q1 FY26
items.quote: This quarter, demand was a little muted in the entire industry and in addition, we had some supply chain issues, which resulted in lower sales.

items.statement: Supply chain issues 50% mitigated; remaining 50% to be resolved in Q4; supplies normalized from Q1 FY26
items.quote: These issues are getting under control. About 50% mitigation has been done and the other 50% mitigation will happen in Q4 as we speak and supplies will be normalized from Q1 of FY'26.

items.statement: Target to increase Sundaram margins by ~200 bps over next couple of quarters via efficiency, productivity improvements and machinery upgradation
items.quote: We are hoping over the next couple of quarters to increase the margin by about 200 basis points, which is why we have bought it at a lower EBITDA multiple for it to be value accurate.

items.statement: Revenue mix: 65-70% two-wheeler/three-wheeler, 10% commercial vehicles, 5-7% tractors, 7-8% off-road, 10% passenger vehicles
items.quote: 65% of our revenue comes from the two -stroke three-wheeler. If you see on the automotive side, 65% to 70% of the total India vehicle production comes from the two -wheeler. This is one and Pricol follows the same standard of what the industry has in terms of percentage.

items.statement: EV contribution to driver information system revenue currently below 10%; increasing continuously as traditional OEMs ramp EV volumes
items.quote: Currently, it is below 10% because if you see the total pie of the EV compared to the total two-wheeler manufacturing is still quite low and it is evolving.

items.statement: TFT clusters contribute 5-7% of revenue; Pricol holds 75-80% market share in two-wheeler TFT; migration from LCD to TFT accelerating
items.quote: Today, 5-7% of our revenue is coming from TFT clusters and as more EV is going up, TFT is something that is going to become a major feature in all these vehicles.

items.statement: Battery Management System under testing with key OEMs; expect some business in H2 FY25, full year sales from FY26
items.quote: May be H2 of this year, we will start some business on the BMS. And next year would be a full year of the battery management system sales.

items.quote: from a future perspective, when we talk about digital, we will -- if there are acquisitions that we think which will align and complement to our line of business
