items.statement: Strong demand drivers include migration to high voltage, rural electrification, EV and renewable infrastructure, underground cabling
items.quote: So, I think there are 3-4 very drivers which are very unstoppable I should say. One is that the migration from low voltage to high voltage because of increase in per capita power consumption, that is inevitable.

items.statement: 9M FY25 product mix: HV cables 61%, LV cables 29%, railway signaling 5%, conductors 5%
items.quote: Product wise contribution 9-month FY25 for HV sales 61%, LV cables 29%, railway signaling cable 5%, conductors 5%.

items.statement: Top 5 customers contribute ~30% of sales, top 10 contribute ~50%; names change quarterly
items.quote: Top 5 buyers comprise of around 30% of our sales and top 10 buyers comprise around 50% of our sales. These names keep on changing.

items.statement: 80% revenue from private clientele (large corporate EPC players and private DISCOMs), 20% government
items.quote: 80% of our business comes from the private clientele.

items.statement: One product UL approved for US market; couple more under pipeline; exclusive US sales team set up
items.quote: on the approval side, we have got one product approved and couple of more products are under pipeline. So, once we have a bouquet of products available, we can hand over, I mean our sales team can hit the market and get the distribution done. We have already set up in the parallel while the approvals are taking place. We have already set up an exclusive sales team for the US market.

items.statement: Working capital days currently below 100 days
items.quote: Currently it would below 100 days.

items.statement: Meaningful reduction in overall debt achieved through financial discipline
items.quote: Our focus on financial discipline has yielded positive results, enabling us to achieve a meaningful reduction in Company's overall debt.

items.statement: Fundraise mix of working capital and CAPEX; ~INR 35 crores for CAPEX, balance for working capital
items.quote: So, fundraise basically, it's a usual mix of working capital and CAPEX. We are doing around 35 crores of CAPEX from the fundraise and balance will be used to fund our working capital.

items.statement: 9M FY25 sales grew 32% YoY; operating margin rose 37% to INR 71.2 crores; PAT up 72% to INR 41.2 crores
items.quote: In 9-month FY25 sales grew by 32% over 9-month FY24 with operating margin rising 37% to INR 71.2 crores. Operating margin was stable at 10.3% in accordance with our long-term guidance and PAT increased by 72% to INR 41.2 crores surpassing FY24 profits

items.statement: New products (data center, wind energy, solar DC cables) under development and approval stages
items.quote: So basically, all these products are under development and at various stages of development. Some of the products are under the approval stages.

items.statement: Government exposure reduced from ~80% (7-8 years ago) to ~20% currently; may decline to 15% over time
items.quote: So, 5 years back or I think 7-8 years back it was very high. It was I think 80% government and 20% private. Now it is completely inverse, 20% is private and 80% is government. And it has continued for last 2-3 years. This mix has continued for last 2-3 years. And this 20% is also very important and required. Maybe it can go down to 15% over a period of time.

items.statement: Export degrowth due to currency issues in African/Asian countries; company works on advance payments only
items.quote: One is that there are in the countries where we deal are African and Asian countries, where we were facing some currency issues. So, we did not want to take any exposure or risk of exporting the goods. And secondly the domestic tailwinds are very strong. So, the focus was also more towards domestic as export is an adjacent market or an alternate market for us.

items.statement: INR 20 crores CAPEX incurred in 9M FY25
items.quote: Overall CAPEX incurred. I will just pull out the number. 20 crores.

items.statement: No quarterly or yearly revenue guidance given; historical cable business CAGR ~20% expected to continue for 3-5 years
items.quote: we don't give a guidance as such but if you look at our last 7-8 years history, we have our cable business has grown by upward of 20% CAGR. So, for next 3-4 years, 5 years I don't think that this trend should discontinue.

items.statement: Management sees immense demand for next 20 years; not concerned about industry overcapacity from peers' CAPEX
items.quote: So, the demand is immense I should say at least for the next 20 years, leave around 2 years, 3 years, 5 years. But for the next 20 years the demand is immense.

items.statement: ROA expected around 1.5-1.6% currently, rising from FY28 onwards as gold loan share falls to ~20% by 2030
items.quote: I think our ROA, what I have told is somewhere around 1.5% to 1.8% range. I think given the overall environmental challenge right now, we will stick to somewhere around 1.5 to 1.6% at this point of time. It will start going up from FY28 onwards again.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio expected to stay in 8-10% of OPEX range for tech spend; no one-time expenses ahead
items.quote: Typically our tech spend has been somewhere around 8% to 9% of our overall OPEX. We believe that some of these CAPEX when they move to OPEX, along with that comes AMC also, which com es as an additional OPEX

items.statement: CBS migration with OGL and OFSAA to complete in Q1 FY26, stabilize by Q2 FY26, leverage from Q3 FY26
items.quote: Our CBS migration along with OGL, OFSAA and some of the other pieces, which we are putting together, will be expected to be completed in Q1 FY26 stabilized by Q2 FY26 and leveraged from Q3 FY26 onwards.

items.statement: NIM sustained at 4.11% for Q3 FY25 despite yield compression and 25 bps penal interest impact
items.quote: NIM could be sustained above 4% both on a quarterly and on YTD basis despite the tight liquidity conditions and higher interest rate cost looming large in th e system. NIM for the quarter stood at 4.11

items.statement: Yield compression due to de-risking high-yield unsecured portfolios (12-16%) and exit of Rs 200 Cr corporate account at 13% yield
items.quote: degrowth has happened in 3- 4 products, which are all high-yielding products viz, Two-wheeler, Personal loans, Agri, MFI etc. Unsecured portfolio, we h ave degrown big time. All these businesses are somewhere, anything between 12% to 16% kind of a yield or may be even higher

items.statement: Net advances grew 26% YoY (2x industry); gold loans 36% YoY, other retail 32%, SME 29%, core corporate >30%
items.quote: Net advance growth of 26% YoY – Higher than 2x times over Industry growth of 12% YoY. Gold portfolio registered a growth of 36% YoY and Other retail by 32% SME growth has been steady at 29%.

items.statement: WSB growth only 5% due to DA portfolio liquidation and selective exits per risk appetite
items.quote: However, the overall WSB growth was at 5% mainly on account of the liquidation of DA portfolio and few exits we opted for as part of our coverage strategy/risk appetite.

items.statement: GNPA 1.58%, NNPA 0.64%, PCR 60.12% (ex-PWO); slippages contained sequentially
items.quote: GNPA & NNPA ratios for the quarter was at 1.58% and 0.64% as against 1.68% and 0.69% for Q2 FY 25. PCR now stands at 60.12% without PWO, which is marginally higher than the previous quarter.

items.statement: Holding Rs 181 Cr provisioning buffer above regulatory requirements; Rs 106 Cr contingency provision retained (Rs 34 Cr mapped to exited large account)
items.quote: Bank is holding a provisioning buffer of about Rs 181 Crs, over and above regulatory requirements. We continue to hold the provision of Rs 106 Crs, which we created during the Covid period and later moved it to contingency provision.

items.statement: Added 34 branches YTD (merged 6); remaining planned expansion to complete in Q4 FY25
items.quote: currently we have a network of 807 branches and 777 ATMs. We have added 34 new branches till 31.12.2024 and as part of the bra nch rationalization merged six branches during the year. The rest of the branch expansion as planned will happen this quarter

items.statement: Cost of funds pressure and 25 bps penal interest impact per quarter; part recovered as penal charges under other income
items.quote: NIM compression has a lso happened because of higher cost of funds and because of that penal intere st impact where we lost around 25 basis points and that continues every quarter

items.statement: Gold loans ~45% of portfolio now, targeting ~20% by 2030; shifting to multi-product franchise (LAP, CV/CE, wealth, corporate salary)
items.quote: When gold loan is slated to be around 20% of the portf olio eventually by 2030 , which is around 45% right now

items.statement: De-growing unsecured (two-wheeler, personal, MFI, agri); growing LAP, CV/CE, auto inventory funding with collateral visibility
items.quote: degrowth has happened in 3- 4 products, which are all high-yielding products viz, Two-wheeler, Personal loans, Agri, MFI etc. Unsecured portfolio, we h ave degrown big time

items.statement: Retail asset strategy shifting to customer-centric franchise model via branches; cross-sell to drive wallet share from FY27-28
items.quote: the long run is not product-centric. Roadmap on the long term is that we will have all businesses and all products, and based on the liability franchise and the customer acquisition we build it in and around the branches. Customer deepening will happen to get a decent wallet

items.statement: LCR >130% at quarter-end (119% average); CD ratio 86%; diversified funding via FCY borrowings and refinance
items.quote: We ended the quarter wit h an LCR of over 130% as on 31.12.24 & 119% on an average basis, which is marginally higher than the previous quarter

items.statement: FCY borrowings and refinance used to bridge deposit-advance gap; borrowing ~12% of portfolio
items.quote: We complimented our funding with FCY borrowings and Refinance based on cost considerations, which helped us in maintaining LCR at comfortable levels.

items.statement: CRAR 21.08%, Tier-1 19.73% (ex-interim PAT); low RWA density (~40% vs industry)
items.quote: On a capital base, our CRAR is at 21.08% and Tier-1 ratio is 19.73 % - this will improve when the profits are reckoned at the end of fourth quarter. We have l ow proportion of risk-weight assets compared to industry, which is marginally higher than 40

items.statement: Other income grew 75% YoY to ~19% of total income; core granular fees ~15% of total income (processing, bancassurance, cards, forex)
items.quote: Other income registered a 75% growth on a YoY basis a nd 10% on a sequential quarter basis. Other income constituted ~19% of the total inco me, which is a significant improvement from what the bank used to do two years

items.statement: Gold loan RBI circular (Sept 30) compliance completed by Dec 31; no business impact; exited sub-Rs 2L agri gold accounts per new collateral rule
items.quote: As on 31st December, as per the timelines stipulated in the circular, we have also communicated to RBI about our compliance to all the points. Hence, it has not impacted us last quarter, I do not think that the circular will impact us this quarter or in future.

items.statement: Gold price rise reduces LTV (74% to 70%); some customer exits/prepayments; managed via 68-75% LTV band (agri up to 85%)
items.quote: In one such scenario, our LTV had moved down from 74% to 70%. It proves that obviously not all customers does that because LTV is goin g down as gold price is going up

items.statement: Conservative de-risking strategy: exiting high-yield unsecured and select corporate accounts despite profitability
items.quote: we decided to de-risk o ur portfolio around a year back, and that is accelerating as we are going, leading to some of the high-yielding portfolios moving out

items.statement: Senior leadership team fully in place; no further senior hires planned
items.quote: All our leadership is in place right now. We do not have any more leadership to be hired in the bank right now at a senior level.

items.statement: Profitability: Net profit Rs 152 Cr (+10% QoQ, marginally up YoY); Operating profit Rs 221 Cr (+13% YoY, +10% QoQ); RoA 1.52%, RoE 15.28%
items.quote: Net profit of Rs 152 Cr for the quarter, marginally up YoY and improved by 10% QoQ. Operating profit of the bank is Rs 221 Crs with a growth of 13% and 10% on a YoY & QoQ basis respectively.

name: SBI Cards and Payment Services Ltd

items.statement: Receivables growth guidance for next year at 12-15%
items.quote: Next year, what we are looking at is in the range of somewhere around 12% to 15% as the receivable growth.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio expected around 52% for the year
items.quote: But on average, as we've said earlier as well, the number should be around that 50%, 55% in a very broad range, but around 52% kind of a number for the year.

items.statement: GNPA stable at 3.24%, expected to start improving
items.quote: Our GNPA for the quarter has remained stable at 3.24% as compared to 3.27% in the previous quarter. We expect the GNPA ratio to start improving now.

items.statement: Gross credit cost increased 40 bps to 9.4%
items.quote: The Gross credit cost has increased by 40 Bps to 9.4% from 9% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Credit costs expected to moderate from inflection point
items.quote: We believe we are at an inflection point in our credit cycle. As we further intensify our efforts on tightening underwriting standards, portfolio management, and collections, we expect the credit costs to start moderating.

items.statement: 30-day and 90-day delinquency improved by 20 bps
items.quote: For the first time in several quarters, the 30-day delinquency and the 90-day delinquency have come off appreciably by 20 basis points.

items.statement: Flows into delinquency improving consistently over last year
items.quote: The performance metrics around our flows into delinquency, as MD sir mentioned, they have been improving. They've been improving consistently over the last 1 year.

items.statement: Flows from delinquency to write-off started improving in last 3 months
items.quote: In the last 3 months, however, it has been coming down. So that reversal o r that change in trend has happened about 3 months ago, and that is what is contributing to the outlook that we are giving to you right now

items.statement: Retail spends grew 10% YoY to Rs 80,792 Cr
items.quote: Retail spends remain strong at Rs 80,792 Cr with 10% YoY increase.

items.statement: New account acquisition at 11.75 lakh with 7% YoY growth
items.quote: During Q3 FY25, our new account acquisition was at 11.75 lakh with a 7% YoY growth.

items.statement: Cards-in-force crossed 2 crore mark with 10% YoY growth
items.quote: Our cards-in-force (CIF) have crossed the 2-crore mark, witnessing a healthy 10% YoY growth.

items.statement: Cost of funds stable at 7.4%, expected to remain at current levels
items.quote: Cost of funds (CoF) has remained stable at 7.4%. We expect CoF to remain at around current levels going forward till we see any rate cut action.

items.statement: Revolve rate stable at 24% for last 4-5 quarters
items.quote: This revolver has been stable as of now for last 4, 5 quarters.

items.statement: New vintages showing slightly lower revolve rates than portfolio average
items.quote: We are able to see after 3 to 4 quarters, we see the revolve trends for vintage more than 6 to 9 months, which we have acquired as of now, but slightly lower than what is the average of the portfolio.

items.statement: Investment increase due to regulatory HQLA requirements and liability book growth
items.quote: This is in line with the regulatory requirements. There was a graded increase in the requirements for keeping HQLA, which is highly liquid assets for LCR purposes. And we've been adding on to that number based on the requirements. And also, our liability book also growing.

items.statement: Bureau reporting moving to fortnightly from monthly, subscribed to bureau trigger product
items.quote: With respect to the 15-day window, so while everybody has started the process, since we subscribe to this product, we will anyway get the information. But yes, we are looking at how we can reduce our bureau pool period with the new updates, which are happening fortnightly.

items.statement: Online spends share at 58.5% of retail spends for nine months
items.quote: Online spends are robust, with a share of around 58.5% of total retail spends for the nine-month period.

items.statement: RuPay card spends at UPI terminals grew over 45% QoQ
items.quote: RuPay card spends at UPI terminals continue to grow and have shown a growth of SBI Cards and more than 45% over the previous quarter

items.statement: Focus on POS EMI conversion and FlexPay instead of inducing revolve
items.quote: We are, however, trying to work more at the point-of-sale EMI conversion and the other product, which is we call as FlexPay, which is where the customer can convert the spend before the payment due date into instalments, so that is the portion on which we are working at and more activity is being done there.

items.statement: Banca channel share increased in new account sourcing
items.quote: The sourcing from the Banca channel has increased in this quarter.

items.statement: Liquidity coverage ratio at 114% vs 100% statutory requirement
items.quote: Liquidity coverage ratio for Q3 FY25 is 114% as against statutory requirement of 100%.

items.statement: Capital Adequacy Ratio at healthy 22.9% vs 18.4% last year
items.quote: Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) for the period ended December 31, 2024, is at a healthy 22.9% as compared to around 18.4% in the same period last fiscal.

items.statement: Spends market share at 15.6% per RBI Dec'24 data
items.quote: SBI Card spends market share is 15.6% (As per RBI Dec'24 data).

items.statement: Cards-in-force market share at 18.7% per RBI Dec'24 data
items.quote: SBI Card CIF market share in Q3 FY25 is 18.7% (As per RBI Dec'24 data).

items.statement: Credit cost normalization pace uncertain, depends on macro and portfolio behavior
items.quote: very difficult to give a firm number of credit costs considering what uncertainties we have seen over a period of time. As I said that the customer behavior has been changing very sharply over a period of time

items.statement: Write-off reduction depends on NPA pool behavior and collection efforts
items.quote: If you strictly speak about write-offs, you will be knowing that we have an NPA pool. We continue to work upon them. The NPA pool has reduced, we continue to work upon them and extract most out of it will depend to what extent the write-offs will be reducing.

items.statement: Yield compression expected to exceed historical 3-3.5% range in FY26
items.quote: we do expect, however, in the future, there could be some stream, more than usual reduction in the yields over the c oming year due to some price

items.statement: Yield adjustment impact to play out over FY26
items.quote: So it will play out in our case also. Don't read it bigger than what it is. But yes, it will happen over financial year '26, FY '26.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin at 47% in Q3 FY25, up 220 bps YoY
items.quote: Despite these times, we had EBITDA percentage at 47%, almost 220 basis points up year -on-year, which I think from an execution discipline, cost management perspective is very sound.

items.statement: PAT margin at 32.6% in Q3 FY25, up ~300 bps YoY
items.quote: PAT grew over 40%. And the PAT percentage is at 32.6%, and this is almost 300 basis points up year-on-year.

items.statement: Equity AUM grew 51% YoY, crossing INR25 lakh crore
items.quote: Overall, AUM grew about 38%, equity assets, which have had a green stellar run grew 51%, but at 38% strong growth, although slower than some of the past quarters, but still very commendable.

items.statement: Equity net inflows at INR97,000 crore in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Equity net inflows were at about INR97,000 crores. So close to a INR1 lakh crore number of equity net inflows is a staggering remarkable number.

items.statement: New SIP registrations grew ~50% YoY in Q3 FY25
items.quote: SIPs, new registrations, while they climbed almost 50% year-on-year, were not as strong as the second quarter.

items.statement: Won all 3 MF-RTA mandates on offer in Q3 FY25 including Jio BlackRock, Pantomath MF, Choice
items.quote: We won all 3 MF-RTA mandates on offer. Jio BlackRock, which was kind of agreed some time back. We were waiting for the execution, so we're formally announcing now. Pantomath MF, which is an emerging but large AIF player in the country. Choice, which is a listed holdco, which has a large broking operation, but also a lot of stuff in distribution and other live capital markets activities.

items.statement: Won second MF-RTA migration mandate from competition in Q3 FY25
items.quote: We also won the second MF-RTA migration mandate from competition. I think a lot of you about knowing the name, tenure and some of the salient details about this.

items.statement: Added 21 new AIF clients in Q3 FY25, GIFT City clients now 25 managing over $1B AUM
items.quote: 21 new clients, 21 new clients during the quarter. GIFT City has been a great story. We now have 25 clients managing over $1 billion of AUM

items.statement: CAMS WealthServ added 53 new mandates, 185+ sign-ups in Q3 FY25
items.quote: But including CAMS WealthServ, which is onboarding platform, almost 53 new mandates. WealthServ almost 185-plus sign-ups.

items.statement: CAMSPay added 24 new logos in Q3 FY25
items.quote: I think from a logo addition perspective, I didn't speak about that, almost 24 new logos added in Q3.

items.statement: CAMS KRA added 20+ financial entities and one top-5 brokerage in Q3 FY25
items.quote: On the KRA side, I spoke about the revenue growth, added almost 20 -plus different financial entities, fin-tech's, MFs, continue to scale up and not have a ban. And added one of the top 5 brokerages.

items.statement: Historical yield compression 3-3.5% annually, expected to be higher in FY26
items.quote: So that's been the long -term range in terms of the yield's compression. What we feel is that the 3.5% might not hold good going forward, at least for the next year.

items.statement: Capex and IT opex larger than usual in FY25 due to platform re-architecture and talent infusion
items.quote: Our capex this year has been larger than usual, also the IT opex. But I'll let Ram Charan kind of give you a little more detail in terms of exact numbers.

items.statement: Set up new GIFT City office in October with capacity for 50+ people
items.quote: GIFT City, decidedly underscoring our leadership, having set up a new office back in October with the capability to seat over 50 people.

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents at INR770 crore at end of Q3 FY25
items.quote: We entered the quarter with a very comfortable cash and cash equivalent of INR770 crores.

items.statement: Interim dividend of INR17.5 per share declared, total FY25 dividend payout INR260 crore
items.quote: The Board was pleased to declare an interim dividend of INR17.5 per share. With this, the total dividend pay-out only for the current year, which is the first quarter dividend, the special dividend that we declared in the second quarter. And this put together is INR260 crores of pay-out of dividend is what we are doing only for the current year.

items.statement: NFO collection share at 70% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: NFO sales, which you know, I mean, new AMCs have to do that, but some of the established AMCs do that just to broaden the pr oduct portfolio and right-size the offerings, 35 new schemes. So almost a scheme every third day. It just creates significant operational demands in the team, but we've come out very well. 70% share of NFO collections

items.statement: Net SIP registration share increased to 64% from 60% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Again, for the quarter, very neat share gain. Net registration share increased to 64% from 60%.

items.statement: Unique investor base at 3.9 crore, share grew 31% vs industry 25% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: And similarly, a very similar trend on unique investor base, which touched INR3.9 crores, just short of INR4 crores. Our share grew 31%, industry was 25%. So again, significantly ahead of industry competition.

items.statement: Transaction volumes grew 40% YoY to 24 crore in Q3 FY25
items.quote: So between technology process, compliance, operations, all of them have done well. Overall unique investor growth, I spoke about, 31% against, so ahead of industry growth. Equity AUM 51%, net sales almost doubling in a year. And new SIP registrations also in a year (19.45 mins) growing about 50%. So I think that this is a good annunciation of what a great product can look like.

items.statement: Significant talent infusion from IITs/IIMs and senior hires in last year, employee cost stable at 32-33% of revenue
items.quote: From an employee perspective, we've seen it to be stable around 32% to 33% of revenue. So barring this one quarter in April, May, June, where there could be some increase because of the annual appraisal impact, it has traditionally been around 2% of revenue.

items.statement: Non-MF business EBITDA margin is close to 15%.
items.quote: Yes. I think while we generally give a range. And I again always caution saying that all these businesses are very different in different stages of where they are in terms of go-to-market. But then just ease of understanding, the bucket of non-MF has got a margin of close to 15%.

items.statement: Expect stable quarterly expenses around INR195-196 crores ex-depreciation, with a couple of crores increase next quarter; employee cost stable at 32-33% of revenue.
items.quote: We've been around the INR195 crores, INR196 crores other than depreciation at the total quarterly expenses. You can say you'll see probably a couple of crores of increase in expenses, but we see a stable expense base.

items.statement: MF revenue growth target 15%, non-MF revenue growth target excess of 20% over coming quarters.
items.quote: So broadly, what we have said is that we would like to grow MF revenue at 15%, non-MF in excess of 20%.

items.statement: AIF revenue expected to grow at baseline 20% over coming quarters.
items.quote: AIF, our belief is domestic AIF and GIFT City is perhaps a 20% growth market, is not a 30%, 35% growth market in AUM. At that level, we are confident we should be able to deliver a baseline 20% growth in the AIF revenue over the coming quarters.

items.statement: Micro-SIP (INR250) expands market to non-salaried; foundational building block for next decade like SIP was for last decade.
items.quote: Think of it as a foundational building block. Just like you saw the normal SIP changed the market in these 10 years, let's say, in 2014, 2015, think of this small ticket SIP to be the next change agent for the next decade.

items.statement: New AMC mandates: Jio BlackRock, Angel, Unifi likely to launch in 6-9 months; Choice, Pantomath, Cosmea (pending license) also signed.
items.quote: What is visible on the horizon, although the dates are still not announced is Jio BlackRock, Angel and Unifi. I rate at least the first two of them, who expressed their ambitions to be scale players, and they have been scale players in various markets by now.

items.statement: Won an inbound mandate from a small old AMC; annual billing a few crore rupees; name to be announced in 1-2 weeks.
items.quote: It's an old AMC. It's a small AMC. The annual billing will be a few crore rupees. Think of it as that size. So we will announce the name maybe in the next week or two.

items.statement: Yield pressure limited to 1-2 customers; impact on revenue growth at most 1-2 percentage points over next 4 quarters; profitability not adversely affected.
items.quote: I don't see that will be significantly different, probably 1% point down, at most 2% points could be the impact. But I think on a best-case scenario, I don't think it will be down by more than 1% point.

items.statement: Non-MF pricing largely stabilized across payments, KRA, AIF; only large insurance deals may see discounted pricing.
items.quote: In terms of non-MF pricing, see, it's largely stabilized. If you see the basic churn we were having was on the account aggregator stuff, I think they have reached a stage where, obviously, there could be some variations here and there, but it's not a steep decline.

items.statement: AIF AUM grew >15% from <INR2 trillion to INR2.35-2.38 trillion; net of falloffs, reasonable growth.
items.quote: On the AIF, our AUM has grown more than 15% percentage in terms of -- it was less than INR2 trillion, and we have kind of come to INR2.38 trillion or INR2.35 trillion is the current AUM that we service.

items.statement: Repository business near breakeven; revenue spike expected when policies scale from 1 crore to 1.5-2 crores in next ~6 months.
items.quote: I think the next 1 year is crucial as we move from INR1 crore to INR1.5 crores, INR1.5 crores to INR2 crores policies. Close to somewhere in this year, you will see a revenue spike in the pure repository business.

items.statement: Capex will continue for Rearc, SEBI compliance, and IT infra; opex stable despite talent and cybersecurity investments.
items.quote: The capex, will continue to make investments in terms of the Rearc, in terms of the other compliances that we need to do for SEBI purposes or for IT infra purposes. But from opex perspective, in spite of continuing to invest in talent and in spite of buying the latest cybersecurity tools, etcetera, we continue to invest in, we don't see a significant change in the cost base.

items.statement: Competitive wins (Navi, new AMC) are inbound at premium pricing; do not discount vs installed base or competitor pricing.
items.quote: Both Navi and this contract were inbound inquiries, which means they wanted to explore a change, came to us. We wanted to see their determination in terms of whether they're really determined or not. And once we believe that this was a dialogue, and we always end up charging a premium.

items.statement: KRA revenue tightly coupled to capital market account opening activity; demand compresses when account openings fall to 60-70% of momentum.
items.quote: You saw tremendous scale coming up because that activity was heightening. In those time periods, when that activity falls to, let's say, 60%, 70% of its traditional momentum, you will see some compression in KRA demand and KRA revenue.

items.statement: Non-MF revenue share target 20% of overall revenue; building blocks in place despite one quarter of 22% growth.
items.quote: And we do have visibility to do that, that a quarter here of 22% down. But then if you see earlier few quarters, it was much more than 30%. So I don't think we should read too much into 1 quarter of 22%.

items.statement: SEBI's INR250 SIP mandate expands market to daily/weekly wage earners; CAMS offers beneficial one-time rate for SIP triggers and KRA for these customers.
items.quote: The thinking behind that is that SIP has been a salaried person's product, somebody who gets a payroll on the first of every month. And now this is distributing it to people, who are non salaried, maybe daily wages or weekly wages. So it significantly expands the market.

items.statement: Payments revenue sequential decline due to one-off annual maintenance collection from NPCI; UPI autopay and ACH transactions stable or growing.
items.quote: This is basically a one-off. There will be some annual maintenance revenue that they get from NPCI that they have to collect from the customers and give it to NPCI. So that kind of was a higher number last month.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue guidance for next financial year: INR 5,500-7,000 crores

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA guidance for next financial year: northwards of INR 1,100 crores

But generally, what happens is, especially in ethnic and wedding wear market, the kind of impact that this will have is not to that extent.

items.statement: Management expects overall revenue growth of 15-20% for next year, targeting 2.5-3x nominal GDP growth organically.
items.quote: Between 15% to 20%, it should be our growth rate.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to improve 20-25 bps year-on-year driven by operational leverage and higher-margin business mix.
items.quote: We will grow margins of 20 to 25 basis points year-on-year, and we expect that to continue.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved 60 bps YoY to 7.4% in Q3 FY25; excluding finance income, margin expanded 90 bps to 7.0%.
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 7.4% versus 6.8% in Q3 FY '24, an improvement of 60 basis points over last year same period.

items.statement: 9M FY25 EBITDA margin rose 120 bps YoY to 7.3%; excluding finance income, up 100 bps to 6.7%.
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the 9-month period is 7.3% versus 6.1% in the 9-month period ending FY '24, a significant improvement of 120 basis points.

items.statement: IFM segment EBITDA margin at 6.1% for 9M FY25; BSS segment EBITDA margin at 9.5% for 9M FY25, both improved consistently YoY.
items.quote: IFM segment EBITDA margin stood at 6.1%, while BSS segment stood at 9.5%, as both IFM as well as BSS margins improved consiste ntly compared to the same time last year

items.statement: IFM revenue grew 9% YoY in Q3 FY25 to INR 455.4 cr; 9M FY25 IFM revenue grew 8% to INR 1,328.7 cr.
items.quote: During Q3 '25, our IFM revenue grew roughly by about 9%, on a year-on-year basis stood at about –INR 455.4 crores.

items.statement: BSS revenue grew 7% YoY in Q3 FY25 to INR 245.1 cr; 9M FY25 BSS revenue grew 19% to INR 717 cr.
items.quote: BSS segment revenues grew by 7% to INR2,451 million in Q3.

items.statement: Added 60 new substantial logos in IFM and 35 in BSS during 9M FY25 (logos with >INR 5 lakh revenue).
items.quote: During the 9 months FY '25, we added 60 logos in IFM segment and 35 new logos in BSS segment.

items.statement: IFM margin improvement driven by shift to high-value contracts (industrial catering, warehouse, production support) and operational efficiency.
items.quote: Our strategy revolving around driving operational efficiency while actively optimizing our low margin contracts have started to pay positive results, evident in improvement in having witnessed the IFM segment EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Denave investing in AI-driven tech (Intellibank) to improve efficiency and margins; expects payback in next few quarters.
items.quote: We successfully have begun utilizing GenAI sales intelligence, which is our proprietary technology called Intellibank. This would also start paying us back probably in the next few quarters coming.

items.statement: Athena lost two large BFSI clients in 9M FY25 (one closed India ops, one sold business); 9M revenue INR 107 cr, full year expected flat at INR 135 cr.
items.quote: The current revenue for the 9-month period is INR 107 crores, and they'll be closing the full-year period with about INR 135 crores, which will be at par with last year what they did.

items.statement: Athena diversifying into non-BFSI sectors (retail, education); new client conversion lead time 2-3 quarters.
items.quote: We have been working continuously on reduc ing our customer concentration in Athena and diversifying into other sec tors like retail, education, etc. The lead time for converting business is about 2 to 3 quarters

items.statement: Global ground handling now operational at all 22 airports; 6-7 airports not yet 100% operational, expected fully operational by Q1 FY26.
items.quote: Even now, when I say we have started operating 22, still 6 or 7 airports are not being 100% operational in terms of getting all the clearances and starting off in terms of equipment and all that. However, all these will be operational, definitely 100% operational, by first quarter of next year.

items.statement: Global broke even in 9M FY25 after INR 9 cr loss last year; expected FY25 profit INR 1-2 cr; FY26 margin expected high single-digit or more.
items.quote: Last year was minus INR9 crores. This year, it will be a positive INR1 crores or INR2 crores.

items.statement: No major capex disclosed; Global investments completed over past 1.5 years to operationalize 22 airports.
items.quote: It has taken about a year, 1.5 years for us to get all these airports actually operational.

items.statement: Company is net cash with net debt/equity of -0.2x as of Dec 31, 2024; all borrowings repaid in Oct 2024; cash balance INR 176 cr.
items.quote: UDS is a net cash company, and net debt to equity is negative 0.2 as on 31st December 2024. We have overall 69,000 people, and IFM stood at 54,053 employees and BSS segment stood at 14,762 employees.

items.statement: Finance cost going forward primarily lease costs; minor cash credit fluctuations possible unless acquisition funded by debt.
items.quote: Predominantly, it will be the lease finance cost, unless we go for an acquisition and get into borrowing.

items.statement: Three active acquisition conversations ongoing (one large, two smaller); no guarantee of closure; organic growth target 15-20% without M&A.
items.quote: We have 3 active conversations that are going on right now and of varying -- one is a fairly large transaction, the other 2 are slightly smaller.

items.statement: Appointed Snehashish as BSS Group CEO to drive synergies across Denave, Matrix, Athena; onboarded Samriti Malhotra as Group CHRO.
items.quote: We have made Mr. Snehashish, our BSS Group CEO, and seeing synergies across Denave, Matrix and Athena. I mean he is given additional responsibilities as the BSS Group CEO, more across the group for the synergies within the BSS segment. We have recently onboarded Samriti Malhotra, our Group CHRO.

items.statement: Stricter regulations driving growth in Matrix background verification (5-6% market CAGR, UDS targeting ~20%) and A&A audit segment.
items.quote: Stringent regulations and high security concerns of employers would give us more kind of opening for the employee background verification.

items.statement: IFM market expected to grow 10% CAGR to INR 67,100 cr by 2029 (Mordor Intelligence); UDS targets 3x nominal GDP growth.
items.quote: As per Mordor Intelligence, the outsourced IFM market is expected to grow at a CAGR of 10% and reach INR 67,100 crores by 2029 from its current size of INR37,700 crores.

items.statement: BSS overall market expected ~9.5% CAGR; UDS targets 3x GDP growth in BSS driven by sales enablement, audit, background verification, mailroom.
items.quote: Way forward, the overall Business Support Services aim to grow at about 9.5% CAGR.

items.statement: Denave facing 2-quarter transition due to AI/tech disruption; margins not expected to soften further; growth to continue.
items.quote: So in the coming year, we expect new logos to kick in. And we also expect our own efforts in AI and the remote agents, etc. Our own efforts there will start paying off. So -- but this year is right now looking like -- the next few months, maybe 2 quarters, are looking like quarters of transition.

items.statement: Athena new BFSI client inflows stagnated due to regulatory uncertainty; non-BFSI ramp-up expected in subsequent quarters.
items.quote: As on date, there is nothing that has hurt them in the existing business with the RBI regulation, but the new inflows are stagnated.

items.statement: IFM margin improvement from contract rationalization (exiting low-margin) and business mix shift to higher-margin industrial services.
items.quote: Like for example, our industrial business could be warehouse, production support, some engineering services mix we have to increase. So if you look at, even the growth was only 8%-9%, but our margins improved because of our efficiencies and the business mix.

items.statement: Denave commenced South Korea operations in Aug 2024; expanding regionally into newer countries.
items.quote: We have commenced business in South Korea through our office setup in August '24.

items.statement: Management to provide subsidiary-level financials (revenue, EBITDA, PBT) for major entities covering 80-90% of revenue/PAT from next quarter.
items.quote: Next quarter onwards, we will call out these names. There's only 3 companies in BSS and 3 in IFM, which I take 90% of the revenue.

items.statement: Management expects continued growth acceleration in flights and buses, with headroom for market share gains, but provides no specific numerical guidance for FY26.
items.quote: I think, look, if you had asked this question one year back, I don't think I would have told you that we would grow flight GTV at 70% plus. So I think we've managed to surprise ourselves, and I think I give a Le Travenues Technology Limited - January 28, 2025 lot of credit on that to the hard work of the team, the product, the tech behind the scenes

items.statement: Overall GTV grew 48% YoY to INR 4,036.3 crores in Q3 FY25, driven by flights, buses, and spiritual tourism.
items.quote: With overall Gross Transaction Value or GTV crossing INR 4036.3 crores this quarter, a 48% increase Y-o-Y and our overall revenue from operations reaching INR 241.8 crores, a 42% increase Y-o-Y for Q3 and a sequential increase of 17% compared to Q2.

items.statement: Flight GTV grew 73% YoY and bus GTV grew 63% YoY in Q3 FY25, leading to market share gains.
items.quote: Our flights and buses business have been the heroes of this growth with flights GTV growing at over 73% Y-o-Y for Q3 and buses GTV growing at over 63% Y-o-Y leading to market share gains.

items.statement: Train GTV grew 27% YoY in Q3 FY25 despite the advance reservation period change from 120 to 60 days by Indian Railways.
items.quote: Despite the change in advance reservation period from 120 days to 60 days by Indian Railways, which had a one-time negative impact on our train segments last quarter, train GTV has still grown at 27% Y-o-Y in Q3 and train revenue from operations has grown by 26% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Monthly active users across ixigo, ConfirmTkt, and AbhiBus crossed 86 million in Q3 FY25, with 31 million passenger segments booked and over 30 million app downloads.
items.value: 86 million MAU, 31 million segments, 30 million downloads
items.quote: Our own data shows that we crossed 86 million monthly active users across ixigo, ConfirmTkt, and AbhiBus, and 31 million passenger segments were booked in Q3. We got over 30 million app downloads last quarter with a growing proportion of our users starting to book flights, buses, trains, and even hotels with us.

items.statement: Passenger segments for Prayagraj in the first 24 days of January grew 4.62 times YoY, with flight and bus searches up nearly 14 times and train searches nearly 10 times due to Maha Kumbh.
items.quote: Our overall passenger segments for Prayagraj in the first 24 days of January alone have grown 4.62 times compared to the same period last year. And within that, though metros are playing a huge role as origin cities, origin towns such as Nagpur, Jaipur, Lucknow, Gorakhpur, and Varanasi are also playing a pivotal role. Our flight and bus searches have grown nearly 14 times for travel to Prayagraj a

items.statement: Spiritual tourism destinations like Varanasi, Gaya, Shirdi, Puri, Haridwar, Katra, Vaishno Devi saw 100% to 150% YoY growth in train bookings.
items.quote: In fact, spiritual tourism as an overall vector for growth has shown remarkable potential for us, with many destinations such as Varanasi, Gaya, Shirdi, Puri, Haridwar, Katra, Vaishno Devi recently seeing a 100% to 150% growth in train bookings if one compares year over year.

items.statement: Group contribution margin grew 32% YoY to INR 102.5 crores, but contribution margin percentage decreased from 45% to 42% due to growth investments.
items.quote: At the group level, our contribution margins, defined as revenue from operations less direct costs, grew to INR 102.5 crores, up from INR 77.5 crores, an increase of 32%. However, the contribution margin percentage slightly decreased this quarter, from 45% to 42%, due to our investment in accelerating growth, something which Rajnish talked about in detail.

items.statement: Contribution margin mix is well-diversified: Trains 39%, Buses 33%, Flights 27% of group contribution margin in Q3 FY25.
items.quote: Last quarter, if you examine the contribution margin, with all three lines of businesses contributing more evenly in the mix, trains constitute 39%, buses constitute 33%, and flights 27% of the overall contribution margin mix, making ixigo a very well-diversified OTA.

items.statement: Food delivery on trains (Zoop) integrated across ixigo and ConfirmTkt apps, seeing decent growth in orders while maintaining profitability; expanding stations, delivery staff, and restaurant partnerships.
items.quote: Last quarter, we integrated Zoop, our latest acquisition across ixigo and ConfirmTkt apps, enabling our rail users to order food and get it delivered to their berth or seat. And we have seen decent growth in food orders. We're expanding the number of stations of our delivery staff, as well as signing up restaurants and chains at more stations. We're also learning ordering patterns to anticipate de

items.statement: Hotels business in early product-market fit and supply build-out phase, seeing double-digit QoQ growth organically from existing user base across flights, trains, buses.
items.quote: Let's talk a bit about hotels as well, where we are still in the early phase of product market fit and supply build-out. As we discover pain areas that hotel bookers face in this industry, we are figuring out ways to solve them through Le Travenues Technology Limited - January 28, 2025 better hotel ranking, NPS measurement, and data science in order to surface the right quality of supply to the us

items.statement: Bus supply expanded with 4 State Road Transport Corporations (SRTCs) and 200+ private bus operators added on AbhiBus in Q3; Abhi Assured operators increased 3x YoY.
items.value: 4 SRTCs, 200+ private operators; Abhi Assured operators 3x YoY
items.quote: We have also expanded our bus supply with 4 State Road Transport Corporations, or SRTCs, and 200-plus private bus operators being added on AbhiBus in Q3. And the number of our Abhi Assured operators has also gone 3x compared to what it was last year.

items.statement: International flight segments grew 61% YoY in Q3; deepening partnerships with international carriers to improve supply and content for Tier 1 users.
items.quote: Tier 1 to Tier 1 flight passenger segments for us have grown with a similar momentum as our NBU flights, bookings over 68% year-on-year Q3, and we have seen our international flight segments growing at 61% year-on-year in Q3. With deepening partnerships with international carriers, we expect improved supply and content even further on international flights in order to serve our Tier 1 users better

items.statement: Onboarded Rohit Sharma as new Brand Ambassador for ixigo Trains to launch digital and offline brand awareness initiatives to build trust and improve brand penetration.
items.quote: It is in this spirit that we have upped our marketing spends a bit on flights and buses and onboarded Rohit Sharma as our new Brand Ambassador for ixigo Trains to launch digital and offline brand awareness initiatives to further build trust and improve penetration of our brands.

items.statement: Bus market penetration remains low at around 20%, indicating significant headroom for growth.
items.quote: If we talk about buses, the overall market penetration is still pretty low at around 20%. So it is pertinent that we continue to double down on growth.

items.statement: Flight market share still relatively small (4th largest OTA by GTV/passenger segments) despite #1 MAU position, indicating headroom for growth.
items.quote: I think if you zoom out and see today our market share is still, we are the fourth largest OTA from GTV or passenger segment perspective. So I think our market share is still not that big compared to some of the incumbents and on the flight side. So I think there is still scope to continue accelerating this growth given that when you compare our MAUs with any other OTAs, we are the number one on M

items.statement: Share of loss from associate Fresh Bus was INR 1.9 crores in Q3 FY25 vs INR 2.1 crores loss in Q3 FY24.
items.quote: Our share of loss from our associate, Fresh Bus, was INR 1.9 crores, compared to a loss of INR 2.1 crores in Q3 FY'24.

items.statement: Tax expenses shifted from a credit of INR 16.7 crores last year to an expense of INR 5.9 crores this year, largely due to deferred tax credit reversal.
items.value: INR 5.9 crores expense (vs INR 16.7 crores credit YoY)
items.quote: Tax expenses shifted from a credit of INR 16.7 crores last year, to an expense of INR 5.9 crores this year, largely due to deferred tax credit reversal.

items.statement: Management guides customer inducement costs (discount + branding + performance) to be around 3.5% of GTV internally, not formal guidance
items.quote: We would look at it as wanting it to be around 3.5%, which is a combination of discount plus branding plus performance.

items.statement: Technology and AI investments expected to continue for next few quarters, may reduce profit margin by a few percentage points
items.quote: I would still guide for this investment to be there for the next few quarters. And it might take a few percentage points away from the PM that we are generating.

items.statement: Technology costs grown over 50% year-on-year; investments in AI, cloud, and re-architecting operations
items.quote: I can clearly see that your technology costs have grown more than 50% year-on-year, if you look at it that way.

items.statement: Hotel business in product-market fit discovery phase, building supply and content; expected to take few quarters to scale
items.quote: On hotels, like Rajneesh and I mentioned, I think it's very early days. So I wish I could talk a lot about it, but honestly, like we're in the product market fit discovery phase and getting the supply right, getting a lot of the content, right.

items.statement: Bus bookings to Prayagraj increased almost 14 times year-on-year due to Maha Kumbh spiritual tourism
items.quote: Prayagraj, which again is in the North, right? I mean, we saw an almost 14 times increase in bus booking Y-o-Y towards Prayagraj, thanks to the Maha Kumbh.

items.statement: Online bus penetration at 20-22%, leaving 80% of market offline as major growth opportunity
items.quote: If you look at online penetration in this space, it's somewhere between 20%-22% as we speak, right? And I think the big opportunity we see on buses is how can we bring those people online to book buses who are today not booking them online at all, right?

items.statement: Annual active users at 80+ million, nearly half of India's internet population; focus on conversions and high-quality users over MAU growth
items.quote: We are already at a point where like 80-plus million MAUs, I don't know how many Internet properties would have that kind of scale.

items.statement: Flight refund average time just over 3 hours; 94% of calls picked up within 2 minutes, up from 92%
items.quote: If you look at our average refund time of just over three hours, that's one of the big pains we keep hearing time and again from people. And then we keep hearing that it's hard to get through to call centers, for OTAs. And again, we decided to publish what percentage of calls we pick up within two minutes. And in that sense, again, we are disclosing that every quarter and that numbers keep moving

items.statement: Management does not track competitor share gains/losses; focuses on product experience and customer service to retain users
items.quote: we have a very different philosophy with Le Travenues Technology Limited - January 28, 2025 respect to how we look at competition because I don't think we're tracking like who is gaining share, who is losing share. I think we're just trying to do a decent job at getting the product experience right and trying to expose flights as an option to millions of users out there who still don't look at tha

items.statement: Competitors can copy features but will always be behind due to customer-obsessed culture and solving right problems at right time
items.quote: Of course they can, anything can be copied today, right? Like anybody can copy anything. And especially when technology has been commoditized, but we don't really worry about them. I'll tell you why because eventually what happens is that if your core focus and culture and DNA is about customer obsession and solving customer problems, then you always have your ears to the ground.

items.statement: GTV run rate reached close to $2 billion ARR in less than 2 years after taking 16 years to reach first billion
items.quote: It took us almost 16 years to get to our first billion run rate of GTV, but it has taken us less than two years to get to close to 2 billion GTV ARR.

items.statement: Bus app maintains 4.8 rating with scale of reviews and downloads, described as very hard to achieve
items.quote: 4.8 app rating with that scale of reviews and downloads is very, very hard to do if you ask any practitioner in our space.

items.statement: Zoop acquisition consolidated in 'others' segment; early integration stages with impressive initial response
items.quote: So Swapnil, it comes in others. At a point of time when it's big enough, we'll move it out. And it's a different segment and we feel that it's early days as of right now. What we are seeing in terms of the integration, the response initially has been very, very impressive.

items.statement: Added 200 more private bus operators and a bunch of SRTCs last quarter; expanding supply while maintaining quality guardrails
items.quote: Last quarter we've added 200 more private operators and a bunch of more SRTCs. So our objective is to have all the supply that is possible to have in terms of bringing them online.

items.statement: Marketing spend optimized for CAC/LTV; most marketing acquisition breaks even by second transaction
items.quote: We are very pertinent about looking at CAC and LTV and making sure that, I mean, most of the marketing acquisition we do from the second transaction itself, we are able to get back the kind of money that we are spending to acquire those users.

items.statement: AI and technology investments critical to protect against disruption; risk of not investing higher than cost of investment
items.quote: If you do not invest in this technology, if you do not protect yourself from that disruption, I think the risks are much higher than that.

items.statement: Internal AI efficiency focus: creating agents across organization to increase observability and automate operational tasks
items.quote: Internally we have AI efficiency as a focus area where we are creating the vision of having agents across the organization that help increase observability and efficiency across all the operational tasks that people are performing and make them automated and efficient.

items.statement: International flights growth driven by GDS integrations, commercial agreements with international airlines, and feature rollout (ixigo Assured, Flight Tracker Pro, Price Lock)
items.quote: international where you need GDS integrations and multiple international airlines to sign up commercially with you. It's something that we've been obviously doubling down on in the last couple of years and the last couple of quarters even more so. The other thing is that we've been obviously enhancing some of the features that make more sense for international travel. For example, ixigo Assured is

items.statement: Operational portfolio of 2,540 MW to give run-rate annual EBITDA of INR 1,750-1,800 crores
items.quote: 2,540 MW, which is operational for us will give us a run rate annual project to bid of around INR 1,750 to INR 1,800 crores.

items.statement: Target 6,970 MW operational capacity by FY27-28
items.quote: We will make all efforts to prepone this, but in the base case we have 6,970 MW of capacity which we will be operating by FY'27-28.

items.statement: Pre-tax ROCE of 14.5% from operational assets
items.quote: In terms of the ROCE, which is basically pre-tax ROCE, we do 14.5%.

items.statement: Operational capacity doubled from 1,340 MW to 2,540 MW in Q3 FY25 via 1,200 MW SECI solar commissioning
items.quote: We have essentially doubled our capacity from 1,340 MW to 2,540 MW. So, we have increased by 90% and this is due to the commissioning of our 300x4, 1,200 MW of solar capacity which is tied up with SECI.

items.statement: 450 MW in advanced construction stages (350 MW solar merchant, 100 MW wind)
items.quote: 450 MW of our capacity is in advanced stages of construction. So, that is something which is in very advanced stages.

items.statement: 350 MW commissioning targeted in Q4 FY25 (may spill to April), 100 MW wind by June-September quarter
items.quote: We are doing our best to commission the 350 MW in this quarter. So, that is the intent that 350 MW gets fully commissioned. Of course, we will do our best to try and do that. It may spill over to April, 350 MW in worst case, but that is what we are trying. And the 100 MW wind, again, we'll try in best case to do it by let's say between June to September quarter.

items.statement: Total contracted portfolio 6.97 GW; won 1,900 MW in FY25 (1,000 MW FDRE, 600 MW solar, 300 MW hybrid)
items.quote: In terms of the new orders and growth side, we have won 1,900 MW of capacity in this financial year. So, our total contracted portfolio is 6.97 GW.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin ~90% on reported basis due to operating leverage
items.quote: As far as margin s are concerned, they are like 90% on the reported basis on account of the higher operating leverage, because now we have higher base of operational assets

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to remain steady at current levels ±2% going forward
items.quote: In terms of the percentage margins, we will be here (+/-2%) right, in terms of the EBITDA margins and the PAT margins.

items.statement: 1,200 MW SECI solar project designed for 30% CUF; achieved 31-33% recently
items.quote: This 1,200 MW is designed to achieve 30% of CUF. When we started for example, last few days we are touching 32, 33, 31, right, so this whole plant will operate at 30% CUF.

items.statement: Merchant solar tariffs recently INR 2.7-3.0/unit; won SECI bid at INR 3.05 for 300 MW merchant plant
items.quote: In terms of the merchant tariff, in the past quarter or so, we have sold power in the range of INR 2.7 to INR 3 sometimes. So, that's the tariff you can assume on an average basis more than INR 3 we have for the merchant plan of 300 MW. Of course, like I said, we have got a PPA of 3.05 for that.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR 6,882 crores from INR 8,755 crores using IPO proceeds (INR 2,070 crores)
items.quote: So, debt has been reduced by around INR 2,070 crores, which has resulted in a steep reduction in the net debt. So, net debt is now at INR 6,882 crores in this quarter as compared to INR 8,755 crores in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Refinanced 50-55% of debt (~INR 5,500 crores) at average 8.8% rate, ~70 bps reduction
items.quote: We have refinanced essentially 50-55% of our debt, which is around INR 5,500 crores, so at an average rate of 8.8% per annum. So, this results in two positives for us. One is the reduction in cost of debt and second is the cash release.

items.statement: Net operational debt/EBITDA ~5x, below guided 5.5x; net debt/equity 1.6x post-IPO
items.quote: If you look at the net operational debt on an annual EBITDA basis for the current financial year, it will be around 5X, which is below our guided range of 5.5X. And net debt-to-equity after raising the primary capital from the IPO currently stood at 1.6X.

items.statement: 1,200 MW SECI project gross block INR 4,600 crores (net of EPC margin)
items.quote: It is INR 4,600 crores. If you, if you look at the, I think the actual CAPEX, so INR 4,600 crores.

items.statement: Cash PAT INR 189 crores in Q3 FY25 (up 52% reported, 149% like-to-like)
items.quote: Our cash PAT for the quarter is INR 189 crores which is up 52% on reported basis and up 149% to be precise on like-to-like asset basis.

items.statement: CUF improved to 23.7% in 9M FY25 (up from last year); expected to rise further as high-CUF projects increase
items.quote: Lastly, from my side, on the operational highlights, we did a large improvement in our CUF, 23.7% is the CUF which we did as compared to the last year , and this CUF I can say for sure that this is going to increase because the proportion of high CU F projects have increased in the

items.statement: Plant availability 99.4%, grid availability 99.6%
items.quote: In terms of plant availability, our plants are running at 99.4% availability and a grid availability of 99.6%.

items.statement: Central offtakers now 67% of portfolio (up from prior), state offtakers 33%
items.quote: In terms of the operational1 portfolio split, now, the central offtakers constitute 67% of our portfolio and states only constitute 33% of the portfolio, which is of course improving the credit rating of the overall portfolio and overall utility business we have

items.statement: ALCM regulations apply only to bids post-circular; no impact on existing PPAs/LOAs
items.quote: It is no impact because if you read the ALCM circular, it is applicable only for the projects where the bids happen post that circular. So, actually those bids are yet to happen. They will start happening now as we speak. So, none of our projects is impacted by those orders whatever we have currently now.

items.statement: CERC infirm power order no impact on renewables; all plants commissioned before Dec 22 effective date
items.quote: No, actually, we read that article, and we were going to release a clarification , our regulatory head has drafted it also, he is going to shortly do it . So, see, in terms of renewables, right, we don't have any fuel charges and other things. So, we have no, no issues with that in terms of the merchant plant or in terms of the, you can say the inf irm power sale

items.statement: No US exposure; all revenue in INR from 25-year PPAs with Indian utilities
items.quote: Right. So, we don't have any sales to US because we are a utility. And in terms of the sale, all of our sale is in 25-year PPA to the utilities in India. So, all of our revenues is in rupees.

items.statement: Hired senior execution president from ABB/Linxon; adding project directors for quality/cost control
items.quote: We are still building more resources on the team side; so a very senior person who joined us as a president of our execution on projects, he came from the very well-established ABB background where he was the M.D. of the ABB Execution India and that company became Linxon. On the quality side also, we are improving because we will do so many projects and we have added many, many project directors.

items.statement: PPA signing for remaining 2,090 MW under-construction capacity expected in 1-2 months; SECI-state negotiations ongoing
items.quote: we are quite positive that the N TPC once again will be signed shortly. So, of course we don't have because this is up to the agency to do it quickly, but what we understand in the last quarter or so, the PPA signing has really picked up pace because lot of FDRE tariffs have been adopted and lot of states have already done, like UP has done

items.statement: Equity funding for 4.6 GW pipeline from three sources: IPO INR 2,400 cr, securitization ~INR 2,500 cr, EPC margins INR 2,000-2,500 cr
items.quote: So, we have raised INR 2,400 crores of IPO money, right.
