items.quote: We reduced the pipeline to 21 days and 21 days is the pipeline now also. So, that was not the case at all.

items.statement: Food inflation at ~8% could cause rural consumers to prioritize food over discretionary spending, potentially reversing rural outperformance
items.quote: But this thing might change because food inflation is very hig h. It's at around 8%. So, if rural also starts prioritizing food as compared to discretionary, thi s thing could change

items.statement: Healthcare portfolio flat due to delayed winters; Chyawanprash declined 3% vs market decline of 6%, gaining 140 bps share; Honey at 54% exit market share
items.quote: The market declined by around 6% and Chyawanpr ash decline was around 3%, thereby we gained shares because there is a decline. So, I thin k it's a matter of time. Also, we are trying to position Chyawanpr ash as an all-weather product

items.statement: Launched science-backed 'Siens' range (collagen powders, multivitamins, gummies) exclusively on Amazon; clinical trials for Khajurprash (30% RDA iron), Honitus (15 min action), Pudin Hara Fizz (30 sec action)
items.quote: We have very recently rolled out a range called Siens only for e-commerce, only exclusively for Amazon, which is all science backed in which you got the collagen powders, and you got the foods of multivitamins for women, multivitamins for men, collagen powder and Gummies.

items.statement: Industry cement demand expected to grow 4-5% in FY25 with H2 much better than H1
items.quote: This demand is expected to grow by 4% to 5% in FY '25, meaning H2 should be much better than H1, further supported by pro infra and housing budget in the 2025.

items.statement: Consolidated cement capacity to reach 104 million tons by Q4 FY25 with Orient acquisition
items.quote: With Orient acquisition at advanced stage, the total capacity by Q4 FY '25 to hit 104 million tons.

items.statement: Target to expand cement capacity to 140 million tons by FY28
items.quote: As we plan to expand our cement capacity to 140 million tons by FY '28, we are pacing well to achieve the stated target.

items.statement: Cost reduction target of INR530 per ton to reach INR3,650 per ton by FY28
items.quote: In December 2023, if you remember, we have indicated a cost reduction target of INR530 per ton, wherein we aspire to achieve and reach to INR3,650 per ton by FY '28.

items.statement: Full year capex target of INR9,000 crores for FY25
items.quote: For the full year, it is closer to INR9,000 crores. And so, another INR2,200 crores will go for this quarter.

items.statement: 9-month capex spend of INR6,200 crores in FY25
items.quote: INR6,200 crores to be precise, which we have achieved so far, and we are well on our target for the financial year.

items.statement: Orient Cement acquisition cash outflow of INR4,000 crores expected in Q4 FY25
items.quote: In terms of the expected outgo for Orient, that is ballpark around INR4,000-odd crores, which will be there.

items.statement: Bhatapara clinker unit and associated grinding units to be commissioned by end of FY25
items.quote: We are on course to commence -- commission our 4-million-ton clinker unit in Bhatapara in Chhattisgarh and associated grinding units of Sankrail, Farakka, both in West Bengal, and Sindri in Jharkhand by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: Salai Banwa grinding unit in UP to be commissioned in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The grinding unit of Salai Banwa in Uttar Pradesh to be commissioned in Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Bathinda and Marwar grinding unit expansions to be commissioned in Q2 FY26
items.quote: And the brownfield expansion of Bathinda grinding unit in Punjab, Marwar grinding unit in Rajasthan to be commissioned in Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: Kalamboli, Dahej, Jodhpur Penna, Krishnapatnam grinding units to be commissioned in Q3 FY26
items.quote: The Kalamboli unit expansion in Maharashtra and Dahej grinding unit expansion in Gujarat, Jodhpur Penna grinding unit, Krishnapatnam grinding unit to be commissioned in Q3 of FY '26.

items.statement: Maratha clinker unit and Warsaliganj grinding unit to be commissioned by end of FY26
items.quote: Further clinker unit of 4 million tons at Maratha in Maharashtra and grinding unit at Warsaliganj in Bihar are also expected to be commissioned by the end of FY '26, enabling us to reach 118 million tons capacity.

items.statement: 14 additional grinding units identified for land acquisition and approvals to reach 140 million tons by FY28
items.quote: We have also identified 14 additional grinding units for which land acquisitions and statutory approvals are under process, which shall enable us to hit 140 million tons by FY '28.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 consolidated EBITDA at INR1,712 crores with 18.4% margin and INR1,038 per ton
items.quote: With improvements mentioned on the cost front, EBITDA stood at INR1,712 crores at a margin of 18.4% and EBITDA per ton of INR1,038.

items.statement: 9M FY25 consolidated EBITDA at INR4,103 crores with 16.3% margin and INR881 per ton
items.quote: The consolidated 9 months Y-o-Y performance, the revenue at INR25,156 crores, operational cost at INR4,520 per ton, EBITDA stood at INR4,103 crores and a margin of 16.3% and EBITDA per ton at INR881.

items.statement: Operational cost at INR4,618 per ton in Q3 FY25 driven by 7% decline in energy cost
items.quote: Operational costs for the quarter is at INR 4,618 per ton. This is driven by a 7% decline in energy cost owing to better fuel management and strong focus on green power.

items.statement: Kiln fuel cost reduced 10% to INR1.66 per 1,000 kcal from INR1.84
items.quote: The kiln fuel costs reduced by 10% to INR1.66 from INR1.84 per 1,000 kilocal.

items.statement: Transportation cost declined 6% to INR1,239 per ton with lead distance reduced 4 km to 285 km
items.quote: The transportation costs declined by 6% at INR1,239 per ton on account of footprint optimization. Overall, lead distance reduced by 4 kilometers to 285 kilometers.

items.statement: Power and fuel cost decreased 7% to INR1,262 per ton in Q3 FY25 from INR1,355 per ton
items.quote: Driven by better fuel management and structural initiatives, our power and fuel costs have decreased 7% to INR1,262 per ton in Q3 FY '25 from INR1,355 per ton in Q3 last year.

items.statement: Green power share in power mix increased to 21.5% from 15.8%
items.quote: The share of green power in power mix has increased to 21.5% from 15.8%.

items.statement: Waste heat recovery capacity at 197 MW, targeting 218 MW by March 2025
items.quote: Our waste heat recovery capacity at the time of takeover was 40 megawatts which we are now targeting to increase to 218 megawatts by March '25. Currently, the WHS capacity is at 197 megawatts.

items.statement: 200 MW solar power project at Khavda, Gujarat commissioned in Q3 FY25
items.quote: 200-megawatt solar power, the project in Gujarat, Khavda, has been commissioned in Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: 1,000 MW renewable energy investment to be completed by June 2026
items.quote: We had earlier announced our investment in 1,000 megawatts RE, which is expected to get commissioned by FY '26. On this account, 200-megawatt solar power at Khavda in Gujarat has been commissioned in Q3.

items.statement: Ordered 11 GPWIS rakes for clinker movement, all delivered and running
items.quote: To further optimize our cost in logistics, we have ordered 11 GPWIS rakes, of which 11 have been delivered and running in approved circuit.

items.statement: Ordered 26 BCFC rakes for fly ash transport, 5 delivered, 4 more expected by March 2025
items.quote: In addition to these, we have also ordered 26 BCFC rakes for safe and cost-efficient transportation of fly ash from thermal power plants to our facilities. Of these 26 BCFC rakes, 5 rakes have been delivered and another 4 are expected to be delivered before March '25.

items.statement: Secured 631 million tons of new limestone reserves in Q3 FY25 via two mine bids
items.quote: To secure our limestone supplies in Q3 FY '25, we have won bids for another 2 mines having reserves of 631 million tons, one in MP and one in Karnataka.

items.statement: Industry demand growth was tepid at 1.5-2% in H1 FY25, expected to rebound to 4-5% in FY25
items.quote: The improved consumption demand in housing and infrastructure segments and increased government spendings are poised to reverse the tepid 1.5% to 2% cement demand growth during H1 of FY '25. This demand is expected to grow by 4% to 5% in FY '25.

items.statement: Ambuja Cements to grow faster than industry
items.quote: Ambuja Cements is well poised to benefit from these trends. The anticipated rebound in demand supported by government initiatives is likely to enhance cement sector performance in the coming quarters. Ambuja Cements will continue to grow at a faster speed than the industry.

items.statement: Blended cements at 82%, premium products share in trade sales volume increased 400 bps to 26%
items.quote: driven by strong focus on micro market management strategy, expansion of dealer network, blended cements at 82%, increase in premium products as a percentage of trade sales volume by 400 bps to 26 percentage.

items.statement: Direct dispatch to customers increased 700 bps to 57%
items.quote: Direct dispatch to customers increased by 700 bps to 57%.

items.statement: Incentive receivables of INR4,500 crores on consolidated basis to be received over 7-9 years
items.quote: Even as we speak, for example, like as an Ambuja consol, we are sitting on a larger incentive bucket of almost INR4,500 crores to be received in due course.

items.statement: Normalized incentive income expected to rise from INR400-500 crores/year to INR600-650 crores/year prospectively
items.quote: Historically, say, it was around, say, INR100-odd crores of incentive per quarter, almost INR400 crores for a year. But this will actually now start moving up to INR600 crores, INR650-odd crores prospectively with new capacities coming in and giving the benefit of incentives.

items.statement: Net worth increased to INR63,000 crores from INR51,000 crores, company remains nil debt with AAA rating
items.quote: I'm glad to share that we have achieved a net worth of almost INR63,000 crores, which was in April INR51,000 crores, so almost up by INR12,000 crores. And we remain nil debt and with the highest rating of AAA.

items.statement: Merger of Penna Cements, Adani Cementation and Sanghi announced, under regulatory approval
items.quote: Already, we have announced one set of transactions to merge some entities, including Penna Cements, Adani Cementation and Sanghi. So, if you see out of all the entities, we've already announced 3 entities, which is currently under regulatory approval stage.

items.statement: Consolidated volume grew 17% YoY in Q3 FY25 to 16.5 million tons
items.quote: Overall, I think our volume has grown by 17%. However, as you know, we also have now volume of Penna and Sanghi in the overall consol volumes. So about 1.4 million tons is coming out of Sanghi and Penna.

items.statement: MSA volumes at 4.5 million tons in Q3 FY25, roughly equal for Ambuja and ACC
items.quote: So, the MSA volumes for this quarter were total about 4.5 million tons overall, more or less equal for both the companies.

items.statement: Penna clinker utilization at 78%, cement utilization sub-40%
items.quote: Penna, I like to mention what my colleague, Vinod, just mentioned, the clinker utilization of Penna is as high as 78% already. However, the cement utilization is sub-40%.

items.statement: Sanghi and Penna costs 10-15% higher than Ambuja, expected to reduce with ramp-up and initiatives
items.quote: So, Sanghi, because it is currently not running in full load. So, I would say it's at least about 10% to 15% higher than Ambuja cost. Penna would be also the same. So, we expect 10% to 15% -- 15% maybe reduction in the cost of both the companies on a per ton basis.

items.statement: India realisations expected flat QoQ in Q4 FY25 unless budget or safeguards provide upside
items.quote: On realisations, we are seeing India realisations QoQ being flat, unless there's something significant in the budget or safeguards which come, then there should be an upside. Otherwise, at minimum, we see it flat.

items.statement: India coking coal cost expected ~$10/t lower in Q4 FY25 vs Q3 FY25
items.quote: In terms of costs, as far as India is concerned, coking coal costs are expected to be about $10 per ton lower in 4Q vs. 3Q.

items.statement: TSUK breakeven targeted by June 2025 (Q1 FY26) assuming current steel prices and continued cost takeout
items.quote: We're certainly focusing on getting it by June 2025. There is a lot of market volatility at this point of time, but we are focusing on internal measures, which essentially include cost takeout.

items.statement: India standalone EBITDA margin ~23% in Q3 FY25; EBITDA/t improved Rs 1,227 QoQ on higher volumes and cost optimisation offsetting realisation drop
items.quote: Tata Steel Standalone revenues for the quarter stood at Rs. 32,760 crores, and EBITDA was Rs. 7,624 crores, which translates to an EBITDA margin of about 23% on reported basis. As provided on slide 30, EBITDA on absolute basis improved by 13% or Rs. 1,227 per ton on QoQ basis

items.statement: India total cost improved ~Rs 2,700/t QoQ (material -Rs 1,300/t, conversion -Rs 1,678/t) vs realisation drop ~Rs 1,500/t
items.quote: Overall, t otal costs have improved by about Rs. 2,700 per ton, helping to more than offset drop in realisation to the tune of about Rs. 1,500 per ton

items.statement: NINL EBITDA margin improved from 13% to 20% QoQ on 17% volume rise and conversion cost reduction ~Rs 3,000/t
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved from 13% in 2Q to 20% in 3Q on account of rise in volumes by about 17% QoQ and as an outcome of cost efficiency through reduction in conversion costs, which reduced by about Rs. 3,000 per ton QoQ.

items.statement: Netherlands spreads at ~€170/t (multi-year low); EBITDA neutral in Q3 vs +£22m in Q2; EBITDA/t down £15 QoQ
items.quote: In Netherlands, raw material to steel price spreads have dipped to multi -year lows with spreads, including energy and carbon cost currently in the region of about €170 per ton. These spreads were last witnessed in 2016. EBITDA for the quarter was n eutral in 3Q compared to +ve £22 million in 2Q. EBITDA per ton declined by about £15 per ton on QoQ basis

items.statement: Net working capital release >Rs 4,000 crore in Q3 FY25; raw material inventory reduced 3-5 days in India and Netherlands
items.quote: In India and Netherlands, raw material inventory has been reduced by about three to five days. All of this has resulted in cashflow release across all geographies and net working capital of more than Rs. 4,000 crore s in this quarter alone

items.statement: Kalinganagar CRM continuous annealing line commissioned Dec 2024; galvanising line (auto grade) coming in next few months; product mix shifting HR→CR→annealed→galvanised
items.quote: The cold rolling mill itself was commissioned, the continuous annealing line has just got commissioned in December and product mix will improve going forward. In the next few months, a galvanising line will also get commissioned, which is auto galvanised, one of the very high-end lines in India.

items.statement: TSUK redundancies ~1,900 since March 2024; more expected in coming quarters as part of fixed cost takeout
items.quote: Total redundancies or people who have left the company since March 2024 was about 1,900 and expect more to leave in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Management expects UCP segment margins to remain in high single digits by end of FY25
items.quote: Generally, we will remain around this high-single digit, our endeavor would be by the end of the year as a Company. And on the segment also, we will try and retain a high single digit in the last quarter as well.

items.statement: Voltbek targets EBITDA breakeven by March 2025
items.quote: We had anticipated that by the end of this year, in the last quarter probably, we will be reaching the EBITDA breakeven, which our endeavor is still there, probably by the month of March, we should be able to hit that number.

items.statement: Chennai AC plant capex of Rs 400 cr spent; additional Rs 400-450 cr earmarked for compressor and capacity ramp-up over 1-1.5 years
items.quote: Besides this, we have also earmarked additional roughly around Rs. 400 crores to Rs. 450 crores which is for compressor manufacturing as well as ramping up our production in Chennai factory from 1 million to take it to 1.5 million and then 2 million.

items.statement: Compressor capex of Rs 250 cr pending technological partnership
items.quote: Compressor capex is about Rs. 250-odd crores, which will take a while. As we are looking for some technological partnership, etc. Unless it is done, we will not be able to commence production of compressors.

items.statement: Chennai AC plant ramping up as planned, gearing for summer season
items.quote: Our newly established air conditioner facility in Chennai continues to ramp up as planned and is gearing up for the season.

items.statement: CR factory teething issues resolving; convertible freezer production started
items.quote: Now, the fast-selling commercial freezer, which are the convertible freezers, etc., which we have started producing, so therefore it has taken a while to start producing in full swing in that factory.

items.statement: UCP segment margin declined to 5.9% in Q3 FY25 from 8% YoY due to ad spend, ISD costs, and CR factory ramp-up costs
items.quote: Firstly, when you are asking why there is pressure on UCP margin. So, we were trying to gain market share, and therefore, we were spending money on ISDs, BTL advertisement, ATL advertisement.

items.statement: Voltbek gross margins improved 300-400 bps; EBITDA breakeven targeted by March 2025
items.quote: And if you look at our gross margins also in this category, we have already increased by almost 300 to 400 basis points in the margin in this category on the gross margin front.

items.statement: No price hike taken in Q3 FY25 despite commodity and forex headwinds; will evaluate pass-through vs value engineering
items.quote: No, we have not taken any price hike in the last quarter, Quarter 3. Because as it is, it's a leaner quarter for especially the air conditioners.

items.statement: Strong summer demand anticipated; consumer financing schemes driving sales growth
items.quote: An anticipated strong summer demand and support from our in-shop demonstrators helped us achieve better performance for all products, with the room air conditioner category experiencing good demand.

items.statement: Voltbek volume growth 59% in Q3 and 56% in 9M FY25; market share gains across categories
items.quote: Business reported a volume growth of 59% in the quarter and 56% in the nine months of the financial year. Steady and robust growth resulted in an improvement in market share across categories.

items.statement: UCP mix in Q3: RAC ~60%, Commercial Refrigeration ~15%, Air Coolers ~5%, Commercial AC balance
items.quote: So, the current quarter, as a part of Segment A: UCP, RAC has been around 60%-odd, commercial refrigeration has been around 15%, air cooler has been around 5%, and commercial air condition has been balance.

items.statement: Elevated commodity prices and steep USD-INR depreciation impacted profitability
items.quote: Elevated commodity prices and a steep depreciation of the USD-INR exchange rate had an impact on profitability.

items.statement: Peak annual depreciation estimated at Rs 70-75 cr post full capitalization of CR and Chennai plants
items.quote: It should be roughly about Rs. 70 crores to Rs. 75 crores for the full year, company wide.

items.statement: PLI benefits for Chennai plant expected from next fiscal year; Pantnagar residual benefits may accrue in Q4 FY25
items.quote: So, I think for Chennai plant, if you are asking in particular, next year onwards, the benefits will start accruing. So, in the next quarter, I do not think anything is coming in from Chennai. But yes, some leftover for Pantnagar, which we have already spent, could get in, in Quarter 4.

items.statement: UCP segment revenue grew 38% YoY to Rs 7,155 cr in 9M FY25; segment PBT up 30% to Rs 548 cr
items.quote: UPBG segment revenue for the nine months' period grew by a remarkable 38%, reaching Rs. 7,155 crores, up from Rs. 5,198 crores in the same period last year. Segment results also saw a significant increase of 30%, amounting to Rs. 548 crores, compared to Rs. 423 crores of PBT in the corresponding nine months of the previous year.

items.statement: Electro-Mechanical Projects segment revenue up 17% YoY to Rs 3,019 cr in 9M FY25; segment PBT Rs 170 cr vs loss of Rs 221 cr last year
items.quote: Over the nine months' period, segment revenue increased by 17%, reaching Rs. 3,019 crores, compared to Rs. 2,585 crores in the same time frame last year. The segment results for the nine months was strong, amounting to Rs. 170 crores, a substantial turnaround from a loss of Rs. 221 crores last year.

items.statement: Consolidated total income up 28% YoY to Rs 10,890 cr in 9M FY25; net profit Rs 599 cr, highest ever 9M profit
items.quote: The Company reported a 28% increase in consolidated total income, reaching Rs. 10,890 crores, up from Rs. 8,477 crores in the same period last year. Profit before tax surged by 172%, hitting Rs. 848 crores compared to Rs. 312 crores previously. Net profit (after tax) also experienced a significant rise at Rs. 599 crores, up from Rs. 137 crores in the corresponding nine months of last year. This ma

items.statement: International projects strategy focused on consolidation in UAE and KSA; selective bidding to avoid past execution hits
items.quote: We are expanding our business or we want to do business in two main geographies, which is UAE and KSA. So, there, we have been executing three, four large projects and some smaller projects, put together 10, 12 projects which we have been carrying out. Therefore, we were prudent in selecting projects in those geographies.

items.statement: Internal restructuring transferring direct investment in overseas subsidiaries to step-down wholly owned subsidiary; economic interest unchanged
items.quote: During the year, as informed earlier, as a part of internal restructuring, the Company's direct investment in existing subsidiaries is being transferred to a step down wholly owned subsidiary of the Company. Post transfer of these investments, the economic interest of the Company in the aforesaid overseas subsidiary companies continues to remain intact.

items.statement: Order book of INR1,636 crores given rig-wise with day rates and contract duration; year-wise breakup provided
items.quote: Thereafter, our order book of INR1,636 crores is given rig-wise with day rates and contract duration.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA run rate achieved in December 2024 quarter should be taken as base for next 4-5 quarters; additional developments will add to earnings
items.quote: But EBITDA -- stand-alone EBITDA run rate, which we have achieved in December '24 quarter should be taken as a base for the next 4, 5 quarters, because all additional developments that will happen will only add further to the earnings of Jindal Drilling.

items.statement: Revenue for Q4 FY25 will be higher than INR239 crores as Jindal Supreme will operate for 90 days vs 75 days in Q3
items.quote: Revenue for Q4 will be higher than INR239 crores, because Jindal Supreme will be working for 90 days.

items.statement: Final stage of acquiring Jindal Pioneer rig; targeting completion within Q4 FY25 (March 2025); purchase price $75 million with no debt on rig
items.quote: We are in the final stage. It is also in our best interest to ensure that this transaction gets concluded within this quarter.

items.statement: Only capex planned is acquisition of Jindal Pioneer; will reassess after transaction concludes
items.quote: The only capex which we are doing is acquisition of Jindal Pioneer, which is expected in this quarter. That is the only acquisition on the cards right now.

items.statement: Jindal Explorer rig contract ends May or September 2025; tender submitted, awaiting outcome; refurbishment takes 4-6 months if de-hired
items.quote: One of the rigs which we are operating, Jindal Explorer, will either get de-hired in May or in September, depending on when the customer decides to de-hire it.

items.statement: Operating margins at 34% in Q3 FY25; expected to normalize at this rate and increase further after Jindal Pioneer acquisition
items.quote: Yes, definitely. And margins will increase further once the acquisition of Jindal Pioneer goes through.

items.statement: Gross debt INR156 crores, cash INR257 crores, net cash INR101 crores as of 31 Dec 2024; net cash position doubled in last 9 months
items.quote: If you refer to Slide 11 of our earnings presentation, gross debt on 31st December '24 is INR156 crores. Cash available with the company is INR257 crores, giving a net cash position of INR101 crores.

items.statement: ONGC press release hiring BP Exploration as technical services provider indicates increased exploration activity and capex; strong tailwind for drilling contractors
items.quote: This is a clear indication that ONGC wants to increase exploration activities. And the fact that they have issued a press release means that further capital expenditure in the oil and gas sector is expected.

items.statement: Day rates for rented rigs are variable; renegotiation occurs when rig rates increase in international market
items.quote: It is variable, because when rig rates increase, then a renegotiation with the rig owner takes place.

items.statement: Natural hedge of 100% on USD payables for rented rigs; foreign exchange gain of ~INR9 crores in Q3 FY25; similar gains expected in Q4 if dollar stays at current levels
items.quote: That is why we have a foreign exchange gain of around INR9 crores in the December quarter. And if the dollar remains at the level where it is right now, we should see similar gains in March quarter.

items.statement: Global jack-up rig day rates up to $180,000 in recent contracts; Indian rates lower but benefit from firm long-term ONGC contracts
items.quote: I see some contracts signed in September, December. They have been in the range of $180,000 kind of day rates.

items.statement: Only risk is securing contracts from ONGC; once awarded, contracts are firm and cannot be cancelled or renegotiated
items.quote: The only risk in this industry is securing a contract from ONGC. There is no other risk which cannot be addressed apart from the ability to secure a contract from ONGC.

items.statement: No diversification into technical exploration services; focused on core rig operations, directional drilling and mud logging; market leadership with 30-35% EBITDA margins
items.quote: We don't want to diversify into sectors which we do not fully understand. Rather, we want to grow in sectors where we are market leaders, thereby playing to our strength.

items.statement: Jindal Pioneer acquisition delayed due to regulatory approval timeline; approval application from April 2024 now infructuous; need customer consent for ownership change
items.quote: When we obtain ed shareholder approval in March of 2024, we wanted to conclude the transaction quickly. Now in order to conclude the transaction quickly, due to the difference in the execution of the transaction and the physical delivery of the rig into India, due to that time gap being longer than is permitted by existing regulations, we have to obtain approval

items.statement: All five rigs deployed in Bombay High; first time in 7-9 years all rigs operational simultaneously in March 2025 quarter
items.quote: That will happen for the first time in March 2025 quarter. First time after a very long duration, maybe 7, 8, 9 years.

items.statement: New rig building not economically viable; $250-300 million capex with 10-15 year payback at $100,000 day rates; barrier to entry protects market position
items.quote: If you're putting in $250 million to $300 million over a period of 3 years and day rates are at $100,000 per day, that is a theoretical figure, then the payback period calculation is more than 10 years.

items.statement: No share buyback program under consideration currently
items.quote: We are not considering any such corporate action right now.

items.statement: Directional drilling and mud logging services are small divisions with good margins but not scalable; entire service universe limited to these
items.quote: In addition to operating jack -up rigs, offshore jack -up Jindal Drilling & Industries Limited 29 January 2025 rigs with ONGC, we also have directional drilling and mud logging services, which are small divisions and give good margin, but it is not possible to scale those businesses up

items.statement: ONGC is primary customer for past 30 years; all five rigs deployed in Bombay High; contracts are firm once awarded
items.quote: We have been su pporting and serving ONGC for past 30 years in their drilling programs. We have always explored opportunities with them. Apart from five offshore jack -up rigs that are currently deployed with ONGC, we also provide mud logging and directional drilling servi ces to the oil and gas

items.statement: Net cash position doubled from INR51 crores to INR101 crores in last 9 months; will improve further as all rigs deployed at higher rates
items.quote: Our net cash position has doubled in last 9 months from INR51 crores to INR101 crores. And going forward, this position will improve as all rigs are deployed at higher rates on new ONGC contracts.

items.statement: General consensus to gradually consolidate rented rigs into Jindal Drilling; acquired two rigs in 2019 and 2021; Pioneer would be third of six rigs
items.quote: There is a general consensus within the company of consolidating rigs gradually into Jindal Drilling. But it has to make economic sense whenever that is undertaken.

items.statement: Refurbishment costs for Jindal Explorer not disclosed; depends on tender criteria and location-specific equipment requirements; takes 4-6 months
items.quote: We are not disclosing that. And it also depends on the tender criteria. Because for different oil wells, the locations are also different. And for those different locations, if new equipment is required, th en it is the responsibility of the contractor to procure that equipment

items.statement: More than 30 rigs operational in India currently; no new rig building started due to unfavorable economics
items.quote: More than 30 rigs, definitely more than 30 rigs. I was not able to take out the latest data. But if you have subscription to Petrodata, then that figure is very easily available.

items.statement: No distressed rig acquisition opportunities in upcycle; opportunities dry up when market is strong
items.quote: We are not getting opportunities to acquire rigs. When the market is in an up cycle, these opportunities dry up.

items.statement: Volume guidance of 1,90,000 tons for FY25 and 12% volume growth for FY26
items.quote: Yes, we should be able to do that. Dhaval Shah: 1,90,000 and 12% volume growth on 1,90,000 base

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 18% maintained; Q3 FY25 at 16.6% seen as bottom
items.quote: Quarter-on-quarter, of course the situation is dynamic, but if you look at a nine month for this particular year, we are still at about 17.7% so, at the 18% EBITDA

items.statement: Management sees Q3 FY25 margin as bottom; expects improvement from One Usha Martin initiatives
items.quote: To be straight to you, I think this is the bottom of the margin. And with the various initiatives of One Usha Martin where we are looking at rationalizing our cost across all our subsidiaries.

items.statement: Wire rope volumes up 18% YoY in India for 9MFY25; Europe facing slowdown in oil & offshore, fishing stable, elevator stable
items.quote: In the domestic market, there is a slowdown in the infrastructure and project execution in India, but with our initiative to work with our dealer network to have a better penetration in the market, we have actually been able to increase our market share in India and increase it almost by 18% year-on-year.

items.statement: Replacement market is 80-85% of demand; slowdown due to equipment idling (e.g., 50 rigs removed in Saudi) not new builds
items.quote: The replacement market is almost 80% to 85% of the demand. It is not 50%-55%, in most products, 80%-85% of the market is replacement.

items.statement: LRPC orders for galvanized/plasticated products in pipeline; expect ramp-up in coming quarters
items.quote: We have got certain orders both from domestic and export markets which we expect to ramp up in the coming quarters depending on the demands of these projects.

items.statement: Zero capex planned for LRPC segment; focus on converting to plasticated/galvanized LRPC
items.quote: No CAPEX at all. Zero CAPEX.

items.statement: Rope capacity utilization 80-85%; wire segment ~50%; LRPC 70-75%
items.quote: For ropes, in Ranchi as well as overall, about 80% to 85% of our capacity would be utilized. In the wires segment, over the years, we have moved out of some low-end wires that we used to manufacture when we had the steel business as well. So, the capacity utilizations for those remains still lower, at around 50% or so. For LRPC, our capacity utilization is about 70%- 75%.

items.statement: European competitors cutting prices to keep plants running; Usha Martin forced to match, pressuring margins
items.quote: If they keep on reducing price, suppose they are supplying at Rs.100 today, and tomorrow we are supplying at Rs. 97, because of the lower demand and their plants still running, they may want to be aggressive in the market, reduce their margin, and keep their plant running. This will also force us to reduce and match prices.

items.statement: Centralizing procurement across geographies to negotiate better terms and standardize input quality
items.quote: Currently, each manufacturing unit is purchasing similar raw materials independently. Consolidating the procurement requirements across the group allows us to negotiate better terms with suppliers across geographies, unlocking cost savings and standardizing input quality globally.

items.statement: Value-added products 71% of wire rope revenue in 9MFY25; elevator sector contributing well
items.quote: Within the wire rope division, value-added products accounted for 71%* of revenue in 9MFY25, with encouraging contributions from the elevator sector.

items.statement: CE certification obtained for ropeway projects; only Indian company with manufacturing capability and CE cert for Parvat Mala
items.quote: As of today, we are the only Company with the manufacturing capability to produce these ropes. To the best of our knowledge, we are also the only Company in India with CE Certification for this.

items.statement: European and Korean competitors aggressive in oil & offshore; Chinese not present in this segment
items.quote: Chinese are not there. South Korean is definitely an important player in this rope industry and there are also the European and the American players, mainly the European manufacturers and the Southeast Asian.

items.statement: Direct shipments from India to replace UK finishing model; will reduce working capital cycle and double freight
items.quote: Now with the direct shipments that have started from India, we will obviously reduce the working capital cycle and also that would help faster deliveries to the customer.

items.statement: Net debt Rs 168 crore as of Dec 2024, 28% of annualized operating EBITDA; manageable despite ongoing capex
items.quote: As at 31st December 2024, our net debt stood at Rs. 168 crore which is 28% of our annualized operating EBITDA. Despite ongoing capital expenditure initiatives including expansions in Ranchi and Thailand and upgrades at the UK facility, our debt level remains well within manageable limits.

items.statement: LRPC regular margin: contribution Rs 4,000-4,500/ton on material margin Rs 12,000-13,000/ton
items.quote: The material margin is close to Rs. 12,000 to 13,000 per ton. And so, the difference between the rod price and the ex-work selling price and our cost of production would be close to Rs. 7,500 per ton which includes the entire direct cost of production. So, the margins are fairly low. If you look at it, the contribution itself is around Rs. 4,000 to 4,500 per ton.

items.statement: Parvat Mala project demand medium to long term; 3-4 years before first rope supply
items.quote: When you initiate such a project, it typically takes three to four years before you even start supplying the first rope. Because that is the last part of the Parvat Mala project.

items.statement: Shifting back-office functions from high-cost subsidiaries to India as part of One Usha Martin
items.quote: Additionally, we are also optimizing our back-office infrastructure by shifting certain support functions from our high-cost subsidiaries locations to India.

items.statement: Brunton Shaw UK model redefined: shifting from wire/strand supply to finished rope supply from India for elevator and fishing; oil & offshore remains in UK
items.quote: For certain product categories, we will now supply finished ropes directly from India, leveraging our enhanced capacities and cost advantages here. However, for some specialized segments such as the large diameter crane ropes used in oil and offshore applications, the UK will remain a critical hub for final production.

items.statement: US FDA EIR received for Tarapur API facility enabling US exports of Ciprofloxacin HCL, Zolpidem Tartrate, Raloxifene HCL, Celecoxib, Niacin
items.quote: We are pleased to announce that Aarti Drugs has recently received approval following a successful inspection by the US FDA plant -- by the US FDA authorities at its API manufacturing facility located at plot number E22, Tarapur Maharashtra.

items.statement: Solar power SPV investment for captive consumption at Gujarat plant; 26.25% equity stake; 8.9 million renewable units per annum; INR 3.6 crore annual savings; operations by end H1 FY26
items.quote: As part of this agreement, Aarti Drugs will acquire at least a 26.25% equity stake in the SPV in compliance with applicable electricity laws. The SPV is formed for developing, constructing, operating and maintaining a solar power plant for captive consumption by the company.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin target 13-14%
items.quote: FY '26, we are aiming for EBITDA margins between 13% and 14%, which highlights our commitment to maintaining financial health and enhancing operational efficiency

items.statement: Revenue target ~INR 4,000 crore consolidated in 3 years (FY27-28)
items.quote: the revenue guidance, what we had given, obviously, we revised it down in last quarter because of the fallen prices to say, roughly around INR 4,000 crores of revenue on a consol basis is still achievable in 3 years' time.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target ~15% in 2 years (FY27) if current conditions persist
items.quote: we should definitely start inching towards 15% EBITDA margins, frankly speaking.

items.statement: Sayakha greenfield specialty chemicals/backward integration plant trial production starting February 2025; operating leverage from subsequent quarter
items.quote: the greenfield project at Sayakha, Gujarat for Specialty Chemicals, which is also related to the backward integration, will commence trial production in this quarter, most probably in the month of February itself.

items.statement: Tarapur greenfield ramp-up to 500+ tons/month by March 2025; total sequential capacity addition 1,600 metric tons/month by end FY26
items.quote: There had been certain teething issues in Tarapur greenfield project, which are sorted now, and we expect to ramp up the production to 500- plus tons per month by end of March '25. In total, we will have a sequential ramp -up of capacity of 1,600 metric tons per month by end of FY '26.

items.statement: 9M FY25 capex INR 136 crore; full year FY25 capex ~INR 200 crore via internal accruals and term loans
items.quote: During 9 months FY '25, the company incurred cap ex of INR136 crores, mainly towards capacity expansion, backward integration and new product launches. We anticipate a total capex of around INR 200 crores for the full year.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 revenue INR 568 crore (-6% YoY); gross profit +7% to INR 207 crore; price decline 2-2.5% YoY in December quarter; prices stable QoQ
items.quote: the company reported a revenue of INR568 crores compared to INR 607 crores, reflecting a slight decline of 6%. This is mainly due to reduced market prices and weaker demand in Formulation segment and Antibiotics API segment.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement expected sequentially as raw material and selling prices stabilize; inventory 90-100 days FIFO accounting
items.quote: now that it has stabilized, I think, the margin -- gross margin should in fact improve on a sequential basis.

items.statement: Volume growth target 15-20% for FY26; 2-3% negative rate variance expected for FY26
items.quote: volume growth, we will definitely try for 15% to 20%, no doubt about that. We'll try to -- with the help of salicylic acid, I hope we'll get to those numbers.

items.statement: US FDA plant potential INR 70-80 crore/year currently; could double with expansion; 30%+ EBITDA margins expected from US FDA facility
items.quote: if we go to the full potential of the plant, we can reach to INR 70 crores to INR 80 crores per annum. But having said that, we had actually, in past, plans to further expand our US FDA block.

items.statement: Meaningful US FDA plant revenue contribution from FY27; European markets first due to prior import alert
items.quote: Probably it will start flowing-in in FY '27.

items.statement: Formulation segment: brownfield expansion added 30% capacity; UK MHRA and US FDA approvals received; new product launches including oncology (dasatinib, lenalidomide, abiraterone) and antidiabetics (DPP-4, SGLT2) over 1.5 years
items.quote: we recently completed a brownfield expansion in the Formulation segment, which has added about 30% additional capacities, for which revenues will start kicking in from Q1. And we have also received the U.K. MHRA and the US FDA approvals for the formulation plant over the last few quarters.

items.statement: Antidiabetic portfolio ~12-13% of standalone API revenue; metformin stable, pioglitazone, teneligliptin, vildagliptin commercial batches
items.quote: antidiabetic on stand -alone basis, I think, it was almost around 12% to 13% now, the antidiabetic segment.

items.statement: Chlorosulfonation line rolled back from 300-400 to 100 tons/month due to quality issues; losses curtailed; margin improvement from March quarter
items.quote: So that is the reason why we have taken a call to roll back that process to the old one where, in fact, last 9 months, we have been suffering losses because of the quality issues for that chlorosulfonation -- the newer chlorosulfonation line, which has been rolled back.

items.statement: ANVISA approval for antifungal product (fluconazole) in Brazil; first-time approval; big market opportunity
items.quote: recently, we were inspected by ANVISA, the Brazilian authority. A few of them were the renewal. So that is okay. But one was related to the antifungal product of ours, which was the first tim e. So that -- it has a big market in Brazil, so that will also help us grow more and more in higher -margin markets.

items.statement: Formulation segment strong order book for next 2 quarters; export-driven growth expected
items.quote: going forward over the next 2 quarters, we have a strong order book. So we will be seeing a good growth, especially in the export segment.

items.statement: Salicylic acid greenfield drag ~1% EBITDA in FY25; process improvements in antibiotics to boost profitability
items.quote: If you talk about EBITDA level, I can say at least a percent of drag it might have created had it been properly utilized.

items.statement: Inventory 90-100 days on FIFO basis; falling raw material and selling prices impacted P&L; stabilization should improve gross margins
items.quote: because we carry an inventory of around 90 to 100 days and we do FIFO basis for accounting, it always impacts our P&L in the falling raw material as well as selling price scenario.

items.statement: EcoVadis score 69 (89th percentile globally); silver medal across all locations; supports marketing in regulated markets
items.quote: our EcoVadis assessment score for current year is 69, 89th percentile globally, and we have fully secured the silver medal for the company as a whole, covering all the locations.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 other expenses higher due to INR 1 crore doubtful debt provision and CPHI fair/Diwali expenses; non-recurring
items.quote: this quarter, we have additionally provided around 1 Cr. of doubtful debts. So there was a slight bump because of that. And certain cost was related to the CPHI fares, which took place in the quarter of December and because of the Diwali expenses.

items.statement: Antibiotic ofloxacin saw higher price decline; metformin prices stable
items.quote: Mainly what we have observed mainly, it is the antibiotic segment, the ofloxacin, where the price decline was more than other products.

items.statement: Formulation facility update capex by end FY25 to broaden market reach and product diversity
items.quote: We are further enhancing our f ormulation capability with the addition of capex by updating facility by the end of this financial year, which will broaden our market reach and product diversity.

items.statement: Targeting 200-250 crore top line in FY26 from toys business at full utilization
items.quote: I think we should be expecting that, and that is what we are targeting.

items.statement: Phase-2 toys expansion planned for H2 FY26 with ~100 crore investment for injection moulded toys plant
items.quote: We anticipate an investment of about Rs. 100 crores for this phase, and we intend to leverage the benefits of the Production Link Incentive Scheme in addition to the newly introduced toy policy.

items.statement: Phase-1 toys capacity expansion completed Dec 2024: 30 tons/day (60-70 lakh value/day) blow/rotational moulding
items.quote: We have completed significant capacity expansion, investing approximately Rs. 46 crores in machinery and tooling, which has allowed us to ramp up our production capacity to up to 30 tons per day.

items.statement: Targeting 4x monthly production by Q4 FY25; expect 100% utilization from April 2025
items.quote: We expect this expansion to help us achieve a 4-fold increase in our monthly production by the final quarter of this financial year.

items.statement: Toys grew 9% QoQ in Q3 FY25; strong partnerships with Amazon, Hamleys, Firstcry, Blinkit; white-label demand from 5-6 major platforms
items.quote: In Q3 of FY'25, the toys business grew by approximately 9% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Automotive down 29% QoQ in Q3 FY25 due to CV market underperformance; 22-24% behind 9-month run-rate vs last year
items.quote: In Quarter 3, the automotive segment experienced a decline of approximately 29% on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Toys EBITDA margin target 22-24% at optimum capacity (blended across toys, preschool furniture, outdoor play)
items.quote: It is about a 22% to 24% blended between toys, preschool furniture, outdoor play equipment. This should be the EBITDA that one should operate on, on optimum capacity.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 revenue Rs 33 crore: auto Rs 24 crore, toys Rs 9 crore; 9M FY25 total Rs 112 crore: auto Rs 77 crore, toys Rs 35 crore
items.quote: So, this quarter we did about 33, out of which about 24 was contributed by auto components, and the remaining was toys.

items.statement: Auto FY25 expected similar or slightly less than FY24's ~135 crore; grows at CV market 4-6% CAGR
items.quote: Last year, I think we did about 135 odd crores and this year, it depends on how the market performs, and then we will close accordingly.

items.statement: Phase-2 to add injection moulded toys (battery-operated cars, role-play toys); currently blow/rotational moulded outdoor toys
items.quote: Under Phase-2 of our expansion plan, looking ahead, we are eager to proceed with Phase-2 of our toys business expansion. This phase will involve the production of injection moulded toys, including battery operated cars and role play toys.

items.statement: White-label partnerships with Amazon, Hamleys, Firstcry, Lifelong Online; Blinkit for OK Play branded quick commerce; target 60-65% branded vs 35-40% white-label long-term
items.quote: We have also started with Lifelong Online. We are also now getting into, we just recently signed up with Blinkit for Quick Commerce.

items.statement: Auto customers: Volvo, Eicher (CV market); no order book visibility, works on replenishment schedules
items.quote: with Lele and Volvo, Eicher being our major customers

items.statement: Budget announced toy cluster scheme with capital subsidies; BIS norms implementation; PLI may be retrospective for past capex
items.quote: The Government has introduced a new scheme for the toy industry, Building on National Action Plan on Toys, details of which will be announced in due course. It is expected to be a fiscal incentive scheme, more intrusive and in form of subsidies on new investments and new employment generation.

items.statement: 20% duty on electronic toy components reduced; benefits Phase-2 battery-operated toy plans
items.quote: This has come up for the battery operated, not the entire product, but just the components and earlier, the duty was higher. Now, it has come down.

items.statement: Air filtration subsidiary MRH signed 10-year exclusive licence with Mann+Hummel for India air purifier manufacturing/distribution
items.quote: We are pleased to announce that it has entered into a 10-year exclusive licensing agreement with Mann + Hummel for the manufacturing and distribution of air purifiers across India.

items.statement: Auto IPO discussed but not demerger; EV business on hold, liquidating inventory
items.quote: No, we are not planning of demerging the auto business. What we were planning was to do an IPO on this separately, but we are still under discussion on that front.

items.statement: May raise more funds via preferential/warrants as opportunities arise; authorized capital largely used
items.quote: See, all of this is very dynamic. It all depends on what opportunities come in. So, yes, we may be raising more funds, but as and when required.

items.statement: Focus on reducing debt; Phase-2 funding depends on balance sheet position at that time
items.quote: I would also like to mention that as of today, we are kind of also stressing on reducing our debt.

items.statement: Indian toy exports up 239% FY23 vs FY15; sector projected $3B by 2028 at 12% CAGR; champion sector status
items.quote: The Indian toy industry as a whole has been experiencing significant growth, with toy exports increasing by 239% in FY'23 compared to FY'15. The sector has also been identified as a champion sector with strong export potential and it is projected to reach 3 billion by 2028, growing at a CAGR of around 12%.

items.statement: Air purifier commercialization timeline uncertain; depends on pilot success and facility setup
items.quote: But we are in the phase of doing various pilots as we speak today. We just completed one in IIT Delhi and the second one in GD Goenka and it all depends. But once when it comes up, the numbers, keeping in mind how big the market is, I mean, it is very difficult to kind of put on what numbers to what extent and at what time it will come.

items.statement: Auto growth tied to CV market cyclicality; no order book visibility
items.quote: In any automotive business, there is not an order book given for the entire upcoming month. There is always a schedule given, and the POs keep coming in, as in when the stock has to be replenished.

items.statement: Own design team and tool-making capability; differentiates from competitors importing used molds
items.quote: We are one of the very few companies in India who has their own design team and our own tool making.

items.statement: Kohler waterless toilet manufacturing partnership uses existing auto moulding capacity; not own product
items.quote: This is a company called Kohler, which you might have heard about. This is an American company, an MNC, which is into sanitary and all. It is their product. It is not our product. We are not selling them. We are manufacturing them.

items.statement: FY25 cement demand growth expected at 4-5% with H2 better than H1
items.quote: This demand is expected to grow by 4% to 5% in FY '25, meaning H2 should be much better than H1, further supported by pro infra and housing budget in the 2025.

items.statement: Target to reach 140 million tons cement capacity by FY28
items.quote: As we plan to expand our cement capacity to 140 million tons by FY '28, we are pacing well to achieve the stated target.

items.statement: Cost reduction target of INR530 per ton to reach INR3,650 per ton by FY28
items.quote: In December 2023, if you remember, we have indicated a cost reduction target of INR530 per ton, wherein we aspire to achieve and reach to INR3,650 per ton by FY '28.

items.statement: Full year FY25 capex target around INR9,000 crores
items.quote: For the full year, it is closer to INR9,000 crores. And so, another INR2,200 crores will go for this quarter.

items.statement: 9 months FY25 capex at INR6,200 crores
items.quote: INR6,200 crores to be precise, which we have achieved so far, and we are well on our target for the financial year.

items.statement: Orient Cement acquisition cash outflow of INR4,000 crores expected in Q4 FY25
items.quote: In terms of the expected outgo for Orient, that is ballpark around INR4,000-odd crores, which will be there.

items.statement: Total capacity to hit 104 million tons by Q4 FY25 with Orient acquisition
items.quote: With Orient acquisition at advanced stage, the total capacity by Q4 FY '25 to hit 104 million tons.

items.statement: 4-million-ton clinker unit at Bhatapara and grinding units at Sankrail, Farakka, Sindri to be commissioned by end of FY25
items.quote: We are on course to commence -- commission our 4-million-ton clinker unit in Bhatapara in Chhattisgarh and associated grinding units of Sankrail, Farakka, both in West Bengal, and Sindri in Jharkhand by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: Salai Banwa grinding unit in UP to be commissioned in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The grinding unit of Salai Banwa in Uttar Pradesh to be commissioned in Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Bathinda and Marwar grinding unit expansions to be commissioned in Q2 FY26
items.quote: And the brownfield expansion of Bathinda grinding unit in Punjab, Marwar grinding unit in Rajasthan to be commissioned in Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: Kalamboli, Dahej, Jodhpur Penna, Krishnapatnam grinding units to be commissioned in Q3 FY26
items.quote: The Kalamboli unit expansion in Maharashtra and Dahej grinding unit expansion in Gujarat, Jodhpur Penna grinding unit, Krishnapatnam grinding unit to be commissioned in Q3 of FY '26.

items.statement: 4-million-ton clinker unit at Maratha and Warsaliganj grinding unit to be commissioned by end of FY26 enabling 118 million tons capacity
items.quote: Further clinker unit of 4 million tons at Maratha in Maharashtra and grinding unit at Warsaliganj in Bihar are also expected to be commissioned by the end of FY '26, enabling us to reach 118 million tons capacity.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 consolidated EBITDA at INR1,712 crores with 18.4% margin and INR1,038 per ton
items.quote: With improvements mentioned on the cost front, EBITDA stood at INR1,712 crores at a margin of 18.4% and EBITDA per ton of INR1,038.

items.statement: 9 months FY25 consolidated EBITDA at INR4,103 crores with 16.3% margin and INR881 per ton
items.quote: The consolidated 9 months Y-o-Y performance, the revenue at INR25,156 crores, operational cost at INR4,520 per ton, EBITDA stood at INR4,103 crores and a margin of 16.3% and EBITDA per ton at INR881.

items.statement: Operational cost at INR4,618 per ton in Q3 FY25 driven by 7% decline in energy cost
items.quote: Operational costs for the quarter is at INR 4,618 per ton. This is driven by a 7% decline in energy cost owing to better fuel management and strong focus on green power.

items.statement: Kiln fuel cost reduced 10% to INR1.66 per 1,000 kilocal from INR1.84
items.quote: The kiln fuel costs reduced by 10% to INR1.66 from INR1.84 per 1,000 kilocal.

items.statement: Transportation cost declined 6% to INR1,239 per ton; lead distance reduced 4 km to 285 km
items.quote: The transportation costs declined by 6% at INR1,239 per ton on account of footprint optimization. Overall, lead distance reduced by 4 kilometers to 285 kilometers.

items.statement: Power and fuel cost decreased 7% to INR1,262 per ton in Q3 FY25 from INR1,355 per ton in Q3 FY24
items.quote: Driven by better fuel management and structural initiatives, our power and fuel costs have decreased 7% to INR1,262 per ton in Q3 FY '25 from INR1,355 per ton in Q3 last year.

items.statement: Share of green power in power mix increased to 21.5% from 15.8%
items.quote: The share of green power in power mix has increased to 21.5% from 15.8%.

items.statement: Waste heat recovery capacity at 197 MW, targeting 218 MW by March 2025
items.quote: Our waste heat recovery capacity at the time of takeover was 40 megawatts which we are now targeting to increase to 218 megawatts by March '25. Currently, the WHS capacity is at 197 megawatts.

items.statement: 200 MW solar power project at Khavda, Gujarat commissioned in Q3 FY25
items.quote: 200-megawatt solar power, the project in Gujarat, Khavda, has been commissioned in Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: 1,000 MW renewable energy investment to be completed by June 2026
items.quote: We had earlier announced our investment in 1,000 megawatts RE, which is expected to get commissioned by FY '26. On this account, 200-megawatt solar power at Khavda in Gujarat has been commissioned in Q3.

items.statement: Ordered 11 GPWIS rakes for clinker movement, all delivered and running
items.quote: To further optimize our cost in logistics, we have ordered 11 GPWIS rakes, of which 11 have been delivered and running in approved circuit.

items.statement: Ordered 26 BCFC rakes for fly ash transport, 5 delivered, 4 more expected by March 2025
items.quote: In addition to these, we have also ordered 26 BCFC rakes for safe and cost-efficient transportation of fly ash from thermal power plants to our facilities. Of these 26 BCFC rakes, 5 rakes have been delivered and another 4 are expected to be delivered before March '25.

items.statement: Secured 631 million tons of new limestone reserves in Q3 FY25 via two mine wins in MP and Karnataka
items.quote: To secure our limestone supplies in Q3 FY '25, we have won bids for another 2 mines having reserves of 631 million tons, one in MP and one in Karnataka.

items.statement: Industry demand growth was tepid at 1.5-2% in H1 FY25, expected to grow 4-5% in FY25
items.quote: The improved consumption demand in housing and infrastructure segments and increased government spendings are poised to reverse the tepid 1.5% to 2% cement demand growth during H1 of FY '25. This demand is expected to grow by 4% to 5% in FY '25.

items.statement: Blended cements at 82%; premium products as percentage of trade sales volume increased by 400 bps to 26%
items.quote: blended cements at 82%, increase in premium products as a percentage of trade sales volume by 400 bps to 26 percentage.

items.statement: Direct dispatch to customers increased by 700 bps to 57%
items.quote: Direct dispatch to customers increased by 700 bps to 57%.

items.statement: Net worth at INR63,000 crores, up INR12,000 crores from April; nil debt with AAA rating
items.quote: I'm glad to share that we have achieved a net worth of almost INR63,000 crores, which was in April INR51,000 crores, so almost up by INR12,000 crores. And we remain nil debt and with the highest rating of AAA.

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents at INR8,755 crores as on December 31
items.quote: As on December 31, the consolidated cash and cash equivalents stood at healthy INR8,755 crores.

items.statement: Merger of Penna Cements, Adani Cementation and Sanghi announced, under regulatory approval
items.quote: Already, we have announced one set of transactions to merge some entities, including Penna Cements, Adani Cementation and Sanghi. So, if you see out of all the entities, we've already announced 3 entities, which is currently under regulatory approval stage.

items.statement: MSA volumes for Q3 FY25 at 4.5 million tons total, roughly equal for Ambuja and ACC
items.quote: So, the MSA volumes for this quarter were total about 4.5 million tons overall, more or less equal for both the companies.

items.statement: Sanghi volume 0.5 million tons, Penna volume 0.9 million tons in Q3 FY25
items.quote: 0.4 million would be Sanghi and I think -- 0.5 million is Sanghi and 0.9 million is Penna.

items.statement: Sanghi cement utilization at 37% in Q3 FY25 vs 22% YoY and 23% QoQ; targeting 80-85% by March end
items.quote: The 37% is the Sanghi cement utilization for this quarter, which was 22% same quarter last year. And in the sequential previous quarter, it was 23%.

items.statement: Penna clinker utilization at 78%, cement utilization sub-40%
items.quote: Penna, I like to mention what my colleague, Vinod, just mentioned, the clinker utilization of Penna is as high as 78% already. However, the cement utilization is sub-40%.

items.statement: Lease expiries in 2030 for some plants; engaging with government through NITI Aayog for respite
items.quote: Second part regarding 2030, yes, there are a few plants for us, which will have some residual limestone. They would be, in Maharashtra one plant, in Madhya Pradesh one plant, and I think mostly in Chhattisgarh one plant and in Himachal one plant. We are making a lot of initiatives, speaking with the government. IIndustry is also working through various forums, NITI Aayog, etcetera.

items.statement: Expect 12% revenue growth for FY25 and early teen revenue growth from FY26 onwards with operating leverage
items.value: 12% for FY25, early teens for FY26+
items.quote: Factoring in these challenges for FY25, we now expect 12% revenue growth while maintaining operating leverage. From FY26 onwards, we aim for an early teen revenue growth along with operating leverage.

items.statement: Expect gross margin around 62% in medium term
items.quote: From the gross margin point of view, we expect the gross margin to be in the region of around 62% in the medium term.

items.statement: US revenue grew 3.6% YoY boosted by strong festive season and improving consumer confidence
items.quote: In the US, revenue grew by 3.6% Y oY, boosted by strong festive season and improving consumer confidence

items.statement: UK revenue grew 6.5% YoY with Ideal World making significant contribution
items.quote: In the UK, the revenue was up 6.5% with Ideal World making a significant contribution.

items.statement: Germany revenue grew 30.7% YoY and achieved EBITDA breakeven in Q3
items.quote: Germany continued its robust performance, posting a 30.7% Yo Y revenue growth. With operations achieving breakeven this quarter, we are confident about maintaining this momentum in Q4 as

items.statement: Gross margin 61.3% in Q3, down 110 bps YoY due to high-end jewelry demand surge and product mix
items.quote: Owing to a surge in demand of high-end jewelry, gross margin came in at 61.3%, which is 110 basis points lower YoY.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 11.5% in Q3, up 40 bps YoY driven by Germany breakeven, Ideal World profitability, operating leverage and cost optimization
items.quote: The EBITDA margin improved to 11.5% this quarter, which is 40 basis points higher than last year. Low gross margins were offset by savings in shipping costs, operating leverage, Germany reaching breakeven levels, and our ongoing cost optimization drive.

items.statement: Germany and Ideal World together consumed ~2.5% of group EBITDA margin in 9M FY25

In October, JEM strengthened its leadership in electric mobility by acquiring Log9 Technology and business assets for the railway and electric truck battery division.

items.statement: Previous Rs 800 crore QIP for wheel project on track; advances released to EPC contractor per schedule
items.quote: The fundraise was specifically for our wheel project and the project is going on track. I think the deadline, so we have released, out of that we have released the advance out of which we had to release to the EPC contractor. And as per the remaining schedule, as and when the funds are going to be required in the project, it will be utilized.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin expanded to 14.4% from 13.9% YoY; PAT margin 9.2%
items.quote: EBITDA grew by 19.5% year -on-year to Rs. 148 crore with an EBITDA margin expansion to 14.4% from 13.9% in Q3 FY24. PAT increased 18.4% year -on-year to approximately Rs. 97 crore with a PAT margin of 9.2%

items.statement: Jupiter Tatravagonka reporting >12% EBITDA margin; expect margin improvement after Orissa backward integration
items.quote: Yes, we are reporting EBITDA of over 12%. And I think next year we are looking to double this revenue and once the Orissa project for the backward integration kicks in, then as I have already mentioned that this would be a more than Rs. 2,000 crore opportunity for us with substantial exports to the European market.

items.statement: Expect Union Budget 2025-26 to drive transformative leap for Indian Railways with capex >Rs 3 lakh crore (15-20% increase)
items.quote: The outlook for the sector remains bright, particularly with expectations that the 2025 -2026 Union budget will drive a transformative leap for Indian railways. Capital expenditure expected to surpass Rs. 3 lakh crore, making a significant 15 %-20% increase over the current fiscal.

items.statement: No significant exposure to US tariffs; sales mainly domestic and European
items.quote: Yes, see as we don't have much exposure to the North American market , lot of our sales is domestic and otherwise also exposure is mainly to the European market . So, we don't see any kind of challenges in the European market with regard to any action with Mr. Trump takes.

items.statement: EV launch delayed 1.5 months due to battery technology upgrade; challenges ironed out; dealer network expanded to 8-10 cities
items.quote: I think more than the timelines, I think we wanted the launch to be around from Jan to Feb because there was a certain change in the battery technology, and we wanted to launch the vehicle with the upgraded battery technology rather than with the earlier battery technology. So, that is what caused this delay of a month and a half. Otherwise, I think we were on track.

items.statement: Interim milestone 333: $3bn order book, ~$2.2bn turnover, 3% PAT in ~2 years (FY27)
items.quote: in about 2 years from now, we should have an order book in hand of about $3 billion. And at that level, we should do a turnov er of close to US$2.2 billion and generate 3% PAT of the company

items.statement: Full-year FY25 PAT expected ~2%; normalized 9M PAT margin 3.4%
items.quote: Currently we're at about 1.5%. If I just talk about the full year, we should be closer to 2% or so approximately and then we have to add that 1% extra post our investment, so nothing to be excluded.

items.statement: New vertical investment to halve in FY26 vs FY25 (INR70-80cr vs INR130-140cr)
items.quote: we are looking at investing half of what we have done this year. So, this should actually come down to about 50% to 60% of what we have done this year.

items.statement: Overall order book $425mn, up 16% YoY; design-led sourcing order book up 25% YoY
items.quote: currently we have an order book of about 425 million on an overall order book basis, while the order book has a growth of 16% overall. But what is important is that in design-led sourcing, which is our main business contributing to more than 87% of revenue, the growth is actually 25% over the same period last year.

items.statement: 9M revenue INR9,052cr, +26% YoY; Q3 GMV +16% YoY
items.quote: PDS has sustained it's growth momentum, delivering a 26% year-on-year increase in the revenue for the 9 months period ended December '24, and reaching a revenue of INR9,052 crores.

items.statement: BCG cost transformation targets 1-2% savings on 50-55% of cost base; high side 3-4%
items.quote: we beli eve from the scale that we have built up, there is potential to get synergies on a high side of 3% to 4%, but surely about 1% to 2% savings from this cost base are surely achievable

items.statement: Normalized PAT margins: Q3 2.6%, 9M 3.4%; reported PAT Q3 INR43cr (+66% YoY), 9M INR167cr (+22% YoY)
items.quote: Our normalized PAT after adjusting for new businesses, stood at INR78 crores for Q3 FY '25 and INR289 crores for the 9-month period, with margins of 2.6% and 3.4%, respectively.

And as part of this transaction, Knit Gallery's existing business currently happening in a different entity will be transferred to the entity that we are acquiring and there will be a business consideration of INR34 crores payable over 3

items.statement: Knit Gallery: 14 manufacturing units, 40mn pieces/yr capacity, all rented premises
items.quote: Knit Gallery operates close to 14 manufacturing units along with warehouses and worker hostels, and has a production capacity of 40 million pieces per year catering to customers in Germany, U.S. and U.K.

items.statement: Key US retailer engagements: Kohl's, Children's Place, Walmart, Target, Fashion Nova, Catalyst Brands (JCPenney, Aeropostale, Brooks Brothers, Eddie Bauer, Forever 21)

Children's Place , another large American retailer is starting to engage with us and Walmart, Target, Fashion Nova, those conversations are quite strategic and moving in the right direction And the biggest retaile r that we have just started conversation is Cata

items.quote: we expect that in this current quarter, we should reduce or contract our balance sheet close to about INR160 crores to INR175 crores and the corresponding impact on working capital as well.

items.statement: Net debt/equity 0.21, net debt/EBITDA 0.82 (ex-new businesses); Knit Gallery adds INR96cr debt (85% working capital)
items.quote: Excluding our new business investments, we clocked a return on capital employed of 25% and net debt to equity of 0.21 and a net debt-to-EBITDA of 0.82.

items.statement: Ted Baker revenue INR355cr (9M), flat YoY; wholesale offset agency loss

And in sourcing as a service in the 9 months period we did approximately 13 million into 87 approximately INR113 crores, we clocked in. So, Ted Baker was flat if I talk about the same period of 9 months last year.

items.statement: Knit Gallery acquisition: 55% stake, INR288cr revenue, INR36cr EBITDA (FY24), 13% EBITDA margin, 6% PAT margin; close by May 2025
items.quote: The combined business generated INR288 crores in revenue in FY '24 with an EBITDA of INR36 crores, and the transaction is expected to close by May 2025.

items.statement: General merchandise and home categories investments firing; manufacturing segment +42% YoY to INR532cr (9M), EBIT 5.6%
items.quote: Our Manufacturing segment achieved a 42% year-over-year growth, generating INR532 crores in revenue. The segment reported an EBIT of 5.6% for the 9 months.

items.statement: Geopolitical shifts (China+1, Bangladesh disruption) driving customer diversification to India; PDS adding India manufacturing base
items.quote: whether it's China plus 1 or disruption in any other part of the world, we believe a very well-diversified manufacturing base and sourcing base should augur very well in terms of our offering to the customer.

items.statement: Centralizing risk, cash, procurement, design, IT, legal, HR; entrepreneurs run front-end; best-practice sharing every 2 months
items.quote: So all the common functions, which are back office or company running functions are run centrally, which is what Sanjay is running, I'm running along with them for growth initiatives, and then the entrepreneurs who are running the businesses, they focus on the client needs, they focus on sales, order execution.

items.statement: No scaled competitor; next largest ~1/3 PDS size; unique platform attracting top talent via equity ownership
items.quote: there is no other scale -up platform that is able to work with these changes and dynamics in the industry to give the services to either the retailers or the brands or the New York IP companies, the way the industry has evolved. There's no scale company, I mean the other biggest competitor we have is now one third our size

items.statement: Make in India alignment; India manufacturing base strategic for customer diversification
items.quote: This acquisition is a significant milestone for PDS reinforcing India's role as a strategic manufacturing and sourcing hub. It strengthens our expertise in apparel manufacturing in the region, aligns with the Make in India initiative.

items.statement: Sourcing gross margin blip -40bps due to Ted Baker agency loss
items.quote: We witnessed a blip of around 40 bps in sourcing gross margins, which were mainly attributable to loss of Ted Baker agency business.

items.statement: Management expects around 10% volume growth in FY26 and EBITDA per SCM in the INR9-12 range
items.quote: Now maybe next year, we will not be able to have that much number, but we are comfortable that around 10% numbers we will be able to clock next financial year also and which will be definitely -- CNG will be a main contributor in that growth along with industrial and commercial segment.

items.statement: Management expects consolidated volume growth of 13-13.5% in FY25 and double-digit growth in FY26
items.quote: So in the year-end we expect it to be around 13% or 13.5%. Next year also we definitely should be in -- at least in the double digit, yes.

items.statement: EBITDA per SCM for 9M FY25 is INR10.3; management expects INR9-12 range going forward

So it is not very off the mark of the guidance which we have given about INR10 to INR12. So we expect similar range to continue and depending on the price of LNG, Henry Hub and other contracts. We may be very comfortable in this range, INR9 to INR11 or INR10 to INR12 rang

Out of these, major will be on steel and low-pressure pipelines. And roughly INR200 crores or plus, minus 10% on CNG. And balance is on steel grid and LMC, last mile connectivity.

items.quote: We also added 9 CNG stations during this quarter. And with this, we have 361 stations as on 31st December, '24. We also have added 83 industries and commercial customers during this quarter. And as on 31st December we have 4,974 industrial and commercial customers.

items.quote: However, part of the APM allocation has been reinstated with effect from 16 January '25. Thus currently, MGL is having 100% APM allocation for its domestic gas and approximately 50% allocation for its CNG sales volume.

items.statement: Landed cost: Henry Hub gas $9.5-10.5/MMBtu; HPHT ~$11/MMBtu (incl. transport); Brent contract ~$7.5/MMBtu (incl. transport); pipeline tariff Zone 1 INR40/MMBtu, Zone 2 INR80/MMBtu, Zone 3 INR108/MMBtu
items.quote: As of now, considering the indices, with respect to Henry Hub, it ranges between $9.5 to around $10.5. HPHT is around -- that is I think available in the public domain, including transportation, it should go around $11, which has $1 per MMBTU transportation and around $10.25 or so as a basic rate.

items.statement: Bombay High Court directed Maharashtra govt to form committee to study phasing out diesel/petrol vehicles in Mumbai/MMR; committee formed 22 Jan 2025 with 3-month deadline; MGL MD included as member
items.quote: They have flagged serious concerns over worrisome pollution levels in the city of Mumbai and MMR region, directing the state government to form a committee to study feasibility of phasing out diesel and petrol driven vehicles from the roads of Mumbai and permit only, motor vehicles which run on CNG and electric charge to reduce pollution to the vehicles.

items.statement: Court also directed bakeries to convert from wood/coal to gas/green fuel within 1 year; management says volume impact from bakeries will be small
items.quote: Mumbai high Court also directed to BMC that the city bakery units should not use the polluting fuel like wood or coal. And they have directed bakery to convert to use a gas or other green fuel in the next 1 year.

items.statement: Scheme of amalgamation of UEPL (wholly owned subsidiary) with MGL approved by Board Oct 2024, submitted to NCLT Mumbai 6 Dec 2024; interim order reserved 17 Jan 2025
items.quote: A scheme of amalgamation or merger of UEPL with MGL was approved by the Board in October '24 last year and the scheme was submitted to NCLT Mumbai on 6 December, 2024. And the matter was heard by the Mumbai bench on January 17, 2025 and they've reserved the pronouncement of its interim order.

items.statement: UEPL merger to provide tax synergies: accumulated losses and depreciation ~INR35 crore; MGL can absorb immediately vs 3-4 years for UEPL standalone
items.quote: In the books of UEPL, currently there are tax losses and accumulated depreciation around INR35 crores, both put together that we will be able to absorb. Also, the capex which we are incurring today, INR150 crores odd and they are not able to absorb that depreciation. On a merged entity basis, we will b e able to absorb that early

items.statement: Board approved interim dividend of 120% (INR12 per equity share) for FY25
items.quote: I'm happy to announce that Board has approved an interim dividend at the rate of 120% that is INR12 per equity share for the current financial year.

MGL as a consolidated entity has achieved total gas sales volume for 9 months ending December 31, 2024 is 4.181 MMSCMD.

items.statement: CNG volume: 2.919 MMSCMD in Q3 FY25 (up 1.16% QoQ, 11.44% YoY in 9M); Industrial/Commercial: 0.646 MMSCMD (up 2.86% QoQ, 25.52% YoY in 9M); Domestic PNG: 0.551 MMSCMD (up 4.32% QoQ, 7.23% YoY in 9M)

Sales for the domestic PNG is 0.551 as compared to the last quarter of 0.528 MMSCMD which is an increase of 4.32%.
