That makes total sale of around 4 million for this 9-month average, okay? If you look at the growth in GA-3, last year average was around 0.163 and we are today at 0.245 which is a growth of almost 49%, 50% over the last year average.

items.statement: 3-wheelers consume 34% of CNG volumes; state transport undertakings (BEST, MSRTC, NMMT, TMT) consume 6%; 98% of 3-wheelers are CNG; BEST has ~2,000 CNG buses, ~1,000 diesel/EV buses
items.quote: So if I have to tell you the customer segment, so Autorickshaw, the 3-wheelers, which you asked, they are the highest consuming segment. They consume about 34% of the total volumes that we sell. BEST and others put together, I will call it, the state trans port undertakings, which also includes MSRTC, NMMT, and TMT. They are consuming about only 6% of the total volumes that we sell

items.statement: UEPL Q3 FY25: Revenue INR102 crore, PAT INR1.27 crore; 9M FY25: Revenue INR275 crore, PAT INR17.51 crore; cash EBITDA ~INR50-55 crore per annum; interest cost is intra-group (MGL loan)
items.quote: Yes. So the revenue that was generated during Q3 was INR102 crores for UEPL with net profit of about INR1.27 crores and cumulative for the 9 months ended UEPL earned INR275 crores. And the net profit after tax generated is INR17.51 crores.

items.statement: UEPL interest cost is on MGL's loan accounted in UEPL books; no separate external debt mentioned for UEPL
items.quote: Compared to MGL, there are two components. O ne is depreciation, you're right. Another is interest cost is also there in UEPL. So if you take cash EBITDA, it is generating around INR50 crores, INR55 crores cash EBITDA per annum as of now. And this interest is also within the group, it is MGL's loan which is getting accounted as a finance cost in the books of UEPL

items.statement: Management sees EV threat as manageable: CNG cheaper than EV in buses; 90% of commercial vehicles (3.5-18 ton) still on diesel; 3-wheeler EV shift can be offset by commercial vehicle conversion
items.quote: So that means 90% vehicles are still to be captured by CNG, which is currently running mostly on diesel. So that segment more than compensate for whatever small segment is lost to EVs. Like if 3 -wheelers goes to EV, we can more than compensate it to the co mmercial vehicles, which can come on CNG as compared to diesel

items.quote: The Phase 1, which I cal l it as a pre -Diwali festive season, and this was October, which saw robust performance across categories, which was driven by strong demand during the festive period, both across online and off-line channels. Phase 2 which was immediately after Diwali, and there was a slowdown. From November until mid-December, we witnessed a noticeable softening in consumer spending acr

items.statement: Expect good summer season with early onset in North and East
items.quote: Right now, we are all expecting and our complete belief is that the summer will be a good one. The entire focus in the organization is to make sure that we are ready for the season with the new products, new launches as well as the right inventory levels across the country.

items.statement: Premium lighting products now 50% of mix, up 400 bps YoY
items.quote: These now contribute almost 50%, which is an improvement of almost 400 basis points on a year-on-year basis, and the traditional lamps do the balance.

items.statement: BLDC and IoT fans 20% of ceiling fan category YTD, growing ~25%
items.quote: At a full year YTD basis, now BLDC and IoT contribute almost 20% of the overall ceiling fans category and growing at almost about 25%.

items.statement: Premium Deco fans ~30-31%, target 45%
items.quote: Our premium in Deco category is approximately 30%, 31% now, and our ambition is to take it to closer to 45%.

items.statement: New product launches contributed 19% of fan revenue in Q3
items.quote: Our new product launches have contributed 19% of our revenues in fans and our new BLDC fans have received good consumer and trade response.

items.statement: Extended direct-to-market to rest of Bengal, now 11 DTM states
items.quote: In this quarter, we extended our direct-to-market presence in rest of Bengal, bringing the total count of direct-to-market states to 11.

items.statement: Gaining market share in both Lighting and Fans categories
items.quote: Overall, we've gained market share in both Lighting as well as Fans category. We've also made strong strides in emerging channels such as e-com.

items.statement: Hyderabad plant operations stabilized, ready for season demand
items.quote: With our Hyderabad plant operations now stabilized, we are ready for season demand. We expect further gains from operating leverage in the quarters ahead.

items.statement: EPR cost impact factored in Q4 FY24, partially absorbed and partially passed through
items.quote: EPR has been factored in. Some bit of it is absorbed as cost, some bit of is passed. We've always maintained that whatever we need to pass to the consumers, we will not shy away from it.

items.statement: Lighting price erosion in commoditized bulbs/battens, value-add and B2B less affected
items.quote: The one part, which we basically com moditized bulbs and battens, those are the ones which are under price erosion. And there is some bit of price erosion which is happening even on the value-add side, but if you play the mix well, you will be able to handle the headwinds

items.statement: Working capital at 16 days, consistently improving
items.quote: Many congratulations for the working capital. So it has been consistently coming off. So 16 days is a fairly good number to it.

items.statement: New CFO Arvind Vats joined, new BU head for Switchgears & Wires Tapas Roy Chowdhury joined
items.quote: As you know, Mr. Saibal Sengupta, our CFO had superannuated and Arvind Vats has joined us as a new CFO. We've also added a dedicated BU head position for Switchgears and Wires to support and expedite our growth in opportunity categories. Mr. Tapas Roy Chow dhury has joined us as a BU head for Switchgears and Wires

items.statement: Leadership hiring largely done, couple of positions remain
items.quote: We are more or less, there are a couple of positions, which are still there. But largely from an overall structure perspective, we have a leadership team, which is there and there are a couple of positions if we need to look at it.

items.statement: Revenue INR 817 cr in Q3, up 8.6% YoY and 24% QoQ, highest quarterly revenue
items.quote: Our top line stood at INR817 crores, 8.6% year-on-year growth and a sequential quarter-on-quarter growth of almost 24%. Incidentally, this is our highest quarterly revenue

items.statement: 9M revenue INR 2,232 cr, up 10.2% YoY
items.quote: Revenue for the 9-month period reached INR2,232 crores, marking a 10.2% year-on-year increase and improving on the last year YTD growth of 8.2%.

items.statement: Lighting & Switchgear revenue up ~12% YoY in Q3
items.quote: Our rapidly growing Lighting and Switchgear segments continue to perform strongly for us, with the year-on-year growth of almost 12%.

items.statement: ECD segment revenue up 7.3% YoY, 30% QoQ in Q3
items.quote: In the ECD segment, we've achieved 7.3% year-on-year revenue growth and a sequential growth of 30% on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: BLDC IoT fan revenue grew 60% YoY in Q3
items.quote: Our BLDC new launches have helped us grow 60%, by 60% in BLDC in IoT category in the ceiling fan category in Q3.

items.statement: Spark Sanchay cost savings INR 52 cr YTD, 13% improvement YoY
items.quote: On the operational front, cost optimization initiatives under Spark Sanchay are delivering results. The program has delivered INR52 crores of savings on a YTD basis, which is a 13% improvement year-on-year.

items.statement: Lighting B2C commoditized segment facing price erosion from new entrants and existing players
items.quote: In the gest to get market share, I hope some of the new entrants as well as some of the existing players do not keep discounting as we move forward.

items.statement: Guides 20-25% AuM growth long-term; expects January growth at 15-20% trajectory
items.quote: We continue to guide on a 20 – 25% of an AuM growth on a long-term basis. I think the traction which we got in the Q3 and the numbers in Jan really give us confidence on delivering the guided AuM growth of ~20. And as we speak, we are expecting January to be at around 15 - 20% on the growth trajectory.

items.statement: Targets opex-to-assets ratio below 3% with ~20 bps annual reduction
items.quote: At the beginning of the financial year we have guided that we will bring down opex to assets ratio by ~20 bps every year to reach below 3%.

items.statement: Guides credit cost below 25 bps on sustainable basis
items.quote: We continue to guide credit cost of below 25 bps on sustainable basis.

items.statement: Aspires to reach Rs 500 bn AuM in next 4-5 years and become Pan-India player
items.quote: We aspire to reach a milestone of Rs. 500 bn in assets under management in the next 4 to 5 years and broaden our horizons as a Pan-India player and continue our cost optimization strategy.

items.statement: Sees demand uptick post-elections driven by PMAY 2.0 affordable supply and self-construction
items.quote: Demand has to see an uptick and specifically in certain segments and verticals as I speak of the PMAY -led affordable supply, which is there.

items.statement: Incremental business yield up 25+ bps across products; disbursement yield improving QoQ
items.quote: Our focus continues to underwrite quality business with risk adjusted return as a result our incremental business yield has gone up by 25 bps+ across products.

items.statement: AuM grew 20% YoY to Rs 192 bn; disbursements Rs 16 bn in Q3 (17% YoY, 23% QoQ)
items.quote: We have delivered AuM growth of 20% Y-o-Y, reaching AuM of Rs 192 bn. In Q3FY25, we disbursed loans worth around Rs 16 bn a growth of 17% Y -o-Y with cumulative disbursement of Rs 41 bn for 9MFY25.

items.statement: Opened 6 branches in 9M FY25; opening 20+ branches in Q4 FY25 mainly in Karnataka and UP
items.quote: We have opened 6 new branches during 9MFY25 and opening another 20+ branches in this quarter predominantly in the states of Karnataka and UP.

items.statement: BPLR hiked 25 bps in October; 30% book fixed, rest floating; cost of borrowings up 9 bps QoQ to 8.24%
items.quote: Our spread improved by 5 bps to 4.94% driven by a 14 -bps expansion in the AUM yield to 13.18% on account of 25 bps increased in BPLR in Q3FY25; whereas our cost of borrowings increased by 9 bps Q-o-Q to 8.24%.

items.statement: ~60% AuM below Rs 15 lakh ticket; ~80% below Rs 25 lakh; yield 200 bps higher on <Rs 15 lakh
items.quote: Renish ~80% of book is less than Rs. 25 lakhs where we focus on less than 15 lakhs, and we have ~60%, book at less than ₹15 lakhs , this is on amount basis. And the volume we have already given in our presentation where 85% book is a less than Rs. 15 lakhs.

items.statement: Targeting 45% share of <Rs 10 lakh tickets (currently 30-35%) for better risk-adjusted yield
items.quote: Our aim presently is to get to the 45%. Currently, we are hovering between 30% to 35% of the loans which are less than Rs. 10 lakhs in ticket size.

items.statement: BT-out rate at ~5.4%, best-in-class; aided by AI predictive models
items.quote: We are happy to note that BT-out % is at ~5.4%. So, I think this is one of the best in class when it compares to the industry peers. Couple of factors really go into this one is aided by our predictive models which are able to predict what is the probability and chance of the BT out.

items.statement: Karnataka E-Khata challenges easing; affordable supply from ULBs supports growth
items.quote: I think what you reflected is E -khata as we see and as we speak, I think we are minimal at this period of time what Karnataka is. But going forward as we talk to the people across, I think that easing out of E -Khatas are moving across. It has started now really getting stabilised.

items.statement: PMAY 2.0 scheme ensures last-mile impact; expects higher budgetary allocation in Union Budget
items.quote: The new PMAY 2 .0 scheme ensures impact till last mile in more efficient way and benefit our customers immensely. We expect more budgetary allocation and supply of Affordable housing in upcoming Union budget enabling faster and deeper penetration of Housing for all.

items.statement: Raised Rs 6.3 bn NCDs from IFC (largest ever); total borrowings Rs 172 bn at 8.41% for 9M FY25
items.quote: I am happy to share that we have successfully raised NCDs amounting to Rs 6.3 bn from the IFC in Q3. This is largest NCD raised by company till date.

items.statement: 51% bank borrowings linked to EBLR/Repo/MCLR <3M enabling fast repricing on rate cuts
items.quote: We have 32% of our Bank borrowing are linked to EBLR such as T-Bill / Repo / MIBOR and 19% are linked <3 -month MCLR which will allow faster reprising of 51% bank borrowing in case of rate cut scenario.

items.statement: 1+ DPD at 3.85% (<4% guided); GNPA 1.14%, NNPA 0.81%; credit cost 15 bps in 9M FY25
items.quote: Our asset quality remains within the guided range with 1 day past due below 4% at 3.85% in Q3 FY25 and Gross Stage 3 & Net Stage 3 under 1.25% stood at 1.14% and 0.81% respectively.

items.statement: ECL model migrated to Deloitte Bolt-on with flow-rate approach and Vasicek macro factors; provisioning stable at 65 bps
items.quote: During this quarter, we have moved our entire ECL provisioning model from our historical model to Bolt-on. It's a universally accepted Deloitte model, wherein when we went live under this, we have made three major changes in our provisioning norms.

items.statement: RoA 3.37% in Q3 FY25 (+31 bps YoY); RoE 14.21% (+115 bps YoY); CRAR 45.56%
items.quote: RoA for the quarter increased by 31 bps YoY to 3.37% in Q3FY25 whereas RoE improved by 115 bps YoY to 14.21% in Q3FY25.

items.statement: Home loan yield 11.5-12%; non-home loan 250 bps higher; MSME 75 bps above LAP
items.quote: Home loan versus, let's say, non -home loan, which is MSME LAP, there is always difference of 250 bps between home loan to non-home loan. Yes, MSME businesses give us another 75 bps better pricing than the LAP portfolio.

items.statement: Employee count 6,284 (+6% YoY) vs 20% AuM growth; RO productivity per file increased
items.quote: Employee count grew by 6% Y-o-Y at 6,284 as of 31st Dec 2024 as against disbursement growth of 11% Y-o-Y and AuM growth of 20% Y-o-Y which indicates our productivity enhancement by various efforts taken by company.

items.statement: Liquidity buffer: Rs 18.95 bn cash/CC + Rs 22.8 bn unavailed sanctions as of Dec 2024
items.quote: As of 31st Dec 2024, we maintained sufficient liquidity in the form of cash and cash equivalents & unavailed CC limit of Rs. 18.95 bn and documented unavailed sanctions of Rs. 22.8 bn.

items.statement: Cautiously optimistic on macro; tighten underwriting if segment strain detected; 6.7% MFI overlap, 2.2% in 90+ DPD
items.quote: If we find anything on the segm ent-wise strain because of the macro environment having a waterfall effect on those economies or on those segments of customers, we hold on to that. So, at this period of time, what we speak, I think we are well guarded with a cautious approach of underwriting and continue to do that in a long -term period.

items.statement: Tech platforms upgraded and stabilizing; AI-driven predictive models for BT-out, collections, underwriting
items.quote: We have completed upgradation of all major tech platforms which are now stabilizing, this was one of the fastest tech implementations in the industry. We believe we have set the foundation for sustainable, scalable and profitable growth.

items.statement: Expect Q4 performance to materially augment 9-month EBITDA of INR5.2 billion
items.quote: The 9 -month EBITDA for the company is INR5.2 billion, and we expect Q4 performance to materially augment this number.

items.statement: Target double-digit RevPAR growth on existing portfolio and add through new assets
items.quote: Very confident that we will deliver double-digit RevPAR growths on our existing portfolio. And we will add through new assets and new inventories.

items.statement: Indian hospitality sector shows resilience with steady economic growth and increasing travel demand
items.quote: The Indian hospitality sector continues to show resilience supported by steady economic growth, stable rate of inflation and increasing demand for travel and tourism despite the state of global geopolitics.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 45.5% for Q3 FY25, up 23% YoY
items.quote: We have reported a strong EBITDA margin of 45.5%.

items.statement: Hospitality segment EBITDA margin at 46.1% for Q3 FY25 with well-managed utilities and payroll costs
items.quote: EBITDA margins for the quarter for Hospitality division was at 46.1%, with well-managed utilities and payroll costs.

items.statement: Rental and annuity EBITDA margin at 79% for Q3 FY25
items.quote: The EBITDA for the division was at INR455 million, with 79% margins.

items.statement: Lease confirmations of additional 400,000 square feet in Q3 FY25, exit monthly run rate of INR20 crores in December 2024
items.quote: Additionally, we achieved significant leasing momentum with lease confirmations of an additional 400,000 square feet in the quarter.

items.statement: Residential sales of 18 apartments in Q3 FY25 at average rate of INR22,000 per sq ft, 50 unsold units remaining
items.quote: We have sold additional 18 units during the quarter. We have reached the last leg of sales for the 9 towers which are ready for handovers.

items.statement: Goa hotel capex ~INR1.4 crore per key for 175-180 keys, approvals in 3-4 months, 30-month construction timeline
items.quote: So roughly the capex is going to be about 1.4 crores per room, per key. We are planning about, around 175 to 180 keys or rooms.

items.statement: Powai Phase 2 commercial capex ~INR800 crores, INR200 crores spent, INR600 crores balance over next 3 quarters
items.quote: So Powai, which is the Powai second -- Phase 2, is roughly 800 crores of capex spend, out of which we have already spent close to 200 crores, so 600 crores is the balance capex which we might be spending in next 3 quarters.

items.statement: Dukes Retreat: 73 rooms operational, full opening targeted end of Q1 FY26
items.quote: The phased opening of The Dukes Retreat continues, 73 rooms -- I repeat. 73 rooms, a restaurant, a bar and a pool are already operational.

items.statement: Four Points Navi Mumbai renovation 20% complete, full inventory completion targeted July 2025
items.quote: Renovations at Four Points By Sheraton Navi Mumbai are progressing well, with roughly 20% of the rooms and public areas currently in the works, with completion targeted for the whole inventory by July 2025.

items.statement: Taj at Terminal 3 Delhi Airport expected to open Q2 FY27
items.quote: The Taj at Terminal 3 Delhi International Airport is expected to open in Q2 of FY '27.

items.statement: Marriott Bengaluru new inventory being released, all operational in current quarter
items.quote: New inventory at Bangalore -- Marriott Bengaluru is being released, as we speak, into operations and will be all in play in the current quarter itself.

items.statement: Plan to reposition Courtyard Aravali to Marriott brand over next 6 months
items.quote: We are also working on our plans to upwardly reposition the spectacular Courtyard by Marriott Aravali to the Marriott brand.

items.statement: Gaurav Singh joined as Chief Operating Officer, Great Place to Work certification for 6th consecutive year
items.quote: I'm pleased to welcome Gaurav Singh, who has recently joined us as our Chief Operating Officer. Gaurav brings with him a rich background in the hospitality sector, and we are confident that his leadership will strengthen our operational excellence.

items.statement: Hospitality ADR up 18% YoY to ~INR13,000, occupancy stable at 70%, RevPAR up 16% to over INR9,000
items.quote: In the Hospitality segment, ADRs have risen by 18% to almost INR13,000 levels for the first time. This is led by strong rate growth in Bengaluru and addition of Courtyard by Marriott Aravali Resort.

items.statement: Bangalore ADR up 31%, occupancy up 4%, RevPAR up ~40%
items.quote: So Bangalore has improved by -- ADR by 31%. You're right. And our occ upancy has also improved by 4% , which is a 40 -odd-percent growth in the RevPAR in that particular hotel.

items.statement: Hyderabad Westin ADR up 28%, structural growth driven by office absorption
items.quote: Incidentally, Hyderabad Westin has also grown at 28%. So the strong story of these 2 what I refer to as new -age cities for India continues to be very robust.

items.statement: Foreign guest share flat at 39% but absolute foreign room nights up 5% YoY to 72,684 in Q3
items.quote: Having said that, whilst your percentages remained flat, absolute numbers are up, so we must be conscious of that, of -- not by a big margin, but they're up 5% over last year. So your number of foreigner room nights in Q3 this year was 72,684 versus 69,326 room nights, foreign room nights, last year.

items.statement: Corporate RFP contracts for last-room-available rates kept limited to enable revenue management
items.quote: We've also this time again kept the RFP contracts for last-room-available rates very limited, which will allow us to again revenue manage the rates as we go forward.

items.statement: Confident JW Marriott Sahar will remain #1 on RevPAR despite new 450-room airport hotel (200 rooms opening soon)
items.quote: We are very confident that the partnership with Marriott with a very strong distribution, sales and loyalty program will continue to get us the premium in that market. We are confident that we will continue to be #1 on the RevPAR basis there.

items.statement: Fairfield budget hotel (2-5x pricing gap) poses no threat to JW Marriott Sahar
items.quote: Fairfield is a budget hotel in the Marriott portfolio. There is no reference point between the two, as far as pricing is concerned. Fairfield to JW Marriott can have a gap of almost -- anywhere between 2x to 5x on the pricing, so I don't think that's a fair comparison.

items.statement: Kerala project fast-tracking government approvals, land transfer between departments underway
items.quote: The government has now announced they're fast -tracking the approval process at their end. Because they will transfer the land from one government department to the second government department before we can start our processes at our end.

items.statement: New Mumbai airport to create capacity for direct US flights, supporting foreign traveler growth
items.quote: Now with this split, it will create an opportunity where they can let out more slots to both domestic and international airline carriers, which will create an opportunity for direct flights from the U.S., both East and West Coast, which I think will support further growth on the foreign travellers.

items.statement: Residential collections INR2.9 billion in 9M FY25, outstanding receivables INR4 billion as of Dec 31
items.quote: Overall collections dur ing the 9 months was INR2.9 billion. And we have an outstanding receivable of INR4 billion as on December 31.

items.statement: Net debt INR15.8 billion as of Dec 31, average cost of finance 8.53% (down 34 bps from Mar 24), peak debt guided at INR19-20 billion
items.quote: The net debt as on December 31 was at INR15.8 billion. We closed the quarter with an average cost of finance standing at 8.53%, a reduction of 34 bps from March '24.

items.statement: Hotels effectively debt-free, commercial LRD eligibility INR1,800 crores covers current net debt
items.quote: Today, if you were to practically look at it from a bird's eye view, all the debt that we have -- almost all of it is actually on the office assets. The hotels are debt free, if you really look at our portfolio.

items.statement: RevPAR grew 16% YoY to over INR9,000, same-store RevPAR up 17%
items.quote: Occupancy remained stable at 70% for the same period, resulting in a 16% RevPAR growth to over INR9,000. On a same -store basis, excluding the newly acquired hotel at Aravali and The Dukes Retreat, occupancy was at 71% and RevPAR continued to grow by 17%.

items.statement: Kerala project timelines fluid, not included in INR20 billion capex guidance
items.quote: Timelines are fluid. I don't want to commit on time lines because of the nature of the transaction. However, this 150-room hotel is a -- the first phase is 150 rooms. Potentially we can go up to 300, 400 rooms, but I don't think the market can support that for now.

items.statement: Reiterated FY25 revenue growth guidance of 18-22% and raised EBITDA margin outlook to 21%+ from 20.5%+
items.quote: We maintain and reiterate our guidance for the revenue we had given at the beginning of the year between 18% to 22%. We have raised our EBITDA outlook from 20.5% + to 21% +, and that is reflected also in the EBITDA margin for this quarter.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin at 21.1% vs 20.8% QoQ; net profit grew 20.4% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA is 21.1% versus 20.8% last quarter. Year-on-year, there is a growth of 20.4% in terms of net profits.

items.statement: SDV opportunity extends beyond EV to digital cockpit, autonomous, cybersecurity, hybrid and conventional powertrain
items.quote: The SDV, as you look at it, it is much beyond EV in that sense. And if you actually ask me, the largest growth will be driven for us in terms of digital cockpit and autonomous in the next few years.

items.statement: Cash increased from INR9.68B to INR14.2B QoQ; DSO improved to 42 days from typical 45 days
items.quote: The cash for the quarter has increased from INR9.68 billion last quarter to INR14.2 billion this quarter. This is a significant cash generation during the quarter. It's an exceptional one. Our DSO is 42 days, which we typically are about 45 days.

items.statement: Interim dividend of INR2.5 per share declared vs INR2.1 last year
items.quote: We have interim dividend of INR2.5 per share as compared to INR2.1 per share last year.

items.statement: Significant one-off expense in Q3 for AI/tech investments, management development, and consultants for off-highway/commercial verticals
items.quote: It's an absolutely one-off kind of a thing increase, but we continue to do that. So I think we had a substantial additional expense during this quarter, where we have actually had a significant investment into both the technology as well as management development, both for AI and competencies.

items.statement: Engaging with acquisition targets but no QIP planned; will fund via internal accruals and borrowing
items.quote: On the M&A side, we continue to engage with few companies. but looking at their sizes and what we see currently, we do not see that we will opt for QIP in the short term. So we believe some of these acquisitions, we will do through internal accruals on the basis of strong cash flow and borrowing.

items.statement: No significant visa/immigration challenges expected; well-prepared for local presence expansion; US policy changes seen as broadening opportunities beyond EV
items.quote: We do not see any significant challenges in terms of visa, etcetera, basically because we believe it is about the talent and not about the immigration. And so we believe that there will be a continued mobility for short-term projects as needed.

items.statement: No broad-based pricing pressure; 90% of clients show no behavior change; margin improvement reflects productivity gains and better revenue mix
items.quote: Nothing is on our territory, that's client-specific, but for a large set of clients, we don't see any changes. And actually, it is reflected in the results. I think the margin is increased and the closures have been higher both in dollar terms and this. So at a high level, we don't see it. It is very customer specific. 90% of the clients, we don't see any changes in the behaviour at all.

items.statement: Committed to cumulative capex of INR6,000 crores by FY28 for battery materials business
items.quote: We are committed to our cumulative capex plan of INR6,000 crores by FY '28, as we had indicated earlier.

items.statement: Battery materials business expected to achieve 2x asset turnover and ~25% EBITDA margins at optimal utilization
items.quote: At optimal utilization level, this business is expected to achieve around 2x asset turnover and approximately 25% EBITDA margins.

items.statement: R-32 capacity expansion of up to 30,000 tons planned with Phase 1 of ~20,000 tons by Q4 FY26
items.quote: We are looking at almost setting up a capacity of 30,000 tons, okay? So -- and we have time in terms of till we can utilize this quota.

items.statement: Salt plant expansion underway based on customer contracts; capex part of existing INR6,000 crore EV plan
items.quote: Our capex plan is still what we had indicated INR 6,000 crores. However, so the intent was to say that we are now reached a point where we feel the capacity addition has to be done.

items.statement: AHF capacity expansion planned to support R-32 and other growth; not included in INR150 crore R-32 capex
items.quote: Yes, we have a plan for AHF as well, Dhruv. Of course, in next quarter, I think we'll share our capex plan for the next year, and then we'll talk about it.

items.statement: Fluoropolymer full capacity utilization expected by end of FY26
items.quote: We expect our full capacity utilization to be there by the end of FY '26, yes.

items.statement: LFP plant mechanical completion expected in several weeks, startup by end of FY25
items.quote: Our LFP plant would be set up in another several few weeks, in fact, mechanical completion and then start up by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: Fluoropolymer volumes declined QoQ due to year-end holidays in key export markets
items.quote: Fluoropolymer volumes declined on a quarter-on-quarter basis, primarily due to year-end holidays in key export market segments.

items.statement: R-125 prices and volumes expected to improve going forward; Q3 seasonally weak
items.quote: For R-125, which is primarily exported to U.S., Q3 is seasonally weak quarter, but both prices and volumes are expected to improve going forward.

items.statement: Specialty chemicals volumes flat in Q3, pickup expected from Q4 FY25 driven by downstream demand
items.quote: Speciality Chemicals remained flat during the quarter, but are likely to see a pickup in volumes starting quarter 4 F Y '25, driven by improving downstream demand

items.statement: EV battery material demand robust from both EV and ESS segments globally and domestically
items.quote: The demand for our products are going to be very robust, not only from the EV segments, but also from the rapidly growing ESS segment.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 26% in Q3 FY25 from 21% in Q3 FY24 driven by better product mix
items.quote: The EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 26%, up from 21% in quarter 3 FY '24.

items.statement: Margin improvement purely from product mix as value-added products and new polymers fraction increases
items.quote: And when coming back to margin improvement, margin improvement is purely by product mix, as our overall fraction of our value-added products and the new polymers are increasing, the margins would keep on going up.

items.statement: Commodity grade PTFE faces pricing pressure from low-cost Chinese suppliers
items.quote: While prices remained stable during the quarter, the commodity grade PTFE continued to face pricing pressures from low-cost suppliers from China.

items.statement: R-22 refrigerant gas prices improved during Q3 with further pickup expected
items.quote: Within f luorochemicals segment, refrigerant gas prices, particularly for R- 22, improved during the quarter with further pickup expected going forward

items.statement: MDC prices improved in Q3 but expected to be muted near-term due to new Indian capacities
items.quote: MDC prices have improved during the quarter. However, it is expected to be muted in near term because of additional capacities being commissioned in India.

items.statement: Caustic soda prices improved after 5-6 weak quarters, boosting Bulk Chemicals performance
items.quote: Caustic soda prices improved after remaining weak for the past 5, 6 quarters, thereby improving the segment's performance.

items.statement: Power cost reduction of 10-12% (~INR100 crores) expected from FY26 via renewable PPAs at INR4/unit
items.quote: We expect a reduction of 10% to 12% -- 10% to 12% reduction. That is around INR100 crores.

items.statement: Weighted average power cost expected around INR4.5/unit with >80% renewable energy at INR4/unit
items.quote: The power purchase agreement that we are -- we have signed for the new energy -- renewable energy is at INR 4. So that would constitute more than 80% of our total requirement. So to that extent, the power -- the weighted average will be in the range of around INR4.5.

items.statement: Fluoropolymer commercial sales from qualified higher-grade products expected from Q4 FY25
items.quote: We have already gone through the qualifications on various grades. We have received qualifications, and we expect now that into commercial sales in quarter 4 onwards.

items.statement: FKM qualifications for ethanol blending done; commercial orders from OEMs/Tier 1 expected from next quarter
items.quote: So we'll start seeing the ramp-ups from the next quarter onwards, and it will keep on happening for quarter-to-quarter probably for the whole financial year.

items.statement: US customers' capacity addition plans intact despite IRA subsidy uncertainty; visibility for next 3-5 years
items.quote: Based on their investment and their capacities, we fairly -- we have a visibility that at least in the next 3 to 5 years, the plan that we had given is going to be intact, okay?

items.statement: Exit of legacy player combined with GFL's higher-grade qualifications to drive significant revenue and profitability increase
items.quote: Looking ahead, the exit of a legacy player, combined with GFL's successful de velopment and qualification of higher -grade fluoropolymers, it is expected to drive a significant increase in revenues and profitability in coming quarters

items.statement: Secured major deal with one of largest global social media networks across their app platforms in India plus significant wins in quick commerce and BFSI

items.statement: Government revenue share expected to reach double digits but below 20% of total revenue in FY25
items.quote: This year, I am giving advance information that we might be, definitely will be in double digit but less than 20%.

items.statement: All Hyundai and Kia models in India to have MapmyIndia maps built in from Q4 FY25; Southeast Asia JV revenue expected from Q1/Q2 FY26

items.statement: IoT installed device base at 600k-700k units generating subscription revenue; nine-month hardware sales ~170k units vs ~300k full year prior
items.quote: Your number is right.

items.statement: A&M license count grew 23% YoY in first nine months of FY25
items.quote: In the first nine months of FY25, our A&M revenue grew by 16% year-on-year and number of licenses grew by 23%.

items.statement: Wins in quick commerce attributed to superior hyper-local map data quality and agile service integration capabilities vs Google Maps
items.quote: The quality of our product specifically the map data and the underlying APIs or SDKs we provide plays a crucial role. When our offering is better than the competition, especially in quick commerce, which is highly hyper-local, that level of detailed mapping is helping us to win.

items.statement: Government receivables under 100 days; no bad debt issues or increasing provisions
items.quote: Even now, if you look at our financial statements, government receivables are overall less than 100 days. While our total receivables include both government and other segments, the key point is that we are not facing bad debt issues, and our provisions for bad debt are not increasing.

items.statement: Technical outsourcing costs spiked in Q3 due to government project scaling and COTS software; costs tied to revenue per accounting standards
items.quote: We incur outsourcing expenses when certain projects need to be scaled up rapidly within a short timeframe, requiring external resources. And also, it includes certain software such as COTS as we call it, which becomes part of it.

items.statement: Map-led business grew 33% YoY to Rs 287 crores in Q3; IoT-led business grew 4% YoY but subscription revenue up 31%
items.quote: Our Map-led business delivered a very strong 33% growth of Rs. 287 crores in Q3 FY25 year-on-year while the IoT led business had a growth of 4% year-on-year during the quarter

items.statement: Large IoT hardware projects delayed from Q3 to FY26; Q4 hardware revenue will not recover the shortfall
items.quote: Well, let's wait. I mean at least it will not happen in Q4. That I can say for sure.

items.statement: Qualcomm partnership for automotive OEM connectivity solutions; revenue impact expected after at least one year
items.quote: This is given that it's for automotive OEMs, the impact on revenue will be seen post 1 year at least.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 gross margin 67.3%, EBITDA margin 47.4%, PAT margin 30.9%
items.quote: The company continues to report industry -leading gross margin of 67.3% and healthy EBITDA margin of 47.4%. The company reported best -in-class PAT margin of around 30.9%.

items.statement: Added ~50,000 sq ft net retail area in Q3; total EBO area 1.75 mn sq ft across 666 stores in 255 cities
items.quote: In this quarter, we expanded our retail footprint by adding approximately 50,000 square feet of net retail area. As of December 2024, Vedant Fashions EBO area stands at 1.75 million sq uare feet, spanning across 666 stores in 255 cities and towns globally

items.statement: FY25 gross store additions targeting 170,000-180,000 sq ft; net additions slower due to closures and rental inflation
items.quote: So, at the gross level, we will be doing a decent amount of opening, close to about 1,70,000, 1,80,000 square feet, which is what we've been focusing on for the entire financial year. So, from a gross perspective, we are on track.

items.statement: No specific FY26 store opening guidance; depends on rental market stabilization; pipeline remains strong
items.quote: However, if the rentals remain at similar levels, then it is difficult to comment on the scale at which we will be opening stores next year. However, from a longer-term aspect, when things do stabilize, I think that's -- from a long-term perspective, definitely we should have stable store openings.

items.statement: AP and Telangana weak vs rest of India; macro headwind affecting sales in those states
items.quote: AP and Telangana as a region is one of our strongest areas in terms of penetration and also the exposure we have in those 2 states. So, I think our performance in those 2 states particularly was pretty weak versus the rest of India doing pretty well in comparison to what was happening in those 2 states.

items.statement: Mohey productivity now near Manyavar levels (25-30% area, 25-30% sales); Twamev growing strongly in metros, 7 EBOs with 2 added in Q3
items.quote: Earlier, it used to achieve close to 70% of Manyavar 's productivity within that area. But now what we are witnessing with all the new stores and even the older stores, we have reached almost Manyavar 's productivity. So, if it has 25% to 30% area, then it's also doing 25% to 30% of the business.

items.statement: Twamev contribution rising in flagship stores; 7 EBOs with 2 added in Q3; super flagship opening Q2 FY26; Twamev women being infused in Manyavar Mohey stores
items.quote: Currently, we have about 7 EBOs with 2 EBOs opening this quarter. And we have a few more EBOs in the pipeline with one super flagship store also that will be opening sometime in the second quarter of next year.

items.statement: ASP grew ~1-1.5% in Q3; premium end and value end both growing, middle segment soft
items.quote: At a company level, our ASP has grown by about 1% or 1.5%. But if you see from a market angle, this has been quite varied. So we see both the premium end growing and the bottom end growing from our company's perspective.

items.statement: No downtrading observed; basket size and average bill value improving; no market share loss vs competitors
items.quote: When we even talk about, let's say, down trading, we don't think that's happening because basket size is improving, average bill value is improving, but the trends are interesting to see how different markets are operating. And all in all, if you ask me, while the number of stores have opened a lot, which is something we've been mentioning from across different players, we still don't feel that we

items.statement: Purchase of stock-in-trade ~20-21% of total stock, now ~24-25% due to aggressive variety strategy; vendor exclusivity maintained
items.quote: Broadly, if I am right, then we would purchase close to about 20%, 21% of our stock overall at the company level. That might be closer to 24%, 25% now. So we will get back with the exact figures, but that's broadly the change, which is 400, 500 basis points from an overall angle.

items.statement: Online channel ~3-4% of sales, growing ~70% in Q3; quick commerce partnerships with Zepto/Blinkit driving growth
items.quote: It's about 3% to 4%, but our growth has been very strong in the online segment. We have been growing probably the fastest in that as a channel. And overall, about 70 -odd percent growth is what we've seen in Q3 when it comes to online.

items.statement: No discounting strategy; discounting against core philosophy and not needed due to low dead stock; marketplace performance strong without discounts
items.quote: discounting as a topic, we feel, is against the core philosophy on which our company has been built, which is when anyone is celebrating, I don't think it is easy to attract them with a discount in the first place. And the second place, dis count majorly is a mechanism of liquidating dead stock, which is something we majorly don't have in our company

items.statement: January sales similar to Q3; only 15 days of normal trading observed; need more data for commentary
items.quote: I think broadly, it's -- what we have seen is only 30 days, of which 15 days are always slower than normal period. So we have only seen about 15 days of January. But in the current 30 days, it's been similar to Q3.

items.statement: Men's conversion 75-80%, women's 60-65%; footfall growth drove SSSG with ASP up ~1%
items.quote: We do about 75% to 80% conversion at a group level when it comes to our men's business and about 60%, 65% conversions now when it comes to our women's wear business. So, these are in line and have been doing pretty well. And in terms of footfall, if you look at the quarter, our ASP growth was about 1%. So, the remaining 1.5%, 2% growth, which came from an SSSG perspective, was all led by slightly

items.statement: Competition not a major factor; 400 stores with no competition, 250-260 with competition; competitive stores performed slightly better over 2 years
items.quote: We have about odd 400 stores where there is no competition next to it, and we have about 250, 260 stores where there is competition next to it. We don't see change in performance in either of these sorts of fleets. In fact, if you look at it from a longer -term 2-year period, the 250 stores would have actually done slightly better off than the remaining sort of the stores that we have which don't

items.statement: Macro headwind on middle-class discretionary spending; category growth expected mid-to-long term; wedding consumption growing structurally
items.quote: We also feel that this is also the case with overall mid -premium discretionary spends. I think the problem, or the macro headwind seems to be a little larger in nature rather than it being something limited to men's ethnic or celebration wear industry.

items.statement: Medium-term retail area growth target of mid-teens (15%) still aspirational; depends on rental normalization
items.quote: Very difficult to answer for the next 1 to 2 years. But typically, what happens and what we have seen over the last 2 decades is the moment this slowness starts again in terms of the retail rental numbers, then we again become very aggressive. So the endeavour is to come back at those numbers, but it also depends on how the rental numbers will move in the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance raised to INR 510-520 crores from earlier INR 475-500 crores
items.quote: But definitely, we may cross INR 500 crores, we may reach somewhere between INR 510 crore, and INR 520 crores.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guidance of 25-30% with 15-20% organic and 10% acquisitive
items.quote: At least 25% to 30%. On which may be , because this year itself, if you see the 41% growth on that 25% is organic growth. So next year, if we say 25% to 30%, maybe 15%. Conservatively 15% to 20% can be organic growth balance 10% can be acquisitive growth.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin guidance 23% reported, 25% adjusted; PAT margin 15.5-16%
items.quote: Expected EBITDA margin we can see around same 24%, 25%. If you take all these adjustments, adjusted EBITDA definitely can be 25%. If non-adjusted EBITDA can be 23%. And then the PAT 15.5% to 16%.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 gross margin impacted by CCA guidelines requiring retail pricing and partner commissions of 40-50%
items.quote: Nowadays, by the guideline we are forced to sell at the retail price and then pay a commission to the partner, so that way, and the commission varies from 40% to 50%.

items.statement: Stock repurchase of INR 2.5-3 crores per quarter impacting gross margin percentage until September next year
items.quote: So what we are doing to agree with the partners is to the extent that they sell in a particular quarter, we will repurchase their old stock. So that also almost comes to some around INR 2.5 crores to INR 3 crores per quarter.

items.quote: So all these put together, it is almost INR 16 crores to INR 17 crores. But though we told INR 90 crores after this INR 17 crores, we may achieve INR 87 crore to INR 90 crores.

items.statement: Trust services volumes declined 40-50% due to income tax rule changes reducing DSC requirement from 36 lakh to 6-7 lakh cases and 10-12 new competitors pricing at INR 600-800 vs company's INR 1,500
items.quote: Volume declined, as I told last time, almost 40% to 50% volume decline is there, one, volume decline is due to the income tax. In income tax, what was happening, earlier other than corporate, even the non-corporate like partnership firm, HUF, individual whoever is doing tax audit, both the tax auditor and them both have to be signed using the digital signature.

items.statement: Strong overseas growth in Americas, Middle East, Africa and Asia Pacific driven by significant deal closures
items.quote: This quarter's growth was driven by strong performance in our overseas markets, particularly in the Americas, Middle East and Africa and Asia Pacific regions, supported by significant deals closures.

Support for delivering for secured cloud workloads in North America for a large ERP platform . Certificate life cycle management for large bank in the Middle East.

items.statement: Cybersecurity now 75% of enterprise revenue vs paperless 25%; cybersecurity growing faster with less competition

items.quote: On the INR 43 crore, I think roughly our own service revenue is INR 5 crores, INR 6 crores and others Ikon and TWO95 maybe around INR 37 crores - INR 38 crores.

items.statement: 10-12 new competitors in trust services selling at INR 600-800 with 50-60% commission vs company's INR 1,500; company avoiding price war
items.quote: Then another thing is some 10 - 12 competitors have come. So some of the business has gone to those competitors, and they are selling at a much lower price. For example, we are selling at INR 1,500. They are all selling at anywhere from INR 600 to INR 800 kind of things, on which itself they give some 50% to 60% commission.

items.statement: Evaluating EU acquisition up to EUR 10-12 million revenue size at 10x EBITDA or 1x revenue; target must be turnable to 15% EBITDA via India cost transfer
items.quote: Size is, we are not looking at very big size because then it will be a very high share dilution and then the other thing will be otherwise, we have to again go to QIP and those kind of things or swap those kind of things. items.statement: Appointed European CEO Carmine Auletta (ex-InfoCert COO) to drive EU acquisition and partnerships; building global partner program with 2,000 partners across strategic, growth and other tiers
items.quote: Yes, we are looking at it. We appointed a European CEO, one person by name Carmine Auletta and he earlier worked as COO in InfoCert. InfoCert is a $150 million company based out of Italy, and they operate throughout Europe.

items.statement: Cash balance stable at INR 166-167 crores at quarter end
items.quote: Cash balance, last quarter end was INR 167 crores. This quarter end also around INR 166 crores or INR 167 crores is there.

items.statement: Headcount stable despite revenue growth due to AI-driven operational efficiency; hiring only sales people abroad
items.quote: So that's why in spite of increase in the revenues, the corresponding manpower has not increased so much. We are able to maintain the manpower at the same level or maybe a little lower level. Today, we are increasing the manpower only for the salespeople abroad, but otherwise the technology team, then the customer service team, operations team, everybody operate at the same level or even at a redu

items.statement: emSigner product gross margin 87-88% excluding hardware; partner commission 25-30% on product license, 7.5-10% on services
items.quote: emSigner also like any other product margin, almost if hardware is not included, it will be 87%, 88% depending on partner margin only will be there. Otherwise there is no other direct cost involved.

items.statement: CCA guidelines mandate single retail pricing for digital signatures eliminating channel differentiation; stock repurchase required for pre-July 15 inventory
items.quote: Now the Controller Certifying Authority has told that you have to always sell the end customer and at a single price, which is published in the website. items.statement: EU regulations now mandate Mobile PKI for digital IDs and signatures creating new opportunities
items.quote: Furthermore recent regulatory developments in the European Union, now mandate the use of Mobile PKI for issuing digital IDs and signatures creating additional opportunities for our solutions.

items.statement: Stock repurchase obligation may continue until September next year at INR 2.5-4 crores per quarter
items.quote: It may go up to September of next year, because otherwise, if we commit to repurchase everything together, then suddenly, we have to sell out all the money and the partners also will not be focused on selling our stock there because today, too many competi tors some 13 - 14 people have

items.statement: No plan to acquire remaining 49% of Ikon; 51% stake sufficient as both parties benefit from product cross-sell
items.quote: No, as of now, there is no plan. There is no discussion with them also. So it's continuing and doing well. So because if you pay this 51% also, then we have to sell out the cash we are preserving.

items.statement: Post Quantum Cryptography POCs underway with 2-3 US and Indian organizations; dual RSA+PQC approach integrated into MCA product; banking and defense sectors expected to adopt first
items.quote: No, still nobody has converted to Post Quantum, but large organizations have started asking for POC, particularly some 2 - 3 US organizations have asked, some Indian organizations have asked for the POC. Those things we have started demonstrating.

items.statement: GenAI integration for deepfake detection, document summarization, risk assessment, security analytics and internal automation; business-side AI features planned for next year
items.quote: We are integrating GenAI into our product suite to address critical use cases such as deepfake detection during identity verification, document summarization, risk assessme nt and security analytics. These capabilities also extended to automating internal processes, ensuring efficiency and scalability in

items.quote: Hardware is very less. It is not significant, one is on the trust services, this 40% to 50% gross margin is there. Then on the service component, whatever service we are providing on that service, whatever that manpower cost is also going into the operating cost. Hardware, not much because this year, even token sales, we are reducing because the margin is very less.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin guidance of 7% (Rs 305-310 cr) maintained; FY26 revenue growth target 30-35% with corresponding EBITDA margin increase
items.quote: For the 9 months FY '25, our EBITDA, operating EBITDA margin stands at 7.2% against a guidance of 7% given at the start of the year. For the quarter, notably, this stands at 9.1%. So, this gives us confidence that 7% achievement would be possible, and if any movement, it will be only north of 7% in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Open order book ~Rs 5,300 cr as of Dec 2024; execution over 9-15 months; auto 30%+, consumer 38-40%, industrial 20-22%, balance healthcare/IT/railway
items.quote: Coming to our open order book visibility a s on date, as on December 2024, it is around 5,300 crores, which comprises almost 30% plus of contribution from auto segment, about 38 to 40% from consumer segment , approximately 20-22% from industrial segment and balance from healthcare plus IT and railway segment as well

items.statement: Q3 FY25 operating EBITDA margin 9.1% (up from 7.2% 9M); 9M gross margin 21.3%, Q3 gross margin 26.7% (+200bps QoQ); improvement driven by product mix shift and operating efficiencies
items.quote: This quarter, we had a strong rebound of the margins led by expansion in gross margins on the back of change in the business mix. The consumer sector business is slightly lower than other segments here. The gross margin for the 9 month is 21.3% and for the quarter it is with a very healthy gross margin of about 26.7%. Broadly 200 bps of expansion on quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Consumer share down to 31% in Q3 (from 54% in Q1, ~40% 9M); target to reduce high-volume consumer to 35% of revenue; industrial 30% in Q3 vs 25% 9M; auto 24% in Q3 vs 21% 9M
items.quote: For example, in Q3, my consumer business is only 31%, high-volume consumer business, which is a tight-margin business, whereas my industrial business is 30% for three months against the average of 25% for 9 months. My automotive is 24% of my revenue for this quarter comes from automotive. For 9 months it is 21%.

items.statement: Exports at 20% of revenue (down from 25%) due to Germany slowdown; expect rebound in FY26 but gradual; MedTech delayed ~9 months, expects recovery in FY26
items.quote: Exports stand at about 20%. Exports have had a subdued sort of muted scenario because our geographies which we are servicing are essentially America and Europe. And in Europe, it's primarily Germany. And Germany is today the sick baby of EU.

items.statement: 9M FY25 capex ~Rs 180 cr (Pune campus, Germany facility, SMT lines); Q4 estimate Rs 32 cr; FY25 total Rs 200-245 cr; FY26 estimate Rs 100-150 cr
items.quote: Coming to my capex, for this 9 months we had spent approximately 180 crores of CAPEX and largely towards building up this new campus facility in Pune and a facility there in Germany. Some bit of additional capex towards some SMT lines and plant and machinery stuffing for new customers' onboarding.

items.statement: Current capacity utilisation ~70% (9M); Pune facility not yet counted in capacity; with marginal balancing equipment, 6,000-6,500 cr revenue achievable on current gross block
items.quote: Currently for the 9 months my capacity utilization is around 70% or little less than 70%. So, if I have done 3,000 or 2,900 crores of revenue at 70% that this takes us to 4,000 crores in the new setups which we have just put in, which are not called or taken into the capacity, would yield additional results.

items.statement: Net working capital 64 days at Dec 2024 (up from ~60); target <60 days sustainable; increase due to new plant inventory and customer onboarding
items.quote: On the working capital side, currently, as on quarter end, we st ood at around 64 days of net working capital days investments. Again, it is slightly higher than the last quarter. We continue to make efforts to keep this net working capital below 60 days on a sustainable basis

items.statement: Gross debt Rs 685 cr; treasury Rs 412 cr; net debt Rs 273 cr; term loan only Rs 65 cr, rest working capital
items.value: Gross Rs 685 cr; Net Rs 273 cr
items.quote: Moving to our debt position, we have a gross debt of approximately 685 crores, against which we are maintaining a treasury of Rs. 412 crore, and with that my net debt position is Rs. 273 crore. Out of this total debt, it is primarily funded through the working capital and only 65 crore is what is the term loan here.

items.statement: ROCE ~13% adjusted for Q3; target 14.5-15% for FY25, 20% by FY27; asset turn 5.5-5.6x, target 6-7x
items.quote: My asset turn for the quarter is about 5.5 x and ROCE for the quarter is around 13% on an adjusted basis. We expect this to improve further as we work on higher utilization of our CAPEX going forward.

items.statement: Merger pending final NCLT order; expected completion in 3-6 months; inorganic acquisitions evaluated for technology, regulatory approvals, product gaps; no active deals
items.quote: Slight a bit of update on the merger side. We are waiting for the final order from the NCLT, and we hope we should be able to complete this merger in another 3-6 months of time.

items.statement: QIP approved but not initiated; only for future growth opportunities (inorganic/OSAT), not for existing business; sufficient internal accruals for current growth
items.quote: We have taken our QIP approv al just to be ready for any future growth. We have never contemplated any growth. J. S. Gujral: Inorganic. Bijay Agrawal: We have never contemplated QIP for our existing business related any kind of a working capital funding. That's very clear

items.statement: PLI benefit accrual: Rs 14 cr for 9M FY25 (net basis); full year estimate Rs 15-17 cr; FY24 full year ~Rs 12-13 cr; shifted from cash to accrual basis
items.quote: On the PLI, for the current year, we are estimating it should be around Rs. 15-17 crore. For the 9 months for current financial year, we have accrued around Rs. 14 crore.

items.statement: Onboarded good automotive and industrial clients in Q3; expect sub-Rs 200 cr revenue from these in FY26; significant revenue from FY27
items.quote: We have onboarded some good automotive and industrial clients in the current quarter , and going forward, which will be '26-'27, we expect significant business from these clien ts. In '25- '26, these clients will be yielding sub-200 crores of revenues

items.statement: Renegotiating prices on high-volume consumer business to improve margins; deliberate strategy to shift to high-margin, low-medium volume business
items.quote: What we have done in the last quarter is that we have started renegotiating prices for the high volume consumer business to see whether we can have a bump in some margins or not. And that is a long-term strategy of the company to move to the high-profit, high-margin business, low-medium-volume, high-margin business.

items.statement: Germany export slowdown may be prolonged; MedTech delayed 9 months; consumer demand seasonality; PLI policy changes; Trump policy uncertainty for US nearshoring
items.quote: Germany is today a sick baby of EU and Trump has just come in. I think it will be a while before the policies gets settled down. But on a long-term basis, again I said we are worried about quarter-on-quarter, short term.

items.statement: Focus on building organization, campus model, talent retention, diversity, social responsibility; new Pune facility commissioned Oct 2024
items.quote: One of the steps is that instead of standalone units, we have started going on the campus routes to save on the cost. That's one of the long-term strategies of the company. We have commissioned or in the process of final commissioning of our facility in Germany.

items.statement: Management revised FY25 revenue guidance downward due to delayed large procurement opportunities
items.quote: So yes, there will be a revision overall on that.

items.statement: Order book at INR 21 crores as of 31st December with L1 pipeline of INR 400-plus crores
items.quote: Our order book as of 31st December stood at approximately INR 21 crores, with an L1 opportunity pipeline of INR 400-plus crores now as compared to INR 300 crores earlier.

items.statement: Demand-to-order conversion below industry expectations in first 3 quarters due to national elections and delayed government procurement
items.quote: The year so far has been a mixed bag for us and the drone industry. While a lot of development is happening on new use cases, products and technologies, the demand-to-order conversion in the first 3 quarters of the year has been below industry expectations.

items.statement: Q3 gross profit margin at 46%, 9M gross profit margin at 32.6%, EBITDA and PAT negative for both periods
items.quote: For the quarter, gross profit stood at INR 8.1 crores, with a gross profit margin of 46%. For 9 months FY '25, gross profit stood at INR 45.9 crores, with a gross profit margin of 32.6%.

items.statement: R&D expenses will increase slightly in absolute terms from INR 53 crores in FY24
items.quote: Hardik, the percentage, of course, will be determined at the end of the year, but the R&D expenses will go up slightly from last year, for sure.

items.quote: I'm pleased to inform you that two of our next-generation products, NETRA 5 and SWITCH V2 are now ready for customer demonstrations, and we'll be officially unveiling them at the global flagship event in the coming month, the Aero India 2025.

items.statement: Tactical UAV platform in advanced prototype stage, middle-mile logistics platform (500 kg MTOW, 100+ kg payload, 100+ km range) in prototype design phase
items.quote: We would be getting into the next revision of the prototype development, which will get closer to what the user final configuration is going to be. items.statement: Run-rate business from civil (police, CAPF, government departments, private enterprises) and defense (command/battalion level, spares) segments
items.quote: These are all civil and some defense business from India itself, run-rate business.

items.statement: Typically only 2 players qualify in specific opportunities; competition credibility varies but deep technical capability needed to sustain

items.statement: Plants not shut during solar hours; operate at technical minimum; ramp up for peak hours; tied up weekly/monthly/6-monthly contracts

items.statement: Surplus cash flow to be utilized for best industry returns per Adani Group DNA; no specific dividend or buyback guidance
items.quote: You know the DNA of the Adani group, and I can assure you that this surplus cash flow will be utilized in a manner that it will give the best of the industry return in the future.

items.statement: ESG score improved from 48 to 68 in S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment; now in top 15% of peer set
items.quote: I am happy to note that our all-round efforts have earned recognition in the form of improved ESG ratings, awarded by various Indian and international ESG rating agencies. Recently, we have improved our score from 48 /100 to 68 /100 in Corporate Sustainability Assessment by S&P Global.

items.quote: I think in our last call we said that we will maintain 60% for 2025-26.

items.statement: Jumbo laminate plant expected revenue INR 100-125 crore in FY26
items.quote: So, we expect the revenues of more than INR 100 to INR 125 crores out of that new plant from laminate and it will be all a specialized product.

items.statement: Jumbo laminate plant EBITDA margin 10-12% in H1 FY26, 12-14% in H2 FY26
items.quote: So, first year the margin should be around 10%-12% for the first two quarters, but later on the second half of the year, yes, we can expect the 12% to 14% margin.

First is like, we would be targeting within the wood panel industry, that is first point. Whatever product we are just planning, it will be within this industry. Secondly, the means of finance for this particu

items.statement: Good order book filling after Diwali; inquiries converting to orders for both MDF and laminates
items.quote: We have a good amount of order books getting filled now after the Diwali. And the inquiries are now getting converted into orders as well.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 MDF EBITDA margin 15.2% (up 1.5-2% QoQ); laminate EBITDA margin 7.7% (down from ~10-11% QoQ)
items.quote: MDF EBITDA was INR 234 million with an improved EBITDA margin of 15.2% in Q3 FY25.

items.statement: Laminate 9M FY25 EBITDA margin 9.9%; Q3 dip due to Diwali plant shutdown and lower utilization
items.quote: The EBITDA margin for laminate was 7.7% during the quarter. For 9 months, FY25, laminate revenue grew 4.3% year-on-year to INR 1,460 million and EBITDA grew 5.2% year-on-year to INR 145 million with a margin of 9.9%.

items.statement: MDF price hike of 2-3% taken last quarter and maintained; further hike expected after BIS implementation

Even import is also expensive nowadays and you know import is completely negligible because it's not even 4,000 - 5,000 CBM a month. So, if we look at Indian capacities 4.2 million and secondly after implementation of BIS , I am sure there will be the importance of brand and oth

items.statement: Raw material prices stable in Q3 FY25 and expected to remain stable; wood cost no increment
items.quote: The raw material prices for this quarter were stable for us. And we also see stable raw material prices for this quarter as well.

items.statement: Domestic MDF demand picking up after Lohri/festive season; export demand strong in Gulf, Israel, Africa
items.quote: For the domestic market after the Lohri and other festive season, now the market is picking up, demand is there.

items.statement: MDF value-added revenue share 54% in Q3 FY25 (target 55%); volume share 44-45% (target 50%)
items.quote: Our target in terms of value-added was 50% and 55% in terms of quantity and value. In terms of value, we have already achieved 54% as of now. Quantity again, it is in the range of 44% - 45% as of now, which we would like to achieve 50%.

items.statement: BIS certification implementation by mid-February expected to curb imports; import volume negligible at 4,000-5,000 CBM/month
items.quote: So, first of all, the Government has already implemented the BIS certification standards which will be done in the mid February. So, the threat of import will be vanished for certain years till the time the other countries' plants are not getting the BIS standards.

We don't want to be too over enthusiastic in saying and quoting a number. But definitely, the objective will be very simple, 25%. But then 20% -- 15% to 20% is not something which we will accept less than that

items.statement: Targets company-level EBITDA margin of 22-25% and restaurant-level EBITDA of 30-32%
items.quote: See, if I may, let's say, for instance, the broad number, if I look at company level EBITDA, if you look at, it is ranging between 22% to 25% on a company level basis. And if you look at the restaurant level basis on the basis of Ind AS accounting, it would be at the range of 30% to 32%.

items.statement: Capex of INR3.5 crores per store with 3-5 year payback and 6-8 month P&L breakeven
items.quote: No, it's actually, the payback is 3 to 5 years, depending on the location, seasonality's, etcetera, or any ad hoc factor in that location itself. But the P&L breakeven is between 6 to 8 months of the store.

items.statement: Expects 20-22% ROE over 5-year period for new stores
items.quote: But we expect that the ROE, which is almost to the extent of -- in 5 years' period, it would be in the range of 20% to 22%.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth of 4.7% in Q3 FY25 with overall revenue growth of 9%
items.quote: If you look at the quarter 3 of FY '25, our same -store sales growth has been around 4.7% and overall revenue growth has been 9%.

items.statement: Renovated stores seeing 20-30% revenue jump
items.quote: So the first thing is that wherever we have done our renovations, that has added to 20% to 30% of revenue jump in our current stores.

items.statement: Liquor sales 10-12% of total revenue, 50% at Episode One, targeting 15% overall with bar upgrades
items.quote: Liquor sales ranges between 10% to 12% of the total revenues, except in the U.S. -- on overall basis, it is. But on wet-led basis, it is 50% at Episode One.

items.quote: Whereas when you talk about anything else like a noodle, the price of the noodle compared to the price of the chicken is much, much lower. And you have so much of noodle and you add a little bit of chicken.

We are innovating formats by giving the same content in Asian.

items.statement: Oh! Calcutta growing 18% with expansion planned in Pune and Chennai
items.quote: Second one is in the form of Oh! Calcutta, which is a growth engine. There's been almost double digit, more than that. In fact, it's almost 18% growth this year.

items.statement: Sweet Bengal expansion paused due to commissary and talent constraints; focusing on Oriental instead
items.quote: We are looking for someone to actually lead this from Haldiram over a period of time, but we've not been able to get the best person. So till then, Mr. Zaki, we would rather -- because what we see, the return on investment and the future of the Asian cuisine is much better than that of maybe a Sweet Bengal compared to the Asian space.

items.statement: Catering division (Speciality Experiences) revenue doubled year-over-year with focused team now in place
items.quote: We started speciality experiences as a wing in Mumbai city just to test it out. And from the revenues of last year to this year, we have seen more than double and getting great feedback as well.

items.quote: Some of the delays happen because of the real estate deliveries. That's the primary reason. items.quote: So I think that Delhi is a new focus. Inshallah, we will be able to start and give you some good news in the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Planning small price increases (INR10-15) due to food inflation while maintaining value positioning
items.quote: So we are considering a small price rise, which is now due and because of the fact that there are tremendous headwinds on the inflation, particularly food. If we increase by INR10, INR15, it doesn't change their

items.quote: That whole thing is going to go down because most of our restaurants have been renovated and repair and maintenance will go down drastically, which we have completely that line item. All operating supplies have been done, and it will last us for 5 to 7 y

items.statement: Long-term supplier relationships (30 years) and bulk purchasing helping contain food cost inflation
items.quote: On the food cost also, in spite of the fact that there has been an inflationary trend in the economy, we have -- because of our relationship with our suppliers and the contracts that we have, long-term ones, we've been keeping our suppliers as partners. items.quote: We are not getting into the mass catering of, say, corporate events as of now -- as of yet. We're going to be penetrating the household caterings and smaller wedding functions at the most, post which we would be expanding into corporates and so on and so forth.

items.statement: Using multi-brand strategy (Mainland China, Asia Kitchen, Gong, Bizarre Asia) to capture Asian market share without brand fatigue
items.quote: And one reason for us to be experimenting with this is because the more chain restaurants come in, in a single city, there tends to be brand fatigue. We do want to dominate the Asian space in every location of a city. But we probably think that same brand creates a fatigue. Hence, we want to be a part of the Asian market share of every location with various brands of ours.

items.statement: Evaluated inorganic opportunities but found targets with negative EBITDA/high debt; preferring organic growth
items.quote: Madam, it's been going on for a long, long time, and we would love to because of the fact that -- but unfortunately, the people who are coming to us with their memorandum, unfortunately, they have EBITDA minus to a debt level. I'm sorry t o say this. And somehow or the other, we've done these mistakes. By adding an inorganic part in our body, we are organically here. What do we gain? We will only

items.statement: Bandwidth of trained manpower biggest constraint for faster expansion
items.quote: Because the bandwidth of trained manpower, which has been the biggest challenge. There's so much of cash lying in the balance sheet in the treasury, we would love to expand much faster.

items.statement: Average order value for Mainland China highest in industry; delivery grew from 1-2% pre-pandemic to meaningful share
items.quote: But our average order value for Mainland China is the highest in the industry. And there has been a respectable growth from the fact that we used to do only 1% or 2% of deliveries pre-pandemic.

items.quote: For example, the JFM, OMD being the be st, that's October, November, December. JFM is usually not good because 28 days in the month of February. And you know that this is the time there are examinations and there are a bit of a headwinds which happen in any restaurant business
