items.quote: So they would rather go to a Zomato Gold or an offering coming in from dine -outs of the world. And even if we give them more discount on the -- or more loyalty points as against discounts, this is not working at this point of time. So we 've just parked it. We've got a software ready. We've already interacted with the partner. But currently, we've parked it.

items.statement: Management expects margins to improve by 100-200 basis points going forward through debottlenecking and modernization efforts.
items.quote: we continue to work on improving our efficiencies and believing all these ongoing efforts will help us in improving margins by 100 to 200 basis points going forward.

items.statement: CMD sees potential for margins to reach 12%-12.5% with internal efforts, but 15%+ requires government policy change on cotton pricing anomaly.
items.quote: I can see the margins going up to 12%-12.5% with all the efforts we are doing on our cost rationalization and the other measures. But to really get beyond 15%, I think then this anomaly has to go.

items.statement: Steady-state margin outlook depends on government cotton policy; margins could jump 300-400 bps if policy changes favorably.
items.quote: if it changes in our favor which we expect, then the margins can go up by 300 or 400 points. So, other than that, we expect the margins to stay where Sportking India Limited January 30, 2025 they are, maybe improve by 100 to 200 points by the ongoing effort we are making in debottlenecking and modernization

items.statement: Management evaluating next expansion phase; decision expected in 2-3 months with 1-year execution timeline once announced.
items.quote: I think we'll be able to share the details maybe in the next two to three months. We are right now working hard onto what product and what line of business in textile we want to grow in.

items.statement: Company has sufficient land for brownfield expansion but may pursue greenfield to diversify geographically closer to ports and cotton regions.
items.quote: So, we have enough space for Brownfield expansion, but we might go for Greenfield. So, that is what the evaluation is happening right now because all our plants are in Punjab, so geographically we might like to diversify and get out of Punjab and go closer to the port and closer to the more abundant regions in cotton.

items.statement: Capacity utilization remains above 95%; debottlenecking adding 4-5% capacity without new capex.
items.quote: Capacity utilization remains more than 95%.

items.statement: Modernization and debottlenecking plans increasing capacity by 4-5% without formal capacity expansion.
items.quote: we have implemented some modernization plans, a lot of debottlenecking plans, where we are increasing our capacity by 4% to 5% without really increasing our capacity.

items.statement: Export order book remains strong for current quarter; domestic demand improving after clampdown on Chinese imports.
items.quote: In exports generally we did well this quarter, so we continue to see a good order book in our export orders for this quarter as well.

items.statement: Export demand robust led by Bangladesh; domestic demand uneven due to Chinese synthetic fiber/yarn imports but improving recently.
items.quote: The exports saw an uptick in demand since last quarter, led by an impressive growth in shipments to Bangladesh. Domestic market saw uneven demand buoyed by the festive season, but at the same time restricted to some extent by continued import from China of synthetic fibers and yarn.

items.statement: Bangladesh market growing steadily at 10-15% annually; no near-term export challenges seen.
items.quote: I don't see Bangladesh going down, I see Bangladesh steadily improving from here and keep on growing by 10% to 15% going forward for the next two, three years.

items.statement: Cotton-yarn spread was Rs.95-100/kg in Q3, slightly improved in current quarter.
items.quote: Q3 the spread for cotton and yarn were maybe about Rs.95 to Rs.100 and slightly better right now in this quarter, we see a slight improvement this quarter.

items.statement: Indian cotton prices at 52,500/candy, down from 54,000; still 1,000-1,100 points above international futures vs normal 500-700 point premium.
items.quote: Indian cotton prices have come down even further. So, from 54, we have slip down to around 52,500 now as we speak, and they continue to be under pressure in spite of the huge operation by the CCI.

items.statement: Management expects cotton crop at 340 lakh bales vs CCI estimate of 305-310; prices to remain under pressure for next 6 months.
items.quote: crop is slightly higher than last year. So, we think that last year the crop was around 325. So, we expect the cotton crop to be closer to 340 this year than 305 or 310. So, we see cotton prices continuing to be under pressure going forward for the next six months

items.statement: Company carrying lower cotton inventory than normal due to high domestic prices vs international; procurement ongoing during harvest season.
items.quote: this year, of course, we are still working at slightly lower stocks than what we have generally at this time of the year, because of higher Indian prices as compared to international prices and a lot of stocks which are there with the government which will come into sale post-March.

items.statement: Nine-month yarn mix: 62% 100% cotton, 30% cotton blended, 3-4% 100% synthetic; value-added share stable, targeting 3-4% increase next year.
items.quote: cotton 100% is around you can say around 62% and cotton blended is about 30% and synthetic 100% is about 3% to 4%.

items.statement: Export contribution reached 57% of revenue in Q3 (Rs.341 cr), driven by Bangladesh; export and domestic yarn pricing similar.
items.quote: Share of export in revenue was approximately INR341 crores for the quarter, representing a 57% contribution from export business to revenue for the quarter.

items.statement: RoDTEP scheme valid until Sept 30, 2025, providing ~3% of FOB export value benefit.
items.quote: It is about 3% of FOB prices of our exports.

items.statement: Merger of garment company (Rs.120-130 cr revenue, 10-15k garments/day) and fabric finisher (Rs.70-80 cr) pending NCLT approval; expected effective FY26-27.
items.quote: One is the purely garment company which right now makes around 10,000-15,000 garments a day with the revenue of around 120 - 130 crores. And the other one is that fabric finishing company, which has a revenue of around 70-80 crores.

items.statement: Merger payment structure still under consideration; details to be shared in couple of months.
items.quote: It's still under consideration. So, we are still not ready with the proposal. As I think in a couple of months, as we are ready with the proposal, we'll share the details.

items.statement: Most cotton inventory pre-sold against 2-3 month order book; no inventory gains expected as prices not rising.
items.quote: most of the inventory we are carrying is pre-sold because we generally have a order book of two to three months also. So, there is not major impact on that.

items.statement: Finance cost increase due to Ind AS MTM forex differences (~Rs.5 cr); actual interest cost ~10.5-11%.
items.quote: The finance cost increasing was mainly due to the differences in the exchange fluctuation to the extent it pertains to the saving and interest cost of foreign currency term loan and a rupee term loan as per Ind AS regulations. This is a notional entry. This includes around Rs.5 crores.

items.statement: Government cotton policy (MSP, CCI operations, import duty) keeping domestic prices 3-5% above international parity, pressuring margins.
items.quote: Generally, Indian cotton prices are at 500 to 700 points higher than the near futures which are right now prevailing at about 1,000 to 1,100 points higher. So, there is a clear difference of 3% to 4% or 5% in the international prices and potential Indian prices where they should be.

items.statement: CCI holding 8.5 million bales, may add 2-3 million more; government may sell at lower prices but structural duty/subsidy issue remains long-term challenge.
items.quote: CCI has accumulated a lot this year which are I would say right now they are sitting at about 8.5 million bales, and by the time the procurement season ends, it might go up by another 20, 30 lakhs.

items.statement: Solar SPV at Bathinda to provide ~1/3 of power needs (additional 13-14% on top of current 13-14%), saving ~Rs.20 cr/year; 4-5 MW plant operational next month.
items.quote: I think right now we are at about 13% to 14% and I think it will be another 13%, 14%. So, I think the totality will be one-third of our capacity will be dependent to get from our own solar.

items.statement: No inventory gains foreseen unless black swan event; cotton prices expected to stay under pressure.
items.quote: No, because we don't see prices going up, so there won't be any inventory gains, I don't foresee that. Only if there are some Black Swan events, but as the condition is today, we don't see cotton prices going up to the high.

items.quote: maybe Rs. 5,000 odd crore next year again, that's on the acquisition side, new project acquisition side

items.statement: Targeting 25-30% CAGR in fresh sales for FY26-FY27 and beyond
items.quote: we will have a CAGR of 25% to 30% is what we are trying to achieve here, fluctuations apart and this trend should continue beyond that also

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA margin threshold of ~25% on weighted average basis across vertical, horizontal, JD and outright projects
items.quote: on a weighted average basis everything put together vertical, horizontal, JDs and outright etc., we are working on a margin threshold of around 25% at EBITDA level

items.statement: Industrial park margins expected to be as good as plotted residential projects
items.quote: It will be as good as a plotted residential project. For us it is also broadly contoured and structured the same way

items.statement: Material and labor costs stable within acceptable fluctuations; overall cost model stable
items.quote: Material cost has not really gone up. I mean within a very acceptable level of fluctuations on either side, they have been fairly consistent. Labor cost also is not going up in any significant way

items.quote: During the quarter operating cash flows amounted to Rs. 74 crore and Rs. 277 crore du ring the nine months. We estimate an unrealized operating cash fl ow exceeding Rs. 3,818 crore coming from the current pipeline of pro jects. This is expected to realise within 3-4

items.statement: Export order book described as healthy with growth in major markets; domestic market also showing growth.

items.statement: Q3 revenue grew 23% YoY driven by recovery from prior supply chain issues, new North American clients, and domestic growth.
items.quote: So, as compared to last year because we had supply chain issues in certain places, so we had some loss of revenue, so we were able to recover that and that's why it shows this kind of growth.

items.statement: Management sees export demand projections lower than last year from European customers but not yet experienced; domestic demand sees some auto sector slowdown but overall growth scope remains large.
items.quote: But definitely looking at the projections that the customers have shared, it is lower than previous year in the export market for wherever we are seeing especially the Europeans and others.

items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was Rs.15 crores, a growth of 31% year-over-year with EBITDA margins of 12.91%.

items.statement: CFO states limited scope for margin expansion beyond 15-16% EBITDA due to 60% raw material cost; expects some improvement with scale and efficiency.
items.quote: So, there is hardly much scope. Maybe with increasing the operations, we may see some margin increase, but there is not much scope there.

items.statement: Safety shoe contribution stable; garment segment grew after resolving supply chain issues; both categories carry ~15% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: What we know and figures which we have shared is like the safety shoe contribution remains almost similar what it was last year nine-month period. But definitely we have grown into garment segment.

items.statement: Nitrile gloves face price competition from China; Mallcom competes on quality-to-price ratio and is pursuing backward integration to reduce costs.
items.quote: The ones we are producing, the biggest competition that we face is from China, they're definitely cheaper in those kind of products, but it depends on the quality as well.

items.statement: US market progress: cracked some large white-label accounts; growth is slow and steady with long gestation periods.
items.quote: Yes, our efforts are also going towards it and we have been able to crack some customers from that market and that's why that market is showing good growth for us.

items.statement: Domestic distribution network of 70-75 distributors; export split ~95-97% white label, rest branded in Southeast Asia, Middle East, Africa.
items.quote: In India, there will be around 70, 75 distributors as on today.

items.statement: Global PPE market ~$60bn, 70% served by China; India gaining share slowly but infrastructure and raw material ecosystem limit speed.
items.quote: So, globally, the market is almost probably $60 billion market and there are some couple of billion dollar companies also operating in this market.

items.statement: BIS certification mandatory for some product categories; where implemented, Chinese imports are far lower; no new BIS standards for Mallcom's range in last 3-4 years.
items.quote: So, in the products which there are certification required, the imports are far, far lesser than in products where no certification is mandatory.

items.statement: Europe projections lower than last year; US growing faster off a small base; China+1 driving some enquiries but conversion slow due to scale and supply chain constraints.
items.quote: US, yes, because we are starting from a smaller base also in the US. So, for us it's going faster. Maybe for the entire economy and the larger mass, it's not.

items.statement: No specific working capital metrics discussed; CFO mentions streamlining operations to increase production efficiency.
items.quote: So, we are investing into two things basically, one into marketing efforts and second is to streamline the operations also, to increase production efficiency also.

items.statement: Company awarded Great Place to Work certification and Outlook Business Spotlight Safety Leadership Award during the quarter.
items.quote: I am also happy to report that during the quarter, the Company has been awarded the prestigious Great Place to Work certification as well as the Outlook Business Spotlight Safety Leadership Award.

items.statement: Trump policy impact uncertain; Europe may slow; China+1 opportunity limited by India's capacity and raw material ecosystem readiness.
items.quote: With Trump coming in, it's too early to say because a lot of comments have been made, but not enough actions. So, everybody is vigilant.

items.statement: India mattress business guided to grow 18-19% over next 2-3 years with EBITDA margins around 15%
items.quote: on the mattress side, we would see at least about 18% growth -- 18% to 19% growth in the coming 2 to 3 years' time. And the margins -- so would be about 15-odd percent as far as the B2C segment is concerned, that is the m attress side

items.statement: B2B business guided to grow 8-10% with consolidated EBITDA margins reaching 12-14% in next 3 years
items.quote: But we anticipate broadly an 8% to 10% growth in B2B, with some broad EBITDA margins, which could take the consolidated EBITDA margin somewhere between 12% to 14% in the next 3 years.

items.statement: Price hikes of 3-5% announced for mattress brands effective February
items.quote: On the price si de, we have already announced a price increase in both the mattress brands of Kurlon and Sleepwell and they will come into effect in the month of February at different points of time

items.statement: GNFC TDI plant shutdown caused 1.5 months of emergency spot purchases at premium prices
items.quote: The local supplier of TDI, which is GNFC, had a sudden plant shutdown in October, which resulted around 1.5 months for us in which we had to purchase TDI from open market on an emergency basis

items.statement: Jabalpur plant focused on INR2,000 price point mattresses for economy segment
items.quote: The entire initiative of Tarang and Aaram is for that segment itself. That in fact, the tent foldable mattress can definitely go inside

items.statement: EBOs grown from 5,000 to 6,700; total touchpoints increased to 12,000
items.quote: EBOs have also grown for us from a 5,000-odd number to about 6,700 that's been there. In fact, the total touch points have increased to 12,000.

items.statement: Kurlon acquisition integration in final stages, acquisition accounting to close within FY25
items.quote: the Kurlon acquisition that was done and the integration, which has been going on is now in their final stages, and we are well on our wa y to closing the acquisition accounting, hopefully in -- with -- definitely within this financial year

items.statement: Capex minimal this year, only maintenance capex planned for next year
items.quote: Our capex this year has been very small in comparison to last year, and we have been very strict on capex. Going forward in the next year, we should have almost only maintenance capex and nothing else.

items.statement: Working capital efficiencies delayed due to Kurlon integration, improvements expected
items.quote: On the working capital front, because of the consolidation of Kurlon and Sleepwell, we have not been able till now to build further efficiencies, but we are in the process of doing so.

items.statement: Net debt INR1,100-1,150 crores pre-lease, INR1,400 crores including lease liabilities
items.value: INR1,100-1,150 crores pre-lease, INR1,400 crores with lease
items.quote: Net deb t would be before lease liabilities around INR1,100 crores, INR1,150 crores and including lease liabilities should be around INR1,400 crores at a consolidated level

items.statement: INR100-150 crores expected from monetization of closed Kurlon plant assets in Q4 FY25 and FY26
items.quote: we have a monetizable asset from some of the plants of K urlon, which we have closed down, and that should be somewhere between INR100 crores to INR150 crores. And we expect that to flow down in the last quarter of this year and the next year

items.statement: Basic customs duty on mattress imports reduced from 25% to 20%, impact seen as insignificant
items.quote: One more thing, which is -- which definitely relates to our industry is a reduction of basic custom duty on the import of mattresses. It was earlier at a rate of 25% and now has been brought down to 20%.

items.statement: Spain subsidiary grew 15% volume YoY, value growth muted due to low raw material prices
items.quote: Interplasp, our company in Spain has grown -- in this year, has grown 15% on a volume basis. What we may not see is the same number getting reflected on the top line. And that's primarily because the raw material prices have fallen to

items.statement: Mattress category penetration opportunity: regional brands >50% market, large non-user base (dari/chatai)
items.quote: In the category of mattress, there is a significant opportunity that India as a country still has on account of 2 things that within the modern mattress segment, the local and the regional brands are still more than half of the market.

items.statement: Other income declined due to mark-to-market losses on debt investments as yields rose
items.quote: In the last quarter, the yields on debt has gone up, which has -- instead of a positive impact, which has resulted into a negative impact on the income from other sources. But yes, that's a

items.statement: SIS targets at least 2x GDP growth (~15% CAGR) and aims to return to pre-COVID EBITDA margins of 6%+ in India Security and FM, 4.5% in International.
items.quote: SIS believes that there is opportunity to grow at least 2x GDP in this type of business. And if you see our historical results, we have also, since listing, our CAGR for revenue is more than 15%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 4.7% in Q3 FY25 from 4.4% in Q2 FY25; India Security stable at 5.5%, FM improved to 4.6%, International recovered to 3.8%.
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, the EBITDA grew by 3.6% on a year-on-year basis. Now it's INR 157 crores and that results in EBITDA margin of 4.7% which is up from 4.4% from the previous quarter.

items.statement: Management targets pre-COVID EBITDA margins: India Security and FM at 6%+, International at 4.5%.
items.quote: SIS believes that as a market leader, we have the pricing power to get to pre-COVID level of profitability. Pre-COVID, SIS security businesses in India were at and above 6% EBITDA mark. The FM business also was at and above 6% mark. The international business was 4.5%.

items.statement: Net debt reduced by INR 225 crores to INR 632 crores; net debt-to-EBITDA improved to 1.07x from 1.47x, lowest in 3 years.
items.quote: We're very happy to report that we have significantly reduced our net debt. It's down by INR 225 crores to INR 632 crores net debt, what was INR 857 crores in the previous quarter. This brings the net debt-to-EBITDA ratio down to 1.07 from 1.47.

items.statement: DSOs improved by 4 days to 69 days; OCF to EBITDA conversion at 163% consolidated, but FM lagging due to weaker collections.
items.quote: DSOs have improved by 4 days down to 69 days from last December, highlighting our efficient working capital management and this has reached INR 150 crores of working capital.

items.statement: FM cash conversion expected to improve in Q4 FY25 to match Security segments.
items.quote: But in Q4, we are expecting that there will be improvement, based on the information we have. So, in Q4, you might see a similar kind of OCF to EBITDA percentage for Facility Management also.

items.statement: VProtect quarterly installations at ~1,000 connections, down from ~3,000 earlier in the year; revenue ~INR 100-120 crores with 15-20% EBITDA.
items.quote: Quarterly installations for VProtect, this quarter would be, I'd say, 1,000-odd connections.

items.statement: Cash Logistics business: Q3 FY25 revenue INR 182 crores (+12% YoY), EBITDA margin 17.1%, PAT INR 13 crores; non-ATM revenue now 84% of topline.
items.quote: We're again very happy to report that the business has achieved highest ever quarterly revenue of INR 182 crores which translates to a growth of 12% on a year-on-year basis. Cash business expanded EBITDA by 15.5%, recording 17.1% as the EBITDA margin.

items.statement: IT development expenses (MySIS, SIS Core, SalesMAX) are fully revenue expensed, not capitalized.
items.quote: We don't capitalize these IT expenses. These are all developmental expenses and they are all revenue expensed.

items.statement: Minimum wage increases are pro-rata pass-through without negotiation; pre-COVID avg 8-9% YoY, recent 9 months ~3%.
items.quote: Post-COVID, let's talk about the most recent year, the 9 months of this financial year. The minimum wage increase is closer to 3%.

items.statement: Upcoming labour code implementation may change minimum wage approach; any hike directly impacts revenue.
items.quote: We believe that with the upcoming labour code implementation, which the Government is talking about, there may be change in that approach. Any change in labour code or minimum wage hike will have a direct corresponding impact on the business overall.

items.statement: Cash Logistics JV (49% stake with Prosegur) exploring IPO/listing put option to monetize value and potentially reduce debt.
items.quote: We had an IPO or a listing put option with our joint venture agreement, and we are exploring whether we can use that to, A - monetize our value of our shareholding in that business and number 2 - maybe even consider bringing back some of the proceeds towards further lowering our debt situation.

items.statement: International Security won Sydney Trains contract worth >AUD 30M; expanding in defence segment.
items.quote: There was one win, a customer called ‘Sydney Trains’, which is upwards of AUD 30 million, which is a sizable win for us. And we have also expanded our presence in defenc e segment which will start kicking in not immediately, but maybe a few quarters down the

items.statement: SIS is largest security player in APAC with >20% share in Australia (AU$1.8-2.5B market); Top 5 in NZ and Singapore.
items.quote: Australia is roughly AU$1.8 billion to AU$2.5 billion security market. And our businesses in Australia accounts for almost 20%, 25% of that market. So we have a very strong market position in Australia. We're not just No. 1, we are greater than 20% market share.

items.statement: Branch capacity being scaled 1.3x via IT overhaul: target 1,200-1,300 employees/branch (from 800-900), 100+ accounts (from 40-50), INR 3Cr+ revenue/branch (from sub-INR 2Cr).
items.quote: So the revenue or the number of contracts or the number of employees, we manage through a single branch, we are trying to increase that capacity by 1.3x. So same branch, let's say, ballpark used to handle 800-odd people, 900 people, will be able to manage 1,200, 1,300 people.

items.statement: International margins pressured by tight labor markets (unemployment <3.5% in Australia, NZ, Singapore); recovery dependent on market easing.
items.quote: The labor market started to tighten post-COVID. We've been reporting that every quarter. In that, the unemployment rate continues to remain at record low levels, sub 3.5% and that's what is affecting us at this point in time.

items.statement: No current view on further receivables or goodwill write-offs; reviewed quarterly by audit committee.
items.quote: As of right now, there is no clear view or direction on that matter. Should this discussion come up, should the auditors feel that there is a requirement or the Audit Committee agrees, obviously, we will notify.

items.statement: Management acknowledges share price below IPO despite 2.5x revenue and 3x EBITDA growth; committed to reducing debt, improving return ratios (>15-20%), and disclosing depreciation breakdown quarterly.
items.quote: I am not sure about stock price, that's not in my control. But the point s you have raised are very valid , perception issues around debt, around return ratio, around depreciation. I will answer all these three through actions , and let's see what the stock market

items.statement: India Security Q3 volume growth satisfactory; price growth dependent on minimum wage hikes which have been subdued post-COVID (~3% vs 8-9% pre-COVID).
items.quote: Volume growth, we are reasonably satisfied with. Price growth is directly linked to minimum wage increase that the government determines. That is not in our hand. For the last few years, minimum wage growth in India during COVID and post-COVID has been rather subdued.

items.statement: Rupee denominated bond to Australian subsidiary causes FX fluctuation impact of ~INR 6 crores in PAT.
items.quote: Actually, that RDB loan is sitting in the books of Indian company, parent company SIS. This RDB loan has been taken, I think in 2018. So whenever there is a fluctuation in exchange rate, we account for that in the PAT. So that is also resulting some change in the PAT movement. And the amount is approx. INR 6 crores.

items.statement: International recruitment/retention efforts expanded to address tight labor markets; India branch scaling via technology not headcount.
items.quote: We have expanded our efforts on recruitment and retention and so on. So, while we are working towards getting there, again, there is a bit of market thing as well which we need to look out for.

items.statement: SEBI's new equity derivative framework and standardized exchange charges implemented in December 2024 significantly reduced exchange turnover and caused volume correction.
items.quote: The rollout of the 1st Phase of measures to strengthen equity derivative framework, standardizing exchange charges, regardless of turnover, etc. , this had a sizeable impact on the turnover of the exchange.

items.statement: Management expects regulatory impact to be absorbed in 1-2 quarters, with volumes and margins recovering thereafter.
items.quote: As in the Quarter 2 call, on the SEBI regulations, we already give the guidance that it will take 1 or 2 quarters, maybe to get adaptive to the new regulations once all the regulations are getting adapted. Then, volumes will go up and margins will be better, and things will again be normal.

items.statement: ADTO dropped from Rs 10,400 crore/day in Q2 to Rs 8,200 crore/day in Q3 due to SEBI regulations, increased ELM, and higher STT.
items.quote: ADTO has dropped from Rs. 10,400 crores from Quarter 2 to Rs. 8,200 crores per day in Quarter 3.

items.statement: MTF book grew from Rs 260 crore to Rs 360 crore QoQ; NBFC loan book grew from Rs 195 crore to Rs 250 crore QoQ.
items.quote: MTF book has gone up from Rs. 260 crores to Rs. 360 crores from Quarter 2 to Quarter 3, NBFC loan book has gone up from Rs. 195 crores to Rs. 250 crores from Quarter 2 to Quarter 3.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue declined 24% QoQ to Rs 342 crore; consolidated PAT declined 34% QoQ to Rs 82 crore.
items.quote: During Quarter 3, the Company has consolidated revenue of Rs. 342 crores compared to Rs. 453 crores showing a decline of 24% on quarter-on-quarter basis, consolidated PAT of Rs. 82 crores showing a decline of 34% on quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Board approved PMS license application and AIF creation; wealth management subsidiary (Share India Wealth Multiplier) approved; targeting launch in Q1/Q2 FY26.
items.quote: The Board of Company has approved to venture into wealth management, and we have already applied for PMS registration, and we are in process of creating an AIF.

items.statement: Added 29 new APs and 8,000-10,000 active clients QoQ; servicing 115 institutional clients.
items.quote: We have added 29 new AP s and some branches from Quarter 2 to Quarter 3. We have added active clients around 8,000-10,000 from Quarter 2 to Quarter 3.

items.statement: Completed strategic investment in Metropolitan Stock Exchange (MSEI) at Rs 2/share for ~5% stake; MSEI plans cash market launch in Q1 FY26 and derivatives later.
items.quote: Recently, we completed our investment in Metropolitan Stock Exchange of India at Rs. 2 per share. We are holding approximately 5% of the equity of the exchange.

items.statement: Rights issue funds fully received by September 2024; consolidated net worth ~Rs 2,300 crore as of December, targeting Rs 2,500 crore by year-end.
items.quote: As of December, we have net worth on consolidated basis around Rs. 2,300 crore and by the end of the year possibly will be crossing Rs. 2,500 crores of net worth.

items.statement: Board approved dividend of Rs 0.20 per share.
items.quote: The Board has also given the approval for the dividend of Rs. 0.2

items.statement: Planning to hire senior wealth management team (2-3 key hires) by end of FY25; RM additions for HNI segment; employee cost ~Rs 100 crore/quarter, not expected to jump significantly short-term.
items.quote: In the beginning part of it, as Sachin sir has already explained that both these products will have their own gestation period. So, we don't see too much of initial employees cost just jumping onto the balance sheet into that scope. But yes, we would be able to provide you a clarity as and when the teams are hired and a lot more things are announced in the public domain in terms of numbers, but on

items.statement: UTrade Algos and Silverleaf acquisitions provide in-house tech stack, reducing vendor dependence and time-to-market for retail products.
items.quote: The critical advantage that I want to highlight is that the most of our tech pieces that we have built are not vendor dependent, are completely in-house in nature, which gives us not only flexibility in terms of customization, but reduces our time to market and go to market very significantly.

items.statement: Market share remained stable QoQ despite industry-wide ADTO decline; management expects to outperform industry as market recovers.
items.quote: Our market share has remained more or less stable in comparison to on a quarter-on-quarter basis and the drop is in line with the overall industry. Having said that, we believe we will outperform the industry as a whole.

items.statement: MSEI investment positions Share India to benefit from third exchange launch; SEBI supports scope for third exchange.
items.quote: Even SEBI believes that there is a scope for third exchange and accordingly, they have given certain approvals. Secondly, you know, on the valuation front also, valuation at which we have entered, we have made this investment looks attractive.

items.statement: MTF book growth funded from balance sheet; potential to outsource MTF funding to third-party NBFCs later as distribution partner.
items.quote: MTF is a product that we believe that we can really get about the strength of a balance sheet because it requires funding from our side. And once you know this business grows, we can look at outsourcing this business to third-party NBFC and sort of becoming a distribution partner for them.

items.statement: Targets at least 20% top-line growth in FY26 vs FY25 and aims to maintain console EBITDA margins around 20% and PAT margins 15-16%
items.quote: we are aiming, as I said, for the coming financial year growth of at least about 20% on the top line vis-a-vis t he financial year’24-25 and margins, we are aiming to, aspiring to maintain at the current levels of about 20%-odd on a console basis EBITDA margin and about 15-16% PAT margin

items.statement: For FY25, aims to limit top-line decline to below 10% and PAT decline to around 20% vs FY24
items.quote: we are aiming that the dip in top line should be at least below 10% and the dip in bottom line should be in the range of aiming to be 20% or at least aim below 20%.

items.statement: Order book at all-time high of Rs 8,000 crore, including Rs 2,800 crore consultancy and Rs 3,600 crore turnkey
items.quote: We have got an order book now of about Rs. 8000 crore, which is an all-time high.

items.statement: Q3 order inflow of 110+ orders worth Rs 1,900+ crore, nearly matching full FY24 inflow of Rs 2,200 crore and 3x Q2 inflow
items.quote: this quarter has broken all records. We have got about 110 plus orders totaling to Rs. 1900 plus crore, which is nearly equivalent to the Rs. 2200 crore which we got in the entire previous financial year, and it is about 3x the order inflow of Quarter 2.

items.statement: Export order book of Rs 1,300 crore (Mozambique, Bangladesh, South Africa); targets minimum 40% revenue realization in FY26
items.value: Rs 1,300 crore order book; 40% execution target
items.quote: We have an order book of export of about Rs. 1300 crore, which includes Mozambique, Bangladesh and South Africa. So, these will definitely, as I said, they have a lead time of about 12 to 18 months. So, we foresee these orders start giving us revenue in the next financial year and out of this order book of 1300 crores in Exports, we aim at least a minimum 40% odd to see the revenue realization in

items.statement: Export margins on new competitive global tenders will be substantially lower than historical 20%, blended around 10% EBITDA
items.quote: definitely much, much lower than the 20%-odd and would be in the range of about 10%-odd broadly.

items.statement: Console EBITDA margins ~20% and PAT margins ~15-16% seen as sustainable floor; Q3 margins improved ~1% sequentially
items.quote: the overall EBITDA margins of about 20% on a console basis and PAT margins of about 15-16% on a console basis. To my mind, as I have b een indicating in the last quarter also, this is the bottom of the barrel that we have reached, and we would strive to maintain these levels of EBITDA and PAT margins on a console basis with a blend of the different streams of high and low margin

items.statement: Turnkey revenue from fresh orders to start in Q4 FY25 and Q1 FY26; older railway electrification orders nearing completion caused YOY dip
items.quote: the fresh order inflows in the turnkey segment and overall, in the last quarter and this financial year, whether it is turn key, consultancy or expotech, will start generating definitely revenue Q4 & Q1 onwards

items.statement: Company is low capex and debt-free; intends to maintain this profile
items.quote: We are a low CAPEX company and debt-free company and we would like to maintain this trend.

items.statement: Dividend payout averaging ~95% over first three quarters of FY25, in line with FY24's 95.2%; policy unchanged
items.quote: the dividend payout for Quarter 3 has been about 95% plus averagi ng out, even if you take all the 3 quarters, it has averaged out to about 95% plus, which is in the range of the overall of last financial year, which again was about 95.2%. So, this is the trend that we would definitely like to continue.

items.statement: Export orders have minimal working capital needs; payments phased with milestones and advances received
items.quote: There will be a very minimal working capital requirement and it will keep coming phase-wise based on the total production that happens and that is the basic model. You see, our working capital requirement in all our export orders is not a very substantial amount. It keeps phased out and we get certain advance also from clients.

items.statement: Consultancy client mix flipped: now ~60% non-IR (state govts, renewables, power transmission, oil, GeM) vs ~40% IR, up from 40% non-IR last year
items.quote: last financial year, if you s ee the total revenue was about 60% from IR and about 40% from non-IR, that has flipped now and now we are about 60% on non-IR in this quarter and about 40% in IR as a client.

items.statement: Turnkey orders are primarily consultancy-design and project management, not pure construction; revenue flows through balance sheet
items.quote: Even the turnkey orders which we are getting, are not really a construction company like orders. They are primarily consultancy design orders where the revenue is flowing through our balance sheet. So, we are not really a construction company.

items.statement: REMC (power procurement consultancy) steady at ~Rs 30-35 crore quarterly revenue, ~Rs 19-20 crore PAT; growing with railway electrification and renewable tenders
items.quote: REMC is primarily a consultancy company for power procurement for Indian railways and it has been showing a steady revenue of about Rs. 30 odd crores on every quarter, Rs. 35 crore in fact this quarter. It is showing a good PAT of Rs. 19-20 crores.

items.statement: Large manufacturing capacity for Bangladesh coach order; manufacturing not a constraint once designs approved
items.quote: manufacturing is not going to take much time because we have a huge manufacturing capacity

items.statement: Zimbabwe order not yet in order book; funding via Afrexim Bank still being pursued, no finality reached
items.quote: In terms of Zimbabwe, you asked a question. Well, still it is not part of our ord er book and the funding which is being sourced by them from AFRIEXIM Bank, is still being pursued jointly by the National Railway of Zimbabwe and us, but it is still to reach a finality

items.statement: Quality assurance revenue share dipped on 9M basis due to new orders kicking in, but sequential bottom reached; larger non-IR client base to drive growth
items.quote: the levels of quality assurance revenue contributing to the overall consultancy revenue will now have seen, as I said again, a few quarters back, the bottom of the barrel is only going to increase now in sequential quarters because of the larger order book and larger client base.

items.statement: Aims to secure at least one export order every quarter; pipeline active across Africa, Southeast Asia, Latin America
items.quote: we have maint ained that. The last 4 trailing quarters, we have got an export order in every quarter. There ar e a lot of bids in the pipeline and we will continue to strive to get at least one export order in every

items.statement: Export order sizes vary widely: Rs 40-50 crore up to Rs 300-500 crore; no single median size given
items.quote: The size of these orders, obviously, can vary as you have seen in the Rs. 1300 crore order book. So, they could vary anything from about Rs. 40, Rs. 50 crores to anything about Rs. 200 to Rs. 300 crores or maybe more.

items.statement: Bangladesh coach order (Rs 900 crore) delayed ~6 months; execution to start mid-to-late FY26 after prototype approvals
items.quote: Bangladesh is about a Rs. 900 crore order and there was a few months of slight hit in terms of movement of this order which has resulted in sliding of the execution to the next financial year. We were hopeful that we would be able to execute at least 40 odd coaches by this financial year, but because of those few months, it has slided into the next financial year.

items.statement: Two bulk export orders (Bangladesh coaches, Mozambique locomotives) to be fully booked within maximum 2 financial years
items.quote: these 2 bul k orders, which are their part of the Rs. 1300 crore, will definitely not spill over to more than maximum 2 financial years. That's the max to my assessment

items.statement: MoUs with Etihad Rail and Abu Dhabi Ports in UAE; office opened; exploring IMEC corridor opportunities with shipping ministry
items.quote: we have a MoU w ith Etihad Rail, which is the leading player in rail infra. We tied up last year with Abu Dhabi Ports, which not only has presence in UAE but across Africa and Asia in ports and other infra like economic zones and logistic parts. So, we are working with them. We a re exploring various opportunities and these are early days. So, I am sure that we will, we have already opened an offi

items.statement: Tie-up with global consultancy major yielding orders: safety audit for Rail Coach Factory Kapurthala and Vande Bharat rake inspection
items.quote: that tie-up has already started yielding results and we have got an order from Rail Coach Factory Kapurthala for the safety audit of the electrical systems in the coaches being manufactured and also we have got an order for Vande Bharat Ra kes also, inspection of quality assurance of Vande Bharat Rakes

items.statement: Cash balance ~Rs 609 crore (own); client funds ~Rs 2,600 crore held separately on both sides of balance sheet
items.quote: our cash balance is about 609 crores and the rest we keep as a client fund which is separate. That is a client fund of about 2600 crores which is taken on both side (asset & liability) side in or books.

items.statement: IMEC corridor opportunities huge but early stage; unfair to quantify addressable market now; expects finite orders in FY26
items.quote: See, this is early days of development of this corridor and our engagement with various players in this has already started and it will be unfair to give number right now, but you can appreciate that the opportunities are huge and our presence there and our MoUs in UAE as well as our working already with the various stakeholders on th e Indian side have opened up a huge number of opportunities and

items.statement: Highest ever quarterly order intake of Rs 11,594.3 crores in Q3 FY25, up 838% YoY driven by large HVDC order
items.quote: The Company reported its highest ever quarterly order intake of Rs. 11,594.3 crores for the Quarter 3, with a year-on-year growth of 838% on the back of large HVDC order to transmit renewable energy from Khavda in Gujarat to Nagpur in Maharashtra over a distance of 1,200 kilometers.

items.statement: Record order backlog of Rs 18,994.4 crores as of December 31, 2024 providing revenue visibility for several quarters
items.quote: During the quarter, the Company also recorded its highest ever order backlog of Rs. 18,994.4 crores, providing revenue visibility for several quarters.

items.statement: Operational EBITDA margin of 10.1% in Q3 FY25, achieving double-digit margins earlier than guided
items.quote: Operational EBITDA if you see, for this quarter stood at Rs. 168.9 crores resulting in a double-digit margin of 10.1%.

items.statement: Maintaining double-digit margin guidance for FY25 as already achieved in Q3
items.quote: We have been always speaking on the same lines. As you see, we have already touched the guidance level that we are talking. So, still we guided the same intention.

items.statement: Announced Rs 2,000 crores investment plan over next four to five years for expansions, capacity building and talent attraction

items.statement: Cover glass margins expected to be attractive due to low competition intensity and import substitution; targeting overall SJS margin levels
items.quote: But what I would like to mention here is wherever competition intensity is low, and the parts are imported, there is a natural tendency that margins should be very attractive. So we are moving with that thesis.

items.statement: No warranty recalls reported; customer relationships stable with contract renewals every 3 years
items.quote: We don't have a single warranty recall, customers are infused with us. They understand that not only this part, we could supply some other parts around this part.

items.statement: IME (In-Mould Electronics) prototypes being developed and supplied to OEMs/Tier 1s; expect penetration to increase in India in next 2-3 years
items.quote: we are actively developing IME parts and supplying these concepts to the OEMs or Tier 1’s to then pitch to the final customer. So I think it's a matter of time, but this is new, not just in India, but globally as well. So I think it is a matter of time between the next 2 to 3 years, you would see IME penetration starting to increase in India

items.statement: Peak net leverage reached; expect 4.5x net debt/EBITDA by end FY25 and 3.5x by FY26, potentially faster with asset recycling
items.quote: We remain fairly confident of achieving the 4.5% net debt to EBITDA on a reported basis, end of the current fiscal year and then subsequently because our EBITDA growth is pretty substantial, we expect that to quickly de-accelerate to 3.5 net debt to EBITDA Levels.

items.statement: Net debt target Rs 1,700-1,800 cr over next 2-3 years driven by cash generation and ~Rs 200 cr asset recycling
items.quote: we actually think that it will be closer to Rs. 1,700-Rs. 1,800 crores of nct debt over the next let us say 2-3 years and that will be a factor of really the cash gencrations and asset recycling

items.statement: Same-store RevPAR grew 15% YoY driven by office market expansion and record 77M airline passengers; new supply remains low
items.quote: We witnessed a very strong 15% RevPAR growth for same-store assets. This was a result of continued demand from an expanding office market across our key cities and a record passenger movement of 77 million passengers during the last quarter.

items.statement: Asset EBITDA margin 41.2% (+90 bps YoY); same-store 42.2%; ACIC 39.4% targeting 40%+ in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Asset EBITDA margin stood at 41.2% demonstrating 90 bps year-on-year improvement. ACIC portfolio margin stands now at 39.4% for the quarter, which should move towards 40% or so going forward in Q4 FY25.

items.statement: Upper upscale/upscale inventory to double from ~1,000 to >2,000 rooms via expansions and new hotels (W Hyderabad, Westin Bangalore, Sheraton Hyderabad, Hyatt Pune, Fairfield Chennai, Holiday Inn Express Kolkata/Bangalore)
items.quote: We are changing the whole portfolio construct where the upper upscale and upscale hotel portfolio through various steps will double in inventory from about 1000 current rooms to over 2000 rooms.

items.statement: IT/ITeS contribution declining relatively; diversification into startups, healthcare, biotech, defense, infrastructure, BFSI consulting, manufacturing, smaller companies
items.quote: we have seen IT/ITeS confribution recede, giving way to other sectors, smaller companies, it could be healtheare, it could be biotech, it could be defense, it could be infrastructure, it could be BFSI consulting, manufacturing and also nuch smaller companies

items.statement: Q4 revenue growth expected higher than Q3 but no definitive guidance given; 60 days remaining in quarter
items.quote: We are seeing pretty good business in books, Shubham. But I would like to abstain from giving a very definitive guidance. But I can for sure say that looking at the business on books today and we still have 60 odd more days to go in the current quarter, the total revenue growth docs remain higher than what we have scen for the prior quarter

items.statement: Management expects new businesses to contribute 25% of revenue in 2-3 years, up from 5% currently, with annuity-driven growth
items.quote: we are largely, as we've been saying, working on a 2-to-3-year timeline where from a 95-5 sort of split between the three core businesses and the set of new businesses, we want to move towards a 75-25 sort of diversification

items.statement: Operating margin aspiration is to improve as SaaS/annuity new businesses scale over next 2-3 years
items.quote: these are mostly SaaS or annuity -based businesses, which we are building. So the margin profile is likely to improve with each passing quarter, we start Protean e building up revenue in each of these new lines, and you will see good margins in the next 2 to 3 years

items.statement: Won CKYC Records Registry 2.0 mandate from CERSAI worth INR 161 crores
items.quote: This particular mandate that we've secured from CERSAI, a government of India undertaking is to upgrade the central KYC records registry. Our superior technology solutioning incorporating cutting-edge emerging technologies was instrumental in winning this mandate, a mandate worth INR161 crores

items.statement: CKYC 2.0 revenue recognition: 60-65% in first 18 months, 30-35% over next 3-4 years
items.quote: I think for first 18 months, I think we will book most of the revenue, which is about 60% - 65% and remaining 30% - 35% in the next 3 - 4 years

items.statement: PAN 2.0 RFP bidding deadline extended to February; revenue recognition if won: 60-65% in first 2-3 years, 30-40% thereafter
items.quote: On this PAN 2.0 project, it is a turnkey project where the revenue will be accounted as per IND AS basis efforts and estimates. So in the initial years, it will be larger share of revenue which will be booked in the next 2-3 years and in the later years it will be a smaller share of the revenue as maintenance

items.statement: Tax services revenue grew 3% YoY driven by market share gain from 52.1% to 59.2% despite 22% PAN market decline
items.quote: Tax services business witnessed a growth of 3% year -on-year. And this was primarily driven by substantial increase in the market share. Protean share market share increased from 52.1% in Q 3FY24 to 59.2% in Q3FY25

items.statement: Pension services grew 12% YoY with 3.05 million new subscribers and 600 corporates added; 97% market share maintained
items.quote: Pension Services. We delivered yet another strong quarter with a growth of 12% year-on-year. During the year, almost 3.05 million new subscribers were onboarded. And at the same time, 600 corporates became part of the NPS ecosystem. We continue to maintain our dominant position with a 97% aggregate market share across NPS and APY

items.statement: Identity services degrew 17% YoY due to high base from Aadhaar-PAN linkage and government schemes
items.quote: In terms of identity services, we witnessed a degrowth. This was a degrowth of around 17% year-on-year. But was again largely attributable to high volumes in the previous years, driven by events like Aadhaar-PAN linkage and some broad-based government schemes

items.statement: eSignPro gaining traction with live customers and healthy pipeline; eStamping added to complete BFSI proposition
items.quote: We are very happy to report that we have live customers running with us, and they are contributing monthly volumes. And again, very clearly being annuity, we see this with every month, each set of customers coming in, the last month's customers keep contributing

items.statement: ONDC infrastructure revenue flat due to cost optimization; transactional SaaS revenue expected to grow as buyer/seller apps scale
items.quote: the transactional revenues are kicking in parallelly, and that is where we will see the numbers moving. But this is going to be clearly SaaS and annuity in nature

items.statement: ONDC buyer/seller tech deals in double digits (10-12) currently in integration pipeline
items.quote: Roughly, the numbers as we speak today, we are looking in double digits, around 10, 12 deals which are currently in the process

items.statement: International business engaged with 19 countries, shortlisted in 4-5 bids, Dubai subsidiary established
items.quote: we are currently engaged with more than 19 countries. There are active opportunities, bids have been submitted, and we've been updating the teams earlier also. But we've been shortlisted in around 4 to 5 bids, and we expect movement on that

items.statement: No specific capex guidance; infrastructure built for scale supporting higher ONDC traffic without proportional cost increase
items.quote: the same infrastructure is supp orting higher volumes because it was built up till a certain scale and capacity

items.statement: Cash and equivalents over INR 750 crores with zero debt; employee headcount flat YoY
items.quote: Our balance sheet continues to remain strong with cash and cash equivalent of more than INR 750 crores with zero debt. Employee headcount as on 31st December 24 stood same like as of 31st March 24

items.statement: eSign commoditized pricing pressure continues; vertical integration via eSignPro+eStamping enables premium pricing
items.quote: it is commoditized and therefore, there's always a push to sort of price compression comes in. But that is where, as we were saying earlier, the vertical integration into a full-fledged digital suite like eSignPro, where we've also now incorporated stamping is where you are able to create value-added services, and you can command a premium

items.statement: Core businesses (tax, pension, identity) historically grow 8-10% YoY; PAN penetration ~35%, 6-7 crore annual issuances
items.quote: All three as we've seen have historically grown around 8% to 10% year-on-year

items.statement: PAN 2.0 bid outcome uncertain; if lost, revenue model unclear as core stack redesign may change distribution services
items.quote: See, as I mentioned to you, again, depends on how the project goes into execution, how it works with the ecosystem because today, a large part of our business is around getting the applicants data onto the IT department. The core redesigned project is talking about redesigning the core stack

items.statement: Leadership hirings and increments in last 2-3 quarters increased employee cost; current quarter level seen as run-rate
items.quote: in the last 2-3 quarters we had many leadership hirings and this was the main reason for increase in employee cost additionally we had increments also in the last 1-2 quarters

items.statement: No fund raise mentioned; strong cash position with zero debt
items.quote: Our balance sheet continues to remain strong with cash and cash equivalent of more than INR 750 crores with zero debt

items.statement: Agri Stack has multiple players; PAN 2.0 RFP competitive; eSign commoditized with price pressure
items.quote: On the agri stack, no, there would be multiple players who will be playing

items.statement: International expansion via Dubai subsidiary targeting 19 countries; 4-5 bids shortlisted
items.quote: We've also incidentally launched our -- or set up Protean International, which is our wholly owned subsidiary out of Dubai. And we will be centering our operations over there into multiple countries

items.statement: AI-led automation of calling processes and support functions to improve efficiency and customer experience
items.quote: we're automating the calling processes using AI and bots and working towards more better customer experience in our various deliveries

items.statement: Management confident of achieving double-digit revenue growth for FY25
items.quote: And at the same time, we are very confident on achieving a double-digit growth in the current year.

items.statement: Creative segment growth guidance maintained at 18-20% for FY25
items.quote: And going forward to Creative, of course, the growth will be better and higher because as we are giving the guidance or maintaining the guidance of 18% to 20% growth in Creative.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to return to 19-19.5% in next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: Right. So in the next 2, 3 quarters, we see the numbers going back to 19% -19.5%.

items.statement: Steel Bottles revenue guidance of INR120 crores by FY27 maintained
items.quote: No, we have always maintained that we'll reach the full capacity of INR120 crores, not even INR100 crores in the third year of operations. So by '27, we look at INR120 crores that's the guidance we have been maintaining, and we are reaching there.

items.statement: Creative segment growth target revised to 20% for FY25 from earlier 28-30%
items.quote: But current year, we will be at 20% growth by the year-end.

items.statement: Export growth targeting double digits from next year onwards
items.quote: So yes, from next year on, of course, we are targeting to grow it in double digits.

items.statement: Q4 is strongest quarter driven by exam season and export push
items.quote: upcoming quarter 4 is always our strongest quarter in terms of demand driven by upcoming exam season and our push in the export market.

items.statement: Pen segment Q3 seasonally weak due to holidays and festivities
items.quote: There has always been a seasonality to the demand during the third quarter in terms of school holidays combined with festivities subduing demand for this category as customer spending gets directed to other products.

items.statement: Steel Bottles Q3 sequentially flat due to post-festival lull of 30-40 days
items.quote: So in this category, Q3 is a slow period because most of the buying happens before the festival season. So normally, there is a lull of almost 30 to 40 days.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin at 17.1%, up 176 bps YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margin was at 17.1%. We saw an impressive margin expansion of 176 basis points year -on-year.

items.statement: 9M FY25 gross margin expanded 100 bps to 51.5% due to premium product mix
items.quote: Gross profit margin came in at 51.5%. Gross profit margins expanded by 100 bps.

items.statement: Employee and other expenses elevated due to headcount additions and distribution optimization
items.quote: Internally, a higher headcount and job work outsourcing raised employee costs and other expenses. And additionally, if you see, Aradhana, the actions were also undertaken to optimize distribution network.

items.statement: FY25 capex target around INR100 crores across all three segments with backward integration
items.quote: In FY '25, around, again, INR100 crores of capex is what we are aiming at, I guess, from the PPT. So will it be possible for you to provide us segment -wise, how much have you incurred like towards Pens, towards Creative, towards Steel Bottle?

items.statement: Mechanical pencil production capacity ramping up, full Pan-India launch in 2 months
items.quote: We have launched only in a few states because we are also ramping up the production capacity, which will take about another 2 months.

items.statement: Steel Bottles distribution at 50 distributors in general trade, expanding modern retail and e-com
items.quote: And currently, we have about 50 distributors, city-wise. And the GT traction is also very encouraging, looking at the numbers.

items.statement: Launched 33 new pens in Q3, 29 in mid-premium/premium segments and 4 at INR10 price point
items.quote: During this quarter, we released 33 new pens, of which 29 are targeted to mid -premium and premium segments and 4 new pens launched in newest price category of INR10.

items.statement: Launched 2mm mechanical pencil as wooden pencil substitute with Pastel and Disney branding
items.quote: Notably amongst them has been the launch of our new 2 mm mechanical pencil r ange. It is a substantial substitute to the traditional wooden pencil and comes in a range of Pastel and Disney-branded pencils.

items.statement: Added 3 new steel bottles in Q3, focusing on quality and distribution reach
items.quote: We added 3 new bottles during the quarter to our portfolio and look towards 2 key levers for growth in the business, providing quality and attractive bottles and increasing distribution reach.

items.statement: Strategic partnership with Maped France for premium stationery distribution in India
items.quote: We took another decisive step in the overall development of our creative brand by partnering up with Maped. Maped is a French brand that has been in existence for close to 8 decades. They manufacture quality and premium stationery products and with this partnership, we will leverage our extensive network of distributors and retail touch points to distri bute Maped's products in India.

items.statement: Disney collaboration progressing with 20 branded products across categories
items.quote: The collaboration with Disney is progressing well. We now manufacture and distribute 20 Disney branded products across categories.

items.statement: Domestic OEM business discounted in future projections, focus on own brands
items.quote: So going forward, we have not even -- we are concentrating on our own brands and in domestic market, and we have not even taken into future projections, have discounted the domestic OEM business.

items.statement: Export own brand sales up 33% YoY to INR26 crores in Q3, 17% sequential growth
items.quote: Export owned brand sales increased by 33% on a year -to-year basis to clock INR26 crores. Exports are stronger in the second half of the year for us, and this is further evidenced by 17% sequential rise in exports own brand sales.

items.statement: Freight costs accepted as new normal, now easing off aiding export growth
items.quote: So what we have done in overall, the freight prices remain to be higher, but now that's a new normal and people have accepted it. But now again, it's easing off. So that's an advantage for us.

items.statement: Expect positive working capital impact in Q4 FY25 with new credit policies
items.quote: So you will see the impact in this quarter when you look at the 31st March quarter, we will see a very positive impact here.

items.statement: Employee costs elevated due to hiring across sales, manufacturing, admin and minimum wage increases
items.quote: During the quarter, employee benefit expenses increased by 14.3% on a year -on-year basis and other expenses increased by 8.4% year -on-year, both coming in lower than gross profit rise of 17 % year-on-year as shared above.

items.statement: Average selling price for pens at INR5.7 in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Yes, it's about INR5.7.

items.statement: Industry saw low to modest growth in CY24 (0-10%, industry 4-5%); CY25 expected to be cautious recovery with encouraging outlook from JPM Healthcare Conference
items.quote: Heading into calendar year '25, this seems to be a year of cautious recovery for the industry. Many of you would have tracked the narrative from the biopharma companies in the JPM Healthcare Conference which happens every year in the early part of Jan and this time happened in SFO in mid Jan. The outlook of most of the top 20 pharma and many mid-tier and small biopharma companies is encouraging.

items.statement: All major client renewals due in Q3 renewed with minor variance; net positive renewal rate entering CY25; pipeline stronger than last year
items.quote: All our major client engagements which were due to renew this quarter have been largely renewed with minor variance without anything being out of line and we enter the calendar year '25 with a net positive rate of renewal. Outside of the renewals, if I look at a pipeline compared to last year, it is clearly stronger.

items.statement: Won five key expansion deals with existing and new customers, deal sizes $2-4 million ACV each, going live in coming month or two
items.quote: I would also like to mention that we won five key deals on expansion into new regions, adjacent areas with existing and new customers with deal sizes of 2 million to 4 million ACV each, which will go live in the coming month or two and start contributing revenues in the

items.statement: Top 5 accounts grew 3.1% QoQ; largest customer at run rate tad below $50M; two previously flagged accounts stabilizing; next 15 customers show good expansion opportunities
items.quote: If you see our revenue from top five accounts has grown 3.1% sequentially. We see continued growth in our largest customer and we are doing a run rate of a tad below USD50 million in this account. In the two specific accounts which we had called out issues in the past, we are seeing stabilization of business and revenues.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 20.8%, up 240 bps QoQ; productivity initiatives and automation absorbed July wage hike impact; ex-one-time items margin 20.5%
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the quarter stood at 20.8%, an improvement of 240 basis points sequentially. Continued productivity improvement initiatives through better capacity management and automation helped absorb the impact of the wage bill hike which was effective July and which you saw reflected in our margins in the last quarter and that impact has been negated and we believe this will continue to play o

items.statement: Automation and productivity initiatives expected to continue offsetting wage bill impact; longer term may pass some benefits to customers to stay competitive
items.quote: Wage bill is an offset. In the longer run would also have to pass on some of these benefits to the customers to remain ahead of the curve in the market and be competitive. So that would be the offset but certainly a net positive to our margins.

items.statement: Opened Hyderabad center (~200 people), registered presence in Spain, expanded London office to 1,800 capacity; continuing to grow footprint and capacity
items.quote: We opened a center in Hyderabad in India. We now have close to 200 people in Hyderabad and the vicinity. We registered a presence in Spain and we started the journey of recruiting people based in Spain. Again, in November, we expanded our office in London UK to 1800 people capacity office and we actually already have more than those people given its hybrid working model and so on.

items.statement: Employee count reducing overall but healthcare domain expertise headcount rising; automation reducing non-domain roles; domain experts needed to drive AI automation in regulated areas
items.quote: Over period the need for this skill set has reduced in the delivery function, but use of this technology, given the maturity curve that we see on the domain side, which is medical and pharma specific is likely to take longer. The low hanging fruit I would say in th is example is the code automation versus say something much more complex from a technology maturity perspective, which is the medical

items.statement: US employee count ~500; 83-84% workforce in India, balance in US, Europe, China, Japan
items.quote: US, our employee count is in the region of 500 people. We have about between 83% and 84% of our workforce in India and the balance outside India, US being the largest, followed by Europe and then China and Japan.

items.statement: Actively scouting M&A with good pipeline; targets sub-$50-60M revenue ($2-50M range); focus on omnichannel capabilities, global footprint, business technology (Veeva/Salesforce migration), analytics, regulatory/medical; disciplined on valua
items.value: sub-$50-$60 million revenue all the way from $2 to $50 million type of revenue range
items.quote: What we have right now in the pipeline are I would call all of them being sub-$50-$60 million revenue all the way from $2 to $50 million type of revenue range right now. And we will be always disciplined in what we pay for these kinds of companies.

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents tad above INR 1,500 crores; strong cash position maintained
items.quote: Our cash position remains strong. We now have a tad above INR 1,500 crores in cash and cash equivalents.

items.statement: Subcontracting costs up marginally due to Spain hiring via third-party before registration; will regularize as employees move to payroll
items.quote: The subcontracting cost has gone up a tad bit, but that is also reflective of the growth I mentioned. One of the contributing factors there is we registered our office in Spain, but people that we took on board have been taken on board ahead of when the registration could be concluded through a third-party service provider. And therefore, there is a marginal uptick in the subcontracting costs.

items.statement: Veeva vs Salesforce tug-of-war seen as net positive; platform changes create technology implementation and operating model work opportunities
items.quote: We agree with that thing there is a tug of war between Veeva and Salesforce and from our perspective, actually there could be a net positive, right given this development for us. Because the opportunities play out at two levels. On the technology level, if somebody is changing the platform, then of course there's a lot of technology implementation work which requires your tech capabilities and dom

items.statement: Continued downward pressure on drug pricing expected regardless of US administration; regulatory complexity increasing across clinical trials, manufacturing, safety driving outsourcing
items.quote: The continued push to cut drug prices will exert pressure on the biopharma business model and margins. Both in the US and the rest of the world, government policies, competitive dynamics and the very rapidly evolving technology landscape, we believe will force biopharma to reimagine how they do commercialization and R&D. This will provide a big impetus to digital first commercial services companie

items.statement: Revenue per employee increasing due to hybrid contracts (output-based pricing), automation, GenAI, RPA; productivity initiatives driving margin improvement
items.quote: We typically have hybrid contracts which are not just time and material or FTE contracts but also output based pricing and which enables us to be involved in this in a much more committed manner. And that keeps showing in the increase in output and more importantly an increase in revenue per employee.

items.statement: Enterprise segments (Commercial & Medical) grew 3.7% QoQ driven by mid-sized pharma; Omnichannel Activation & Others grew 11.8% QoQ due to new project kickoffs; omnichannel shifting from short projects to longer enterprise agreements
items.quote: Our enterprise businesses which comprise the Enterprise Commercial Solutions and Enterprise Medical Solutions segments, grew at a healthy rate of 3.7% sequentially and most of this came in from growth in the mid-sized pharma clients which are beyond the top 20 globally ranked pharma as Manish already alluded to. Our other segments, omnichannel activation and others also grew 11.8% sequentially.

items.statement: Omnichannel segment: 6-7 logos generating 70-80% revenue (up from ~55%); engagements lengthening from 6-9 months to 12+ months, converting to enterprise agreements
items.quote: Today we have I would say six to seven logos in omnichannel activation which is getting us give or take a little between 70% to 80% of the revenues in that segment. And if I dial back, this would have been lower in that 55% ish range whic h means that we are getting entrenched more and more with customers with higher value and longer duration engagement

items.statement: Geographic split: North America 69.3%, Europe 27.9% (shift <1% from NA to Europe); >95% revenue from US and EU regions
items.quote: Our geographical split based on location of origination remained in line with the previous quarter. North America revenue came in at 69.3%, Europe revenue at 27.9%, both varying by just under 1% with shift from North America in favor of Europe.

items.statement: Top 20 pharma expansion pursuits progressing slower than anticipated; 2-4 top 20 companies still have weak new product pipelines
items.quote: Our pursuit for large scale expansion with few of our top 10 to 20 customers continue to make progress, though a bit slower than what we originally anticipated. But with the increased momentum in the industry as a whole and these customers in particular, we remain optimistic about closing these pursuits in the next few quarters.

items.statement: No explicit numerical guidance provided; management expects momentum to continue into new calendar year
items.quote: We have had an exciting quarter and we are hopeful that the financial performance and growth that we have delivered is something that we continue from a momentum perspective into the new calendar year as well.

items.statement: Q3 historically quieter due to festival season impact; double-digit growth in production, sales, operating EBITDA YoY but flat QoQ
items.quote: As we move through the fiscal year, it is important to note that the third quarter has historically been a quieter period for us. This trend is primarily driven by the varying levels of impact that the Indian festival season has on all our business divisions, this year has been no exception.

items.statement: FMCG demand slowdown in India seen as opportunity; collaborating with FMCG R&D to develop market-winning fragrances and flavors
items.quote: Despite a slowdown in FMCG demand in India, we view this as an opportunity. Our creative teams in the Fragrance & Flavor division are actively collaborating with R&D and product development teams at FMCG companies to develop market-winning fragrances and flavors.

items.statement: Fine fragrance demand surging due to new launches, social media influence, and shift to daily essential usage from special occasions
items.quote: Fine fragrance has been another key growth driver and continues to be a significant and profitable part of our Fragrance division. The category has seen a surge in demand due to new product launches, social media influence on consumer preferences, and a shift in fragrance usage behavior due to glob al warming

items.statement: Input costs expected to be firm but mild to moderate; watching rupee depreciation, US tariffs, and pricing trends
items.quote: We foresee a firmer output for input costs across our supply chains and business divisions. While we expect these impacts to be mild to moderate for now, we are closely watching key macroe conomics factors, including the depreciation of the Indian rupee, which could have cost implications in the near-term; the recent tariffs imposed by the USA on certain countries, which may influence global trade

items.statement: Input cost pricing relatively stable across board except pinene firming up; no spikes seen like in past
items.quote: But more or less, across the board we are seeing relative amount of stability in pricing on the input costs, except pinene which has firmed up, but not in the form of spikes as we have seen in the past.

items.statement: Successfully defended US FDA certification for camphor during recent audit at Bareilly facility
items.quote: On the regulatory front, we are pleased to inform our investors that we have successfully defended our U.S. FDA certification for camphor during a recent concluded U.S. FDA audit at our Bareilly facility.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA Rs 23 cr, up 60% YoY; EBITDA margin 10.15%, up 301 bps YoY; nine months EBITDA margin 10.86% vs 4.19% YoY
items.quote: In terms of profitability, EBITDA was reported at Rs. 23 crores, which increased by 60% year-on-year. Our EBITDA margin stood at 10.15%, representing a 301 basis points improvement year-on-year.

items.statement: Aspire to achieve normalized EBITDA margins of 10% to 12%; sticking to guidance of under-commit and over-deliver
items.quote: So, that's the overall piece if you look at our journey from 2018 to 2025. And that's why we are now looking more at consolidation, because I think that whole program, which was charted out has now seen the light of the day. And hopefully, as we go and become more mature in all the products, we should see more normalized margins, but we will stick to the guidance of 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Newly commissioned multi-product hydrogenation facility at Vadodara and single product plant at Mahad ramping up month-over-month
items.quote: As highlighted in our earlier investor call, our newly commissioned multi-product hydrogenation facility at Vadodara and a single product plant at Mahad have been ramping up production month-over-month, further strengthening our Specialty Chemicals portfolio.

items.statement: Existing plants running at optimal 80-90% utilization; new plants at Mahad and hydrogenation facility above 50% planned capacity; hydrogenation at 60-70% by end FY25, optimal by end FY26; Mahad at 40-50%
items.quote: So, if you look at our current capacity utilization for plants which are already existing, I think all of them are running at optimal c apacity. When I say optimal, we are looking at anywhere between 80% to 90%. For the plants that have been recently commissioned, which are plants at Mahad and the multi-product hydrogenation facility, those have capacity utilization which is relatively les s. But

items.statement: Hydrogenation facility expected at optimal utilization by end FY26; Mahad plant to reach optimal capacity in 4-6 quarters
items.quote: I think we should, by the end of '25 in the hydrogenation facility we are already seeing utilization between 60% to 70%. And when it comes to by end of FY '26, we should probably be running that plant at optimal levels. And Mahad is less, Mahad is anywhere between say 40% to 50%, because it's recently commissioned. But I am sure we will have substantially higher capacity utilization in the coming

items.statement: New products from commissioned plants accepted by customers in India and globally; customers allocate volumes over 2-3 cycles before substantial allocation
items.quote: In terms of the new products that have been launched, we are glad to info rm you that they have been accepted by customers in India as well as globally. So we are pretty confident assuming that the demand now is more or less stable globally, w e will have volume growth in our current set of products as well as the new products that are being launched in the recently commissioned plants

items.statement: Camphor powder prices currently Rs 450-500/kg vs Rs 380-420/kg same time last year; selling price does not reflect actual production cost due to overcapacity
items.quote: So, I think currently in the current situation, the powd ered camphor prices would range anywhere between Rs. 450 to Rs. 500. And if you looked at the similar time last year, they were at around Rs. 380 to Rs. 420

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity 0.45x as of Dec 31, 2024; depreciation to increase to Rs 7 cr/quarter with full Mahad capex depreciation
