items.statement: Digital Prime Personal Loan launching in Q4 FY25 as industry-first 24/7 zero-touch product for prime salaried
items.quote: We are also ready to launch , and I think this is important, an industry-first 24/7 Digital Prime Personal Loan in Q4 FY24-25. We believe we are paradigm pioneers and industry first. items.statement: AI use-cases going live in credit, risk, collections, digital marketing, compliance, audit, HR by Q4 FY25; customer-facing in FY26
items.quote: The plan is to go live with use cases, rather targeted use cases across credit and risk management, across collections, we've identified digital marketing, compliance, audit and HR by Q4FY25. items.statement: First large-scale NBFC to deploy automated campaign and collection workflow platform with AI-driven micro-strategies over next 2 quarters
items.quote: Secondly, we will be the first large-scale NBFC to deploy an automated campaign and collection workflow platform, enabling sophisticated micro strategies tailored by time, user person a, loan type, communication channel and content. items.statement: DPDP compliance and zero-touch architecture being implemented across digital ecosystem
items.quote: Across board, there is an equal emphasis on resilience, cybersecurity, and ensuring compliance to the fast-approaching DPDP (Digital personal data protection) norms. items.statement: AI governance and monitoring framework in place alongside technology infrastructure
items.quote: Yes, I must confess, we are deeply mindful that AI is not without its risks and in parallel, we're putting across a clear governance and monitoring around it along with a sound technology infrastructure.

items.statement: FY25 R&D spend expected to be less than 7% of sales

items.statement: Emerging markets revenue $277 million, up 10.1% YoY; constant currency growth 14%
items.quote: Our revenue in emerging markets were at US$277 million, up by 10.1% over Q3 last year. The underlying growth in constant currency terms was 14% year-on-year for Q3.

items.statement: Global Specialty sales up 24.8% YoY to $370 million

items.statement: India business predominantly branded generics; trade contribution negligible

items.statement: Net cash of US$3 billion at consolidated level as of Dec 31, 2024

items.quote: Other expenses were at 31.2% of sales, lower year-on-year on account of lower R&D and lower selling and distribution expenses.

items.quote: Generic business, what you are referring to, Novartis, long- listed brands, there is a price pressure. Every year, there is a price decrease ranging from 5% to 7%, depending on the product. So our focus is to continue to grow ILUMYA business.

items.quote: IRDAI regulation on capping of price hikes to 10% for senior citizens, we welcome that regulation because if you look at the principle of insurance, it is to take care of societal need which is there, that's why insurance industry got created.

items.quote: We continue to be focused on data-led decision-making. Significant investments are being made on data and analytics through our direct sales, through upsell and cross-sell initiatives.

items.statement: Both insurance companies among most solvent in industry with solvency in excess of 300%
items.quote: Again, both the insurance companies are among the most solvent in the industry with solvency in excess of 300% for both.

items.statement: No forward-looking guidance given; management does not make forward-looking statements; BALIC growth trajectory expected to recover but no specific numbers provided

items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR127 crores, which is 6% improvement over Q3 F '24. EBITDA margins also improved to 32.4%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA INR 178 cr, up 30% YoY; EBITDA margin 25%, up 450 bps YoY.
items.quote: EBITDA was INR178 crores, which is up 30% and our EBITDA margin is at 25%, which is up 450 basis point versus Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Resort revenue grew 12% YoY to INR 107 cr with occupancy of 84.2% on expanded inventory.
items.quote: overall, I think -- this is a combination of the various resort experiences, finding a lot of favour with our members and also occupancy rate of 84.2%, which we achieved this quarter.

items.quote: our AUR is about INR6.16 lakhs for the quarter which is up 37% Y-o-Y, which is a significant addition compared to last year.

items.quote: We added 3,000 members during the quarter at a net level. Mahindra Holidays & And within this, there are 2 channels, which are doing really well. I think if I look at referrals and digital, they are doing well within

items.statement: Deferred revenue at highest level of INR 5,722 cr; cash position improved to INR 1,482 cr after capex.
items.quote: Deferred revenue is at its highest level right now is INR5,722 crores. And our cash position also improved to INR1,482 crores after making a decent amount of capex investment.

items.statement: Referral channel has highest conversion rate; cost of acquisition similar but conversion better.

items.statement: Non-steel revenue share target of 20-25% in next four to five years from current ~10%
items.quote: Today, the non-steel is about 10%, but our target in the next five years is to take it up to 20%, 25%.

items.statement: Retail EBITDA margin improvement target of at least 1% over next couple of years driven by non-steel mix
items.quote: In a couple of years, definitely we would like that to go by at least 1% at this point.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 steel volume of 2.15 lakh tonnes, up 37% YoY; nine months volume of 5.84 lakh tonnes, up 27% YoY
items.quote: We achieved a significant milestone in our steel segment, recording our highest-ever quarterly sales volume of 2.15 lakh tonnes. This represents a 37% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Non-steel segment Q3 sales of Rs 154 crores, up 19% YoY; nine months up 29% YoY, now >10% of top-line
items.quote: This quarter, we achieved record sales of Rs. 154 crores in this segment, reflecting a 19% year-on-year growth in Q3, and even higher 29% growth in nine months FY '25.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 blended EBITDA margin 2.84% vs 3.42% in Q3 FY24, flat vs Q2 FY25; nine months inventory losses ~Rs 22 crores
items.quote: Despite our best efforts to operate efficiently in the face of such headwinds, our EBITDA margins for the quarter stood at 2.84%, lower compared to 3.42% in Q3 FY '24 and relatively flat compared to Q2 of FY '25.

items.statement: Blended steel realizations down ~6% in Q2 and further ~3% in Q3, ~10% decline year-to-date limiting top-line growth by 8-10%
items.period: Q2 FY25, Q3 FY25, nine months FY25
items.quote: We experienced a blended 6% decrease in realizations in Q2, followed by a further 3% reduction in Q3, resulting in an approximate total decline of approximately 10% in steel prices year-to-date.

items.statement: Creditor acceptances reduced from Rs 460 crores to Rs 400 crores in Q3; working capital days improved from 36 to 33, target 30 days
items.quote: For the creditors, for acceptance, it's around Rs. 400 crores. So, comparing with the last quarter, around Rs. 460 crores, we have reduced around Rs. 60 crores.

items.statement: Group debt ~Rs 500 crores at Q3 end; cost of debt ~9-9.5%; aim to hold absolute interest cost stable despite growth
items.quote: Our group level debt as on quarter end Q3, it is around Rs. 500 crores.

items.statement: Dealer financing program initiated to reduce on-balance-sheet debt; tangible debt reduction expected from Q1 FY26
items.quote: We could see some reduction hopefully in this quarter itself and definitely tangible results from Q1 next year.

items.statement: Manufacturing capacity expansion focus post-demerger to improve efficiencies and ROCE
items.quote: So, our first aim right now is to try and improve capacities. That is what we are working at and trying to focus with the much more focused management bandwidth internally.

items.statement: Demerger EGM scheduled for February 12; expect completion by H1 FY26 subject to NCLT bench availability
items.quote: We have scheduled a shareholder Extraordinary General Meeting, EGM, on Febru ary 12th, to vote on the demerger proposals. Subject to the results of this meeting and subsequent regulatory processes, we anticipate completing the entire demerger process by H1 FY '26

items.statement: Fotia own brand expanded to Quartz Sinks and Adhesives beyond tiles; geographical footprint expanding from Kerala to Bangalore
items.quote: we have expanded its p roduct range to include Quartz Sinks and Adhesives, beyond the initial offering of tiles. We have started expanding the geographical footprint of Fotia after the initial launch in Kerala, and we have a limited presence in Bangalore

items.statement: Maharashtra emerged as significant win in West/Central India non-retail-first expansion; flats volume up 37% YoY in nine months
items.quote: I am pleased to report that the growth of these new markets has been impressive, with Maharashtra emerging as a significant win for Shankara beyond our traditional southern states.

items.statement: Steel price volatility remains key risk; inventory losses of Rs 22 crores in nine months; Q4 currently stable but dependent on global cycle
items.quote: It is currently stable.

items.statement: 126 operational fulfillment centers including stores; omnichannel marketplace model serving all customer categories
items.quote: Our extensive market presence through 126 operational fulfillment centers, including our stores, ensures we are visible and accessible in our chosen markets.

items.statement: No dividend or buyback mentioned; focus on debt reduction and demerger to unlock value
items.quote: We remain committed to creating value for our shareholder and look forward to your continued support.

items.statement: Upper limit for net debt-to-EBITDA is 2.5x, including current CAPEX and any further inorganic growth.
items.quote: Our overall cap is 2.5x net debt-to-EBITDA. This would include not only current CAPEX but also any further inorganic growth or whatever else we may do, including on and off-balance sheet debt.

items.statement: Rs. 500-600 crore CAPEX over next 3-4 months towards brownfield expansions.
items.quote: Now other than that, we are looking at Rs. 500-600 crore over the next 3-4 months of CAPEX towards the brownfields and then thereafter.

items.statement: Medical equipment investment for Thane and Mohali built-to-suit projects is Rs. 150-200 crore, back-ended to last 3-6 months before commissioning.
items.quote: Essentially, it's going to be medical equipment, which will be let's say about Rs. 150-200 crores. But that only happens at the end when it's constructed – the last 3-6 months or whatever.

items.statement: 128 beds at Max Lucknow: 64 commissioned in Jan 2025, balance 64 in Feb 2025; awaiting approval for 13th-17th floors adding 140 beds.
items.quote: 128 beds at Max Lucknow – 64 beds have been commissioned in January 2025, and the balance 64 beds will be added in February 2025. Further, we are awaiting in -principal approval for the existing 13 th to 17th floors for hospital use, which will add another 140 beds almost immediately

items.statement: 127 beds at Max Nagpur: 12 added in Oct 2024; environmental clearance expected by Mar 2025, completion 24 months thereafter.
items.quote: 127 beds at Max Nagpur – 12 beds have been added in October 2024. For the balance beds on additional floors, we are expecting the environmental clearance (EC) to come by March 2025. Project completion should take another 24 months thereafter.

items.statement: 268 beds at Nanavati Phase 1: interior fit-out in progress, completion expected in 3-4 months.
items.quote: 268 beds at Nanavati in Phase 1 – Interior fit -out work s are in progress currently. The project continues to be on schedule and we expect completion within the next 3 to 4

items.statement: 400 beds at Max Smart (Saket Complex): structural work mostly complete, on track for completion in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: 400 beds at Max Smart (Saket Complex) – Majority of the structural work is complete. The project is on track and we expect its completion within Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: 155 beds at Mohali: interior work in progress, completion expected by Q1 FY26.
items.quote: 155 beds at Moha li – Interior work is in progress and we expect its completion again by Q1 FY '26

items.statement: 500 beds at Sector-56 Gurgaon: structural work in progress, first phase of 300 beds by end of Q3 FY26.
items.quote: 500 beds at Sector-56 Gurgaon – Structural work is in progress. We expect completion of the first phase of 300 beds by the end of Q3 FY '26.

items.statement: 367 beds at Patparganj: environmental clearance received, tendering in progress, largely on schedule.
items.quote: 367 beds at Patparganj – Post receipt of environmental clearance (EC), tendering work is in progress currently. This project is largely on schedule.

items.statement: 550 beds at Max Vikrant (Saket Complex): forest approval delayed due to Supreme Court proceedings on tree felling for past 6 months; all other approvals in place.
items.quote: 550 beds at Max Vikrant (Saket Complex) – Forest approval is delayed due to Supreme Court proceedings in relation to tree felling involving DD A and the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi for the past 6 months. They have not permitted anybody to remove any trees in Delhi, but we think that this should get fairly resolved soon. All other statutory approvals are in

items.statement: 400 beds at Zirakpur, Mohali: fire NOC received, project completion expected within 30 months.
items.quote: 400 beds at Zirakpur, M ohali – No objection certificate (NOC) from fire department has been received. Project is expected to be completed within 30 months

items.statement: Thane built-to-suit 500-bed hospital approved, expected commissioning in 2028 (3-3.5 years including permissions).
items.quote: Our Board has accorded its approval to enter into an asset -light ‘built-to-suit’ agreement for a 500 -bed hospital at a prime location in Thane , to be set up by the partner as per our specifications on a built -up area of appr oximately 6 lakh square feet. The hospital is expected to be commissioned in 2028

items.statement: Mohali (Zirakpur) built-to-suit capacity enhanced to 400 beds from 250 beds previously planned.
items.quote: The Board has also provided its approval for enhancing the capacity of our upcoming asset-light ‘built-to-suit’ hospital in Mohali (Zirakpur) to 400 beds from 250 beds planned previously.

items.statement: Network operating EBITDA margin 27.3% in Q3 FY25; Existing Units improved margin by 70 bps to 28.6%.
items.quote: Network operating EBITDA margins stood at 27.3% for the quarter. Existing Units improved their EBITDA margin by 70 basis points to 28.6%.

items.statement: Asset-light model EBITDA margin (pre-Ind AS) expected to be 5-6% lower than mature hospital margin of 29-30%.
items.quote: It should depend on what the maturity of the hospital is, but I think it should be lesser by 5-6%.

items.statement: Insurance price hikes occur on rolling basis every two years at 12-13% (approx 6% annual medical inflation); no impact from IRDAI senior citizen premium cap.
items.quote: The price change on insurance every two years is about 12-13% at best. So, that comes to a medical inflation of about 6% per year effectively, at best, 5.5-6% a year.

items.statement: Q3 occupancy healthy even during Diwali (typically weak); occupied bed days grew 36% YoY and 8% QoQ.
items.quote: Occupancy level s in the Diwali month made a lot of difference. Typically, the occupancies do drop, but this time it did not happen. It is also because of the fact that Diwali was at the very end of the month, which also helped in a way

items.statement: Oncology mix 25%+ network-wide; new hospitals lower (Dwarka ~12%, Lucknow ~10-11%); Lucknow bunker expected operational by July to boost oncology.
items.quote: In the new hospitals , it should be increasing considerably in fa ct. In Lucknow, for example, the new bunker is yet to get ready and is expected to be operational by July. Thereafter, oncology revenue should increase

items.statement: International patient revenue Rs. 201 crore, up 28% YoY and 8% QoQ despite Bangladesh/Yemen footfall contraction.
items.quote: The international patient revenue stood at Rs. 201 crores, registering a growth of 28% year-on-year and 8% quarter-on-quarter, despite contraction in patient footfalls from Bangladesh and Yemen due to political unrest.

items.statement: Free cash flow from operations Rs. 303 crore in Q3 FY25; Rs. 1,025 crore in 9M FY25 after interest, tax, working capital changes and routine CAPEX.
items.quote: Overall free cash flow from operations was Rs. 303 crores. During the quarter, Rs. 362 crore was deployed towards ongoing capacity expansion projects and upgradation of facilities at acquired hospitals, while Rs. 146 crore was distributed as dividend and Rs. 1,716 crore (net of cash at Jaypee Healthcare Limited) was used for Jaypee acquisition.

items.statement: Jaypee Healthcare became wholly-owned subsidiary in Q3; reported gross revenue Rs. 112 crore, operating EBITDA Rs. 23 crore at 21% margin.
items.value: Rs. 112 crore revenue, Rs. 23 crore EBITDA
items.quote: Jaypee Healthcare Limited became a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company during the quarter. Jaypee Noida is presently being integrated into our Network and reported a gross revenue of Rs. 112 crores with an operating EBITDA of Rs. 23 crores at a margin of 21% in the third quarter.

items.statement: Rs. 146 crore distributed as dividend in Q3 FY25 and 9M FY25.
items.quote: Rs. 146 crore was distributed as dividend and Rs. 1,716 crore (net of cash at Jaypee Healthcare Limited) was used for Jaypee acquisition.

items.statement: Network ARPOB Rs. 75,900 (flat YoY/QoQ); Like-for-like Existing Units ARPOB grew 7% YoY and 3% QoQ.
items.quote: Average revenue per occupied bed (ARPOB) for the quarter stood at Rs. 75,900, remaining relatively flat both year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter. Like-for-like ARPOB for Existing Units, however, grew by 7% year-on-year and 3% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Network occupancy 75% vs 73% YoY; occupied bed days grew 36% YoY and 8% QoQ.
items.quote: Our average occupancy for the Network stood at 75% versus 73% in Q3 last year and 79% in the trailing quarter, while the occupied bed days (OBDs) grew by 36% year-on-year and 8% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Annualized EBITDA per bed Rs. 73 lakhs network; Like-for-like Existing Units Rs. 82.6 lakhs, up 9% YoY.
items.quote: Annualized EBITDA per bed for the network stood at Rs. 73 lakhs. Like-for-like EBITDA per bed for Existing Units stood at Rs. 82.6 lakhs, reflecting a growth of 9% year-on-year.

items.statement: Max Vikrant (Saket) 550-bed project forest approval delayed 6 months due to Supreme Court proceedings on tree felling; resolution expected soon.
items.quote: Forest approval is delayed due to Supreme Court proceedings in relation to tree felling involving DD A and the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi for the past 6 months. They have not permitted anybody to remove any trees in Delhi, but we think that this should get fairly resolved soon

items.statement: Expect 300 net store additions in FY25
items.quote: We expect a total of 300 net store additions in the current financial year.

items.statement: Target at least 600 net store additions in FY26
items.quote: No, I think it will be at least 600 stores for -- I don't think it will be less than 600 stores.

items.statement: Private label share to grow ~1% per quarter on MRP basis
items.quote: So think about the private label as going up by roughly around 1% every quarter on the volume basis, which is on MRP basis, which means additional margin of roughly around 15 to 20 basis points maximum per quarter.

items.statement: Pharmacy GMV growth expected at inflation plus, in line with pharma market
items.quote: So it should be the usual listing of inflation plus kind of thing or it should be in line with the typical pharma market growth out there.

items.statement: Store-level EBITDA margin target 10-11% for mature stores
items.quote: For us, it is more important that we maintain the store-level EBITDA of 10% or 11% rather than just trying for same-store sales growth and all.

items.statement: Normalized SSSG expected at 4-5% steady state
items.quote: 4% to 5% is what we are looking at, actually. That is a number at least we can be at a steady state as far as the profitability is concerned.

items.statement: Net 60 stores added in Q3 FY25; 205 net additions YTD; network at 4,612 stores, 2.4M sq ft
items.quote: Taking into account both openings and closures, we achieved a net addition of 60 stores during the quarter, compared to the 108 stores added in quarter 2 and 37 stores in quarter 1, totaling 205 stores on YTD basis.

items.statement: Store-level EBITDA margin 11% for stores >12 months; 11.3% for >24 months; 8% for 13-24 months
items.quote: While stores greater than 12 months had a margin of 11%, this was 11.3% for stores greater than 24 months and 8% for stores in the 13- to 24-month age bracket.

items.statement: Private label mix drove ~60 bps gross margin improvement; non-pharma private label ~20 bps; lower inventory provision ~60 bps
items.quote: In terms of the movement, I would say around 60 basis points came in because of our increase in the private label Pharma share mix. 20 basis points came in because of the non-Pharma private label share mix. And due to lower inventory provision, we had a 60 basis positive impact during the current quarter.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu minimum wage hike 28% and new warehouse costs offset gross margin gains at EBITDA level
items.quote: For example, in Tamil Nadu, the minimum wages increased by 28%. This has also eaten away some portion of our store-level EBITDA. And we also set up, as we had explained earlier, certain warehouses, which has costed us some amount of money.

items.statement: Private label advertised at 50-80% discount; average discount ~50-51%; not expected to reduce significantly
items.quote: Okay. About our private label discount itself, we advertise a 50% to 80% discount based on the molecule. And I think the average discount tough comes out to around 50%, 51%, that's all, because most of the higher selling drugs are all around the 50% discount.

items.statement: Private label coverage at ~68% of medicines; target 75-77% excluding insulin (10%) and patented (5%)
items.quote: We are today, for the overall set of medicines, we probably are there at roughly around 68%. I expect insulins, which cover around 10% of the overall medicine sale, and some branded products will be another 5%, so which means that leaves at least around 85% to be targeted. I expect, if not 85%, it will probably take the 68% to maybe 75% to 77% or so.

items.statement: Diagnostics revenue INR 274.7M in Q3 FY25 vs INR 196M YoY; operating EBITDA INR 22.1M (8.1%) vs loss YoY
items.quote: Diagnostics grew -- revenue grew to INR 274.7 million in quarter 3 compared to INR 196 million in quarter 3 of the last year. Diagnostics segment recorded an operating EBITDA of INR 22.1 million, representing 8.1% compared to a loss of INR 34.1 million in quarter 3 last year.

items.statement: Net working capital 61 days in Q3; warehouse inventory 36 days; first-year store inventory 88 days; mature store inventory 40 days
items.quote: Our net working capital for Q3 was 61 days. The inventory in our warehouse was 36 days. In Q3, the inventory level of our first year stores was 88 days. In comparison for our stores older than 12 months, the inventory was 40 days.

items.statement: Quick commerce not seen as margin drag if delivery fee charged; 2-hour delivery already in dense urban areas; no plan for 10-20 min free delivery
items.quote: As long as the customer is willing to pay the delivery fee, I don't think there will be a drag at all. If the delivery were to be 100% free, today we charge around INR 20. If we shift to a 0 delivery fee and also try to kill ourselves by doing a 10-minute delivery, then, yes, it would be a drag.

items.statement: Store breakeven: 55% of Jan-Jun 2024 cohort broke even within 6 months; cohort overall breakeven in 6 months
items.quote: For stores opened between January 2024 and June 2024, approximately 55% of them achieved breakeven within 6 months of operations. As a cohort, all stores combined reached breakeven in 6 months.

items.statement: Store-level operating ROCE 61.7% for stores >12 months
items.quote: The store level operating ROCE of these stores stood at 61.7%.

items.statement: Diagnostics active plans 152k, underlying lives 315k as of Dec 31; on-time renewal rate 26% in Q3 vs 25% in Q2
items.quote: As on 31st of December, we had 152,000 active plans and 315,000 underlying lives. Our current observed on-time renewal rate was 26% in Q3 versus 25% in Q2.

items.statement: Super-fast store growth may have compromised supply chain; new warehouses aim to fix
items.quote: Possibly, some of the stuff which we're doing on the warehousing and everything else will add a little bit of efficiency and all. Possibly that our super quick addition of stores may have compromised the supply chain a little bit.

items.statement: Seasonal holiday effect cited for sequential GMV decline; no other structural reason identified
items.quote: A little bit of effect of seasonality, holiday season and everything else. And honestly, I can't think of any other reason out there.

items.statement: Private label chronic vs acute split mirrors branded: 60-70% chronic; top 10 molecules include 6 chronic, 4 acute
items.quote: The private label share of chronic versus acute is exactly the same as it is for the regular brands. So I think 60% to 70% of our sales are private label comes from the chronic segment.

items.statement: Guidance to open 70-80 branches per full year
items.quote: the guidance remains the same, we will be opening close to 70, 80 branches in a full year.

items.statement: AUM growth guidance of 25% year-on-year maintained
items.quote: we have grown our AUM to 11,178 crores, which is 25.4% year -on-year. This is as per our guidance in the last quarter.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance maintained at 75-100 basis points
items.quote: our guidance to you on the credi t cost is typically that the business model of Five Star can take a credit cost or will have to operate at a credit cost of around 75 to 100 basis points and I think we continue to maintain that same view

items.statement: Collection efficiency dipped marginally in Oct-Nov due to festivals and rains; December and January improved
items.quote: The entire NBFC sector or banking sector face some kind of collections drop in October and November, predominantly to the festival, weather, rainfall across South. So, that was through. December picked up very well and it is continuing in January.

items.statement: NIM compressed to 16.56% from 16.8% YoY due to 15-20 bps yield drop on incremental loans and higher borrowings
items.quote: Our NIM dropped from 16.8% in Q3 of last financial year to about 16.5 6%. This is primarily on account of the drop in yields and some increase in our borrowings.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio at 34.87% including credit cost; guided to maintain 35-36% range
items.quote: The cost-to-income remains robust, so we are at about less than 35%, 34.87% to be precise for this quarter as against 34.42% in December of last year. So, as we have been guiding, we are maintaining our numbers and we will continue to operate at around the 35% to 36% kind of cost -to-income.

items.statement: AUM grew 25.4% YoY to Rs 11,178 crore; active loan base 4.4 lakh (+22% YoY)
items.quote: Next, taking you to the AUM, we have grown our AUM to 11,178 crores, which is 25.4% year -on-year. This is as per our guidance in the last quarter.

items.statement: Added 69 branches in Q3 (41 split, 28 new); total branches 729 (+249 in 12 months)
items.quote: we have opened 69 branches in the last quarter. Within that, 44 was split branch. We have already explained to the market what a split means for Five Star, derisking the loans and derisking the stance. So, out of 69, 41 was split branch and 28 was new branch

items.statement: Gross NPA (IRAC) rose 15 bps QoQ to 1.62%; unique collection efficiency 97%, general 98% (flat QoQ)
items.quote: Gross NPA, as per IRAC, gross NPA increased from 1.47% in September quarter to 1.62% in December quarter, with an increase of 15 bps. I think this is one of the best asset quality which you would have ever encountered in small ticket lenders.

items.statement: 30+ DPD increased 70 bps QoQ; management expects stabilization in Q4 with denominator effect and seasonal improvement
items.quote: while there is a little bit of an inch up in our 30 -plus numbers which has increased by about 70 basis points on QoQ basis, we believe that , given the times , I think t hese are extremely good numbers that the Company has managed to achieve, and from here onwards, it should hopefully look better because Q4 typically tends to be a very good quarter for every financial institution.

items.statement: Write-offs of Rs 36 crore in 9M FY25; gross NPA including write-backs would be 1.93%
items.quote: in last nine months, we have written down 36 crores of assets. Even if you add back this 36 crores to the gross NPA, I am happy to say we are less than 2%, which is 1.93% is our gross NPA if you write back the write-off of 36 crores to the gross NPA

items.statement: Stage-3 provision coverage maintained above 50%; overall provision coverage flat at 1.66% of AUM
items.quote: On Stage-3, we continue to maintain over 50% provision coverage. There has been a little bit of drop in Stage-3 and Stage-2. But this is compensated at an overall level. The drop is primarily on account of some overlays we have created on the restructured portfolio

items.statement: Credit cost for Q3 at 0.69% (below guided 0.75-1% range); no significant increase expected in Q4
items.quote: And of course, the credit cost as we guided was 0.75% to 1%, our credit cost for this quarter is 0.69%.

items.statement: Incremental borrowing cost flat at 9.56% in Q3 vs 9.57% in Q2; average cost of funds down 2 bps to 9.63%
items.quote: our incremental borrowing cost in the tight liquidity environment also was one of the best, our incremental borrowing cost was 9.56% in December quarter versus 9.57% in September quarter.

items.statement: Bank borrowing share reduced from 70% to 65%; 35% from capital markets and developmental institutions; 46 lenders
items.quote: our reliance on banks - as we had guided you in the past, we are trying to diversify our borrowing base. So, our reliance on banks has actually come down from 70% to 65%, with 35% of our borrowings coming in from capital markets, from developmental institutions, both domestic and international

items.statement: Received sanctions of Rs 1,400 crore, drew Rs 1,045 crore; liquidity buffer Rs 2,145 crore plus Rs 600 crore unavailed lines
items.quote: during the quarter, we received sanctions of about 1,400 crores drawing about 1,045 crores. And as of December, our liquidity buffer stood at about 2,145 crores and without including unavailed sanction lines of about 600 crores.

items.statement: No adverse RBI action; regulator shared inputs on growth and lending rates; company proactively cut growth guidance and yields
items.quote: First of all, let me categorically clarify, there have been no problems highlighted by RBI. So, it is just that they keep giving some inputs be it on the growth side, be it on the lending rates and all that, and their perspective of how the environment is shaping up

items.statement: MFIN guardrails from April may boost demand for secured loans; no material stress expected on Five Star's portfolio
items.quote: if the guard rails stuck in April onwards, that will create a good demand for middle and lower middle class customers to come to Five Star. That is most positive way, but we have to wait and see whether they are going to implement in April or they are going to further delay it going forward.

items.statement: Overleveraged portfolio (bureau scrub) shows similar collection efficiency and bucketing as overall portfolio; no higher stress observed
items.quote: even on the overleverage portfolio, our unique customer collection efficiency and the portfolio bucketing is almost completely similar to what we are seeing on the overall portfolio. So, it is not like we are seeing any kind of higher stress or elevated stress on this overleveraged portfolio.

items.statement: Average ticket size Rs 3.5 lakh; NPA book of Rs 180 crore spread across 6,000+ customers (~Rs 3 lakh avg); SARFAESI not applicable for most
items.quote: Five Star's average ticket size is 3.5 lakhs. We have to keep this in mind. As Srikanth said, whatever the historical write-off what we have done in last 20 -years is 180 or NPA at 180 crores which comes from 6,000 customers which is around 3 lakhs.

items.statement: ~6,000 relationship officers (4,500 business, 1,300-1,400 collection); additional collection support deployed in stressed pockets
items.quote: today the number of relationship officers we had was about 6,000 people. This is broadly broken up into 4,500, 4,600 business officers and about 1,300 to 1,400 collection officers.

items.statement: ROA 8.10%, ROE 18.49% in Q3; profit Rs 274 crore (+26% YoY); net worth crossed Rs 6,000 crore
items.quote: With all above aspects, our profitability was very good. We are able to generate 274 crores of profit in three months, which is 26% growth year-on-year. And to end up, we had a healthy ROA of 8.10% and a very healthy ROE of 18.49%.

items.statement: Static pool peak NPA at 33-36 months around 2.5% of disbursement; write-off policy after 4 years NPA but conservative practice at ~2 years
items.quote: typically the NPAs peak around 33 to 36 months and in today's scenario it is anywhere around 2.5% or thereabouts.

items.statement: Overleverage from unsecured loans (not just MFI) driving 30+ DPD rise; focus on arresting forward flows, not rollbacks
items.quote: This is seen across. We would like to blame it more on overleverage, which cannot be restricted only to MFI. So, in some scenarios we have seen that the overleverage has happened because of unsecured personal loans as well.

items.statement: BT-out rate low at 2-3%; average borrower credit score ~500; prepayment penalty only within first year
items.quote: Today, BT out will be more around 2% to 3%. Yes. So, it's not a very significant number. It's not like there are too many players who are willing to acquire these customers because it's also not an easy customer segment to serve.

items.statement: Dividend policy to be announced upon reaching a milestone; no inorganic moves planned for next two quarters
items.quote: Yes, as and when we reach a milestone, definitely, we wanted to share that, we are waiting for that, you will hear the good news very soon.

items.statement: Target to double portfolio to 6 GW in couple of years and reach 10 GW in 3-4 years
items.quote: As per the business targets, which I already mentioned in my opening remarks, in a couple of years, our target is to double it to 6 gigawatt. And within 3 to 4 years, we need to achieve a portfolio of 10 gigawatts.

items.statement: Wind O&M portfolio at 3.5 GW end of Q3 FY25 with 96.2% machine availability
items.quote: At the end of the quarter, Inox Green's wind O&M portfolio stood around 3.5 gigawatt, machine availability for the entire portfolio for Q3 FY '25 was at 96.2 percentage.

items.statement: Organic portfolio growth to ~7.2 GW by FY27 with 300-400 MW in Q4 FY25, 1.2 GW in FY26, 2 GW in FY27
items.quote: So as we are at a 3.5 gigawatt by December, we will commission near to about 300-400 megawatt in quarter 4. So broadly by FY '25, and we will be 4 gigawatt portfolio plus minus 100 megawatt, 200 megawatt here and there, then we will get commissioned 1200 megawatts in subsequent year and then 2 gigawatts. So organically, our portfolio will increase to somewhere around 7.2 gigawatts.

items.statement: Targeting 2-3 GW inorganic acquisition via NCLT route over next 12-18 months
items.quote: Inorganically, as Mr. Akhil has mentioned that we have already -- we are in advanced stages of Acquisition -we are planning to acquire one company in NCLT . We are evaluating the other proposals as well. So putting together, we are very hopeful that around 2 to 3 gigawatts when we acquire in next 12 to 18 months.

items.statement: Already invested in debt of large NCLT company; COC controlled by Inox Green; completion expected in 6-9 months
items.quote: As you are aware, we have recently participated in one of the large companies in India. And that company also will be folded in our fleet as and when the NCLT process gets complete. Today the COC is directly controlled by us.

items.statement: INR300 cr deployed from fundraise; another INR200-250 cr to be deployed in 2-3 months for acquisitions
items.quote: We have utilized close to INR300 crores as on date. We intend to utilize another INR200, INR250 over the period of next 2 to 3 months.

items.statement: Total fundraise INR1,050 cr; INR550-560 cr received; INR300 cr used for acquisition, INR70-80 cr for debt reduction
items.quote: No, I think the total was INR1,050 crores, as you would remember. And that’s obviously, we have received. Manish, correct me if I'm wrong. INR550-odd crores already in the company. The ba lance are callable money. And as and when required, it could all be infused. Out of INR560 crores I mentioned to you, approximately INR300 crores is being used for the acquisition, another INR70 crores, INR80 cro

items.statement: Resco demerger awaiting BSE/NSE approvals in first half of February; NCLT process 6-9 months; completion targeted within calendar year
items.quote: We are awaiting the regulatory approvals the BSE, NSE approvals are likely to be available to us in the first week to 15 days of February. Once the regulatory approval comes in, the demerger will be done through NCLT and that would take, say, another 6 to 9 months as the case may be. We are hopeful that within this calendar year we will have the demerger of the business.

items.statement: Post-demerger, depreciation removed; EBITDA to translate directly to PAT/PBT; asset-light balance sheet
items.quote: So when you're looking into the next year's balance sheet of Inox Green, it would be an asset-light balance sheet. And it would also have no depreciation charges as a continued item. What it means is that our profitability will be far more stronger.

items.statement: Inox Green shareholders to receive Resco shares; minority shareholders get 10% of consolidated entity (20% of Resco)
items.quote: So the minority shareholder of Inox Green will get 10% in the consolidated entity. So currently, 50% is owned by the minority shareholders in Inox Green, so if we take our math accordingly, then the 20% shares of the Resco will be owned by the Inox Green shareholders, so 10% by the minority and 10% by the promoters accordingly.

items.statement: Accumulated tax losses of INR700 cr to remain with Inox Green post-demerger
items.quote: INR700 odd crores is the tax losses, which the company carries.

items.statement: Solar/hybrid O&M entry expected FY26; margins lower than wind but higher than industry due to synergies; wind to remain majority for 2-3 years
items.quote: Basically, the execution on solar is expected in the next FY. So as soon as the time line of 8 to 9 months, the project commissioning, so it will be taken over by Inox Green. So the financial will be reflecting post that.

items.statement: Non-comprehensive O&M contracts realize INR3-3.5 lakh/MW vs INR8 lakh/MW for comprehensive
items.quote: Out of 3.5 gigawatts of portfolio, there are certain comprehensive O&M contracts and some are non-comprehensive O&M contracts. Though the EBITDA margin will remain the same in terms of the per megawatt basis. But the revenue realization on a non-comprehensive O&M contract would be somewhere around 3 to 3.5 lakhs, which translated to this difference.

items.statement: 9-month revenue INR167 cr annualizes to ~INR240 cr; 3.5 GW portfolio at INR8 lakh/MW implies INR280 cr potential
items.quote: Looking at the 9 months number, which is INR167 crores, we are looking at that level. And obviously, the 3.3 gigawatts that we have done. As many of them has come during this year also. So obviously, they are not a true reflection of the full year from operations.

items.statement: NCLT acquisition process lengthy; requires patience, legal due diligence, and perseverance
items.quote: I think it's a patient game, #1. You have to understand the legality of each and every asset. So to that extent, there is a fair amount of hard work in the, I would say, the core cost that one has to endeavor.

items.statement: Commissioning-to-O&M gap 6-12 months; revenue starts after commissioning
items.quote: The gap between the supplies and commissioning, you can take anywhere between 6 to 12. S.K. Mathusudhana: Yes, yes, maximum

items.statement: Customers 'married' to Inox Green for 25+ years due to ownership of substations, land, EHV lines
items.quote: Customers are only owning the WTGs and they are kind of married to us for a long period of time, like more than 25 years until the life of the WTGs.

items.statement: Wind O&M complexity (OEM ownership of substations, land, connectivity) creates barrier to entry; peers cannot match 50% EBITDA margins
items.quote: First of all, first of all, we are an Indian OEM with a strong presence, and we own the substation, we develop the substation land connectivity, and we also install the wind turbines, right? As Inox green, we are operating substations, lines connectivity -- sorry, the EHV lines and turbines, okay? items.statement: Drone technology deployed for substation/EHV line inspection and turbine blade cleaning; improves efficiency and safety
items.quote: Recently, we have successfully deployed drone technology for our inspection of substations, 33 kV and EHV line for early defect identification reification and improving the reliability of the system. This has improved our efficiency, turning -- reducing the turnaround time for the cleaning process and cu tting down the unsafe manpower wo

items.statement: Management expects to operate at similar levels as the last 9 months in the near term.
items.quote: As of now, we believe that we'll operate more or less at the same levels where we are -- we have closed this current 9 months.

items.statement: Demand remains sluggish for the last two years; export inquiries have started coming in since December.
items.quote: We are seeing -- we are receiving inquiries, which were earlier like in the month of December, which was not at all there. We have started getting those inquiries, and we are waiting for it to get converted into orders.

items.statement: Gross margins improved slightly from 31% to 32.5% quarter-on-quarter; absolute gross margin stable at INR 94-95 crores.
items.quote: If you look at our gross margins, they have only gone up from 31% to almost 32.5% compared to the previous quarter, if you are comparing with that.

items.statement: Fabric revenue share increased from 6.5% in FY24 to 7.8% in 9M FY25; export share rose from 15% to 18%.
items.quote: Our share of the revenue from fabric increased from 6.5% in FY '24 to now 7.8%. Similarly, our share of exports increased from 15% in FY '24 to 18% now.

items.statement: Total committed capex over INR 1,000 crores; INR 350 crores already deployed; INR 215 crores for 25,000 spindles by June 2025; INR 38 crores for 40 knitting machines by December 2025.
items.quote: We are committed to investment of over INR1,000 crores, of which INR350 crores have already been deployed. The addition of 25,000 new spindles is progressing as per schedule with operations expected to commence by June 2025. We have undertaken a new project to set up 40 knitting machines in our existing location at a capex of INR38 crores.

items.statement: Cotton prices supported by CCI purchases and expected to remain stable; yarn prices range-bound.
items.quote: With the arrival of new cotton crop, domestic cotton prices have been supported by aggressive purchase from CCI. Yarn prices have mostly remained range bound, and it is expected that the cotton prices will remain stable.

items.statement: 70% of energy from renewable sources; power cost competitive and protected from increases.
items.quote: Almost 70% of our energy comes from the renewable base. And there is -- because of this, our power cost has remained very, very competitive, and that has really helped GHCL maintain its margins.

items.statement: Released INR 84 crores of working capital in 9M FY25.
items.quote: There was a release of working capital to the tune of INR84 crores.

items.statement: Net cash surplus of INR 25 crores; repaid INR 61 crores debt in 9M FY25; target debt-equity ratio below 0.5:1.
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains robust with a net cash surplus of INR25 crores. During 9-month period, we generated INR80 crores of cash inflows, which was utilized towards INR75 crores as growth capex, INR61 crores as debt repayment and INR5 crores as a dividend payment.

items.statement: Future capex to be funded by internal accruals and bank finance; maintain debt-equity within 0.5:1.
items.quote: Going forward, our plan is to have -- to use both internal accruals as well as bank financing. And we'll maintain and we are confident because we are virtually a zero debt company as of now, rather there is a cash surplus on the balance sheet. So both from the internal accruals plus bank finance, we'll be able to finance this capex. But we'll remain very much within those declared boundaries of de

items.statement: Plant operating at optimal utilization (~99%) despite demand headwinds.
items.quote: this tougher period of last 2 years. And that is precisely the reason that despite such headwinds, we have been able to operate at closer to full capacity utilization. And as you know, that some of the steps which we took like our customer serviceability, our customer focus, our journey from a commodity yarn to a value- added yarn, utilization of 99% and our focus on renewable energy

items.statement: Longest period of sluggish yarn demand in two decades; recovery timing uncertain.
items.quote: See, the demand still remains sluggish. So -- and this is probably the longest period of sluggishness in yarn market that we are seeing, almost now 2 years. And even now, the market remains a little subdued, as I have mentioned in my opening remarks, then this is the longest period.

items.statement: Aiming for mid-teens revenue growth for the next couple of years
items.quote: Going ahead, our company is aiming for mid-teens revenue growth for the next couple of years, driven by the expansion of new store locations across both new and established markets, depending upon a rebound in the industry demand for premium and mid-premium brands.

items.statement: Expecting high single-digit revenue growth for FY25
items.quote: We already mentioned that we would grow in high single-digit growth.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance range of 27% to 30% for FY26
items.quote: EBITDA should be in the range of 27% to 30%, Ruchita.

items.statement: Plan to open 20-25 stores in FY26, with potential for 40-50 depending on market conditions
items.quote: Ruchita, we intend to even now this year, open about 20, 25 stores, and we will be ready to open even 40 or 50 depending on how the market pans out.

items.statement: Opened 27 gross new stores and 10 net new stores in 9M FY25, total store count 435
items.quote: Till December, we have opened 27 new stores on a gross basis, 10 new stores on a net basis, taking our total count to 435 stores across 243 cities in India.

items.statement: Expect to open 18-20 net new stores in FY25
items.quote: By the end of the year, I think we are confident that we should be able to open between -- at a gross level -- I mean, net level, sorry, about 18 to 20 stores.

items.statement: Store refurbishment and launch can be completed within 30 days
items.quote: And typically, a store, once we get it, depending on store to store, but we can refurbish the store and get it up and running within 30 days without any problem.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 210 bps to 61.9% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Additionally, our performance led to an expansion in gross margins by 210 basis points, reaching 61.9% for this quarter.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 230 bps to 30.6% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: for the Q3 FY '25 stood at INR47.6 crores, that is a growth of 12% year-on-year. Our EBITDA margin stood at 30.6%, which is an increase of 230 basis points

items.statement: Subdued demand for premium and mid-premium branded apparel due to reduced discretionary spending and weaker consumer sentiment
items.quote: Despite facing challenges such as subdued demand for premium and mid-premium branded apparel, primarily driven by reduced discretionary spending and weaker consumer sentiment, impacting overall industry consumption.

items.statement: Expect consumption to improve with recent tax reductions for middle class
items.quote: Additionally, we expect consumption to improve with the recent boost given by tax reductions.

items.statement: Inventory days reduced from 77 in March 2024 to 66 in December 2024
items.quote: Our proactive efforts to efficiently manage inventory have contributed to this performance with inventory days being reduced from 77 in March 2024 to 66 days in Dec 2024, demonstrating our capability to optimize working capital without compromising on growth.

items.statement: No further reduction in inventory days expected; current level considered healthy and to be maintained
items.quote: We are not expecting further reductions in the inventory days. We are at a very healthy level of inventory as of now.

items.statement: Net debt to equity at negative 0.13x as of 9M FY25
items.quote: Our net debt to equity stands at negative 0.13x.

items.statement: Company has been dividend-paying for last 10-12 years and will continue
items.quote: We are more a stable com pany. We have been a dividend- paying company for the last 10, 12 years and shall continue to do so

items.statement: No buyback plans currently
items.quote: We haven't thought about it for the moment, Jaimin.

items.statement: Constant premiumization in product mix ongoing
items.quote: However, there is a constant premiumization that's happening in the brand in terms of the product mix, et cetera, which is a constant work in progress and -- something that keeps going on.

items.statement: No price hike in last year; future hikes depend on raw material costs and inflation
items.quote: Could be a slight level of price hike. There hasn't been any price hike in the last year. But depending on the raw material costs and inflation, et cetera, price hike is a function of that.

items.statement: Digital business turnover grew to INR8.64 crores in 9M FY25 from INR3.62 crores in 9M FY24
items.quote: We successfully achieved a business turnover of INR8.64 crores in the first 9 months of FY '25, a significant improvement compared to INR3.62 crores recorded during the same period in FY '24.

items.statement: Positioned as bridge between mass and premium; among top 3 brands in mid-premium to premium menswear per Technopak report
items.quote: As per the Technopak report released just before we had got listed, we are among the top 3 brands in the country. I'll refrain from naming them. It's there in the report.

items.statement: Value fashion brands not a threat due to unique product differentiation and brand tribe
items.quote: And we can very confidently say that the type of variety and the type of fashion that we have in our brand is very unique, and you will not find it in any other brand at that price point, the type of unique expressive fashion that we make and we stand for, and we have a following of a tribe.

items.statement: Budget tax reductions for middle class expected to boost discretionary spending and benefit sector
items.quote: In the recently announced budget, a key focus has been placed on stimulating economic growth by enhancing the purchasing power of the middle class. One of the significant measures introduced to achieve this objective is the reduction in tax rates aimed at providing financial relief to middle-income households.

items.statement: ROCE 20.4% and ROE 19.9% for 9M FY25
items.quote: ROCE and ROE stood at 20.4% and 19.9%, respectively.

items.statement: Growth dependent on market demand rebound; wait-and-watch approach on store expansion
items.quote: We are certainly going to keep our eye on what's happening in the market, Apurva. And we are hoping for a good rebound in the market, thanks to the tax reductions that the gover nment has proposed in the hands of the middle class. And it will be a wait -and-watch

items.statement: Long-term aspiration to double business in 5 years, timeline may vary by a year
items.quote: See internally double in the 5-year period. However, depending on market, it could take a year less or a year more to achieve that.

items.statement: No plans to enter value segment or launch women/kids categories in next 2-3 years

The outlook of most of the top 20 pharma and many mid-tier and small biopharma companies is encouraging.

items.statement: All major client renewals due in Q3 largely renewed with minor variance; net positive renewal rate entering CY25; pipeline stronger vs last year
items.quote: All our major client engagements which were due to renew this quarter have been largely renewed with minor variance without anything being out of line and we enter the calendar year '25 with a net positive rate of renewal. Outside of the renewals, if I look at a pipeline compared to last year, it is clearly stronger.

items.statement: Won five key expansion deals with existing and new customers, deal sizes $2-4 million ACV each, going live in coming month or two
items.quote: Other than the regular renewals and conversion of pipeline in the quarter gone by, I would also like to mention that we won five key deals on expansion into new regions, adjacent areas with existing and new customers with deal sizes of 2 million to 4 million ACV each, which will go live in the coming month or two and start contributing revenues in the upcomi ng quarters

items.statement: Top 5 accounts revenue grew 3.1% QoQ; largest account at run rate tad below $50M; two previously flagged accounts stabilizing; next 15 customers show good expansion opportunities
items.quote: If you see our revenue from top five accounts has grown 3.1% sequentially. We see continued growth in our largest customer and we are doing a run rate of a tad below USD50 million in this account. In the two specific accounts which we had called out issues in the past, we are seeing stabilization of business and revenues.

items.statement: Active clients grew from 68 to 75; $1M+ clients grew from 37 to 38; >95% revenue from US and EU
items.quote: Total number of active clients grew from 68 to 75 and the USD1 million clients grew from 37 to 38 in Q3. More than 95% of our revenues continues to come from the US and EU regions.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 20.8%, up 240 bps QoQ; productivity improvements and automation absorbed July wage hike impact; ex-one-offs margin 20.5%
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the quarter stood at 20.8%, an improvement of 240 basis points sequentially. items.quote: PAT for the quarter stood at INR1,097 million, an improvement of 19.6% sequentially and the PAT margins came in at 15.2%, an improvement of 190 basis points sequentially. This is largely in line with the growth of our EBITDA.

items.statement: Opened Hyderabad center (~200 people), registered presence in Spain, expanded London office to 1,800 capacity
items.quote: We opened a center in Hyderabad in India. We now have close to 200 people in Hyderabad and the vicinity. Again, in November, we expanded our office in London UK to 1800 people capacity office and we actually already have more than those people given its hybrid working model and so on.

items.quote: The r egulatory complexity continues to increase across clinical trials, manufacturing and safety, putting increased pressure on in house regulatory teams and driving greater outsourcing as well as adoption of technology. items.quote: Our geographical split based on location of origination remained in line with the previous quarter. North America revenue came in at 69.3%, Europe revenue at 27.9%, both varying by just under 1% with shift from North America in favor of Europe.

items.quote: Our enterprise businesses which comprise the Enterprise Commercial Solutions and Enterprise Medical Solutions segments, grew at a healthy rate of 3.7% sequentially and most of this came in from growth in the mid-sized pharma clients which are beyond the top 20 globally ranked pharma as Manish already alluded to. items.statement: No explicit numerical guidance given; management hopeful momentum continues into new calendar year
items.quote: We have had an exciting quarter and we are hopeful that the financial performance and growth that we have delivered is something that we continue from a momentum perspective into the new calendar year as well.

items.quote: Having consistently achieved market++ (plus-plus) growth over the years, we expect to continue performing at the same level moving forward, along with demonstrating strong operating leverage, achieving expanding profitability.

items.statement: UniReco commercial launch expected by end of Q1 FY26.
items.quote: We remain on track for a commercial launch by the end of Quarter 1 FY26, and this will further enhance our position as a comprehensive e-commerce enablement platform.

items.quote: See, we mentioned in the earlier earnings call as well that our steady-state price continues to be in the range of Rs. 1.2 to Rs. 1.3 per item for Uniware, our flagship platform.

items.statement: Overall e-commerce market growing early to mid single digits this year.
items.quote: And this year, we see that the overall market is growing in early to mid single digits.

items.statement: NRR continues to be more than 100%.
items.quote: In spite of the overall muted growth in the e-commerce market, we still continue to demonstrate a 100% plus NRR.

items.statement: Overall e-commerce volumes remain muted.
items.quote: So, we continue to see the overall e-commerce volumes to be muted and that's why our endeavor is to have a one-stop shop for e-commerce businesses across three platforms which is Convertway, Uniware and Shipway so that increasingly more and more businesses can opt for services that are available under a single umbrella and we continue to drive adoption across the ecosystem.

items.statement: Shipway annual run rate ranges between INR 70 to 80 crore.
items.quote: Yes, that ranges between INR 70 to Rs. 80 crore of annual run rate.

items.statement: Aim to make Shipway PAT positive very soon.

items.quote: Reversal INR 22 million is the number.

items.statement: Average revenue per shipment INR 70 to 80.

items.statement: Aluminum frame facility of 36,000 metric tons per annum to meet captive needs.
items.quote: Our aluminum frame manufacturing business with a 36,000 metric ton per annum facility to meet our full captive needs and to increase our share of total value addition and profitable margin.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin improved to 29.97% in Q3 FY25 from 17.30% in Q3 FY24.

items.statement: Prices are stable, no significant change quarter on quarter.

items.statement: Rooftop market expected to touch 9 to 10 GW over next 1 to 2 years.
items.quote: So we do expect the rooftop market alone in India to touch about 9 to 10 gigawatts over the next 1 to 2 years.

items.statement: India module demand expected to grow 15-20% year-on-year over next 3-5 years.
items.quote: We expect that number to grow by about 15% to 20% year-on-year over the next three to five years.

And they are currently underway or kind of finishing. And there is a pretty positive trend that we are seeing among all these three bookings which will play out for us in FY26

items.statement: Retail store expansion is a ~36-month journey; ~12-13 months in, another 20-24 months to reach threshold store levels, calibrated to environment.
items.quote: If you see we have been really below threshold levels on stores. So, we are just in the middle of it. We'll take maybe it's another it's an overall 36-month journey for us. I would say we are maybe 12, 13 months into it. It would take another couple of years, I think really to get the journey get completed

items.statement: Garmenting capacity expansion underway; once complete, company expects to become third largest suit maker worldwide.
items.quote: We are currently expanding our capacity, a move that will significantly bolster our g lobal standing. Once this expansion is complete, we expect to become the third largest suit maker worldwide, paving the way for further growth and customer

With this, we will be entering the core Innerwear category and this will be a new range which is made with trendy design and very differentiated new age

items.quote: The net working capital stands at 89 days which is INR1 ,553 crores in December '24 versus 97 days INR1 ,692 crores in September '24. This decrease is mainly due to reduction in trade receivables and good inventory control

items.statement: Company is net debt-free with net cash of INR 61 crore as of Q3 FY25.
items.quote: On the balance sheet front, we have reclaimed our net debt free position with a net cash of INR61 crores as of Q3 FY25

items.quote: The rentals residing in interest is close to around INR20 crores

items.statement: Consciously deferred 1-2% annual price increases in branded textile due to weak market sentiment; will resume if economy improves.
items.quote: We also have the ability to take and we do tend to take 1% to 2% price increases every year in a branded textile segment. This time because of the weak market we started a year back, we have taken a conscious choice not to do that price increase because the market sentiment has been tough

items.statement: Higher freight costs due to Red Sea crisis impacted garmenting margins in Q3 FY25.
items.quote: higher freight costs on account of the Red Sea crisis

items.statement: Ethnix by Raymond expected to cross INR 100 crore revenue this year, proving concept after 2 years.
items.quote: Ethnics is a brand which has been 2 years into the making right now. We are going to be crossing 100 odd crores threshold level this year on Ethnics

items.statement: Urban discretionary spending under pressure from high food inflation; wedding season staggered over 100-120 days, not concentrated.
items.quote: there is definitely some counter effect which is happening in the market of this urban discretionary spend, which may have played its role in wedding not being as bullish in terms of spend as it would have otherwise

items.statement: Incremental blue-collar manpower training costs incurred due to garmenting capacity expansion.
items.quote: incremental cost of blue -collar manpower training as a result of capacity expansion

items.statement: 1.4 GW Mono PERC cell lines to start commercial operations in 10-15 days; 4 GW TOPCon lines by April-May 2025
items.quote: As far as 1.4 gigawatt cell line is concerned, it's a matter of days. I would say anywhere between the next 10 to 15 days or even earlier than that. We will have our COD declared. As far as 4 gigawatts of TopCON line is concerned, we will, like I said in my opening commentary, anywhere between April and March, we should be in a position to start commercial operations.

items.statement: Odisha PLI facility for ingots, cells, wafers on track for 2027 operations
items.quote: The Odisha facility, the PLI facility is very much on track. We have talked about 2027 of operation and we continue to be optimistic that we will start at that point in time.

items.statement: Order book stands at 26.5 GW (~INR 50,000 crore) as of yesterday, 54% overseas and 46% India

This also includes order from our subsidiary, WRTL, which is a separately listed entity under Waaree Energies Limited. This order book is well diversified between India and international markets, with 54% overseas and 46% from India

items.statement: Order book execution timeline spans up to 2 years
items.quote: You're absolutely right. It has got orders, all the way from now to the gestation period of two years.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin 22.84% vs 19.28% for 9M FY25; margin expansion driven by input cost decline, order mix optimization, retail focus, supply chain diversification, and productivity gains
items.quote: EBITDA for Q3 FY '25 stood at INR809 crores, a significant growth of 257 % year-on-year basis, and a margin of 22.84%.

items.quote: So currently, the cell price is anywhere between four, I would say, $0.4. That's the average which is currently running. That's for the India market. And of course, for the US market, it is higher.

items.quote: India is on the track to become a dominant force in solar energy, with a larger growth rate, where in 2024, we are at 98 gigawatts overall solar capacity, and in 2030, we are going to be at 280 gigawatts.

items.statement: US solar market at 30-35 GW currently, targeting 100-220 GW by 2030
items.quote: So US market on an overall basis is I would say somewhere around 30-35GW right now. And we have climbed to about 100 gigawatts to 220 gigawatts by 2030.

items.quote: In India, MNRE has provided clear direction by applying Approved List Of Models And Manufacturers, in short, ALMM, to solar modules, which will be extended to solar cells by June 2026. Anti-dumping duty applied to various parts of the value chain will also help in Atmanirbhar Bharat.

items.statement: US IRA policy uncertainty; business structured to be profitable without IRA benefits
items.quote: Our objective is to create operations that can thrive independently without being dependent on external factors. Our U.S. operations are structured to be profitable on their own merit. That being said, if IRA or similar program continue in some form, it wi ll undoubtedly provide significant additional benefit to the business

items.quote: Our revenue mix for the last quarter was 79% from India and 21% from international markets, which reflects differences in the project timeline between regions. items.quote: Whilst visa was a fairly large issue, I would say maybe a quarter ago. At this point in time, those issues are significantly alleviated. I'm not saying they are completely gone. items.statement: 9M FY25 volume growth 48% YoY

I think most of the additions of whatever cel l capacities have been talked about now sort of add up to in the region of somewhere around 40 to 50 odd gigawatts

If at all we get into that.

items.quote: So broadly, directionally, we'll be using about 30% of our internal approvals to fund some of the newer businesses. But, we will potentially be taking decisions on the funding portfolio a little later. And we have a bit of an NDA restriction, honestly speaking, because of which we may not be in a position to talk about this in the details.

items.quote: We are not giving out an outlook for FY'26 as of now, but definitely I will point you towards our investor deck and if you can see there, that the volume has jumped 48% versus last year. So, that is an important metric to note.

items.statement: Nine months FY25 revenue exceeded full year FY24 revenue; Q4 FY25 revenue is upside.
items.quote: In the nine months FY25, we have exceeded the full year FY'24 revenue. So, whatever we do in Q4 is now upside.

items.statement: Payments business achieved industry-leading gross margin of 19% in nine months FY25.
items.quote: I am quite delighted that we have achieved this GMV and revenue growth with an industry-leading gross margin of 19%.

items.statement: Adding approximately 5 million users per quarter and 1-1.5 lakh merchants per quarter.
items.quote: We are adding healthily five million users every quarter, approximately 20 million every year. On the merchant side, we are adding about 1 to 1.5 lakh merchants every quarter.

items.statement: Payments contributed 73% of nine months FY25 revenue (~555 crores), up from 30% in FY24; financial services contributed 346 crores, higher than full year FY24.
items.quote: The beauty of our platform business is, interestingly in FY25 nine months, 73% of the revenue, that is about 555 crores has come from the payments business and in the full year of financial year '24, it was actually quite opposite, where 70% of the revenue had come from distribution of financial products.

items.statement: Financial services take rate guided at 5-6% ballpark on secular basis; Q3 take rate higher due to base effect and mix shift to larger ticket loans.

items.statement: ZIP EMI gross take rate ~11%; net contribution margin 4-5% after 5% FLDG cost and 2% underwriting/collection/marketing costs.
items.quote: On the ZIP EMI product, our gross take rate is around 11%. And against that, we have credit cost, we have underwriting cost, we have collection cost, we have marketing cost. So, you add all these costs, so we make roughly 4% to 5% as a net.

items.statement: Lending-related expenses at ~9% of revenue in Q3 (vs 3-4% historically), subsuming expected delinquencies; higher due to lower revenue base.
items.quote: Now, if you see that expense is more in the 9% ballpark. This expense is a combination of the credit cost as well as other cost, direct cost relating to lending such as underwriting, collection, etc., to some extent and therefore this subsume the expected delinquency in our portfolio.

items.statement: All RBI licenses (PPI Wallet, BBPS, PAPG via Zeak) and IRDA/SEBI licenses current with no adverse action; DLG contracts up to 5% loss guarantee now active post RBI FAQs in summer 2024.

items.quote: The capital is not MobiKwlk February 04, 2025 yet deployed per se. But specifically, the capital raise in the IPO is not yet deployed

items.statement: Fixed costs held constant at 111-115 crores QoQ; will continue to optimize and not increase fixed costs.
items.quote: On a QoQ basis, if you see the fixed costs has MobiKwlk February 04, 2025 actually held constant in the 111, 115 crores sort of ballpark zip code. And I think going forward we will continue to synergize and optimize on cost, definitely not increase it

items.quote: MobiKwik is now the First Fintech to do a Full-Scale Production Launch of India's CBDC Project with the blessings of RBI and in partnership with YES Bank.

items.statement: Roughly 40% of lending portfolio now under FLDG contracts; all new contracts moving to FLDG model.
items.quote: If I look at it as a percentage of my overall portfolio, then roughly a shade under 40% would today be under FLDG.

items.statement: Financial services revenue declined QoQ due to sectoral headwinds in unsecured lending; green shoots seen, expect disbursals to return to FY24 levels.
items.quote: However, of course, on a quarterly basis, we see that there is a decline. This decline is mostly driven by sectoral headwinds and we see green shoots and we expect that disbursals will come back to the same level as FY'24.

items.statement: Scaling down ZIP EMI due to lower partner appetite for small-ticket unsecured loans; replacing with secured FD-backed RuPay Credit Card (in beta) with no credit cost.
items.quote: The new secured credit card product that we are trying to use to offset that, is currently in beta. So, it is not available at scale to all of our users. We expect to take the product out of beta and make it live on production for all users fairly soon.

items.statement: Wallet GMV growing >100% for several years; 3X growth in FY25; largest wallet player in India, 5th on BBPS, 16th on UPI by GMV.
items.quote: if you look at our numbers for the last several years, you will see that the payments GMV has been growing at more than 100% for several years. And in of course, in this year, we have grown 3X.

items.statement: IPO completed Dec 18, 2024 raising 572 crores; first large equity raise in 3.5 years; capital allocation planning underway.
items.quote: Now, the IPO has given the company access to 572 crores in capital, only at the end of 2024. This is definitely the first large equity raise for the company in the last 3.5 years.

items.statement: Customer acquisition cost ~Rs 37 (vs Rs 34 previous quarter); marginal fluctuation due to Google AdWords and currency factors; CAC very low vs peers.
items.quote: if you see our last quarter was roughly around 34, this quarter is like 37. So, Rs.4-5 cost will go up and down because if you see the main tool that we use to acquire new users is basically Google Adwords etc., and there are multiple factors like currency fluctuation, etc., also comes into picture.

items.statement: Insurance distribution license (IRDA) and RIA license (SEBI) held; insurance launch expected in calendar 2025; Lens.AI savings platform scaling.
items.quote: Similarly, we also have the Insurance Distribution License, which we are yet to launch, but in 2025 this calendar year, we expect to launch that also.

items.statement: Not expecting significant impact if Paytm wallet license restored; wallet GMV growing strongly independent of competitor actions; many new wallet license applicants.
items.quote: we don't expect that there will be a significant impact for any new player joining the ecosystem, as you can see, many more people are applying now for wallet licenses.

items.statement: Fixed costs in check QoQ; will further optimize for operating leverage; financial services to bounce back; insurance/savings launches in 2025; payments growing strongly.
items.quote: fixed cost in Q3 are in check in line with what they were in Q2. We will continue to further optimize them even as we scale our businesses so that operating leverage will eventually kick in. We will bounce back in the distribution of financial products, we will launch the new insurance and savings businesses I spoke about, and payments of course keeps growing at a very nice clip.

items.statement: Platform scale: 172 million users, ~5 million merchants; largest wallet player, 5th on BBPS, 16th on UPI by GMV.
items.quote: we are today with 172 million users and just shy of 5 million merchants.

items.statement: Jewellery EBIT margin guidance of 11% to 11.5% on standalone annualized basis
items.quote: therefore, long story short, I think we can expect to be anchored around the current levels of EBIT margins. And for an annualized basis between 11% to 11.5% is what I think we are likely to realistically achieve

items.statement: Gold price surge diluting studded GC percentages due to changing gold-diamond weight mix
items.quote: The second big factor that is playing out is, there is a certain dilution in the GC percentages for studded, largely because of this unprecedented rise in gold price.

items.statement: 11% EBIT margin seen as threshold on annualized basis; unlikely to go below except in extreme situations
items.quote: But by and large, not going below 11% on an annualized basis is for sure my threshold.

items.statement: Upper-middle and affluent segments driving consumption; wealth effect from market cap gains and rising taxpayer base
items.quote: Those which are catering to the upper middle class and above, like Titan company is, is performing better than typically mass-market volume kind of sectors.

items.statement: Q4 started well but gold price volatility from US tariff news creating uncertainty; customers waiting for price stabilization
items.quote: So, we started very well in the first few weeks of January, first 2 to 3 weeks. And then suddenly after many exciting developments in the international, especially US, has created a lot of excitement on gold price again and dollars.

items.statement: Gold growing faster than studded; gold coins exceptionally strong in Q3 as investment demand
items.quote: Now what happened in this quarter is that the rate at which gold is growing, is kind of exceeding significantly the rate at which studded is going.

items.statement: Studded growth driven by high-value collections and wedding jewellery; buyer growth healthier in studded than gold
items.quote: We did a lot of exhibitions of special collections, red carpet, etcetera. We also did a lot of activity around wedding collections.

items.statement: 48% new buyers, 52% repeat buyers in Q3; new buyer growth in studded under ₹1 lakh segment across Tanishq, CaratLane, Mia
items.quote: In terms of new versus repeat for the quarter 3 that was -- that we declared results for, 48% new and 52% repeat.

items.statement: Customer database exceeds 4 crore; CRM enables personalized outreach for milestone events and purchase history
items.quote: Our total customer database exceeds 4 crores today. And a very good part of these 4 crore customers are personally known to our staff, their milestone events in their lives, their purchase history, all that is known through our CRM system.

items.statement: Competitive intensity high and dynamic; reviewed weekly by operating teams, monthly by Ajoy, quarterly at Board level
items.quote: Competitive activity, yes, of course, I mean all of us know and you would also obviously have it in the back of your mind is a daily affair.

items.statement: Gold price wars intense in Q2 but stabilized in Q3; making charges unchanged; further curbs on illegal imports may help stability
items.quote: I think in quarter 2 the gold rate -- price wars on the gold rate was quite intense. That seems to have kind of stabilized in quarter 3.

items.statement: Reducing gold price premium vs competitors eases customer acquisition; premium rationalized over 5 years toward making charges and product mix
items.quote: Yes, whenever we have brought down the premium on our gold prices vis-a-vis our, let's say, most relevant competitor in the market, we have seen customer acquisition becomes much easier.

items.statement: Taneira store expansion continuing but focused on metros and Tier-1 cities; only 1 L3 store opened in Q3 vs 7 last year
items.quote: We opened only one store in this quarter, but we are continuing to -- we'll continue to open stores. Now we are focusing more on metros and Tier-1 cities, and not going to smaller towns.

items.statement: Jewellery same-store growth improved to 22% in Q3 from 15% in Q2 driven by ticket size growth in gold and high-value studded sales
items.quote: Jewellery SSG has clearly improved from 15% in Q2 to 22% in Q3.

items.statement: CaratLane like-for-like store growth 16% in Q3 and 21% in Q2, significantly higher than previous 4-5 quarters
items.quote: I can give you some indication of our like-to-like store growth which is also very good, the 16% in quarter Sensitivity: Internal 3 and previous quarter is 21% which is significantly higher than what happened in the previous four or five
