items.quote: And in Q3, for example, we've seen 33% growth in Fastrack and 24% growth in Sonata, which is about a lot of product and restaging and new products.

items.statement: Analog watches: over 50% of retail sales for gifting, strongly correlated with wedding season
items.quote: Our estimate in retail is more than 50% is for gifting. And we know a large part of that is for wedding.

items.statement: Diamond prices stable at retail level for small stones; wholesale big-stone price declines not impacting Titan's studded jewellery
items.quote: So, when it comes to small stones, which is, by the way, the bulk of our studded jewellery, there is a very different outlook and reality.

items.statement: Gold lease rates showing slight increase indicated by banks; supply situation being monitored; other levers available via spot, GIFT City, exchange
items.quote: But definitely the initial indications are that the gold on lease rates could go up. It's just that we need to wait for a month or two to understand how the supply, and therefore the pricing, will play out.

items.statement: Budget plugged gold alloy import loophole; any reduction in illegal gold flows welcome but difficult to quantify impact
items.quote: Anything which helps prevent or reduce illegal flows of gold in the country is most welcome is what I would say.

items.statement: New income tax regime with higher disposable income expected to benefit entire consumption sector including jewellery
items.quote: I think it will benefit the whole consumption sector, not just the jewellery sector. Of course, we will get our due share of that.

items.statement: Gold price volatility (25% YoY, 5% monthly swings) making margin prediction difficult; US tariff and dollar dynamics adding uncertainty
items.quote: Overall, if you see over the last 1 year, it's a 25% jump in gold price. And diamond prices have remained where they are.

items.statement: LGD (lab-grown diamond) stores proliferating in some markets like Borivali; monitoring portfolio impact across Tanishq, CaratLane, Mia
items.quote: So, thanks for sharing this sharper question. We will -- I will identify certain markets and keep a close track on it.

items.statement: 90% of sales through EBF model with 1,000 partners across country; described as unique competitive advantage with 'fire in belly and heart'
items.quote: We have 1,000 partners across the length and breadth of the country. No company can boast of 1,000 people with fire in their belly as well as in their hearts, and actually driving the performance of the company that we all boast.

items.statement: International growth exceptional in GCC and North America
items.quote: And even internationally, I mean we didn't speak at all to the question, but if you look at the international growth, it's exceptional in GCC and North America.

items.statement: Wearables category correcting sharply; re-looking strategy to play to strengths in design, trust, quality, channel access, higher price points; results expected in 6-18 months
items.quote: And I think that strategy has already started seeing some green shoots. We should be able to implement and see the results in the next, I'd say, 6 to 18 months.

items.statement: Power demand increased in last month; expects peak demand of 265-270 GW this summer
items.quote: But we do find that in last 1 month, the demand of power has increased. And we are expecting that this year, the summer will be much more intense compared to the last year where we had a very long monsoon. Considering that, we do expect that there will be a peak demand of nearly 265 to 270 gigawatt.

items.statement: Nuclear Power Act amendment will allow private sector investment; awaiting policy details
items.quote: The second big announcement by the Finance Minister was about nuclear power that the Nuclear Power Act will be amended which will allow private sector investment in nuclear power.

items.statement: Committed to 70% clean energy by 2030; currently at 43%
items.quote: As we move forward, we are committed to our overall goal that we will achieve 70% of clean energy by 2030. We are already at 43% and the various projects which are under implementation, we should be in a position to meet those targets.

items.statement: Spent INR12,000 crore capex in 9M FY25; plans INR10,000 crore in Q4 for total ~INR22,000 crore FY25
items.quote: During the last 9 months, we have spent capex of nearly INR12,000 crores, which was the total capex that we spent in the previous financial year. And we have plans to spend another INR10,000 crores in this quarter. So we'll have end of the year total capex of nearly INR22,000 crores.

items.statement: Net debt INR44,700 crore; debt-to-equity 1.1:1; net debt to EBITDA <3x
items.quote: Our debt today is -- our net debt is about INR 44,700 crores and our debt to equity is 1.1:1 and our debt -- net debt to underlying EBITDA is less than 3.

items.statement: First 2 GW cell line stabilized at ~90%; second 2 GW commissioned Jan, expects stabilization by Feb
items.quote: Our cell plant which was commissioned in the month of November, the first 2 gigawatt is now more or less stabilized. The second 2 gigawatt also has been commissioned in January and is under stabilization process. And we expect that within February, it will get stabilized and will be able to produce at full capacity during the next financial year.

items.statement: Won 4 transmission bids; all under construction; expect completion in FY26 except one 15-month project
items.quote: Our transmission business, again, we've done a huge amount of work. We won four bids and construction activity of all those four projects are going up -- going on. And we expect that in FY '26, all of them will be completed excepting one 15 months and the benefit of that in terms of revenue, EBITDA and PAT will start coming from FY '26 onwards.

items.statement: Renewable EBITDA up 38% YoY; rooftop revenue crossed INR500 crore in quarter with healthy EBITDA and PAT
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the renewable business itself has gone up by 38%. And also our PAT has gone up for renewable business in this quarter as well as for the full 9 months.

items.statement: Module approved list in place since Apr 2024; cell manufacturer list effective Jun 2026 (extended to Jul 2026)
items.quote: So already the module approved list of module manufacturer is already in place since last year, 1st April 2024. And the approved list of cell manufacturers will get implemented from 1st June 2026. And I think it has already been extended. It's earlier for sales, it was 1st April '26. Now it has been extended to 1st July 2026.

items.statement: 1,100 MW wind turbines under implementation; another 1.6 GW ordering in next 60 days
items.quote: So as we have shared with you, 1,000 megawatts, we had already, in fact, 1,100-odd megawatt, we have already done. Those wind turbines are already under implementation. And all of them will get commissioned in the next 3 months to 12 months. There's another 1.6 gigawatts that we will be ordering. All this ordering will happen in the next 60 days.

items.statement: Targets 2-2.5 GW renewable capacity additions annually for FY26 and FY27
items.quote: Puneet, so I think Puneet, just to kind of recall on a discussion granted, normally, what you have said, our intention is to have about rough definitely 2 gigawatt of installations every year. Praveer Sinha: 2 to 2.5. Sanjeev Churiwala: 2 to 2.5 gigawatt of installations every year.

items.statement: Actively pursuing UP discom privatization bids; will bid aggressively when tenders released
items.quote: We are actively pursuing that and -- or we will actively pursue that because we have excellent experience of carrying out similar type of work in Odisha, where we were able to cater to both urban and rural consumers which no other utility has experienced in the country. And as and when the bids come, we will definitely bid and we expect that we'l l be able to be successful in these bids

items.statement: Pump storage civil work started; civil order finalization this month; Bhutan hydro project at full pace
items.quote: So the three project activities has already started and basic site civil work has started. The order for civil will be finalized within this month, and we also expect the last of clearances. And full-fledged work will start from next month.

items.statement: EPC margins 5-7% on YTD basis; Q3 optically high at 16% due to revenue reversal post-merger
items.quote: The best way to look is at the year to date number, which reflects the right position, and they're kind of in the range of 5% to 7% on EPC margin, which has always been our guidance.

items.statement: Section-11 continuation for Mundra plant expected this month due to high power demand
items.quote: As I mentioned to you that there is a huge demand of power, and I expect that to meet this additional demand of power, all the imported coal -based plants will be asked to continue operations. And we do expect that government will take the call on this in the later part of this month.

items.statement: Rooftop solar target 3 million households in 3 years (~10 lakh/year); MoUs signed with states
items.quote: The 3 million means 30 lakhs in 3 years means average 10 lakhs per year. It can be more also. So it all depends on how quickly, we are able to streamline our processes and implement them.

items.statement: Rooftop solar cost INR60,000-65,000 per kW on sale basis; earns profit margin not IRR
items.quote: So basically, the cost of 1 kilowatt of rooftop is about INR60,000 to INR65,000 depending upon the location. And this is on a sale basis. So that means there is no IRR in this, but there is a profit margin that we have.

items.statement: Nuclear project timelines: 24 months approvals + 4-5 years construction; economics premature to estimate
items.quote: It all takes about 24 months. And thereafter, the construction period is 4 to 5 years. So it's a little longish, but I can assure you that these projects are today becoming very common in various parts of the world.

items.statement: Odisha discoms: Q1 impacted by elections; Q3 shows substantial improvement in billing/collection efficiency
items.quote: In the first quarter, we could not do much because there were elections in Odisha and because of that reason, a lot of action on billing collection could not be done. It has got up in the last quarter. And the last quarter, that is the present quarter, you will see a substantial improvement on building efficiency, collection efficiency.

items.statement: Merged 25 companies including WREL into TPREL effective Apr 2024; simplifying GENCO structure
items.quote: So about 25 companies have now been merged with TPREL and that merger is effective from 1st of April. So the financials that you see is from. Anuj Upadhyay: Okay. So the WREL that has been now move to TPREL? Sanjeev Churiwala: So WREL is basically a GENCO , generating company and as part of our strategy, we have moved it and merged with TPREL, which is also has

items.statement: Selective in transmission bidding; only bid where returns are optimal and complexity manageable
items.quote: We are also very selective in our bidding. We don't want to go and bid out everywhere where we think that the returns are suboptimal or we think the territory, the geography and the complexities are very high, but it could be very, very high. So yes, we have been very selective. But in this selectiveness, we're also trying to see that we only bid for projects where we get good returns.

items.statement: EPC strategy shift: pure EPC without land acquisition; focus on in-house and group captive projects
items.quote: We have undergone a change in the way we were doing EPC. We now do pure EPC without land. Again, we used to acquire land also for the EPC projects. So we do not do that. Secondly, we wanted to execute all these projects before we take more orders and plan as a part of our order book.

items.statement: Renewable generation 9M higher YoY despite Q3 weather impact; extended monsoon reduced solar output
items.quote: Also, how -- if you see on a 9-month basis, the generation is much higher than compared to last year. So what we have to see is because also of the weather factor changes like this year, the monsoon was much extended, was right up to October. So many of the solar plants would not generate, which they could have otherwise down.

items.statement: EPC revenue reversal INR300 crore due to merger accounting; no profitability impact
items.quote: As you are aware, that our EPC business, which was a separate legal entity, has now become a merged entity. Per say, the intercompany delegate is not happening. And as such, the revenue is lower because we have kind of cooled up about INR 300-odd crores to replace the correct accounting principles post-merger. That has no implications on the profitability.

items.statement: Invested nearly INR 5,800 Crores between 2020 and 2025; 10th factory in Odisha to begin soon
items.quote: between 2020 and 2025, we would be investing almost INR 5,800 Crores and that is a significant amount of money for a food processing c ompany. The investment in the 10 th factory in Odisha is to begin very

items.statement: Added over 35% capacity for MAGGI, coffee and chocolates since 2020; Sanand confectionery factory operational
items.quote: The capacities that we have added for MAGGI, coffee and chocolates is more than 35%. We would not put that up ladies and gentlemen unless we were confident about the future.

items.statement: Aims to increase innovation contribution to sales from 6.5% to at least 10%
items.quote: Today, they contribute 6.5% to sales. I would like to see this ambition go to at least to 10%, which would be a good number to have as far as innovation is concerned.

items.statement: Improved operating margins by almost 500 basis points over the last decade; EBITDA margins up similarly
items.quote: I am very happy to see that in the last decade almost 500 basis points of operating margins have been improved as a company. If you look at it in terms of EBITDA, it is about the same.

items.statement: Coffee prices up 75% point-to-point; cocoa up 40-50%; wheat to increase due to procurement price hike; pricing is last lever after cost efficiencies
items.quote: Point to point between this year and last year, the coffee prices are up 75%. It is very difficult for any c ompany to survive with 75% increases and still manage growth. And so, that is where it is. Our exposure is relatively lower to cocoa, but nevertheless I think the price of cocoa has been significantly impacted and continues to rise dramatically again in the 40- 50% kind of range of increase

items.statement: Urban growth tapered; rural growth looking up; urban unemployment, tepid real wage growth, post-COVID moderation cited as reasons
items.quote: Urban growth has tapered downwards. Rural growth is looking upwards, but yet I think the cause for concern on growth continues to remain. It is not something that we are completely out of the woods. Urban unemployment, tepid real wage growth and post COVID moderation are what we see as the three big reasons.

items.statement: Portfolio balanced: Milk Products & Nutrition 39% (6% growth), Prepared Dishes 31% (19% growth), Confectionery 16% (14% growth), Powdered & Liquid Beverages growing well
items.quote: About 39% coming from M ilk Products and Nutrition. It is a more mature category in terms of its size and heft with a 6% growth. Our P repared Dishes and Cooking Aids, MAGGI, that came back from the dead literally in 2015 roaring to a 19% growth during this period with a 31% contribution

items.statement: Reaches 5.3 million outlets; added highest percentage of outlets among F&B peers in 2024 (~5%); covers 200,000+ villages vs 70,000 in 2020
items.quote: In 2024, amongst the F&B companies added in percentage term, the maximum number of outlets close to 5% of outlets have been added and is the highest gain amongst peers in 2024.

items.statement: Volume growth CAGR of 9.5% from 2015 to 2023; company DNA is penetration-led, volume-led growth
items.quote: This growth for us has been 9.5% growth from 2015 to 2023. What I would like to leave you with is a simple message. This c ompany knows how to generate volume growth. That is what is our DNA

items.statement: Takes regional competition seriously; uses campaigns, digital interventions, price-point strategies (e.g., Rs.10 pack, value at Rs.7) to defend share
items.quote: I said we take regional competition seriously and therefore there are campaigns, which are building awareness of taste and quality at a granular local level. There are digital interventions, but there are also other media interventions. There are price point strategies that are there.

items.statement: NESPRESSO launching in India; boutique opening in Delhi soon, then Mumbai; sources premium arabica/robusta from ~2,000 Indian farmers
items.quote: The NESPRESSO website is now live. We will be opening shortly a boutique in Delhi to begin with and then it will go to Bombay and to various other places as we go.

items.statement: Joint venture with Dr. Reddy's (49:51) integrated successfully since July last year; double-digit growth; new launches from Nestlé Health Science and Dr. Reddy's portfolios on the anvil
items.quote: The integration has been successful. The teams are working well together. They came together only in July of last year, but I think the integration has been strong and solid. They have shown double digit growth, which is also encouraging.

items.statement: Introduced successor Manish Tiwari (joined 48 hours ago); emphasizes inclusive, diverse culture and gender diversity as key management philosophy
items.quote: I also have the privilege today like all good succession plannings to introduce my successor Manish Tiwari. Manish has just joined 48 hours ago

items.statement: Supply chain efficiency improved via quick commerce demands; Blinkit challenge reduced delivery from two days to one day, targeting hours; digital twins at Bhiwandi DC
items.quote: Blinkit asks us a question saying I deliver in eight minutes, why should you take two days? Good question. So, Nestlé puts its hat on it, works, puts systems, puts practices and ensures that at least we get it down to one day and hopefully now we will get it down to a couple of hours.

items.statement: Milk relatively stable; coffee up 75%; cocoa up 40-50%; wheat to rise due to procurement price increase; packaging stable; edible oils up recently
items.quote: I think milk is being rel atively stable, coffee has been a complete super inflation, almost a chaotic curve to follow. Point to point between this year and last year, the coffee prices are up 75

items.statement: Geopolitics beyond competence but impacts supply chain and future output profiles; commodity inflation (coffee, cocoa, wheat) remains a worry factor
items.quote: There is a third piece on geopolitics that I will not talk about because that is a subject that is beyond my pale of competence. But you all know the consequences of geopolitics and how it is going to play with the supply chain and future output profiles of this country.

items.statement: Operating margin band of 20-21% seen as optimal to support growth journey; no forward guidance given
items.quote: As you know, our operating margins, which were about 16.5% have gone up in the last 10 years to about 21- 22%. The band between 20 and 21 is where we have been operating for a reasonably long time.

items.statement: Coffee price increases up 75% point-to-point difficult to absorb fully; some pricing pressure expected in coffee, lower in other categories
items.quote: if I told you point to point price up by 75% is very difficult despite all the project Sharks that I can do and optimization that I can do for me to absorb 75% of a coffee price increase.

items.statement: Pricing is last resort; primary levers are astute buying, material usage improvements, and asset efficiency
items.quote: For us, pricing is the last. For us, astute buying, because we have economies of scale, material usage improvements through specifications and more effective or more efficient utilization of the assets that we have got is the primary scope that we would like to use.

items.statement: Milk and nutrition category hit strongly by inflation; price increases restricted volume growth; competition from cooperatives adds pressure
items.quote: Look, milk and nutrition as a category has been probably one of those that has been hit very strongly by inflation. And as you know that our portfolio there , have also had the impact of price increases that clearly has restricted the volume growth.

items.statement: MAGGI volume growth impacted by price increase from Rs 5 to Rs 7 and expanded snacking competition including regional players
items.quote: I think the price inflation clearly has played a role because we ourselves had to take up the price from five to seven. We could not digest that anymore. And that took a little bit of a toll in terms of the volume evolution of the brand.

items.statement: 60% of growth to come from core categories; premiumization within core to increase market share and portfolio resilience
items.quote: Premiumization and growing the core as key strategies, the core is still important to us, 60% of the growth will come from the core.

items.statement: Innovation pipeline of 50-60 ideas pruned to 15-20 manageable projects; calibrated investment across years to protect core
items.quote: So, let us say if I have innovation ideas of potentially 50- 60, I will have to prune it down to 15- 20 to be able to manage it. And within that, then to calibrate and see which are the big ticket items.

items.statement: Channel conflict managed via curated promotions, portfolio pricing, and internal caps; traditional trade still 75-80% of sales
items.quote: We have a certain internal kind of cap that we set for ourselves saying, not beyond this do we go. Yet of course, there is a fierce war out there. And sometimes people could use us as a loss leader.

items.statement: Rs 10 price point introduced as value pack in specific geographies and channels; not ubiquitous to avoid down-trading from Rs 15 single pack
items.quote: So, Rs.10 has been more put in as a value pack. In the geographies in which it has been introduced where the single packs are relatively not as salient, it is giving us good results.

items.statement: Coffee capacity doubled at Nanjangud; expected to improve manufacturing efficiencies
items.quote: We have doubled our coffee capacities now in Nanjangud. And hopefully that will lead to better efficiencies in coffee manufacture.

items.statement: Outlet expansion target of ~6 million outlets in coming years; focus shifting to depth of penetration via portfolio, price points, frequency
items.quote: I think the outlet expansion, I would reckon, ballpark till about 6 million outlets is what we should be looking at in the coming years.

items.statement: Noodles market share stable at ~60%; baby foods share strong; chocolates distinct #2 to Mondelez but wafer-based KITKAT/MUNCH share up; coffee now market leader
items.quote: Market shares I think noodles have been fairly stable. There can be a little bit of quarterly blips up and down but it is in the region of about 60 odd percent, which is where it was.

items.statement: Sustainable coffee procurement at 55% with Rs 3-4/kg premium passed to farmers; biomass facility in Moga uses 4% of district stubble
items.quote: About 55% of the coffee is procured sustainably, it takes time to convert farmers into a sustainable way because they have to trade off the price with the yield.

items.statement: GHG emissions down 61% since 2008; energy usage down 29%; water usage down 50%; wastewater generation down 60%; plastic neutral since 2020
items.quote: GHG emissions down by 61%, this is from the period 2008, it is a 15-year reporting cycle that we have, consistent with our sustainability report.

items.statement: Women represent 50% of Board, 21% of field force, ~25% of white-collar; Sanand factory majority women; Odisha factory to be majority women; attrition 10% or less
items.quote: Happy to report and you know it already that 50% of my B oard consists of leading women independent directors. We have amongst the highest representation in the field force in FMCG at 21% and we have about a fourth of our white collar which consists of women.

items.statement: Volume growth historically ~9-9.5% of 11.2% total growth; recently reversed to pricing-led due to commodity inflation
items.quote: Remember our volume growth has been almost 9-9.5%. So it has been in that 11.2 % growth, about 9% has been volume, so 2% has been pricing. Now it is the other way around.

items.statement: Appetite for inorganic growth continues; no deals fructified yet but interest remains
items.quote: Look, I think, Latika, the appetite for inorganic growth continues. Though you may say you have not made anything happen, and unfortunately nothing has fructified so far.

items.statement: Digital transformation underway across consumer, customer, value chain, employees; AI journey from MIDAS (2019) to demand forecasting, retailer segmentation, MROI marketing simulation
items.quote: Today we have an interesting project called MROI, which is r eturn on investment of marketing support that will give us a simulation using AI of all that you have done in the past in terms of activities, budgets, returns and outcomes.

items.statement: If commodity inflation (coffee, cocoa, wheat) does not improve, market dynamics will change; willing to take margin hit on categories for known periods
items.quote: But if the situation does not improve, then the whole dynamics of the market will change. We do not have a policy that every SKU of the category should make the same margins.

items.statement: Healthcare partnership with Dr. Reddy's and Nestlé Health Science targeting INR 24,000 Cr opportunity; new launches on anvil
items.quote: I talked there about INR 24,000 Crores, that is just a number. But it is a large opportunity. It is an opportunity that also does good for the c ompany and does good for society.

items.statement: 13 distribution centres transformed (26 moves); >50% sales covered; digital twin at Bhiwandi DC for planning and resource allocation
items.quote: We have effectively transformed about 13 distribution centr es. That means, ladies and gentlemen, 26 moves because each one is a move in itself. Almost more than half of the sales have been covered.

items.statement: Out-of-home: 940 franchised Nestlé Kiosks (Retail One); not significant revenue contributor but drives trials and marketing; 20 million annual footfall
items.quote: The 940 are all; we do not run any outlets ourselves. So these are franchised outlets but however the model is little bit different that there are larger franchises who will have 5 -10 of these per franchise.

items.statement: Social initiatives: 14M beneficiaries (13M via Project Jagriti), 70K street hawkers trained, 20 schools under Project Jigyasa, 14 villages in Nuh district impacting 18K people
items.quote: There are about 14 million beneficiaries that are impacted as a result of what Nestlé does. About 13 million has been through Project Jagriti, which is an adolescent and young adult programme centered around nutrition, around healthy habits, about preventing earl y marriages and of really trying to ensure that people lead healthy lives.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 volume growth 1.6%, value growth -7.8% due to weak festive demand, muted urban sentiment, and downtrading
items.quote: When we look at the overall numbers for Q3 it has been a weak demand period. The overall consumer sentiments have been muted as we are seeing across a lot of industries to that extent.

items.statement: 9M FY25 volume growth 2.8%, value growth -5.8%
items.quote: Same numbers if we were to see over a nine-month period, the volume growth is closer to about 2.8% and the comparative value growth is minus 5.8%.

items.statement: Industrial segment outperformed decorative; combined decorative plus industrial volume growth 1.7%, value growth -6.6% in Q3
items.quote: When we look at the whole area of industrial as well. So, the total decorative plus industrial business overall combined, the performance gets slightly better given the fact that industrial segment has done slightly better as compared to the retail segment.

items.statement: 5-year volume CAGR 12.1% for decorative business, 10.8% for combined decorative plus industrial
items.quote: If you notice in Q2 it had come down a little. It has gone up now in Q3 at about 12.1 % in terms of CAGR. So, that is something which we are still maintaining as we look at from the point of view of the decorative business.

items.statement: Distribution expanded to ~169,000 retail touchpoints; Beautiful Homes Painting Services in 650+ towns with strong NPS
items.quote: In terms of what is happening across India, we have now about 1.69 lakh retail counters across the country to that extent. And that is something which is a constant endeavour in terms of what we see that we are available at every consumer point across the country.

items.statement: New products contributed over 12% of overall revenues in Q3; launched Apex Ultima Suprema Air-O-Clean with photocatalytic technology
items.quote: The new products contributed to about 12% of the overall revenues in Q3. We've been speaking about our backward integration projects. The VAM-VAE project which is coming up at Dahej and the White Cement which is coming at Fujairah, Dubai, both are on track.

items.statement: Backward integration projects VAM-VAE at Dahej and White Cement at Fujairah, Dubai on track
items.quote: We've been speaking about our backward integration projects. The VAM-VAE project which is coming up at Dahej and the White Cement which is coming at Fujairah, Dubai, both are on track.

items.statement: B2B/Projects business picked up in Q3 driven by factories, builders, and government segment after 3 slow quarters
items.quote: From the point of view of the B2B business has done quite well. The projects / institution business overall picked up in Q3 as compared to Q2. We saw some traction happening in terms of the government spending also coming live.

items.statement: Standalone gross margin improved sequentially to 43.2% in Q3 from 41.1% in Q2, but down ~100 bps YoY; PBDIT margin 20.7%
items.quote: The gross margins have improved sequentially if you see from 41.1 o/o to about 43.2% overall. So, that is something which is strong which has happened in terms of the sequential movement.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin 42.3% in Q3, PBDIT margin 19.2%; 9M consolidated PBDIT margin 17.9%
items.quote: When we go to consolidated financials the picture is a little bit similar. You know, you have a top line which is at about minus 6% in terms of what we see overall at Q3 and gross margins at about 42.3% and a PBDIT margin of about 19.2%.

items.statement: PPGAP (Auto/Refinish JV) PBT margin at all-time high 22.1% in Q3; APPPG (Protective/Powder) PBT margin 8.4% vs 11.5% last year
items.quote: But I think the best which has happened is the profitability is something which is doing extremely good. PBT margins are at about all time high of about 22% here.

items.statement: Price increase of 1.2% taken in Q2 with 0.4% carryover into Q3; average price decrease of 0.3% on select products end Jan 2025
items.quote: This quarter we have seen price deflation and as you are aware we had announced a price increase in Q2 of about 1.2% and it has a carryover effect of about 0.4% in Q3.

items.statement: Expect some softening in raw material prices; weakening rupee a key concern
items.quote: From a point of view of raw material prices you know, we see some softening. The buoyant dollar is something which is a concern. We are already seeing weakening in the rupee.

items.statement: Maintain PBDIT margin guidance of 18-20% for FY25; aim for single-digit volume growth and better product mix for decent value growth
items.quote: We are very clear that we are not running after price strongly to that extent. We want to kind of really concentrate at looking at some of the segments where we have a strong leverage in terms of going forward and we would like to maintain our overall guidance of 18 to 20% as we go ahead.

items.statement: Cautiously optimistic on recovery over next couple of quarters; urban stress continues, rural demand expected to accelerate in Q4 and Q1 FY26 on good monsoons and government spending
items.quote: As we go forward, we definitely see the stress in terms of the urban areas will continue. We are optimistic about some of the rural, you know, towns batting to that extent. So, therefore our overall intention is that it is a little bit of a cautious optimistic approach in terms of what we see as a recovery for the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: New competition present across price points but no unique value proposition yet; impact too early to assess; trade schemes remain dynamic and vary by region
items.quote: But at the moment, very difficult to say that if they have a proposition for the customer coming in. And a lot of things obviously at the moment are looking at price and discounting led in terms of what we see in the market.

items.statement: Decorative industry volume estimated at -4% to -5% in Q3; industrial market still growing
items.quote: I would say that at least the decorative industry is definitely ranging anywhere around minus 4%, minus 5%, kind of zone in terms of what we see. The Industrial is still up in terms of the overall market.

items.statement: B2B business ~16-17% of revenue; targeting double-digit growth driven by factory capex, government spending, and hospitality
items.quote: Today the segment would be somewhere in the range of about 16, 17% contribution. And we would definitely like to see that given the growth trajectory here, we have grown at very good numbers this year in Q2, and we would like to kind of have double-digit kind of growth numbers as far as the B2B business is concerned.

items.statement: Home Decor: Kitchen revenue grew ~3% in Q3, 5% 9M; Bath similar; White Teak & Weatherseal single-digit growth; Weatherseal impacted by BIS challenges
items.quote: In terms of what we were seeing, we have in Q3 grown in Kitchen at about 3%, but at a nine-monthly level, we are at about 5% level. And ditto with, you know, the Bath area as well in terms of the growths.

items.statement: International business: Q3 revenue growth 5% in INR, 17.1% in constant currency; Middle East +20%, Asia recovering (Sri Lanka, Bangladesh), Africa impacted by Egypt/Ethiopia currency devaluation
items.quote: In INR terms, we have grown at about 5% at an overall global level and a strong 17% in constant currency terms. If we look at from the point of view of various regions, the Middle East region has done spectacularly well at 20% growth in terms of Q3.

items.statement: Employee costs controlled via productivity improvements; sales & distribution expenses up due to competition intensity
items.quote: As we had said that we had looked at possibly, you know, manning more people in the beginning so that we could really cater to our network far more strongly. Post that we have also taken steps in terms of how we can boost the productivity of the people much more.

items.statement: Urban demand stress expected to continue for at least two quarters; rupee weakness a concern for input costs
items.quote: We are already seeing weakening in the rupee. And that is something which we will have to watch out and see in terms of how it pans out. So, that is the overall outlook in terms of what we see for Q4.

items.statement: Launched Nilaya Wall WRAP (zero PVC, zero VOC, water-based) enabling 2 BHK painting in 3 days; mechanized painting training across 23 centres
items.quote: We have launched this product called the Nilaya Wall WRAP, which is called Nilaya Play and Nilaya Ones. This is a wonder product in terms of what we are introducing, which is absolutely green with no VOC and it does not consume any water also at all.

items.statement: Neo Latex category potential >5 lakh KL; Asian Paints currently at 7-9% penetration
items.quote: Almost the potential is more than 5 lakh KL in terms of the overall category. As 33 | P a g e I see it, we are just scraping possibly at the moment, you know, 7 to 9% of that overall pie which is

items.statement: FY25 pre-sales guidance of INR1,200 crores
items.quote: FY '25, we should do around INR1,200 crores in terms of pre-sales.

items.statement: FY26 pre-sales guidance of INR1,550-1,600 crores
items.quote: FY '26 will be around INR1,550 crores to INR1,600 crores of pre-sales.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guidance of 20-25%
items.quote: Yes, I think we should be able to achieve around 20%, 25% growth guidance as we had mentioned out in the first quarter.

items.statement: FY26 revenue CAGR target of 26%
items.quote: And for FY '26 also, we look to grow at a CAGR of 26%.

items.statement: World Villas FY25 sales target of 25-35 additional units
items.quote: I think we should be able to do another, say, sales of 25 to 35 units till the year-end.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 average realization expected above INR6,000 per sq ft
items.quote: But I think Q4 will go back, say, upwards of INR6,000.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 sales booking of 551 units, 4.74 lakh sq ft, INR265.5 crores value
items.quote: The company has achieved sales booking of 551 units, which is equivalent to 4.74 lakh square feet, amounting to INR265.5 crores in terms of value.

items.statement: Total collection in Q3 FY25 of INR129.1 crores
items.quote: The total collection for the quarter stands at INR129.1 crores.

items.statement: Current GDV stands at INR12,500 crores
items.quote: Our current GDV stands at INR12,500 crores.

items.statement: Land bank increased from 220 to 307 acres in FY25, achieving 300+ acres guidance
items.quote: we have been able to increase our land bank from 220 acres in April 2024 to 307 acres in December 2024. So, we have achieved our guidance of crossing 300-plus acres of land in FY '25.

items.statement: Acquired 23 acres at Chowk for Town Villas with INR2,500 crores GDV potential
items.quote: we have acquired 23 acres of additional land at Chowk for our second horizontal project, which will be named as Town Villas, which shall have a total GDV potential of INR2,500 crores.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin at 28%, highest in company history
items.quote: The EBITDA margin has been recorded at the highest for any particular quarter in the history of the company at 28% and the same was at 22% in the year prior.

items.statement: Project-level EBITDA margin target of 30-33%
items.quote: overall, at a project level, we target 30%, 33% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Embedded EBITDA margin of ~30% on INR12,500 crores GDV, implying INR3,700 crores EBITDA
items.quote: We should do an EBITDA of around 30% average, so around INR3,700 crores.

items.statement: Average realization down in Q3 due to Jodhpur project mix; MMR pricing increased
items.quote: So, this quarter is a downtrend in Q3 in terms of per square foot realization because we have sold a good amount of inventory in our Jodhpur projects in this quarter. So, that's why the realization has come down at an overall company level. But in terms of per square feet pricing, we have been able to increase it across the entire MMR region

items.statement: Expected minimum price rise of INR500 per sq ft in airport area over next year
items.quote: It will vary from location-to-location, but on an average minimum price rise we can expect is INR500 per square foot on salable area.

items.statement: Arihant Aspire achieving INR7,000 per sq ft in airport area, expecting INR500 jump
items.quote: So, Arihant Aspire, we are now achieving around INR7,000 per square foot on salable area. And I think we can expect a INR500 jump over the next 1 year easily.

items.statement: FY25 capex of INR25-30 crores for World Villas, Club 10, and hotel; FY26-27 ramp-up
items.quote: I think we will be doing a total expenditure of around INR25 crores, INR30 crores for these 3 projects in FY '25. But FY '26 onwards, it will gear up.

items.statement: World Villas timeline: 2 years development, first deliveries Dec 2026; Club 10 by CY27; hotel by Mar 2028
items.quote: Timeline for Villas is 2 years. So, December '26, we should be starting with the first deliveries. And for FY '27, we should be able to complete the Gymkhana also in calendar year '27, sorry. And hotel will be taking more time. That will get ready, say, by March '28.

items.statement: Strong demand across all segments; Shilphata project sold 250 units at 20% premium to peers
items.quote: we launched a project at Shilphata in this quarter, it has done very good amount of sales also. Somewhere close to 250 units have been sold already in the project. We've got a very good response in terms of pricing, have been able to achieve a 20% higher price than majority of the neighbouring developers.

items.statement: Expect 10 lakh jobs and population doubling to 80 lakhs in 10 years driving housing demand
items.quote: We see job creation of multiple categories across blue collar, white collar to the tune of 10 lakh jobs over the next 7 years to 10 years, which will indirectly mean an increase in population of 40 lakhs. So, current population is also around 40 lakhs existing, and that is going to double in the next 10 years.

items.statement: Debt to increase slightly in FY25; major repayment starts FY27; secured debt at 10-10.5%
items.quote: This financial year, debt will increase slightly from the existing. We're not looking at any decrease in debt. Debt, because majority of the debt is now secured. So, there are obviously moratoriums offered by the banks for 2 years, 3 years and then the repayment starts. So, debt repayment for our company will majorly begin in FY '27.

items.statement: Unsecured debt of INR280 crores from promoter families at 13% accrued annually
items.quote: All majority of the funds are from promoters of ASL and then promoters of ASL and their subsidiaries. So, in the subsidiaries, we have Agarwal family who have put in their stake. So, it's a mix of Chhajer and Agarwal families who are -- who have put in all the money. And the average rates are at 13% per annum, which are accrued on a yearly basis.

items.statement: Achieved BBB- credit rating from Acuite and India Ratings with stable outlook
items.quote: So latest exercise we have done. We have been able to achieve a BBB- credit rating, which is a stable outlook.

items.statement: Ready possession inventory reduced from INR55 crores (Apr 2024) to INR17 crores (Dec 2024)
items.quote: We would also like to highlight that we have been able to bring down our ready possession inventory from INR55 crores in April 2024 to INR17 crores in December 2024.

items.statement: Q3 sales mix: 6% premium, 63% mid-income, 31% affordable; portfolio mix: 25% premium, 37% mid-income, 38% affordable
items.quote: With respect to the revenue mix of the sales done, 6% is from premium housing, 63% is from mid-income housing and 31% is from affordable housing.

items.statement: Free cash flow target of 20% of airport area GDV (INR7,500-8,000 crores); total portfolio FCF ~INR3,000 crores over 5-7 years
items.quote: Free cash flows, we should be able to do 20%.

items.statement: INR500 per sq ft price hike on 18 mn sq ft portfolio adds ~INR900 crores GDV
items.quote: around, 18 million square feet today. INR500 means around INR100 crores -- INR90 crores, INR100 crores. Raaj: INR900 crores, I think. Parth Chhajer: Sorry, yes, INR900 crores, yes. INR18 million, correct

items.statement: Union Budget exemption of second self-occupied property from annual value benefits second home buyers and projects
items.quote: the Union Budget was announced 3 days ago, which provides a fillip to the real estate sector by exempting the second self-occupied property from annual value, thus simplifying tax compliance and offering great financial flexibility.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance of 20% for FY25 may fall short by 3-5%; long-term target of 20% volume growth for next 3-5 years maintained
items.quote: Because of flat volume in quarter two, we may fall short by 3 % to 5% of our stipulated guidance of 20% volume growth for FY25. We continue to target 20% volume growth for the next 3 to 5 years, led by our efforts on the marketing front.

items.statement: Revenue target of Rs 500 crore by FY27; long-term vision to reach Rs 1,000 crore
items.quote: So, as I already mentioned that the first, we want to achieve Rs. 500 crores of revenue till 2027. But if we don't talk about the numbers the first thing what our goal plan is that we want to be a national leading position into white glue and we want to be continuous journey into this particular segment till Rs. 1,000 crores of journey.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 25% for longer term; current year may land at 29%
items.quote: So, I think this year we may land on 29% of EBITDA. And for the longer term we are giving the guidance always for the 25% of EBITDA.

items.statement: Q3 volume grew 18% YoY; Q1 grew 20%, Q2 was flat due to monsoon and weak demand
items.quote: As quarter one, we were able to achieve 20% volume growth. Due to monsoon and all over less demand in quarter two it was flat. And now quarter three witnessed revival in our volume growth. Volumes for quarter three grew at 18% YOY.

items.statement: New states showing strong growth from low base; targeting 100 tons/month per state
items.quote: But we are targeting every state as 100 tons per month, at least. So, it is generated Rs. 2.5 crores of, almost Rs. 20 crores, Rs. 25 crores of revenue yearly. So, we are targeting for every state to generate at least for that, the newer states we are talking.

items.statement: Gross margin >30% in Q3 due to softer raw material prices and volume leverage; steady-state gross margin seen at 65%
items.quote: The higher margins of more than 30% was led by softer raw material prices and increased volumes, thereby offering us better spread and operating leverage.

items.statement: Gross margin sustained at ~70% this year; steady-state 65% assuming current VAM prices and one-quarter lag to pass on increases
items.quote: We have stayed at around 70% gross margin throughout this year. So, we expect that to continue.

items.statement: Brownfield expansion of 1,500 tonnes/month over 1.5 years at existing plant; greenfield near Ahmedabad for storage and up to 3,500 tonnes/month manufacturing
items.quote: In terms of our capacity expansions and CapEx plans, we are looking to add another 1,500 tonnes per month over the next 1.5 years at our existing plant, while we are looking at doing greenfield expansions for a new facility on the outskirts of Ahmedabad to meet the initial needs of our storage of raw material, finished goods etc. , along with the potential to go up to manufacturing of 3,500 tonnes

items.statement: Greenfield capex estimated at Rs 40-45 crore over next three years, funded from internal accruals
items.quote: Second plan is, as I mentioned, that Greenfield we are planning in the next three years. So maybe we'll require Rs. 40 crores to Rs. 45 crores for that. But it will be used by gradually, not in a single day.

items.statement: Branches increased from 38 to 42 in Q3 (32 in Q1); 10 branches added in 9 months, mostly in UP, Delhi, West Bengal, Karnataka
items.quote: We have increased the number of branches to 42 during quarter three. That was earlier 38.

items.statement: Retailer margin 7-13%, carpenter loyalty 7-13% (Rs 15-20/kg); Pidilite offers 4-6% to dealers and 2-4% loyalty
items.quote: So basically, we are passing a 7% to 13% depends upon the developed territory or developing territory, for the retailers, and for the carpenters, same 7% to 13%.

items.statement: Realisation dropped ~1.5% in Q3 due to in-bill discounts for new placements and OEM mix; average realisation stable over past year
items.quote: So yeah, basically it can say because as I mentioned that now we are in 10 products. So that has a different strategy and actually we are for the retailers, we are running the different strategies also to grow the market.

items.statement: VAM (95% of raw material) is crude derivative; price range Rs 60-75/kg historically stable except COVID period
items.quote: So basically, it is a crude derivative . But as I mentioned that in VAM particular, there is not much variations in the price happens only, except the COVID. Because of that 2 , 3 years that was disturbed because all the chemical materials and all the freight components. So otherwise, it is almost Rs. 60 to Rs. 75 between per kg.

items.statement: Revenue split 50% bulk packs (30/50/60 kg) and 50% retail packs (500g to 20 kg); 10 product variants now
items.quote: No, actually, it is mixed. But I can give you the brief , bulk packing is the 30, 50 and 60 kg. So, our half revenue is from 30, 50, 60 kg and half revenue is from 500g, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20 kg.

items.statement: Average debtor days 118; mature states 75-80 days, new states 100-120 days; write-offs <1% over 17 years
items.quote: Sir, it is averagely 118 days around. But if we talk about the old states where we are already mature and developed. So that is 75 to 80 days around. And for the newer market, it goes to the 100, 120 days.

items.statement: No fundraise planned; capacity expansions funded entirely from internal accruals
items.quote: Internal accruals only.

items.statement: Dividend payout 15% of profit for last 3-4 years; management open to increasing payout ratio
items.quote: First, you already mentioned that dividends. So, dividend, we are giving the 15% of the profit to our investor last three, four years. So, we will continue for that. Definitely we can.

items.statement: Onboarded CMO, Marketing Manager and ASMs; separate sales, marketing and promotion teams created
items.quote: While also strengthening our sales force parallelly, we have onboarded CMO, Marketing Manager and few ASMs.

items.statement: NSE listing criteria (Rs 75 crore net worth for 3 years) to be met by March 2025; listing targeted next year
items.quote: There is a criteria of NSE listing. So, we will be going to fulfil these criteria in this March. So, we are going to go for the NSE next year. So, there is the criteria of Rs. 75 crore of Net worth should be last 3 years. So that criteria will be fulfilled in this March.

items.statement: Aim to maintain #2 position in wood synthetic adhesives; target 30% market share in Rs 7,500 crore market
items.quote: Overall, we believe we are focused in our approach to markets and our strategy to maintain our number two position in the w ood synthetic market and we are aiming to increase our market share, as the largest

items.statement: Moat built on 17-year trust with carpenters and retailers; asset-light model with low capex and technology needs
items.quote: So basically, it is -- see, if you can see, this is not overnight journey. Sorry. Vijay Shah: Go ahead, sir. Utkarsh J Patel: Yeah. So, it is not an overnight journey. And 17 years we have invested into this business. And the main effort is to build the trust into the carpenter's mind and into the retailer's mind

items.statement: Return on capital employed ~40%; expected to remain stable as cash deployed in network expansion and greenfield
items.quote: I think that will be continuous as it is for that because already, we are having this -- sitting on the cash, so we will utilize into the proper way and we will continue for that. So that will be as same what it is right now. So almost 40% around.

items.statement: Taparia Group family office acquired 3% equity last week
items.quote: Second thing, recently Taparia Group is onboarded in our stock already last week. So, it's good news that they have invested in our stock for 3% of equity.

items.statement: Management aims to double PAT margin from current ~2.5% over time, not in one or two quarters
items.quote: Yes, we gradually want to increase definitely, you know over a period of time , not in a one month or two month or one quarter or two quarter, double it, definitely double it.

items.statement: Revenue growth of 25% YoY for 9M FY25 expected to be maintained but margin expansion is the priority
items.quote: Yes, we will all try to maintain it, but to be honest, it will come by own. But we are not very much concerned about the revenue growth. It will come, sir. We are more concerned about the margin expansion now

items.statement: Budget announcement of 120 new airport locations and potential ATF under GST seen as positive for air cargo demand
items.quote: This will definitely have a huge positive impact on our operation as we are a pan-India company. And wherever the cargo facilitating in the airport will be there, by default we will also be there.

items.statement: Operating margin pressure acknowledged due to higher share of lower-margin international business; shifting mix to domestic to improve margins
items.quote: Internet, although money come very fast, but margins are lower. So, we are aware of that one. So, we are now thinking of changing our product mix further again to focusing more on the domestic so that our product margin can improve.

items.statement: Plan to increase B2C share within logistics and warehousing to improve margins
items.quote: We will be going by our logistic sector or the warehouse only. I am not telling about something we will go by unrelated sector. But there also we will go more into B2C into the B2B where definitely margins are higher.

items.statement: 9-month volume increased to 43,635 tonnes from 41,953 tonnes YoY; Q3 volume dipped QoQ to 14,376 tonnes from 14,724 tonnes due to seasonality
items.quote: Domestic plus international cumulative we have 43,635 for 9-month ended 31st December 2024. So, we have achieved a volume of 43,635 compared to earlier 9-month of 41,953.

items.statement: Pune warehouse project to resume after GST demand of INR 33 crore dropped on 5 Feb 2025 freeing up capital
items.quote: Now we can that capital which is because regulatory compliance was supreme, now that capital got free, now we can again actively look into that our Pune thing.

items.statement: GST demand of INR 33 crore completely dropped on 5 February 2025
items.quote: we had a demand of GST of 33 crore, which I am happy to share has been dropped as early as yesterday on the 5t h February 2025 completely dropped

items.statement: Implemented automated debtor control system blocking accounts exceeding credit period; 99% bookings now via FreightPILL mobile app
items.quote: If any debtor is going beyond the credit period approved as per the contract, his or her account will get blocked, and only after getting the money or after the very senior management intervention, this account will get unblocked.

items.statement: Company is net debt-free with INR 8 crore net cash balance per cash flow statement
items.quote: Cash balance right now if I go by my cash flow , statutory cash flow, net-net after loan and everything INR 8 crore is there already there apart from the some liquid investment and all this one.

items.statement: Actively pursuing monetisation of non-core assets; discussions in advanced stage
items.quote: We are actively pursuing how to monetize our loan for assets. And I hope very soon I will be able to give you some good news on this account also.

items.statement: Promoters increased net holding via rights issue subscription exceeding shares sold for personal needs
items.quote: Between October to December, we have a right too where promoter has subscribed more than their quota, okay? Ankur Sawaria: Okay. Mahesh Fogla: For that reason, they have got a holding and then they have sold some share, but definitely the subscription was much, much larger, and as a result, net-net, they have increased their holding

items.statement: Aviation turbine fuel (ATF) at 30-40% of aircraft operating cost; bringing ATF under GST would lower costs and boost sector profitability
items.quote: Around 30% to 40% of the cost of operation is on ATF, and if it comes under this GST, then definitely the cost of operation of the aircraft come down bringing the overall efficiency in the aviation sector and improve the profitability of all people.

items.statement: One-off INR 45 lakh loss in Q3 from gratuity/leave encashment provisions and mark-to-market loss on blue-chip investments
items.quote: This INR 45 lakh is basically that one only, and we have certain investment also in blue chip company which mark -to-market we have to do as per the regulation. So, that is temporary mark-to-market loss is out there.

items.statement: Holds double-digit market share in a competitive industry; focuses on sustainable growth over volume shortcuts
items.quote: We have just to tell you right now also double-digit markets there in our area of operation. Okay. So, it's not that we don't, we have a major share of markets that were double digits in the industry, which is very competitive industry.

items.statement: 9-month gross operational income including GST grew 25% YoY to INR 302.16 crore
items.quote: We have a gross operational income including a GST is of INR 302.16 crores against 9 months of the last year of INR 241.54 crores. Tthis 9 months INR 302.16 crores we have achieved again the last year of INR 241.54 crores, giving us an increase in a 9 month to 9 month of 25%.

items.statement: Management expects to achieve over 100 crore EBITDA for FY25, excluding one-time provision reversal.
items.quote: definitely we seem to be on track in terms of the EBITDA for 100 crore.

items.statement: Historic EBITDA margin range is 35-42%; 35% considered standard benchmark going forward.
items.quote: it is fair to assume 35% to be our standard benchmark, which in the last few years or the last 15 months has not necessarily been the case

items.statement: New properties expected to stabilize at 60-65% occupancy and ~30% EBITDA margin in first year.
items.quote: Basically, broadly, they will have around 60 to 65 percent occupancy because the first-year stabilization takes some time. So, it will be fair enough to take 60 to 65 percent occupancy. EBITDA, you can take it around 30 percent.

items.statement: Pune market outlook is very robust, supported by GCCs, services, education, and events; management is very bullish.
items.quote: the long-term prospects of Pune are very robust, and we are very bullish on Pune in that regard.

items.statement: Ayodhya hotel running at 90%+ occupancy in Jan-Feb due to Mahakumbh circuit; ARR 15,000-20,000.
items.quote: Occupancy-wise, sir, right now, we are going at 90 plus occupancy and hopefully, sir, we will give you some more good news of some additional hotels in Ayodhya.

items.statement: Goa Orchid (Passaros) commenced operations 17 Jan 2025; currently 57 rooms, targeting 58.
items.quote: Right now, it is 57. One room is pending because that is a sort of different and a unique room and that will take a little longer. But we are at 57 right now but it will eventually be 58.

items.statement: Pune Orchid expansion from 410 to 500 rooms will take 12-15 months; hotel will operate with 350-380 rooms during renovation.
items.quote: Pune will take approximately anywhere between 12 to 15 months to come to the 500 mark.

items.statement: F&B contributes ~40% of revenue (range 30-45% by hotel); overall company mix ~37% F&B, 63% rooms.
items.quote: It is 40 percent, sir. Broadly, hotel-to-hotel, it fluctuates between 30 and 45 percent. We have also given it in our presentation. There is a matrix which is there, which is around 37-63 as a whole Company

items.statement: Repeat customers contribute 34% of sales; channel mix: 30-35% corporate, 20% travel agents, 25-30% OTA, 10-15% direct/loyalty, 5-7% airline crew.
items.quote: we have a very high repeat of 34% repeat customers in our entire, so 34% of our sales, which comes from repeat customers

items.statement: Digital channels (website, loyalty, OTAs) generate ~150 crore revenue annually.
items.quote: approximately 150 crore is the revenue that comes from the digital streams, which includes your website, your orchid reward program, your online marketing travel agents like MakeMyTrip, Booking.com, ClearTrip, Agoda, Yatra, all these people

items.statement: Goa Passaros ARR jumped from 3,000-3,500 to 7,000-7,500 post-rebranding; overall brand ARR expected to move north of 7,000.
items.quote: Earlier the average rate over there was 3000-3500. Today the average selling rate in Goa Passaros was around 7000- 7500. So, that jump will definitely reflect in the times to come and that is why and this is just now. We are just now opened the hotel and this is the ARR. So, if the ARR we expect to obviously go north of 7000.

items.statement: Operating leverage: fixed costs (rent, power, labor) stay flat while revenue grows; food cost rises with banquet volumes.
items.quote: when your lobby is your lobby, your lobby when you are doing a 50% occupancy, or a 100% occupancy will consume the same amount of electricity. So, when you end up doing more business, your basically metrics of these things come down. What will increase is your food cost.

items.statement: Balance sheet cleaned up; contingent liabilities removed; new balance sheet much thinner.
items.quote: the new balance sheet when you will see it, will be much thinner than the previous one because various things which were contingent liabilities and other aspects, all that has been cleaned up systematically

items.statement: Supreme Court ruling bars any other entity from using 'Orchid' with prefix/suffix in India; Kamat owns the brand.
items.quote: Royal Orchid basically lost the case. They cannot use the word Orchid. Actually no one in India can use the word Orchid with prefix or suffix as per the Supreme Court and this is a landmark judgment we won many years back.

items.statement: World is VUCA; management plans in short innings (T20) rather than long-term test match due to geopolitical uncertainty.
items.quote: the world will be a very VUCA world. So, we should take everything as a short innings T20 rather than thinking of a test match

items.statement: Q3 FY25 consolidated revenue 111 crore (+29% YoY), EBITDA 44 crore (+70% YoY), EBITDA margin 39.77%, PAT 26 crore.
items.quote: The consolidated revenue for the third quarter was 111 crores, representing the increase of around 29% year-on-year basis. EBITDA for Q3 FY'24 was 44 crores, reflecting the growth of around 70% year-on-year basis, with the EBITDA margin reported 39.77%, which comes 40%.

items.statement: 9M FY25 consolidated revenue 270 crore (+22.8% YoY), EBITDA 80 crore (+18.3% YoY), EBITDA margin 29.63%, PAT 36 crore.
items.quote: For the 9 months of Financial Year 2025, the consolidated revenue stood INR 270 crores, representing the growth of 22.8% year-on-year basis. The total EBITDA stood INR 80 crores, which rose by 18.3% year-on-year, with EBITDA margin reported 29.63%.

items.statement: Mahodadhi Palace (Puri) running only 25 rooms during renovation; ARR/occupancy suppressed intentionally; full 160-room luxury heritage hotel to launch post-renovation.
items.quote: Sir, unfortunately, that project behind, we are not able to command the kind of rates that we expect because the property right now, the 25 rooms which are on, that is on basically because behind there is a work going on.

items.statement: No plans for cloud kitchens; standalone restaurants only near existing hotels for operational control; outdoor catering is niche.
items.quote: we have no intentions to go into cloud kitchen, or into any segment like that. That segment, sir, is a different segment altogether, and it is not something suited for us.

items.statement: 9-month throughput grew 7.8% YoY; EXIM up 5%, domestic up 7.8%. Q3 throughput grew 11.6% YoY with EXIM up 8% and domestic up 24.7%.
items.quote: I'm happy to inform that there has been a throughput growth of 7.8% in the 9-month period ending on December 31, 2024, in which EXIM registered a growth of 5% and domestic stream registered a growth of 7.8%.

items.statement: January volumes recovered fully with double-digit growth in both EXIM and domestic, expected to continue through March.
items.quote: And now if fully recovered in the current quarter, we are experiencing a double-digit growth.

items.statement: EXIM market share gained 73 bps pan-India; Mundra up 180 bps, Pipavav up 278 bps in 9M FY25.
items.quote: I am further happy to inform that we gained an EXIM market share also in Pan-India basis by 73 basis points. And at Mundra Port, we gained market share by 180 basis points. And at the Pipavav Port, we gained market share by 278 basis points.

items.statement: Rail freight margin increased 15 bps YoY to 25.76% in 9M FY25; operating margin flat YoY at over 30%.
items.quote: Our rail freight margin increased by 15 basis points year-on-year from 25.61% to 25.76%. Operating margin was flat, same year-on-year, more than 30%.

items.statement: Operating income grew 4.23% and PAT grew 3.6% YoY in 9M FY25.
items.quote: Further, we had operating income growth of 4.23% and PAT growth of 3.6% despite challenges on geopolitical front.

items.statement: Double stack rakes grew 11.25% to 4,608 in 9M FY25; 4 rakes commissioned, total fleet 382; 6,868 containers procured, domestic fleet now 51,236.
items.quote: 11.25% in double stack rakes. Last year, we did 4,142 double stack rakes in the 9 months. And this year, we have done 4,608 double stack rakes. For catering to our demand, which is increasing day by day, we have added infrastructure. In the 9 months, Container Corporation of we have commissioned 4 rakes. Now our total fleet stands at 382. As on December 31, we procured 6,868 containers, and now ou

items.statement: FY25 capex revised up 40% to INR 855 crore from INR 610 crore; INR 444 crore spent by Dec 31.
items.quote: Board of Directors have decided that we will increase our capex by 40%. It was a -- capex budget for this financial year was INR610 crores. Out of which, already INR444 crores we have achieved. Now we have revised it upward 40% to INR855 crores that we will be spending by this year-end.

items.statement: Capex expected to remain around INR 855 crore annually for next 3 years (FY26-FY28).
items.quote: All I can say is, for the next 3 years also in the same range we will be spending. If you remember some 4, 5 years back, we used to spend INR1,000 crores every year. So figure will be remaining around this number.

items.statement: Targets by 2028: 80 terminals, 500+ owned rakes, ~70,000 container fleet.
items.quote: I'm happy to inform that by 2028, that is 3 years from now, we will be having 80 terminals. We will be having 500-plus rakes ownership by CONCOR, and we will be having around 70,000 container fleets.

items.statement: Interim dividend of INR 4.25 per share (par INR 5) declared; total interim dividend INR 9.50 (190% of par).
items.quote: I'm also happy to inform that we have declared an interim dividend of INR4.25 on share of par value INR5. So till now, we have declared a total interim dividend of INR9.50, which is 190% of the par value.

items.statement: Export growth in 9M: RMG 92%, auto parts 21%, food items 22%, paper 20%, fabrics 37%. Import growth: auto parts 34%, raw cotton 77%.
items.quote: exports in RMG, ready-made garments, increased by 92%, export of auto parts increased by 21%, export of our food items, 22%; paper products, 20%, fabrics, 37%. In imports, auto parts increased by 34%, raw cotton increased by 77%.

items.statement: Procuring 1,000 tank containers for bulk cement; supply started from Braithwaite; expected major domestic growth driver.
items.quote: The new initiatives, which will be the growth drivers for the company in the coming months will be bulk cement in tank containers. We are procuring 1,000 tank containers. And from yesterday, we have started receiving the supply of tank containers from our sister PSU Braithwaite.

items.statement: Confident of achieving historic 5 million TEU handling target in FY25.
items.quote: And we are on the correct track to achieve the historic 5 million TEUs handling targets that we will be having in this financial year. I'm quite confident that we will be able to achieve 5 million TEUs, which will be the landmark for the company.

items.statement: No specific Q4 volume guidance given; FY26 guidance to be provided in next call.
items.quote: See, FY '25, I would not like to give any further guidance because now only one quarter is remaining. And whatever we were expecting because of the geopolitical disturbances, we could not reach that number in EXIM. In domestic, of course, we'll be reaching that number. But FY '26, let us wait for 2, 3 months more. I will give a guidance in my next call.

items.statement: No pricing changes made; EXIM realization drop due to volume decline, not pricing; lead distance stable (708 to 704 km).
items.quote: No. We have not done any pricing change. Normally, whatever prices we declare, we keep it stable. We frequently don't go for pricing change. So pricing changes were not done. It was purely as a result of volumes.

items.statement: Empty running cost 9M FY25: EXIM INR 89.70 cr, domestic INR 220.92 cr, total INR 310.61 cr.
items.quote: Yes, 9-month period, EXIM was INR89.70 crores and domestic was INR220.92 crores, total INR310.61 crores.

items.statement: Land license fee (LLF) run rate ~INR 89.42 cr/quarter; targeting INR 350 cr for FY25; 7% annual escalation expected but surrenders may contain growth.
items.quote: In the quarter if you see Q-on-Q December quarter '23, it was INR71.95 crores. And in the current quarter, we have booked INR89.42 crores. items.statement: Decided not to migrate brownfield terminals (e.g., TKD) to Gati Shakti due to uncertainty; will use Gati Shakti only for greenfield projects.
items.quote: At present, our management has taken a decision that we will not be going for that option because there is a lot of uncertainty involved in. If Brownfield terminals are migrating to Gati Shakti, then there is a big element of uncertainty. So we have decided that we will not be using that facility provided by Indian Railways, but for Greenfield projects we are going for Gati Shakti only.

items.statement: Depreciation policy change reduced wagon useful life impact by INR 79 cr for 9M; Q3 depreciation INR 12.5 cr vs INR 36.7 cr for 9M; run rate ~INR 130-140 cr/quarter going forward.
items.quote: if we see for the period, the impact of the change in the age of our useful life of our wagon, the impact is INR79 crores. So effectively, our wagon depreciation for the current quarter is INR12.5 crores. And for the period, it is INR36.7 crores

items.statement: Domestic realization improved QoQ due to reduced empty running; competitive rates offered for empty return legs.
items.quote: Basically, it is because of the reduction in empty running in domestic. We are getting very good circuits and traffic on both the sides. And our domestic team has worked very hard. And one very good initiative that we took was, the containers which were coming -- running empty in empty direction, we have given very competitive rates so that at least we get some money.

items.statement: Geopolitical disruptions causing erratic vessel schedules, longer transit times, higher equipment deployment; resolution would boost growth but timing uncertain.
items.quote: Geopolitical, if it is stabilized, then it will be very good because the vessel schedules which are quite erratic now. And sometimes vessels will stop coming. Then after some months, suddenly, a lot of vessels will be coming. So all these things, uncertainties will be over, and we will be -- vessels will be running as per schedule.

items.statement: FMCG sector showed steady demand; urban stable but soft sequentially, rural improved growing at 2x suburban YoY for third straight quarter
items.quote: Urban demand remained stable yet soft on a sequential basis whereas rural contin ued to witness improvement, growing at 2x suburban on a year-on-year basis for the third consecutive quarter.

items.statement: On track to achieve double-digit consolidated revenue growth for full year FY25
items.quote: We are on track to achieve double digit consolidated revenue growth for the full year.

items.statement: Committed to top quartile volume growth in India business and double-digit consolidated revenue growth in near and medium term
items.quote: We remain committed to achieving top quartile volume growth in the India business and double-digit consolidated revenue growth in the near and medium term, as well as double digit constant currency growth in the international business.

items.statement: Aim to deliver double-digit EBITDA margin in Digital First portfolio by FY27
items.quote: We maintain our aspirations to achieve double digit EBITDA margin in the Digital first portfolio by FY2 7.

items.statement: Foods business scaled to around ₹1,000 crores ARR in Q3; Foods and premium personal care including Digital First brands combined ARR around ₹1,900 crores
items.quote: The composite revenue share of Foods and premium personal care including Digital first brands in the d omestic business stood higher at 21% in 9M'FY25 despite significant pricing growth in the core portfolios . These businesses are now clocking a combined ARR of around ₹1,900 crores

items.statement: Digital First portfolio reached ₹600 crores ARR in Q3; Beardo on track for double-digit EBITDA margins
items.quote: The digital first portfolio scaled ahead of expectation, reached ₹600 crores in ARR in Q3. Beardo is on track to deliver double digit EBITDA margins

items.statement: Expect to hold about 20% operating margin for FY25 despite higher copra costs and denominator effect from higher top line growth
items.quote: So, as a result, and mix of all this, we believe we should be able to hold about 20% operating margin for the year.

items.statement: Foods portfolio gross margin improved 800 bps last year; masala oats now at near company average EBITDA margin
items.quote: As you would recall last year, we improved the gross margin by 800 basis points and we are working towards capability building. Are we there fully? We are not there, but still we are 7 or 8 , I mean 7 on 10 today.

items.statement: Took another round of price hikes in Parachute at end of Q3 as copra prices expected to remain firm near term
items.quote: We have taken another round of price hikes towards the end of Q3 as forecast suggest copra prices to remain firm in the near term.

items.statement: Copra prices follow 18-24 month cycle; nearing end of inflationary cycle, prices expected to cool from early Q1 FY26 when flush season resumes
items.quote: As far as copra is concerned, it follows an 18-to-24-month cycle and we are nearing the end of the inflationary cycle. Prices are expected to cool down once the flush season resumes from early Q1 'FY26.

items.statement: Foods and premium personal care including Digital First brands now 21% of domestic revenue in 9M FY25 despite core portfolio pricing growth
items.quote: The composite revenue share of Foods and premium personal care including Digital first brands in the d omestic business stood higher at 21% in 9M'FY25 despite significant pricing growth in the core portfolios .

items.statement: Alternate channels driving growth and gaining salience; GT channel seeing prolonged sluggishness due to inter-channel dynamics and consumer behavior shift
items.quote: From a channel perspective, alternate channels continue to drive growth and gain salience. The GT channel has seen prolonged sluggishness due to the evolving inter channel dynamics, conflict and shift in consumer behavior.

items.statement: Project SETU extended to 11 states to revive GT growth; expanding food outlets and chemist/cosmetic channels
items.quote: Project SETU has extended into 11 states now. We expect the results of initiatives to revive GT growth to reflect in our performance over the coming quarters while the improving consumption trends persist.

items.statement: International business sustained double-digit constant currency growth; currency headwinds had 2% impact on consolidated EBITDA this quarter
items.quote: The international business sustained its double-digit constant currency growth momentum. The business has continued to chart a resilient top line and profitability performance despite the impact of currency headwinds in key markets. Currency headwinds had a 2% impact on consolidated EBITDA this quarter.

items.statement: Quick commerce growing 50%+; modern trade and marketplace e-commerce still growing double-digit
items.quote: The growth in quick commerce is being 50%+

items.statement: Rural demand growing at 2x suburban YoY for third consecutive quarter; HPC categories outperforming packaged food
items.quote: rural contin ued to witness improvement, growing at 2x suburban on a year-on-year basis for the third consecutive quarter. Resultantly, HPC categories continue d to outperform packaged food on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Facing unreasonable competition in bottom-of-pyramid VAHO segment with disproportionately unsustainable BTL; not competing on BTL but investing in mid/premium segments
items.quote: We are facing unreasonable competition with disproportionately unsustainable BTL, which we don't want to compete with because we believe in long term equity building and in terms of ATL works far more better in long term equity creation than BTL.

items.statement: Saffola edible oils stable despite significant price hikes driven by import duty hike; expect brand to remain steady unless significant vegetable oil price volatility
items.quote: Saffola edible oils also demonstrated stability despite significant price hikes over the past few months driven by the import duty hike, we expect the brand to remain steady unless there is significant volatility in vegetable oil prices.

items.statement: GT channel has higher receivables and working capital intensity; debtor days slightly increased but under tight control
items.quote: Now in terms of working capital intensity of course the receivables etc. is higher for GT channel and that is why you would have seen that debtor days would have slightly increased. But over there also we are having a very tight control

items.statement: Unique M&A strategy for digital brands is win-win; founders earn out over 3-year period while seeding founders' mentality within leadership
items.quote: This has been made possible by our unique M&A strategy which is a win-win for both of us and the founders, and our ability to learn from them with humility and seed founders' mentality within our leadership in the process over a 3-year period where they earn out.

items.statement: Transient profitability pressure from higher-than-expected input inflation; copra inflationary cycle nearing end but gains will come with lag due to inventory position
items.quote: While input inflation has been higher than expected, this has put some transient pressure on profitability.
