Prices are expected to cool down once the flush season resumes from early Q1 'FY26. However, the gains will come to us with some lag since we maintain some level of position

items.statement: Sustainability 2.0 framework yielding positive progress across all key focus areas; dedicated to creating shared value for long-term sustainable differentiated growth
items.quote: Our Sustainability 2.0 framework is yielding positive progress across all key focus areas, we are confident that our dedication to creating shared value for all will drive long term sustainable and differentiated growth.

items.statement: Pan-India residential absorption growing ~6% YoY; affordable segment declining while premium and luxury segments gaining share
items.quote: Market at a Pan-India level continues to see healthy absorption growth at around 6% year-over-year. New launches are a little bit higher, more than 6.2% year-on-year.

items.statement: Pricing stabilizing at 5% YoY in MMR, 10%+ in Bengaluru, 6% in Pune
items.quote: Pricing has now stabilized at 5%. It was very high for the last few years, but it is stabilizing at 5%.

items.statement: GDV additions of INR14,000 crores in 9M FY25, INR15,000 crores including Bangalore airport deal
items.quote: During the 9-month FY '25, we have completed a GDV addition of roughly INR14,000 crores. And if you include the transaction, we did 10 days back in Bangalore, it's another INR1,000 crores.

items.quote: We have signed up a major land parcel in joint development, 37 acre in Bhandup. It's roughly 4 million RERA net area, 6.4 million of saleable area. Target potential is INR12,000 crores.

items.quote: Sales, we've achieved a presale of INR1,749 crores in the 9-month FY '25 versus INR1,243 crores in the 9 months for last financial year, reflects 41% growth.

items.quote: In 9 months, FY '25, our new launch sales contributed INR1,019 crores, 58% of the INR1,749 crores overall sales.

items.quote: The total of amount related to land in terms of outflows was close to about INR600 crores, between INR600 crores to INR650 crores to be precise.

items.quote: We are exploring a couple of other funding options, and we'll let you know once we have some decision on that.

items.quote: We have a whole crew of team that knows what to do and what not to do.

items.quote: Since the market has buoyancy, most of the players are focusing on GDV acquisitions, making sure their balance sheet is strong enough to absorb the cost, the capital required to pursue these GDV additions.

items.statement: Long-term presales guidance given; revenue recognition guidance withheld due to OC approval uncertainty
items.quote: The way we look at the business is how much is the presale that we are targeting. And I've given a long-term guidance on that, right?

items.statement: Budget 2025 income tax benefits expected to positively impact individual buying power; finer details under evaluation
items.quote: We're still evaluating that. But overall, we think that income tax and some of the other benefits will have positive imp act on the buying power of individuals

items.statement: Targets double-digit revenue growth on a yearly basis
items.quote: Our target has always been to be conservatively thinking that we want to have a double-digit growth.

items.quote: Total amount spent on Kakinada project, including assets capitalized till December 31, 2024 is ₹1,340 crores.

items.quote: if you see only the results of Freight Car division we have an EBITDA of INRINR11.85 crores that is almost 12% over.

items.statement: Railway rolling stock budget stable at ~INR46,000 crores; no cut in allocation; long-term plan targets 47% rail share in logistics by 2030
items.quote: it is still in and around INR46,000 crores so far the railway estimation goes and as per information available to us. So it is not necessary -- I mean, let us be practical. It is not necessary to increase the budget allocation every time.

items.statement: Private sector demand growing in coal, mining, minerals, food grain, container, perishable, auto segments; expect large railway tender due per national rail plan
items.quote: We also feel that the private sector investment will grow in the infrastructure, various things like minerals, coal, iron ore and this food grain and container movement, perishable, auto. So these things will get a very good momentum in the coming year.

items.statement: Wheelset shortage from Rail Wheel Factory resolved; railway permitted imported wheelsets (mainly from China) on replenishment basis until April 2026
items.quote: railway has taken a pragmatic decision along with discussion with the industry that they have allowed us to use the imported wheelset. So I was answering to the question of the wheelset problem. So I would like to point out to you, it is so far, so long it's resolved in the sense that for private wagons manufacturing, we used to import wheels and railway has given us permission to use tho se impor

items.statement: Producing three new generation double-deck wagon designs (Act 1, Act 2, Act 3) for SUVs, tractors; developed refrigerated milk tank wagons for Amul; design centralized in global capability center
items.quote: New generation is of three types. It is called Act 1, Act 2, Act 3. So we have the most order of Act 1 and is also the most expensive wagon order and we are delivering it continuously. Act 2 is our first time to develop and Act 3 is also our design.

items.statement: Delivered 2,714 freight cars in Q3 FY25 (54.6% YoY growth); 8,015 freight cars in 9M FY25 (70% YoY growth)
items.quote: In Q3 FY '25, we delivered 2,714 freight cars, marking a 54.6% Y -o-Y growth compared to same period last year when we did 1,756 freight cars. Our cumulative deliveries for the first 9 months of FY '25 stood at 8,015 freight cars, reflecting a 70% increase from the same period last year.

items.statement: Jindal Rail (Texmaco West) produced 526 wagons in Q3 FY25 (INR265 crores revenue, INR35.72 crores PBT); 1,417 wagons in 9M FY25 (INR692 crores revenue, INR98.45 crores PBT)
items.quote: So for the quarter ended, Jindal has done around 526 wagons and a turnover of INR265 crores. They have reported a PAT of -- sorry, PBT of INR35.72 crores. For the 9 months ended, they had done 1,417 wagons, a turnover of INR692 crores and a PBT of INR98.45 crores.

items.statement: Wheelset supply disruption identified as key operational risk; mitigated by import permission until April 2026; geopolitical uncertainty noted as external risk
items.quote: Threat, of course, is perhaps is a kind of an unknown thing that what would be the global dynamics in terms of the geopolitical situation, we do not know. But India, I think, is on a right trajectory.

items.statement: Management declined to provide specific FY26 volume or margin guidance; referred to previous investor guidelines; confident of growth trajectory and improvement
items.quote: Mr. Poddar, I cannot comment on -- I mean on a futuristic numbers or a statement, but I can only stand by to the plan which company shared already with the investors earlier and we have given a guideline that time. So -- and we are very much confident to be maintaining and working to improve upon.

items.statement: Design capabilities centralized in global capability center; strategic acquisitions (Saira for interiors) to build passenger mobility expertise
items.quote: You will be happy to hear that our Texmaco Rail & entire design is getting centralized in a global capability center . We will be one of the most leading design hub in these concepts which you are talking

items.statement: Other expenses increased from INR27 crores to INR35.98 crores due to management initiatives for future growth
items.quote: There has been certain initiatives taken by management for the future growth and the prospect of the company with the results of which you will see in the coming quarters, because of which the expen se you see has gone up from INR27 crores to around INR35.98 crores.

items.statement: No shift in government mindset toward rail freight; rail share target of 47% by 2030 remains; rail freight revenue grew to INR1.88 lakh crores
items.quote: No, we do not see any such shift in the mindset at all, because it is not sustainable. In railway, we have to move more and more for better connectivity. I mean, lesser number of logistic cost. And for carbon emission, targets and everything for the global requirement.

items.statement: National Rail Plan targets INR38,000-40,000 crores annual wagon procurement; private investment boost seen as positive for order pipeline
items.quote: if we calculate the national rail plan, so it comes around INR38,000 to INR40,000 per annum only. And with the boost of the private investment, so which is a very, very healthy and on track, very good thing for us.

items.statement: Expect robust business performance in medium term with good visibility from enquiry and order book for coming couple of years
items.quote: As for the outlook of the business goes, we expect to maintain a robust business performance in the medium term, not only for this year, but for the coming years.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 order booking ₹5.26 billion, flat YoY; export order booking grew 9% YoY to ₹3.46 billion (66% of total)
items.quote: We have a healthy quarterly order booking of ₹5.26 billion during the third quarter and a record carry forward order book as on 31st of December of ₹18.19 billion, which is an increase of 15% YoY.

items.statement: 9M FY25 order booking ₹17.3 billion, up 20% YoY; domestic down 3% to ₹6.6 billion, export up 41% to ₹10.7 billion (62% of total)
items.quote: As far as order booking for the nine month period for the Company is concerned, we achieved an order booking of ₹17.3 billion as opposed to an order booking of ₹14.4 billion in the same period of FY 24, which is an increase of 20%.

items.statement: Closing order book as of Dec 31, 2024 at ₹18.19 billion, up 15% YoY; domestic ₹6.4 billion (-22% YoY), export ₹11.8 billion (+55% YoY, 65% of total)
items.quote: The outstanding total order booking position and at ₹18.2 billion as of the 31st of December 2024, which is 15% higher than the previous year, and the domestic outstanding order book stands at ₹6.4 billion, which is lower by 22% as compared to the previous year, while export outstanding order book stood at ₹11.8 billion which is a 55% increase YoY and contributes 65% to the closing order book.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA ₹1.31 billion, up 30% YoY; margin 26.1%, up 270 bps YoY
items.quote: We also had, as I said, the highest ever quarterly EBITDA of ₹1.31 billion, which was up 30% YoY with a margin of 26.1%, which was an increase of 2 70 basis points YoY.

items.statement: 9M FY25 EBITDA margin 25.7%, up 280 bps YoY
items.quote: EBITDA as well has increased by 38% and EBITDA margins have increased by 280 basis points to 25.7% for this nine-month period.

items.statement: Domestic order booking subdued in Q3 but enquiry pipeline up 59% YoY in Q3 and 75% YTD; optimistic on Q4 finalisation
items.quote: In Q3 alone in the domestic side, we saw around 59% YoY growth on the enquiry pipeline, whereas YTD growth is something like around 75%. So enquiry pipeline-wise, compared to muted Q1, Q2, Q3 is a very, very interesting quarter.

items.statement: Export demand strong across renewable energy, waste-to-energy, biomass, geothermal, small modular reactors, and oil & gas
items.quote: Order booking continues to reflect good demand in the renewable energy space, particularly from waste -to-energy segment as well as biomass -based energy generation segments.

items.statement: Product segment Q3 order booking ₹4 billion (+6% YoY), turnover ₹3.3 billion (+14% YoY); 9M order booking ₹12.8 billion (+30% YoY), turnover ₹9.7 billion (+21% YoY)
items.quote: As far as the segments go, the Product order booking has increased by 6% YoY in the third quarter, and was up to ₹4 billion, and the Product segment turnover was at ₹3.3 billion during the quarter, an increase of 14%.

items.statement: Aftermarket Q3 order booking ₹1.3 billion (-17% YoY) but turnover record ₹1.8 billion (+22% YoY); confident of growth in higher value-added refurbishment
items.quote: The Aftermarket segment, which is a segment which constitutes not only our own spares and services, but also our refurbishment business, which caters to third party, has registered an order booking of ₹1.3 billion in the third quarter, a decline of 17% when compared to the corresponding period to previous year.

items.statement: Capex to increase to ₹120-150 crore over next couple of years for capacity expansion (additional bay) and R&D testing infrastructure
items.quote: But it is well within a range of somewhere in the region of, I would say, ₹120 - ₹150 crore over the next couple of years.

items.statement: Adding one more assembly bay at Sompura facility; no new land needed as existing land converted to freehold
items.quote: One more bay will come up now.

items.statement: Export sales 49% of Q3 revenue (up from 44% YoY); rupee depreciation positive with hedged book, benefits to flow through other income
items.quote: Export as a percentage of sales increased 49% in this quarter as compared to 44% in the previous year.

items.statement: Rupee depreciation positive for dollar-based exports; hedging policy in place with mark-to-market gains this quarter
items.quote: No, it is positive. There have been some mark -to-market gains already in this quarter. We run a hedging policy, which is pretty much hedged.

items.statement: Received notice of award for 160 MWh CO2-based long duration energy storage system at NTPC Kudgi for ~₹2.9 billion; scope includes design, engineering, fabrication, erection, commissioning, testing
items.quote: We are pleased to report that in January 2025, the Company received a notice of award to set up 160 mega-watt-hour long duration energy storage system (LDES) at NTPC's Kudgi Supercritical Thermal Power Plant premises. The greenfield development will be undertaken by Triveni Turbines for a consideration of approximately ₹2.9 billion.

items.statement: CO2 turbine current cost ~$200,000/MWh; target $120,000-$125,000/MWh for parity with lithium-ion; product life 30-35 years with minimal degradation
items.quote: Current cost is somewhere in the region about $200,000 a MW hour. Our attempt would be to get this to somewhere in the region of about $120,000 to $125,000 per MW hour.

items.statement: Board approved interim dividend of 200% (₹2 per ₹1 share) for FY25, up 54% YoY
items.quote: The Board of Directors of the Company have approved a payment of an interim dividend of 200%, which is ₹2 per equity share of ₹1 each for the financial year ending March 31, 2025, and this represents a 54% increase in the interim dividend.

items.statement: Workforce doubled over last 3-4 years; service engineer demand unlimited, planning to hire in hundreds over next several years
items.quote: Actually, the number of service engineers that we may wish to employ over the next several years will be in the 100s.

items.statement: Domestic market share ~50% maintained; competitive intensity increased but pricing not preferred competition lever; may back off on price to protect value-added services
items.quote: Our current market share in the domestic market would be somewhere around 50%. That's where we've typically maintained it for the nine months period, which would be somewhere there only.

items.statement: NTPC CO2 storage project not immensely profitable initially; taken to prove capabilities; not dilutive to earnings; normal domestic margins expected over time
items.quote: The fact is that this is not an immensely profitable order as this has been taken in the short term. We hope to be able to value engineer as we do go about executing this project.

items.statement: U.S. operations incurring loss >₹20 crore in FY25, fully factored into results; optimistic on FY26 with Q4 order flow and enquiry traction
items.quote: Like I said in the previous call that we would be incurring a loss in this market in excess of about ₹20 crore (₹200 million), which is fully factored into not only the nine-month results, but will be into the full -year results.

items.statement: South Africa SADC utility outages reduced >200 days no outage; order quantum down but mix shifted to higher value-added parts business with better margins
items.quote: Although the quan tum of order book has gone down in FY 25, but the mix of business that we are doing is much more value added, and we are getting better margins from that market.

items.statement: U.S. enquiry pipeline growing, better awareness for offerings; certifications and permits causing delay but capability building underway
items.quote: In the United States, our enquiry book is growing, and we are seeing that there is better awareness for our offerings in the U.S. market, and we are getting more enquiries.

items.statement: Supply chain largely indigenous; agnostic to tariffs from neighbouring countries; capable of localisation if customers demand
items.quote: As far as the supply chain base goes, we have a largely indigenous supply chain base. We're quite agnostic to any tariffs that may b e put with neighbouring countries, etc.

items.statement: Domestic market degrew in 9M FY25; Q4 FY24 was weak due to elections; caution against extrapolating Q4 growth to full year
items.quote: You have to keep in mind that Q4 of last year of FY 24 was a weak quarter. It is a weak quarter, given the fact that elections are just around the corner.

items.statement: R&D expenditure increasing in both manpower and capital investment for testing infrastructure; focusing on CO2 systems (subcritical, supercritical, transcritical) and steam cycle efficiency
items.quote: Our efforts in terms of expenditure on this will increase, as I've spoken about in the previous quarters. We will continue to invest not only in the manpower that is neces sary to expand our efforts into technology and R&D, but also capital investment, which will be required to adequately test and ensure that we are reaching the pinnacle of what these investments can achieve.

items.statement: NBFC AUM target Rs. 300 cr by FY25, Rs. 550 cr by FY26, Rs. 800 cr by FY27
items.quote: Currently, our AUM stands at approximately Rs. 250 crores, and we plan to close FY ‘25 with an AUM of around Rs. 300 crores. By FY ’26, we aim to reach Rs. 550 crores. And by FY ‘27 we project our AUM will reach Rs. 800 crores.

items.statement: iServeU net revenue target Rs. 70-80 cr by FY26, Rs. 150 cr by FY27
items.quote: We expect iServeU to generate net revenues of approximately Rs. 70 crores to 80 crores by FY ‘26, with projections to double that figure by FY ‘27, reaching around Rs. 150 crores in net revenue.

items.statement: iServeU EBITDA margin target 12-15% FY26, 18-20% FY27
items.quote: In terms of profitability, we anticipate iServeU’s EBITDA margin to be in the range of 12% to 15% for FY ‘26, improving to 18% to 20% by FY ‘27.

items.statement: Niyogin AI ARR target Rs. 3-5 cr by FY27
items.quote: By FY ‘27, we expect Niyogin AI to generate anywhere between Rs. 3 crores to Rs. 5 crores in ARR, driven by both deeper penetration with existing clients and new customer acquisitions.

items.statement: iServeU secured long-term contracts worth >Rs. 350 cr net revenue over 3-5 years with banks like BoB, Canara, Kotak, Axis
items.quote: We have successfully onboarded clients such as banks like Bank of Baroda, Cana ra Bank, Kotak Mahindra and Axis Bank, securing long term contracts with a worth of more than Rs. 350 crores in net revenue, with a significant amount of upside potential

items.statement: iServeU contract pipeline expanded to ~7 lakh devices with wins from BoB, Axis, Suryoday SFB
items.quote: Additionally, our contract pipeline expanded to approximately 7 lakh devices with key wins from Bank of Baroda, Axis Bank and Suryoday Small Finance Bank.

items.statement: iServeU device margin range 55-70% varying by contract
items.quote: the margin would vary from sort of 55% to 70%, that's what we have seen so far. But as Tash rightly said, it varies from contract to contract, but it would be a range of 55% to 70%.

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA loss Rs. 2 cr in Q3 FY25 vs loss Rs. 0.5 cr Q2 FY25
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA, excluding ESOP cost, for Q3 FY ‘25 showed a loss of Rs. 2 crores compared to a loss of Rs. 50 lakhs in Q2 FY ’25.

items.statement: NBFC loan processing grew 245% YoY and 26% QoQ to 90,093 loans in Q3 FY25
items.quote: In Q3 of FY ‘25, we processed 90,093 loans through our network, reflecting a 245% year-on-year growth and a 26% quarter-on-quarter increase.

items.statement: NBFC finance professional network grew 10% YoY to 6,307 as of Dec 2024
items.quote: Our network of finance professionals grew by 10% year-on-year, reaching 6,307 as of December 31, 2024.

items.statement: iServeU TSP/SaaS revenue grew from 8% to 53% of total net revenue
items.quote: Last year that TSP revenue contribution was only 8% of the total net revenue. However, till date, till third quarter of this year, TSP revenue has grown substantially, and now it represents around 53% of our total revenue.

items.statement: Embedded lending disbursed >Rs. 200 cr till Q3 FY25: 56% EDI, 16% EWI, 6% EMI, 22% bullet
items.quote: cumulatively, we have disbursed more than Rs. 200-plus crores in embedded lending with current LSPs till Q3 of FY ’25, with 56% allocated to EDI approximately, 16% to EWI program, 6% to EMI program and remaining 22% to bullet repayment.

items.statement: NBFC has 5+ LSPs with 2 EDI, 2 EWI, 3 EMI, 1 bullet programs; ticket Rs. 15k-5L, tenor 30-250+ days
items.quote: Currently we have more than five LSPs, which is loan service providers, with two EDI programs which is equated daily installment programs ; two EWI s, which is weekly programs; and three EMI programs with one bullet repayment program running

items.statement: iServeU device disbursement rate >50,000 devices per quarter maintained
items.quote: However, this was partially offset by strong performance in our SaaS vertical well maintained a device disbursement rate of over 50,000 devices performance quarter.

items.statement: iServeU FY27 growth funded by ~Rs. 50 cr debt and ~Rs. 50 cr equity
items.quote: This growth is expected to be funded through a combination of debt and equity, with about Rs. 50 crores expected from each.

items.statement: NBFC to receive ~Rs. 60 cr equity from warrant maturity next month
items.quote: As many of you know, we are set to receive an equity infusion of approximately Rs. 60 crores from the maturity of our warrants next month.

items.statement: Demerger subject to shareholder, creditor, RBI, DFC, NCLT, SEBI approvals
items.quote: This transaction is obviously subject to customary regulatory approvals, including approvals from shareholders and creditors, RBI, DFC, NCLT and SEBI.

items.statement: RBI cloud policy and bank cloud policies now enable iServeU SaaS model
items.quote: Today, all of our customers have a set cloud policy. Even RBI and also regulators across the world, they have specific policies around the cloud because that is the need of the hour.

items.statement: Consolidated AUM including off-book Rs. 242 cr; cash & equivalents Rs. 78 cr as of Dec 2024
items.quote: Our AUM, including off book exposures, stands at Rs. 242 crores. As of December 31, 2024, consolidated cash and cash equivalents stood at Rs. 78 crores.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth expected ~12-13% vs earlier 18-20% guidance; FY26 revenue growth guidance maintained at 18-20%
items.quote: FY'25 I think we will miss the 18%, 20% growth, we are about 12% in nine months and my sense is as we see things probably we will end the year somewhere in the PAT of 12%, 13% of growth in FY'25. FY'26, we maintain that we should be in the band of 18%, 20% type of a top line growth.

items.statement: Capex spent Rs190 cr in 9M FY25; full-year FY25 capex ~Rs250 cr; FY26 capex ~Rs100 cr (pending project spend)
items.value: Rs190 cr (9M), Rs250 cr (FY25), Rs100 cr (FY26)
items.quote: So, for the nine months we have spent close to around including the new project around Rs.190 crores, we expect including the project it should be in the range of around Rs.250-odd crores and for FY'26 including some of the CAPEX which we need to do for the project pending CAPEX for the project, it should be in the range of around Rs.100-odd crores.

items.statement: Particle board plant commercial production started 23 Jan 2025; targeting 40-50% utilization in FY26, breakeven at ~50% utilization
items.quote: And we should be looking at 40% to 50% kind of utilization in FY'26 and we should be near breakeven at I think a 50% kind of a utilization level.

items.statement: Doors order book and pending orders encouraging; door plant full capacity value Rs80-100 cr; plywood sales ~2x YoY in FY25, targeting another 2x in FY26
items.quote: So, on the door business, it's decent traction, our order book and pending orders is quite encouraging and so we think the business will keep improving in these three months and even in the coming one and two years.

items.statement: Q3 growth subdued at ~7% YoY; domestic laminates & decorative veneer under pressure; export laminates +12% YoY; Jan demand 'okay'
items.quote: On Q3, the quarter was slightly subdued in terms of growth . While the flooring door and plywood businesses did better , the export of laminate s also did better comparatively with slightly over 12% growth. Domestic laminates and domestic decorative veneer is where we had sales

items.statement: Raw material costs largely stable; plywood wood costs stable after Q2 price hikes; freight stable; laminate gross margin 53-55% band sustainable
items.quote: Raw material costs are by and large being stable in most of our segments. In the plywood segment, cost continue s to remain slightly higher, but we have already taken price increases for that in Q2. So, from a raw material side, by and large, we think that part will be stable

items.statement: Working capital cycle 67 days in Q3 vs 59 days in Q2; debtors under control; inventories slightly higher including particle board raw material
items.quote: In the current quarter, working capital cycle stood at 67 days as compared to 59 days in Q2 of this year.

items.statement: Net debt Rs1,012 cr in Q3; peak debt ~Rs1,050 cr in FY25; expected to fall below Rs1,000 cr in FY26; net debt/EBITDA ~4x currently
items.quote: Debt is also at the highest level because most of the CAPEX has already been done. And since we don't have any large CAPEX going forward, so whatever cash will be generated, that will be used to bring this debt down and we believe that it will be lower than this year.

items.statement: Flooring EBITDA positive in Q3 & 9M; doors losses reducing; veneer & allied EBITDA margin 2.6% in Q3, targeting 4-5% in FY26
items.quote: So, going ahead, our sense is this will keep improving , like floor has become EBITDA positive in Q3 and in nine months . The losses in door vertical has reduced. So, we think now with these three categories

items.statement: Europe largest export market (Central, Eastern, Western Europe + UK); US ~5-6% of export revenue; winning share in Europe, US flattish
items.quote: Europe has become our largest market which is all central, eastern, western Europe and UK combined. So, we are doing pretty okay there. US, I would say we are flattish more or less.

items.statement: Board announced 1:1 bonus share issue; first bonus in company's 10-year listed history (completing 10 years March 2025)
items.quote: Our company is completing 10-years of listing in March 2025 and the board has announced 1:1 bonus share issue and this will be our first bonus share issue by the company.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; focus on execution and channel expansion (plywood channel ~80% done in South, Maharashtra launch April 2025)
items.quote: The channel expansion or the creation I think up to 80% is actually done in South India. Also, started opening markets of Maharashtra in April 2025.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 saw 404 movie releases vs 502 in Q3 FY24 and 470 in Q2 FY25; decline in releases reduced theatrical and digitalization revenue.
items.quote: In total, 404 movies were released (including versions/languages) during the quarter, compared to 502 in Q3FY24 and 470 in Q2FY25. The decline in number of releases contributed to decrease in both theatrical and digitalization revenue.

items.statement: Advertisement revenue grew 20% YoY and 88% QoQ in Q3 FY25 driven by strong film performance.
items.quote: Riding on the success of films in November and "Pushpa 2" in December, Q3 FY25 experienced robust advertisement revenue growth, driven by the exceptional performance of standout films that captivated audiences and attracted advertisers. This success resulted in a 20% YoY increase and an 88% percent improvement on a QoQ basis.

items.statement: Product sales grew 54% YoY and 91% QoQ in Q3 FY25.
items.quote: Additionally, product sales grew by 54% YoY and 91% QoQ.

items.statement: Total revenue increased 17% YoY and 43% QoQ in Q3 FY25.
items.quote: Overall, our total revenue for the quarter saw a healthy 17% YoY increase and a 43% percent increase on QoQ basis.

items.statement: Advertisement screen network grew to 3,863 screens, up 13% YoY and 3% QoQ.
items.quote: On the screen network front, our advertisement screen network grew to 3,863 screens, marking a 13% year-over-year increase. This includes 2,246 multiplex screens and 1,617 single screens, with the addition of 456 advertisement screens over the past year an d a 3% increase on a quarter-over-quarter basis.

items.statement: Advertisement screen network at 3,735 screens, up 13% YoY but down 1% QoQ.
items.quote: On the screen network front, the advertisement screen network grew to 3,735 screens, marking a 13% year -over-year. This includes 2,122 multiplex screens and 1,613 single screens, with the addition of 432 advertisement screens over the past year. However, there was a 1% decline quarter-over-quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated Q3 FY25 revenue Rs 1,387 million vs Rs 1,184 million in Q3 FY24; EBITDA Rs 305 million, up 199% QoQ and 65% YoY; net profit Rs 153 million vs Rs 46 million in Q3 FY24 and net loss of Rs 9 million in Q2 FY25.
items.quote: The consolidated revenue for Q3 FY25 stood at Rs 1,387 million compared to Rs 1,184 million in Q3 FY24, showing a 17% increase on YoY basis, primarily driven by advertisement revenue and product sales. EBITDA Q3 FY25 stands out as the best quarter in the current financial year with EBITDA reaching Rs 305 million, that is 199 % QoQ and 65% YoY increase. The company reported a net profit of INR 153

items.statement: 9MFY25 revenue Rs 3,300 million vs Rs 2,909 million in 9MFY24; EBITDA Rs 473 million vs Rs 524 million; PAT Rs 103 million in both periods.
items.quote: Regarding nine -month performance, consolidated revenues amounted to Rs 3,300 million, compared to Rs. 2,909 million in 9MFY24. EBITDA for 9MFY25 was Rs. 473 million, compared to Rs. 524 million in 9MFY24, mainly due to lower exhibitor revenue. On the PAT front, the company reported a net profit of Rs. 103 million in both 9MFY25 and 9MFY24.

items.statement: Consolidated cash at end of Q3 FY25 was Rs 917 million; net cash Rs 259 million after debt.
items.quote: The consolidated cash at the end of the quarter was ₹917 million, and the net cash was ₹259 million after considering outstanding debt.

items.statement: Organizational restructuring commenced; benefits expected from middle of next financial year.
items.quote: I would also like to inform you that we have commenced the organizational level restructuring exercise, and the benefits of the restructuring exercise will start occurring from middle of next financial year.

items.statement: Upcoming Q4 FY25 film pipeline includes Sky Force, Deva, Vidaamuyarchi, Sanghvi and Sons, Chhaava, Captain America: Brave New World, and Sikander (28 March 2025).
items.quote: Looking ahead, though the quarter began on a quieter note with the release of films like "Game Changer", "Emergency" and Azaad", the upcoming release pipeline looks promising with releases such as "Sky Force", "Deva", "Vidaamuyarchi", "Sanghvi and Sons", "Chhaava", English film "Captain America-Brave New World" and Salman Khan starer "Sikander", which is expected to be released on 28th March 2025.

items.statement: FY26 content pipeline expected to be one of the best in 3-4 years with Hollywood, South, regional and Hindi films lined up.
items.quote: But that FY26 lineup is expected to be one of the best lineups that w e have seen in the last 3,4 years. So, it is a very healthy lineup.

items.statement: Advertisement minutes sold at 5.67 in Q3 FY25, up from last year; corporate ad revenue Rs 35 crore in Q3 FY25, highest ever.
items.quote: this quarter has been the largest grossing corporate advertisement quarter in the history of UFO when we have done Rs 35 crores.

items.statement: Product sales margins remain intact above 22%, slightly higher at 25% in Q3 FY25 vs normal 21-23%.
items.quote: The important poin t there is in the business, though the sales have gone up, the margins have remained intact. And we still have in excess of 22%, in fact, a higher margin in this quarter. Those margins are also slightly higher, what we see 25% should ideally in a normal scenario be between 21-23%.

items.statement: Product sales run rate normally Rs 25-35 crore per quarter; Q3 FY25 Rs 43 crore was elevated due to Middle East order timing, not annualizable.
items.quote: So, what you have seen last year, sale of product being in the range of Rs 28 crores, so anywhere between Rs 30-35 crores, Rs 25-35 crores could be the run rate that we generally take at our end.

items.statement: Re-releases indicate audience urge to return to cinemas; they fill dry weeks and generate ad revenue.
items.quote: Now re -releases give us an opportunity that normally in any year you don't have a good content week on week. You have some dry period s. Now if the re -release is doing good, then people can you know keep offering re-releases in the market. Coming to our role, when the re-release comes, we are very much in a position to release it on our network. In fact, many of these movies could be on our libr

items.statement: Central government advertising remains a challenge with no guarantee of revival; state government advertising continues to grow.
items.quote: Our state revenue continues to keep advertising and growing with us.

items.statement: Focus on deepening retail advertising to reduce content dependency; retail ads currently near insignificant in 5.67 minutes.

items.statement: Targets 12-15% volume growth for FY26
items.quote: And next year also we are expecting to grow by 12% to 15% for next year.

items.statement: Projects FY25 EBITDA of Rs 225-230 crore on conservative basis

items.statement: Silchar grinding unit commissioning by Dec 2025 (FY26); Jorhat grinding unit in FY27
items.quote: No, that is fixed, FY '26 we have chosen for Silchar, and for Jorhat FY '27, that will still remain the same.

items.statement: Incurred Rs 440 crore capex in 9M FY25; expects Rs 200-250 crore in Q4 FY25

items.statement: Plans Rs 600 crore capex in FY26 and Rs 300-400 crore in FY27
items.quote: FY '26 should be around Rs. 600 crores. And say, another Rs. 300 crores to Rs. 400 crores you can take for FY '27.

items.statement: New 3.3 mtpa clinker line at Lumshnong operating at ~70% utilization in Q4 FY25

items.statement: New 2 mtpa grinding unit at Guwahati also at ~70% utilization
items.quote: Similarly is the case with new grinding unit at Guwahati . Now, with increased volume, we will definitely look for some share in non-trade markets also.

items.statement: Northeast industry demand flat in 9M FY25; company grew ~10% YoY
items.quote: If you consider the demand of the industry as a whole, then the demand was flat tish. And we are expecting to grow by 6%, 7% this year

items.statement: Northeast prices stable with slight positive bias; no price cuts expected

items.statement: Outside Northeast prices bottomed in Q3; stable or rising in Q4 with Bihar hike impact
items.quote: prices from here, even it will be either flat or there will be increase in prices.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA/ton Rs 1,000 vs Rs 1,576 YoY; 9M FY25 Rs 1,005 vs Rs 1,304 YoY
items.quote: On per ton EBITDA front, it is Rs. 1,000 during this quarter as against Rs. 1,576 per ton same quarter last year.

items.statement: Fuel mix: 77% FSA coal, 13% biomass, ~20% Nagaland coal (sum >100% per transcript)
items.quote: 77% from the fuel supply arrangement. And 13% is biomass, and 20% around is Nagaland coal. So, this is the mix for this quarter.

items.statement: Q3 government incentive income Rs 43 crore; expects Rs 50+ crore/quarter in Q4
items.quote: Third quarter total incentive is Rs. 43 crores.

items.statement: Gross debt Rs 420 crore, net debt ~Rs 400 crore as of Dec 2024
items.quote: So, we have total Rs. 420 crores, currently December is I think around Rs. 420 crores, and net debt is around Rs. 400 crores.

items.statement: Trade share 51% in Q3 (down from ~90% earlier); non-trade rising due to new capacity
items.quote: Share of trade in Q3 was around 51% and rest has been non-trade.

items.statement: Trade-non-trade price gap in Northeast Rs 25-30 per bag
items.quote: Northeast trade prices generally Rs. 25 to Rs. 30 gap is there.

items.statement: Dalmia expansion not expected to disrupt pricing discipline in Northeast
items.quote: I do not think that there should be any call on price discipline. So , we do not expect much of prices getting down.

items.statement: Northeast consolidation unlikely: small plants (<1 mtpa), land/licence hurdles, 4-5 yr lead time
items.quote: If you go and put a new plant , if you are able to do it considering all the hurdles also, then also minimum four to five years is the minimum timeline. So, I do not think that in the immediate future or near future something big is going to happen in Northeast.

items.statement: Premium cement share 12% in Q3 (up from 9% YoY)
items.quote: Premium share in this quarter is 12%.

items.statement: Lead distance 222 km in Q3
items.quote: Lead distance, 222 kilometers.

items.statement: Kilocalorie cost ~1.5, flat QoQ
items.quote: K-cal cost is the same, around 1.5. That was more or less in the same line as last quarter.

items.statement: Siliguri grinding unit utilization ~45-50% in Q3
items.quote: Siliguri plant, because last year also it was around 45% till now, but we are hopeful that it will be 50%.

items.statement: Road repair on Silchar-Khliehriat highway constrained Q3 clinker dispatch; expects resolution in Q4
items.quote: there were some issues so far as Silchar, Khliehriat road highway is concerned, there is some long-time repair work which was due for long time. Now the government has released funds, and the work is going on full -fledged.

items.statement: Q3 one-off costs: Rs 10 crore shutdown + Rs 30+ crore clinker purchase = ~Rs 40 crore EBITDA impact
items.quote: Because 1.5 lakh tons we have purchased clinker, that is almost about Rs. 30 crores. At Rs. 30 plus crores is the shutdown cost, then Rs. 40 crores is the one-off kind of thing in this quarter.

items.statement: Cement blend: ~11% OPC, rest PPC in Q3

items.statement: AAC block project in advanced stage; commissioning expected in Q4 FY25
items.quote: So, far as AAC block project is concerned, it is in advance stage. Except for some tidbits, I think in this quarter the project should be commissioned.

items.statement: WHR 12 MW to be operational in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Yes, yes. WHR will be operational in this quarter.

items.statement: Rajasthan greenfield project on track: mine bid won (65 mt deposit), exploration and land acquisition underway
items.quote: we have already won the bid for Rajasthan mines, deposit w as around 65 millions. The exploration for testing is going on. And side by side this land acquisition process is also going on. So, we stand committed to the Rajasthan project.

items.statement: US shrimp demand improving as inventory levels decline, suggesting recovery in consumption and higher import volumes ahead
items.quote: In regards to the demand from the U.S. specifically, which is one of the largest global markets for shrimp, it has continued to show improvement as inventory levels have been gradually declining.

items.statement: EU market remained robust with 73% YoY sales growth in Q3 FY25 and 42% YoY growth in 9M FY25
items.quote: The European Union market remained robust. The Company recorded a 73% year-over-year sales growth during Q3 FY '25 and 42% year-over-year growth on 9 months FY '25.

items.statement: EU share in sales mix increased to 45% in Q3 FY25 from 36% in Q3 FY24 and to 45% in 9M FY25 from 30% in 9M FY24
items.quote: The share of the EU market in the overall sales mix increased to 45% in the Q3 FY 25 from 36% in Q3 FY 24 and to 45% in 9 months FY '25 versus 30% in 9 months FY '24, resulting in a more geographically diverse sales mix.

items.statement: Long-pending ready-to-eat approvals for new facility awaited for almost 5 years due to regulatory issues between India and EU
items.quote: We remain optimistic about the market's growth potential and the opportunities it offers, especially once our long pending ready-to-eat approvals are also secured for our new facility, which we have been waiting literally for the past almost 5 years due to some regulatory issues between both the country, India and the EU.

items.statement: Average realization grew 13% YoY and 8% QoQ to Rs. 749 per kg in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Our average realization registered a growth of 13% year-on-year and 8% quarter-on-quarter in Q3 FY '25 to Rs. 749 per kilo.

items.statement: Average raw material purchase cost rose 21% YoY and 15% QoQ to Rs. 372 per kg in Q3 FY25 due to supply constraints from conservative farmer stocking
items.quote: Our average purchase cost of raw materials grew 21% year-on-year and 15% quarter-on-quarter to Rs. 372 per kilo in Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: Rising shrimp prices expected to encourage farmers to increase seed stocking in upcoming cropping season already in process
items.quote: the rising shrimp prices are definitely expected to encourage shrimp farmers to increase seed stocking, which was as explained earlier, which was lacking in most of 2024, and we are expecting it to be increasing in the upcoming cropping season, which is already in the process right now.

items.quote: Our gross margins stood lower at 25% in Q3 FY '25, mainly due to the higher raw material prices which I have just explained. The gross margin in nine months FY 25 were at 28%.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization around 35%, expected to improve if supply conditions get better in Q4
items.quote: currently we are still running at around 35% capacity utilization currently, but we expect that to be improving based on the supply conditions.

items.statement: Diversifying sales to EU market to mitigate CVD impact on US sales; EU volumes growing significantly each quarter

items.statement: Order book intact and good; company waiting for supply to fulfill commitments

items.statement: Hatchery enquiries for shrimp seed improving; increasing broodstock imports to produce more post-larvae; targeting 100% buyback of hatchery output for traceability
items.quote: To put it straight off, hatchery, definitely we are having a very good improvement in the enquiries with regard to the seed. And for a few other purposes, we have also been requesting and kind of insisting that all the produce from our hatchery seed, all in its entirety, should be coming back to us as a raw material.

items.statement: Indian shrimp has better realization than Ecuador in US market due to wider product portfolio, established reputation, reliability and quality consistency despite longer logistics
items.quote: India definitely has an edge with regard to consistent deliveries and also consistency in quality. Of course there are certain, like one of the major disadvantage when you ask between the countries which you are trying to compare is the logistical, you know, I mean the time of if the shipments from that country would go like in 10 days, but our shipments could take 30 to 40 days.

items.statement: INR realization benefiting from rupee depreciation from ~84.5-85 to 87+ per USD; dollar realization stable with minor improvements

items.statement: Ecuador facing energy crisis affecting production and exports to US; impact duration uncertain

items.statement: New facility capacity inaccessible for EU market due to pending regulatory approvals affecting both ready-to-cook and ready-to-eat
items.quote: our new facility where we have majority of the capacity as most of you would know is inaccessible. I mean, the EU market is inaccessible to that capacity, both ready-to-cook and ready-to-cat. That's where we are getting affected

items.statement: South Korea market entry initiated; growing business with new and existing EU customers beyond US and EU
items.quote: In South Korea, we are starting there. items.statement: EBITDA margins (excl. non-recurring) improved 200 bps YoY in Q3 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA margins (excluding non-recurring items) improved in Q3 FY25 by 200 basis points as compared to Q3 FY24.

items.statement: Animal Feed EBIT/Tn improved 45% YoY to ₹1,925 in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Further, our EBIT /Tn significantly improved by 45% from ₹ 1,338 in Q3 FY24 to ₹ 1,925 in Q3 FY25.

items.statement: Animal Feed EBIT/Tn expected over ₹2,100 in Q4 FY25 and ₹1,800-2,000 in FY26
items.quote: we believe that we will be able to get EBIT of over ₹ 2,100 per ton in Q4. If you ask me, if we are able to hold onto all the benefits which we have got this year apart from raw material, we should be able to hold on to ₹ 1,800 to ₹ 2,000 per ton in FY26 also.

items.statement: Astec CDMO FY25 expected flat YoY (~₹270 cr); FY26 guided 30-35% growth with confirmed orders
items.quote: this year CDMO there will be no growth, it will be flat and next year we are expecting, if you ask me today 30% (+/-2%) to (+/-3%) will definitely happen

items.statement: Astec CDMO FY26 growth guidance 40% YoY; prices stabilizing after China bottom-out
items.quote: our guidance remains that year -on-year we will be growing at 40%.

items.statement: Standalone Crop Protection Q3 volumes subdued due to low pest infestation and material taken back for hygiene; Q4 expected significant improvement
items.quote: Q4 is a very normal Q4. The expectation is of a good year and you will see a significant improvement in Q4 over Q3 in both the top-line and bottom-line.

items.statement: Vegetable Oil Q3 FY25 revenue up 45% YoY on higher CPO/PKO prices and improved OER despite flat FFB arrivals
items.quote: This also reflected in a 45% year-on-year increase in segment revenue despite flat fresh fruit bunch arrivals.

items.statement: Vegetable Oil outlook bullish due to Indonesia B20 mandate, 20% import duty, and lower global production
items.quote: palm oil prices had started rising internationally also because of the B20 mandate by the Indonesian government, which was supposed to be implemented from 1 st of January, and that postponed to 15 th of February Indonesia, taking off 40% of their palm oil for biodiesel, it is a very big thing

items.statement: 20% import duty on palm oil benefits Vegetable Oil segment; 80% of price benefit passes to farmers
items.quote: We have to thank Government of India for that. Whatever we did, we were doing it earlier also, but that 20% duty was not there.

items.statement: Dairy Q3 EBITDA dropped 5.4% YoY due to sudden milk procurement price hike; consumer price increase taken 21 Jan; Q4 expected better
items.quote: EBITDA dropped by 5.4% as compared to Q3 FY24. I think one of the chief reasons for drop in EBITDA in Q3 was sudden increase in the milk procurement prices.

items.statement: Poultry 9M FY25 mix: live birds 26% (from 41%), RGC 54% (from 43%), Yummiez 20% (from 15.9%); target live birds ~20%
items.quote: Nine-months FY24 live birds was 41%, it is now 26%, Yummiez is nine-months last year 15.9%, this year 20%, and RGC nine-months last year 43%, this year 54%.

items.statement: Poultry plants at 90% utilisation; aim to upsell and expand RGC margins by couple of points in FY26
items.quote: both our plants in Hoskote, Bangalore and Taloja, Mumbai, we are operating at 90% capacity utilization. So, this is a year for upselling and expanding the margins of Real Good Chicken. Some of it you will see QoQ this year and we are very hopeful that we will be able to improve the margin by couple of points in FY26 also.

items.statement: Consolidated capex ₹161 cr in 9M FY25; full year FY25 ~₹220 cr; similar plan for FY26
items.quote: ₹ 161 crores of CAPEX has been done by GAVL consolidated in the first nine-months. We'll end up at about ₹ 220 crores or so and we have a similar CAPEX plan for next year.

items.statement: Palm oil area expansion 13,000-14,000 hectares in FY25 (2.5x last year); can repeat for 4-5 years
items.quote: We might end up anything between 13,000 to 14,00 0 hectare expansion this year as compared to last year it was almost 2.5 times, last year we were around 5,000 hectares.

items.statement: FFB arrivals Q3 FY25: 146,000 tons; 9M FY25: 479,000 tons
items.quote: So, Q3, we got 1,46,000 tons, nine-months we got 4,79,000 tons.

items.statement: Astec Enterprise business FY26 volume growth expected 14-16%; cautious inventory management for accretive margins
items.quote: I think we are bit cautious on the enterprise business. So, we are expecting anything between 14% to 16% growth next year.

items.statement: ₹1,000 cr debt raise enabling resolution postponed; may need only ₹500-600 cr; focusing on working capital reduction
items.quote: We are looking at internal accruals, etc., because we want to drive down our working capital significantly in this quarter. I think we have plans to do that. So, we just postpone that because we may not need 1,000 crores, we may need ₹ 600 - 500 crores.

items.statement: Management evaluating structural simplification to improve visibility and valuation; more details later
items.quote: I think we are cognizant of that fact, we are thinking about how to simplify the structure so that you all get more visibility. So, I think this is also something which we are working on. Probably in time to come you'll hear more about this.

items.statement: Animal Feed margins structurally dependent on commodity prices (corn, DORB) and regulatory changes; regional competition limits pricing premium to 1-1.5%
items.quote: Today, our big competitor for corn is ethanol. So, suddenly the entire game for corn has changed. The base price of 18,000 two years ago, today the base price is ₹ 24,000 - ₹ 25,000 and last year it went up to ₹ 30,000.

items.statement: GCPL pet food pilot plant ready in few weeks; full 35,000-40,000 tpa plant by end FY26
items.quote: The full -fledged 35,000 to 40,000 ton per annum plant will only come towards the end of FY26.

items.statement: ACI Godrej Bangladesh JV revenue declined 13% YoY in Q3 FY25 due to economic and political instability
items.quote: GAVL joint franchise in Bangladesh, ACI Godrej recorded decline in revenues of 13% year-on-year in the Q3 FY25 due to the ongoing economic challenges and political instability in Bangladesh.

items.statement: Corn base price risen from ₹18,000 to ₹24,000-25,000 (peaked ₹30,000) due to ethanol demand; DORB price fell from ₹18,000-19,000 to ₹11,000-12,000 after Bangladesh export ban
items.quote: The base price of 18,000 two years ago, today the base price is ₹ 24,000 - ₹ 25,000 and last year it went up to ₹ 30,000. This is one example. The second example is which is DORB, one of the biggest consumer of our DORB was Bangladesh. Now, since we banned the exports to Bangladesh, the price which used to rein at ₹ 18,000, ₹ 19,000 a ton is now at ₹ 11,000, ₹ 12,000 a ton.

items.statement: Tubes manufacturing contract extended until H1 2027 with expected revenue of INR365 crores over contract period
items.quote: We are pleased to announce that our tubes manufacturing contract has been extended until the first half of 2027 with an expected revenue of INR365 crores over the contract period.

items.statement: Pipes and tubes capacity increased to 534,000 metric tons as of Q2 FY25; further expansion to 700,000 metric tons planned with INR25 crores investment funded through internal accruals
items.quote: In the pipes and tube segment, we have successfully installed and commissioned additional capacity bringing our total capacity to 534000 metric tons as of quarter 2 FY '25. Looking ahead, we plan to further expand this capacity to 700,000 metric tons with a planned investment of about INR25 crores which will be entirely funded through internal accruals.

items.statement: Previous 15-18% top-line growth guidance for FY25 will not be met; updated guidance to be shared in Q4 FY25 call
items.quote: No, I don't think we'll be meeting that, and updated guidance will be shared in the March quarter call. But as things stand now, I do not think that we will be meeting the 18% top line growth target.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to remain within previously indicated guidance range with slight expansion going forward
items.quote: So, I think the margins and cash flows will remain on the indicated guidance that we've given in the past, we don't expect to vary from that greatly. Harsh Bansal: Yes. So, we have indicated some expansion in the EBITDA margin going forward a little bit, probably as per the guidance

items.statement: Business model isolates company from raw material price fluctuations as raw material is supplied free of cost by customers for value addition
items.quote: But our business model doesn't envisage the purchasing of such raw materials. And therefore, we are not really -- we are isolated from the cyclicity and the fluctuations of the raw material. The industry we are in, the raw material is supplied as a free cost supply from our customers which we do value addition to and supply back to them.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle improved to 68 days in December 2024 from 96 days in March 2024
items.quote: Additionally, our cash conversion cycle stood at 68 days in December '24 as against 96 days in March 2024.

items.statement: Net debt increased to INR151 crores in December 2024 from INR99 crores in March 2024 due to ongoing expansion capex
items.quote: Net debt stood at INR151 crores in December '24 as compared to INR99 crores in March '24. This was largely due to the capex incurred for our ongoing expansion.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 operating revenue INR147 crores (2.5% YoY growth); 9M FY25 operating revenue INR471 crores (2.3% YoY growth)
items.quote: During this quarter, our company earned an operating revenue of INR147 crores, reflecting a modest 2.5% increase. For the 9 months FY '25, operating income stood at INR471 crores, a similar 2.3% rise over the same period last year.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 operating EBITDA INR36 crores at 24.5% margin; 9M FY25 operating EBITDA INR114 crores at 24.1% margin
items.quote: Quarterly Operating EBITDA stood at INR36 crores with an operating margin of 24.5%. On a 9-month basis, quarterly operating EBITDA was INR114 crores with a margin of 24.1%.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 PAT INR17 crores at 11.6% margin; 9M FY25 PAT INR57 crores at 12% margin
items.quote: We reported a quarterly profit after tax of INR17 crores. The quarterly PAT margin stood at 11.6%, while the 9-month PAT stood at INR57 crores and PAT margin stood at 12%.

items.statement: ROE 11.1% and ROCE 13.4% for December 2024 period vs 10.1% and 12.5% in March 2024
items.quote: ROE and ROCE for the December '24 period stood at 11.1% and 13.4% respectively, as compared to 10.1% and 12.5% in March '24.

items.statement: Planned INR25 crores investment for pipes and tubes capacity expansion to 700,000 metric tons fully funded through internal accruals
items.quote: Looking ahead, we plan to further expand this capacity to 700,000 metric tons with a planned investment of about INR25 crores which will be entirely funded through internal accruals.

items.statement: New facilities planned for infrastructure, solar and defence sectors with efficient capex enabling high volume value-added production
items.quote: The company plans to establish new facilities focusing on three sectors: infrastructure, solar and defence. These facilities will be designed to operate with a very efficient capital expenditure while enabling high volume and value-added production.

items.statement: GPGC sheets conversion agreement through CRM complex extended until February 2025; long-term contract negotiations in final stages
items.quote: Additionally, the agreement for the conversion of GPGC sheets through the CRM complex has been extended until February 2025. Negotiations for a long-term contract are in the final stages, and we are confident of finalizing the agreement.

items.statement: Dividend policy maintained at 15-20% of net profit; interim dividend not declared, final dividend expected

And profit before tax is 246.37 crores, registering a 19.7% increase with respect to the corresp

items.statement: Three Contico quick-service outlets in Hyderabad in early proof-of-concept stage; no expansion planned yet
items.quote: We have guided last time also that we have started three kiosks in, not kiosks, these are three, you know, quick service outlets by the name “Contico” in Hyderabad. We are still building it up. These are very initial days. Retail is a little, you know, it's not so easy to kind of scale it up very quickly because first we want to be very sure of the proof of concept.

items.statement: Post-renovation first full year revenue target INR170 crores with EBITDA north of INR60 crores
items.quote: So where potentially post-renovation, in the first full year, we're looking at revenues of about INR170 crores with an EBITDA north of INR60 crores.

items.statement: Post-renovation ADR target INR9,500 to INR10,500
items.quote: Post-renovation, we expect our ADRs to significantly improve to INR9,500 to INR10,500 mark.

items.statement: Courtyard by Marriott renovation adding 56 rooms, gym, spa, rooftop bar by end of June
items.quote: We are expecting all these floors to be operational by the end of June of this year.

items.statement: Marriott convention center and select guest rooms renovation from April 2025 over two years
items.quote: In the Marriott property, the convention center and select guest rooms attached to the convention center will undergo renovation from April 2025. The Marriott property will undergo renovation in a phase-wise manner over two years.

items.statement: Courtyard renovation adding 56 new guest rooms on sixth and seventh floors
items.quote: by the end of June, we expect 56 new guest rooms to be added to the sixth and seventh floor

items.statement: Hyderabad supply growing 3-4% annually vs demand growing 10-12% annually
items.quote: Even in Hyderabad, there have been a lot of reports about how supply is only growing at about 3% to 4% per year, whereas the demand is growing at about 10%, 12% every year.

items.statement: Domestic travel at all-time high, strong demand in metro cities
items.quote: industry continues to experience strong demand, particularly in the metro cities. We have observed significant improvement in ADRs and RevPar. Domestic travel seems to be at an all- time high, which is a good indicator for the times to come

items.statement: Additional ADR jump flow-through profit almost 95%
items.quote: the flow-through profit in this additional ADR jump is almost about 95%.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 ADR INR7,423, up from Q2 INR6,063
items.quote: The ADR also was significantly higher at INR7,423 and compared to Q2, it was significantly higher, which the ADR in Q2 was only INR6,063.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 revenue INR37.75 crores up 16% from Q2, EBITDA INR11.35 crores up 43% from Q2
items.quote: The revenue from operations was INR37.75 crores, which is up 16% from Q2, and an EBITDA of INR11.35 crores, which is up 43% from Q2.

items.statement: Current occupancy ~70% in central business district Hyderabad, compset 65-70%
items.quote: we're almost at about a 70% occupancy mark.

items.statement: Rights issue subscribed close to 112%, full allotment completed
items.quote: the company's recent rights issue received an overwhelming response and was subscribed to close to 112%, reflecting strong investor confidence and demand.

items.statement: Evaluating another hotel in Hyderabad, aiming to expand portfolio to three hotels soon
items.quote: we are evaluating another hotel in Hyderabad. Once we have the definitive agreement signed, we will make that announcement. But we are looking at expanding our portfolio to three hotels very, very soon.

items.statement: Budget announcements positive for hospitality sector, providing tailwinds
items.quote: that was actually very good to hear from my finance minister that, they have very good ideas for the hospitality sector in general.

items.statement: Targets 20-25% CAGR EBITDA over 3-5 years and INR1,800-2,200 crore EBITDA with 14-15% ROCE/ROIC in 3-year plan
items.quote: Our focus is on sustainable mid- to long-term growth targeting roughly 20% to 25% CAGR EBITDA over 3 to 5 year's time frame.

items.statement: FY25 capex guidance unchanged at INR1,300-1,500 crore; INR1,020 crore spent in 9M FY25; FY26 capex to be lower than INR1,000 crore
items.quote: Our projected capital expenditure for FY '25 remains unchanged as we have m entioned in the last quarter, INR1,300 to INR1,500 crore, with over INR380 crore spent in Q3 and about INR1,020 crore in the 9-month year -till-date time frame

items.statement: Nitrotoluene expansion 30 to 45 KTPA and ethylation 8-10 to 25-30 KTPA commissioned in Q3; MMA at 200 KTPA; Zone IV commissioning gradually through FY26
items.quote: Our nitrotoluene plant expansion from 30 to 45 KTPA got commissioned this quarter, is expected to yield benefits now in the subsequent quarters. Our expansion of ethylation facility from 8 to 10 KTPA to about 25 to 30 KTPA also got commissioned this quarter.

items.statement: MMA production grew from 59 KT in FY24 to 88 KT in 9M FY25; bulk shipment capability established in Q3
items.quote: on a 9-month basis if you look at MMA, at least at the production level, we were roughly at 59 kt for the previous financial year; versus this year, first 9 months, we a re roughly at 88 kt

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA grew 17% QoQ to INR236 crore; gross margin pressure from aniline inventory liquidation and MMA pricing; expects improvement in Q4
items.quote: EBITDA grew by 17% Q-o-Q to INR236 crore. Growth was primarily led by volumes, operating leverage and product mix improvements.

items.statement: Pricing pressure persists in agrochemical intermediates and China-linked chains; MMA pricing at 1.8-2x MTBE; gasoline-naphtha spread at ~9.5 in Q3, improving in Jan
items.quote: Roughly you can assume that MMA at any point in time would be roughly 1.8x to 2x of MTBE pricing.

items.statement: Non-energy volumes up 14% YoY, 8% QoQ; energy volumes up 10% QoQ; agrochemical inventory normalized; polymer/additives recovery path
items.quote: Volumes in the non-energy business grew by 14% Y-o-Y and 8% Q-o-Q, while the growth in the energy business came in at 10% quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Zone IV to produce 25-30 products across chlorotoluene, dichlorotoluene, toluene photochlorination chains targeting agro, pharma, dyes; 60-40 domestic-export split
items.quote: If you look at the potential product portfolio in that zone, it's broadly focusing on 3 value chains. One is the chlorotoluene value chain, dichlorotoluene value chain and toluene photochlorination value chain.

items.statement: Signed 2 renewable PPAs (Cleanmax, Prozeal); renewable share to exceed 75% by Q1 FY27; significant power cost savings expected
items.quote: We signed 2 renewable energy power purchase agreements for solar and hybrid power with Cleanmax and Prozeal. With this, AIL's renewable share in total power purchase is expected to exceed 75% by Q1 FY '27.

items.statement: Net debt ~INR3,600 crore; $140M ECB largely unhedged with 9-year repayment; forex MTM loss INR23 crore in Q3
items.quote: On the debt number, we are fairly similar to around INR3,600 crore of debt broadly on that, on net debt basis.

items.statement: Export revenue ~INR1,009 crore in Q3 vs INR900 crore in Q2; bulk MMA shipment shifted from Dec to Jan
items.quote: On last quarter, the export numbers were roughly around INR900 crore; and this quarter, around INR1,009 crore.

items.statement: JV with Re Sustainability for chemical recycling of plastic waste; 500 TPD target by 2030; INR100 crore committed in Year 1 (INR50 crore each)
items.quote: Re Sustainability and Recycling Private Limited; and Aarti Circularity Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of AIL, have joined hands to establish transformative first-of -its-kind India joint venture company for driving the development of plastic material r ecycling facilities which will use advanced chemical recycling technology

items.statement: US tariff policy uncertainty for polymer/additives; potential tailwinds for polymer/additives and agrochem intermediates (S-Metachlor, Dicamba) if China faces tariffs
items.quote: Polymer and additives is a segment where we have significant exposure to U.S. market; I think, could ideally see tailwind because there we compete against China for most of our products going into U.S. market.

items.statement: Cost optimization program 30-40% complete; targeting INR150-200 crore savings over 12-18 months
items.quote: I think we are kind of 30% -40% there in terms of that journey. I think there still remains a lot of what's to be done, but we are confident of completing that exercise, as I mentioned in the last call, in the next sort of 12 to 18 months kind of time frame.

items.statement: Rupee depreciation benefits net exporter; relative CNY depreciation offsets advantage; $140M ECB MTM loss INR23 crore in Q3
items.quote: PAT was reported at INR46 crore. This was impacted by high finance costs due to forex mark-to-market loss of INR23 crore on a long-term ECB loan arising due to rupee depreciation.

items.statement: Agrochem and polymer/additives face Chinese overcapacity; dyes/pigments 75% domestic with Heubach acquisition helping; pharma 99% domestic
items.quote: In the dye, pigments, printing inks market, 75% of our market actually comes in the domestic market. Only 25% is export. Even within that now, with Heubach getting acquired by an Indian entity, we expect our share of domestic market to go up.

items.statement: US policy changes create 2025 demand uncertainty for polymer/additives; tariff repercussions may increase competition in other markets
items.quote: Despite s ome uncertainty surrounding 2025 demand due to potential U.S. policy changes, we remain focused on increasing our market share in the global markets, especially in the U.S. and Japan, for polymer and additives segment

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; focus on R&D for new products in circularity, battery, electronic chemicals
items.quote: We continue to leverage R&D to explore new products, seek long-term partnerships, implement our cost improvement initiatives; and targeting high-growth sectors such as circularity, battery and electronic chemicals.

items.statement: Tax rate marginally negative/near zero in FY25; low single-digit in FY26 due to IT depreciation benefits from project commercialization
items.quote: The tax rate in this year, considering that a lot of projects are getting commercialized and there will be some IT depreciation benefits; will continue to remain the way it is currently. So it will be marginally negative and or about closer to 0.

items.statement: Targeting high-teens CAGR revenue growth over next 3-5 years and EBITDA margins well above 20%
items.quote: I think we are anticipating a growth in the next 3 to 5 years of high teens per year-on-year CAGR if you were to project ourselves out and we were sitting together here in FY '28, 3-4 years from now, and we have to review where the business was in FY '24 and where we are stepwise, we'll get there. And margins will cross then margins will cross the 20% number. I mean, our aim is to get well in exce

items.statement: Expect positive results full year led by stronger profit and margin growth
items.quote: As we approach the end of this financial year, we expect to deliver positive results on a full year basis, led by stronger profit and margin growth.

items.statement: CDMO revenue to overtake generics, targeting 60-40 split from current 50-50
items.quote: But from a going forward, I think CDMO will overtake the generics business. So it may be working towards a 60-40 type of split from a revenue perspective.

items.statement: Animal Health division targeting INR400+ crores revenue over next 5 years
items.quote: I think over the next 5 years, we'd like this to become an independent division by itself, stand-alone, just like we have Pharmaceuticals and we have the Crop Protection division. So, we really see a significant amount of growth in excess of INR400-plus crores of business over the next 5 years.

items.statement: Capitalized new multipurpose facility at Panoli for INR340 crores last month, expect ramp-up over 2-3 years
items.quote: We have capitalized our new multipurpose facility at Panoli last month. We expect the ramp -up from this facility over the next 2 to 3 years

items.statement: 30-40% of annual capex is replacement, balance is debottlenecking growth capex
items.quote: See, 30% to 40% will be replacement capex. The balance will be the debottleneck growth capex.

items.statement: Pharma CDMO pipeline has 13-14 products, mostly Phase II-III, two near launch end FY26
items.quote: So, we have currently about , 13 to 14 products in the CDMO under various pipelines, and most of them are between Phase II and Phase III. Phase IV is already getting into launch mode. Out of that, two products are very close to launch, which we expected to be launched in -- towards the end of financial year FY '26.

items.statement: Crop Protection CDMO has 8 active projects under filing or launch in next 2-3 years
items.quote: And we have several, as Vimal mentioned, we have more than 8 active projects which are under filing or under launch in the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Pharma EBIT margin improved 450 bps YoY to 11% in Q3 on better mix and operating leverage
items.quote: For the Pharma business, for the quarter ended December 31, 2024, our Pharmaceutical business reported revenues of INR293 crores and an EBIT of INR33 crores, which is a significant increase of 450 basis points on a Y-o-Y basis based on improvement in product mix and operating leverage.

items.statement: 9M Pharma EBIT margin doubled from 5% to 10% YoY
items.quote: But if you look at annually, it's a correct way to look at our business, because on a 9-month basis, our Pharma business has grown from 5% to 10% EBIT, that's doubled --.

items.statement: Global crop protection industry expected to stabilize in next 2-3 quarters despite China pricing pressure
items.quote: Despite the ongoing challenges such as pricing pressure from competitors, especially from China, the global crop protection industry is expected to stabilize in the next 2 to 3 quarters.

items.statement: API business seeing volume recovery and steady uptake expected in coming quarters
items.quote: For our API business, we are witnessing recovery on the back of improved volume uptakes, which is expected to remain steady in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Pharma volume grew 3.7% and value grew 7.1% YoY in 9M
items.quote: And in Pharma, just 3.7%. Raj Desai: And on value terms? Kuldeep Jain: In value terms, our crop growth was -- degrowth was 3.3%, while the Pharma growth was 7.1

items.statement: Intense pricing pressure and dumping from Chinese competitors continues for generics and commodity products
items.quote: Although China Plus One is expected to strengthen in the current operating environment, intense pricing pressure and dumping continues from the Chinese competitors for generics and commodity products.

items.statement: Pharma product development pipeline includes 8-9 products, targeting 3-4 launches annually
items.quote: Currently, our product development pipeline includes eight to nine products, and we're anticipating to launch three to four products annually.

items.statement: CDMO seeing increased RFPs from global innovators, particularly for NCE molecules
items.quote: Our CDMO business experienced an uptick in inquiries, particularly with a greater focus on N CE molecules fr om various innovator companies

items.statement: Strengthened front-end business development teams globally to capture more opportunities
items.quote: We have further strengthened our front-end business development teams globally, which will help us capture more opportunities as they present themselves.

items.statement: US imposed additional 10% tariffs on Chinese chemicals, creating opportunity for India but situation volatile
items.quote: we've heard the news this morning about 10% tariffs on chemical companies in China. We're obviously looking at that. Those are in addition to supposedly 25% already existing tariffs that they have in place. But look, it's a volatile situation, right

items.statement: Gross debt INR731 crores as of December 2024
items.quote: See, our debt was INR731 crores. It was December 2024.

items.statement: Board recommended interim dividend of INR0.6 per share (30% of face value)
items.quote: Board of Directors at the Board meeting concluded this afternoon have recommended an interim dividend of INR0.6 per share, which is 30% of the face value.

items.statement: Investing 4.5-5% of revenue in R&D to drive innovation
items.quote: Additionally, we are consistently investing about 4.5% to 5% of our revenue into our R&D to drive innovation in products and services that meet the changing demands of all our customers.

items.statement: MDF full-year margin guidance reduced to 13-14% from earlier 16%+
items.quote: As a result, we are reducing our full year margin guidance to 13 -14% as against earlier of 16% plus.

items.statement: Plywood Q4 EBITDA margin target of 10%+
items.quote: So of course, it is not for the full quarter. But all these things, our initiatives clearly shows us that we should be able to move to 10% plus margin.

items.statement: Plywood FY25 volume growth target ~7%+; MDF FY25 volume growth target ~50% YoY
items.quote: So FY '25, the volume, I think we are at around 5.7% right now. And with quarter 4, we will try to be anywhere around 7% plus. Not easy, but definitely, we have plans. Let's see how it pans out. And for MDF, we had initially targeted almost a 50% growth over last year. We should be around that number for the full year.

items.statement: Plywood expansion capex INR134 crore for 13.5 mn sqm (25% capacity addition), trial runs end Q4 FY26, commercial production FY27
items.quote: It's already announced. I think INR134 crores, to be very precise is the number what we have declared. This will give us a new capacity of 13.5 million square meters, which is almost an addition of 25% capacity over our present manufacturing capacity.

items.statement: MDF HDF flooring line delayed 6 months, equipment arrival March 2025, functional May 2025; glue plant completion this quarter
items.quote: Construction of our HDF flooring line has been delayed by 6 months due to the late arrival of major equipment, which is likely to arrive in the month of March and will be fully functional in the month of May '25. Construction of our glue plant is also likely to be completed in this quarter.

items.statement: MDF brownfield 20% expansion on hold due to 30-day shutdown risk; no new MDF capex planned currently
items.quote: So, brownfield, honestly, we have a provision to increase 20% of the capacity of this existing line, where we've already kind of incurred the cost because we've already imported the equipment for extension and it's been lying with us for the last 1 year. But since we have only one plant, expanding this line by 20% means disrupting supply for 30 days. And at the moment, we are not in a position to

items.statement: Furniture & fittings JV started Phase 1 manufacturing late November, expects sales in Q4, initial dealer response very encouraging
items.quote: We started with the entire Phase 1 product range manufacturing from almost November end. We expect to see some sales in quarter 4 where we launched the business and showcased the abilities to our dealers. We have already participated in 2 flagship exhibitions in the last quarter at Delhi and Mumbai, and the initial response to our product group has been very, very encouraging.

items.statement: MDF Q3 EBITDA margin declined to 10.4% from 11.8% QoQ due to high raw material cost and plant shutdown
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin declined to 10.4% as against 11.8% in the previous quarter. This was due to high raw material costs and unexpected plant shutdown in the month of December, which led to lower volume sales.

items.statement: BIS/QCO implementation for plywood from February 25; expected to curb imports and benefit organized players
items.quote: So it was to be implemented in February end. I think the date was 25th of February or so. So I'm sure that the final whatever notification or something which has to come will come. Because the ministry has been very vocal in many of their statements, even including print media, that they are not going to give any further extension on the same.

items.statement: MDF QCO effective February, imports stocked 2-3 months extra; domestic volumes expected to improve post mid-April/early May
items.quote: And the fact that QCO is coming in February and February is the last date to import, so people have imported extra inventory as well. So post mid -April or starting early May, I feel that there will be increase in the domestic volume because I feel people have stocked up typically for 2, 3 months extra.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt INR413 crore; year-end guided ~INR450 crore, net debt/equity ~0.55 (down from peak 0.98 in Mar'23)
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, our net debt levels are at INR413 crores. At the year -end, our debt on a cautious approach would be around INR450 crores as guided earlier, which means our net debt -to- equity ratio at the year-end would be around 0.55 despite expansion and setting up of 2 new line of businesses. ... So on March '22, our debt equity was somewhere around 0.55, and then the whole capex cyc

items.statement: MDF adding HDF flooring line to improve value-added sales and product mix
items.quote: Number two, we are adding a flooring line to our existing MDF line. which will help us increase the value-added sales and help us improve the product mix further.

items.statement: MDF exports negligible; focus on domestic market due to limited single-line capacity
items.quote: Export numbers are negligible in our case because the revenues in exports are much lower than in the domestic segment. And since we have a very limited capacity, only one line to sell, our focus is only the domestic market.
