items.statement: Unorganized players feeling heat from timber price increases; BIS implementation expected to narrow price gap and favor organized players
items.quote: So if that happens, I mean, it automatically differentiates between the rightful organized players and unorganized players. Because we all know that there is an iota of difference in the product level itself. So that will pose a lot of problem for them to cater to the various standards. And if they really cater to, then their prices will shot up. So that will not be very then exciting for the deal

items.statement: Luxury/ultra-luxury residential sales share rose from ~10% to ~30% in 3 years, positive for branded plywood/MDF
items.quote: when I was looking at some data, the residential sales in the country where the volume of luxury and ultra - luxury used to be around 10% 3 years back, is now almost around 30% or 31%. So these are very encouraging signs for any branded goods player.

items.statement: MDF plant shutdown due to Siemens motor failure caused ~INR10 crore revenue loss in Q3
items.quote: About INR10 crores, I think.

items.statement: Laminate trading initiative in very small way, not worth mentioning; will evaluate over next 1-2 quarters
items.quote: We thought about it, but then we thought that we have too many things on the platter. We have done it in a very small way, but I don't think it is at this point of time worth mentioning. Maybe we look at it how it pans out in the next 1 or 2 quarters.

items.statement: Furniture & fittings JV (with Turkey partner) delayed 5-6 months due to machinery delivery; initial dealer meet this month, budgeting in couple of months
items.quote: the whole plan, I would say, in a way, got delayed by 5 to 6 months because the machineries which were to come from Turkey got delayed and then the installation of the same, all those things. So as I said that last month was the first month when we started the production properly with the new machine. And so -- and this month, we have a full -fledged dealer meet, inviting and showcasing them our p

items.statement: Management expects to meet FY26 revenue target of INR600 crores based on new product launches and JV benefits
items.quote: Nevertheless, for FY '26, we are still expecting to meet what you mentioned, based on the seeding activities which I mentioned that we have done in recent quarters.

items.statement: Mitsubishi JV commercial production expected to start July 2025 with benefits from Q2 FY26
items.quote: Yes. So Mitsubishi, yes. The commercial production is going to start from July '25.

items.statement: Morris Co. JV manufacturing facility in Kolkata expected operational Q2 or Q3 next financial year
items.quote: The JV with Morris Co. is advancing well, and we anticipate benefits to start accruing from Q2 or Q3 of next financial year, once our new manufacturing facility becomes operational, which is expected within the same timeframe in Kolkata.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded to 32.9% in Q3 FY25 from 31.5% last year; EBITDA margin maintained at 12%
items.quote: Gross profit rose by 2.9% year-on-year to INR4,017 lakhs, with gross margin expanding to 32.9% from 31.5% last year.

items.statement: Non-pen category margins expected to be slightly lower than pen margins due to outsourced production
items.quote: Honestly, you know, it will be a little lower because these non-stationary and non-pen categories are mostly outsourced.

items.statement: Non-pen contribution currently less than 10%, targeting 30% in medium term with 70-30 pen to non-pen ratio
items.quote: So, currently the contribution of non-pen would be less than 10%. So, which is quite, you know, lopsided I would say towards the core category. So, I think ideally, we are looking at least in the medium term 70-30 kind of a ratio.

items.statement: Markers and mechanical pencils launching Q1 FY26; Linc calculators launched Q4 FY25 targeting affordable segment
items.quote: Markers and mechanical pencils are set for launch in Q1 FY '26, further strengthening our presence in writing instruments. Lin c calculators launched in Q4 cater to the affordable segment, expanding our customer reach

items.statement: Domestic pen market estimated to grow 5-6% annually, driven by premiumization and market share gains
items.quote: So, well, of course, the market estimates are that the category growth is -- of course, it is slightly stunted, but it is still more than 5%. So it could be around 5% to 6%.

items.statement: Reintroduced three legacy Linc products at INR5-6 price point through cost engineering to counter competition
items.quote: So, we have actually reintroduced three products, which we had in the past, not really, -- we had actually discontinued, but we did some cost engineering and then reintroduced three products at that price point without any new investment.

items.statement: Export realizations 5-10% better than domestic; higher export contribution drove ASP improvement
items.quote: In the range of 5% to 10%.

items.statement: Export business growing double-digit across Latin America, North America, Eastern Europe, Africa, Asia Pacific; new markets Morocco, Indonesia, Turkey added
items.quote: We are on a double-digit growth, and we expect it to grow this in the coming quarters. Our export business is quite distributed across the globe.

items.statement: Active retail outlets reduced to ~100,000 from 250,000 enrolled due to inactive non-stationery outlets; focusing on activating existing network
items.quote: So currently the active outlets are about 100,000 outlets. So as such there has been no increase if you say lately. It is just that we are trying to make these 250,000 outlets which are enrolled trying to make some of them active every month.

items.statement: Non-pen products currently reaching 15,000-20,000 outlets vs full network; same salesforce leveraging existing distribution
items.quote: I think about what? 15,000, 20,000 outlets.

items.statement: Competitors aggressively entering sub-INR10 price segment as low-hanging fruit; Linc refocusing on legacy below-INR10 portfolio
items.quote: Actually, you see, you know, after we launched Pentonic, the industry actually moved towards the INR10 and above pens. But as you rightly mentioned that some of our peers, they have -- they found the below INR10 price segment as low hanging fruit.

items.statement: India stationery market projected 13% CAGR to INR72,000 crores by FY28; writing instruments INR13,000 crores; global per capita consumption 9x India
items.quote: With India's stationery and art materials market projected to grow at 13% CAGR, reaching INR72,000 crores by FY '28, we see tremendous expansion opportunities.

items.statement: Operational cash flow INR4,200 lakhs for nine months; net debt negative at INR2,149 lakhs
items.quote: Operational efficiency re mained strong, generating a cash flow of INR4,200 lakhs from operations for the nine -month period. Further, our net debt was negative at INR21,49 lakhs

items.statement: INR5 price segment considered shrinking; competitors' aggressive pricing may be temporary to medium-term
items.quote: Because we feel that the INR5 price segment is a shrinking segment. So and that's the reason that our focus was more on the INR10 and above price segment.

items.statement: Strategy shifted from aggressive non-stationery outlet expansion to deeper penetration of existing stationery outlets and adjacent categories
items.quote: We realized that the ballpen category is very competitive and the cost of reaching those outlets was really quite high. So, we tweaked our strategy of rather serving more deeply our existing stationary outlets and expand into other adjacent categories.

items.statement: Management guided for double-digit top-line growth and EBITDA growth in sync or faster than top-line growth for FY26.
items.quote: Double-digit growth. I think we remain double-digit growth on our top line and EBITDA growth to be in sync or faster than our top line growth.

items.statement: Management expects to reach 17-18% EBITDA margins in the next 6 to 8 quarters driven by gross margin improvement and operating leverage.
items.quote: So, in next, I think 6 to 8 quarters, we should see us touching a much higher level of EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Gross margins have held steady with a slight upward trajectory both sequentially and year-on-year due to hedging, product mix, and calibrated price adjustments.
items.quote: Despite inflationary pressure, gross margin has held steady with a slight upward trajectory in both sequential and year-on-year basis.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 16.5% year-on-year to INR 148 million; EBITDA growth has been faster than top-line growth in the last two quarters leading to small EBITDA margin improvement.
items.quote: EBITDA grew by 16.5% year-on-year to INR148 million. Net profit after tax surged to INR 64 million.

items.statement: Rural consumption expanding steadily; urban demand remains sluggish; small unit packs growing faster; premiumization trend strong.
items.quote: While rural consumption continued to expand steadily, the urban demand remains sluggish. Notably, small unit packs are growing at a faster pace, while the trend towards premiumization remains strong.

items.statement: Management expects urban demand setback to be temporary and anticipates revival in coming quarters, supported by Budget 2025 measures.
items.quote: We expect that the demand setback, especially in urban areas is temporary in nature and anticipate a revival in the coming quarters. Additionally, supportive measures in budget 2025 are expected to boost the user sentiment and drive upward consumption trends.

items.statement: Completed acquisition of 100% equity of Naturell (India) Private Limited; financial results include about one month's performance contributing low single-digit share of top line at breakeven EBITDA.
items.quote: During the quarter, company successfully completed the acquisition of 100% equity share capital of Naturell (India) Private Limited. As a result, the financial results include about one month's performance of the Naturell business.

items.statement: Naturell business had 3-5% margins pre-acquisition; management expects margins to grow to a much higher level with synergies and scale, targeting EPS accretion in FY26.
items.quote: Prior to acquisition, we saw a 3% to 5% kind of margins, but with synergy and scale and our work with them, we obviously expect the margins to grow in -- to a much higher level. And we believe FY '26, we could have an EPS accretive on this business.

items.statement: Personal Care segment grew 50.3% YoY; Food & Nutrition segment grew 8.8% YoY.
items.quote: The Personal Care segment witnessed strong consumer demand, achieving a remarkable double-digit growth of 50.3% for the quarter and continuing its upward trajectory over the last few quarters. At the same time, Food & Nutrition segment recorded a growth of 8.8% for the quarter.

items.statement: Launched Nutralite DoodhShakti processed cheese, Naturell choco-filled fiber bar, melting chocolate, fruit-filled bars (Blueberry Blast, Berry Delight), protein bar bytes; extended Sugar Free Delight cookies; launched AI-powered Nutralite r
items.quote: Nutralite DoodhShakti professional range expanded into processed cheese category. Naturell business introduced a choco-filled fiber bar, melting chocolate, along with 2 variants under the fruit-filled bar range, Blueberry Blast and Berry Delight as well as protein bar bytes.

items.statement: Price increases being taken across multiple commodity-led products wherever costs are rising; pricing is the primary lever for margin protection.
items.quote: Yes. So there would be a price increase across multiple products wherever we are seeing the costs going up, largely commodity-led products, we are taking whatever required price increases.

items.statement: Cost efficiency targets set annually by manufacturing and supply chain teams across vendor negotiation, new vendor development, yield improvement; no fixed percentage target disclosed.
items.quote: We -- I cannot share a specific target, but I can tell you that there is, every year, we plan a certain numbers to come through, better efficiency, better cost takeouts, which work across various levers, which could be in terms of vendor negotiation, vendor develop -- new vendor development. Various -- I mean these are standard things that most procurement teams will do. There is yield improvement

items.statement: Hedging strategies include forward buying of commodities (e.g., palm oil) when opportunities arise; category-specific policies based on experience and expert advice; refined palm oil sourced locally, crude sourced globally when needed.
items.quote: Category to category. For example, when we buy palm oil, Malaysian palm oil would share the forward numbers for several quarters. Now if the procurement team with some advice does feel forward, we will do it. And that too also the seller should be available. It's not just palm board because we buy refined palm oil. We do some cover. So it's specific to categories that we have commodities we are bu

items.statement: Debt has been coming down over the coming years, supporting net profit improvement beyond EBITDA.
items.quote: So beyond EBITDA, in fact, because our -- largely the debt has also come down over the coming years. So we believe our -- we'll keep getting better at it, and therefore, you should see some further improvement.

items.statement: Sweeteners portfolio (Sugar Free, Sugar Free Delight, I'm lite) recovered after WHO and trademark issues in FY24 were addressed and reversed.
items.quote: We had challenges in FY '24, largely in the early part of FY '24, which is related to Sweeteners, both from WHO and some trademark issues, which have got reversed and which have been addressed by us, and we've seen a positive momentum back on the brand on the portfolio of sweeteners between Sugar Free, Sugar Free Delight and I'm lite.

items.statement: True North (large investor) has run full fund cycle; management not privy to their selling plans; selling pressure exists but liquidity also discussed by investors.
items.quote: I think True North is a large investor who came on board at the time of acquisition. They have run the full cycle from their fund point of view. We're not specific privy to their plans. So they will take the call when they have to. So I'm here, the selling pressure, but I also hear some investors also talking about liquidity of our shares. So I can only say that you will have to reach out to them

items.statement: Consolidated net sales grew 12.7% YoY to INR 4,508 million with volume growth of 4.8% YoY.
items.quote: Our net sales grew by 12.7% to INR 4,508 million.

items.statement: Net profit after tax surged to INR 64 million.
items.quote: Net profit after tax surged to INR 64 million.

items.statement: AI and data analytics used for Nutralite Chef recipe platform and recommendation engine for 1,500-1,600 salesmen servicing 6+ lakh outlets; digital marketing share increased significantly.
items.quote: We're also using AI -- not AI, but digital data and analytics on recommendation engine for our salesmen at the last mile. So almost 1,500, 1,600 of our salesmen at the last mile who service more than 6 lakh outlets, they work on handles, which are -- where they pickup orders. Now there is a recommendation engine based on data and analytics which suggests them what they could sell more in this shop

items.statement: No specific capex guidance disclosed; focus on category development, brand extensions, and bolt-on acquisitions to fill gaps.
items.quote: But be assured that we are quite focused on growing the categories and segments, and therefore, our investment is largely focused on category development, followed by extending -- making our brands much larger so leverage our brand presence, which is much larger than the category that we already operate in.

items.statement: Company expects 20%+ growth as new normal, with 50-100 bps annual margin improvement over next 4-5 years.
items.quote: So, now we see that the new normal for this Company should be 20% plus growth. And today for us, maybe if you look at let us say predictability, let's say predictable growth for this Company, as we have seen already four year growth cycle now, from FY22 to 25 numbers which will be almost we are 9 months over.

items.statement: Nine-month capex Rs. 222 crores; full-year budget Rs. 300 crores; new plants to cost Rs. 400-500 crores over 18-20 months.
items.quote: So, this year we have done around close in 9 months Rs. 222 crores of CAPEX and budget of Rs. 300 crores. And probably another few more months of CAPEX and FY26 will then probably our CAPEX cycle for the old plants which were established between 23 and 24 will be over and then we will focus on the new plants which we are establishing , three new plants which were establishing.

items.statement: Dialysis machine run rate 40-50 per month; FY25 installations 300-350, next year to double.
items.quote: No, we will not be able to do 500 installations this year. This year we will be able to do between 300 and 350 installations. I don't have a real figure, but it should be around 350 plus. And then next year maybe we will double the installations.

items.statement: EBITDA margin projected at 27% for FY25, with 100-150 bps improvement over last year.
items.quote: And on the margin side, I think, we have already projected close to 27% EBITDA margin for this year. Last year, we were close to 26% this year, 100 bps improvement, 100-150 bps.

items.statement: Domestic price hikes typically 3-4% per year.
items.quote: It depends. So, sometimes the contracts are longer, you don't get a price hike. But typically, we can take between 3% to 4% price hike per year.

items.statement: Domestic business expected to end FY25 with over 20% overall growth.
items.quote: And hopefully, the current financial year, we should e nd up more than 20% overall growth rate in the domestic business.

items.statement: Exports growing at 28% in nine months, 30% in Q3; on track to deliver committed growth.
items.quote: Exports in the first nine months have shown a great growth. They have been growing at around 28% closely. And if you look at the quarter itself, it's grown by around 30%. So, overall, we are on track to deliver the committed growth.

items.statement: Europe expected to end FY25 with 27-28% growth.
items.quote: Europe has overall grown by around 30% in nine months. Last quarter growth was around 20%. And I think overall we should end up between 27 %-28% growth for Europe by the end of the year, which is a very healthy growth.

items.statement: Renal business targeting 20-25% market share by 2030.
items.quote: But our target is to maybe reach let's say, by 2030 around 20% to 25% of the market share.

items.statement: US business first stronger wave expected in FY27.
items.quote: We see the first stronger wave coming in FY27 because we have some more products to be included in the list, and they're undergoing some clinical trials and regulatory approval, and they will also start contributing to revenue maybe end of this year or early next year.

items.statement: US tariffs expected to be neutral for company as they apply equally to all countries.
items.quote: So, they don't impact India as such, but I think as these tariffs are also in China and maybe even if it comes on India, it will be neutral for us because it will be equally applicable to all the countries. So, we don't expect any impact of this tariffs.

items.statement: QIP proceeds: Rs. 500 crores for new capex, part designated for acquisition.
items.quote: Correct. There's a segmentation of QIP proceeds, so Rs. 500 crores is for new CAPEX, and that is where we will be using it.

items.statement: New plants to be commissioned in 18-21 months.
items.quote: And then all the QIP proceeds will be used for the three new plan ts, which are under construction right now , and will go live in 18 to 21 months.

items.statement: Solar power JV operational by September-October, aiming for green power.
items.quote: And hopefully this will be operational by end of September, October. And after that, most of the polymed manufacturing facility will be running on green power.

items.statement: Targeting 1.5x total EBITDA in FY26 vs FY25 and at least 300 bps EBITDA margin expansion
items.quote: the value -- absolute value of EBITDA, which will be 1.5x the FY '25 figures. And the points, that is the percentage of EBITDA, which is going to be at least 300 bps higher than t his FY '25

items.statement: Core domains EBITDA growth targets: Defence 55-60%, ESAI 50-55%, Aerospace 45-50%
items.quote: We are looking at -- see, the 3 verticals for when we say, we are at the core to grow at around 50% , then 55% to 60% at defence, 50% to 55% at ESAI and 45% to 50% at aerospace.

items.statement: 5-year vision: $1 billion revenue with 35% EBITDA margin by 2029
items.quote: in 5 years from now or 2029, we should be -- at least we -- I want to be, I don't know whether it's appropriate to say, it should be $1 billion in revenue and it should have at least 35

items.statement: Strategic Investments 1 & 2 estimated at INR 180 crores for radar hangars, integration, testing and high-end electronic manufacturing
items.quote: The 1 and 2 probably will take about INR150 crores to INR200 crores. We are -- probably peg it around INR180 crores, let us say.

items.statement: DAC (Devanahalli Atmanirbhar Cluster) investment to be detailed in Q1 FY26 after Aero India customer feedback
items.quote: The third is a fairly huge project, which is DAC, which will -- address it separately. We are coming with the strategy. But basically, that will be addressed in the Q1 of FY '26.

items.statement: New 180,000 sq ft facility at Aero Land (BIAL) ready by February end, moving in by June 1; more than doubles current footprint
items.quote: Our own facility that we have own joint development with another builder. So, this will be ready by February end. So, we will do interiors, etc. We'll move into this facility by around end of May. That's the plan. So , by first of June, we'll be in this facility. It will be 180,000 square feet facility.

items.statement: Electronic City hangar and additional floor for defense/radar teams under construction
items.quote: We are going to build our own hanger. We are going to test the hanger, integrate and so on. And also, it has drone building and so on. So anti-drone -- so we are building a hangar immediately, also building one more floor so that our defense, direct defense team and radar team and all can move there.

items.statement: Order book at $83 million (~INR 710 crores) as of 31 Dec 2024
items.quote: The order book as on 31st December was at $83 million or about INR710 crores.

items.statement: Defense order book visibility ~16x quarterly revenue (combined production + prototype)
items.quote: Our Q3 value into you can safely multiply 16x, will be our order book.

items.statement: Core EBITDA margin expanded 450 bps YoY to 21.3% in Q3 FY25; Defence 18%, Aerospace 24%
items.quote: Core segment EBITDA grew by 68% year -on-year with a significant margin expansion of 450 basis points from 16.8% in Q3 FY '24 to 21.3% in Q3 '25.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 14.6% in Q3 FY25, up 200 bps YoY and 220 bps QoQ
items.quote: The EBITDA margin expanded by 200 basis points year -on-year and 220 basis points quarter -on-quarter, reaching 14.6% for Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: Defence revenue grew 88% YoY in Q3 FY25 driven by order execution; Aerospace grew 11% YoY
items.quote: Defence posted an impressive 88% year-on-year growth, while Aerospace grew by 11% year-on-year.

items.statement: Ashwini radar: supplying 3 subsystems; order placed on BEL and in FY26 order book
items.quote: We are supplying 3 different subsystems to this radar. And already, the order is placed on BEL and we are part of the BEL ecosystem and we have our order book for FY '26. There is -- Ashwini is part of our order book.

items.statement: LCA Mk1A and Sukhoi upgrades on track for FY26; combined revenue ~INR 100 crores
items.quote: Combined between Sukhoi and LCA, it will be more or less, yes, you're right because we are working onit. Further, it also depends on the exact number of Sukhois that are getting upgraded

items.statement: Offset business: strong growth expected from new Rafale marine and naval orders; prime offset partner for global OEMs for 10 years
items.quote: In the Offset business, certainly, there is a very strong growth happening. As we know, already the Ministry of Defense is working out on placing certain new orders on marine rafale and also certain other naval projects.

items.statement: ESAI shifting from design to box-building, prototype and batch production (1k-10k units); adding thermal management via add-solution; targeting edge micro data centers
items.quote: We are making box. So we are into box building earlier -- we used to do only design. Now we are building the box. Now we are building some prototype, some batch production, this would go up to 1,000, 2,000, 10,000 numbers of batches of these products.

items.statement: ESAI partnering with TI, NVIDIA, NXP, Qualcomm; pursuing ST; sector-agnostic including SDV/auto (Aptiv), Apple, Amazon
items.quote: We are working with all the 4 at least major chip manufacturers, Texas Instruments, NVIDIA, NXP and Qualcomm, so we are working in partnership with them. We are trying to get into a new partnership with ST and other companies.

items.statement: ESAI customers include Axon (drone controllers under NATO certification evaluation), Aptiv, Apple, Amazon
items.quote: Currently, our drone controllers are deployed by Axon. They are evaluating it. This is a very high-end customer, almost like that first responder drones, et c. Once we have the complete evaluation is completed, we have to get the NATO certification, etc., for global sales

items.statement: Plan to hire more sales team across geographies for big deals and long-term relationships
items.quote: Alfonso feels that we need more sales team and sales presence and different geographies and so on. So Alfonso will decide and hire more sales people in this.

items.statement: No inorganic acquisitions planned for FY26 unless exotic opportunity arises; ESAI growth via DeepTech fund/incubation instead of M&A
items.quote: We are not planning anything right now on inorganic acquisitions as of now, okay? Our focus is only these 2 things. -- we have a different strategy for ESAI. Again, we'll come back to you. It's not inorganic acquisitions but there will be certain requi rements there also

items.statement: DAC investment size uncertain; depends on Aero India customer feedback; funding plan for INR 180 cr capex under consideration
items.quote: We are going to start up circulate what we are going to do is a dry run with our customers during air show and see how many people are interested, how many people are taking and that will help us recalibrating our vision. And post that, it's going to be February, whole February we are going to see how it is accepted by our customer, received by our customer. Based on that, we'll come with a number

items.statement: Non-core revenue declined 11% YoY to INR 68 crores; reported negative EBITDA of INR 4 crores in Q3 FY25
items.quote: The non-core business, predominantly driven by automotive experienced 11% decline year-on-year with the revenue decreasing from INR76 crores in Q3 FY '24 to INR68 crores in Q3 of FY '25. The non-core segment reported a negative EBITDA of INR4 crores in Q3 FY '25 compared to a positive EBITDA of INR3 crores in Q3 of FY '24.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated EBITDA guided at INR700 crores including other income
items.quote: At the consolidated level, we reiterate that our EBITDA for financial year '24-'25 is expected to be INR700 crores and ROCE is expected to be 17%, which does not include the expected gain on the sale of completed assets.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated total income expected around INR3,700 crores
items.quote: So we anticipate the consolidated revenue to be somewhere close to INR3,700 crores total income.

items.statement: FY26 order inflow target INR8,000-10,000 crores including spillover from FY25
items.quote: We believe that we should be able to make up for this loss of about INR4,000 crores plus the additional INR6,000 crores in FY '26. So we should be garnering an inflowsomewhere between INR8,000 crores to INR10,000 crores order book in the FY '26.

items.statement: Revenue and EBITDA growth guided at 15-20% YoY for FY26 and FY27
items.quote: So we expect the -- our revenues and our margins to grow in the ranges of 15% to 20% year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Consolidated order book at INR14,500 crores as of Q3 FY25
items.quote: I'm pleased to announce that our consolidated order book stands at INR14,500 crores, of which around INR9,300 crores comes from water, about INR1,950 crores from tunneling segment and remaining INR1,750 crores from transportation sector.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated order book target INR15,000-20,000 crores depending on award timing
items.quote: we are on track to close FY '25 with a consolidated order book of -- in the range of INR 15,000 crores to INR20,000 crores depending upon the timing of awards.

items.statement: WMEL order book INR2,600 crores as of Dec 31, 2024 with 23 projects
items.quote: On the financial front, our WMEL order book as on December 31, 2024, is INR2,600 crores. The order book entails 23 projects, which are spread across large dia tunnels, micro and segment tunneling, marine works, rehabilitation of sewer lines and bridge construction and is largely executable over the next 36 months.

items.statement: WMEL FY25 order inflow expected INR1,900 crores including L1 positions
items.quote: So Michigan has had INR1,700 crores that we have received as incoming orders for the year. And we still have some contracts that we are L1. We are hoping that another INR200 crores to INR400 crores will come in before the March 31st fiscal deadline and add to this number. So we expect to end the year with an order inflow of about INR1,900 crores.

items.statement: Strong water pipeline in Maharashtra, MP, Rajasthan, Odisha with orders expected in 45 days to 3 months
items.quote: So the water pipeline is pretty strong. As I said in my opening statement, we see a lot of orders coming through going forward in Maharashtra, in MP, in Rajasthan, in Odisha. So we see a lot of orders being announced and which being expected in any time between 45 days to about 3 months period.

items.statement: Identified INR6 lakh crores project pipeline over 5-7 years across water, BOT toll, large diameter tunneling
items.quote: We have identified over INR6 lakh crores worth of projects across key segments over the next 5 to 7 years. This includes opportunities in water supply, wastewater treatment, water transmission, BOT Toll projects and large diameter tunneling.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 19.6% in Q3 FY25, 9M FY25 margin ~19%
items.quote: Our consolidated EBITDA for Q3 FY '25 is INR180 crores against INR174 crores in Q3 FY '24. This EBITDA works out to margin of 19.6%.

items.statement: WMEL 9M FY25 EBITDA margin approximately 23%
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin works out to be approximately 23% for the 9 months FY '25.

items.statement: SmartOps projects expected to achieve at least 30% gross margin
items.quote: Now the percentages that this brings to our EBITDA levels in terms of the earnings, we expect that we will not be earning less than 30% on the gross levels in terms of percentage profit margins.

items.statement: Dharavi-Ghatkopar tunnel project INR1,989 crores to be executed through WMEL
items.quote: In line with our strategic growth areas, we have secured an order of INR1,989 crores to construct our water conveyance tunnel from Dharavi to Ghatkopar in Mumbai. This project complements our ongoing work at Dharavi STP. We will implement this project through Welspun Michigan, leveraging their expertise in Thane.

items.statement: TBM for Dharavi-Ghatkopar tunnel finalized, delivery expected in 16 months
items.quote: Our TBM has been finalized and an MoU and order has bee n placed. This delivery is expected in 16 months. And it will be just in time once the shaft completion project has been executed.

items.statement: Dharavi Wastewater Treatment Facility targeting completion by Q3 2026 ahead of schedule
items.quote: This project aims for completion by the third quarter of 2026, ahead of its schedule.

items.statement: Aunta-Simaria road project on track for provisional completion by end of FY25
items.quote: We are on track to achieve provisional completion for Aunta-Simaria road and project by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: Segmental revenue Q3 FY25: Transport INR328 crores, Water INR365 crores, Tunneling INR174 crores
items.quote: Out of total consolidated operational revenue of INR867 crores, INR328 crores comes from transport, INR365 crores is contributed by water and the balance of INR174 crores is being contributed by tunneling work.

items.statement: Water pipeline split: 40% transmission, 30% treatment, balance distribution and O&M
items.quote: So the segmentation of this is available, and bulk transmission is about 40% of this pipeline and about 30% is treatment. The balance comes from other distribution, et cetera, et cetera.

items.statement: SmartOps secured 2 orders: Durga Kund Varanasi and Chandrabhaga River Pandharpur
items.quote: I'm extremely happy to share that we are about to hand over 2 prestigious projects executed using this technology. One is a rejuvenation of the Holy Durga Kund in Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh, and the second is on the Chandrabhaga River at the Vitthal Mandir in Pandharpur, Maharashtra.

items.statement: SmartOps FY25 revenue contribution INR43-45 crores, FY26 target INR150-200 crores
items.quote: The 2 orders of Varanasi and Pandharpur will contribute about anywhere between INR43 crores to INR45 crores to our top line sales in terms of fiscal year '25. And we hope that we will achieve easily 100% to 150% increase for the next FY '26 projection.

items.statement: Limited competition in specialized water/tunneling projects due to technical qualifications
items.quote: In the kind of projects that we participate, there are limited players because you need technical qualifications, et cetera, et cetera. So we don't see very intense competition. We don't participate by design in areas which are intensely competitive.

items.statement: No competing technology equivalent to SmartOps currently known
items.quote: At least to the best of my knowledge, there is no competing technology equivalent to this at this point in time.

items.statement: Standalone debt-free with INR844 crores cash reserve as of Dec 31, 2024
items.quote: We remain debt free on a stand-alone basis with cash reserve of INR844 crores, which will allow us to grow the business to the next level.

items.statement: Consolidated debt INR1,122 crores at SPV level for HAM projects
items.quote: Consolidated INR1,122 crores. And we don't have any debt on the -- at stand-alone level.

items.statement: Received INR169 crores advance from Actis for 51% MCP stake sale
items.quote: Basically, we have taken one advance of INR169 crores from the Actis for the 51% MCP stake, which we are going to sell. So this is advance, which is interest -- it will come -- it will be adjusted against our consideration of 51% when we sell this.

items.statement: Dharavi-Ghatkopar tunnel approvals expected in 4-6 months
items.quote: The necessary permissions are being processed, and we expect a 4- to 6-month process time for such permissions to be granted.

items.statement: MCP 51% stake sale to Actis expected to close in H1 FY26 after COD and NHAI approval
items.quote: Just to add to what Lalit has told, we anticipate in the H1 of FY '26, this whole transfer to take place. And this notional loss that we are making will get consummated rewritten in once -- the equity of 51% is transferred to Actis.

items.statement: FY25 order inflow only INR2,000 crores vs INR6,000 crores target due to award delays
items.quote: Based on these guidance, we anticipated that we will be having an order book of about INR6,000 crores addition. However, given that this INR2,000 crores may not come and certain projects are delayed in award, we are not very hopeful that any new award will come in the current financial year.

items.statement: Full-year volume guidance of 250,000-260,000 tons for FY25
items.quote: So for the total profit -- and that compares to INR256 crores in the sequential second quarter, and it's a little lower from INR280 crores approximately in the third quarter last year. So with that, our full year volume, which is 187,000 tons for the 9 months, looks to be between 250,000 and 260,000 depending on invoicing, etcetera, is the guidance for the full year.

items.statement: Expect return to 25,000-30,000 tons annual volume growth in next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: But over next 2, 3 quarters, it looks like that we should be back on a 25,000, 30,000 ton annual addition on a rolling basis.

items.statement: Capex guidance: up to INR50 crore renewable power, INR35-50 crore maintenance, plus USD50 million for China and Ghana plants
items.value: INR35-50 crore maintenance + INR50 crore renewable + USD50 million overseas
items.quote: So this year -- the next coming year, we'll do about -- up to INR50 crores in renewable power. And I think we'll be done with most of the strategy as far as optimizing power cost is concerned, up to INR50 crores in maintenance capex per year. So once you remove that, not more than INR35 crores to INR50 crores of maintenance capex, plus our investment in the 2 plants that we've announced.

items.statement: India capacity frozen at 460,000 tons; 36,000 ton expansion paused
items.quote: We are now staying put with our current capacity in India, which stands at 460,000 tons. We had earlier announced a plant in India for 80,000, which we scaled down to 36,000. But now with our intent to do -- to set up production outside of India, we are now staying put and pausing any work on any further capacity addition in India.

items.statement: Total capex for China and Ghana plants estimated at USD50 million
items.quote: And the total capex for both plants is currently established at -- estimated at USD50 million.

items.statement: Destocking at one large customer expected to reverse from June quarter
items.quote: I think at least for one customer, we expect that to come back from the June quarter. Some in March, but mostly in June quarter.

items.statement: Operating margins currently 27-28%; believe structurally better than 21-22% but not guiding
items.quote: Even if you knock off my treasury and other income, we are talking of operating margins in the range of 27%, 28%. We do believe that this is helping us through multiple factors, product mix being one of them.

items.statement: Raw material costs stable for last 2 quarters; freight rates easing in many corridors
items.quote: I think raw material continues to be -- is a little stable for last 2 quarters. So our raw material cost as a percent of sales adjusted for inventory, I think, is broadly in line with the sequential second quarter. So I think that volatility looks to have eased out. Also on the freight, the shipping side of things, it looks a little better.

items.statement: Product mix improvement supporting higher margins
items.quote: We do believe that this is helping us through multiple factors, product mix being one of them.

items.statement: No major customer losses; destocking temporary
items.quote: I don't think we have lost any major customers. That is your first answer from our side.

items.statement: No significant competition from Molycop in high chrome segment
items.quote: No, I don't think so. I'm sorry, I can't go beyond that, but there really is not, I would say, a threat or a competition for us.

items.statement: China plant targeting production start in H2 FY26; Ghana plant over next 18 months
items.quote: China should start contributing something in the second half of next year. That is what the target is, but let's see. We are working very hard. Our teams are already there. Ghana should happen over next 18 months, that is how it looks like.

items.statement: US tariffs not expected to impact China plant as US not primary destination
items.quote: Not really. I mean, U.S. is not -- may not be the destination country from China. I mean there is -- we're trying to do a few things. And today, it is considering that U.S. may not be the top destination from that plant.

items.statement: Mining liners ramp slower than expected; rubber/composite liners just started small quantities
items.quote: The trajectory is a little slower than how we had expected. In fact, there were quite a bit of learnings in terms of how -- what customers looking at their perception, what is our approach and strategy to go break some of those customers. I think we are delayed with full utilization.

items.statement: Rubber and composite liners started small deliveries; will ramp over next year
items.quote: Yes, we just started small quantities. They'll ramp up over the next 1 year.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 sales volume 65,780 tons; 9M FY25 volume 187,000 tons
items.quote: Headline numbers, our sales tonnages are at 65,780, approximately 66,000 tons, up from 60,000 tons in the sequential second quarter and down from about 74,000 tons in third quarter last year. So for the 9 months to date, our total tonnage stands at about 187,000 tons.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 realization INR160 per kg
items.quote: I think rest of the other numbers remain at par with our working capital, our cash on the block after -- cash on the books after the buyback proceeds were paid out. I think everything else is in sync. I think I'll head on to the important numbers -- the important announcement. Sorry, before that, our realization for the quarter is at about INR160 per kilo.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 revenue INR1,050 crore, EBITDA INR354.57 crore, PAT INR259.22 crore
items.value: Revenue INR1,050 cr, EBITDA INR354.57 cr, PAT INR259.22 cr
items.quote: The revenue for the quarter is at INR1,050 crores, our EBITDA is at INR354.57 crores and our profit after tax is at INR259.22 crores.

items.statement: Working capital and cash position in sync after buyback payout
items.quote: I think rest of the other numbers remain at par with our working capital, our cash on the block after -- cash on the books after the buyback proceeds were paid out. I think everything else is in sync.

items.statement: Strategy shift driven by volatile freight environment (rates up 5x) and geopolitical fragility
items.quote: The change in mindset comes from 5 years of facing volatile and -- volatile freight environment where freight rates have gone up as high as 5x, corrected back and then went up again. I think we -- it's an acknowledgment that we live in a very, very fragile environment where there were 2 wars in recent history, 1 still continues on.

items.statement: Modular overseas plants designed to be capital efficient with latest automation technology
items.quote: We are using the latest manufacturing technology, which allows us to reduce capital investment or do it in a modular fashion, while being capital efficient and utilizing the best automation methods currently available in our space.

items.statement: Overseas plants aim to reduce freight cost, transit time and create market access
items.quote: Think of these as our attempt to get production closer to markets, which includes our access to certain markets, reduces freight cost and the shipping transit time.

items.statement: Not ready to give firm volume guidance for FY26; expect clarity in 2-3 quarters
items.quote: So for now, we are at 250,000 and no clear guidance for exactly the next 4 quarters or the FY '25-'26. But we -- as we -- it looks like that whatever headwinds are settling down a bit, we should have better clarity in the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: FY25 constant currency revenue growth guidance revised to 21.8%-22.3%
items.quote: We now expect our revenue to grow in the range of 21.8% to 22.3% in constant currency terms.

items.statement: FY25 normalized EBIT margin guided at 11-11.5% excluding acquisition one-time charges
items.quote: For operating margins, we expect a normalized FY25 EBIT margin, excluding one-time charges related to the acquisitions, to be in the 11 to 11.5% band.

items.statement: Expect 50-75 bps annual margin expansion in FY26
items.quote: So, let me first state at the outset that we do expect the 50 to 75 basis points playing out in FY26.

items.statement: Q3 EBIT margin at 11.1%, stable QoQ and YoY; nine-month normalized margin 11.1% within guided band
items.quote: Our operating profit was Rs. 2,333 million, up 37% over Q3 of last year, and translates to EBIT margin of 11.1%, same as normalized margin in Q2.

items.statement: Revenue grew 32% YoY (30% USD, 28% CC); fifth straight quarter of >3% QoQ CC growth
items.quote: Our revenue grew by 32% YoY and came in at Rs. 21 billion. In U.S. dollar terms, the growth was 30% YoY and 8.4% QoQ at US$ 249 million.

items.statement: Three large deals (ACV >$5M) signed in Q3, third straight quarter; exit deal pipeline among highest ever
items.quote: In Q3, we signed three large deals. As you are aware, we consider a deal with ACV of over 5 million as a large deal. This is the third straight quarter of at -least three large deal wins and despite that, our Q3 exit deal pipeline was among the highest ever.

items.statement: Top 5 client revenue share down to 29.2% from 35.8%; top 10 down to 43.5% from 52% YoY
items.quote: The share of revenues from our top five clients has come down to 29.2% versus 35.8%, and our top 10 clients to 43.5% from 52% in Q3 of last year.

items.statement: Added 13 new logos in Q3 including 5 strategic logos (potential >$5M annual revenue)
items.quote: During the quarter, we also added 13 new logos, including five strategic logos. We defined a strategic logo as one where we see the potential of at -least US$5 million of annual revenue.

items.statement: Added new seat capacities in Bangalore, Hyderabad, Mumbai, and UK in Q3
items.quote: We continue to invest in expanding our execution infrastructure. In Q3, we have added new seat capacities in Bangalore, Hyderabad, Mumbai, and the UK.

items.statement: Acquired 100% of AccunAI (Jaipur AI startup) for Rs. 80M total consideration
items.quote: We have acquired a 100% stake in AccunAI, a provider of AI development services based out of Jaipur, India. It is a startup which is also a vendor to Firstsource for AI development services and crowdsourcing. We liked their capabilities and decided to bring them in-house for a total purchase consideration of Rs. 80 million, and this was a 100% acquisition.

items.statement: Board declared interim dividend of Rs. 4 per share
items.quote: I am also pleased to share that the Board has declared an interim dividend of Rs. 4 per share.

items.statement: DSO at 67 days in Q3 (vs 65 in Q2), expected to normalize by Q4; FCF/PAT 159% in Q3, 78% for 9M
items.quote: Reported DSO was slightly higher at 67 days in Q3, which is normally the soft collection quarter, especially in the US, versus 65 days in the Q2. We expect it to normalized by Q4.

items.statement: Cash balance Rs. 2.5B; net debt Rs. 10.2B at end of Q3
items.quote: Our cash balance, including investment, stood at Rs. 2.5 billion and our net debt was Rs. 10.2 billion at the end of Q3.

items.statement: Hedge book: GBP 74.9M covered at Rs. 106-114; USD 168M covered at Rs. 85.5-88.5
items.quote: Our hedge book as of 31 st December was as follows : We had coverage of GBP 74.9 million for the next 12 months, with a n average rate ranging from Rs. 106 to Rs. 114 per pound, and coverage of US $168 million, within a range of Rs. 85.5 to Rs. 88.5 to the dollar.

items.statement: Onshore revenue mix shifted from 74% to 60%; offshore/nearshore from 26% to 40% YoY
items.quote: If you look at where we are today, for Q3 of FY25, that's changed to 60% coming from onshore and 40% going from offshore and nearshore side.

items.statement: Healthcare vertical flat QoQ, up 31% YoY CC; payer deal conversations resumed, expect closures in Q4
items.quote: Q3FY25 was expectedly a modest quarter. Our revenues were flat quarter-on-quarter, they were up 31% year-on-year in constant currency terms.

items.statement: BFS vertical up 1.6% QoQ, 8% YoY CC; added 7 new logos; broadening portfolio beyond mortgage
items.quote: In Q3FY25, our BFS vertical was up 1.6% QoQ and 8% YoY in constant currency terms. We added seven new logos in this vertical in Q3.

items.statement: Diverse portfolio up 80% QoQ, 193% YoY CC due to full quarter Ascensos impact
items.quote: Our diverse portfolio grew 80% QoQ and 193% YoY in constant currency terms due to the full quarter impact of the Ascensos acquisition.

items.statement: Constant currency revenue growth 28% YoY in Q3, highest in 14 quarters; 9M FY25 CC growth 22%
items.quote: In constant currency, this translates to a YoY growth of 28%. This is the highest growth YoY in terms of constant currency in the last 14 quarters.

items.statement: Gaining market share vs closest global publicly traded peers based on trailing 4-quarter revenues
items.quote: Our improved growth momentum is helping us gain market share against the basket of our closest globally publicly traded peers based on trailing four quarters reported revenues.

items.statement: Mortgage acquisition performance impacted by industry-level changes; other acquisitions delivering better than estimated
items.quote: Otherwise , all are performing better, including the ones where we are taking a reversal, I think businesses are delivering more than what we estimated as revenue.

items.statement: ESG score of 81 by S&P Global, top 99th percentile in DJSI 2024, top 5 in peer group
items.quote: I am also proud to report that Firstsource achieved an ESG score of 81 by S&P Global that puts us in the top 99th percentile of the Dow Jones Sustainability Index of 2024 and amongst the top five in our peer group.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin expected within 19%-21% range despite Q3 at 23%
items.quote: For the FY25 as a whole, we are quite confident it will still be within this 19% to 21%.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin 23% driven by stable raw material costs, higher sewing efficiency, controlled operating costs
items.quote: Stability in raw material costs, sustained higher sewing efficiency, and controlled operating costs have contributed to strong EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded YoY due to stable raw material prices and significantly increased sewing efficiency
items.quote: The reason, as we said, is two. One, definitely the raw material prices have remained stable. In fact, on a year-to-year basis, raw material prices have slightly improved over the last year. The sewing efficiency has significantly increased.

items.statement: Consumer demand remained subdued in Q3; festive uptick in early Q3 did not sustain in November-December
items.quote: We did see some level of uptake during the initial portion of the quarter, largely attributed to the festive. However, November and December has remained subdued.

items.statement: Tier-3 and Tier-4 cities showing better growth rates than metros, partly due to inorganic expansion
items.quote: as you go deeper in the country, the growth rate seems better. Again, these are not likes to like, it's also because of inorganic expansion in these areas

items.statement: Channel inventory reduced by ~5 days since start of year; now at ~17.7-18 million pieces, near optimum for innerwear
items.quote: We have seen about 5 days reduction in inventory across the channel. We are today holding about 17.7, almost 18 million pieces of inventory as far as the channel is concerned.

items.statement: Odisha plant and KR Pet sewing facility (~2000 machines) to meet capacity needs for next 3 years; Odisha can run two shifts
items.quote: These two factories is around 2000 sewing machines. And with that, I think our requirement for the next three years will be met with these two factories.

items.statement: No price increase taken in FY25; unlikely in Q4; FY26 pricing decision pending budget finalization
items.quote: Definitely this year we have not taken any price increase. And even in the next quarter, it's unlikely. But for FY26, we are just in the midst of the budgeting session.

items.statement: Premium products across all categories grew better; category mix drives realization variation quarter to quarter
items.quote: One of the trends I can say, which we are able to see is that the premium products ranges in all of our categories have done comparatively better.

items.statement: E-commerce highest growing channel, followed by modern retail, then general trade (low single-digit growth)
items.quote: The highest growing channel for us has been e-commerce followed by modern retail and then general trade.

items.statement: No evidence of shelf share loss in general trade; exclusive stores insulated from competition
items.quote: We have not seen evidence of loss of shel f share in the general trade market, which is a significant portion of our business. And the rest of the business that we operate with are anyway exclusive stores, which is in a way isolated from competition

items.statement: Odisha plant eligible for state subsidies: wage subsidy 5-6 years, power, water, local GST, some capex subsidy
items.quote: One major part is definitely the state subsidy on account of wages. So, there are significant wages subsidy for employees on- road for next 5 to 6 years. That is definitely a big contributor. And apart from that, there are subsidies in power, in water usage, even local GST. So, there are several subsidies in pipeline, even to some extent, CAPEX subsidy is also there

items.statement: Karthik Yathindra promoted to CEO Designate, assumes CEO role effective April 1; stable leadership team with decade-plus tenure
items.quote: I am pleased to inform you that Karthik will assume the role of CEO effective April 1st.

items.statement: Sales volume 57.8M pieces (+4.7% YoY) in Q3; 170.4M pieces (+4.6% YoY) in 9M FY25
items.quote: We recorded sales volume of 57.8 million pieces, which was a growth of 4.7% year-on-year.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free
items.quote: We continue to be debt free.

items.statement: IT costs rising from digitization and business process re-engineering; marketing and other expenses planned higher in Q4
items.quote: One is definitely the IT cost, which has just started coming in, which is part of our digitization efforts. We have just started the business process re-engineering study, which is kind of playing out now. So, we will definitely see a higher elevated cost as far as IT is concerned in the coming up quarter.

items.statement: ARS (Auto Replenishment System) covers 92% of business via 84% of distributors; improved inventory optimization and order fulfillment
items.quote: Today, close to 92% of our overall business is on ARS, which has been a significant improvement from where we started. And month on month, we have seen more portion of our business come under the ARS scope. So, almost 84% of our distributors who contribute to 92% of our business are now under ARS.

items.statement: FY25 volume growth expected at 8-9%, down from earlier 10-15% target
items.quote: FY '25, we thought we will be in the region of 10% to 15%, but probably it looks like we might end up close to 8% to 9% growth overall in this year concluding in March

items.statement: FY26 volume growth targeted at double digits, internally aiming for 15%
items.quote: coming to next year we are confident we'll be in double digits because what I explained to the previous question

items.statement: EBITDA per kg expected to cross INR38 in Q4 FY25, INR40 target for FY26
items.quote: Probably in the Q4 we may see the number crossing INR38 as the pharma contributions are substantially improving compared to the previous quarters

items.statement: EBITDA margin for FY25 expected at 8-9%, double digits for FY26
items.quote: we may end up somewhere close to 8%, 9% this year because what we thought in terms of ABG, we lost in Asian Paints, half of it at least

items.statement: Pharma sales jumped from INR2.27 crore in Q3 to INR2.1 crore in January alone
items.quote: But in the month of January itself, we have crossed INR2.1 crores due to the commercialization of the samples that were approved during the last several months

items.statement: Pharma revenue target INR30-35 crore for FY26, INR60-65 crore for FY27
items.quote: From INR8 crores, we are aiming at almost INR30 crores, INR35 crores turnover coming from pharma in the next financial year

items.statement: Food & FMCG growth expected at 10-12% in FY26 vs 7.3% in 9M FY25
items.quote: So going forward, even food and FMCG, we anticipate double-digit growth from 7.3% this year. It should be in the range of around 10% to 12%

items.statement: Thin wall packaging growth targeted at 15% in FY26
items.quote: We should be close to 15% in the thin packs next year

items.statement: Qpack (square pack) growth expected at 18-20% in FY26
items.quote: Coming to Qpack, I'm confident it will be again 18%, 20% kind of growth next year

items.statement: Asian Paints volume down 10% in 9M FY25 due to tepid growth and vendor redistribution
items.quote: Major reduction is from Asian Paints because they are one of our largest customers even today. So there, we lost almost 10% volume

items.statement: Aditya Birla Group projecting 40-50% volume growth for FY26
items.quote: Their volume growth, they are projecting 40% to 50% compared to this current financial year

items.statement: Pharma EBITDA per kg at INR300-350 vs company average INR206
items.quote: As we grow in pharma, per kg realization could be more than INR300 to INR350, whereas our current average is INR206

items.statement: Pharma EBITDA margins 37-38%, canisters over 50%, ROCE 28-29% at utilization
items.quote: ROCE, what we generally monitor is definitely much better in pharma in terms of EBITDA, I can say if it is 38% or 37% in current product mix, anything above 100 to 150 is possible in pharma

items.statement: Paint segment EBITDA margins below company average, screen printing products less encouraging
items.quote: In the paint industry as of today the EBITDA margins are below the -- our overall company average

items.statement: 12 pharma clients audited and cleared, commercial supplies started December
items.quote: 12 of the reasonably big pharma players in India have already audited our premises in the last 10 months. And all of them cleared our premises for the next steps

items.statement: Surf Excel and Horlicks orders ramping up, Surf Excel volumes may grow 40-50% in FY26
items.quote: the indications are whatever we sold this year might almost at least grow by 40%, 50% next year

items.statement: FY26 capex planned at INR60-65 crore vs INR120-130 crore in recent years
items.quote: our investment next year may come down substantially from INR120 crores for th e last 3 years, including this year to around INR60 crores, INR65 crores for the next financial

items.statement: Pharma capex INR25-40 crore in FY26 for capacity doubling
items.quote: INR25 crores to INR40 crores is investment we are planning for pharma next financial year

items.statement: Overall capacity utilization at 70%, new plants at Cheyyar/Mahad/Panipat below 50%
items.quote: Capacity utilization is still around 70% overall company level, but the plants at Cheyyar and Mahad, especially Panipat which have been created in anticipation of ABG's growth, there the percentages are still 60% compared to the initial capacity

items.statement: Installed capacity over 53,000 tons per annum, FY25 output ~39,000 tons
items.quote: The base capacity is more than 53,000 tons as of today per annum. And this year we may hit close to 40,000

items.statement: IML printing capacity increasing 35-40% by end-February with new machines
items.quote: certainly by end of February, we are ready to have almost 35% to 40% increase in the capacity of IML print labels

items.statement: Raw material prices up ~INR4/kg in 9M, selling prices up ~INR8/kg
items.quote: if you take 9 months it's gone up by around INR4. So the selling price could go up by around INR8

items.statement: Pharma at 1.19% of turnover, 0.6% of volume in Q3; paint 48% volume, lube 24.6%
items.quote: pharma is 1.19% in terms of percentage in the turnover sid e. In the volume side, paint is still 48%; lube is 24.6

items.statement: Asian Paints contributes ~30% of sales, lost 10% volume due to pricing
items.quote: Our -- we never anticipated a drop in Asian Paints volumes in this year. So that growth they contribute almost 30%, 33% of our sales even today, 30%

items.statement: Increased competition in food/FMCG from small regional players in ice cream/dairy
items.quote: Yes, there is an increased competition, especially in the nooks and corners of the country, small players with a couple of machines and a few product range they are entering

items.statement: Pharma competitors: Shriji Polymers, Gerresheimer, Gopaldas, Dr Pack, Bericap
items.quote: Yes, Shriji Polymers, Gerresheimer, Gopaldas, there are 3, 4 well-established players in pharma sector

items.statement: Exporting 1 million canisters/month to US client directly
items.quote: one consignment of 1 million pieces of canisters are being exported to U.S. directly

items.statement: Other expenses up 30% YoY due to INR96 lakh legal costs for patent protection and trade fair participation
items.quote: INR96 lakhs to be precise in the first 9 months. So that is one reason for expenditure increase. And general expenditure that includes travel and trade fairs

items.statement: Depreciation ~INR50 crore in FY25 (INR36 crore YTD), interest costs rising from new plant capitalization
items.quote: we have depreciated almost like -- we're going to depreciate, I'd say, almost INR50 crores in this current financial year. So far, already INR36 crores has been depreciated

items.statement: IML labelled containers grew from 64% to 73.4% of volumes in Q3 YoY
items.quote: overall labelled containers have grown up from 64% last Q3 to 73.4%

items.statement: Asian Paints volume loss of 10% hit overall growth by ~3 percentage points
items.quote: a big 10% drop in the volume has hit us by almost 3 percentage points

items.statement: Printing capacity shortfall caused lost business in Qpack and thin wall in peak season
items.quote: Our two things majorly, one of them is our misplanning in printing capacity or a reduction of the printing machine in a vital time has made us lose some part of business both in Qpacks and thin wall

items.statement: FY25 operating revenue guidance raised to minimum INR4,550 cr for PG Electroplast plus INR550 cr from Goodworth JV, total group revenue ~INR5,100 cr (~86% YoY growth)
items.quote: For FY '25, we have updated our guidance for operating revenues to a minimum of INR4,550 crores for PG Electroplast and an additional INR550 crores from our joint venture, Goodworth Electronics, employing a total group revenue of around INR5,100 crores, which reflects an impressive growth rate of around 86% compared to FY '24 numbers.

items.statement: FY25 net profit guidance for PG Electroplast raised to at least INR280 cr (~105% YoY growth vs FY24 INR137 cr)
items.quote: Furthermore, we are also adjusting our net profit guidance for PG Electroplast to at least INR280 crores, which represents a substantial increase of around 105% over FY '24 net profit of INR137 crores.

items.statement: FY25 product segment revenue expected to grow 98% to INR3,300 cr from INR1,668 cr in FY24
items.quote: The anticipated growth in our product segment, which includes washing machines, room air conditioners, and air coolers is expected to grow by 98%, rising from INR1,668 crores in FY '24 to INR3,300 crores.

items.statement: FY25 capex guidance set at INR370-380 cr, on track with satisfactory progress on infrastructure and capacity expansion
items.quote: Capital expenditure guidance is set between INR370 crores and INR380 crores with satisfactory progress observed in all infrastructure and capacity expansion initiatives.

items.statement: Order book and overall visibility for product division remain very strong, positioning company for significant growth trajectory
items.quote: The order book and overall visibility for the product division remain s very strong, positioning this company towards significantly enhancing its growth trajectory in the product business throughout this financial year.

items.statement: 9M FY25 EBITDA margin improved slightly due to cost management, reduced commodity prices, and operating leverage benefits
items.quote: In this period of 9 months, we have seen a slight improvement in the margin largely because of cost management, reduced commodity price, and benefits of operating leverage.

items.statement: Average selling prices slightly reduced in 9M FY25 vs last year due to reduced commodity prices
items.quote: Also, during this period, the average selling price for most of our products is slightly reduced in comparison to last year, largely due to reduced commodity prices during this period.

items.statement: Availability of imported raw materials posed significant challenges in 9M FY25
items.quote: Also, I want to highlight that the availability of imported raw materials has posed significant challenges during the first 9 months.

items.statement: Q3 gross margin decline vs Q2 due to product mix shift: higher AC proportion (lower gross contribution) vs washing machines (higher gross contribution)
items.quote: No, it is actually the product mix change because Q2 typically is slightly better for the washing machines and the proportion of washing machine sales is higher there. And in the Q3 and in the rest of the other quarters, the AC washing sales are as a proportion are typically higher. And gross contribution in the AC business is slightly lower than the gross contribution in washing machines.

items.statement: Inventory elevated at >INR1,025 cr at end of 9M FY25 due to preparation for robust upcoming AC season
items.quote: Additionally, inventory levels are elevated, exceeding INR1,025 crores. This is actually as a result of preparation for the forthcoming air conditioning season, which we anticipate to be very robust.

items.statement: Net cash position of INR793 cr at end of 9M FY25
items.quote: At the conclusion of the 9 months, the balance sheet reflects a net cash position of INR793 crores.

items.statement: QIP funds being used for working capital, new growth opportunities capex, and infrastructure for future growth
items.quote: Partly, this money is being used for working capital because the working capital intensity has gone up. Partially is being for these new growth opportunities, what we are looking at, and this money will be used for those capex only.

items.statement: Bhiwadi AC plant almost commissioned, trial production underway, awaiting BIS certification, expected to start final production this month or next
items.quote: We are commissioning a plant in Bhiwadi for making AC, which has actually been almost commissioned, and we are right now doing trial production and also we are waiting for BIS certification. So that will go into final production from next month, or probably most likely towards the end of this month.

items.statement: Greater Noida washing machine capacity expansion expected to start production end April or early May
items.quote: Apart from that, we are also constructing a plant in Greater Noida for expanding the capacity of washing machines, which we think we should be able to start production probably from the end April or early May.

items.statement: Current AC capacity ~3.5 lakh units/month across both plants
items.quote: So right now, the total capacity that we have is close to about 3.5 lakh ACs that we can do in both the places put together on a monthly basis.

items.statement: Compressor plant building under construction, initial production expected in 9 months after finalization, full ramp-up in additional 3 months
items.quote: See, the building is already under construction. We expect to start initial production in next 9 months once we finalize from the moment we finalize, 9 months is, I think, is a good period that we'll be able to start the initial production and another 3 months to fully ramp up that production.

items.statement: Top 5 clients in AC and washing machine contribute ~50-60% of revenue; no AC client >15%, but one washing machine client >15%
items.quote: I can tell you that the Top 5 clients in both AC and washing machine will be probably contributing close to 50% to 60% of the revenue.

items.statement: ~90%+ of revenue growth from mining existing clients rather than new client additions
items.quote: So I can say probably on a ballpark, almost 90% plus revenue growth is coming from mining the existing clients only.

items.statement: Company estimates ~1.2 ACs manufactured by PG for every 10 ACs sold in India; ~1 washing machine per 10 sold
items.quote: Right now, that figure should be, in our opinion, close to about 1.2 ACs being manufactured by PG for the 10 ACs getting sold in India.

items.statement: Outsourcing share in RAC market estimated to have rebounded above 40% in FY25 after declining to 37-38% last year
items.quote: And this is the year when this has started rebounding and then I am making assertion because on the basis of the fact that in the first 9 months, all the 3 large outsourcing companies in the AC have shown much higher growth than the industry growth . Therefore, this year, probably that number is probably inching back above 40% in our estimate.

items.statement: PLI for compressors not pursued due to onerous targets; compressor manufacturing to be done outside PLI
items.quote: So it was not making sense for us to go for a PLI for a compressor. And that's why we have not actually included it in the PLI application for compressors. So, we will be doing compressors if we do outside of it.

items.statement: PLI income of INR30 cr for FY24 performance to be recognized in Q4 FY25; FY25 PLI expected INR37.5 cr, FY27 INR52 cr, FY28 INR60 cr
items.quote: We have built in about INR30 crores of money, which we will be getting from PLI for our last year's performance, which is FY '24 year performance. So the way we account is that we account PLI only when we receive it. So that we will be getting in the fourth quarter, and that will bump up the margins.

items.statement: State government incentives expected ~INR25 cr/year for next 12 years once application accepted
items.quote: On the state government benefits, we hope to get about INR25 crores each year for the next 12 years once we make an application and our application is accepted, so which we intend to do maybe next year.

items.statement: Advanced discussions for compressor tie-up; targeting ~17% ROC, margin accretive as largely for in-house use
items.quote: For compressors, we look at, at least 17% to 16% or 18% around 17% of ROC for this number. And at a company level, it will be actually margin accretive because largely it will be for our own in-house only.

items.statement: EV assembly business with battery expected to start in 2-4 months, targeting ~INR500 cr sales by year 2 with single client
items.quote: We hope that by the second year, we should be reaching about INR500 crores kind of sales in that business with this client only.

items.statement: Q4 ordering remains very strong, explicit guidance for at least 48% overall sales growth in Q4, largely driven by AC
items.quote: See Q4 ordering remains very strong, and we have given actually explicit guidance for Q4. Now we are talking of at least 48% growth in the overall sales. And that will largely be driven by actually AC because in this season now we are entering an off-season for washing machine.

items.statement: Historical 30-35% CAGR over 8-9 years; enough opportunities to continue similar growth, planning infra and capacities accordingly
items.quote: The company historically has been maintaining a growth CAGR for the last 8, or 9 years at about 30%, 35%. We think that we right now have enough opportunities to continue to see that kind of growth, and we will be making all the efforts to probably achieve those kinds of numbers in the coming years as well.

items.statement: Compressor shortage challenge for industry, but company amply covered till end of June due to elevated inventory
items.quote: As Pramodji has earlier disclosed in the call that we have elevated levels of inventory. This has been done in anticipation of the shortage of compressors. So as far as we are concerned, we don't see major -- see, there is a challenge for the industry. That is there. Definitely, it is there. But we believe that we are a little better prepared and we are amply covered till the end of June to take c

items.statement: Goodworth JV revenue INR436 cr in 9M FY25; EBITDA decent but net profit low due to interest and depreciation; expected to turn profitable in FY26 with 1-2% PAT margins
items.quote: Basically, I think INR436 crores was the revenue in the in the first 9 months. We have actually on the EBITDA done decently, but it's just that the profit or the net is low because of interest and depreciation costs. We are working towards it. And we think that next year, we should be profitable in that business.

items.statement: Festive and winter demand was good; rural/semi-urban sentiment promising; youth share of business rose from 22% to 27%
items.quote: The festivals has been quite good. I would not say it has been very good, because the way we expected, it did not perform as good as that in the last few days of the festival. But yes, post the festival, things were very good. We saw overall demand spurting up because of the marriage season, as well as the winter sale which got generated.

items.statement: Youth share of business increased from 22% to 27%; focused on Gen Z population
items.quote: The youth share of our business has literally gone up because that share used to be somewhere around 22% earlier, now has gone up to 27%.

items.statement: Targeting mid to high single-digit growth going forward

items.statement: No long-term debt on books; comfortable cash position with ample working capital limits

items.statement: Maintains H2 volume growth guidance of 7-8%.
