items.statement: Maintains H2 EBITDA increase guidance of INR150 per tonne.
items.quote: And we are also keeping our projection of what we said about H2 EBITDA increase, which we had indicated between first half to second half, H2 average would be about INR 150 increase in the EBITDA, and we are maintaining that and no change in that.

items.statement: Full year capex expected at INR500 crores.
items.quote: Capex for the whole year, we are looking at a number of INR500 crores.

items.statement: 9-month capex around INR300 crores.
items.quote: 9 months, it is around INR300 crores.

items.statement: Incentive accrual for the year expected around INR100 crores.
items.quote: For this year, as guided earlier, we are expecting total incentive accrual to be around INR 100 crores.

items.statement: 9-month incentive accruals around INR60 crores.
items.quote: For 9 months, that accruals is around INR60 crores.

items.statement: Own coal usage was 15% in Q3.
items.quote: Yes. Our own coal was to the tune of 15% in this quarter.

items.statement: Captive coal share to rise to 30-32% after Bikram reaches optimum.
items.quote: And once Bikram Coal Block comes on field, once that achieved the optimum level of production, it should go up to around 30% -- between 30%, 32% of our total.

items.statement: Bikram coal to reach optimum in FY27.
items.quote: I think next year , it will not reach optimum level. Optimum level will be reached in the next financial year, that is '26-'27.

items.statement: Marki-Barka coal to meet 55-60% of total coal requirements.
items.quote: Marki-Barka once that comes, it will be around 55% -- between 55% and 60% of our total requirements.

items.statement: Green power target 35% in 1-1.5 years.
items.quote: So our aim is to reach to the level of 35%. But it will take -- as you rightly said, it will take another 1 year to 1.5 years.

items.statement: Pet coke price expected to range $100-110.
items.quote: And we expect this to range between $100 to $110 pet coke prices.

items.statement: Net debt around INR3,000 crores as of Q3.
items.quote: Our net debt as of the third quarter is around INR3,000 crores.

items.statement: Closing incentive balance INR435 crores as of Dec 31, 2024.
items.quote: As our closing balance is about INR435 crores as of 31 December '24, this is excluding the West Bengal incentive which is under litigation.

items.statement: Received INR187 crores cash subsidy this financial year.
items.quote: INR187 crores in this financial year.

items.statement: Industry demand growth seen at 4-5% in FY25 and 6-7% in FY26
items.quote: Going forward, what we at JK Lakshmi see is that this year the growth is going to be around 4 % to 5%, somewhere around that, and next year FY26 may be around 6 % to 7%.

items.statement: Consolidated volume growth estimated at 7-8% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Fourth quarter, our estimation is likely to grow at about 7% to 8% and we are going to be in alignment with that, right, 8% I would say.

items.statement: Consolidated volume growth expected to exceed industry 6-7% in FY26
items.quote: I think we are going to do better because I think we have now Udaipur and Surat also in place. So, our growth is going to be better than industry.

items.statement: Surat grinding unit: 0.8 mt phase by Mar 2025, 0.6 mt by Jun 2025
items.quote: First phase is going to get commissioned in the month of March itself or February end, which is about half of the capacity about 0.8 million tons, and another rest of 0.6 million tons during around June 2025.

items.statement: Standalone capacity addition: 1.35 mt in FY26, ~2.5 mt in FY27 (Durg & Prayagraj)
items.quote: FY26 I think on a standalone basis I think we will adding 1.35 million tons only. This is what is the reason as far as FY26 goes. In FY27 may be during Q2 or Q3 we will be adding this Durg and Prayagraj. So, that activity you can see about 2.5 million

items.statement: Current prices Rs 75-100/t above Q3 FY25 average
items.quote: I would say definitely about Rs.75 to Rs.100.

items.statement: Brand rejuvenation targets Rs 80-100/t price positioning improvement
items.quote: the idea is to improve price positioning and perhaps I think that is going to give some good benefit in terms of at least improving our price positioning by Rs.80 to Rs.100 a ton.

items.statement: Renewable energy share 48% in Q3 FY25; targeting further increase
items.quote: In the last quarter it was at 48%.

items.statement: Fuel cost Rs 1.57 per 1,000 km in Q3 FY25
items.quote: fuel was at 1.57 for 1,000 Kms.

items.statement: Standalone gross debt Rs 650 cr, cash Rs 300 cr, net debt Rs 50 cr; Consolidated gross debt Rs 2,150 cr, cash Rs 400 cr, net debt Rs 1,750 cr
items.value: Standalone net 50 cr; Consol net 1,750 cr
items.quote: Standalone gross debt is 650 crores, 300 crores of cash, so net debt is 50 crores on standalone basis. On a consol basis, gross debt is 2,150, 400 is the cash, so 1750 is the net debt on consol basis.

items.statement: Launched 'JK Lakshmi Green Plus' on 14 Jan 2025; brand architecture unified Pan-India
items.quote: we have launched a new brand called JK Lakshmi Green Plus. So, we have launched on 14th of January this year and the initial feedback from the market is very encouraging.

items.statement: Demand improved from December 2024; good in operating markets; prices improving
items.quote: last quarter from December, demand has started improving, demand is good in our operating markets and so is the prices also are improving.

items.statement: Budget capex Rs 11.21 lakh cr (half cement-linked) to drive demand in FY26
items.quote: budget also has the CAPEX of about 11.21 lakh crores. And out of that, half of that is going to be in areas where cement is directly related.

items.statement: Madhavan Menon announced retirement after 25 years; Mahesh Iyer to succeed as Executive Chairman with systematic transition plan
items.quote: I've completed 25 years at Thomas Cook. And having done all that I've done over this period, I thought it was time to pass the baton on to Mahesh, who has worked with me through these entire 25 years

items.statement: Consolidated Nature Trails brand and 3 resorts from Sterling into TCIL domestic operations to expand offerings and leverage distribution
items.quote: The second important announcement that we made was obviously about the consolidation of the Nature Trails brand and its operations into TCIL's domestic operations

items.statement: Guided 12-15% top-line growth for travel segment; aim to reach 5% EBIT margin by end of FY2026
items.quote: We've said 12% to 15% growth is our guidance on the travel segment. And I think MICE is going to be no exception to that

items.statement: Travel vertical EBIT margin at 3.9% for 9M FY25; adjusted for one-offs would be 4.1-4.2%, progressing toward 5% target
items.quote: if you look at our EBIT margin on the travel vertical, we are holding at 3.9%. Now if you look at FY '24 and compare that to FY '25 for the 9-month period, the 3.9% is despite the one -offs that we have seen in the curren t quarter

items.statement: India businesses led growth: Financial Services +16%, DMS +19%, B2C +29%, Sterling +12% YoY in Q3
items.quote: If you look at financial services, the turnover increased 16% year-on-year. If you look at DMS, it increased by 19% year-on-year. If you look at the B2C segment, was up by 29%

items.statement: Forward bookings show 20%+ PAX growth and 25-28% volume growth for current quarter; Europe summer bookings picking up
items.quote: I'm looking at more than 20% PAX growth in the current quarter, and I'm looking at volume growth, which tops 25% to 28%

items.statement: Sterling launched 3 new resorts in Q3 (Wayanad, Coorg, Ranthambore); portfolio now 48 locations, 57 resorts; asset-right model with limited capex
items.quote: During the quarter, Sterling launched three new reso rts, Sterling Lontano in Wayanad, Kerala. This takes us to the third resort in Wayanad, Sterling Coorg in Karnataka and Sterling Ranthambore in Rajasthan

items.statement: Sterling occupancy at 61% in Q3 despite 16% room night increase; average room rate INR 6,788; pipeline of new destinations for 2025
items.quote: Our occupancies for Q3 were at 61%, also indicating the headroom available actually for us for further revenue expansion. This is despite our available room nights having gone up by 16% over Q3 FY '24

items.statement: Thai Baht depreciated 8% in 45 days (Sep-Nov) causing ~INR 5.5 cr EBIT impact; rates now stable at 34.1-34.2/USD
items.quote: Between 30th September and the 15th of November, the Thai Baht depreciated against the dollar by an astounding 8%, which is very unusual

items.statement: Government MICE contracts have payment schedules; final 3-4 month delay factored into workings; all prior dues recovered
items.quote: The contracts are drawn out in such a way that there is a payment schedule that the government has agreed with us. And I'm happy to let you know that payments as per that schedule have come in, in most cases

items.statement: Sterling EBITDA margin 38.8% in Q3 (above 30-35% threshold); income INR 1,389M, EBITDA INR 539M, EBIT INR 427M
items.quote: Our EBITDA margins for Q3 FY '25 has exceeded our intended threshold of 30% to 35% to close at 38.8%

items.statement: Financial Services EBIT margin expanded 592 bps in Q3; 9M EBIT margin up 700 bps; borderless prepaid float INR 1,364 cr (+13% YoY)
items.quote: EBIT margins in the Financial Services for the 9 months, actually improved by 700 basis points

items.statement: Digital adoption in FX at 22%; 2,900 video KYC transactions at 85% success rate; WhatsApp channel tracking ~2,000 transactions
items.quote: We're currently at about 22% digital adoption and the float on the borderless prepaid card continued to grow

items.statement: Corporate Travel non-air business grew 54%, card business 131%; non-air share rose from 5% to 8% of portfolio in 2024
items.quote: our non -air and card business has grown by 54% and 131%, resp ectively. These are 2 levers for margin expansion

items.statement: DEI renewal rate >92%; 17 partnerships renewed in UAE, Maldives, Singapore; 2 new partnerships in India, Maldives; 3 operationally launched
items.quote: We've had more than 92% renewal rate, 17 new partnerships renewed in UAE and Maldives and Singapore

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions impacted Dubai (Nov occupancy tepid, Jan 85-90%); East Africa lost customer contributing 25% of sales; currency volatility risk
items.quote: Demand in Dubai was tepid all the way through November because of the problems that Israel and Iran had and combine that with Syria, Lebanon and Yemen

items.statement: Sterling DTA not fully utilized; will evaluate lower tax regime after full utilization in current quarter
items.quote: It is not yet fully utilized. There is still something left, which will happen in this quarter, in the current quarter. And thereafter, the company will take a call on that

items.statement: Kumbh Mela: 1,000 tents booked, ~1,400 passengers traveled, expect ~2,000 by season end; Japan cherry blossom season delayed to mid-April, at 85-90% of last year volumes
items.quote: We've booked about 1,000 tents, close to about 1,400 passengers have travelled through us till date. And we expect by the time this season ends or the Kumbh Mela ends, we would have roughly close to about 2,000 passengers

items.statement: Pricing strategy well-benchmarked; tactical moves based on competition; raised prices at Kumbh where demand outpaced supply
items.quote: Currently, the pricing and discount strategy that we play is well benchmarked to how the markets across are operating

items.statement: ASEAN currency volatility (Thai Baht -8% in 45 days) impacted DMS profitability; USD/INR volatility from Trump tariff talk noted but not expected to cause dramatic change
items.quote: In the foreign exchange space, there has been some degree of volatility because of the Trump -- the new US regime that's in place and talking up the dollar with tariffs, etc

items.statement: Expects tractor industry to grow over 15% in Q4, taking full-year growth to possibly over 7%
items.quote: We expect the industry in the Quarter 4 to grow by over 15%, which will take the full year growth to possibly over 7%.

items.statement: Sees strong signs of tractor demand growth in Q4 driven by reservoir levels, Rabi sowing, MSP and terms of trade
items.quote: There are several reasons driving this optimism. One is , the reservoir levels, which are at a very good level, 16% above LPA, a good progress on the Rabi sowing, good growth on the Kharif crop.

items.statement: Farm co-tractor margin improved 260 bps YoY to 19.5%; overall Farm margin at 18.1%
items.quote: The Farm margins and especially the co-tractor margin, which is domestic plus tractor exports from India, we've gone up to 19.5% margin, which is an improvement o f 2.6 points over last year's same

items.statement: Auto standalone margin improved 120 bps YoY to 9.7%
items.quote: The Auto standalone margin grew to 9.7%, an increase of 1.2 share points.

items.statement: Auto consolidated margin at 8.6% includes EV marketing spend, depreciation and manpower costs
items.quote: Which is 8.6. So, that has the impact of little bit of depreciation and the marketing spend plus the manpower costs of the field team and all of that which was all costs in Q3.

items.statement: Will increase 3XO capacity by a couple of thousand units within 3-4 months; ROXX capacity to increase by 1,500-2,000 units by June-July
items.quote: We are working on increasing the total 9,000 by a couple of thousand because it's going to be within the same infrastr ucture. That will take another 3 -4

items.statement: 3XO capacity currently 9,000/month constrained by gasoline-diesel mix; ROXX now has complete fungibility with 3-door Thar
items.quote: 3XO we have a capacity of about 9000. Firstly, we are constrained by the mix of gasoline and diesel because we had estimated about 65% -70% to be gasoline and balance to be diesel.

items.statement: EV launches (BE 6, XEV 9E) targeting initial volume of ~5,000/month combined; bookings open Feb 14 across 250+ outlets
items.quote: We should be able to do a starting initial volume of about 5,000 a month for both the products together. We have also put out the full price list with the schedule of which variants will start when, with bookings opening on 14th Feb.

items.statement: EV pricing applicable at time of delivery, not locked to volume; will work on cost reduction and localization post-launch
items.quote: What we have said on pricing is pricing at time of delivery, which after learning over multiple launches, we find that that's the best way to handle it rather than try to put a volume or whatever

items.statement: Auto price hikes of 0.7% YTD Dec and additional 0.8% in January
items.quote: Price hikes, basically, Auto YTD December, which was about 0.7, and then we have taken another 0.8 in January.

items.statement: Strong demand for 3XO and ROXX with long waiting lists; South Africa 3XO run rate ~700/month
items.quote: We are also seeing a very strong demand from South Africa. 3XO we have launched there a few months back. Right now the run rate is almost 700 a month.

items.statement: EV buyers largely new to Mahindra, from luxury car segment (25-30 lakh bracket); multi-car owners
items.quote: Actually, I should have covered that. Again, what we are hearing right now is a very large proportion of people who never considered Mahindra. These are people who are in the 25 lakh, 30 lakh car bracket, looking at luxury brands or owning a luxury brand.

items.statement: EV category penetration in 3-wheelers rose from 9% to 25% in few quarters; competition helps grow category
items.quote: The important point here is, now the category penetration for electric to the total three-wheeler market is close to 25%. Just few quarters back, that was 9.

items.statement: CAFE 3 norms still under debate with no consensus; likely delayed
items.quote: Theoretically, yes, because there's so much discussion yet and there is no consensus on what exactly it should be. There's a SIAM view and even within the government there are multiple views.

items.statement: Auto exports grew ~80% in last 4 months; leveraging existing markets (South Africa, Australia, Chile) with current portfolio
items.quote: If you can share some thoughts on how you see the drivers of growth because you have a great set of portfolio, how you can leverage that in various global markets?

items.statement: Mahindra brand tractor inventory correction largely done; no significant correction needed in Q4
items.quote: We're by and large done, so there'll be almost no need to do any significant correction in Q4. We did some in Q3 as well.

items.statement: No captive financing for SCVs; first-time buyers 40-60% of market but no financing stress seen
items.quote: First time buyers are typically market load operators because they are people who become self-employed entrepreneurs by buying a vehicle and putting it on a stand or attaching it to captive use. That even today in the market sits at about depending on the less than 2 ton and 2-3.5 ton, it is still in the region of 40%-60%.

items.statement: PLI for LMM (104 cr) accrued mostly in FY24 and fully received; MEAL PLI accrual depends on milestones and supplier certifications
items.quote: So, most of it was accrued in F24 and we've received all of it. 100% of what we accrued has been received.

items.statement: SUV revenue market share up 200 bps to 23%; LCV market share up 230 bps to 51.9%; Farm market share up 240 bps to 44.2% (highest ever quarter)
items.quote: Auto volume up 16%, SUV market share up 200 basis points to 23% from a revenue standpoint. Farm volume up 20%, market share up 240 basis points at 44.2% right now.

items.statement: Hospitality occupancy at 84%, average unit realization up 37%
items.quote: Hospitality sees an 84% occupancy rate, average unit realization at an increase of 37%.

items.statement: Real estate: Bhandup land acquisition 37 acres, 12,000 crore GDV
items.quote: And this is something , in addition to other wins that the business has had, has put the business very much on a very strong momentum, and one that is looking at significant growth in the coming years.

items.statement: KG Mobility mark-to-market loss impacted consolidated profit; core organic profit growth strong
items.quote: The main reason for that is we had a mark-to-market impact this quarter from KG Mobility, the investment that we have in KG Mobility.

items.statement: EV ramp-up will prioritize quality over speed; sold <2,000 units in Jan for dealer displays/test drives
items.quote: We started 9e in December, we started BE in January and last month we sold less than 2000, which is mainly for dealer displays and test drives and we're going to ramp up slowly.

items.statement: All critical EV integrating software (BMS, zonal architecture, ECU) owned in-house by MEAL
items.quote: No, all critical integrating software is owned by us. So, the BMS software is ours, all the zonal architecture, ECU software, all of that is owned by us.

items.statement: Will separate EV contract manufacturing margin and born-electric end-to-end margin in reporting from Q4
items.quote: So, we will see an impact of that on the standalone numbers by way of margin, and hence, we will show you the numbers separately.

items.statement: EPS growth target 15-20% from FY21 onwards; currently well ahead and aiming to stay consistent
items.quote: Second is on EPS, we've talked about a 15 to 20% growth in EPS from F21 onwards. I think we are well ahead of that at this point in time, and we hope to stay consistent in terms of growth in EPS as well.

items.statement: Consolidated ROE maintained around 18%
items.quote: ROE stays around 18%. I've always mentioned that it will be plu s-minus. So that is something that we managed to stay at that level

items.statement: EV per-unit net variable margin not negative; EBIT losses initially due to depreciation burden, not outsized
items.quote: none of our vehicles on a per unit basis are selling at a loss on the net variable margin basis. What you are going to see, like in any startup operations, is a heavy burden of depreciation and that at an EBIT level wil l drive certain losses but it's part of the business plan

items.statement: Cumulative 6-6.5% price increase planned across Q3, Q4 and Q1 next year to offset 11% commodity inflation
items.quote: We've already taken in Q3 2%. In Q4, it's going to be another 2.5%. And then in Q1, which is going to be the Q1 of next year, it's going to be another 1.5%. So cumulatively, it's going to be 6%, 6.5% price increase.

items.statement: Cost efficiency target of 2.5% of revenue for next year, potentially higher
items.quote: We are again looking at 2.5% for next year, and hopefully even more than that.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR150-200 crores for FY26 unless volume increases require more
items.quote: So INR150 crores to INR200 crores is what we'll keep it at, unless there is a volume increase.

items.statement: Staff cost growth target at 0.75x of top line growth
items.quote: Our principle is that our -- if our top line growth is X, our fixed cost growth or our people cost growth should be 0.75X.

items.statement: PAT margin at 13% for the quarter, up over last 3 quarters
items.quote: And if you were to look at the ratios, the numbers have moved up in the last 3 quarters, and we are at profit after tax of 13%.

items.statement: Targeting current EBITDA margin range, no forward forecast given
items.quote: So we will stay in the current range, I would say. That would be the range that we would look at, although we don't give any forward-looking forecast, but I would say current range is what we would target.

items.statement: Commodity inflation at ~11% for the quarter, led by palm oil at 43% and cocoa at 103%
items.quote: Our inflation for our products that we buy is about 11%. This would have been at least 2% to 4% higher had we not done the forward buying.

items.statement: Revenue growth of 6.5% with volume growth almost at par, indicating no price increase impact yet
items.quote: If you were to look at our revenue growth and our volume growth, they are almost at par, which shows that we have not taken any price increase till now.

items.statement: Core biscuits volume growth at 5.5%, adjacencies growing faster creating 0.8-0.9% delta
items.quote: It's about 5.5%. So not a big difference. There's a delta, because as I said, the adjacency business is much smaller for us but growing faster.

items.statement: Direct distribution expanded from 27.9 lakh to 28.8 lakh outlets, rural distributors from 30,000 to 31,000
items.quote: We have moved from March '24 of 27.9 lakh outlets to 28.8 lakh outlets. And even our rural distri butors have moved up from 30,000 to 31

items.statement: Adjacencies growing strongly: croissant to cross INR200 crores next year, milk shakes already crossed INR200 crores
items.quote: Today, our croissant business is -- next year will cross INR200 crores, right. Our milk shakes business has already crossed INR200 crores, right.

items.statement: E-commerce contribution higher for adjacencies: croissant 17%, cake 9%, dairy 11% vs biscuits ~4%
items.quote: For example, biscuits is 4% as far as e-com is concerned or slightly lower than 4%. But let's say, I'm just giving you 1 or 2 numbers so that you get an idea. For croissant, it's 17%; for cake, it's 9%, right; for dairy, it's 11%.

items.statement: Focus states contribute ~15% of revenue, growing at 1.3-1.4x national average, market share half of rest of India
items.quote: These states basically contributes about 15-odd percent to our overall revenue. And they have been growing at about 1.3 to 1.4x, which means that over a period of time from 12%, 13%, they've moved to 15%, 16%.

items.statement: No concern from new entrants like Amul or Reliance tie-up; brands provide competitive moat
items.quote: Not really, Abneesh. We haven't seen any signs of worry at this point in time. And if we do see something, we will obviously react at that point in time.

items.statement: Three new large facilities commissioned at Ranjangaon, UP, TN, Bihar plus Orissa expansion providing capacity headroom
items.quote: We've recently put up 3 large facilities, Ranjangaon, UP and in TN, also in Bihar, Bihta, and we've expanded our Orissa facility as well.

items.statement: Forward buying saved 2-4% on commodity inflation; wheat season starting March may normalize flour prices
items.quote: This would have been at least 2% to 4% higher had we not done the forward buying, and we hadn't had that advantage of that forward buying.

items.statement: Stock appreciation rights provision volatility: INR25 cr in Q1, INR50 cr charge in Q2, INR75 cr write-back in Q3
items.quote: Last quarter end, the share price was INR6,338, that became about INR4,762 as of 31st of December, and that had an impact of about INR75 crores in the quarter.

items.statement: PLI and other incentives expected to continue at similar run rate of ~INR125 cr per quarter
items.quote: We estimate that for the coming years, the incentives that we should be able to get, subject to our fulfilling certain conditions that are prescribed under PLI for that, we expect it to be on similar lines as current year.

items.statement: Palm oil import duties confirmed permanent by Finance Minister to indigenize fats production
items.quote: As our Honorable Finance Minister has said, this is basically going to stay because they want to indigenize fats in India.

items.statement: Urban retail channel is 1.3x company average profitability, distribution revamp targeting expansion from 250k to 400k outlets
items.quote: And just to remind you, we are talking about this in urban retail, right. And urban retail is the channel, which is the most profitable channel for us. That is 1.3x the profit of the company, the urban retail channel.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY25 and beyond is 15.5% to 17.5% with bias towards higher end
items.quote: While we did 17.7% in Q3, we don't expect to maintain that 17.7% to be very frank . The guidance that we are giving is in the range of 15 .5% to 17.5% with a slight bias towards the higher end of the range.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance for FY26 is mid to high teens
items.quote: We are looking at mid to high teens kind of growth in terms of revenue.

items.statement: Maintenance capex guided at Rs. 15-20 crore; exploring Rs. 35-50 crore investment to expand Prag Distillery capacity from 6 lakh to 36 lakh cases per annum
items.value: Rs. 15-20 crore maintenance; Rs. 35-50 crore expansion
items.quote: In terms of our CAPEX plans, while maintenance CAPEX will range between Rs.15 to 20 crore, we are exploring making an investment amounting to around Rs.35 to 50 crore for the expansion of our own unit in Andhra Pradesh, housed in our wholly-owned subsidiary, Prag Distillery Private Limited.

items.statement: Prag Distillery capacity expansion planned from 6 lakh to 36 lakh cases per annum in Andhra Pradesh
items.value: 6 lakh to 36 lakh cases per annum
items.quote: This investment will enable us to expand our capacity from around 6 lakh cases per annum to 36 lakh cases per annum.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin at 17.7%, up 408 bps YoY; nine-month margin at 17.2% (15.9% adjusted for subsidy)
items.quote: EBITDA margins expanded by 408 basis points to 17.7% on the back of lower NSR and reduced S&D expenses.

items.statement: Excluding Andhra Pradesh, primary volumes grew 10% YoY in Q3; southern states grew 11%; January 2025 volumes grew 14% YoY
items.quote: Excluding Andhra, our primary volumes in Q3 grew by 10%, indicating strong growth in our other states, especially the southern states, which grew 11% over the same period.

items.statement: Andhra Pradesh secondary volumes grew 8% YoY in Q3 despite primary volume degrowth due to RTM transition
items.quote: Despite degrowth in primary volumes, secondary volumes in Andhra Pradesh grew at 8%, indicating strong brand equity for our products.

items.statement: Market share in key southern states increased to 6.2% in Q3 from 5.8% in FY24; Telangana share expanded to 7.4% from 6.8%
items.quote: TI market share as percentage of overall IMFL in its key southern states has now increased to 6.2% in Q3 from 5.8%, as was seen in FY24.

items.statement: Price correction of ~Rs. 200 per case in Andhra Pradesh impacted NSR; NSR per case at Rs. 1,161 in Q3 vs Rs. 1,270 in Q2
items.quote: The price correction in Andhra blended level on a state basis would be around Rs. 200, reduction.

items.statement: ENA prices expected to remain stable, not highly inflationary; glass and packaging costs stable with some correction seen
items.quote: Yes, for the moment, we are assuming that ENA would range in this region. We haven't taken any kind of reduction on ENA prices currently, but our expectation is that it shouldn't be highly inflationary going forward.

items.statement: Karnataka volume growth >20% YoY driven by excise duty reduction on premium products; NIP 180ml price reduced from Rs. 257 to Rs. 235
items.quote: Karnataka, one of the primary drivers was that the excise duty was reduced on premium products, which led to a price correction, and the price correction has enabled us to deliver strong volume growth in Karnataka.

items.statement: Export volumes in nine months FY25 exceeded full-year FY24 volumes; strong traction in Africa, Middle East, Southeast Asia; Monarch launched in exports first
items.quote: In fact, entire volume which we had done in the previous year, we have completed in nine months itself. Overall, we see a good traction on the export business, particularly in African markets, Middle East, Southeast Asia.

items.statement: Gross debt reduced by Rs. 47 crore in Q3 via Kotak term loan repayment; aggregate gross debt now Rs. 45 crore with net cash of Rs. 31 crore
items.value: Rs. 45 crore gross debt; Rs. 31 crore net cash
items.quote: In Q3, we have reduced our gross debt by Rs.47 crore. This reduction in gross debt was predominantly on account of full repayment of Kotak Bank term loan. Our aggregate gross debt now stands at Rs.45 crore with net cash balance of Rs.31 crore.

items.statement: A&SP reinvestment rate at 1-1.7% of net revenue; guided to increase going forward
items.quote: Our A&SP reinvestment rates range anywhere between 1% to 1.5-1.7%, depending upon the quarter. We end up doing more A&SP spends during the peak seasons as such.

items.statement: Open to tactical acquisitions; 20% stake in Samsara with pathway to increase; evaluating opportunities in whisky and other categories
items.quote: Tactical acquisitions we certainly remain open to. I hope that addressed your question. I think more in terms of distribution of the surplus cash I think that would be more of a Board decision.

items.statement: Expect more states to adopt progressive liquor policies like UP and Andhra Pradesh; Karnataka excise duty reduction on premium products drove volume growth
items.quote: I do expect that there will be more states which will take cues from maybe, if I had to name states, maybe UP and Andhra Pradesh, which have been progressive in the outlook towards the trade.

items.statement: Tax assessment orders received up to AY 23-24; AY 24-25 order pending; company in appeal; tax provision decision deferred until all orders received
items.quote: With respect to the search operation we have received the order still AY 23-24 itself, but not for AY 24-25. Once we receive the order, then accordingly, we will be able to take a call as to how much tax provision if any needs to be made.

items.statement: Current auditors' term extended to FY2027; will explore appointment of new auditor after tenure ends
items.quote: Last year, it has been extended for 3 years, so FY2027.

items.statement: Subsidy income of Rs. 16 crore received in 9M FY25; further subsidy expected in Q4 but amount not quantified
items.quote: We do expect further subsidy to be received in Q4, but it will be difficult at this point to quantify the amount.

items.statement: Q3 order bookings INR20.8bn, down 12% YoY; excluding large transformer order last year, bookings grew significantly
items.quote: Our order book Q3 saw bookings of INR20.8 billion, down by 12% year-on-year compared to INR23.7 billion in quarter ended December '23.

items.statement: Order backlog INR107.8bn as at Dec'24 vs INR62.7bn as at Mar'24, up 72%, record high giving strong revenue visibility
items.quote: Our order backlog stood at INR107.8 billion as at December '24 versus INR62.7 billion as at March, up by 72%.

items.statement: Aim to deliver mid-to-high teens EBITDA margin
items.quote: we aim to be deliver mid to high teens of EBITDA. That is what the team will keep on working to ensure this is what we want to deliver.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA INR1.8bn at 16.7% of revenue vs INR966m at 11.5% YoY; 9M EBITDA INR5.6bn at 18% vs INR2bn at 9.2% YoY
items.quote: We achieved an EBITDA of INR1.8 billion compared to an EBITDA of INR966 million in the corresponding quarter last year. This is a significant increase, almost about 80% increase in the EBITDA on quarterly basis.

items.statement: 9M gross margin 39.8% vs 34.9% YoY, up ~5pp; target gross margin range 35-40%
items.quote: And if you look at the 9 -month performance, we delivered 39.8% gross margin compared to 34.9% in the corresponding 9 -month period last year, which is roughly 5 percentage point increase on a like-to-like basis versus last year.

items.statement: Strong demand for grid modernization, decarbonization, cybersecurity; no slowdown seen up to this quarter
items.quote: Demand for our products remains strong as customers modernize and invest in critical grid components such as transformers, switchgears, control relay panels, software solutions, and HVDC systems.

items.statement: Not seeing slowdown in ordering momentum; sufficient time for opportunities; sustained pipeline for 12-18 months including HVDC
items.quote: So, Umesh, if we talk about up till this quarter, at least we are not seeing any slowdown in this quarter which is ongoing.

items.statement: Capex plan ~INR800m (USD 8-10m) for FY25-26; brownfield expansion space available at Vadodara; evaluating capacity needs constantly
items.quote: I think in last call, Parikshit, we talked about $8 million to $10 million or about roughly INR800 million of capex that we plan.

items.statement: Transformer factory expansion underway; brownfield space available; not fully utilizing capacity; debottlenecking ongoing
items.quote: In fact, there is an expansion, which is already happening -- which is happening at our transformer factory. And also, we are looking at other product lines as well where we can do the expansion.

items.statement: Q3 order booking 85% domestic, 15% export; 9M 61% domestic, 39% export; target 30% export share of inflows including parent
items.quote: On a 9-month basis, out of INR77.8 billion of orders, about 61% orders are from the domestic market and 39% from export.

items.statement: 75-80% of 9M export orders from group entities; direct participation in Africa, SE Asia, LatAm, parts of Europe, Australia
items.quote: On a 9-month basis, roughly 75% to 80% of the export orders are from the group entities.

items.statement: Pricing power supported by raw material cost increases; no significant margin change expected in next 12-18 months; supply chain bottlenecks persist
items.quote: There is a big jump in the raw material prices, which is also happening, which is pushing up the end product prices. So, it's not that the OEMs are just unilaterally increasing the prices.

items.statement: Supply chain constraints on international vendors; component capacity not growing fast enough to feed OEMs globally
items.quote: Today, there is a challenge on the supply chain side. And there are a lot of international vendors or there is a lot of international supply chain also on which the vendors are dependent.

items.statement: Backlog: 68% private, 28% central utilities/PSUs, 4% state utilities; export orders from Portugal, Spain; data center order in Mumbai
items.quote: Of this backlog, 68% backlog is from the private customers and INR29 billion or 28% of the backlog is from the central utilities and public sector enterprises and a very small INR4.6 billion or 4% of the backlog of order in hand is from the state utilities.

items.statement: Cash & equivalents INR8.6bn Dec'24 vs INR2.8bn Mar'24; generated INR1.9bn in Q3 and INR6.4bn in 9M before dividend
items.quote: Cash and cash equivalent balance improved, and stood at INR8.6 billion as on 31st December versus INR2.8 billion as on 31st March 2024.

items.statement: No borrowings mentioned; surplus cash invested in cash pools and fixed income securities; Board evaluating deployment options
items.quote: So, there are various options the Board is evaluating, and we'll share when there is a specific decision from the Board. But at present, we continue to invest in the cash pool and fixed income securities.

items.statement: Employee cost 9M INR310cr vs INR279cr YoY (+10-11%); run rate ~INR105cr/qtr; Q2 spike due to specific benefit reserves
items.quote: Employee cost has increased on a 9-month basis, if you look at this. The last year 9 months, we had INR2.7 billion or INR279 crores. And this time, we have INR310 crores.

items.statement: STATCOM addressable market INR3,000-3,500cr; participating in bids
items.quote: So, we are looking at the market size, we are looking at about close to about INR3,000 crores to INR3,500 crores of market for STATCOM.

items.statement: Supply chain bottlenecks remain biggest industry challenge; raw material cost pressure; capacity expansion limited by component supply
items.quote: So, till the time the investments are not happening on an equal scale with the supply chain side, this challenge will remain as one of the biggest for the industry.

items.statement: 9M revenue mix: 75% products, 25% projects; automation share stable; not disclosing detailed product line splits
items.quote: On a 9-month basis, roughly 25% of the revenue is from the projects and 75% revenue is from the products.

items.statement: 9M order book INR77.8bn vs INR44.5bn YoY (+75%); Q3 key orders: Sterlite Grid 765kV GIS/transformers, 400kV AIS for 1.4GW solar, 765kV breakers, 200kV GIS for data center, export to Portugal/Spain
items.quote: And similarly, on a full year basis, we achieved order book of INR77.8 billion compared to INR44.5 billion in the last year, which represents 75% growth.

items.statement: No specific export-domestic revenue split guidance; both markets important; endeavour to maintain ~INR17bn/qtr order run rate (ex-large export order)
items.quote: We have never specified a number of export versus domestic. We always communicated that both markets are important for us, and we continue to work in this direction to bring in as much business as we can.

items.statement: Long duration orders ~INR30-35bn (large export); rest 18-24 months execution; ~30% variable price contracts; conservative costing with inflation buffers
items.quote: So, the long duration orders are roughly INR30 billion to INR35 billion, and those are related to the large export orders that we have booked. Rest of the orders have the execution timeline of 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: Q3 revenue INR10.7bn (+28% YoY); 9M revenue INR31.3bn (+39% YoY), nearly equal to full FY24 revenue; domestic 78%/73%, export 22%/27%
items.quote: Our Q3 revenues stood at INR10.7 billion versus INR8.4 billion in Q3 FY '23 -'24, up by 28%.

items.statement: Export margins 3-5pp better than domestic; gap narrowing recently; blended 9M EBITDA 18% at high end of mid-to-high teens target
items.quote: Generally, the margin on export is better than the margin on the domestic side. There is 3 percentage point to 5 percentage point difference. But off late, we have seen that the margins in the domestic side is also picking up.

items.statement: Other income INR26cr: ~INR10cr interest on cash pools, ~INR10cr interest on tax refund, ~INR4-5cr bad debt recovery
items.quote: Roughly, let's say, INR100 million out of INR250 million is the interest on cash pools. Almost in similar range, we have a interest on refund. And the third element is roughly INR40 million to INR50 million of recovery of bad debt.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 EBITDA margin guidance maintained at around 15% on consolidated basis
items.quote: I think our guidance was that we'll be hovering the full year around 15%. I think we are still on track.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue CAGR target of about 10% over next 3-5 years
items.quote: But I think if we are able to do a CAGR of about 10-odd percent in the short term, we'll be happy with that.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 standalone EBITDA margin 13.2% due to one-time business development costs; 9M margin 14.4% in line with guidance
items.quote: The number for Q3 FY '25 at 13.2% is an anomaly for that quarter because of certain one-time expenses on business development.

items.statement: HVDC contactor business expected to have operating losses for first 18-24 months, then healthy double-digit margins by FY28
items.quote: On a steady-state basis going third, fourth year, this business is going to have a healthy double-digit margin structure.

items.statement: INR30 crore capex over next 18 months for both HVDC contactor and latching relay lines under Sterling Tech-Mobility
items.quote: We're looking at a INR30 crores-odd capex in the next 18 months.

items.statement: MCU capacity over 700,000 units annually with current configuration; no immediate expansion planned
items.quote: Our current capacity is -- I mean, depending on how we configure the shifts, et cetera, is over 700,000 units.

items.statement: South fastener plant operating at ~60% utilization; can support INR800-850 crore revenue at full capacity
items.quote: The South plant is currently probably operating at about a level of 60%.

items.statement: HVDC contactor production to start Q2 FY26 with live customer orders; FY26 revenue ~INR30 crore
items.quote: On an FY '26 basis, we're looking at a marginal revenue of about INR30-odd crores only.

items.statement: Latching relay partnership with Meishuo Electric projected to generate INR200+ crore revenue by FY30
items.quote: This collaboration is projected to generate INR200 crores plus revenue in FY '30

items.statement: Not participating in Ola Gen 3 integrated platform; remain single source for Gen 2
items.quote: We are not participating in the Gen 3 with Ola. We are -- we continue to be single source on Gen 2.

items.statement: Integrated motor-controller unit 5-10% cheaper than separate units; 3-in-1 adds ~INR20-25 over 2-in-1
items.quote: An integrated unit will possibly be somewhere like INR90 or INR95. So, there will be a 5% to 10% reduction in the cost of the 2 units

items.statement: MCU pricing ranges INR3,500-4,000 (low end) to >INR4 lakh (high end); represents 3-10% of vehicle BOM
items.quote: Our lowest cost MCU would be about INR3,500, INR4,000 and our most expensive motor control unit would be more than INR4 lakh.

items.statement: First Indian company to manufacture HVDC contactors locally; currently all imported
items.quote: As far as HVDC contactors are concerned, we expect to be the first company in India to manufacture these locally.

items.statement: Latching relay imports currently INR150-200 crore from China; market growing across EVs, smart metering, hybrids
items.quote: Currently, all the imports are coming in from China. Our estimation is that the current imports are in the range of about INR150 crores to INR200 crores

items.statement: Standalone revenue grew 8.7% YoY in Q3 FY25 vs industry 3.1%; 9M consolidated revenue up 24.5% to INR832 crore driven by SGEM (56% growth)
items.quote: The company registered a steady state performance with a consolidated top line revenue increasing by 24.5% year-on-year to INR832 crores in 9 months of FY '25.

items.statement: Fastener business growing 7-9% YoY vs industry 3%; guidance to maintain few percentage points above industry growth
items.quote: Fastener is a very mature business with us. We'll be up 7%, 8%, 9% this year. Industry is only up 3%.

items.statement: New business losses marginal relative to balance sheet size; no material impact on overall profitability
items.quote: These are marginal numbers. The loss numbers are marginal numbers for the balance sheet size we have or the P&L we have.

items.statement: Building own IP and tech centers; team developed independent MCU with owned IP; long-term goal technology independence
items.quote: The team has been able to develop an independent MCU now with IP owned by us. So, it's a process which takes some time to do, but we are very clear that we want to be independent, long term

items.statement: EV component integration trend (motor+controller+charger) will play out over several years; programs locked for FY28-29
items.quote: This is a trend that will take several years to actually play out. It's because already companies have locked in programs for the next couple of years.

items.statement: Magnetics facility with MOTIVELINK for Hyundai/Kia anchor business expected ready in 8-10 months
items.quote: Our magnetics business with MOTIVELINK or Yongin Electronics is an anchor business with Hyundai and Kia. We are hoping to have manufacturing facilities ready for that as well in the next -- my guess would be 8 to 10 months.

items.statement: Greenfield alkaline battery plant in Jammu with Rs. 180 crore outlay, commercial production expected by end of calendar year
items.quote: We have finalized plans for a greenfield production facility for alkaline batteries with a capital outlay of Rs. 180 crore. This facility, located in Jammu, is expected to commence commercial production by the end of this calendar year.

items.statement: Jammu alkaline plant to start at Rs. 100 crore annual revenue, scalable to Rs. 400 crore
items.quote: So, I am saying that first year, we may start with the Rs. 100 crore revenue from that plant on annualized basis, and which could go up to Rs. 400 crore.

items.statement: Jammu plant financed 75% debt, 25% internal accruals
items.quote: So, of course some part will be going internally if you have, I have already mentioned that like land we have internally paid money so maybe it's a 75-25 type of financing, 25% will be internal things and 75% probably will take from the banks and other financial institutions

items.statement: Domestic alkaline manufacturing expected to improve alkaline margins by 8-10%
items.quote: And we expect 8% to 10% margin improvement is possible on alkaline part of this operation through domestic manufacturing.

items.statement: Debt repaid Rs. 35-40 crore YTD, targeting Rs. 225-230 crore by year-end on like-to-like basis excluding project capex
items.quote: This year also by this time we have almost paid around Rs. 35- Rs. 40 crore debt and in fact we have funded the Jammu land purchase from that money. So, we are in the course of the similar kind of, if you see like to like, we'll be ending the year at the like to like of debt payment, like last year we paid around Rs. 85 crore. So, maybe year end, we are targeting around, right now we are around Rs

items.statement: Peak debt expected at Rs. 325-330 crore including Jammu plant capex
items.quote: Maximum, I think maybe another Rs. 100 odd crore because if you take some, we'll also pay back some. So, as we have got Rs. 150 odd crore of debt we need for this plant. So, maybe if I add that mathematically and Rs. 50 odd crore I will repay as a part of my, so maximum I think around Rs. 325 to Rs. 330 odd crore would be the peak

items.statement: Alkaline battery segment growing at strong double-digit rate, carbon zinc flat to marginal volume growth
items.quote: So, as Suvamoy mentioned, actually if you see, alkaline is really growing up, like we may be growing 2x rate, but as a segment it is showing at least very strong double-digit growth. And we look forward to the segment to grow up, while the carbon zinc may remain flat or a very marginal volume growth

items.statement: Battery revenue split YTD: carbon zinc Rs. 615 crore, alkaline Rs. 41 crore (15% premium alkaline)
items.quote: Out of the segment, around Rs 615 crore is carbon zinc and alkaline is around Rs. 41 crore. 15% of that is a premium battery, alkaline.

items.statement: Flashlight revenue split: 60% battery-operated, 40% rechargeable
items.quote: So, 60% is battery operated and 40% is rechargeable.

items.statement: Alkaline battery market share doubled to 11% in Q3, aspiration to reach 20% next, eventually 53%
items.quote: Our market share in this category has nearly doubled to 11% at the quarter's end, driven by strong product propositions, robust distribution and consistent marketing efforts.

items.statement: Overall battery market share maintained at 53% across carbon zinc and alkaline
items.quote: Overall, we maintained a 53% market share in the total battery market, spanning both carbon zinc and alkaline segments.

items.statement: Rechargeable flashlights now 70% of market, Eveready at 30% share, up from late entry
items.quote: So, rechargeable flashlights have come over the last 5 years and today occupy about 70% of the market. We are very strong in the battery operated one where we hold something like 70% odd of the market. And we have been somewhat late in trend to the rechargeable one. We have taken giant strides for the last 2 years. We have launched a few products and today we are about 30% of the market.

items.statement: BIS mandatory certification for flashlights gazetted, 6-month transition period, expected to weed out unorganized players
items.quote: BIS has now come out with a mandatory certification which has been of course approved by the Government whereby all products, all flashlight products would require mandatory certification whether these are imported, or they are manufactured within the country. We believe that this will weed out bulk of the unorganized, so-called unethical segment.

items.statement: Rechargeable flashlight growth expected to uptick immediately post BIS implementation
items.quote: Yes, we see the possibility of an immediate uptick to this.

items.statement: Alkaline market share to remain around 11% for next 2-3 months, next target 20%
items.quote: So, we are currently at 11%. I would imagine to remain somewhere around this level by the next 2 to 3 months. But we would keep on this journey, whereby our next step would be to go to 20% kind of level.

items.statement: Company-level sustainable gross margin aspiration 40-45%, currently around 38-45% depending on measure
items.quote: I guess we should look for 40%, it will be our inspiration to be there in a 39% to 40% but it all depends on that. So, as you know as of now, we have achieved 38% plus, so if you ask me, our aspiration will be towards 40%

items.statement: Consumer pricing unchanged by Jammu plant: popular carbon zinc Rs. 14, premium carbon zinc Rs. 18, popular alkaline Rs. 22, premium alkaline Rs. 50
items.quote: There is a popular battery which is more rural oriented that sells at Rs. 14. There is a premium offering of carbon zinc which sells in the more city-like markets, which is at Rs. 18. You have correctly mentioned the value alkaline. The popular alkaline sells at Rs. 22 and then there is a premium alkaline selling at Rs. 50. So, this is the condition today. The Jammu plant is not going to change th

items.statement: Budget import duty removal applies to zinc ash/scrap, not virgin zinc used by company
items.quote: The duty removal is on the zinc ash, scrap zinc ash not on the virgin zinc material.

items.statement: MD Suvamoy Saha reappointed for 6 months (Mar-Sep 2025) to execute succession plan and consolidate gains
items.quote: The objectives for me are two-pronged, primary objectives. One is to see a succession plan installed and executed by the time I leave this position. Number two is we would focus on consolidating the gains that have started accruing to the company.

items.statement: CCI penalty case (Rs. 170 crore) hearing deferred to May 5, 2025, company to defend position
items.quote: So, there was a hearing supposed to be on 28 th-29th of January, which has now been deferred to the 5th of May. So, basically not much movement has taken place on this case. We would of course robustly defend our position.

items.statement: Electrical distributor network at 250 active distributors, target to double in short term
items.quote: We today work with about 250 odd active distributors. Our aim is to make it at least double in the short run.

items.statement: Battery manufacturing has 2-3 month raw material price lag affecting cost pass-through
items.quote: Because you know the battery has a manufacturing time lag, you need to have a battery age for certain period. So, at least 2 to 3 months price lag will come in the manufacturing cost.

items.statement: A&P spend at 10-11% of revenue for next couple of quarters, may reduce to 8-9% as revenue scales
items.quote: So, with respect to A&P, while we are all looking forward to a 10% to 11%, but it does not mean that always it will be 10% to 11%. As the revenue is scaled up, maybe that we can restrict ourselves to 8% to 9% as well, but it is a matter of time. But at this point of time, I think quite some time we have not advertised and now since last 6 to 8 quarter we are building on the TVCs and other digital

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin improved 18.7% YoY despite forex impact and higher zinc costs; PAT up 56%; YTD EBITDA margin 12.1%, PAT margin 6.9%
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved by 18.7% over same quarter last year despite forex impact and higher zinc costs. PAT grew by 56%. The YTD EBITDA and PAT margins stood at 12.1% and 6.9% respectively, both improving over the previous year.

items.statement: Guidance for FY25 and FY26 is high single digits to low double digits volume growth; Q4 expected to be slightly better than Q3
items.value: high single digits to low double digits
items.quote: FY '25, '26, we're looking at high single digits and low double digits.

items.statement: EBITDA margin will be maintained or improved slightly depending on sales volume; brand spend maintained at 2.5% of sales
items.quote: EBITDA margin, we will be improving or maintaining for sure, but improving a little bit depending on how much we are able to sell. Brand spend will be maintained at 2.5%.

items.statement: Domestic demand weaker for industry; Morbi exports down from INR20,000 cr to INR13,000-14,000 cr; green shoots seen in builder orders for Q1/Q2 next year
items.quote: the Morbi industry is only in negative growth. Some of them are shut permanently, some of them are shut for this whole month of January.

items.statement: Operating margin maintained at 8.4% in Q3; gross margin improved 1.4%; gas price up 4%; target 1-1.5% margin improvement from capacity utilization and value-added mix
items.quote: Operating margins were maintained at 8.4%, which is similar to the last quarter. Gross margins improved by 1.4% in Q3.

items.statement: Strong builder orders secured in Dec/Jan; supplies starting Feb/March, bulk in Q1/Q2 next year; project mix to rise 2-3%
items.quote: the kind of orders we have secured with the residential builders and some commercial builders in the month of December and also in January, they're very, very positive.

items.statement: Overall capacity utilization up from 77% to above 80%; bathware at 87% sanitaryware, optimum for faucets; Max plant at 51%, new launch in March/April
items.quote: Capacity utilization went up from 77% to a little above 80%.

items.statement: FY25 capex limited to balancing equipment plus INR10 cr acquisition; FY26 no major capex planned; sanitaryware/fittings expansion needed in 12-18 months
items.quote: Other than balancing equipment for FY '25, which is a new INR10 crore acquisition which we're doing other than the normal balancing equipment, and FY '26, as far as currently is concerned, we have no such plan for any major capex.

items.statement: GVT/PVT mix at 38% (up from 34% last year), targeting 40%+; bathware sales at 8.5% of total; retail 77-80%, project 10-11% govt + 8-9% private, export 2-3%
items.quote: Last year, it was 34% in Q3, and we said we will take it up to 40%. So we are at about 38%, and this is continuing to grow, and it will cross 40% very soon.

items.statement: Retail sales grew in volumes; project sales to increase from next year; builder orders secured but bulk supplies from Q1/Q2 next year
items.quote: Retail sales has grown in terms of volumes. Because builders haven't grown and export has not grown. So whatever has grown has come from retail only.

items.statement: Working capital largely maintained; inventory buildup slight; receivables up only 1-2 days; no sales bought
items.quote: Working capital was largely maintained. We had a little bit buildup in the inventory. So whatever you see a little bit extra is on the inventory side, whereas the balance sheet has been under check.

items.statement: Total debt including JVs at INR299 cr (78% in two new JVs); term loan INR58 cr, current maturities INR41 cr, working capital INR101 cr; asset turnover 2.3x
items.quote: The total debt, inclusive of JV has been brought down. It now stands at INR299 crores, inclusive of all working capital and term loans.

items.statement: Exited two JVs (ceramic wall tiles and GVT) with INR9.42 cr exceptional gain and INR20 cr capital release; acquired 51% in construction chemical business in Bahadurgarh, path to 100% in 3-5 years
items.quote: We do have an exceptional gain of INR9.42 crores with the disinvestment of the 2 JVs and a capital release of INR20 crores, which can be utilized for new strategic investments.

items.statement: Gas pricing: North INR43, West INR49, South INR51; rupee depreciation from 85 to 88 may increase gas cost 1-2%; average realization maintained by not discounting
items.quote: Our Northern plant, the pricing was INR43. Our Western plants, all our Western plants, including the Morbi joint ventures were at INR49, and the Southern plant was at INR51.

items.statement: Distribution network expanded: 134 net dealers and 46 showrooms added in 9 months to Q3
items.quote: Our distribution network increased. We added 134 net dealers and 46 showrooms in the 9 months, which is up to Q3.

items.statement: Economy lagging; need government spending to spur demand; IHB deferred; Morbi oversupply pressuring domestic market; wars ending may improve exports and reduce domestic pressure
items.quote: The economy clearly is lagging, and we need some government spending and to spur up the normal demand.

items.statement: Employee cost up 12-13% due to new hires for strategic initiatives and increments; will normalize when sales pick up
items.quote: No, it's all to do with sales. I mean, we have got some new people in for new strategic initiatives such as this particular acquisition, which we're doing.

items.statement: Receivables well controlled; no sales bought; no cheap quality materials sold; receivables up only 1-2 days
items.quote: And we have not bought any sales. Therefore, our receivables have only gone up by a day or 2, which is in line -- much better than the industry, but in line with our expectations.

items.statement: Management confident of meeting FY25 growth and profitability aspirations
items.quote: We're confident of meeting our growth and profitability aspirations for the fiscal year 2025.

items.statement: US business expected to grow high single digit in FY26
items.quote: we will s till see a high single digit kind of growth, at least for the US overall geography for us and that is what our best estimate is.

items.statement: Sentynl Therapeutics expected to break even in FY26 post CUTX-101 launch
items.quote: I think post CUTX launch, we believe that FY26, we can see break-even for this business.

items.statement: International markets business targeting 23%+ EBITDA margin in next 1-2 years
items.quote: I very strongly believe that it can achieve 23 plus percent EBITDA margin in the next one or two years.

items.statement: Higher capex cycle expected over next two years for complex dosage forms
items.quote: we do believe we need higher capacities with different complex dosage forms. So, there is going to be a higher cycle of capex at least for this coming year and maybe one more.

items.statement: Capex expected to be 20-30% higher than last five-year average
items.quote: So, this higher capex would be up to the tune of what maybe 20%-30% higher than the last five -year or how should we think about it? Dr. Sharvil Patel: Yeah.

items.statement: US business filed 10 ANDAs and received 3 approvals in Q3 FY25
items.quote: We filed 10 additional ANDA s and received approval for 3 new products during the quarter.

items.statement: Launched 5 new products in US including Sitagliptin 505(b)(2) franchise
items.quote: We 3 of 27 launched 5 new products during the quarter. New launches include all three brands of Sita gliptin 505(b)(2) franchise, viz. ZituvioTM, Zituvimet TM and Zituvimet TM XR tablets

items.statement: Secured CVS Caremark formulary placement for Sitagliptin franchise from Jan 1, 2025
items.quote: We entered into an agreement with CVS Caremark to add ZituvioTM, ZituvimetTM and Zituvimet TM XR tablets to its formulary. These products were added to the formulary from the 1 st of January 2025.

items.statement: Seven 505(b)(2) products commercialized in US with 3-4 more licenses expected in next few quarters
items.quote: we have now seven 505(b)(2)s and 8 of 27 we continue to believe that in the next few quarters, we'll have four more licensed products on the 505(b)(2) side

items.statement: Q3 FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin 26.3% vs 24.5% YoY, adjusted 28.1%
items.quote: Reported EBITDA margin for the quarter was 26.3% versus 24.5% in quarter three FY24. EBITDA margin improved despite 250 basis points year-on-year increase in the R &D spend . Adjusted for certain non -recurring expenses, the EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 28.1%.

items.statement: Non-recurring expenses of ~₹95 crore in Q3 FY25 including ₹51 crore incentives, ₹27 crore legal fees, ₹17 crore GST loss
items.quote: there are about 95 crores worth of expenses in this quarter, which are of a non -recurring nature , which includes about 51 crore of provision for incentives , especially given our achievement in US business. items.statement: Targets 60% net EBITDA margin post-renovation on sustainable basis
items.quote: Patanjali Keswani 60%.

items.statement: Expects mid-teens RevPAR growth going forward
items.quote: We would like to have mid-teens growth at the least.

items.statement: Aims to be debt-free in 2-3 years, potentially earlier if Fleur lists
items.quote: we will be debt free in three years. Now the point I am trying to make is that we will be probably debt free earlier the minute we list Fleur.

items.statement: Targets Rs. 11,500-12,000 ARR at 85% occupancy for stabilized Aurika Mumbai
items.quote: Stabilized to me would probably be H2 next year when on a sustained basis we will be north of 85% at Rs. 11,000 plus ARR.

items.statement: Shillong PPP project estimated at Rs. 120 crore for 120 rooms with Rs. 35 crore equity
items.quote: We don't think we will invest more than Rs. 120 crores for 120 rooms because we get a 5% interest subvention, so instead of borrowing money at 8%-8.5%, we will effectively get debt at 3%-3.5%.

items.statement: Total inventory reached 200 hotels and 16,385 rooms (112 operational with 10,317 rooms, 88 pipeline with 6,068 rooms)
items.quote: As of December 31st, 2024, the total inventory of the group, for those of you who like cricket as I do, it was a double century. The total inventory stood at 200 hotels and 16,385 rooms, broken into 112 operational hotels with 10,317 rooms and a pipeline of 88 more hotels with 6,068 rooms.

items.statement: Signed 13 new management/franchise contracts adding 766 rooms, operationalized 1 hotel with 38 rooms in Q3
items.quote: On the asset light side, we signed 13 new management and franchise contracts, adding 766 new rooms to our pipeline and operationalized 1 hotel adding 38 rooms to the portfolio.

items.statement: Expects to hit 20,000 rooms in next 12-15 months, earlier than CY28 vision
items.quote: I had said we would be 20,000 rooms in our CY28 Vision, but we are already at over 16,000 and I am pretty confident we will hit 20,000 in the next 12 months to 15 months, signed and operational.

items.statement: Received letter of award for Aurika Shillong PPP project with 120 rooms, operational in 2.5-3 years
items.quote: this quarter, Lemon Tree received a letter of award from the Directorate of Tourism , Government of M eghalaya for the redevelopment, operation and maintenance of the existing Orchid Hotel in Shillon g under the design, build, finance, operate and transfer mode on a PPP basis. This will be redeveloped as Aurika, Shillong and will be operational within the next 2.5 years to 3 years

items.statement: Q3 FY25 net EBITDA margin 51.9%, up 316 bps YoY
items.quote: Lemon Tree recorded its highest ever third quarter revenue this year at Rs. 355.8 crore. Our revenue grew 22% compared to Q3 last year while net EBITDA grew 30% YoY to Rs. 184.8 crore translating into a net EBITDA margin of 51.9% which increased by 316 bps YoY.

items.statement: Keys portfolio EBITDA target Rs. 60 crore (Rs. 6.5 lakh per key), currently Rs. 3.5 lakh per key annually
items.quote: I had said earlier that we will definitely target a Rs. 60 crore EBITDA from keys, which means really Rs. 6.5 lakhs a Key. Currently, if you look at our EBITDA for the Keys portfolio, it is Rs. 1 lakh, a quarter or I think Rs. 3.5 lakhs a year. We will double that.

items.statement: Renovated Keys Pimpri achieved 24% ARR increase and 80-90% occupancy
items.quote: this hotel, which has got fully renovated, the ARR is 24% over what it was pre-renovation. And now, because the rooms are back, it is doing 90% occupancy – between 80%-90%.

items.statement: Aurika Mumbai Q4 occupancy north of 85%, ARR north of Rs. 9,500; target Rs. 11,000+ ARR at 85% occupancy for stabilization
items.quote: In fact, I think our occupancy is north of 85% and average rate is north of Rs. 9500. But for me that is still not stabilization because as I had mentioned, I think maybe a couple of concalls before, we would like this hotel to be at around Rs. 11,500 to Rs. 12,000 ARR, at about 85% occupancy.

items.statement: Demand growth expected to outpace supply; significant increase in discretionary spending on branded mid-market hotels in India
items.quote: With demand growth expected to outpace supply and an expected significant increase in discretionary spending on branded mid -market hotels in India , w e think this increased investment in renovation will allow us to position Lemon Tree as the largest and preferred brand in the mid-market

items.statement: Foreign demand 15-20% at Aurika Mumbai; focused on capturing Indian domestic demand
items.quote: Foreign demand would be maybe 15%-20%.

items.statement: Not concerned about Navi Mumbai airport impact on Aurika Mumbai; expects temporary blip absorbed by demand growth
items.quote: I don't see based on my experience in airport markets, I don't see that really affecting Mumbai, especially Mumbai I should say.

items.statement: Shillong PPP qualifies for capital subsidy, full GST reimbursement, 5% interest subvention under Meghalaya policy
items.quote: This project qualifies for significant capital subsidy and incentives, including full GST reimbursement and interest subvention by 5% under the Meghalaya Industrial and Investment Promotion Policy 24 and various other policies.

items.statement: 9M FY25 cash profit Rs. 240 crore, repaid Rs. 150 crore debt
items.quote: Our cash profit for the nine months is Rs. 240 crores and we paid back Rs. 150 odd crores of debt which is reflecting in our gross debt fall and we had another Rs. 40 odd crores of cash.

items.statement: Fleur Hotels listing planned in next 1.5-2 years; expects $100 million EBITDA at listing
items.quote: we think it will have a really solid listing because we think it's EBITDA will be $100 million when it lists.

items.statement: Amicably parted ways with Aurika Coorg; close to signing long-lease Aurika Varanasi targeting Rs. 50,000/night market
items.quote: we have amicably parted ways with the Coorg Hotel due to some reasons I am really not at liberty to disclose but Aurika is very much in our strategy. We are very close to signing on long lease, an outstanding Aurika in Varanasi which as you know is a Rs. 50,000 a night market.

items.statement: Wage bill growth ~1.2% annually over 15 years; strategy of internal transfers to new hotels at lower cost than external hires
items.quote: our average wage bill inflation in 15 years is about 1.2%.

items.statement: Q3 FY25: Gross ARR Rs. 6,763 (+7% YoY), Occupancy 74.2% (+826 bps YoY), RevPAR Rs. 5,018 (+21% YoY)
items.quote: Q3 FY25 recorded a gross ARR of Rs. 6,763 which increased 7% YoY. The occupancy for the quarter stood at 74.2%, an increase of 826 bps YoY. This is translated into a RevPAR of Rs. 5,018 which increased 21% YoY.

items.statement: Management fees Rs. 43.7 crore in Q3 (+35% YoY); third-party fees Rs. 18.4 crore (+24%), Fleur fees Rs. 25.3 crore (+45%)
items.quote: Fees from third party-owned hotels for management and franchise contracts stood Rs. 18.4 crore in Q3 FY25, an increase of 24% YoY. Fees from Fleur hotels stood at Rs. 25.3 crore in Q3 FY25, an increase of 45% YoY. Total management fees for Lemon Tree stood at Rs. 43.7 crore in Q3, an increase of 35% YoY.

items.statement: Pipeline conversion risk from owners unable to fund/finish hotels on time
items.quote: Where I see possible slippages is that we have in this pipeline of signed converting to operational, there have been slippages when owners are not being able to fund/finish their hotels on time. So, that is the only concern I have.

items.statement: Franchise growth requires strict quality control to protect brand; net promoter score tracked frequently
items.quote: But when we grow through franchise route this will be the single most important thing, we keep an eye on . P lease rest assured it will be a number one priority of the management to ensure that growth does not come at the cost of the

items.statement: Unexecuted order book is INR280 crores and total order book is around INR557 crores
items.quote: Unexecuted order book is INR280 crores and total order book is around INR557 crores.

items.statement: Management plans to double the order book in coming months with spillover in March FY25 and FY26
items.quote: So definitely, we plan to double this order book in the coming months. It's in due to elections this year, lot of orders were delayed. But now there will be a good spillover in March FY '25, as well as for the FY '26.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 revenue was INR22.56 crores, down sequentially from Q2 due to election delays
items.quote: In Q3 FY '25, Dhruv Consultancy has recorded a total revenue of INR22.56 crores

items.statement: 9M FY25 revenue grew 31.5% YoY to INR75.49 crores
items.quote: For 9 months FY '25, the company delivered strong reporting total revenue of INR75.49 crores, a 31.5% year-over-year increase.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin was 20% at INR4.47 crores, PAT margin 9.52% at INR2.15 crores
items.quote: In Q3 FY '25, Dhruv Consultancy has recorded a total revenue of INR22.56 crores with EBITDA rising to INR4.47 crores, reflecting a healthy EBITDA margin of 20%.

items.statement: 9M FY25 EBITDA margin improved to 14.89% at INR11.24 crores, PAT margin 6.5% at INR4.91 crores
items.quote: EBITDA reached INR11.24 crores, with an improved EBITDA margin of 14.89%. Profit after tax stood at INR4.91 crores, maintaining a PAT margin of 6.5%
