items.quote: And hence, the initial mobilization expenses, as has been the trend before is slightly on a higher side. But going ahead, these projects are with good profit as usual. And going ahead, it will help us improve our EBITDA margins also.

items.statement: March FY25 looks quite good with stable governments; significant increase expected from FY24 but no specific numbers disclosed
items.quote: March '25 looks to be quite good with now new stable governments coming in the state, as well as center. So March '25 looks quite good for us.

items.statement: Not allowed to disclose specific top-line or bottom-line growth numbers for next 2-3 years
items.quote: We are actually not allowed to disclose any numbers as such. But as I've already mentioned that we expect a significant increase in March itself.

items.statement: Preferential proceeds used to purchase second falling weight deflectometer and second mobile bridge inspection unit
items.quote: our preferential money proceeds have been used to purchase two major equipment. One is the falling weight deflectometer which is the second one now and a mobile bridge inspection unit is also a second one.

items.statement: Reducing dependency on government sector; awarded projects from private clients HCC, GR Infra, Chinmaya Vibhooti Mission in Q3 FY25
items.quote: If you can see in the quarter 3 FY '25, we have been awarded with quite a few major projects from HCC, GR Infra, Chinmaya Vibhooti Mission. So we -- our dependency on the government sector is slowly, slowly reducing, which is a very big positive impact.

items.statement: Targeting larger ticket projects of INR20 crores+ domestically, up from INR5-6 crores previously
items.quote: We are widening our client base in India to larger ticket sized projects, say minimum INR20 crores now and more such orders we are expecting in the future. So same order which we were getting for INR5 crores, now we are getting for INR20 crores.

items.statement: Present in 25 of 29 Indian states; focus now on international expansion to sub-Saharan Africa, Southeast Asia, South Asia, Gulf, and outsourcing from developed economies
items.quote: So out-of-the 29 states that are there in India, we are already working in 25 states barring a few that is Tripura and Jammu and Kashmir. So small, small states in the Far East that are there, Nagaland. So, these are the states that are still there. And as far as India is concerned, I would say that we have already expanded our base from North to South and East to West. Now our focus is on the int

items.statement: International pipeline includes projects in Tanzania, Ghana, Zambia, and a single INR200 crores project in Philippines; FY25-26 expected to be dominated by international market
items.quote: We have a few projects in pipeline in the international market. One is in Tanzania, Ghana, then in Zambia and there is a major project coming up in Philippines, which itself is a single INR200 crores project. So, FY '25 -- FY '25-'26 looks to be dominated by the international market for us

items.statement: First ever general consultancy contract and largest railway project (INR11.05 crores, 24 months) for Garkhal Bridge in Himachal Pradesh
items.quote: We have received a notice to proceed for consultancy services on the Garkhal Bridge project in Himachal Pradesh, where we will observe the construction of cantilever bridge. The contract value is INR11.05 crores, which will be executed over a period of 24 months. This engagement represents company's first ever general consultancy contract and its largest project in our railway sector to date.

items.statement: Strategic focus on replicating highway success in 5-6 new sectors: railways, metros, airports, public health engineering, energy and power
items.quote: Secondly, we plan to replicate this success story in other sectors of infrastructure. So the national implementation plan says that infrastructure has 22 sectors. So we are going to identify five or -- we have identified five or six sectors, namely the railways, metros, airports, public health engineering, energy and power.

items.statement: Among top 3-4 highway consultants in India; now eligible for any large-sized ticket projects on own eligibility without JVs
items.quote: the company in the highway sector, especially now that the company is among the top three, four consultants in India in the highway sector, we can now qualify for any large sized ticket projects on our own eligibility.

items.statement: JV/association extent minimal (5-10% share) and only for industry relations or special expertise; Dhruv solely eligible for most projects
items.quote: There is an association that is there. So the associate is hardly 5% or 10% of -- 5% or 10% of share is what they have. It is just to maintain good relations in the industry with your competitors. Otherwise, Dhruv is solely eligible to qualify for projects on their own -- on our own.

items.statement: Declared interim dividend of INR0.1 per share
items.quote: We are pleased to announce our interim dividend of INR0.1 per share, reflecting our commitment to delivering shareholder value.

items.statement: Non-fund-based requirements (bank guarantees) needed for new projects; in talks with existing bankers who are happy to assist
items.quote: And secondly, the fund requirement, yes, there will be a fund requirement -- there will be a non-fund-based requirement. As and when we are being received projects, bank guarantees would be required and our banks -- we are in talks with our bankers, our present bankers, who are happy to assist us for the same.

items.statement: Manpower hiring on contract basis for supervision assignments; corporate office has 100+ employees; ESOPs and international opportunities give talent edge; AI being explored to reduce human dependency
items.quote: Our HR and our recruitment team is well capable of doing that. And people are actually preferring coming to our company since in our domain, we are the only listed company. We are giving ESOPs to our employees. So, we have an edge over our competitors when it comes to talent acquisition.

items.statement: Site manpower automatically demobilized after project completion; no net increase in permanent headcount
items.quote: And once the project is -- once the project is completed, that manpower, which is deployed on the site is automatically demobilized and their services are concluded. So, net of net, there is no increase in the manpower on the site.

items.statement: State and central elections (code of conduct) delayed order finalization in Q3; orders pushed to Q4 FY25
items.quote: The major reason for a dip in the quarter-to-quarter revenue was the elections that were there in the state. So we were expecting a few orders in the Q3 FY '25, which will now be pushed to the Q4 FY '25.

items.statement: Union budget provisions show increased investment in railways, metros, ports, airports, energy and power beyond highways
items.quote: And the budget provisions being made by the central government are very higher as compared to previous years for these sectors also. Of course, highways would remain our core dominant sector

items.statement: First international project in Mozambique; team established in Africa; opportunities in government and private sectors across roads and railways
items.quote: Mozambique, we have already established ourselves and our team is right now sitting in Africa, where not just in the government sector, but there are lot of opportunities in the private sector also in the international market, in roads as well as in railway sector.

items.statement: International tenders require local manpower hiring; forming JVs/associations with local partners for liaisoning and political scenarios
items.quote: what the international tender says that you need to have -- you need to hire local manpower as well when it comes to providing manpower at the site. So, we give a combination of international and local -- local manpower. So, for this, we form a JV or an association with local partners there.

items.statement: Order inflow: secured LOA for authority engineer from MSIDC worth INR23.46 crores (11 packages); NHAI and MoRTH contracts in Karnataka; U.P. Bridge Corporation empanelment extension; Assam Road and Rural Bridge Project shortlist (1,184 brid
items.quote: We were recently awarded with an LOA for authority engineer in association with Maps Global Tech with a total contract value of INR23.46 crores from Maharashtra State Industrial Development Corporation.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 revenue growth guidance ~13% and EBITDA margin 25%+
items.quote: We remain on track to achieve our guidance of approximately 13% revenue growth in Q4 and EBITDA margins in the range of 25% plus for Q4 '25 and going forward, reaffirming the strength of our strategy and execution.

items.statement: Core Diagnostics acquisition closing by February end; revenue contribution from March; margin dilution for 2-3 years but EPS accretive year 1
items.quote: We aim to finalize the acquisition by the end of this month with Core expected to c ontribute to MHL's revenue starting in March of this financial year. Once Core is fully integrated into Metropolis systems and processes, we anticipate a fair number of operational efficiencies with synergies driving an expansion in margin profile of Core from Q1 FY '26 itself

items.statement: Actively pursuing bolt-on acquisitions in North India; targets are city-leading B2C labs with high EBITDA, ROCE, OCF/EBITDA
items.quote: We are in advanced stages of evaluating a few such acquisitions that have successfully built strong B2C brands in North Indian cities. These align well with our goal of expanding our footprint in the region through acquisitions focused on creating a string of pearls that enhance our presence and capability.

items.statement: Organic margin expansion expected as lab expansion slows; Core acquisition dilutes group margin for 2-3 years
items.quote: On an organic basis, I think you will get a better margin expansion going forward. And also, we will also be adding more acquisitions, some of which could be coming at a much better EBITDA level.

items.statement: Micro-marketing pricing adjustments net +2% revenue uplift from Q4; market-specific not product-specific
items.quote: The net results of this would be upside of about 2%, which is coming in from this quarter. So we did market-specific pricing, not necessarily product specific across the board. So only a few markets, prices have gone up, and a few markets, we corrected the prices downwards. The net impact, like I said, is about 2%.

items.statement: Collection center to lab ratio ~22x; target 30x in 2 years as lab additions slow and center additions accelerate
items.quote: Maybe at the end of 2 years from now, this could be 30 collection centers for a lab. So that's actually the endeavor. That's the plan that we have in mind.

items.statement: Working capital cycle 13 days as of Dec 31, 2024; net cash surplus INR 205 cr
items.quote: We have a net cash surplus of INR 205 crores as of 31st of December 2024. We also have a working capital cycle of 13 days.

items.statement: Core acquisition funded by ~INR 135 cr internal cash plus stock swap
items.quote: We will be using approximately INR 135 crores of internal cash for this acquisition, and the balance will be a stock swap.

items.statement: New CFO Sameer Patel joining Feb 10; background Deloitte audit and 8 years as CFO at large listed QSR chain
items.quote: Our new CFO, Sameer Patel, will be joining February 10, as already announced. His background is audit services at Deloitte and then business and finance roles in retail chains. His last role being 8 years at a large public listed QSR chain, where he has been CFO for many of those 8 years.

items.statement: Online players grew at industry pace post-COVID, not taking share from incumbents; no new entrants since 2022; Metropolis fastest-growing in Mumbai/Maharashtra
items.quote: So I think that pace of taking business from unorganized players has significantly come down for the o nline guys, because we saw that pace really grow during COVID, but not really sustained post. And really, the market has gone back to where the online players are growing actually at the same pace now as the rest of the industry and not significantly faste r. And obviously, they still continue to

items.statement: Institutional/PPP business defocused; selective participation only where margins and receivables are smooth; no new contracts expected in next 6-8 months
items.quote: We have been very selective in this segment, places where we can really make enough margin and the whole receivable process is relatively smooth. That's only kind of PPP that we are getting into. Very selectively we are doing it. And we are not actively considering any new contracts as we speak, which can translate into revenue in the next 6 months to 8 months' time.

items.statement: Dollar depreciation pressure on reagent costs; offset by efficiencies and productivity; no immediate cost escalation expected
items.quote: we definitely have some impact of the dollar. There's no doubt about it. But we, at the same time, start figuring out how better negotiation and better efficiencies can chip in. So as a result, largely, we try to kind of t ake care of the increased pressure because of dollar through our efficiencies and our productivity, et cetera. So I'm not expecting an immediate escalation on the cost because o

items.quote: So we should definitely get into aro und 8% to 10% upside in the next 2 to 3 years' time on the B2C segment

items.statement: B2B partner portal launched for real-time tracking, transparency, workflow efficiency; B2B revenue +10% YoY
items.quote: As a part of this effort, we have launched a dedicated partner portal, which pr ovides a comprehensive, transparent and efficient digital platform for our B2B partners. This portal enables real-time sample tracking, offering end -to-end visibility across the diagnostic process, along with improving communication and streamlining workflows

items.statement: Mumbai: 7 labs, ~500 collection centers; adding 30-50 centers/year for next couple years; no new labs needed
items.quote: I mean labs, of course, we don't require additional labs in Mumbai. We have 7 labs in Mumbai, and that is good enough to ser ve the geographies of Mumbai. And I think that trajectory should continue maybe in the next couple of years as well

items.statement: Aim to close FY25 with EBITDA margins in guided 20-22% range; nine-month EBITDA at 22.1% ahead of guidance
items.quote: We aim to close the year with margins to be in our guided range of 20% to 22%. For the nine-month period, we are ahead of those guidance number.

items.quote: EBITDA, including other income came in at about ₹117 crores, which is 21.1% of our total income compared to 21.7% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Wage hike impact on Q3 margins ~0.9% for senior profiles; GenAI investments $3.5M for nine months; net new sales engine also pressuring margins

items.quote: Apart from the projects we have already delivered in these few months, we have about fifteen projects in a proof-of-concept(PoC) stage, which will lead to significant orders and projects in the next fiscal.

items.quote: If you notice the BFSI segment was the best performing segment for us last quarter. I would attribute a big part of that to the Arttha banking platform because we were able to close two deals, finish the implementation and the recognition of those revenues is what has led to quite a bit of the growth that we see in the BFSI vertical.

items.statement: US financial services thriving with robust economy, stable inflation, buoyant job market; Healthcare/Life Sciences growing rapidly; Retail/CPG discretionary pressures easing; EduTech softness in higher education
items.quote: The financial services sector in the U.S. is thriving bolstered by a robust economy, stable inflation and a buoyant job market. items.quote: The bill rates on GenAI services is superior to even our traditional, but our PDES, Analytics, and related Digital services.

items.statement: Arttha banking platform license revenue recognized on closing; implementation revenue over time; Q4 expected stronger for Arttha closures; GAVS Middle East acquisition opens new geographies for Arttha
items.quote: We are looking at a much better Q4 from Arttha banking as far as revenue closures are concerned. License has got two elements. items.statement: 85 $1B+ revenue customers contribute 47% of revenue (was 60 same time last year); 7 new logos in Q3 across geos/verticals; net new sales team built pipeline with 1 closure and 2 advanced prospects
items.quote: We have eighty five billion $ corporations that are customers with more than US $1 billion in annual revenues who contribute to 47% of our overall revenues. To put things in perspective, this count of US $1 billion customers was sixty same time last year.

items.statement: Net new sales team (hunters) separated from farmers/client partners; Chief Growth Officer onboarded August; team in place Nov-Dec; 7 new logos in Q3; momentum expected in Q4 and FY26
items.quote: We had seven new logos cutting across various geos and verticals last quarter, and we expect this momentum to continue into Q4 and into FY 26.

items.statement: Signed agreement Feb 2 to acquire GAVS Technologies Middle East business (90+ people, 2 BFSI customers); completion in few days; incremental revenue from Q4; Middle East to become significant contributor over next year
items.quote: Finally, I'm happy to share that on 2nd February, we signed agreement to acquire the Middle East business of GAVS Technologies Limited. items.statement: PureSoftware and Aureus acquisitions successfully integrated under One Happiest Minds; driving efficiencies in sales, delivery, operations; cross-selling wins in BFSI (Aureus) and IMSS (PureSoftware)
items.quote: PureSoftware and Aureus, companies we acquired in the past year have been successfully integrated under One Happiest Minds, and we are together driving efficiencies in sales, delivery and more importantly, operations.

items.statement: Cash and equivalents ₹1,495 crores; cash conversion 97.5% of EBITDA; DSO stable at ~84 days; RoCE 21.8%, RoE 14% annualized
items.quote: We reported a healthy cash and cash equivalent balances of about ₹1,495 crores with a continued strong conversion ratio of 97.5% of EBITDA. Our Day Sales Outstanding (DSO) continues to be stable at about 84 days.

items.statement: Cash EPS ₹6.16 in Q3 (12.6% YoY growth); annualized Cash EPS ₹24.6 vs ₹22.93 previous year
items.quote: Our cash EPS for the quarter was ₹6.16, showing a good year-over-year growth of 12.6%. Annualized Cash EPS stands at about ₹24.6 per share compared to the ₹22.93 in the previous year.

items.statement: GenAI productivity gains (5-10% development contraction) passed to customers in renewals/RFPs; margins maintained as lower cost offsets lower price; Jevons Paradox expected to drive demand
items.quote: On the supply side, the expected contraction at the development stage is between 5% to 10%. In new business, we are beginning to see some bit of that. Using AI automation CoPilot and the similar tools, we should see the benefit. So I'm talking about it from a pricing model.

items.statement: Differentiated GenAI tracking (pure GBS revenue vs competitors counting large projects with small AI component); replicable horizontal solutions (e.g., investor relations bot on Azure Marketplace); verticalized sales with domain experts
items.quote: So that way, by creating GBS as a separate business unit, we wanted to completely focus on the generative AI and the solutions primarily around generative AI. So that way the revenue that goes into the PDES or IMSS is not counted as a generative AI-related project.

items.statement: Cybersecurity a business imperative; helping customers navigate global regulatory convergence; Middle East bank chose risk/governance consulting services
items.quote: Cybersecurity continues to be a business imperative for our customers. Through our comprehensive offerings in this space, we are helping business navigate towards a global regulatory convergence. items.statement: Medium-term organic revenue CAGR 13-15%; Cash Logistics 10-13%, MS & Tech 15%+, AIoT RMS 15-20%

items.quote: We had completed 15% of this order book at end of H1, have ramped it up with 30% completion at the end of Q3 and our focus remains on getting 60% of this order book live by Q4. The impact from this itself is to the tune of INR 150 crores lower revenue in FY '25.

items.statement: MS & Tech order wins over INR 700 cr this year, majority recurring services revenue

items.quote: Historically, our card margins was over 20%. However, in last 6 to 9 months, or in 1 year, that rates have settled and because of that, now the margins have improved up to the normal level.

items.statement: Capex INR 50 cr in 9M FY25; full year guidance INR 150-200 cr, mostly for MS order execution
items.quote: Our CAPEX spend has been INR 50 crores in 9 months of the year and we expect this to be INR 150 crores to INR 200 crore for the full year.

items.statement: AIoT RMS business targeting 10% of revenue by FY27 organically (currently 7%)
items.quote: Our overall Software and RMS business is 7 percentage of our overall revenue. So, our goal is to get to the 10% mark by FY '27 on organic basis.

items.quote: The margin profile of any of our AIoT businesses where we choose to work in is reasonably good, and IRRs will range in the 18% to 25% range.

items.quote: And, you know, hopefully we'll end the year at, you know, higher than that, you know, between 16 to 20% is when we should end the year.

items.quote: As it currently stands out, it's an open -ended date given out saying that this is the MDR and this will remain as we keep moving forward because the minimum cost which any company incurs is a bare minimum cost in terms of running the entire issuance stack and that number for different banks and different players is a number where they just break even at that 1% scale because of the kind of market

items.statement: Tolling market share reached close to 43% by December.
items.quote: By December, and we already reached close to what 43%.

items.statement: Employee cost reduction included one-time leave encashment and gratuity reversals of INR1.5 crores to INR1.7 crores.
items.quote: I think the third point, just a one time, is that in December, some of our leave lapses, etc. happen. So, there are some reversals in leave encashment and gratuity. So, that is to the extent of INR1.5 crores to INR1.7 crores.

items.statement: Company continues to move towards variabilization of workforce.
items.quote: So, Gaurav, I think two things. One, as you have consistently said, we continue to move more towards the variabilization of the workforce , so that you would see that the other expenses has gone up.

items.statement: Expects current growth to continue in new segments.
items.quote: See, I can't like, I mean, we as we discussed last call, like we as a philosophy have taken not to provide guidance, b ut yes you can continue to expect the current growth coming through.

items.statement: Fuel vertical positioned for 20-25% YoY growth.
items.quote: we have been able to comfortably position a growth rate of 20%, 25% year-on-year in that vertical.

items.statement: Classified revenue projected max INR200 crores in 5-6 years.
items.quote: And the revenue projection of that vertical probably will be max INR200 crores in probably 5 -6 years down the line on an annualized revenue basis.

items.statement: Vehicle finance origination doubling every six months.
items.quote: That's a business vertical, which is growing, probably every six months it's doubling .

items.statement: Expects better disbursements as partners' measured approach eases.
items.quote: As we see into this quarter that measure d approach slowly is going away. So, we expect to see better disbursements, b ut yes Q3 was definitely measured by our partners.

items.statement: Brokerage business needs 6-8 quarters for understanding.
items.quote: But by when and how much, I think we need to wait for at least six to eight quarters to get some understanding in that business.

items.statement: Fuel sensor at INR10-11k profitable on first sale.
items.quote: Yes, at between INR10 to INR11,000, we will be in money in the first sale.

items.statement: May reduce fuel sensor price further at higher scale.
items.quote: Yes, I mean, because right now, we are only talking numbers like mere thousands. And as soon as we hit 10,000s, right, we can definitely get more.

items.statement: Customer acquisition cost per vertical INR1300-1400 per truck.
items.quote: Like, the cost of acquisition of a customer on any one of the verticals for at a truck level, typically hovers in the range of like, INR1300, INR1400, like kind of number, right?

items.statement: Telematics growth trending as before.
items.quote: I think at this point in time, what you can infer is that broadly the growth is trending, how it was trending before in terms of telematics devices. Broadly, we are in the same course.

items.statement: Renewal rates early 70s first year, early 80s to late 80s thereafter.
items.quote: We typically have that the first year annual rate typically is roughly in the range of like early 70s in terms of annual rate. After that, typically, the renewal rates are in the early 80s to late 80s on a continual basis.

items.statement: Fuel sensor revenue model: upfront first year, then annual subscription.
items.quote: Yes, it's again – yes, it's the same model we charge upfront for the first year because that includes the device cost. And after that it's annual recurring subscription which again comes for annual and it's an annuity income again, nature of revenue again will be similar as the GPS revenue.

items.statement: Fuel vertical faces headwinds from OMC structure and cash usage.
items.quote: So Indian market structure, why is it different from those markets is that point number one, we have a oil marketing company structure, where there are largely four oil marketing companies, there's only one private and three government owned, right? So the real intensity to fight, for customers in terms of loyalty, etc., isn't that high, that's point number one.

items.statement: No material update on GNSS; backend work ongoing.
items.quote: So back end work is the toll charge of work, which will calculate the distance, which will map the toll plazas, do the lat longs, and like, send on a real time basis really how much money to be deducted, etc. So that work is on a priority happening , but materially, we don't have any updates on that.

items.statement: IMACID expansion capex is $173 million
items.quote: Abhay Baijal: $173 million.

items.statement: Total capex incurred in 9 months is Rs 357 crore, of which TAN is Rs 250 crore
items.quote: Anand Agarwal: Current year, we have actually invested around Rs. 357 crore of CAPEX, out of which, TAN is around Rs. 250 crore.

items.statement: TAN project commercial production date is January 26; positive contribution expected in FY27
items.quote: Abhay Baijal: Yes, I will just make this point . January 26 is the date of commercial production delivery. That means it meets all parameters in terms of capacity , in terms of efficiency, in terms of quality. The trial will begin before January 26.

items.statement: 3% energy efficiency saving from Rs 5,000 per Gcal translates to EBITDA gain
items.quote: Abhay Baijal: See, I will just give you , this is a rough computation. 3% saving from Rs. 5,000 per Gcal.

items.statement: Q3 production volumes: Gadepan-I 2.96 lakh tons, Gadepan-II 2.67 lakh tons, Gadepan-III 3.55 lakh tons, total 9.18 lakh tons
items.quote: Anuj Jain: Gadepan-I, in the quarter, we had production of 2.96 lakh tons and Gadepan-Il 2.67 lakh tons, and Gadepan Ill 3.55 lakh tons. So, total put together we had production of 9.18 lakh tons.

items.statement: Gas cost for Q3 is about $15.85 per MMBTU on NCV basis
items.quote: Anuj Jain: Gas cost for Q3 is about $15.85 per MMBTU on NCV basis.

items.statement: No equity investment required for IMACID expansion; JV has enough cash
items.quote: Abhay Baijal: We don't have to invest. They have got enough cash.

items.statement: Dividend from IMACID may go up or down; may be reinvested tactically
items.quote: Abhay Baijal: Dividend will go up and down . We may take dividend and then reinvest back into them. That's up to us what we want to do. That's a tactical decision from time to time.

items.statement: Actively discussing phosphate supply chain investments in phosphate-rich countries; will lead to international investments
items.quote: Let me also tell you that Chambal is quite serious in looking at ensuring Phosphate supply or securing Phosphate supply chains in Phosphate rich countries. So, there are discussions which are on, we will inform you from time to time as to what we are and what our progress in that matter is

items.statement: Q4 urea volume run rate estimated at 1-1.5 lakh tons below normal due to Gadepan-III turnaround and short shutdowns
items.quote: So, I would only hazard a guess. Assuming that the plants run full capacity, if you minus the amount of 3,900 tons per day for Gadepan-III for about 30 days, that's the amount of minus that you will get. But there are one or two nibbling problems in Gadepan-I and II, very short shutdowns will be taken. So, I would guess between 1 lakh to 1.5 lakhs tons

items.statement: Net cash position of Rs 3,000 crore at end of Q3; no debt
items.quote: Abhay Baijal: There is no debt. Cash is high. Rs. 3,000 crore.

items.statement: CPC-SN revenue split approximately 65:35 or 70:30 depending on quarter
items.quote: Abhay Baijal: I think it is, if I am not wrong, either 65:35 or 70:30, depending on which quarter we sell what.

items.statement: IMACID expansion adds 2 lakh metric tons; 70-75% comes to India, balance to OCP for global supply
items.quote: Abhay Baijal: We already manufacture 5 lakh tons in IMACID. 70% to 75% of that material comes to India. Balance 20%-25%, 30%, depending on supply circumstances is transferred to OCP sometimes, which they use for their global supply. In this, additional 2 lakh metric tons, we have to see how we can find the markets to absorb these quantities, either in India or abroad.

items.statement: Energy efficiency gains and incremental production add to EBITDA but subject to gain-sharing formula beyond RAC
items.quote: Abhay Baijal: Yes, they add to the EBITDA, but you made an important point as to whether some gain sharing takes place. Yes, there is a gain sharing formula. And on the additional production that we do, it goes beyond the RAC.

items.statement: Surplus ammonia sales of 80,000-81,000 tons in nine months with reasonable four-digit profits
items.quote: Abhay Baijal: Profits, see, this year have been a little soft. I would say we have done I think about 80,000 - 81,000 tons of sales till now. I think a reasonable four-digit profits are there.

items.statement: Tied up hybrid wheat, millet, maize, mustard seeds for new seeds focus area
items.quote: Abhay Baijal: I just mentioned that we have tied up, in terms of hybrid wheat, in terms of millet, in terms of maize, in terms of mustard.

items.statement: NPK sales start from Q1 next year for Kharif; quantities tied up and adequately stocked
items.quote: Abhay Baijal: Q4 FY‘25 normally is not a quarter for sales of NPK. Its sales will start basically from first quarter of next year, which is when the Kharif really kicks in. So, it's not really a quarter where we will have high sales. But coming back to what you said about NPK, let me tell you that we have tied up some quantities for the Kharif in the NPK side, and we are adequately stocked for it

items.statement: TAN project includes provision for LDAN equipment alongside HDAN to avoid future long shutdowns
items.quote: Baijal: Let me just clarify to you. We have made a provision to install L DAN equipment alongside the original configuration. Because, if we had not done that, then we would have to take a very long shutdown sometime in the future or to shut the plant for four months, six months, ten months, in order to incorporate those things

items.statement: Crop protection FY27 revenue target of Rs 1,750 crore is on gross basis; net basis would be ~20% lower at 20-22% margin
items.quote: Anand Agarwal: The FY-27 number which we had told, was a gross number. And what we have to put up in our accounts is a net number, and that is the difference. So, it will be somewhere around 20- 22%.

items.statement: Crop protection business continues to grow at current rates; targeting 3-4 new product launches annually and widening channel
items.quote: Abhay Baijal: We continue to grow at the rates that we have been doing. In fact, try ing to better it. That's my brief to the team. Therefore, if you recall, in my opening statement we said that we are now starting to get Gen 1x molecules and we are creating strong alliances with companies which have got research base. And therefore, we are introducing those new products and therefore expanding th

items.statement: TAN plant breakeven at 80-85% utilization; target is 100%+ operation
items.quote: As far as the IRR is concerned, it is computed on a conservative basis. And that, I would say, they have got a certain breakeven number. I would not tell you what th e breakeven is, but we will be above breakeven even at 80- 85

items.statement: Capital allocation focus on global phosphate supply chain, seeds re-entry, biologicals targeting Rs 300-400 crore sales by FY28-29, and specialty nutrients
items.quote: Abhay Baijal: I think I just made a mention of global phosphate supply chain somewhere. I think that will be one of the breakthroughs that if I could do, or the Company could do during this time, that will create a very strong base for Chambal to be a global phosphate player. And that is one area we are definitely looking into. Seeds is another area we are looking into. There, we will start with r

items.statement: India sugar production expected at 26.5-27 million tons for SY2024-25; higher production expected for SY2025-26
items.quote: So, Rohit, to answer your first thing that the sugar production that we are seeing for the year '24-'25, it will be in the range of 26.5 million to 27 million ton, is what we are seeing India to do for this year.

items.statement: Government allocated export quota of 10,256 tons; company plans to sell quota to mills near ports rather than export directly
items.quote: Government has allowed exports of 1 million tons of sugar. The company has been allocated export quota of 10,256 tons with the flexibility to either directly export sugar or exchange it with another sugar mill for domestic quota.

items.statement: Ethanol price from C-heavy molasses increased by INR1.69/liter; no increase for syrup and B-heavy molasses-based ethanol
items.quote: On ethanol front, the government has increased price of ethanol derived from C-heavy molasses by INR1.69 per liter. There's no increase in price for syrup and B-heavy molasses-based ethanol.

items.statement: Ethanol production mix for FY25: ~30% syrup, ~40% B-heavy, ~30% grain (maize); switched from syrup to B-heavy on Jan 28 due to no price increase for syrup
items.quote: I think I would say that as of now, because till January 28, we ran on syrup. So till January 28, almost a third went to syrup. The next would be about, I would say so if I was to do the mix, I would say 30% is syrup, 40% will be B-heavy, 30% would be grain.

items.statement: Molasses transfer prices: C-heavy at INR850, B-heavy at INR1,200
items.quote: The C-heavy, we are doing at INR850 and B-heavy is INR1,200.

items.statement: Sugar realization improved to ~INR41 ex-mill from INR37.5-38 earlier
items.quote: So earlier, we were selling at about INR37.5, INR38. Right now, the price is around INR41 ex-mill.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA INR48.1 cr vs INR69.5 cr YoY; PBT INR21.5 cr vs INR47.5 cr; PAT INR15 cr vs INR31.6 cr; lower due to ~50% drop in ethanol sales volume
items.quote: Consequence mainly to lower ethanol sales, EBITDA in this quarter is at INR48.1 crores versus INR69.5 crores. PBT is INR21.5 crores versus INR47.5 crores. Profit after tax is INR15 crores versus INR31.6 crores.

items.statement: Gross recovery Q3 FY25 at 10.17% vs 11.01% YoY due to red rot and agro-climatic factors; plant cane recovery now near last year levels
items.quote: The gross recovery in this quarter is lower at 10.17% versus 11.01% in the corresponding quarter last year. This is mainly due to red rot as also various agro-climatic factors.

items.statement: Cane crush Q3 FY25: 11.33 lakh tons vs higher last year due to 9-day later season start (Nov 7 vs Oct 30); full season crush expected similar to last year
items.quote: As you are aware that both our plants started crushing with effect from November 7, 2024, and during the quarter, we have crushed 11.33 lakh tons of cane. This is lower than last year same quarter, since last year both the plants started on October 30, 2023.

items.statement: Varietal shift plan underway for 2 years to combat red rot; seed availability secured; Dhampur: 75% Co 0238, 25% other varieties next season; Rajpura: 65% Co 0238, 35% others
items.quote: So if I talk about both the plants individually, in Dhampur, we are hoping that 75 will still stay in 238, 25 will go to others, 118 and everything else. Rajpura, it will be about 65 will go to 238 and 35 will be for other seeds.

items.statement: Recovery outlook: Dhampur down ~0.7%, Rajpura down ~0.3-0.4% for full season vs last year; plant cane pol now equal to last year
items.quote: So we are hoping, in Dhampur, we will have a lower by about 0.7., Rajpura to be lower by about 0.3 to 0.4.

items.statement: Buyback or dividend options open; decision after March 2025 based on final financials; buyback done ~2 years ago at ~INR300
items.quote: We will have to examine it after March is out exactly as to how much we would like to do vis-a-vis dividend or buyback. So both options are open as of now.

items.statement: No expansion plans for 2025; all plants fully set
items.quote: No plans at all. All our plants are all set. We are fully set on all our sites. So there is no expansion plan for the year 2025.

items.statement: All forex exposure fully hedged per company policy; no currency risk
items.quote: As we all know, during the quarter, U.S. dollar has moved significantly. However, as per the company's forex policy, all the exposure is fully hedged. Therefore, we do not run any risk on this account.

items.statement: Government balancing sugar and ethanol prices to ensure cane price payment; E20 blending target progressing; syrup/B-heavy ethanol prices not raised for ESY2024-25 due to cane availability concerns
items.quote: I think that government is also playing a very key role and a very smart role in this that they are trying to balance out, that whenever the seed and sugar prices are starting to drop, they will make the price higher or the other way around.

items.statement: Red rot in cane continues to impact North India; varietal shift is 2-year process; cyclicality reduced due to product flexibility (syrup, B-heavy, C-heavy, grain)
items.quote: Now 30 years back, so I'll start the story from then when we all joined, cyclicality was a reality in sugar, because we didn't have any other products which we could use for sugarcane. But now with this syrup, B-heavy and C, that has changed a lot.

items.statement: 9M FY25 consolidated EBITDA INR84.8 cr vs INR192.7 cr YoY; PBT INR3.9 cr vs INR123.3 cr; PAT INR3.4 cr vs INR82.7 cr; cash profit INR46.4 cr vs INR144.3 cr
items.quote: During the period ended December '24, consolidated revenue from operations stands at INR1,846.1 crores. It was INR1,979 crores in the previous year in the comparable period. EBITDA is INR84.8 crores, which was INR192.7 crores.

items.statement: Management expects double-digit revenue growth for next fiscal year (FY26)
items.quote: Looking at our first nine months performance and looking at how this quarter has started, we believe that will be a repeat next year, a double-digit revenue growth for next year.

items.statement: ICE EBITDA margin was 16% in Q3 FY25; overall EBITDA margin improved 50 bps YoY to 14.5% after EV investments of ₹137 cr
items.quote: The EBITDA margins during the quarter for ICE business stood at 16%, driven by mix improvement, lower material cost and LEAP savings, while we continue to invest behind brand building and new businesses. During the quarter, after taking into account the investments behind EV business, ₹137 crores, the overall EBITDA margin improved by 50 basis to 14.5% year-on-year.

items.statement: Highest-ever quarterly retail of over 2 million units; market share expanded 520 bps QoQ to 32.8% per Vahan
items.quote: As per Vahan, our market share for the quarter expanded by 520 basis point s quarter-on-quarter to 32.8%. We achieved our highest ever retail in the quarter of more than 2 million units

items.statement: Continued investment in premium and EV portfolio, Hero 2.0 and Premia stores, digital and technology; EV investment ₹137 cr in Q3
items.quote: Moving ahead, we will continue our investments behind new products and segments. We remain consistent in our commitment towards investing behind the premium and EV portfolio and improved customer service in store with Hero 2.0 and Premia and online with investments behind digital an d technology

items.statement: Hero 2.0 stores reached almost 700 in under 700 days (>1 store/day); Premia stores crossed 60, targeting 100 soon
items.quote: We have clocked now almost 700 2.0 stores in less than 700 days, at the speed of more than one store a day. Our Premia stores continue, which has crossed 60. It will cross 100 soon.

items.statement: Rural contribution rose ~3% in Q3 during festive season; momentum expected to continue in FY26 aided by government measures
items.quote: In Quarter 3, we did see a big spike in the rural demand. The contribution of rural went up almost by 3%, as we saw in the festive season. We expect the momentum to continue going forward in the next financial year as well.

items.statement: OBD-II Phase B compliance will require marginal price increase of 1-2% across portfolio due to additional hardware
items.quote: As far as the price is concerned, there's going to be a marginal price increase of 1% - 2% because of the additional hardware that would be installed in the products and that would be valid across the industry.

items.statement: RM cost flat QoQ; EV investment lower by 50 bps sequentially due to V1-to-V2 transition reducing dispatches, per-unit investment unchanged
items.value: flat RM, EV invest -50 bps QoQ
items.quote: On a quarter-on-quarter basis, the material cost is almost flat, you are right. In the EV business, I talked about that during the quarter, we made an investment of ₹137 crores, which compared to the previous quarter is lower by 50 basis points.

items.statement: No structural shift from motorcycles to scooters/EVs seen; 100cc contraction is affordability/penetration issue, not preference change
items.quote: Yes, absolutely. There is no structural kind of changes that we are seeing. It's a question of how we as leaders are also coming in, as I have described to you in quite detail.

items.statement: OBD-II Phase B: all Hero models already on FI, so 1-2% price impact; carburetor vehicles cannot comply, must convert to FI
items.quote: We are on track as far as OBD-II Phase-B is concerned. This is slightly different from the earlier one, in the sense that we can manufacture up to the 31st March and thereafter it can be sold also in the market. But OBD-II Phase-B we have to necessarily manufacture from 1st of April.

items.statement: Hero FinCorp loan book ₹55,500 cr (+13% YoY); credit cost up ~150 bps to ~6% due to lower collection efficiency in personal loans; collections improving in Dec-Jan
items.quote: HFCL Q3, the loan book size is ₹55,500 which is an increase of 13% versus last year, right . So, business continues to grow. Yes , during the quarter and for the last two, three quarters, we have seen lower collection efficiency especially in the personal loan categories. As a result of that, the credit cost has moved up b y almost 150 basis

items.statement: CEO transition: Niranjan Gupta steps down 1 May; Vikram Kasbekar (48 yrs auto exp, 20+ yrs at Hero) takes over as CEO; Ranjivjit Singh exits, Ashutosh Varma becomes CBO India Business 1 May
items.quote: Finally, I would like to thank all of you who have given me your trust, support and confi dence over the last eight years and 32 earning calls and Vikram now will be taking over from me from 1st of May and I am sure you will provide same support to him moving forward

items.statement: Interim dividend declared at ₹100 per share
items.quote: I am happy to share that the Company has declared an interim dividend of ₹100 per share.

items.statement: 125cc market share rose from 13% in Q4 FY24 to comfortably above 20% in Q3 FY25; journey to continue
items.quote: 125cc, we have gained remarkably well from a 13% share in Quarter 4 of the last fiscal. We are now comfortably above 20% and the journey will continue on that.

items.statement: NBFC delinquencies rising at bottom of pyramid; no pullback in lending willingness but collections stressed; Hero FinCorp focusing on collections and credit underwriting
items.quote: There hasn't been a pullback on the willing ness to lend, but certainly in terms of the collections, I think most of the NBFCs who serve the bottom of the pyramid in some parts of it are having a little bit of uptick on the delinquencies

items.statement: EV transition V1-to-V2 caused lower dispatches in Q3; channel now full of V2, daily sales throughput back to normal; market share recovery expected by end-Feb/Mar
items.quote: We were going through the transition from V1 to V2 in the last one and a half months and hence you might have seen some lower dispatches. But as we said, the intent is not to lower the investment. We have filled the pipeline in the market and you'll start seeing much better market share starting this month.

items.statement: Targets 7 lakh tons hot metal and 5.7-6 lakh tons saleable pig iron in next 12 months
items.quote: Going forward, we are looking that next 12 months, we should be able to produce hot metal of 7 lakh tons and saleable pig iron should come to about 6 lakh ton or 5,70,000 tons

items.statement: Expects casting volumes of 1.7-1.75 lakh tons in FY26 including Oliver
items.quote: I think it could be maybe about 1,75,000, 1,70,000 kind of numbers. We are yet to finalize the plans, but that's the kind of numbers I look forward for the next year.

items.statement: Targets tube volumes of 2 lakh tons in FY26
items.quote: I definitely look forward to producing and selling 1,50,000 ton next year, and Ahmed nagar contributing anywhere between 40,000 to 45,000. So we can look forward to tube volumes of 2 lakh metric ton next year for the whole year.

items.statement: Plans to add 70-80 MW equivalent renewable capacity in next 1 year
items.quote: I would say that we are looking forward to add another 70 megawatt equivalent in next 1 year time. So about 25 megawatt of wind will mean 50 megawatt of solar plus 30 megawatt of solar, about another 70 to 80 megawatt equivalent in the next 1-year time.

items.statement: Expects INR500-600 crore capex in FY26 including INR200 crore for renewable energy
items.quote: I expect in the range of INR500 crores to INR600 crores would be the capex, out of which INR200 crores would be the renewable energy.

items.statement: Operating 69 MW of 70 MW solar plant; Bharat Mines operational and consuming iron ore
items.quote: We have commissioned the solar power plant, Phase I and Phase II are now in place. We are operating close to 69 megawatt out of the 70-megawatt power plant. And as I mentioned, Bharat Mines operations are on, and we are moving the iron ore and have started consuming the iron ore.

items.statement: Baramati tube capacity enhanced to 12,500 tons/month from 10,000 tons/month
items.quote: we have enhan ced the Baramati manufacturing capacity and the plant has come to the level of manufacturing 12,500 metric ton per month from the level of 10,000 metric ton per month

items.statement: Oliver trial production started; expects ramp-up from Feb-Mar and volumes from Q1 FY26
items.quote: We have started trial production and sample supplies from Oliver and we expect that from the month of February and March, we should be able to start ramping up of the production and sales and Oliver should start giving us the volumes from quarter 1 of next financial year.

items.statement: Sees improvement in casting demand from tractor, earthmoving and commercial vehicle sectors from Jan-Feb
items.quote: Over to the next quarter, we are seeing some improvement in almost all the sectors from January, February onwards, better demand forecast from the casting, from the tractor industry as well as earthmoving equipment and commercial ve hicle also, schedules are better compared to the last 2 quarters

items.statement: Commercial vehicle customer volumes grew 30-40% from 7,000-8,000 to 10,000 vehicles/month
items.quote: The customers from 7,000 to 8,000 vehicles per month have moved to 10,000 vehicles per month. It is something like 30% to 40% growth on commercial vehicles with one customer.

items.statement: Pig iron and steel margins under pressure due to high input costs and bottomed-out pig iron prices
items.quote: The major pressure is on the pig iron and steel margins because of the increased input costs and almost bottoming down to lowest possible prices on pig iron across the regions.

items.statement: Expects benefit from reduced coking coal prices (3-month lag) and own iron ore consumption
items.quote: We expect to get some benefit of reduced cost coming on account of two things. One is because of reduced coking coal prices quarter-on-quarter because of the reducing coking coal prices. Typically, we have 3 months inventory, so we get delayed benefit by 3 months. Also, we have started operating Bharat Mines, and we are gradually increasing the consumption or utilization of our own iron ore.

items.statement: Oxygen enrichment saves ~20 kg coke/ton hot metal (~INR600/ton); targeting additional 10 kg savings
items.quote: So we can s ay that about 20 kg of co -consumption saving benefit we get, which is about INR600 per ton of hot metal. And we're trying to improve the oxygen enrichment utilization so that we can go to maybe 135 kg, 140 kg, another 10 kg co -consumption benefit in both t he grades

items.statement: Blended coal cost $205/t in Q3, $195/t in Q4, expects $177/t next quarter; dollar strengthening offsets benefit
items.period: Q3 FY25, Q4 FY25, Q1 FY26
items.quote: Q3 was, I think, $205 blended cost. And this quarter would be blended $195. I expect it to go down to $177 next quarter, blended-- our blended coal cost in dollars. And unfortunately, dollar is also becoming stronger day by day. So again, putting pressure on cost.

items.statement: Targets 2-2.5 lakh tons iron ore consumption in FY26 (25-30% of requirement) from current 1.2 lakh tons
items.quote: Next year, going forward, I look forward to mining and utilizing maybe 2 lakh to 2.5 lakh ton from 1.2 Lakhs ton which becomes, say, 25%, 30% of the total iron ore.

items.statement: Ford order of ~1,000 tons/month (12,000 tons/year) for Solapur; another 1,000-1,200 tons/month in development
items.quote: One big order is from Ford, which has to come to about something like 1,000 ton per month, 12,000 tons per annum. That's one. And also another 1,000 to 1,200 tons per month is in the development stage.

items.statement: Oliver expected to contribute 15,000 tons in FY26; existing lines 1.4-1.5 lakh tons
items.quote: I think I'm looking for 15,000 Oliver and 1,60,000 existing. So 1,40,000 to 1,50,000, 20,000 coming from the existing 4 lines and 15,000 from the Oliver. That comes to 1,75,000.

items.statement: Gaining market share in block and head castings across auto, tractor, earthmoving; Oliver to add housing capacity
items.quote: we are gaining market share in block and head. critical items, auto, tractors, earthmoving, across, we are gaining on the block and head. Maybe we are slightly go ing not that strong and losing something on the housing and focus on block and head. But with the Oliver coming, that 30,000 would be mainly housings. So that's where we want to ensure that we regain the lost capacity, but also go higher

items.statement: 26 casting customers cover all major OEMs; focus on increasing share with 15 smaller customers from 1-3% to 5%
items.quote: Leaving the Top 5, 6 customers, the remaining, at least, 15 customers, our share of business is like 1% to 3%. And that is pretty too low. And opportunity lies with every customer to go to at least 5% business.

items.statement: Fixed corporate costs not expected to increase significantly beyond inflation as current structure supports ₹8,000-10,000 crores sales scale

items.statement: Management expects steady-state working capital of 35-40 days
items.quote: We still feel, Nitin, the working capital range on a steady-state basis, we should consider between 35 to 40 days.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 2.3-2.5% for next year
items.quote: We had been talking about an EBITDA between 2.3% to 2.5%. We still feel that can be the trend as we move into the future.

items.statement: Weighted average tax rate expected to rise to 25-26% from next year due to Global Minimum Tax
items.quote: I think a steady-state range should be between 25% to 26% from next year.

items.statement: Q3 revenue grew 14% YoY to INR 26,764 crores, highest quarterly revenue ever
items.quote: This has been the highest quarter revenue recorded at INR 26,764 crores and the highest quarterly profit ever at INR 400 crores. Our revenues grew at 14% with profit growing at 17% faster than the revenues.

items.statement: Optimistic on Q4 outlook driven by India fiscal year-end spend, deal backlog, Cloud and TSG momentum
items.quote: For Q4, with the fiscal year-end for India for many corporates and government with the budget spend, backlog of deals we have carried over from Q3 as well as momentum in both the Cloud and the Technology Solutions Group, we are optimistic on Q4.

items.statement: Turkey PC market decline moderating; software growing 10-15% of business; mobility flattish
items.quote: The PC business was declining in the high teens in the last 2 quarters. But this quarter, based on the results that we saw, the decline was not as bad. It is still declining. So going forward, we don't see a recovery, but we see the decline in the market opportunity not to be as steep.

items.statement: Saudi Arabia showing nominal growth in Q4 FY25 and Q1 FY26; bullish from April 2025
items.quote: This quarter was a nominal growth. And the coming quarter, Q1, we do expect to see nominal growth as well. But into the new fiscal year, starting April 1, we are bullish on Saudi.

items.statement: CY25 outlook bullish across all verticals: Mobility, TSG, Cloud, and PC refresh in H2
items.quote: CY '25, we definitely see bullishness across all the verticals.

items.statement: Q3 PAT margin 1.5%; gross margin impacted by large deal mix, competition, normalization
items.quote: Overall, PAT percentage was at 1.5%. It has been a continuing story of profitable growth over the quarters with growth coming back strongly.

items.statement: Inventory provision reversal added ~11 bps to gross margin vs normal 6 bps; delta ~17 bps
items.quote: It's about 11 bps reversal. Normally, on average, you will find about 6 bps the positive provision. So, the delta is about 17 bps.

items.statement: Cloud business gross margin 5-7% on resell/consumption, 20%+ on professional services; higher than TSG, PC, Mobility
items.quote: the typical gross margins for resell in the Cloud business is 5% plus. And then when you drive consumption and workloads, specific programs that you bring to the table, you can get on the higher side, maybe 6%, 7%. And when you get into Professional Services, you can make margins 20% plus

items.statement: Q3 working capital improved to 33 days from 36 days; ROCE 27%
items.quote: The business teams and operations did an excellent job of working capital, and we achieved 33-day working capital, an improvement of 3 days. ROCE was at 27%.

items.statement: Turkey Arena net debt reduced from $153M to $137M; aged inventory and overdues reduced; headcount down 15%
items.quote: Net debt end of Q1, we were at about $153 million and end of December, it had come down to $137 million. Also, working capital days had come down. The percentage of aged inventory to the total inventory had come down. The percentage of overdues have come down.

items.statement: Gross debt/equity 0.4x, net debt/equity 0.2x; Paynet divestment to further improve leverage
items.quote: Our gross debt to equity is about 0.4x. Net debt to equity is about 0.2x. That's the way we are geared. And if the Payne t transaction gets consummated whenever it is, that's going to have an added advantage in terms of this debt equity

items.statement: OPEX grew only 1% vs 14% revenue growth; investing in Cloud, TSG, Mobility growth areas
items.quote: OPEX control on spend was very good this quarter. It just grew at 1%, much slower than the revenue growth.

items.statement: Data center equipment and services a key driver of large deals in India and UAE
items.quote: Data center is also clearly a driver, both in India and in UAE. And both these markets, we have participated both directly in the purchase of equipment into t he data centers as well as when the data centers create capacity , and we need take care of that demand through our mid

items.statement: AI-enabled smartphones and PCs expected to drive refresh cycle in next 1-2 years
items.quote: 1 cycle of demand is coming in the next 1 to 2 years, and that will enable people having to change their smartphones and PCs, because the same capability is not available in the previous operating system or the previous chip technology or the platform technology they own

items.statement: Top 20 brands contribute >80% of revenue; next 50 brands ~15%; ~400 brands total
items.quote: The total portfolio is about 400 brands. The top 20 brands contribute to more than 80% of our business. And then the next 50 brands contribute about 15%, and then there are a few hundred brands that contribute to the last 5% of the business.

items.statement: Not losing Apple share in Distribution Addressable Market (DTAM) in India and MEA
items.quote: Within the DTAM, both in India and Middle East Africa, we are not losing share.

items.statement: Paynet divestment: Competition Commission approval obtained; awaiting Central Bank approval
items.quote: With regards to the Paynet divestment from Arena, approvals from Competition Commission have been obtained. We are still awaiting approval from Central Bank.

items.statement: Turkey inflation below 45%, Lira interest rates down to 45%; GDP projected to decline YoY next year
items.quote: Inflation is now down below 45%. The Lira interest rates have been getting revised and now down to 45%.

items.statement: EBITDA at 2.5% in Q3, 2.3% for 9M FY25 (includes other income)
items.quote: This quarter, we had been in the top end of the EBITDA, which is at 2.5%. But if you take for the full 9 months, it is at 2.3%.

items.statement: CEO reappointed for 5 years; Board evaluates on tracked metrics plus ROCE and future strategy
items.quote: There are some standard performance metrics the Board evaluates, the complete leadership team, and accordingly, the CEOs. We do follow the same metrics in this case. I can tell you whatever you track, plus we consider ROCE as an important metric is what we are all the thing weighted on, plus the strategy into the future.

items.statement: March festive season in Middle East and Turkey may cause demand slowness in Q4
items.quote: March being a festive month in many parts of Middle East and Turkey, we could see some slowness in demand in that part of the world.

items.statement: Solar business model shifted to local panels and Redington Solar Franchise (RSFC) under PM rooftop program
items.quote: We have actually created now what is called as the Redington Solar Franchise. It's called the RSFC franchise that we have created. And we are working with EPCs who want to be part of our franchisee model, along with the Prime Minister Program of subsidizing rooftops.

items.quote: 3,300 for gas. That is our target now.

items.quote: And as regards the capex incurred is already about INR23,000 crores until December, out of which about INR 12,000 crores by way of debt financing.

items.quote: It is about INR535 crores for the 9 months, I'm talking about the 9 months. And for the quarter, it is about INR200 crores -- INR210 crores.

items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance maintained at INR 12.75 billion; initial FY26 guidance set at INR 15 billion with upside potential
items.quote: Guidance for this year, FY '25 will continue to be INR 12.75 billion and initial guidance for FY '26 will be INR 15 billion with an upside potential based on the current order inflow rates.

items.statement: Management expects to upgrade FY26 guidance in upcoming quarters and commits to 20% compounded annual growth for FY27
items.quote: We have projected something like a compounded 20% growth. And we will upgrade the performance as and when we see the -- once we come closer to those dates. But right now, we will commit that we can do a definite 20% compounded growth year-on-year.

items.statement: Q3 order inflow INR 4.07 billion, highest ever; 9M order inflow up 40% YoY; 71% exports, 29% domestic
items.quote: The order inflow for the quarter is INR 4.07 billion, highest ever since the inception of the company. Order inflow has increased 52% quarter -to-quarter and 40% in the 9 -month to 9 -month comparison basis. 71% of our quarterly order inflow is exports, while 29% is domestic.

items.quote: Order book of Manufacturing segment is INR 13.09 billion, which consists of INR 9.6 billion manufacturing business and INR 3.33 billion railway business. Sales and aftermarket is INR 0.13 billion and INR 0.03 billion is Turkey business.

items.quote: The gas engine and gas turbine business continues to be driven by demand from CHP, that is combined heat and power plants, AI, server farms and data centers, grid stabilization units and Ukraine. items.statement: Current capacity INR 12.5B; new plant raises to INR 18B; efficiency gains can push to INR 23B; no fourth plant planned before 2028
items.quote: Yes, INR 1,250 crores is the existing capacity, and INR 1,800 crores is the planned capacity. And say, we are expecting something like another 20% output more from the 20%, 25% more approximately from efficiency improvements.

items.quote: I would to put a cap on the EBITDA margin. So I would say factoring something like 17.5% or taking to say between 17% and 18%, I think, would be where we're going to be for this financial year.

items.statement: Euro weakness (1.03-1.04 vs 1.1-1.12 six months ago) affects margins despite hedging; raw material environment stable for FY26
items.quote: We are very heavily exposed to the euro. We have a lot of sales in euros. So currently, the euro is relatively weak against the dollar. It's like at 1.03, 1.04. It was 1.1, 1.12 just 6 months ago.

items.quote: Number one growth is coming from the gas side. Number two, growth coming from the steam turbine side. Number three growth coming from the hydro side. And then, of course, the traction businesses and motor businesses are relatively new businesses for us coming from a small base.

items.statement: Repeat business from prime movers (gas turbine/engine OEMs); not tender-dependent; marquee motor references being built for API-qualified oil/gas, compressor, pump markets

items.quote: Our exports to the U.S. will be something like 8% of our overall turnover. And the products that we are exporting to the U.S. to our OE to the gas turbine manufacturers over there have a 2-year qualification, which is required for any other generator manufacturer to, let's say, replace us in the event that duties do come in.

items.statement: Inventory days 140-159 partly due to steel/copper stocking; targeting reduction via cycle time improvement and supply stability
items.quote: But part of it is due to the large stocking of steel and copper, not due to manufacturing inefficiencies. But we will bring it down even if we are going to stock. So we will look at cycle time reduction, it will come down.

items.statement: Order inflow run-rate INR 4B/quarter (INR 16B annualized) seen as new normal for next several quarters
items.quote: We can certainly say that would be the new normal of the average order inflow for the next few quarters. In some quarters, we could have greater than INR 400 crores. In some quarters, it could be a little bit less.

items.statement: Wind turbine generator segment unlikely to contribute due to unfavorable liability clauses; not banking on it for near-term growth
items.quote: Looking at the nature of the wind business and the nature of the contracts which are over there, it's unlikely that we will make big inroads into this business. So I'm not banking on the wind business for our growth.

items.quote: We have been hiring, we've been training people. I would to put a cap on the EBITDA margin. So I would say factoring something like 17.5% or taking to say between 17% and 18%, I think, would be where we're going to be for this financial year.

items.statement: No fourth plant planned; focus on sweating existing assets via lean manufacturing, automation, cycle time reduction after current expansion completes
items.quote: No, we are not going to be putting a fourth facility. In fact, we have identified huge potential for us to use our existing facilities in a more efficient way using Japanese methods like Kaizen and lean manufacturing, single piece flow.

items.quote: There no progress in terms of new orders. We are actively bidding for new projects in the U.S. and they are under finalization stages. We are in the race. We are in the final list of approved vendors, and we are hoping that we will win.

items.quote: That plant alone will have about slightly less than 300,000 capacity.

items.quote: We are at about 80% plus, but we don't share utilization numbers just because we can augment it very quickly.

items.quote: We are hoping for a similar margin profile, and though it is too early to yet take a call on that.

items.quote: In Q3 FY25, passenger vehicle production volumes registered modest growth of approximately 3% year-on-year, reaching around 11.7 lakh units.

items.quote: The control arm business, we are gaining market share and now we have won another good order here, so first focus is of course to strengthen the control arm and axle assembly business.

items.quote: The dividend policy right now is roughly 10%-30% of that and so that is really a plan going forward.

items.quote: With all our customers, we have a mechanism called indexing, right? So, it is index based on fluctuation.
