items.statement: AP ARPP growth driven by insurance renewal price hikes, case mix change, and Queen's NRI cash/insurance payer mix with minimal scheme work
items.quote: There is a price hike because of insurance renewals. There has been a case mix change. And also, Queen's NRI is largely driven by cash and insurance as a payer and very little scheme work. So, all these 3 factors pulled the ARPP up.

items.statement: Telangana/AP ARPOB growth to continue at same rate; ALOS reduction from 3.5 to 3.3-3.4 targeted; IP and OP volumes growing significantly
items.quote: So, Harit, both in Telangana and in Andhra for the first 9 months, there has been a significant growth in both volume, IP and OP volume as well as ARPP in absolute number. So, I think that will continue to do. That will continue to grow at the same growth rate. And there will be more efforts in trying to reduce the ALOS from the current 3.5 to probably 3.3, 3.4. And that impact on the ARPOB will r

items.statement: Nashik ARPOB currently INR 24-25k vs Nagpur INR 34-35k; blended Maharashtra INR 28-29k; expect Nashik to reach INR 30-33k at maturity (12 months)
items.quote: It will be in line with Nagpur, around INR 32,000, INR 33,000. Right now, it's around INR 24,000, INR 25,000. Nagpur continues to be at INR 34,000, INR 35,000. So, a blended number came out to be around INR 28,000, INR 29,000. But I think once it matures or towards the end of the first 12 months, we should get to INR 30,000, INR 33,000 kind of ARPOB.

items.statement: International patient revenue: INR 40-50 cr this FY from Telangana; target INR 100-150 cr over time; Bangalore and Thane better positioned for medical tourism; currently minimal EBITDA from international
items.quote: This year, we should do around INR 40 crores to INR 50 crores of revenue from international patients. We are hoping that it will go up to INR 100 crores, INR 150 crores over a period of time, just from the Telangana cluster. But I think given Bangalore and Thane, both the locations are very well poised for international patients. We are hopeful that the contribution for international from these 2

items.statement: Sri Suresh Patel (former CMD Andhra Bank, former CVC) joined Board; strengthening project delivery teams for faster execution; leveraging experienced cluster heads in Karnataka (20-25 yrs exp) and Kerala
items.quote: I'm glad to inform that a distinguished personality has joined our Board. He is Sri Suresh Patel, who held many prime positions in his illustrious career. He was CMD of erstwhile Andhra Bank, presently Union Bank of India. Later occupied 1 of the top positions in the country as CVC, that is Central Vigilance Commissioner. Our Board will be greatly enriched with his contributions.

items.statement: Thane market: Jupiter announcing second hospital reinforces opportunity; 4-5 year window before competitors commission; enough demand for 3-4 large players to coexist; doctor attraction not a problem
items.quote: It just reinforces our thought process that there is a lot of opportunity in Thane. And given that Jupiter announced its second hospital in Thane is even more reassuring. I think there is an opportunity for all of us to coexist. And the good part is there is a good 4, 5-year window before these hospitals get commissioned. So, it gives us a good runway to get ourselves established in those micro ma

items.statement: Specialty mix fragmented: cardiac 17-18%; renal, neuro, ortho, oncology, gastro each 9-10%; perception is multi-specialty; all Kerala hospitals to offer tertiary/quaternary care with oncology phased in
items.quote: So, it's a fragmented split, the specialties. Cardiac is around 17%, 18%. Rest of the specialties like renal, neuro, orthopedics, oncology, gastro are around 9% to 10%. So, it's quite fragmented across all specialties.

items.statement: Nashik oncology excluded due to contractual obligation; all other greenfield projects include oncology from day 1; Kerala hospitals add oncology in phased expansion due to space constraints
items.quote: Nashik, contractually, we are obligated to not do oncology, and that's why oncology is out of the equation there. As far as Kerala is concerned, the way the current hospitals are designed is it does not have space for oncology. So, when we ramp up the current hospitals and then do the next phase of expansion, that's why we are bringing oncology.

items.statement: Nagpur vendor advance write-offs: INR 3.5 cr this quarter, INR 3 cr last quarter; remaining INR 50 lakh - 1 cr expected in Q4 FY25; most write-offs done
items.quote: So, in Nagpur, before we took over, there were a lot of advances which were given and we haven't obtained any services or the vendors have not provided any goods against those particular advances. So, we have taken a write-off against these advances in the last quarter and this quarter. Most part of it is done. In Q4 of this financial year, you will see about some INR 50 lakh, INR 1 crore kind of

items.statement: Minority interest 9.9% in Q3, 10-11% for 9M; only incremental minority from Karnataka cluster (20% to management team); Thane 100% owned, Kondapur part of existing
items.quote: So, it is 9.9% in Q3. And if you're asking about 9 months, it would be somewhere in the range of 10% to 11% in the same range it would be, not more than that.

items.statement: Project delivery identified as key area to strengthen; building consistent teams for future asset execution; leveraging experienced cluster heads for Karnataka and Kerala scaling
items.quote: As far as where we would like to strengthen, I think on the project delivery, there is scope for us to improve further. We'd like to strengthen that, and we are trying to build teams to strengthen that because we want to do a lot more assets in the future. So, we need to have a consistent team that we should be able to achieve on that.

items.statement: Marketing expense is controllable and will be managed based on annual strategy; Beauty marketing at 10.1% this quarter vs 9.5% last year
items.quote: But yes, I think it is something that can easily be controlled. It's a marketing expenses considered available expense and totally controllable. So, it's more in line with -- for that year, what strategy we would like to follow.

items.statement: Consolidated GMV grew 25% YoY to INR 4,528 crores in Q3 FY25
items.quote: we are delighted to have a pretty good growth momentum at the GMV level where for the quarter, our GMV is at INR 4,528 crores, which is 25% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Consolidated gross profit grew 30% YoY to INR 991 crores; EBITDA grew 42% YoY to INR 140.8 crores; PAT grew 51% YoY to INR 26.4 crores
items.quote: From a gross profit perspective, it's been a fantastic quarter with gross profit at INR 991 crores, which is a 30% year -on-year increase. And the EBITDA has also come out at a pretty healthy level of INR 140.8 crores, which is a 42% year -on-year growth.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 69 bps YoY in Q3 and 42 bps for 9M FY25
items.quote: this is one of the factors which has led to a healthy EBITDA margin expansion of 69 basis points during the quarter and 42 basis points for the 9-month period.

items.statement: Fashion gross margin improved over 700 bps YoY from 44% to 51% in Q3
items.quote: seen a more than 700 basis points improvement in gross margin, which is a significant move from 44% last year, same quarter to 51% this year

items.statement: Beauty GMV grew 32% YoY to INR 3,389 crores in Q3; 9M GMV grew 30% to INR 8,716 crores
items.quote: the Beauty growth has come out at 32% year-on-year growth at INR3,389 crores. And when you look at it from a 9-month perspective, it's been a 30% year-on-year growth at INR8,716 crores.

items.statement: Fashion GMV grew 8% YoY to INR 1,130 crores in Q3; 9M GMV grew 10% to INR 2,767 crores
items.quote: From a Fashion perspective, while the GMV growth for the quarter is at 8% year -on-year, and the GMV number is INR1,130 crores for the quarter

items.statement: eB2B GMV grew 53% YoY to INR 260 crores; run rate INR 1,000 crores; 2.6 lakh retailers across 1,100 cities
items.quote: we grew GMV by 53%. And by delivering about INR 260 crores, we now are at a run rate of INR1,000 crore GMV.

items.statement: Pink Friday sale delivered 36% GMV growth, 86M visits, 55% customer growth, >4% conversion
items.quote: The sale delivered a growth of 36% year-over-year GMV terms. And we got over 86 million visits to the app across the 10-day period of the sale. Customer growth was strong at 55%.

items.statement: Physical retail at 221 stores (47 added in FY25, 12 in Q3); 2.1 lakh sq ft across 73 cities; 3 new cities added in Q3
items.quote: We are today at 221 stores, largest beauty retail network in the country. And of these, about 12 stores were launched during the quarter.

items.statement: 6 flagship stores (3,000+ sq ft) launched in major metros; more planned in coming months
items.quote: As a result, we have launched 6 flagship stores across I ndia. These are large format stores, 3,000 square feet plus and many more to

items.statement: 200 Beauty brands and 217 Fashion brands launched in FY25; key global launches: NARS, Eucerin, ghd, Kérastase, Laura Mercier, OUAI, TIRTIR, Numbuzin, AXIS-Y, Foot Locker, Snitch, Victoria's Secret
items.quote: In the Beauty business, if we talk about like we've seen some of the most accelerated brand launches at 200 in Beauty business and 217 Fashion brands.

items.statement: Working capital days consistently reducing, down to 36 days; fixed asset turnover 9.4%; ROCE >10%
items.quote: Working capital days have been con sistently reducing and have come down to 36 days. And this has resulted in the ROCE of the overall One Nykaa business coming in at upwards of 10

items.statement: New businesses (Fashion, eB2B) funded through Beauty internal accruals; no external fund raise mentioned
items.quote: the Beauty business is funding the growth of the newer businesses, which is Fashion and Nykaa D. So, all in all, through internal accruals, we have been able to manage to fund the new businesses

items.statement: 70% of Beauty orders delivered same/next day in top 110 cities; significant improvement in order-to-delivery timelines
items.quote: 70% of our beauty orders are delivered within the same or next day in top 110 cities. And overall, also, there has been huge improvement in order to delivery timelines for Beauty business.

items.statement: B2B contribution margin improved 500 bps; losses reducing significantly as business matures
items.quote: contribution margin improvement of 500 basis points. So, we believe that trend will continue. So, losses will reduce in B2B.

items.statement: Beauty EBITDA margin increased despite higher marketing investment for new customer acquisition
items.quote: while given the focus on new customer acquisition, et c, there is higher investment in marketing, in spite of that, the EBITDA margin for the Beauty vertical has actually gone up.

items.statement: Marketing income improving as brands shift spend from promos back to advertising; early signs suggest trend continues
items.quote: that trend has finally seems to be reversing and brands realize that they cannot -- there is significant brand awareness work to be done in a market -- in a nascent market like India. So, a lot of the money that was being deployed for promo is now being redeployed into advertising, and that's a plus for us.

items.statement: LBB acquisition enables in-house events and content creation; revenues captured in Fashion with associated expenses
items.quote: Profile is all event activity. They charge clients for various event activity, which is all costed individual event based on estimation of the costs.

items.statement: Fashion revenue growth 21% includes LBB and improved GMV-to-NSV ratio from controlling leakages; revenue growth higher than GMV growth
items.quote: revenue growth momentum has been higher than the GMV growth momentum. And what we disclose is basically vertical level reporting, and this is what the number is at the vertical level.

items.statement: Working capital days consistently declining; reduction representative of ongoing trend
items.quote: directionally, as you would see over the last few quarters, the working capital days have been consistently coming down. So, in that sense, the reduction which you are seeing, you can take it as a representative of an ongoing basis.

items.statement: GCC in base for 4 quarters; current quarter slightly higher due to second store opening but not called out separately
items.quote: last year was the first time that had come in and it was not really there in the base, whereas now consistently 4 quarters, we have had GCC come into the base, although the current quarter would be a little higher given that we have now opened the second store, et cetera.

items.statement: GCC store rollout slower than expected; e-com rollout pending technology stack adoption; some investment over last year
items.quote: the rollout of the stores has been slower than expected and e -com rollout is also pen ding adoption of the technology stack over time. So, I think in that sense, in the GCC right now, the level of activity is not very high to be needing to call it out. But yes, there's been some investment in GCC over last 1 year.

items.statement: Beauty EBITDA margin range 7.5%-9%; steady state depends on retail mix, private label profitability, superstore losses, eB2B investment
items.quote: we have seen the margin hovering in the range of, let's say, 7.5% at the low end to 9% at the high end. Are we actually at that level? Or do we see room to improve? And how far are we from a steady -state margin?

items.statement: Fashion marketing expense rose from 24.6% to 30.5%; controlled marketing could have delivered EBITDA breakeven this quarter
items.quote: if our marketing expense, which became adverse from 24.6% to 30.5%, if that had stayed under control, we could have possibly had EBITDA margin breakeven this quarter.

items.statement: Comfortable with Fashion breakeven next year; confident as new-to-repeat customer ratio improves and assortment expands
items.quote: we remain comfortable because if you look at it, like if our marketing expense, which became adverse from 24.6% to 30.5%, if that had stayed under control, we could have possibly had EBITDA margin breakeven this quarter. So, I think the main thing here to balance, and that is what it is for all e-commerce businesses is to balance between growth and profitability

items.statement: eB2B covers 1,100 cities; added 250 cities last year; expansion paced to maintain unit economics, not targeting full country coverage
items.quote: we already cover 1,100 cities, which is very wide. And like you saw last year, we increased by 250 cities. So, I don't think overnight is going to change to like covering 3,000 cities or anything like that.

items.statement: 70%+ of orders across 110 cities at same-day/next-day delivery; order-to-delivery reduced from 4+ days to <2 days over 2-3 years
items.quote: today, as we've said before, 70% plus of orders across 110 cities are sitting at same day or next day delivery. So, our speed is getting a lot better.

items.statement: No meaningful KPI difference between SDD/NDD and slower delivery cohorts; speed rolled out across full assortment pan-India
items.quote: there is no real difference in the KPIs for consumers who are receiving orders same day or next day versus those for whom it is taking slightly longer, whether it be on average order value or anything like that.

items.statement: Own fashion brands ~10-12% of fashion GMV; not pursuing ultra-fast fashion speed; focus on monthly new drops and third-party fast fashion partners
items.quote: our own brands on our platform is not a very large contributor. I mean we've always announced it that it's about 10% to 12%, but that was always -- we had said the GMV of our own brands to a GMV of our fashion omni -channel business.

items.statement: Beauty gross margin improved from 42.2% to 43.4% YoY; each underlying business improving margin but mix shifts can mask consolidated improvement
items.quote: We have had some improvement in gross profit margin in overall in Beauty business, like it's moved up from 42.2% a year ago to 43.4% now.

items.statement: Nykaa positions as retailer first; own brands built as independent brands with distribution strength; not aiming to match largest fast fashion players
items.quote: we want our fashion labels to be enablers to our dot-com business and, they are being built as brands with the journey, which is independent of just our platform and beyond that also. But I don't think the ambition is to build a very big fashion brand with the aggression of trying to match some of the fastest, largest fashion brands in the country.

items.statement: KFC store expansion guidance of 70-80 stores per year
items.quote: On KFC, we are saying anywhere between 70-80, which has been roughly a pace of expansion over the last 3 years. We should be able to continue this.

items.statement: Pizza Hut store expansion guidance of 20-25 stores per year
items.quote: On Pizza Hut, again, we'll be cautious, perhaps 20-25 is what we are looking at.

items.statement: Sri Lanka revenue CAGR target of at least 15% over medium to long term
items.quote: So, I think we should be at least aiming for a 15% revenue CAGR over there.

items.statement: KFC capex per store at INR 2 crore, Pizza Hut at INR 1.35-1.4 crore
items.quote: KFC continues to be in the range of INR 2 odd crores per store, and Pizza Hut is in the range of INR 1.35-1.4 crores per store.

items.statement: Added 54 restaurants in Q3 FY25, total 963 stores
items.quote: In the quarter, we added 54 restaurants, taking our total to 963.

items.statement: KFC SSSG improved to -3% in Q3 from -5% in Q1 and -8% in Q2, SSTG flat at 0%
items.quote: Our KFC SSSG trajectory improved slightly versus our previous 2 quarters. SSSG came in as negative 3%. The heartening part was SSTG was 0% in this.

items.statement: Pizza Hut SSSG turned positive 5% after 8 quarters, ADS stable at INR 48,000
items.quote: Pizza Hut delivered a sales growth of 10% and positive SSSG of 5% after 8 quarters. ADS has remained stable in line with the previous 2 quarters at INR 48,000.

items.statement: Sri Lanka SSSG 14% with double-digit transaction growth, best quarter in 2.5 years
items.quote: The SSSG was 14%, backed by double-digit transaction growth. So that was the heartening part of the transaction, double-digit same-store transaction growth.

items.statement: KFC restaurant EBITDA margin 15.4%, down 60 bps YoY; consolidated EBITDA margin 18.5%, up 10 bps YoY
items.quote: Restaurant EBITDA increased 9% year-on-year, and restaurant EBITDA margin was 15.4%, down by 60 basis points year-on-year. Our Consolidated EBITDA of INR 140 crores at 18.5% increased year-on-year by 14%, up 10 basis points.

items.statement: Pizza Hut restaurant EBITDA margin 4.7%, up 10 bps YoY
items.quote: Gross margin largely remained stable, and the restaurant EBITDA came at 4.7%, which was 10 basis points higher than last year.

items.statement: Sri Lanka restaurant EBITDA margin 17.8%, up 360 bps YoY
items.quote: Restaurant EBITDA came in at 17.8%, which was up by 360 basis points.

items.statement: KFC margin floor around 18% at flat to positive SSSG; need >5% SSSG for margin expansion
items.quote: Over a longer period, we require a 5% SSSG just to take care of the inflation. And the current level, the floor is around 18%. So if you're able to get an SSSG of flat to positive, I think that should be the range.

items.statement: Pizza Hut ADS of INR 47-48k yields ~5% margin; INR 50k yields high single digit; INR 55k needed for double-digit margin
items.value: INR 47,000-48,000 (5%), INR 50,000 (high single digit), INR 55,000 (double digit)
items.quote: If it's in the range of INR 47,000-48,000, you are at where you are, that 5% range, which include additional marketing spends as well by the way. If you fall below that, you go towards that breakeven or even loss making. And you move towards INR 50,000, maybe you are high single digit. You need to move towards that INR 55,000 mark to go towards double digit.

items.statement: KFC value structure: INR 99 core, INR 149 individual meals, INR 399 group meals
items.quote: On value, we've got now a sharp 3-tier value structure in core at INR 99, individual meal offerings at INR 149 and then group meals at INR 399.

items.statement: KFC focusing on core variety products: chicken on bone, Zinger Burger, rolls, wings, boneless (popcorn and strips)
items.quote: Our core variety products are chicken on the bone, Zinger Burger, rolls, wings and boneless, which is popcorn and strips.

items.statement: KFC late-night contributes nearly 10% of business in stores operating late night
items.quote: Now late night, for example, is nearly 10% of our business in the stores that we operate late night.

items.statement: Budget tax relief of INR 1 lakh crore to middle class seen as positive for consumption
items.quote: And the fact that there is INR1 lakh crores that has been given back to middle class consumers is only a positive. We are hoping and wondering as to how soon we will see that reflect in consumption, but that can only be a positive.

items.statement: No material change in other income; regular business activity
items.quote: Regular, regular. So nothing that is very specific different.

items.statement: KFC ADS INR 115,000 including 90 new stores opened in last calendar year (22% store growth)
items.quote: The ADS was INR 115,000. This includes 90 stores which we opened in the last calendar year, that's 22% store growth.

items.statement: Sri Lanka revenue grew 15% in LKR and 30% in INR
items.quote: Overall revenue grew by 15% in LKR and 30% in INR.

items.statement: Consumer sentiment remains soft; no material pickup expected in KFC demand in Q4
items.quote: When we enter into Q4, we still see the consumer demand environment being challenging. So, we don't see a big pickup from a demand perspective on KFC.

items.statement: ESG: DJSI score 50, ranked No.1 among Indian QSR brands for 2nd consecutive year, No.7 globally in 97th percentile
items.quote: DJSI ratings, we scored 50 and this actually allowed us to be ranked No. 1 amongst all QSR brands in India for second consecutive year. We were ranked No. 7 amongst global QSR companies, placed in 97th percentile amongst global QSR companies.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 revenue outlook of $100-105 million reaffirmed; Q4 sequential revenue growth guided at 2-3%
items.quote: Our current performance is definitely tracking towards that number. We expect to close, on a full year basis, our numbers will be in that range that we had indicated in our Analyst Day.

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin guided at 24-25% excluding forex impact; long-term PAT margin expected at 20%
items.quote: On the EBITDA side, our expectation is that the margin in this particular quarter was impacted by this forex loss that we had, but we don't expect a similar sort of a charge in the following quarters, which means that at least on the EBITDA side, we will be in the range of 24% to 25% for the subsequent quarter.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guidance retained at 18-20% range pending strategy finalization
items.quote: We would like to be a bit conservative and then put out a guidance more in the 18% to 20% kind of a range in terms of what we see.

items.statement: Order book expected to jump ~35% year-over-year by end of Q4 FY25
items.quote: Now with that context in mind, if I look at what were the order book number at the end of quarter 4 last year versus where we expect to be at the end of this year, there will be a good 35% kind of a jump in terms of the order book.

items.statement: Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin 26.1% vs reported 22.1% due to INR 6.8 crore forex loss and retention bonus charges
items.quote: Now had these two things not been there, our business EBITDA or the adjusted EBITDA that we reported would have come in at 26.1%, which is reflective of the strong operating performance that we were able to deliver in this particular quarter.

items.statement: Strong traction in large deals and new logos; 10 new logos added in Q3, half Fortune 500; over 10 GenAI engagements this fiscal
items.quote: We do see some traction coming back in terms of bigger deals that we have been pursuing over the last several quarters. And this is something that I've been highlighting in earlier interactions, and we were very happy to note that we were able to close some of these big deals.

items.statement: BFSI vertical crossed $10M annual revenue run-rate, growing >40% YoY; CPG vertical facing headwinds from market conditions and tariff concerns
items.quote: Another important highlight for us was the very strong performance of the BFSI vertical. We have crossed the $10 million mark in terms of the revenues that we are expecting for this vertical in this year. And overall, for the full year, we will be growing in excess of 40% rate when we tie it up at the end of the year.

items.statement: Generative AI ~10% of current fiscal work; pipeline shows ~20% of conversations for next year; building 4 GenAI solutions plus wrappers on existing solutions
items.quote: Even in this fiscal, about 10% of the work that we are doing is around Generative AI. If I look at the pipeline for the next year, almost 20% of the conversations that we are having are all around Generative AI.

items.statement: Largest single SOW won at existing account; 3 former clients re-engaged; 2 large Indian business houses added via GCC/India practice
items.quote: One of the notable big deals is something that we have shared as part of the press release as well. It's the largest deal that we have done till date in terms of annual revenue from a single statement of work, and this is one of our existing accounts.

items.statement: Continued investment in GenAI R&D, Databricks capability, and Europe front-end team; investments may stay ahead of revenue visibility by 1-2% EBITDA impact
items.quote: We will also continue to invest for building out our Databricks capability, which again, from a strategic standpoint, we believe is going to be a strong pillar of growth for us. So some of these investments, I would say, will continue to sort of stay ahead of revenue visibility in some sense.

items.statement: Intra-group loans to UK, Netherlands, Germany subsidiaries caused INR 6.8 crore forex loss; corrective actions underway to reduce subsidiary debt and forex volatility
items.quote: So, these are loans that we had given out to our subsidiaries in U.K., Netherlands and Germany to capitalize them. And there was a sharp movement in the INR versus the GBP and euro, which meant that for this particular quarter, the total loss that we had to book on account of the forex movement was close to about INR 6.8 crore.

items.statement: Headcount ~1,600+ including Decision Point; 2 Databricks partner champions named; Databricks COE lead on Partner Advisory Board
items.quote: Our overall headcount for this quarter, including the Decision Point employees came in at about 1,600-plus employees.

items.statement: Actively evaluating M&A opportunities in data engineering/Databricks space; selective approach given Decision Point integration and CPG headwinds
items.quote: Our M&A corporate development team is still in action and the team is still identifying and continuously evaluating and bringing opportunities to the table. So that work is still on. So if we find a good opportunity around that, we will definitely pursue it.

items.statement: Dollar revenue $27.2M in Q3 vs $25.1M in Q2 (+8.4% QoQ); organic and inorganic both grew ~9% sequentially
items.quote: In terms of the dollar revenue growth itself for this particular quarter, the dollar revenue came in at $27.2 million compared to about $25.1 million in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Cash balance >INR 1,000 crore at quarter end reflecting strong cash generation
items.quote: Our cash balance again stood at in excess of about INR 1,000 crore as at the end of the last quarter, which reflects the strong cash generation capability of the business.

items.statement: Industry inflection from DeepSeek/reasoning models may automate current FTE work; need 2-3x work volume or product model shift to sustain revenue run-rate
items.quote: Now we believe that, that is an opportunity for us as well because these things need to be put together and they need to be built. But what that will also mean is that for the current quantum of work that is being done, the productivity benefit will significantly kick in.

items.statement: Clients expecting faster turnaround (weeks vs months); building solutions/assets to capture productivity benefits via new contracting models
items.quote: What clients were willing to wait for, for a couple of months or 3 months, the expectation is that it will now be done in weeks. The good thing is that the evolving technology stack actually allows you to do that.

items.statement: Tariff implications a concern for CPG/LatAm revenues; lost SEZ tax benefit (10AA) in Chennai delivery centers this year
items.quote: Any tariff kind of impact that might be there could impact the revenues from LatAm, could impact revenues from China, for example, right, for some of the CPG companies that we work with.

items.statement: $3.2M large deal fully ramped (40+ team) contributing in Q3; full benefit visible in Q3 vs 1 month in Q2
items.quote: It's fully ramped up already. So it's a 40-member plus team. We have fully ramped up that project and we have started executing.

items.statement: US 90% of revenue; Europe/LatAm small but expected to grow with Decision Point integration; forex loss INR 6.8 crore on intra-group loans
items.quote: In terms of, I would say, the geographical split of revenues, U.S. still continues to be the dominant geography, contributing about 90% of our overall revenues

items.statement: Decision Point retention bonus charges to continue for 5 more quarters; amortization of intangibles over ~5 years
items.quote: And that is expected to continue for another 5 quarters, post which you will not see the impact of the transaction related cost that we are currently disclosing under adjusted EBITDA.

items.statement: Express Parcel steady-state service EBITDA margin target 17-20%
items.quote: I think for the Express Parcel business, service EBITDA margins will remain in the 17% to 20% range.

items.statement: PTL revenue growth target 25-30% for next financial year
items.quote: Our own ambition internally is certainly to grow the business overall at nearly 25% to 30% in the next financial year.

items.statement: Capex as percentage of revenue expected to be 5.6% or lower this year, long-term target 3.5-4%
items.quote: will end up with CapEx as a percentage of revenue being 5.6% Delhivery Ltd Q3 FY25 Earnings Call- Hosted by Macquarie Feb 7, 2025 or lower. And this has been declining YoY. We've indicated that over the long term we expect CapEx to settle at between 3.5% and 4% of revenue

items.statement: Rapid commerce revenue expected Rs 80-100 crore through the financial year
items.quote: I expect that this business will add maybe somewhere between Rs. 80 crores and Rs. 100 crores of revenue to Delhivery through the financial year.

items.statement: Express Parcel service EBITDA margin improved QoQ from 15.1% to 15.6% but depressed YoY due to fixed cost buildup and fleet cost inflation
items.quote: The Express Parcel business saw marginal growth in service EBITDA between Q2 and Q3 with growth from Rs. 196 crores of service EBITDA in Q2 to Rs. 232 crores of service EBITDA in Q3. Improvement in the overall service EBITDA margin from 15.1% to 15.6%.

items.statement: PTL service EBITDA margin improved to 3.8%, highest in 11 quarters, with sequential improvement expected to continue
items.quote: The Part Truckload business' service EBITDA margin has improved from 2.9% to 3.8%, which is the highest service EBITDA margin that this business has generated in the last 11 quarters, sequential improvement will continue.

items.statement: Corporate overheads flat for 11 quarters at Rs 211 crore (8.9% of revenue), glide path toward 6% continues
items.quote: Overall, corporate overheads have remained broadly flat for the last 11 quarters. They are currently at Rs. 211 crores, which represents 8.9% of total revenue versus 10.2% at the start of the year, and the broad glide path down towards 6% of revenues continues.

items.statement: E-commerce industry volume growth muted; D2C volumes grew ~30% YoY, SME volumes grew >50% YoY
items.quote: The heartening sort of piece of our volumes has been that our direct-to-consumer business has grown close to about 30% YoY, and our SME business has actually grown over 50% YoY.

items.statement: Overall e-commerce growth moderated this financial year; marketplaces experiencing muted volume growth
items.quote: I think overall e-commerce growth has certainly moderated, Aditya. There's no question in this financial year. I think there's no question. The larger marketplaces obviously are private, so I don't know exactly what their numbers are going to turn out to be. But every indicator that we have from them is that volume growth has been fairly muted for all of them.

items.statement: PTL December volumes highest since Spoton integration at ~147,000 tons; January continued strongly
items.quote: In fact, December was our highest month ever since the integration with Spoton at close to, if I'm not mistaken, about 147,000 tons of freight. And January has continued more or less in the same way.

items.statement: HPCL partnership starting, will bring significant volume to PTL network
items.quote: And we also announced, of course, that we have a big partnership which is starting with HPCL, which is going to be a significant volume into the PTL network.

items.statement: Capex as percentage of revenue 5.6% or lower this year, declining YoY; no major capex planned for next year, only routine hub upgrades
items.quote: I think this year we will end up with CapEx as a percentage of revenue being 5.6% Delhivery Ltd Q3 FY25 Earnings Call- Hosted by Macquarie Feb 7, 2025 or lower. And this has been declining YoY. We've indicated that over the long term we expect CapEx to settle at between 3.5% and 4% of revenue, which is largely going to be maintenance CapEx, upgrade CapEx as we need. I don't think we have any very

items.statement: Infrastructure at 20.6 million sq ft including 0.5 million sq ft temporary peak season capacity; 112 major gateways/hubs, 45 automated sort centers with 65 sorters; sufficient capacity in network, utilization expected to rise next year
items.quote: Infrastructure in Q3 had grown to 20.6 million square feet. However, this includes close to about 0.5 million square feet of temporary infrastructure that's built up for the peak season and is then let go off in Q4. We continue to operate 112 major gateways and hubs across the country, including 45 automated sort centers equipped with 65 sorters.

items.statement: Fleet costs spiked in first week of October due to intra-city vehicle shortage; shifting to fixed contracts for next year
items.quote: And as a consequence of that, supply was limited and overall pricing of the fleet went up compared to what we'd expected. I think we had been operating so far with a completely third-party fleet. And our decision is that we will sign more long-term contracts with our fleet partners, locking in these rates for next year a lot better.

items.statement: PTL yield improved from ~Rs 10.3/kg to ~Rs 11.1/kg over 6-7 quarters; heavier loads improving tractor-trailer utilization; reseller program targeting reverse line-haul routes for higher incremental margins
items.quote: If you look at it, yield, I think over a six, seven quarter period has gone from about Rs. 10.3 per kilogram to nearly about Rs. 11.1 per kilogram. So, I think that is part of what will continue to drive growth in margins.

items.statement: Delhivery >100% of Express Parcel industry profit pool; competitors' losses increasing; industry consolidation expected as capital flows constrained
items.quote: The reality is that last year we had the same discussion in terms of how long these losses can sustain, and I think the reality is that incremental capital flow into this industry is now going to be severely constrained. And I think in the interest of sustaining themselves as going concerns, I think competition is going to have to look at their business models.

items.statement: Variablized networks have higher costs and worse service metrics; Delhivery cost per delivery 8-10% lower than in-house variablized networks
items.quote: I mean we've done the benchmarking and our belief is that our cost of delivery is anywhere between 8% and 10% lower than even the in-house variablized networks.

items.statement: Top 5 customers <50% of revenue; Meesho insourcing impact largely done; active conversations with customers on outsourcing more
items.quote: Our top clients, as I've mentioned, our top three or four clients put together, top five customers will form close to less than half of the overall revenue of Delhivery. So, we don't have a very significant client concentration as a whole.

items.statement: Two new independent directors added: Sameer Mehta (Boat) and Namita Thapar (Emcure); Mani Venkatesh joining as Chief Business Officer from March 1
items.quote: I'd like to place on record a warm welcome to the two new independent directors on the Board of Delhivery, Mr. Sameer Mehta from Boat and Ms. Namita Thapar from Emcure Pharmaceuticals. And an announcement that Ms. Mani Venkatesh will be joining us as Chief Business Officer of Delhivery from the 1st of March.

items.statement: E-commerce consumption slowdown affecting volumes; first-party logistics arms' strategy fluid; industry structure dynamic with weekly changes
items.quote: and we'll see how that plays out. These are active conversations that we are having with all of our customers. And if there's even minor shifts in their strategy, the upside to Delhivery could be large. But it's hard to say at this point I think because these strategies are still relatively fluid. But I think the reality is that overall, from an insourcing standpoint, most of the sort of insourcin

items.statement: Targets volume growth of 13%-14% annually for next 3-4 years to reach 65%-70% capacity utilisation
items.quote: See, so largely, our target is to grow volume -wise by 13%-14%, that's what our target is. Thi s quarter was an exception, but, yes, the overall target is to grow volume at 13% at least. And that's what we have built the capacity in last three, four years, and that’s what our target is for next three, four years

items.statement: Plans Rs 40-50 crore capex in FY26 for efficiency; Hazelnut acquisition needs minimal capex
items.quote: from CAPEX lens, from overall Bikaji lens, we see close to Rs. 40-50 Crores of CAPEX largely to build efficiency in the system, that's what we will do next year.

items.statement: Took price hikes in Q3; plans 1-1.5% more in Feb-March; expects ASP growth of 3-3.5% YoY in Q4
items.quote: So, largely, that's what we will do, we will do 1%-1.5% price increase in Feb and March first week, that's what, we will do, number one.

items.statement: Product mix stable YoY; western snacks share fell to 6.8% from 7.5% due to conscious production cut; large packs 61%, impulse 35%
items.quote: In terms of, if we look at our product mix , it is broadly in line with what it was last year. So, 62.9% it was last year Quarter 4 for namkeens and Bhujia put together, which is now at 62.1%. So, the only thing if you refer to this sheet of ours , is the western snacks contribution. So, last year, if we look at Quarter 3, it was at 7.5%, which has come down to 6.8%.

items.statement: Hedges all key commodities except edible oil via long-term vendor contracts started 1.5-2 years ago
items.quote: So, normally we do , like for key commodity, other than edible oil , we do long term contracts with the vendors to help the price , and that's what we started 1.5-2 years back . And this has helped us in protecting the margin.

items.statement: No major acquisitions planned; focus on organic growth and capacity utilisation
items.quote: So, we do not see any major acquisitions in coming years, t hat's what our plan is , to grow organically and to utilize the capacity what we have already built

items.statement: Revenue volume growth 8% in Q3 (vs reported 3% due to 10% extra grammage in base); YTD volume growth 11%, revenue volume growth 13.3%
items.quote: If we speak about our revenue volume growth, so, it's 8% and this somehow connects with your grammage cut. last year, in this quarter, all our large packs had 10% extra, which was not the case this year.

items.statement: Exports grew 32.6% in Q3 and ~21% YTD
items.quote: if we look at, in this quarter post-tax revenue growth is 10.8%, focus states growing at 14.7% , other states at 8.7%, and exports had done good, is at 32.6% growth.

items.statement: Small regional players continue to exit in inflationary environment; Nielsen shows 200+ reported companies per state with some weeded out
items.quote: Small, regional players, few will come, few will go, that will always be happening kind of a stuff. Because certain companies are not able to sustain , not able to though even survive in the kind of environment of inflation and all this stuff. So, that always will be the story.

items.statement: PLI income booked at Rs 14 crore per quarter; expects to receive FY24 PLI by March 2025
items.quote: currently we are booking PLI income, this year we booked PLI close to Rs. 14 Cores per quarter, and we will receive PLI from government maybe in this quarter, 3rd Quarter by March, when government is very proactive to do all the audits and to release the fund s. So, by March, we will receive PLI of last year , FY ‘24

items.statement: Quick commerce grew 86% in Q3 on small base
items.quote: So, yes, because of the small bases what we have, so yes, this quarter again it has grown about 86% growth.

items.statement: Price increases region-specific based on commodity impact and competitive intensity; MRP hikes national, trade schemes vary by state
items.quote: So, normally, it is based on region, we see which region is having much impact, because mix is different in every region. So, we see region wise, and then, eventually we take the price hike like MRP increase in family pack nationally, that's what we do.

items.statement: Focus states grew 14.7% in Q3, core states 10.8%, other states 8.7%; YTD focus 17.1%, core 11.9%, others 23.7%
items.quote: if we look at, in this quarter post-tax revenue growth is 10.8%, focus states growing at 14.7% , other states at 8.7%, and exports had done good, is at 32.6% growth. At a YTD basis, core states have grown at 11.9%, focus states is 17.1%, and others is 23.7%.

items.statement: Family packs grew 11.6%, impulse packs 12.9% in Q3; large pack mix 61%, impulse 35%
items.quote: Our flagship of the continuity on the large pack continues, so, the mix of products between impulse and the large pack is 61% from large pack, and 35% coming from impulse pack. Both the family pack and impulse pack has done well in the quarter, so, family pack growing at 11.6%, impulse slightly higher at 12.9% growth.

items.statement: Construction equipment end market soft globally; largest customer seeing early to mid-double-digit decline, inventory destocking amplifying impact on Uniparts sales
items.quote: Our largest global customer is witnessing early to mid-double-digit decline in this segment. This impact on our sales to them is higher than that due to some impact of inventory destocking.

items.statement: Large agriculture equipment sluggish in US and Europe with inventory correction; small ag equipment in North America and Japan weakening further, Europe and India stable to marginally positive
items.quote: Coming to large ag demand, sluggishness in large agriculture equipment is hurting overall short-term demand in US and Europe with some additional element of inventory correction.

items.statement: Aftermarket segment performing well post inventory correction, demand normalizing, likely to grow 25-30% YoY this fiscal
items.quote: Our aftermarket segment is performing well post the inventory correction cycle, and that part of demand is seemingly normalizing now. This segment is likely to grow 25% to 30% year-on-year in this fiscal itself.

items.statement: Trailing 12-month new business awards approximately INR203 crores annualized potential value across PMP, large ag assemblies, ag machinery in India, high horsepower 3-Point Linkage, and below 70 HP tractor geographic expansion
items.quote: Total new business award value during trailing 12 months has been approximately INR203 crores, which represents annualized potential value of underlying projects.

items.statement: Q4 revenue expected between Q1 and Q2 FY25 levels; sequential improvement expected; mid-teens revenue growth guided for FY26 driven by new business implementation
items.quote: I think it will be between the -- it could be the second best between whatever we were in quarter 1 and quarter 2, I think we will reach that point in any case. So you will see that swing back come over.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin 17.9%; medium-term target of 20%+ remains; margin improvement expected as operating deleverage reverses with growth
items.quote: Medium-term indication of the 20% plus remains. I think we are getting back to that.

items.statement: Cash outgo towards capex commitments approximately INR11 crores in Q3
items.quote: Cash outgo towards capex commitments during the quarter has been approximately INR11 crores.

items.statement: Mexico near-shoring step one is stocking operation; manufacturing to be considered in second phase based on best-cost-country model; Bobcat awarded $6.5M business starting Jan 2026
items.quote: Step one is stocking. And once that is stabilized, Mexico is a new working environment for us. So we want to learn about the environment before we make significant bigger investments there.

items.statement: Inflationary pressure on operating costs in medium term to be partially mitigated through operational efficiencies; rupee depreciation helps competitiveness vs US but similar vs Chinese yuan
items.quote: Inflationary pressure on operating cost remains in the medium-term to be partially mitigated through operational efficiencies.

items.statement: Fabrication platform gaining traction with large awards; expanding system boundaries strategy adding more content per vehicle; 3-Point Linkage growth shifting to >70 HP tractors
items.quote: We have added more capabilities on the fabrication side of our business, which is not even a full platform just now. But if you remember from our earlier strategy, we had identified 3 platforms, PTO, fabrications and hydraulics.

items.statement: Relationship with Caterpillar growing rapidly across multiple divisions; large new awards from another customer for Mexico operations; processing large RFQs with CNH Construction; expanding with Kobelco, Kubota, CNH
items.quote: I think the bigger one that is moving along is our, as Gurdeep alluded in the call earlier that our relationship with the largest one, Caterpillar is really, really growing very rapidly.

items.statement: Net working capital (inventory, receivables, payables) at approximately 151 days of trailing 12-month revenue as of Dec 31, 2024; decreased by ~INR21 crores during quarter
items.quote: The net working capital comprising of big 3 elements of inventory, accounts receivables and accounts payables as number of days of trailing 12 months revenue from operations stood at approximately 151 days as on 31st December 2024.

items.statement: Balance sheet net debt free with group net cash position at INR208 crores; healthy free cash flows at ~16% of revenue from operations
items.quote: The company's balance sheet continues to be net debt free with group net cash position at INR208 crores.

items.statement: Enabling resolution for up to INR1,500 crores passed; actively evaluating inorganic growth options but focused on strategically fit, manageable size acquisitions
items.quote: Yes, the enabling resolution may be large, but I think we will be -- for us, that's more an enabling thing. What I'm actually working on or what the team is working on is more at a situation where it will be strategically very positive to the company.

items.statement: Stated dividend policy 25% of profit or above; currently paying 80-90% of profits due to surplus cash; total dividend ~INR14 this year close to YTD EPS
items.quote: The stated policy is 25% of profit or above. While this year itself with the second interim dividend, total dividend has been about INR14 or so, which is very close to the Y-T-D EPS as well.

items.statement: Tanushree Bagrodia joined as Group COO and Board member in November; Sudhakar Kolli outgoing Group COO recognized for contributions
items.quote: I wish to introduce Ms. Tanushree Bagrodia, who joined us in November as Group Chief Operating Officer, and she is also a member of our Board of Directors.

items.statement: Macro concerns: global economic slowdown, geopolitical uncertainties, evolving trade tariff environment, persistent inflation, elevated interest rates remain key monitorables
items.quote: Macro concerns over global economic slowdown, geopolitical uncertainties, evolving global trade tariff environment and impact of persistent inflation as well as elevated interest rates continues to be key monitorable.

items.statement: US tariffs on Chinese imports creating opportunity; Uniparts dual-shore manufacturing and Mexico near-shoring provide flexibility; customers increasing India staffing for China shift
items.quote: If the tariffs come on India as well, that's going to be a challenge, right? So -- but at the same time, yes, here's the thing. I don't care where the tariffs go. And the reason for that is wherever the tariffs go, Uniparts is in a better position than anybody else to deal with it.

items.statement: Warehouse model sales mix at 46-47% of revenue for 9M FY25; up from 42-43% three years ago; expected to grow further as customers prefer risk-averse supply chain management
items.quote: I believe it's in the region of 46% to 47% of our sales are coming from there.

items.statement: China sourcing issues driving more business to India; Uniparts seeing increased RFQs and customer staffing in India; fabrication awards increasing as customers shift from China
items.quote: And I think we are seeing a significant amount of traction on the fabrication side of business as more and more issues emerge with China, I think you will see more and more India come into that place.

items.statement: Tariff environment evolving; Uniparts positioned to handle tariffs on any geography via dual-shore, Mexico near-shoring, and flexible delivery model
items.quote: If I need to ramp up in India, I'll ramp up in India. If I need to ramp up in the US, I'll ramp up in the US. If I need to do something and with a dual-shore mix of that, we are able to do that.

items.statement: Actively pursuing acquisitions consuming significant management time; criteria well-defined for strategic fit adding third platform (PTO, hydraulics, or fabrications) targeting 25-30% revenue contribution
items.quote: I've always said that we have 2 platforms, which is 3-Point Linkage and PMP, and we had 3 identified platforms. PTO, hydraulic and fabrications. And I think strategically, we are looking at it to be in one of those.

items.statement: Existing OEM business flat to low single-digit growth; aftermarket driving 2-3% growth; new business awards (INR203 crores trailing 12M) to drive mid-teens FY26 growth
items.quote: The existing business on the OEM side is not going to drive the growth. For me the aftermarket is driving it from here. But the significant large one, if you factor that like what I said, the trailing 12 months, we've had about INR203 crores of new awards.

items.statement: Large ag equipment and construction equipment cycles still tough; small tractor cycle (2.5 years) showing green shoots; aftermarket inventory correction complete
items.quote: The large agricultural equipment, the pain is not fully gone, Mohammed. Some of that is still going to continue. And I think I alluded it earlier also, it's going to probably get started.

items.statement: Korea showing significant revenue jumps from new awards; Japan new business offset by existing market slowdown; >70 HP tractor market share target 20-25% in 5 years from current 8-9%
items.quote: Over the next 5 years, could we be 20%, 25% of the market? The answer is yes.

items.statement: UTV/ATV pilot didn't take off; launching marketing campaign, online retail sales, and dealer distributor tools; taking longer than expected
items.quote: We have launched over there a complete marketing campaign in the different stores over there. We are also now going to be launching our own online retail sales on that as well as tools to take it to the dealer distributor market.

items.statement: Reiterated FY25 guidance: 40-45 branch additions, 30-35% AUM growth, ~6% spread, 40-50 bps credit cost
items.quote: We continue to maintain our guidance what we indicated during our previous calls. Branch addition of around 40-45 for the year. Maintain margins at around 6%. Credit cost in a range of 40 to 50 bps. Loan growth in a range of 30% to 35%.

items.statement: Opened 42 new branches in 9MFY25, total network at 265 branches
items.quote: We guided for 40 to 45 branches each year for the next few years, on that note, we opened 42 new branches in the first nine months of this financial year.

items.statement: AUM grew 36% YoY to Rs 7,619 crore in Q3FY25
items.quote: We are pleased to report an AUM growth of 36% YoY to Rs. 7,619 crores supported by disbursement growth of 29%, this quarter, we clocked Rs. 879 crores of disbursement.

items.statement: Spread maintained at ~6%, portfolio yield 14.9%, cost of funds stable at 8.8%
items.quote: Our margins are consistently above 6% in line with our guidance for the medium term.

items.statement: 30+ DPD at 3.7% in Q3FY25, up 10 bps QoQ; Stage-III stable at 1.2%, PCR 25%
items.quote: We witnessed a marginal uptick in 30 + to 3.7% in Q3FY25, forward flow stabilized in December and traction looks positive going forward.

items.statement: Credit cost stable at 50 bps for Q3FY25, within 40-50 bps guidance
items.quote: Credit cost for the quarter is stable at 50 basis points, which is broadly in line with our guidance.

items.statement: Cost of funds contained at 8.8% despite 30 bps MCLR increase; gap vs peers narrowed from 0.7% to 0.4%
items.quote: Our cost of fund is stable at 8.8% in spite of increase of about 30 basis points in the MCLR by banks in the last 12 months.

items.statement: BT-out rate stable at 5.5% range for many quarters
items.quote: BT rate remains the range of 5.5%. That is consistent from quite a few quarters and that looks trends as of now basically.

items.statement: ESOP coverage extended from 10% to 25% of staff (branch manager and above) to reduce attrition
items.quote: Earlier apart from frontliners which includes loan officers or collection officers, we were having some 10% of people covered under ESOP policy. That has been extended to now 25%, which is branch manager and above.

items.statement: Overall attrition 37-38%; >1 year tenure attrition 15-17%; ESOP employees <10% attrition
items.quote: If you talk about greater than one year what you asked, I think that the attrition level is in the range of 15% to 17%.

items.statement: PMAY scheme: 18-20% of home loan sourcing in 2021; new scheme disbursements just starting, data entry on portal begun
items.quote: Last time when this scheme came, our home loans particularly because this scheme is largely for home loan, so 18% to 20% of sourcing happened through the help of the scheme particularly when it came in 2021.

items.statement: Undrawn sanction of Rs 450 crore from National Housing Bank
items.quote: We have an undrawn sanction of Rs. 450 crores from National Housing Bank as well.

items.statement: Borrowing profile: ~1/3 repo-linked, ~2/3 MCLR-linked (mostly 1-year reset); rate cut benefits to reflect in 6-8 months
items.quote: Around one-third of the total borrowings are linked to repo rate, which may come down in a quarter period of time. But the larger part of the borrowing is linked to MCLR wherein we will have to remain dependent on when the bank will pass it on.

items.statement: MP portfolio stress stabilizing after team exits; new sales and collection leads in place
items.quote: We have had a new set of people in state. We are talking about Madhya Pradesh particularly. So, our new resource, the lead is there both in sales and collection. And yes, it will take some time to come to correct, but things are large in control.

items.statement: Strong demand in affordable housing in Tier-2/3 cities driven by PMAY II and government initiatives
items.quote: We continue to see strong growth potential in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities particularly for home loans and mortgages because of various government initiatives like PMAY II.

items.statement: Self-employed share increased to ~74% from 70-72% YoY; no material difference in asset quality vs salaried
items.quote: I think self-employed is increasing from year-on-year basis; last year it was around 70%, 72%, today it stands around 74% something in that piece. So, it is improving in that side.

items.statement: BT-outs mainly to larger institutions in Tier-2 markets; in-house retention team engages customers to contain outflows
items.quote: most of these customers, they move to the bigger institution and these BT generally happen in bigg er markets like a Tier-2 market for us in that case, because there's a more intensive competition in those places

items.statement: No fund raise discussed; net worth crossed Rs 2,500 crore
items.quote: Our Networth crossed Rs. 2,500 crores.

items.statement: ROA 5.5%, ROE 15.1% at 2.8x leverage in Q3FY25
items.quote: The ROA for the quarter is stable at 5.5%. ROE for the quarter is 15.1% at a leverage of 2.8 times. It is up by 40 basis points QoQ.

items.statement: 1+ DPD at 7-7.5%, up ~100 bps YoY; expect improvement in Q4 as January collections better than December
items.quote: One plus is around 7% to 7.5%, and Q4 is better normally than the rest of the quarters and we also expect so, as we enter to the new quarter and spend almost 30, 35 days into that piece.

items.statement: On-book yield 14.9%, disbursement yield 15%; expect to maintain spreads at 6% for at least a year
items.quote: We are in a range of 14.9% to 15%. At least for a year or so, we feel that we are going to maintain it. But as time keeps changing, there may be rate cuts or things around that piece. So, we can tweak out. But we consistently try to maintain spreads of 6%.

items.statement: Employee cost split: 60% field, 40% supervisory/head office; 78% executives, 15-18% supervisory, 4-5% head office
items.quote: If you see the cost wise, it is slightly different, overall about 60% of the cost is coming from the field and remaining 40% is coming from the supervisory and the head office.

items.statement: Credit norms reviewed monthly at branch/geography level; tightening measures in MP showing results
items.quote: So, every quarter we review the credit norms, in fact, our credit backgrounds are reviewed month-on-month basis and this is a continuous process. So, instead of tightening a norm at a general Company level, we go a little deeper and we even try to understand what's happening in typical geographies even up to the branch level.

items.statement: Fee income ~1.7-1.8% of average AUM; driven by cross-sell, foreclosure, servicing, application fees; co-lending at 8% of disbursements
items.quote: Broadly it remains at around 1.7% to 1.8% of the total average AUM, and it broadly consists of three, four parameters which include cross-sell, foreclosure income or loan servicing income and loan application fees.

items.statement: Technical write-offs Rs 6 crore in 9MFY25; recovered Rs 4 crore from prior write-offs; ECL provision Rs 61 crore vs regulatory Rs 37 crore
items.quote: During the nine month period, we have done a technical write-off of about Rs. 6-odd crores and parallelly we have also recovered about Rs. 4 crores from the NPAs that we have written off in earlier years.

items.statement: FY25 pre-sales guidance revised to Rs 500-550 crore (residential only)
items.quote: Meanwhile, from a residential-to-residential segment, we are revising our guidance between Rs. 500 crores to Rs. 550 crores.

items.statement: FY25 total revenue guidance Rs 500-520 crore
items.quote: So, overall, for the nine months we have already achieved Rs. 416 crores. So, we are expecting overall for FY '25 Rs. 500 crores to Rs. 520 crores range.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 revenue target Rs 100-110 crore, PAT target Rs 30-35 crore
items.quote: 4th Quarter we are targeting Rs. 100 crores, Rs. 110 crores, which is in line with the overall guidance for FY '25, in line with the overall guidance. And PAT for quarter four will be close to Rs. 100 crores, Rs. 110 crores type we are targeting, overall. Quarter four will be around Rs. 30 crores to Rs. 35 crores we are targeting.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin target 40-45% for FY25
items.quote: So, it would be more of a normalized, in the range of 40% to 45% we are expecting. It also depends upon the revenue being recognized, depends on the work progress. So, accordingly, those will pan out. And the product mix also is an important factor. But we are targeting in the range of 40% to 45%.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin impacted by value luxury mix (62% of revenue) and Rs 15 crore one-time litigation settlement
items.quote: 62% of our total revenue for the quarter was from the value luxury projects like Vitalis, which yielded did lower margins thereby impacting our EBITDA margins for Quarter 3 FY '25. Additionally, higher operating costs further impacted profitability as during the quarter., wee took a one-time fee of Rs. 15 crores to a settlement of a litigation with one of our JDA partners.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 launch pipeline: commercial Rs 1,200 crore GDV + two residential Rs 400 crore GDV = Rs 1,600 crore total
items.quote: To quantify the commercial launches, around Rs. 1,200 crores launch. And the two residential projects are estimated to have Rs. 400 crores of GDV . So, Rs. 1,600 crores of launch we are expecting in the first quarter of next financial year.

items.statement: Ongoing projects inventory ~Rs 300 crore (~50,000 sq ft) remaining
items.quote: Rs. 300 crores is the. Inventory we are estimating which is left in the ongoing development.

items.statement: Strong demand in South Central Mumbai micro-markets (Shivaji Park, Prabhadevi, Tulsi Pipe Road) for both residential and commercial
items.quote: So, the areas which we are operating, we do not feel that we will have any problem in terms of pre-sales because we are at very, very prime locations. So, the launches which we are planning is at Shivaji Park, one at Prabha Devi just behind Siddhivinayak Temple, the third commercial project is on Tulsi Pipe Road which is the main Senapati Bapat. So, we are at landmark locations. The product mix is

items.statement: Q3 pre-sales driven by luxury segment (Palette, Ocean Star) yielding highest-ever realization Rs 64,321/sq ft
items.quote: The quarter that went by witnessed the highest-ever realization of Rs. 64,321, driven primarily by increased sales from luxury projects like Palette and Ocean Star.

items.statement: 9M FY25 realization up 25% YoY to Rs 53,455/sq ft; Q3 realization Rs 64,319/sq ft
items.quote: Realization s grew '25% year-over-year to Rs. 53,455 per square feet from Rs. 42,767 per square feet in nine months FY '24. For the Quarter 3 FY '25, pre-sales stood at 16,656 square feet in terms of area. And in terms of value, pre-sales stood at Rs. 107 crores from which Rs. 5 crores were from the commercial shop sales. Collections stood at Rs. 84 crores and realizations were Rs. 64,319 per squa

items.statement: Acquired adjacent land parcel on Tulsi Pipe Road, increasing commercial project GDV from Rs 475 crore to Rs 1,200 crore
items.quote: A key milestone in this journey has been the acquisition of the land just adjacent to our existing land parcel on Tulsi Pipe Road, significantly strengthening our development potential in this prime location.
