items.statement: Paddy inventory 341,000 tons, rice inventory 458,000 tons as of Dec 31, 2024
items.quote: On a volume basis, as of December 31, 2024, paddy and rice inventory stood at 341,000 tons and 458,000 tons, respectively, compared to 491,000 tons of paddy and 395,000 tons of rice in December '2023.

items.statement: Net debt sharply reduced to INR 92 crores as of Dec 31, 2024 from INR 901 crores YoY
items.quote: One of the standard highlights in the quarter is a sharp reduction in net debt, which now stands at INR 92 crores as of December 31 , '2024, down from INR 901 crores last year.

items.statement: Finance cost lower at INR 1.2 crores vs INR 7.5 crores YoY due to lower borrowings
items.quote: Finance cost for the quarter was lower at INR 1.2 crores as against INR 7.5 crores due to lower borrowings.

items.statement: Government removed minimum export price of $950/MT for basmati in Sept 2024
items.quote: In September 2024, the Government of India removed the minimum ex port price of $950 per metric ton for basmati rice exports.

items.statement: Market share gains: General trade +360 bps to 38.2%, Modern trade +140 bps to 42.3%, E-commerce +470 bps to 42.8%
items.quote: In general trade, we have gained 360 basis points to reach a 38.2% market share. In modern t rade, our market share grew by 140 basis points to reach 42.3% levels. And in e -commerce, we gained a dominant 470 basis points to achieve 42.8%.

items.statement: Household penetration increased 400 bps YoY
items.quote: Additionally, our household penetration in India has increased by 400 basis points compared to the same quarte r last year, further cementing our leadership in the market.

items.statement: Launched Uplife health brand with edible oils (Lite and Gut Pro variants)
items.quote: A landmark development this quarter has been the launch of our new health-focused brand, Uplife. Uplife embodies the philosophy of Live Life Unbound and serves as our entry into the rapidly growing health and wellness space. Our first foray is into the healthy e dible oils category launched in 2 variants: Uplife Lite for weight management and Uplife Gut Pro for gut health.

items.statement: Lost market share to Pakistan during export curbs; confident of recovery via brand positioning and competitive pricing
items.quote: However, India lost some market share to Pakistan during the period of export curbs. We are confident that lost market share will be recovered through strong brand positioning and competitive pricing.

items.statement: Next year basmati production estimated 10% lower; prices unlikely to fall further
items.quote: Next year, the production according to our estimate, would be lesser by 10% over this year. So this is the right price. We feel that this price in basmati rice will not come again.

items.statement: No inventory loss expected despite paddy price decline; 95% crop already procured
items.quote: No, there is no inventory loss. We are regularly buying. there's no question, 95% of paddy has already come. And we are selling on the basis of our inventory valuation only. There's no question of any inventory loss.

items.statement: Healthy edible oil market size ~INR 1,800 crores, growing >20% YoY
items.quote: Healthy edible oil market size i s around INR 1,800 crores per annum and is growing at more than 20% year-over-year.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target of Rs 2,200 crore deferred by at least one year to FY27
items.quote: I think 3 -4 years back, we have put the target. And due to some delays, what we are seeing from the EV OEMs. So, maybe that we need to post by at least one year.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 gross margin fell 543 bps YoY to 45.81% due to adverse mix and new plant fixed costs
items.quote: The gross margin for the quarter came at 45.81% marking a decline of 543 basis points from 51.24% in Quarter 3 of FY24.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin dropped to 9% from 13% YoY; management expects sequential recovery
items.quote: The EBITDA was Rs. 35 crore compared to Rs. 53 crore in Quarter 3 of FY24, with a margin of 9% versus 13% in Quarter 3 last year.

items.statement: Upfront costs for new EV projects and automation ~Rs 4-5 crore in Q3; expected to decline in Q4
items.quote: It is a decent amount because approximately we can say that it is in the range of Rs. 4 crore to Rs. 5 crore that we have lost for the development of the new projects.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 capex Rs 42 crore; 9M FY25 capex ~Rs 140 crore; Q4 FY25 capex expected Rs 20-25 crore
items.quote: Our capital expenditure for Quarter 3 stood at Rs. 42 crore while for nine months of FY25, it was around Rs. 140 crore with investments directed towards machinery and new product development. For Quarter 4, we expect further CAPEX of around Rs. 20 crore to Rs. 25

items.statement: EV parts development capex to add Rs 250-300 crore capacity over next two years
items.quote: So, that I think this major CAPEX is going on for the EV parts that developments are going on and hopefully because this will give additional approximately Rs. 250 crore to Rs. 300 crore in that range of additional capacity in the next coming two years.

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs 9,000 crore as of today; Q3 added 7 parts worth ~Rs 500 crore
items.quote: So, Yash, our order book is around Rs. 9,000 crore as on today. So, we have added in this quarter also the 7 parts which is almost Rs. 500 crore turnover from the new order.

items.statement: Order book covers next 5 years till FY29 based on current run-rate
items.quote: Yes, it is for 5 years, till 2028-29.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 revenue Rs 393 crore down 3% YoY; export weakness in Europe and customer-specific disruptions
items.quote: Revenues for Quarter 3 FY25 stood at Rs. 393 crore compared to Rs. 406 crore in Quarter 3 FY24. Top -line was impacted by subdued demand in key export markets with severe weakness in Europe.

items.statement: 9M FY25 revenue Rs 1,298 crore up 14% YoY
items.quote: For the 9 -month period, total revenue stood at Rs. 1,298 crore up 14% from the Rs. 1,142 crore in 9 months FY24.

items.statement: Global auto volumes fell 4.6% YoY in Q3; Europe -5%, North America -4.5%; India +6.6%
items.quote: In Q3 FY25, Global Auto Industry witnessed 4.6% YOY degrowth in volumes. Within this, Europe volume declined by 5% and North America by 4.5% respectively.

items.statement: No single customer >20% of turnover; balanced portfolio
items.quote: No, Faisal. We have a very balanced customer portfolio and right now none of our customers contributes more than 20% of our turnover.

items.statement: Japanese OEM hybrid volumes to rise ~80% over next 2 years post Q3 plant shutdown
items.quote: After the plant shutdown in Quarter 3, we anticipate the volume to pick up in Quarter 4. In fact, over the next two years, the expectation is that the monthly supplies of cylinder heads will increase by roughly 80%.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 average capacity utilisation 70-75%; new plants in ramp-up phase
items.quote: Yes, Jyoti, currently we are running if we specifically see Quarter 3, so we are running at the capacity of around 70% -75%.

items.statement: Exports 24% of revenue in 9M FY25 vs 28% YoY; Europe 65-70% of exports, USA 30-35%; Europe decline sharper
items.quote: If you see Europe and the UK, they contribute almost 65% to 70% of our exports and 30% -35% is USA, but if you see in the decline side, so we have seen more decline in Europe as compared to the USA.

items.statement: Aluminium prices up over 3-4 years; value addition not keeping pace, compressing gross margins structurally
items.quote: Mainly, the raw material cost is going up when you see comparison for the last 3-4 years. So, when you are talking about from FY2021, the prices of aluminum have gone up, but not the value additions have not grown in the same proportion.

items.statement: ROCE improving continuously over last 4-5 years; Q3 worst quarter but recovery expected
items.quote: Progress is going on, maybe if you see year-on-year, last 4-5 years. So, there is a continuous improvement in the ROCE and definitely this is on and quarter -on-quarter basis, maybe this is the worst quarter we have seen in this Quarter 3, but after that you can easily see that there is continuous improvement in the ROCE.

items.statement: Tariff war uncertainty in US; India-US relations may benefit but clarity needed in 1-2 months
items.quote: We are also keeping our fingers crossed. We are seeing with lots of things right now that tariff war is going on, new tariffs on some countries that is going on. Hopefully, India has a good relationship with the US, so hopefully we should be benefited.

items.statement: EV demand weak globally and in India; recovery expected in 1-2 years
items.quote: Yes, so as you know, the EV is not doing good globally. You know that we have taken lots of new order from the EV and currently we are seeing the demand is not very good in India and also on the export market. But we are very hopeful that in 1 or 2 years, the demand should pick up.

items.statement: Q3 marked bottom for revenue and margins; sequential improvement expected from Q4 FY25 into FY26
items.quote: We also believe the Quarter 3 marked the bottom of the cyclicity in the industry and that there will be an improvement in export markets of Europe and US as well as an enhanced demand environment in India. This will ensure that our revenue and margins performance will improve going forward, starting with sequential improvement in Quarter 4 and further building up into FY26.

items.statement: Revenue growth faster than 30% FY25 guidance; maintain 22-23% CAGR for music vertical medium term; consolidated PBT to double in 3-4 years; annual adjusted EBITDA guidance 32-33% excluding live events spikes; PBT modest growth this year the
items.quote: Our revenue has seen substantial growth faster than our guidance of 30% revenue increase for FY '25.

items.statement: Invest over INR 1,000 crores in new music content between FY25-FY27; INR 500 crores already secured; five-year payback period maintained with 55-75 years of returns thereafter
items.quote: Between FY '25 to FY '27, we will be investing over INR 1,000 crores in new music content. Of this amount of INR 1,000 crores, content worth INR 500 crores has already been secured.

items.statement: Q3 adjusted EBITDA fell to 21% due to 58% revenue from low-margin live events (INR 279 cr revenue, INR 22 cr profit); excluding events adjusted EBITDA maintained at healthy 40%; annual guidance 32-33% excluding live events spikes
items.quote: Our disproportionate 58% of this quarter's revenue has come through events, which, as I have said in the past, is a low margin percentage business. To put it in perspective, INR. 279 crores came from live events with INR. 22 crores profit. This disproportionate share of live events has resulted in adjusted EBITDA falling to 21%.

items.statement: Video business expected to deliver high single-digit EBITDA margins; Carvaan margins to improve as retail transitions to e-commerce; live events margins at best high single digits but high IRR due to short capital lock-in (30-90 days)
items.quote: So, the video business should be able to give you high single digits margin percentages. Again, the great thing about the video business is that if you play it properly, the IRRs are far higher because you do not end up investing a lot of your own money in the movie.

items.statement: Music licensing grew ~20% YoY; YouTube revenue growth maintained; audio streaming moving toward paid subscription wall with Airtel Wynk shutdown leaving only 2 free platforms expected to turn paid in 4-5 quarters; publishing business growin
items.quote: Let me start as always with the music business, which comprises of licensing and artist management. It grew by close to 20% on a year-on-year basis. Our revenues from YouTube maintained their growth trajectory.

items.statement: Released ~1,200 original/premium recreation songs across 9 languages in Q3; aggressive content release of INR 235 crores in 9M FY25; full year content investment upwards of INR 300 crores; forayed into hip-hop via MTV Hustle Season 4 acquir
items.quote: The nine months of this year have seen the most aggressive content release ever from Saregama. We released close to Rs. 235 crores worth of content which include content cost and relevant marketing over the nine months.

items.statement: Music line-up for next 12 months secured including major films: Maddock's Sky Force, Thama, Mammootty's Bazooka, Dharma's Sarzameen, Sanjay Leela Bhansali's Love and War; target 25-30% market share of new music releases to double licensing
items.quote: Our line-up for the next 12 months is all in place. We will have music from some of the biggest films of the year. This includes Maddock's Sky Force, which got released in the month of January, Maddock's next movie called Thama, Mammootty's Bazooka, Dharma's Sarzameen, Sanjay Leela Bhansali's Love and War etc.

items.statement: Content investment charge-off 29% higher YoY in Q3; transitional phase where incremental revenue matches charge-off for next 4 quarters; then content investment grows linearly and revenue exceeds charge-off from year 3; 36% of new content c
items.quote: This quarter, the charge-off on account of the new content was 29% higher than the same quarter last year. We are in a transitional state currently, where our new content expenses are going up in a step fashion, resulting in incremental revenue just about matching the content charge-off.

items.statement: Artist management roster now ~200 artists; added Tony Kakkar (8M followers) and Rehaan Roy (6M followers) in Q3; music artists becoming sought-after brand ambassadors (e.g., Diljit Dosanjh); digital advertising growing 15%+ benefiting influ
items.quote: During this quarter, two big artists got added to our roster, Tony Kakkar with an 8 million follower base, and Rehaan Roy with a 6 million follower base. Overall, we now manage around 200 artists.

items.statement: Digital footprint of owned channels grew from under 300M to 324M followers across YouTube, Instagram, Facebook; Stree 2 songs generating 10M additional streams daily (1.9B YouTube views, 450M Spotify streams in 6 months); Amaran biggest Tam
items.quote: I am very happy to share that the digital footprint of Saregama owned and controlled channels, which were under 300 million as of last quarter, have grown up to 324 million followers across YouTube, Instagram, and Facebook.

items.statement: Board declared interim dividend of Rs. 4.5 per share
items.quote: Lastly, I am pleased to share that the Board has declared an interim dividend of Rs. 4.5 per share.

items.statement: Audio streaming industry transitioning from free to paid model; 4 of 8 platforms (Gaana, Hungama, Resso, Airtel Wynk) shut or went paid in last 18 months; minimum guarantees lost but customers migrating to paid tiers or other free platforms
items.quote: Over the last 18 months or so, four of the platforms have either shut shop or have gone completely behind the paid wall. Gaana and Hungama have gone fully behind the paid wall, while Resso and Airtel Wynk have shut shop.

items.statement: Live events performance (Diljit tour) may not repeat every quarter; Carvaan retail revenue fell 39% YoY to INR 22 crores; video business had quiet quarter with no movie releases and one unsold movie charged off as non-cash expense; employee
items.quote: This quarter saw the retail revenue of Rs. 22 crores, which was a 39% drop over the last year.

items.statement: Pocket Aces integration ongoing; targeting breakeven by end of FY25; employee costs as % of revenue stable at 11-12% excluding bonus quarter and live events denominator effect; management hiring from FMCG/consumer durables/services for dive
items.quote: We are reasonably confident that we will be able to get them to breakeven or very close to breakeven, as promised earlier, by the end of the financial year.

items.statement: Live events vertical scaling with dedicated team; IP-based shows (Javed Akhtar, Zeenat Aman, Say Cheese Grandpa kids musicals) alongside artist tours; exploring international tours and collaborations; treated as #1 live events producer in I
items.quote: We are also developing in parallel IP-based shows, which are independent of an individual artist, but the IP becomes bigger. Like this series that we have, where in we get a big Bollywood star of yesteryears, who tells us the stories of his or her movies and the songs behind it.

items.statement: Content acquisition via data-driven predictive models; 80% content / 20% marketing split; five-year payback guideline adhered to; outperforming 5-year payback over last 4 years; never pay 40-50% of film cost for music rights
items.quote: So, the entire money that we are spending on the content acquisition and the marketing cost that is incurred on the content. Typically, our ratios are INR80 on content and INR20 on marketing. So, if I spend INR100 without loading the cost, without factoring the time value of money we will recover these INR100 over the next five years.

items.statement: Higher hit ratio than competitors across all languages due to data-driven acquisition; market share growing in all major languages (now #1 or #2); entered Chhattisgarhi and achieved #1 position; only music label with integrated live events
items.quote: You will see Saregama's market share going up across all languages. We have one language where we are relatively weak and one language that we have not entered ourselves into. Apart from that, in every major language, you will see us either at the number one or number two position.

items.statement: FY25 turnover guidance revised to INR 3,200-3,500 crores depending on change order finalization
items.quote: At this moment, we are working with our clients for some change orders. And till the time change orders are finalized, we are expecting to remain same billing turnover of the last year, around INR3,200 crores, INR2,500 crores. And in case we are able to finalize our change order, then definitely, we are going to hit the figure of INR3,500 crores.

items.statement: All-time high order book of INR 11,353 crores as of Dec 31, 2024
items.quote: The company has an all-time high order book of INR11,353 crores, comprising under Consultancy segment of INR 5,554 crores and under LSTK segment of INR5,799 crores, as on 31st December 2024.

items.statement: Consultancy segment profit ~20%, LSTK segment profit ~5-6%
items.quote: In the EPCM job, we are having a segment profit of around 20%. And in the LSTK jobs, our segment profit is around 5% to 6%.

items.statement: Operating margin increased to 11% in Q3 from 7% in Q2
items.quote: This resulted in operating margin incr eased to 11% in December '24 quarter from 7% in September '24 quarter.

items.statement: Targeting all upcoming projects in India, confident of sustaining order inflow growth
items.quote: Yes, definitely, we are sure. We are targeting all the projects which are coming in India. And we are very sure we will be technical consultant of all the clients, favorite consultant of all the clients in the future also.

items.statement: NRL investment of INR 835 crores total (INR 700 crores + INR 135 crores), INR 35 crores pending
items.quote: We have made INR700 crores plus INR135 crores is the additional investment. Out of that, we have paid, I think INR 100 crores we already around INR 34 crores, INR 35 crores recently we paid.

items.statement: Order book execution timeline 3-4 years for large projects
items.quote: These projects are bigger in size. Generally, they are being executed in 3 to 4 years. Unless there is some short job, which may be completed in 1 year or so. Generally, bigger projects are completed 3 to 4 years.

items.statement: IOCL Paradip PMC-1 awarded, PMC-2 (~INR 700 crores) expected in weeks
items.quote: The PM package 1 on has been awarded to us recently, I think last week, it has been awarded to us. And package number two is expected to be awarded in next couple of weeks.

items.statement: BPCL Andhra petrochemical complex initial studies underway, major tender next FY
items.quote: Initially, it would be initial studies, pre-project activities and all those things activities will be there. Later on, it would be the major tender would come, but not in this quarter itself. It should come somewhere in the next financial year or towards the end of this quarter.

items.statement: CPCL Nagapattinam expansion on hold due to land issues
items.quote: It's -- I think the project is kind of on hold because of the land issues. So, we are yet to hear from them further decision on the project from the IOCL side and CPCL side.

items.statement: Consultancy order book target INR 8,000-8,500 crores, currently INR 5,554 crores
items.quote: In the previous conference call, you had said that the order book in Consultancy segment is expected to reach about INR8,000 crores to INR8,500 crores.

items.statement: Consultancy revenue recognition: 5-7% year 1, ~35% years 2-3
items.quote: Around 36 to 40 months. So, during the first year, the revenue recognition 5% to 7% and in the second and third year, the revenue recognition is around 35%.

items.statement: Abu Dhabi office doing well with ADNOC assignments, targeting Middle East growth
items.quote: But definitely, with respect to the overseas business like our Abu Dhabi office is doing pretty well. They are doing a lot of assignments, engineering assignments. They have been getting a lot of projects, engineering -- midsized consultancy projects from the ADNOC group of companies in the Offshore segment and the Onshore oil and gas segment in the refinery and petrochemical segment.

items.statement: International consultancy order inflow ~INR 40-50 crores per project, multiple midsized projects
items.quote: Around INR40 crores, INR 50 crores each. So, there will be many such projects accumulated many such projects. It will be midsized projects, totally accumulated and they add to the book business for -- apart from that, there are certain projects, major projects are also EPCM projects are also in the bidding phase.

items.statement: Expanding beyond hydrocarbons into infrastructure (44% of segment), metallurgy, coal gasification, green hydrogen, data centers
items.quote: You must have seen the infrastructure has grown from earlier 25% to 44% in this segment. So, we're getting a lot of assignments in the infrastructure segment also. So, all the segments would be contributing in these efforts.

items.statement: Government approved incentives for coal gasification projects, bidding underway
items.quote: We are bidding for the upcoming coal gasification projects wherein the government has given some -- approved the incentives for the upcoming coal gasification projects, which are there on the anvil. So, we'll be targeting those.

items.statement: West Coast Refinery future uncertain, may not proceed or split into two refineries
items.quote: West Coast Refinery, we do not know the future of it because we have been hearing like it's always published in the paper that may not come. They might decide to go for two refineries at two different locations. So, we don't see any future at this point of time for this refinery.

items.statement: Cash on books ~INR 1,000 crores at end of Q3
items.quote: Cash is around INR1000 crores.

items.statement: Expect substantial turnover increase in FY26, FY27 from strong order book execution
items.quote: So going forward in the financial year '26, '27, there will be a substantial increase in the turnover. We are expecting an increase in the turnover.

items.statement: 9M FY25 order inflow ~INR 7,000 crores, ~130% growth vs 9M FY24
items.quote: First question on the order inflow, which we have received during the 9 months is close to INR 7,000 crores compared to -- which is almost 130% growth compared to 9-month period of last year.

items.statement: Bina and Kochi refinery expansions expected within 1 year
items.quote: There are two refineries who are sort of thinking of expanding -- thinking of going for the expansion in the times to come. So that would definitely happen within 1 year time. The Bina refinery and the Kochi refinery, both of them would be expanding.

items.statement: Oil-to-chemical projects: 4-5 feasibility studies ongoing, 2-3 expected to materialize in a year
items.quote: There are 4, 5 such kind of projects and studies are on. At least 2 or 3 should realize, and 2 or 3 should be materialized in the times to come in a years' time.

items.statement: Successfully winning competitive bids despite being a Government of India company
items.quote: We are very much competitive. We are bidding very -- despite being the -- facing various challenges being the Government of India -- company, but still, we are getting the jobs on competition basis and very successfully getting those assignments.

items.statement: Focus on employee productivity improvement and brand visibility enhancement
items.quote: Management has put in a lot of focus on the new sectors, new areas, improvement of efficiency of the working productivity of the employees. All these segments, we have been focusing not only on the business, all the fronts, new technology initiatives, visibility of company as a brand in the market.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target over 6% for FY25 and 7-8% for FY26
items.quote: We see from this year, as we begin the quarter Q4, Jan to March, the impact of GPI which will start coming in, which is already rolled out, and we see the EBITDA margin ending in the year over 6%.

items.statement: Revenue growth target 8-10% from FY25 onwards, 10% above market growth
items.quote: We see ourselves growing it in the range of 8 to 10% from this year onwards. If you see FY '25 onwards, we see ourselves growing at 8-10%.

items.statement: Gross margin target 27% for FY25 and 29% by FY27
items.quote: So, we are right now at 26.2 for 9 months. So, we, for the current year itself, we are looking at 27. So, as you said, 29% for '27 is very much in sight and very much doable.

items.statement: Capex of Rs 11 crore spent so far in FY25, budget of Rs 15 crore for FY25 and Rs 20 crore for FY26
items.quote: So, we had done a CAPEX of 11 crores so far. There is small CAPEX which could complete the 15 crore budget for the current year. Next year also we are keeping a budget of 20 crore CAPEX.

items.statement: Opened new surface transshipment center in Vijayawada; plan to open 8 new hubs by end of FY26
items.quote: On the infrastructure front, I am pleased to share that during the quarter, we have opened our new surface transshipment center in Vijaywada, and we plan to open eight new hubs by the end of Financial Year 2026.

items.statement: 8 of 21 large STCs renovated; 6-7 more to be upgraded in next 12 months
items.quote: And we have now renovated of the 21 large Surface Transshipment Centers we have across the country, 8 have been renovated with the upgradation of infrastructure, newer sites, more cross docking bays, dock levelers, MHE machines. And in the next 12 months, we have identified 6 to 7 such STCs to further upgrade them.

items.statement: General Price Increase (GPI) rolled out; single-digit realization so far, improving month-on-month through March and into June
items.quote: As of today, we have realized a single-digit GPI realization, and that will improve month-on-month into March, and as I said, month-on-month into June.

items.statement: Express business gross margin improved 340 bps YoY to 25% in Q3 FY25; 9-month gross margin 26.2% vs 24% YoY
items.quote: Corresponding gross margin has improved by over 340 bps year-on-year and stands at 25% for Q3 FY '25 as compared to 21.7% for the quarter ended December 2023.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 4.8% in Q3 FY25 vs 1.6% YoY; 9-month Express EBITDA margin 5.4% vs 3.5% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margin for Q3 FY '25 stood at 4.8% as against 1.6% during Q3 FY '24 on consolidated basis.

items.statement: Highest ever volume in Q3 FY25; Express tonnage 331,000 MT in Q3 FY25 vs 319,000 MT YoY and 313,000 MT QoQ
items.quote: Another milestone that I would like to highlight here is that Allcargo Gati has registered its highest ever volume in the quarter ended of December 2024.

items.statement: Average DSO reduced to 68 days in Q3 FY25, lowest since Q1 FY24, down from 74 days YoY
items.quote: We are able to reduce our average DSO to 68 days in Q3 FY '25 which is lowest in since Q1 FY '24. For the last quarter of the similar corresponding year, our DSO was 74 days.

items.statement: Sold one fuel pump in Belagavi for Rs 3 crore; process underway to sell remaining two
items.quote: In line with our strategy to exit non-core businesses during the quarter, we have announced the sale of one of our fuel pumps in Belagavi for a realization of 3 crores. We are in the process of selling the remaining two fuel pumps.

items.statement: Quick commerce B2B business growing very strongly with three large players; FMCG only single-digit contributor
items.quote: Yes, very good growth. We are growing much higher than the growth of the market. We operate with the large three quick commerce players who deliver shipments to your homes. So, that business is growing very, very strongly.

items.statement: MSME and retail client mix improvement delayed due to MSME stress; cautious approach until macro improves
items.quote: You will also be very, very cognizant of the fact that MSMEs are under a lot o f stress because of the, you know, environment that we have on the front and because of that stress, we are kind of approaching them with a little bit of caution and sensitivity

items.statement: Organized sector gaining share from unorganized due to formalization (e-way bill, GST); no real dent from unorganized sector
items.quote: So, we are seeing that swing happening from unorganized to the organized market. So, we are very happy that that is the situation we are currently in. So, no real competition or impact or dent from the unorganized sector on the organized.

items.statement: Express logistics market expected to grow at 11% CAGR to 2029; company targets 8-10% growth
items.quote: So, 2-3 years, the market is expected, this Express business market I think is slated to grow at 11% from current year onwards to, let's say, 2029, if you see.

items.statement: Oracle Fusion ERP live; full modules go-live from July 1, 2025
items.quote: Another milestone we achieved on the ERP front where our Oracle Fusion ERP is up and live and which will finally go live from 1st July from all the modules point out.

items.statement: MSME stress and inflation impacting retail/MSME acquisition pace; GPI tail extends to June due to RFQ cycles
items.quote: MSMEs are under a lot o f stress because of the, you know, environment that we have on the front and because of that stress, we are kind of approaching them with a little bit of caution and sensitivity

items.statement: Capex for current year will be lower than FY2024 and continue to unwind in FY2026
items.quote: We believe that our capex for the current year will be lower than FY2024, and this will continue to unwind in FY2026.

items.statement: Q3 capex was Rs 6,860 crore; rolled out 5,214 sites and 13,950 route km of fiber
items.quote: Capex for the quarter was 6860 Crores. We rolled out 5214 network sites and over 13,950 route kilometers of fiber in the quarter.

items.statement: Radio capex has decelerated significantly and will continue to decelerate next year; transport, homes, B2B and data centers remain key capex areas
items.quote: Radio, which has been a substantial part of our capex. This one has decelerated very, very significantly, and we expect it to continue to decelerate next year.

items.statement: Planning to transfer ~16,100 towers (12,700 from Airtel, 3,400 from Hexacom) to Indus Towers
items.quote: we are planning to transfer about 16,100 telecom towers, approximately 12,700 from Bharti Airtel and about 3400 from Bharti Hexacom to Indus Towers.

items.statement: Hexacom EBITDA margin 53% (+300 bps QoQ); EBITDAaL margin 46.3%
items.quote: EBITDA stood at Rs.1194 Crores with EBITDA margin of 53% improving by almost 300 bps. EBITDAaL, which is the new terminology that we have introduced, and the right one to monitor the organization’s performance, for the quarter was 1042 Crores with a margin of 46.3

items.statement: Airtel Business revenue ~Rs 5,650 crore, up 8.7% YoY
items.quote: Airtel Business we delivered revenue of just under 5650 Crores. This is a growth of 8.7% over the same period last year.

items.statement: ARPU rose to Rs 245 from Rs 233 QoQ; drivers: feature-to-smartphone, prepaid-to-postpaid, data monetization, international roaming
items.quote: ARPU came in at Rs.245 compared to 233 last quarter; another quarter of industry leading growth. ARPU drivers on an underlying basis remain intact; these are basically feature phone to smartphone upgrades, prepaid to postpaid upgrades, data monetization, and growth of international roaming.

items.statement: Hexacom ARPU grew 5.7% QoQ to Rs 241
items.quote: The company delivered another quarter of industry leading ARPU growth of 5.7% to reach 241.

items.statement: 5G base reached 120M; 5G handsets >80% of smartphone shipments
items.quote: We ended the quarter with a 5G base of 120 million, 5G shipments continue to grow now contributing over 80% of overall smartphone shipments and we continue to get our fair share from growing 5G handset adoption.

items.statement: Airtel Finance: 1M+ customers served, Rs 4,600 crore disbursed, AUM Rs 2,500 crore; Payments Bank: 87M monthly transacting users, ARR ~Rs 2,800 crore (+50% YoY), deposits Rs 3,300 crore (+42% YoY)
items.quote: Airtel Finance has served over a million customers till date across various financial products with over 4600 Crores of total disbursement and a current AUM of 2500 Crores. On the Payments Bank, the monthly transacting users stood at 87 million, annualized revenue run rate now is about 2800 Crores, growing at 50% year-on-year. Deposits remain robust at over 3300 Crores growing by 42% year-on-year.

items.statement: Partnered with Bajaj Finance to create large digital financial services platform; Airtel to offer Bajaj's 27 product lines on Thanks App and stores
items.quote: To increase supply, we partnered with Bajaj Finance to create one of India's largest digital platforms for financial services. The partnership combines Airtel's digital platforms and omni-channel capabilities with Bajaj Finance portfolio of 27 product lines and strong underwriting strength.

items.statement: Operating free cash flow (EBITDAaL minus capex) Rs 9,440 crore in Q3
items.quote: We delivered strong operating free cash flow; this is really EBITDAaL minus capex of 9440 Crores.

items.statement: Free cash flow to be used for deleveraging, step-up in dividend, and selective prudent M&A/bolt-on acquisitions
items.quote: Opportunities for free cash flow, I think, will be some amount of deleveraging, which will continue as you also pointed out. There will be a step-up of dividend for sure and that is a second area of free cash flow and the third, we will be selective and very prudent in any investments we make.

items.statement: ARPU still lowest globally; further tariff repair needed for industry financial stability
items.quote: Finally, I want to underscore that ARPU in India continues to be the lowest globally. Tariff repair is needed some more for the industry to be financially stable and deliver reasonable returns on a sustained basis.

items.statement: Exceptional charge of Rs 1,400 crore in Hexacom from periodic asset/liability review; provision for regulatory dues; one-time, no cash payout
items.quote: Well as any other organization, there is a periodic review of the carrying value of various assets and liabilities, so in that review, it was felt that there is a provision which has to be taken. There were also some reversals on account of the recent court judgement on passive infrastructure, it is a combination of this. There is no cash payout or anything of that sort.

items.statement: FWA ready on SA architecture; can launch immediately; currently on NSA; thousands of customers tested for 3-4 months
items.quote: we have already tested fully the SA solution for FWA, we have proven it, and given the empty network, we are not seeing any uplink differentiation. Secondly, we are fully ready to launch FWA, like if it can be done tomorrow morning, we can do it tomorrow morning if we want to and so, we will do it at the point that we need to.

items.statement: Transport blueprint accelerated over last 2 years; using fiber nodes, FTTH, and E-band microwave; now largely caught up with blueprint
items.quote: about two years back, we created a five year transport blueprint and all we are doing is trying to accelerate that blueprint. For the last two years the only effort has been to say do more, do more, do more so that that blueprint is actually met. We are not yet in line with exactly where that blueprint is, but every month in the last eight quarters, every quarter we have made progress and we are n

items.statement: EBITDAaL introduced as key metric: Q3 consolidated EBITDAaL Rs 16,306 crore at 49.3% margin; Hexacom EBITDAaL Rs 1,042 crore at 46.3% margin
items.quote: We are now reporting EBITDAaL, which is EBITDA after lease obligations. We believe this is a true reflection of our underlying margin and leverage. As a management team, this is a metric we track so as to drive the right behavior about the underlying health of the business. EBITDAaL for the quarter stood at 16,306 Crores with a margin of 49.3%.

items.statement: Gaana expected to break even in next 4 to 5 quarters
items.quote: As Gaana revenues continue to scale, losses are narrowing, reinforcing our expectation that the business will likely break even in the next 4 to 5 quarters.

items.statement: Full impact of Gaana price revision to reflect from FY26
items.quote: Since our pricing plans follow our annual subscription model, we expect the full impact of the price revision to reflect from FY '26 onwards.

items.statement: Radio volumes down 3% YoY due to shorter festive season and weak economy
items.quote: The volumes have gone down by about 3% over last year. And that comes from a point of view, that there was a shorter festive season.

items.statement: Overall ad sales muted across media; shift to experiential marketing
items.quote: If you look at the market factors also, there is a shift in media, which is moving towards more experiential marketing rather than advertising sales.

items.statement: EBITDA excluding digital at INR38.8 crores with 28% margin
items.quote: EBITDA excluding digital stood at INR38.8 crores with EBITDA margins at a healthy 28%.

items.statement: Margin pressure due to product mix shift from radio to events
items.quote: It's a product mix change. If you do more events and less radio , , radio is more profitable than any other business.

items.statement: Concerts have lower margins than managed events
items.quote: If you look at the media business or the experiential business, the concerts will generally have a less margin compared to managed events.

items.statement: Non-FCT segment grew 21% YoY to INR50 crores driven by events
items.quote: On the other hand, the non -FCT segment witnessed strong momentum, growing 21% year -on-year to INR50 crores.

items.statement: Digital revenue INR15.4 crores, up 151% YoY; Gaana revenue INR12.6 crores
items.quote: Our digital business continued to deliver exceptional growth with revenue reaching INR15.4 crores, up by 151% year-on-year, largely fuelled by the strong performance of Gaana.

items.statement: Gaana annual pack price increased from INR299 to INR599 in July 2024
items.quote: As you may recall, we launched an updated version of Gaana in July 2024 with a revised pricing moving from INR299 to INR599 for our annual pack pricing.

items.statement: Radio yields flat QoQ but 25% below pre-COVID levels
items.quote: So, on overall radio yield on quarter-on-quarter, we're almost about flat. But pre-COVID level, as I said, it's about 25% down.

items.statement: Radio revenue at 75-80% of pre-COVID levels
items.quote: So, if I just compare radio to radio, it could be about 75% to 80% of pre-COVID levels.

items.statement: Invested INR10.5 crores in digital during quarter, down 26% from Q1
items.quote: We remain committed to strengthening our digital offerings, investing INR10.5 crores during the quarter, which is almost 26% down over Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Gaana cash burn INR10 crores in Q3, 25% less than Q1
items.quote: So, this quarter, we burned about INR10-odd crores, which is almost 25% less than what we spent in Q1.

items.statement: Radio utilization 71% (11 minutes/hour inventory); significant headroom
items.quote: It's about 71% the way we count, but at an inventory level, it's about 11 minutes an hour. So, there's a lot of volume available on that for us.

items.statement: Radio 63% of total revenue YTD vs 71% last year; digital 26% of radio revenue
items.quote: At YTD levels, radio contributes to 63% of our total revenues compared to almost 71% last year.

items.statement: Auto, jewellery, health/pharma performed well; real estate, consumer durables, apparel weak
items.quote: I would say auto has done well relatively because of last year impact. Last year, auto was not doing so well. So, from a base point of view, automobile and health and pharma has done reasonably well plus the jewellery section.

items.statement: Radio maintains 27% market share; Gaana competes with Spotify in paid market
items.quote: However, pricing remained stable, and we continue to maintain our revenue leadership position in the segment with a healthy 27% market share.

items.statement: Gaana paid subscriber growth ~15% YTD; blended ARPU ~INR300
items.quote: At YTD levels, our paid subscriber growth has been healthy and in the range of approximately 15%.

items.statement: Gaana paid market share increasing quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: Our paid market share is also increasing quarter -on-quarter.

items.statement: Cash balance INR344 crores as of Dec 31, 2024
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains strong with a cash balance of INR344 crores as of December 31, 2024.

items.statement: Consistent dividend policy; will evaluate payout now that Gaana stabilizing
items.quote: The way we look at it is, for us, we have been consistent on the dividend policy from day 1 for every year-on-year.

items.statement: Ad sales model in transition across media; vanilla advertising muted
items.quote: The overall ad sales business is going through a shift, it is in a transition phase, and we'll have to weather that storm.

items.statement: Management expects next financial year to be better than current year
items.quote: We are cautiously optimistic that the positive cycle for the textile sector may start in the next financial year.

items.statement: Spinning capacity utilization at 97% for 9 months FY25 vs 91% last year
items.quote: Our spinning capacity used in current 9 months was 97% against 91% in the corresponding period.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin 42% in Q3 FY25, up 4% YoY; EBITDA INR7 cr vs -INR1 cr YoY
items.quote: For Q3 '25, our consolidated total income came in at INR658 crores. Gross margin was at 42%, which was higher by 4% on a year-on-year basis. EBITDA is at INR7 crores from minus INR1 crore for the corresponding period.

items.statement: EBITDA margins low due to demand-supply mismatch; expected to improve when demand emerges
items.quote: And that should keep on improving going forward. But the demand has to emerge and for which we are optimistic.

items.statement: Shifting mix from apparel to non-apparel; adding value-added products like lycra twisted and core spin yarns
items.quote: We are changing product mix to some extent like from apparel to non-apparel, we are increasing. We are going in value-added products like lycra twisted yarn and lycra core spin yarn.

items.statement: Spent INR50 cr this year on automation and modernization in dyed yarn
items.quote: This year also we have spent INR50 crores for different types of automation and other things which can be possible and something like that.

items.statement: Recycled fiber unit running at 110% capacity (130 t/day vs 120 t/day); Q3 production 12,000 tons
items.quote: 120 tonnes/day, whereas we have produced 130 tonnes/day. But the point here is that basically this unit was set up for captive consumption to have the better quality of yarn because otherwise, when we used to purchase from outside, there used to be variation in the supply of the fiber. So that was basically meant for our own fiber. But having said so, there has been an increase in the PET bottle p

items.statement: PET bottle-fiber price delta narrowed by INR3-4/kg vs last year, pressuring recycled fiber margins
items.quote: It is basically the delta between the PET bottle and the fiber price. So the last year delta used to be higher by INR3 to INR4 per kg. And this year, in this quarter, particularly, delta has been lower by that much amount.

items.statement: Tightened credit to domestic wholesalers in home textiles due to payment issues; exports to Middle East suffered
items.quote: Secondly, we intentionally reduced our domestic sales to some extent, particularly to the wholesalers because we find that the payment issue is coming there. So we have tightened our credit to the domestic wholesalers, not for other things.

items.statement: Rupee depreciation helps margins on US exports but competing currencies depreciated more; limited benefit overall
items.quote: Depreciation of rupee will definitely improve the margin, but in products which we export to USA. If you talk to other countries like South Korea or any other country, the depreciation in their currency has been much more than our currency. So there, we don't get benefit. So it is the competing countries currency, we say it's rupee versus dollar. So wherever it is and whatever we are exporting to

items.statement: Government imposed 20% or INR115/kg customs duty on imported knitted fabrics to restrict China imports
items.quote: Another step taken by government is the imposition of custom duty of flat 20% or INR115 per kg, whichever is higher on imported knitted fabrics. This will restrict such imports from China and is a very positive step for domestic yarn manufacturing.

items.statement: Employee cost at 15% of turnover vs peers at 10%; workforce optimization and automation underway; expects improvement in FY26
items.quote: If you will see the next year, say FY25-26, I am hopeful that the percentage will come down.

items.statement: Domestic demand muted due to geopolitical uncertainty; expects improvement from budget measures, lower rates, better crops
items.quote: We are optimistic about the prospects and the Indian domestic market is expected to boost up on the benefits given in the budget, but the situation at present remains muted due to wait-and-watch approach regarding the geopolitical landscape, post Trump administration's uncertainties and its implications for the trade.

items.statement: Value-added yarn share normally 15-20% but currently lower due to recessionary demand for cheapest yarn
items.quote: Normally, we used to have about 20% of the value-added yarn, but it is fluctuating now. Because in such recession times when the demand is low, people want the cheapest type of yarn. They don't need those type of yarn except for specific application. So demand of those type yarn is a little lower at this point of time. But we hope that as the things improve going forward, the demand will again com

items.quote: s currency is depreciated much more than us. So suppose China is exporting to USA, and we are exporting to USA, we are in the same boat. And if China is exporting to some other sum Laxl:ins and industries limited Sutlej Textiles and Industries Limited February 1 0, 2025 country, we are also exporting to same country, we are almost in the same boat. But where Indian market is concerned, it's a diff

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio maintained below 1, currently at 0.85; focus on strengthening balance sheet
items.quote: We have consistently maintained our debt-equity ratio below 1. Presently, it is at 0.85.

items.statement: No volume growth in yarn as all spindles operating; home textile export volumes flat, domestic volumes intentionally reduced
items.quote: As I mentioned to you, if you compare Q2, Q3, since we have operated all the spindles in Q2 as well as in Q3, there has not been any volume growth because until unless the demand pattern changes, volume growth cannot happen. If you talk of the home textile, in exports, our volume growth has been the same. And in domestic, of course, intentionally, we have reduced our volume there.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions, Red Sea crisis, Trump policy uncertainty, and competing country currency depreciation are key risks
items.quote: Positioning of key countries like Turkey has been worsening due to continuous increase in the interest rates, and consequent negative impact on the demand of the dyed yarn. Further, the positioning of tariff may take some more time to stabilize. The fourth quarter will be of particular importance as it will set the tone for the next financial year.

items.statement: Hospital margin guidance for FY25 is around 20.5%
items.quote: Yes. So we are maintaining our margin guidelines where we have said for the current financial year, we should be for Hospital business around 20.5% and for the Diagnostic bu siness around 21%, 22

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY25 is around INR 900 crore including INR 600 crore expansion and INR 300 crore maintenance
items.quote: So, capex for all the brownfield projects that we are moving forward and there is a capex requirement for normal maintenance also. So , total capex need for a year is around INR 900 crore, which includes expansion -related need of around INR 600 crore and INR 300 crore is basically maintenance capex.

items.statement: Hospital revenue growth guidance medium-term around 14% year-on-year
items.quote: I will say ARPOB growth will be in the range of 5% to 6% going forward. And I'm first talking of the Hospital business, and our revenue growth should be somewhere around 14% year -on-year.

items.statement: ARPOB growth guidance going forward 5-6%
items.quote: I will say ARPOB growth will be in the range of 5% to 6% going forward.

items.statement: Diagnostics growth expected to reach industry levels of 8-10% by Q2 FY26
items.quote: And we are hopeful that by the second quarter of next year, we would be able to reach industry levels of growth.

items.statement: Brownfield bed additions estimated at 350-400 beds per year including FY26 and beyond
items.quote: Yes. So we are estimating around this number, 350 to 400 type of number year -on-year. It all depends how quickly we can operationalize our brownfield expansion.

items.statement: Manesar greenfield facility started with 53 beds, another 50 beds to open, targeting breakeven at INR 9 crore monthly revenue by Q1 FY26
items.quote: You are right. So currently, the hospital is functional. We have opened only 53 beds right now. Maybe another 50 beds, we will be opening by

items.statement: Hospital occupancy improved to 67% in Q3 FY25 from 64% in Q3 FY24, occupied beds up 6.2% to 2,790
items.quote: Hospital occupancy improved to 67% compared to 64% in Q3 of financial year '24. This translated into occupied beds increased by 6.2% to 2,790 beds compared to 2,627 beds in Q3 of financial year '24.

items.statement: Consolidated operating EBITDA margin 19.4% in Q3 FY25 vs 16.9% in Q3 FY24, up 250 bps
items.quote: Our consolidated operating EBITDA increased 32% to INR 375 crores, delivering a margin of 19.4% versus 16.9% in Q3 of financial year '24.

items.statement: Hospital operating EBITDA margin 20% in Q3 FY25 vs 18% in Q3 FY24, up 200 bps
items.quote: The Hospital business reported an operating EBITDA of INR 325 crores, driving a 200-basis point improvement in margin from 18% in Q3 financial year '24 to 20% in Q3 of finan cial year '25

items.statement: Diagnostics operating EBITDA margin 14.4% in Q3 FY25 vs 10% in Q3 FY24; adjusted margin 21.3% vs 18.3%
items.quote: On the Diagnostic business front, operating EBITDA margin stood at 14.4% versus 10% in Q3 of financial year '24. Excluding one-offs, the operating EBITDA margin stood at 21.3% versus 18.3% in Q3FY24.

items.statement: Target to reach 25% hospital EBITDA margin sooner than later
items.quote: Yes, we are targeting margin expansion. And hopefully, we'll be seeing margi n improvement year-on-year. So our ultimate target is to reach to 25% sooner than later.

items.statement: Agilus added 160+ customer touch points in Q3 FY25 and 500+ in 9M FY25, total 4,126 as of Dec 31
items.quote: As part of our ongoing network expansion strategy, the total number of new customer touch points reached 4,126 as of December 31.

items.statement: ARPOB growth 9.9% in Q3 FY25 driven primarily by case mix (specialties like oncology, BMT) with only ~1.5% from price increases
items.quote: Out of this 9%, just maybe about 1.5% or so will be because of the price revisions. have taken very minor price increases earlier in the year. And other than that, there is essentially the case mix, which has been happening.

items.statement: Diagnostics took price increase in Feb 2024, not contemplating further price increases currently
items.quote: As of now, price increase, we have taken a price increase in February of '24. We have taken a price increase. So I think we are not contemplating any price increase as of now.

items.statement: Key specialties (Oncology, Neurosciences, Cardiac, Gastro, Ortho, Renal) grew 17% YoY, contributing 62% of hospital revenue; Oncology up 30%, Neurosciences up 18%
items.quote: Collectively, these specialties achieved a 17% year-on-year growth and contributed 62% to the overall Hospital business revenue compared to 61% in Q3 of financial year '24.

items.statement: Robotic surgeries up 77% YoY, neurosciences procedures up 23% YoY in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Key surgical procedure volumes performed across neurosciences and robotic surgeries witnessed a strong growth of 23% and 77%, respectively, compared to the corresponding previous period.

items.statement: Medical travel revenue grew 17% YoY to INR 132 crore in Q3 FY25, contribution ~8% of hospital revenue
items.quote: Our revenues from medical travel grew 17% compared to Q3 of financial year '24 to reach INR 132 crores. Revenue contribution of international business stood at approximately 8%, which is similar to Q3 of financial year '24.

items.statement: Digital channel revenues grew 36% YoY in Q3 FY25, contributing 29.9% of hospital revenue vs 25.7% in Q3 FY24
items.quote: Revenues from digital channels where website, mobile applications and digital campaigns witnessed a 36% year-on-year growth in Q3 of financial year '25. Digital revenues contributed to approximately 29.9% to overall hospital revenues versus 25.7% in Q3 of '24.

items.statement: Net debt-to-EBITDA 0.41x as of Dec 31, 2024 vs 0.45x a year ago; net debt INR 644 crore; raised INR 1,550 crore NCDs in Dec 2024 to acquire 31.52% Agilus stake
items.quote: we remain comfortable and healthy with a net debt -to-EBITDA of 0.41x as on December 31, 2024, as against 0.45x on December 31, 2023. Our net debt stands at INR 644 crores as on December 31, 2024. In December 2024, we successfully raised INR 1,550 crores through the issuance of nonconvertible debentures

items.statement: After full PE buyout in Jan 2025, gross debt ~INR 2,300 crore, net debt ~INR 2,000 crore at consolidated level
items.quote: Up to December, we have only acquired IFC stake. Other 2 private equity stake we acquired in the month of January. So after acquiring private equity stake, our gross debt is around INR 2,300 crores at consol level and net debt of around INR 2,000 crores.

items.statement: Divested Richmond Road Hospital in Bangalore in Dec 2024, third divestment after Malar and Vadapalani; Richmond Road had INR 8 crore EBITDA loss last year
items.quote: Continuing with the portfolio rationalization strategy, we divested business operations of Richmond Road Hospital in Bangalore in December of 2024. This divestment supports our focus on improving overall profitability and margins. This is the third facility divested by the company after the divestment of Malar facility and Vadapalani facility in Chennai.

items.statement: Actively evaluating M&A and land acquisition opportunities fitting cluster strategy; some deals in pipeline
items.quote: We are looking at land as well bec ause there are certain areas where we are seeing a lot of development and we feel that there is a future potential, whereas no assets would be available in those geographies. So in such areas, we are scouting for land as well

items.statement: Agilus conducted 10.29 million tests in Q3 FY25 vs 9.85 million in Q3 FY24; 31.31 million tests in 9M FY25
items.quote: In the quarter 3, we conducted a total number of 10.29 million tests compared to 9.85 million tests in the corresponding quarter last year. In the 9-month period, we have conducted a total of 31.31 million tests.

items.statement: Agilus wellness portfolio revenue grew 17% YoY in Q3 FY25 and 9M FY25, contributing 10% of operating revenue
items.quote: The preventive portfolio revenues in Agilus overall revenue grew 17% in Q3 and contributed 10% to the operating revenues versus 9% in Q3 of financial year '24.

items.statement: Talent acquisition and retention described as ongoing battle not war; no major concern for large chains in metros; supply of specialists improving due to medical education reforms
items.quote: Yes. Shyam, I think the talent acquisition and talent retention is an ongoing. I would say it is not a war, but a battle, which keeps happening here and there. But I think overall, there is no reason for concern.

items.statement: Legal costs to remain elevated in early next year, expected to taper down post court decisions on forensic audit and brand acquisition
items.quote: So I think the early part of next year also, there will be some significantly higher legal costs. But post that, we should see these costs coming down.

items.statement: Rebranding one-off expenses of ~INR 50 crore planned for FY25, major balance in Q4, possible carryover to Q1 FY26
items.quote: We had planned to spend about INR 50 crores on rebranding this year. So I th ink over the last quarter and maybe a little bit flow through into next quarter may happen. So it will be in Q4 is what the major balance will happen in the Q4 respect.

items.statement: Secured INR192.8 crore lifetime new orders in Q3 FY25 (INR107.6 crore EV, INR85.1 crore non-EV); INR75 crore additional orders since Nov 13 con call
items.quote: During quarter 3 financial year '25, I'm delighted to share that we have secured lifetime new orders of value INR192.8 crores, comprising of INR107.6 crores from EV vehicles and INR85.1 crores from non-EV vehicles.

items.statement: Total new orders for 9M FY25 at INR459 crore (INR110 crore EV, INR349 crore ICE) to be executed over 4-5 years
items.quote: In the total 9 months, including quarter 1, quarter 2 and quarter 3 put together, our new order book is for INR459 crores, which wil l be executed in the next 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: Expect further capacity utilization improvement in Q4 FY25 due to increased sales and cost optimization
items.quote: Our current capacity utilization for the 9 months stood at 73%, and we anticipate further improvement in quarter 4 due to increased sales and cost optimization measures.

items.statement: Planned capex for FY25 around INR35-40 crore (INR10 crore for Chennai facility, INR10 crore new infrastructure/SPMs, 50% maintenance)
items.quote: So this year our total planned capex is around INR35 crores to INR40 crores. And out of that because we are also as a customer based in the south in Chennai. So, there would be some capex also, that around INR10 crores even there.

items.statement: Standalone Q3 FY25 gross margin 42.9%, EBITDA margin 11.1%; Consolidated Q3 FY25 gross margin 42.8%, EBITDA margin 10%
items.quote: The gross profit increased 16.9% year-on-year to INR58 crores with margins improving to 42.9%. EBITDA surged 38.1% year-on-year to INR15 crores with an EBITDA margin of 11.1%.

items.statement: Gross margins declined from 50%+ to ~43% over last 2-3 years due to material costs; internal target higher than guided 12% EBITDA margin but difficult to achieve 18-19% historical levels
items.quote: Earlier, our -- the gross margin used to be more than 50%. So eventually in last 2 to 3 years, it has gone down significantly. It has co mes down to around 43%.

items.statement: Raw material costs stable this year; injection molding (48% of business) has 100% pass-through contracts; extrusion materials (PVC, EPDM, steel) seeing stable to slightly declining trends
items.quote: On the injection side, we use our primary material is polypropylene. And other than that, we use lot of materials like ABS, engineering plastics basically. On the extrusion side, our basic materials are PVC and thermoplastics and EPDM rubber.

items.statement: Injection molding ~48% of business (lower margins, competitive); Extrusion ~52% (higher margins); EV orders growing (INR110 crore of INR459 crore 9M orders)
items.quote: From business point of view, if you look at the total pie chart, injection business roughly is about 48% this year and extrusion business is roughly 52% this year.

items.statement: Started deliveries for Maruti new Swift and Honda Amaze in Q3; active engagement with all PV makers for future models; Suzuki Motorcycles business received
items.quote: During the quarter under review, we have started deliveries of our products for Maruti new Swift as well as Honda Amaze. We continue our active engagement with all the passenger vehicle makers for securing new business for the future models.

items.statement: Meraki Precision Molds (tool room) contributed 5% to revenue in Q3 with multifold YoY growth; 102 molds YTD, 30 in Q3; 41% orders from non-automotive
items.quote: In Q3 financial year '25, Meraki contributed 5% to the total revenue and delivered a solid multifold growth on a year -on-year basis. This expansion marks an important shift, demonstrating not just growth but also resilience in the face of changing market dynamics. 41% of the orders came from the nonautomotive sector.

items.statement: Aftermarket (Elpis) grew 30% YoY in Q3, contributing 4% to revenue; 1,300 SKUs, 151 dealers; targeting 10% revenue contribution in few years
items.quote: The aftermarket business is thriving with strong momentum reflected in key growth areas. Expanding the portfolio to 1,300 SKUs is a significant leap for us, bro adening the options available to meet the diver se needs of the market.

items.statement: Lithium-ion battery business has negative EBITDA of INR1.2 crore in Q3; focus on cash-neutral in 2-3 quarters, then improve capacity utilization
items.quote: Currently, in the opening speech also MD sir has mentioned that we are still facing the challenges in that. So there is a negative EBITDA of INR1.2 crores in this quarter also.

items.statement: Will maintain borrowings at current level for next 2-3 years due to capex plans; then reduce net debt
items.quote: Yes, so long-term debt side, as you mentioned that next year we will try to maintain at this level only because we also have certain the plans --capex plan also. So on the next 2 years to 3 years, we will try to maintain it that level only.

items.statement: Aftermarket expanding to neighboring countries and GCC/UAE (strategy finalization by end of Q4 or Q1 FY26); Industrial products started exports to US market

items.quote: So if you are to ask me on a blended basis, I would say Sammaan Capital would be generating about a 10.5% yield. Sammaan Finserve will be generating around 12% to 12.5% yield. And on that basis, we will be generating a 4-plus percent ROA in each of the two companies.

items.statement: Flow cost of capital 9.5-10%; earn 80bps spread on assigned portion plus 50bps management fee on full loan; insurance attachment adds 4x multiplier on retained portion

items.statement: Branch network at 214 consolidated; targeting 25% annual growth to 300-330 branches by FY27
items.quote: We stand at about 214 branches consolidated for both the companies, and we expect this to be going up at a pace of about 25% per year for the next 3 years. We should be at over 300 branches, 300 to 330 branches by fiscal '27.

items.statement: On-balance sheet borrowings grew 3x YoY to INR9,248 crores YTD FY25; 12 banks sanctioned fresh term facilities
items.quote: The on-balance sheet borrowings have grown 3x in a comparable period versus last financial year. The rollover of our cash credit facilities, etcetera, continue versus INR2,951 crores in the same period last year, which is a growth of 3x.

items.statement: NCD investor base expanded to 85,000+ retail/HNI investors to mitigate lack of deposit license

items.statement: Engaged with rating agencies; optimistic of positive ratings trajectory in near term
items.quote: We believe this has greatly boosted the credit profile of the company, translating to steady flow of on-balance sheet debt capital. It is also supporting the asset-light model. And I believe now we are well positioned on the credit ratings front to have a positive ratings trajectory. We are engaged with the rating agencies and are optimistic of a positive ratings trajectory in the near term.

items.statement: Quarterly disbursements increased 8.3% YoY to INR168 crores in Q3 FY25

items.quote: Our secured loan book now makes up approximately 38% of the AUM as of quarter 3 financial year '25, rising from 17% in quarter 3 last year, and we remain on track to achieve our 40% target by March '25. In fact, we will definitely exceed this target.

As you grow in larger size, it's easier to get borrowing from banks, etcetera, when you are more of a secured lender.

items.statement: Monthly collection efficiency updates to be provided to investors starting January until recovery to Feb/Mar 2024 levels
items.quote: One initiative which we have taken is that to give investors monthly data point. So, we started with January. And every month, at least till it recovers to the February level, which we used to see we will be giving monthly updates on the collection.
