items.quote: On the fleet side, we entered with an agreement with AGP City Gas, which is Pratham and Think Gas and successfully conducted the product launch in December 2024 with thousands of cards being issued and hundreds of gas stations being enabled to accept our cards.

items.statement: Seven-year Mastercard partnership for software platform and card solutions recommendation to corporate customers, banks and fintechs
items.quote: We have signed a significant agreement with Mastercard, which is a seven-year partnership. Under this partnership, Mastercard will recommend our software platform and card solutions to their corporate customers and other entities like banks and fintechs.

items.statement: HDFC Bank partnership to bundle credit cards with Zaggle software, expense management, employee benefits and Zoyer platform
items.quote: Further, the much awaited HDFC Bank partnership has come in as a major addition to the list of our partner banks. In this agreement, HDFC credit cards will be bundled with our software, expense management and employee benefits as well as our Zoyer platform and offered to their corporate customers.

items.statement: Strategic partnership with Strada (global HRMS provider) to offer Zaggle SaaS and payment products to Fortune 500 clients
items.quote: We have entered into a strategic partnership with Strada, which is a large MNC HRMS solution provider working with multiple global Fortune 500 companies, wherein they offer the Zaggle SaaS and payment products to Strada's clients.

items.statement: Revenue mix: SaaS/platform fees INR 8.9 crores, Program fees INR 135 crores, Propel Points INR 192 crores (57% of revenue) in Q3 FY25
items.quote: During the quarter, our SaaS fee / platform fee / service fee contributed to about INR 8.9 crores. Our program fees contributed about INR 135 crores. Propel Points revenue consisted of 57% of our revenue, which contributed 192 crores.

items.statement: Zoyer started clocking revenues in April 2024, contributing significantly to growth
items.quote: It is very heartening to see that Zoyer, which started clocking revenues only in April 2024, is contributing significantly to Zaggle's growth.

items.statement: Program Fees expected to grow fastest among three revenue lines in next 2-3 years
items.quote: But in the next two, three years, we see our Program Fees grow at the fastest pace because there is a lot of traction there.

items.statement: AI chatbot RazBot achieved 60% deflection rate, targeting 99%+
items.quote: Zaggle's AI-driven chatbot, RazBot, it is called RazBot, has achieved a deflection rate of 60%. And we intend to enhance the deflection rate to about 99%.

items.statement: Propel gross margins at ~3% in Q3, expected to improve to 7-9% range in Q4 as overriding commissions kick in
items.quote: Basically, a lot of the ORCs, overriding commissions, are something that come in the Q4. Q3, very small merchants were able to cross some of the base thresholds. These are slab structures. So, the real increase in the margins, we anticipate to see some of it, we anticipate to see most of it actually in this. quarter.

items.statement: Conglomerate account revenue potential estimated at 50-65 crores per conglomerate
items.quote: So, you know, depends on the conglomerate person, you know, what kind of use in a conglomerate, but on an average, per account, you can take the potential could be to do about anywhere, about 50 to 65 crores per conglomerate is how you can look at it.

items.statement: Interchange EBITDA margins much higher than blended margins, Propel margins lower
items.quote: Interchange is much higher. Oh no, no. Much, much higher. Much, much higher.

items.statement: Employee costs normalized at INR 17 crores including INR 2 crores ESOP expenses
items.quote: So, employee cost is normalized. That includes 2 crore of ESOP expenses, Rohan. And this is factored in normal employee growth level, which we had in the paper.

items.statement: Other OPEX increased by INR 4 crores due to new product launches (fleet solutions) that couldn't be capitalized
items.quote: So, basically, Prateek, there were a couple of products which went live during the quarter, right? That requires one kind of, and which can't be capitalized. Those are ad hoc expenses, which we need to put it every time whenever the new product launch happens.

items.statement: Appointed Virat Sunil Diwanji as Non-Executive Director, seasoned banker with 30+ years experience at Kotak Group
items.quote: I would also like to welcome Mr. Virat Sunil Diwanji to our team as the Non-Executive Director of the Company. He is a seasoned banker with over 30 years of experience in building, managing and growing businesses across assets and liabilities.

items.statement: Union Budget 2025 tax reforms have very little or no impact on SAVE business (meal benefits only 0.48% of revenue)
items.quote: We want to take this opportunity to clarify that we see very little or no impact of this change in our SAVE business, which comprises of employee expense management, reimbursements and benefits. The employees in the 5 to 15 lakh salary range only take meal benefits, which form a meager 0.48% of our current revenue.

items.statement: Old tax regime continuing, slightly beneficial but company not dependent on tax benefits
items.quote: Additionally, we have partnered with multiple service providers in areas like financial services, healthcare, taxation, et cetera to provide value-added services to over 3 million plus active users.

items.statement: ESOP expenses expected in range of INR 9-10 crores for FY25
items.quote: During FY '25, we expect to record total ESOP expenses in the range of INR 9 to 10 crore.

items.statement: Presales guidance of INR21,000 crores cumulatively over next 3 years with 15-20% YoY growth
items.quote: Over the next 3 years, we aim to achieve presales booking of INR21,000 crores cumulatively.

items.statement: Annual business development target of at least 3 million sq ft and INR4,000-5,000 crores GDV
items.quote: Our stated guidance is to continue to add at least 3 million square foot every year. If you look at our track record of FY '25, we have surpassed that by more than 2x.

items.statement: Achieved INR5,200 crores presales in 9M FY25 with INR750 crores collections, 300% YoY growth
items.quote: The company has surpassed its full year sales - achieving about INR5,200 crores of presales in the first 9 months itself. This reinforces our strong execution and market leadership position, demonstrating a year-on-year growth of nearly 300%.

items.statement: Estate 128 Phase 2 achieved INR869 crores presales; combined phases at INR2,730 crores with INR550 crores collected
items.quote: With the successful launch of Estate 128 Phase 2, we have achieved INR869 crores in presales. This takes the combined project sales for both the phases now at INR2,730 crores. We have, in total, collected INR550 crores from Estate 128.

items.statement: Estate 360 recorded INR4,325 crores presales with 90% units sold and INR645 crores collected
items.quote: Coming to Estate 360, our Gurugram launch, we have recorded INR4,325 crores in presales with 90% of units sold and INR645 crores collected.

items.statement: Planning INR875 crores capex over next 2 years for commercial portfolio with financial closure achieved
items.quote: On our capex, we are planning to deploy an amount of close to INR875 crores in the next 2 years across our commercial portfolio. These projects have already achieved the financial closure through equity commitment from New York Life and the raising of debt from a consortium of banks led by SBI and ICICI Bank.

items.statement: Planning INR5,000 crores capex for launched residential assets funded from sales receivables
items.quote: In the residential space, we are planning to deploy an amount of close to INR5,000 crores across already launched assets. This capital is expected to be deployed from the sales receivables from the existing sales.

items.statement: Acquired 10.33 acres in Noida Sector 105 adding 2.6M sq ft mixed-use with INR3,000+ crores GDV and INR140 crores annuity potential
items.quote: Our latest acquisition of 10-acre land parcel in Noida in Sector 105 adds 2.6 million square feet of mixed-use development potential with a gross development value of INR3,000 crores plus an annuity income potential of INR140 crores.

items.statement: Delhi One project received NCLAT approval, on track for FY26 launch with 2.5M sq ft potential and INR1,500 crores GDV from new sales
items.quote: The Delhi One project received NCLAT approval, and we are on track to take over the entity housing the development with expected launch in FY '26. It has 2.5 million square foot of development potential between sold and unsold units and a GDV potential of INR1,500 crores from new sales.

items.statement: Planning 18.23 acres launch adjacent to Estate 360 in CY2025 with 4M sq ft potential and INR9,000 crores GDV
items.quote: Our plan is to launch 18.23 acres adjacent to Estate 360 in calendar year 2025 is on track. This has a development potential of 4 million square foot and GDV potential of INR9,000 crores.

items.statement: Estate 128 margin guidance 40-45%, Estate 360 at 20-25% due to JDA structure; both targeting 35%+ IRR
items.quote: In joint development, as you know, the land payment happens through revenue share over a period of time, which makes cost look inflated. And hence, for a like-for-like comparison, we also look at IRRs. And on the IRR front, both the projects have a very good healthy IRR of -- in both the projects, we are estimating to cross 35% plus IRR in both the projects.

items.statement: Expecting margin improvement on remaining 10% Estate 360 inventory through price hikes and distribution expansion
items.quote: And also the objective is to inch up the price with this 10% remaining inventory. So yes, we should see improvement in margin. Exactly how much, we will come back and update you as we move in that direction.

items.statement: NCR luxury segment seeing price appreciation; land supply adequate with 700 acres transacted in Delhi NCR in CY2024
items.quote: If you look at the data for last 2 years, there has been enough supply of land. In fact, in calendar year 2024 itself, out of 1,700 acres of land that got transacted pan-India, almost 700 acres is in Delhi NCR, implying more than 100 million square foot of development potential.

items.statement: 9M FY25 operating cash flow at INR400 crores, expected to reach INR700-750 crores by FY25 end
items.quote: So for the 9 months, the operating cash flow stands at close to INR400 crores. And this number is expected to go to a number of close to INR700 - 750 crores by the end of the financial year.

items.statement: Estate 128 Phase 1 collected INR450 crores (25%), next INR450 crores due March-April; Phase 2 collected INR100 crores with 25% expected this FY
items.quote: From the Phase 1, we had done a collection of INR450 crores, which was close to 25% at the time of the launch itself. The next installment, as I said, becomes due in the month of March, April, and we expect the money to be collected, another INR450 crores to come at that point of time.

items.statement: Total debt INR1,125 crores including INR800 crores LRD; cash INR1,600 crores resulting in net cash surplus of INR300 crores
items.quote: On the liquidity front, currently, we have a debt of INR1,125 crores, including an LRD, lease rental discounting debt of INR800 crores. Against that, we have a cash and cash equivalents of INR1,600 crores, resulting in a net cash surplus of INR300 crores.

items.statement: INR1,300 crores growth capital raised; INR350 crores from QIP earmarked for Sector 105 development
items.quote: With a very solid balance sheet and INR1,300 crores of growth capital raised, we are well positioned to scale further.

items.statement: Commercial portfolio at peak occupancy poised to generate INR725 crores annuity rental income over next 5 years
items.quote: Overall, our commercial portfolio, including operational assets under development and those at design stage at peak occupancy is poised to generate INR725 crores in annuity rental income over the next 5 years.

items.statement: Max Square achieved 93% occupancy with 25% rental premium; closed 150,000 sq ft GCC deal, one of largest in Noida
items.quote: Coming to Max Square, with a leasable area of 6.8 lakh square foot, we have achieved 93% occupancy with rental premium of over 25% compared to prevailing market rate in the micro market. It featured a significant leasing transaction that we recently closed of approximately 150,000 square foot, making it one of the largest GCC deals in Noida.

items.statement: Expanding distribution to 10 upcountry and 8-10 international markets for next Gurugram launch
items.quote: We have already initiated a business development plan for our upcountry and international market, touch at least 10 upcountry and 8 to 10 international markets in coming months as we move towards launch of our next project in Gurgaon.

items.statement: Optimistic on Delhi land pooling policy with 6.5M sq ft residential potential; not included in current guidance
items.quote: To put that in context, we are talking about almost 6.5-odd million square feet of development potential that's primarily residential that could potentially open up in Delhi, in the geography of Delhi.

items.statement: Management maintains conservative guidance approach despite strong demand; willing to upsize if market sustains
items.quote: I think we have always focused on trying to meet the guidance that we have been giving for the last 2 or 3 years. And I think we would like to be a little conservative in our approach to continue to do that.

items.statement: Acquiring 3 floors in Max Towers for INR105 crores, increasing ownership from 3.1 to 3.6 lakh sq ft (63% of total)
items.quote: First, we are in the process of acquiring 3 floors in Max Towers for INR105 crores, consolidating our ownership. Post acquisition, area under our ownership has increased from 3.1 lakh square foot to 3.6 lakh square foot, representing 63% of total.

items.statement: Robust pipeline of 7M sq ft with INR14,000+ crores GDV planned for FY26-27 across residential, commercial, mixed-use
items.quote: A robust pipeline of 7 million square feet with a GDV potential of INR14,000-plus crores is planned for FY '26 and '27, further strengthening our growth outlook.

items.statement: NCR luxury/premium housing strong with 4-7 quarters to sell vs 7 quarters overall; GCCs driving 40% of office leasing
items.quote: However, on the premium and luxury side, they showed stronger absorption with the quarters to sell of around 4 in the INR20 million to INR50 million price point and 3 quarters in the INR50 million to INR100 million price point, which we believe is a very healthy level given historic trends.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guidance of 18-20% year-on-year
items.quote: And our guidance, what we have provided is like around 18% to 20% growth year-on-year. I think we are very confident to achieve.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin guidance of 21-25%
items.quote: We have already given the range actually. Our expected EBITDA must be 21% to 25%.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth target of at least 20% over FY25
items.quote: Our next year target is almost whatever revenue we will achieve this year-end, will be at least 20% higher than what we have projected.

items.statement: Order backlog of INR 1,341 crores as of 31 Dec 2024 with 63% exports
items.quote: Our order backlog on 31st December 2024 was INR 1,341 crores, with 45% coming from Industrial Gas, 36% coming from LNG and 19% coming from Cryo-Scientific division. Exports comprised of 63% of the total order backlog.

items.statement: Q3 order inflows of INR 493 crores driven by Bahamas LNG and Highview Power orders
items.quote: Total order inflows during Q3 was INR 493 crore, comprising 41% from IG, 49% from LNG and 10% from the Cryo-Scientific division.

items.statement: Strong LNG demand from mini-terminals, fueling stations, and industrial fuel switching
items.quote: The segment is experiencing a robust demand of LNG storage and transportation tanks. items.statement: Steel capacity expansion to 300 MT by 2030 driving industrial gas demand
items.quote: In Industrial Gas segment, the robustness of the steel industry inspires confidence as we anticipate significant expansion over the next decade, with the steel production capacity aimed to increase to 300 million tons by 2030 from the current 180 million tons.

items.statement: Capex of INR 80-100 crores in FY25, infrastructure ready for next 2 years
items.quote: Last year also, we did almost INR 100 crores. And this year also, we are doing INR 80 crores to INR 100 crores. And we are almost now ready for next 2 years from the Capex perspective and infrastructure perspective, we are now ready.

items.statement: Savli plant capacity expansion and cryoshop commissioning by end of March 2025
items.quote: Our Savli plant for the beverage kegs is fully ready. The cryoshop is almost getting ready by end of March. We will be fully commissioning that plant.

items.statement: EBITDA margins slightly better on mega projects like Bahamas LNG terminal
items.quote: Definitely, we told you last time as well, the margins are slightly better when we go for mega projects like whatever we have received in Bahamas and many other complex projects the margins are better.

items.statement: Chinese LNG fuel tanks 10-15% cheaper; anti-dumping case filed
items.quote: They are cheaper by around 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Beverage keg revenue INR 7 crores in Q3, targeting INR 30-35 crores for FY25
items.quote: Total 9 months for beverage kegs, it will be around INR 19 crores and we may end up into INR 30-35 crores by end of March.

items.statement: LNG fueling station market share 65-70%; GAIL/BPCL to tender 15-20 stations
items.quote: So, far, our LNG fueling station and LCNG station, our market share is almost like 65% to 70%. That is our ratio as on today. And very recently, the GAIL, BPCL are going to release tender for additional around 15 to 20 such stations.

items.statement: INOX Air Products buys 100% of cryogenic equipment from INOX India (~10% of ASU project value)
items.quote: So, whatever they buy for the cryogenic part of it, storage, distribution and this one, we always take almost 100%. So, on an average, in air separation plant, if it is INR 1,000 crores investment, we get around INR 100 crores. So, almost 10% of that.

items.statement: Nuclear Energy Mission INR 20,000 crore allocation for SMRs; INOX positioned for cryogenic storage
items.quote: The INR 20,000 crore allocation for Nuclear Energy Mission, particularly for small modular reactors, is a visionary move that will accelerate the adoption of efficient and sustainable nuclear power.

items.statement: Targeting 300,000 kegs annual capacity in 1-2 years
items.quote: We have put our plan for 300,000 kegs, and we should achieve that in next 1 or 2 years now.

items.statement: ISRO third launchpad RFQ in 5-6 months, orders by end FY26, revenue 12-18 months later
items.quote: RFQ is in process. It will take around 5 to 6 months for making the RFQ, and then only the tender will be released. items.statement: Net free cash INR 293 crores as of Dec 2024
items.quote: The Company has a comfortable net free cash of 293 crores as of December '24, which provides us adequate room to raise debt in the future.

items.statement: Other income ~INR 15-16 crores per quarter from scrap and mutual fund gains
items.quote: Yes, around that. Yes, yes.

items.quote: So Industrial business that what we are targeting 18% to 20% will come in the next 2 years.

items.statement: Management targets Passenger Vehicle segment to account for 8-10% of overall revenues in next few years
items.quote: We remain confident that the segment will account for 8% to 10% of our overall revenues in the next few years.

items.quote: We are excited to share a significant INR650 crore capex investment to establish state -of-the-art forging capabilities in heavyweight component segment, focusing on large crankshafts, axles, gears, oil and gas valves and other precision machined components.

items.quote: So yes, this INR650 crores capex that is planned, it includes the first phase of the forging as well as the machining lines, where approximately INR300 crores will go on the forging setup and approximately INR200 crores will go on the machining side and balance towards the infrastructure.

items.statement: New heavyweight facility targets 0.5-0.6x asset turn in 2 years, 0.8x in 3 years, full potential 1.2-1.3x
items.quote: So doing the sampling as the single orders are large, we expect to touch around 0.5 to 0.6 kind of asset turn on this in 2 years' timeframe and around 0.8x kind of asset turn in 3 years is what we are targeting on this.

items.statement: Machining capacity expansion on track to reach 62,000 tons by end of Q4 FY25
items.quote: On the machining capacities, the plan was to touch 62,000 tons by end of quarter 4, and we are in line with those capex.

items.quote: The deliveries of e -axle components for North American clients have also commenced during this quarter.

items.quote: Industry data indicates 7% year -on-year decline in the medium and heavy truck segment for the 9 M FY25 period.

items.quote: Our Industrial business segment has witnessed a significant growth on a year-on-year basis, and its share has now increased from 11% to 14% in 9M FY25 in overall revenues.

items.statement: New heavyweight facility expected to stabilize at >30% EBITDA margin, gross margin >35%, realization >INR500/kg
items.quote: Roughly, this will go upwards of INR500 a kg and with a very high terms of gross margin. So -- and initially, we'll have certain costs involved with it with the ramp -up. items.statement: Steel price decline impacted revenue by INR10 crores in Q3 and INR34 crores in 9M FY25; scrap price hit INR15-18 crores in 9M
items.quote: Yes. It is INR10 crores for the quarter. And around INR34 crores for the 9 months.

items.statement: Realization per kg improved by INR9 YoY to INR248/kg in 9M FY25 despite softening raw material prices
items.quote: Realization per kg stood at INR248 per kg, reflecting an improvement of INR9 per kg Y-o-Y. This is despite softening of raw material prices during this period.

items.statement: Direct exports 19% of revenue, indirect exports ~9%; North America direct+indirect exposure only 3-4% of total revenue
items.quote: Currently, the export share for the company is around 19% on a direct basis and around 9% on the indirect basis.

items.quote: And these testing's have taken over a period of 1 year, and it involves current capacities, which cannot be created overnight. So as of now, we don't see any threat of tariffs on the products which are going to be sourced from us in terms of North American market.

items.quote: On the Industrial, the realization I've just check is around INR300 plus, which will continue to be maintained between INR300 to INR350 a kg on the Industrial side.

items.quote: So top line, I suppose it will be around -- as far as right now, we are looking at I think INR520 crores to INR530 crores should be or INR535 crores should be the top line and the bottom line I think let us say INR35 crores is what we have committed.

items.statement: Strong demand across organized retail, job work and wholesale segments
items.quote: The demand is strong. And the demand we are into an organized segment of doing retail or job work or wholesale. And I think the way we are operating, we will be meeting 35% to 40% of revenue guidelines.

items.quote: Just, let's say, if I'm doing Indriya or I'm doing -- that will be a direct competition to most of our clients. And if we are having the confidence, they have already got the learning curve, it is better to right now penetrate the existing client.

items.statement: Paints business capex 90% complete, 5 plants almost completed, 6th plant at Kharagpur expected Q1 FY26
items.quote: As far as the capex in Paints business is concerned, we are almost done. I think we have already done 90% of the capex for the paints business. As told earlier, 5 plants are almost completed. 6th plant is getting completed in Q1.

items.statement: Birla Opus to become second largest player by installed capacity in Indian decorative paints market with Chamarajanagar and Mahad plants
items.quote: With commencement of commercial production at Chamarajanagar in November '24 and Mahad expected in this quarter, that is Q4 FY '25, Birla Opus would be the second largest player by installed capacity in the Indian decorative paints market.

items.statement: Renewable energy installed capacity at 1.2 GW, up 37% from March 2024, another 0.8 GW under advanced commissioning, targeting nearly 2 GW by end of current financial year
items.quote: With the projects under implementation, the capacity is expected to reach nearly 2 gigawatts by end of current financial year.

items.statement: Domestic gray cement volume grew 11% Y-o-Y in Q3 FY25, demand improving across individual house builder, infrastructure and urban housing sectors
items.quote: Demand across all sectors, that is individual house builder, infrastructure sector and urban housing growth has been improving and domestic gray cement volume grew by 11% Y-o-Y in the quarter gone by.

items.statement: Global cellulosic fibre demand stable with improving price trends, China operating rates at 89% and low inventory of 8 days
items.quote: Improved demand condition in China helped by pre-Chinese New Year demand has led to higher operating rates at 89% and low inventory of 8 days in China.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA lower by 9% Y-o-Y due to lower cement profitability and initial Birla Opus investments
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA for the quarter is ₹4,668 crores is lower by 9% Y-o-Y, mainly due to lower profitability in cement business and initial investments in building Birla Opus.

items.statement: Chemicals EBITDA up 25% Y-o-Y led by higher caustic soda realisation and improved chlorine derivatives profitability
items.quote: Chemicals business EBITDA for Q3 FY '25 was up 25% Y-o-Y, mainly led by higher realisation in caustic soda prices and improved profitability in chlorine derivatives segment.

items.statement: Epoxy margins under pressure due to 13% weighted average increase in BPA and ECH prices, not fully passed on, partly due to FTA with Korean producers
items.quote: BPA and ECH prices have both been going up, as you know. Between the 2, I think average increase over the quarter has been about 13% weighted average. And we have been able to pass on not all of the price increase.

items.statement: CSF input prices (pulp, caustic soda, sulphur) up more than 10%, impact higher than realisation gains
items.quote: The key input prices, which is pulp and caustic soda and sulphur, all these prices have moved up almost more than, I mean, in the higher double digit, more than 10%.

items.statement: Chlorine realisation negative ₹7,000-7,500 per ton in Q3, Q4 more negative than Q3
items.quote: For the reporting quarter, chlorine was about ₹7,000-7,500 negative. And the prices continue to be under pressure.

items.statement: Total lending portfolio (NBFC and Housing Finance) grew 27% Y-o-Y to over ₹1,46,000 crores
items.quote: The total lending portfolio, which includes NBFC and Housing Finance loan book grew by 27% Y-o-Y to over ₹1,46,000 crores.

items.statement: Birla Pivot added new product categories, launched Birla Pivot Bathware expanding private label portfolio beyond Tiles and Plywood
items.quote: The business has launched Birla Pivot Bathware, expanding its private label portfolio beyond Tiles and Plywood.

items.statement: Birla Opus sell-out 65-70% of primary sales, dealer inventory healthy, dealer network close to 50,000 target for first year
items.quote: Literally 65% to 70% of what we have sold and have sold out. And actually, the inventory that we have lying at the dealers is very healthy compared to other companies.

items.statement: Birla Opus gaining market share quarter-on-quarter, exit market share target high single digits for FY25
items.quote: We are gaining market share quarter-on-quarter because I think it's a long journey. So fundamentally, trying to get more dealers to back more aggressively with us.

items.statement: Epoxy business faces competition from Korean producers importing LER duty-free under FTA, industry hoping government will address
items.quote: Partly also because of the FTA, our country has with the Korean producers, who are able to bring in LER duty free. And as you know, as an industry, we are hoping that the government will address this.

items.statement: U.S. and Europe considering tariffs on epoxy resins from Asian countries, India may benefit if tariffs lower than on China/Korea
items.quote: While both U.S. and Europe are looking at tariffs on epoxy resins, there are other jurisdictions such as Korea and China, which are likely to be more severely impacted if you look at what type of a grant filing has been done.

items.statement: Epoxy exports less than 15%, closer to 10% of sales, Grasim primarily domestic player in epoxy
items.quote: Exports make up probably less than 15%, maybe closer to 10% of our epoxy sales. So we are basically a domestic player as far as the Grasim is considered in epoxy.

items.statement: Caustic soda sales volume growth muted at 1% Y-o-Y due to lower production at Vilayat restricted by lower power availability, expected to improve
items.quote: Caustic soda sales volume growth was muted at 1% Y-o-Y due to lower production at Vilayat restricted by lower power availability, which is expected to improve in coming quarters.

items.statement: India Cement open offer concluded and integration completed, Kesoram cement acquisition awaiting mine transfer approvals, integration expected in current financial year
items.quote: The India Cement Limited open offer was concluded in the current quarter and the integration was completed. The acquisition of Kesoram cement business is awaiting approval with regards to transfer of mines in Telangana and Karnataka.

items.statement: NBFC revenue grew 12% Y-o-Y, Housing Finance grew 45% Y-o-Y, NIM declined 88 bps Y-o-Y, Housing Finance net interest income declined 43 bps
items.quote: Given the competitive intensity and changing cost of borrowing, the NIM for NBFC business declined by 88 bps Y-o-Y and net interest income for Housing Finance business declined by 43 bps.

items.statement: Life insurance revenue grew 5% Y-o-Y, health insurance grew 38% Y-o-Y
items.quote: Life and health insurance segment reported Y-o-Y revenue growth of 5% and 38%, respectively.

items.statement: Amalgamation of Aditya Birla Finance with Aditya Birla Capital approved by shareholders, awaiting NCLT Ahmedabad approval, expected completion by March 2025
items.quote: Amalgamation of Aditya Birla Finance with Aditya Birla Capital announced in March '24 has received approval from shareholders. The amalgamation scheme now awaits approval from NCLT Ahmedabad and is expected to get completed by March '25.

items.statement: Rising policy uncertainties, protectionism and geopolitical tension signal more volatile and fragmented global economy in 2025
items.quote: As we enter 2025, rising policy, uncertainties, protectionism and geopolitical tension signal a more volatile and fragmented global economy.

items.statement: Medical device business expected to be ~30% of revenue in next 3 years
items.quote: We anticipate that our medical device business will compromise about 30% of our revenues over the next 3 years, enhancing organizational value significantly.

items.statement: Expect utilization to increase to ~80% in next 2-3 years
items.quote: We expect to increase utilization level to around 80% in the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Commercial supply of Semaglutide pens to start by Q2 FY26
items.quote: Yes, we should start manufacturing and supplying by quarter 2 of FY '26.

items.statement: Adding 50-60 million pen/auto-injector capacity by Dec 2026
items.quote: Between now -- let's say, between now and December '26, we're looking at adding another 50 million to 60 million capacities on pens and auto-injector combined.

items.statement: Auto-injector line of 20-25 million capacity coming up Q3 calendar 2026
items.quote: That line will obviously be a kind of a 25 million capacity line. 20 million to 25 million. I have not figured out the exact math yet, but somewhere around consider 20 million as capacity for the auto-injector, which will come up in Q3 calendar '26.

items.statement: First 80 PPM Semaglutide line expected by Sep-Oct 2025
items.quote: As early as September, October of this year.

items.statement: Current pen capacity 35-40 million; auto-injector ~6 million
items.quote: So the current capacity is somewhere between 35 million to 40 million depending on the pen, combination which is the 35 million -- and we are looking at adding another 50 million to 60 million capacity.

items.statement: Insulin pen 8-cavity qualification completing Mar-Apr 2025
items.quote: We are under the last phase of qualifications. We're trying to do our best to complete it this quarter. But it could spill over into April. So between March and April, we'll finish qualifications on the increased cavitation.

items.statement: Signed 6 new healthcare contracts for pen/auto-injectors (GLP-1, insulin, parathyroid hormone, migraine)
items.quote: In the healthcare space, during Q3 FY '25, we have successfully signed six additional contracts with different customers for pen injectors and auto-injectors for GLP-1 and other therapies.

items.statement: Awarded new business from 2 global retail chains; supplies start Q1/Q2 FY26
items.quote: In the Consumer segment, we've been awarded new business from 2 global retail chains. Supplies for the same will start from Q1 and Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: Healthcare segment grew 62% YoY in Q3 FY25
items.quote: This is mainly due to increased sales from our Healthcare segment, which grew by 62% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Consumer segment grew 20% YoY to INR141 cr in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Despite the ongoing geopolitical challenges, revenues from this segment grew by 20% year-on-year to INR141 crores in Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: Industrial segment declined 8% YoY to INR12.5 cr in Q3 FY25
items.quote: In the Industrial segment, we've unfortunately had a small amount of degrowth by 8% year-on-year to INR12.5 crores in Q3.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 gross margin 47.5%, EBITDA margin 23.4% (+260 bps YoY)
items.quote: We delivered a robust top line growth of 25% to INR197.6 crores in Q3 FY '25 and have improved our gross margin and EBITDA margin, which stands at 47.5% and 23.4%, respectively.

items.statement: 9M FY25 EBITDA margin 21.7% (+330 bps YoY)
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 21.7%, an increase of 330 bps over 9 months FY '24.

items.statement: Pen realization broad range $2-$8 depending on therapy, volumes, MOQ, colors
items.quote: Broad range could be something as low as $2 to maybe $7.5, $8 for different therapies.

items.statement: Pharma segment grew 57% YoY in 9M FY25 to INR108.6 cr
items.quote: In the Pharma segment revenue stood at INR108.6 crores during 9 months FY '25 as compared to INR69.1 crores for 9 months FY '24, a growth of 57%.

items.statement: Own IP-led platforms to contribute higher revenue vs contract manufacturing over 3-5 years
items.quote: As we move forward over the next 3 to 5 years, you will see our own IP-led pen platforms contributing much higher revenue as compared to contract manufacturing.

items.quote: So we have not done any business with either of these customers over the last 5 years. With one of them, we have done some business prior to 5 years. So I think we will take it as a new customer.

items.statement: Multiple customers on Semaglutide and auto-injector programs
items.quote: So we have multiple customers on the same therapy. So if you look at Sema, we have multiple customers on Sema. We have multiple customers on the auto-injector for Sema or other therapies which we are looking at.

items.statement: Exports 79% of revenue in Q3 and 9M FY25
items.quote: Exports during Q3 FY '25 and 9 months, FY '25 stood at 79% and 79%, respectively, of total revenue.

items.quote: So, sales have been above expectation in terms of velocity in all our projects. As you've been tracking our investor presentation, we managed to sell out most of our inventory on launch.

items.quote: So, these are first-time homebuyers. These are people looking for upgrade and then they are, what you talked about influx of investment from outside. Now on outside, we mean parts of UP, which are East of Lucknow.

items.statement: Revenue target revised to around INR1,200 crores in 3.5 years from earlier INR1,300 crores
items.quote: I think given scenario, less keeping current prices in mind, I would say, about INR1,200 around that.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 17-20% in 3.5-4 years
items.quote: It's difficult to predict, but definitely, it will be about 17% to 20%.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 13.78% from 9.7% in Q2
items.quote: The margins also improved from 9.7% to 13.78%.

items.statement: Formulations EBITDA margin improved to 15.85% in Q3 from 13.17% in Q2
items.quote: The percentage margins improved to 15.85% as compared to 13.17% in quarter 2.

items.statement: API EBITDA margin doubled to 11.57% in Q3 from 5.76% in Q2
items.quote: EBITDA margin in quarter 3 was 11.57% as against 5.76% in quarter 2, which is almost double when you compare the quarters.

items.statement: 26 CMO/CDMO projects completed or near completion; 18 under implementation
items.quote: CMO and CDMO projects of 26 projects, with all including, which are near completion or completed. Commercial supplies are starting in this quarter or I mean all the projects, if I say, by first quarter of next year.

items.statement: Targeting >50% of business from CMO/CDMO in 2 years
items.quote: I mean we see 2 years from now, more than 60% business should come from CMO and CDMO.

items.statement: Capex for formulations ~INR10 crores in 9M FY25; Panoli capex nearly complete
items.quote: It's normal capex of about INR10 crores or so in formulations for 9 months.

items.statement: No large capex expected for next 1-2 years except potential vial filling line
items.quote: I don't see very large capex except if we are putting up a vial filling for pen arms. Other than that, I don't see a very large capex.

items.statement: Panoli plant trial production ongoing; commercial production expected start of Q1 FY26
items.quote: We have started our production for validation and trial and other things, and expect in beginning of Q1 to start commercial production out there.

items.statement: Panoli API capacity utilization expected 40% in FY26, 80% in FY27
items.quote: Panoli will be stabilizing next year, I mean we'll be doing about 40% of capacity utilization next year and second year about 80%.

items.statement: Shifting from amoxicillin to amoxicillin-clavulanate to reduce price competition
items.quote: we are focusi ng and moving more towards the combination of amoxicillin with clavulanic acid, which has a higher value and is safer in terms of pricing competition

items.statement: Expanding Faropenem capacity; new products less susceptible to price competition
items.quote: Plus the new products like Faropenem or other products, which are giving good margins and they are growing. They are less susceptible to price competition, and we are expanding like capacity of Faropenem also.

items.statement: Chinese price pressure across API industry, especially fermentation-based products
items.quote: We saw not only in Penems, but generally across the API industry, the Chinese bringing down prices.

items.statement: Meropenem market share increased to ~20 tons this year from 12-14 tons last year
items.quote: We would be doing about 20 tons this year, as compared to many 12 or 13 tons last year, 14 tons.

items.statement: Chinese competition limited in formulations due to regulatory barriers in India
items.quote: Formulations cannot come into the country because they are not registered and would not be able to register.

items.statement: Debt primarily working capital; term loan ~INR10-12 crores for Panoli; 30% working capital limits unutilized
items.quote: Our debt is basically working capital debt, except one term loan, which is there, we have not taken any term loan thereafter. It was taken for Panoli 4 years back. That would be now about, let's say, INR10 crores, INR12 crores or so.

items.statement: ESOP of 340,000-375,000 shares at INR179; 40% exercisable from Sep'24, 30% from Sep'25, 30% from Sep'26
items.quote: We have given about 340,000 375,000 shares is ESOP at a rate of 179. And 40% of that is exercisable after 1 year, which is from September '24 till August '25, they can exercise at any point of time. 30% would be September '25 onwards and 30% would be September '26 onwards.

items.statement: Government assured protection for domestically produced fermentation-based KSMs
items.quote: The government has already assured that such basic KSMs, which will be made from fermentation in India to make us self dependent, the government will protect us.

items.statement: Chinese KSM price drops as India builds capacity; battlefield shifting from APIs to KSMs
items.quote: Since India is going very aggressive on development of KSMs, whether synthetics or fermentation, we are seeing a trend where China is dropping prices of KSMs.

items.statement: CMO/CDMO projects for regulated markets across therapeutic areas: antibiotics, diabetic, cardiac, pain, GI, CNS
items.quote: It can be an antibiotic, definitely, antibiotics are there. There are so me diabetic or cardiac or pain management or gastrointestinal, there are various segments

items.statement: Meropenem, Azithromycin, Ticagrelor at bottom of price cycle; limited further downside
items.quote: These products -- I mean, these are almost at their bottom, I mean, barring another 3%, 4%, 5% one can say. But in the cycle of a product for last 2 years, I mean Meropenem is on a downward gone to a situation where Chinese are not recovering their cost also.

items.statement: Demand for offshore oil and gas services remains substantial in India, supported by energy demand growth and 22% projected refinery capacity expansion.
items.quote: As the country advances towards becoming a $4 trillion economy, energy demand is expected to rise significantly. India's reliance on fossil fuels, particularly natural gas, it remains high, and it provides opportunities for offshore operators like Seamec.

items.quote: PEARL, there is a rethinking by the management. So there are some issues going on. So as of now, the management is rethinking on that acquisition of PEARL because there are issues going on with the seller. So right now, it is on pause.

items.statement: Nusantara expected to add around INR135 crores revenue on a full-year basis.

items.statement: Two dry docks planned this year for Seamec Paladin and Seamec II; dry docks factored into contract planning to minimize disruption.
items.quote: So the Seamec Paladin and Seamec II will be likely going for the dry dock.

items.quote: Seamec Princess also is likely to get the contract award. We are in advanced stage. So as and when it gets finalized, it will be intimated to the exchanges during the as per the practice.

items.quote: replacement market in terms of the numbers from the previous corresponding quarter, we had grown at 16% and the passenger car radial had grown at 24%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin contracted 309 bps QoQ to 9.1% due to sluggish OEM demand and higher natural rubber costs
items.quote: EBITDA margins during the quarter were recorded at 9.1% vis-à-vis 12.2% in the previous quarter, which has contracted by 309 basis points due to sluggish demand in OEM and the higher raw material costs, primarily driven by a significant rise in natural rubber prices.

items.statement: Average raw material basket increased 2% QoQ; natural rubber prices rose sharply due to seasonal and climatic factors in Southeast Asia
items.quote: the average raw material prices have increased 2% on a quarter-on-quarter basis and here I would say that the natural rubber prices have actually played little havoc and the reason of which is actually because of the season changing and the climatic impact in this availability of natural rubber plus labor availability as well in the Southeast Asian belt.

items.statement: Strategic raw material inventory built in Q1-Q2 depleted in Q3, causing full impact of higher costs; most high-cost inventory consumed in Q3
items.quote: in Q1 and Q2, we had taken some strategic stocking of the material which helped us to evade some of the cost in Q2. But then that strategic inventory had depleted and Q3 saw the full impact of the raw material.

items.statement: Expect margin improvement in Q4 as high-cost inventory consumed, unless raw material prices rise further
items.quote: the good thing is that most of the inventory has already been consumed in Q3, so in Q4, we can expect some improvement in margins unless there is again some increase in raw material prices going forward.

items.statement: Pricing increased 1% QoQ; 4-5% under-recovery remains to be passed on depending on competitive market dynamics
items.quote: We have increased our pricing on a quarter-on-quarter basis to 1% and wherever price revision we could do, we have done that, and also we have improved our product mix. There is still some under recovery of 4%- 5% yet to be done.

items.quote: We already have an ongoing capex program of Rs.1,400 crores, out of which Rs.1,000 crores plus is for the PCR expansion, which we've already shared and another Rs.400 odd crores is a combination of TBR and all steel light truck radial. That is going on track.

items.statement: Year-to-date capex spend of Rs.600 crores against annual outlay of Rs.800 crores for first three quarters
items.quote: the outlay is about Rs.800 crores in these three quarters period. We have already spent about Rs.600 crores.

items.statement: Radial capacity utilization over 80%; PCR utilization close to 90%; Bus utilization 70%+; expansions not yet included in current utilization
items.quote: in terms of capacity utilization for radial, we are in excess of 80% , for Bus also, utilizations are at around 70 % plus, and this includes whatever capacities have already expanded that have been taken into consideration.

items.statement: PCR capacity utilization close to 90%
items.quote: PCR, as I said, it is close to 90%.

items.statement: Cavendish Industries posted highest ever quarterly revenue of Rs.1,025 crores with EBITDA of Rs.92 crores at 9% margin
items.quote: Cavendish posted a top line of Rs.1,025 crores, the highest ever for a quarter with EBITDA of Rs.92 crores, registering a margin of 9%.

items.statement: JK Tornel Mexico revenue Rs.507 crores (1,282M pesos) flat YoY; EBITDA margin steady at 7.9%; raw material basket up 12% QoQ largely passed to customers
items.quote: revenues for Q3 stood at 1,282 million pesos, equivalent to Rs.507 crores compared to 1,301 million pesos in constant currency terms. The decline in revenue was primarily due to the Christmas holidays and the appreciation of the Indian rupee against the Mexican peso. However, EBITDA margin remained steady at 7.9%.

items.statement: Mexican Peso depreciated 6% vs USD, supporting future exports; 25% US import duty on Mexican goods put on hold for one month
items.quote: Additionally, the Mexican Peso depreciated by 6% against the US dollar in the last quarter, which should support JK Tornel's exports in the coming quarters.

items.statement: North America accounts for ~5% of JK Tornel exports; majority to Brazil and Latin America; expanding to USA with higher rim sizes
items.quote: North America, about 5% of the total export because we are exporting more to Brazil and to Latin America. But we are now increasing our exports to USA with the higher rim sizes

items.quote: Net Debt of the company as on 31 st Dec'24 was Rs.4,317 crores which is net of the cash available with the company and the $100 million loan which we have tied up with IFC is for the expansions which are under implementation at this point in time and partly this loan will be used for replacing the high-cost debt in Cavendish Industries Limited.

items.statement: Long-term debt reduction on schedule; short-term working capital borrowings increased for strategic inventory, to normalize in 1-2 quarters; finance cost expected to decrease next fiscal year
items.quote: Debt reduction on the long-term borrowing spaces, we have been going ahead as per schedule and as we envisaged earlier. It's only in the short term the working capital borrowings have gone up in the last nine months period and this is to maintain the strategic inventory and also some finished goods inventory were accumulated but this is going to get corrected in next one or two quarters.

items.statement: Long-term industry EBITDA margin range 12-15%; FY26 margin target depends on raw material volatility and passing on FY25 under-recovery; sharper guidance next quarter
items.quote: generally, as we had earlier also said that in the longer term the industry is somewhere between that 12% to 15% range. So, let's see we will have to kind of keep it like that as of now, but maybe in the next quarter, we will be able to give you a sharper number on that.

items.statement: Replacement demand promising; OEM recovery path; CV demand to benefit from infrastructure and mining; PCR and TBR key growth segments in replacement; 2/3 wheelers also strong
items.quote: In the replacement market, we expect both the truck and bus radial as well as the passenger car radial to be the two growth segments. items.statement: Capex for new kiln completed in December-January; switchover to new kiln planned for end of February or first week of March, taking 20-25 days
items.quote: We have just now completed the CAPEX in December- January and we are in a process to switch over to the new kiln. items.quote: So typically, any cement plants and basically what we have done is we have projected to begin with, we have projected 50 % utilization. But if the market demand increases , there's always a scope for improvement. But to be on the safer side, we have taken 50% capacity utilization.

items.statement: Q3FY25 EBITDA margin 26.26% (solar-driven); cement EBITDA per ton <Rs.50 vs South peers ~Rs.422; target to reach South peer levels (~Rs.420-460) plus solar benefit after new kiln

items.statement: Q1-Q2 FY25 weak due to elections and monsoons; Q3 volumes began stabilizing; Q4 showing strong offtake across all plants; expect sustained demand from government infrastructure spend
items.quote: Q1-Q2 was extremely bad mainly because of election and then the monsoons. The fag end of Q3 showed some kind of an improvement and Q4 has shown the very good offtake for all the cement plants in the country.

items.statement: Cement revenue ~76% in Q3FY25; solar revenue ~15%; solar share to decline as captive consumption rises to 90-95% with new kiln; solar EBITDA benefit retained via internal power cost <Rs.1.50/unit
