EBITDA margins were at 81.39%. Profit after tax for the quarter stood at approximately INR 58 crores which also grew by 12% year on year, while PAT margins were 35.57%.

items.statement: 9M FY25 total income INR 484 crores (7% YoY), EBITDA INR 386 crores (8% YoY), EBITDA margin 79.74%, PAT INR 165 crores (7% YoY), PAT margin 33.99%
items.quote: For the 9 months of the Financial Year 2025, the Company reported a total income of approximately INR 484 crores representing a growth of 7% year on year. EBITDA stood at INR 386 crores, an increase of 8% year on year and EBITDA margins were 79.74%. Profit after tax was INR 165 crores, an increase of 7% year on year and PAT margins were 33.99%.

items.statement: Company will remain in old tax regime for FY25; decision for FY26 can be made anytime before filing returns in September 2026
items.quote: Just to clarify, for FY25, we need to decide by the time of filing the returns, which happens in September of 25 and for FY26, we need to decide by the time of filing the return for FY26, which is September of 26. So, therefore, for FY25, as of now, it will be decided to be in the old tax regime and for FY26, the timeline for the decision is before you file the returns, you can decide at any time

items.statement: No significant progress to report on Nirlon House; discussions ongoing
items.quote: So there is nothing significant to say in that regard. We are in various discussions and if there is anything significant to say, we will update you.

items.statement: Demerger of automotive and industrial businesses into two separate listed companies is underway; carve-out financials for prior three years submitted to SEBI.
items.quote: We have been operating them fairly independently, but we believe by separating them into 2 separate companies, it will create additional value for everyone.

items.statement: Automotive margin profile globally lower than industrial; in India, carve-out financials show similar margins (~14-15%) for both due to different localization mix (auto 95%, industrial 40%).
items.quote: If you look at financial year '23, '24, the margins were similar, right? It kind of stood around 14%, 15% each for both of them.

items.statement: Overall margin down ~4.5% YoY in Q3 due to high cost of traded products; traded margins rationalized to mid-single digits from near double digits in prior years.
items.quote: Our overall margin was down by around 4.5% year-over-year. And one of the reasons why it was lower was the high cost of the traded products.

items.statement: Expect further improvement in traded product margins in Q4 FY25 as rationalization continues.
items.quote: We are expecting some further improvement as we move to next quarter. So you should see some further rationalization on the traded product cost as we move to Q4 of this financial year.

items.statement: Long-term margin improvement expected through localization; current year margins likely lower than last two years.
items.quote: We do expect our margins to improve, right? Not -- again, currently -- the current year margins are going to be lower than -- are likely to be lower than what you have seen in the last 2 financial years.

items.statement: Industrial grew 23% YoY in Q3 (distribution ~20%, general machinery ~23%, wind ~16%, rail & defense ~23%); automotive grew ~10% (aftermarket ~18%, 2W ~10%, PV ~11%, tractors ~30%+).
items.quote: Industrial grew by around 23% year-over-year for this quarter. And Automotive growth was around 10%.

items.statement: Outlook for next quarter: infrastructure spending to drive metals, heavy industry; general machinery and distribution strong; 2W strong, PV seasonal.
items.quote: Outlook, I'd say continues to be strong, driven primarily by infrastructure spending, which at least for the coming quarter, right?

items.statement: Industrial growth in Q3 driven ~19% by volume; growth mix of market share gains and underlying market strength.
items.quote: In Industrial almost 19% was driven on account of strong volume growth year-over-year out of the 23%.

items.statement: Wind business 4-5% of total revenue; margins mid to high-single digit after portfolio pruning; some business won back at better margins.
items.quote: Overall, it kind of continues to be in the range of 4% to 5% of our total business. In terms of margins, the margins on the wind business after portfolio pruning, they have become definitely positive, and they continue to be in the range of mid to high-single digit.

items.statement: Capex spend ~INR 100 crore so far in FY25; full year expected INR 120-130 crore, in line with prior guidance.
items.quote: We have spent close to almost already around INR100 crores for this financial year. So we kind of continue to be in the range -- we will continue to be in the range of INR120 crores to INR130 crores.

items.statement: Korea plant machinery transfer to India still in process; production expected to start in a couple of quarters.
items.quote: The transfer is still in process. We are -- it will take maybe a couple of quarters for it to kind of start production.

items.statement: Localization at 40% for industrial (listed entity); evaluating further localization vs. importing from global SKF network to optimize supply chain and ROIC.
items.quote: We are continuing to expand wherever there's capacity needed. So in the automotive, for example, we need more capacity, and we will invest fairly rapidly.

items.statement: Traded business ~39% of overall revenue in Q3; traded margins at mid-single digit operating level, down from near double digits in FY24.
items.quote: Q3 traded business was to the tune of around 39% overall.

items.statement: Revenue mix Q3: Industrial 54%, Auto 39%, Exports 7%; within industrial, distribution ~24%, vehicle aftermarket ~12%.
items.quote: industrial is around 54%, Auto is at 39% and exports is at around 7%, right? And within industrial -- overall, I would say, industrial distribution is around 24% and vehicle aftermarket is around 12

items.statement: Gaining market share in 2W with Bajaj and Honda; onboarding new industrial part sellers and AIDs; increasing share with existing and new OEMs in general machinery.
items.quote: In some segments, we are gaining market share. So say, for example, 2-wheelers, we continue to gain market share with customers like Bajaj and Honda.

items.statement: Aware of new competitor capacity in SRB/CRB for industrial; localizing to remain competitive; more announcements expected.
items.quote: We are aware that this is happening. We also are localizing as much as possible, whether it is in the listed entity or in the unlisted one.

items.statement: Traded margins governed by FEMA and transfer pricing rules; cannot issue debit/credit notes to foreign suppliers to recover excess margins.
items.quote: Under the FEMA Regulations, we cannot go and recover that by issuing a debit note to a supplier.

items.statement: SKF Technology (unlisted) to remain separate; will serve both auto and industrial entities post-demerger; no merger planned currently.
items.quote: At this point, there's no plan to merge that. We'll continue to serve both -- serve the entities as separate entities.

items.statement: Manufacturing asset split between demerged entities not finalized; options include transfer of assets or contract manufacturing; decision expected in next couple of months.
items.quote: We are still working through manufacturing split exactly. But as soon as we have some information on that or clarity on that, we will walk you through.

items.statement: Services business (predominantly industrial) will move to industrial entity post-demerger.
items.quote: The services business is predominantly industrial. It will move to the industrial business.

items.statement: JSG lubrication acquisition (global) may bring opportunities to India; lubrication business currently not in listed entity; structure under evaluation.
items.quote: This is an opportunity for us to bring some of those solutions also into India. It's still early days.

items.statement: Portfolio pruning continuous in wind and other segments; exit unprofitable products unless price increase or value proposition viable.
items.quote: Portfolio pruning is a continuous process wherever we see opportunities, wherever we see that as a company we are making losses, we constantly prune those products.

items.statement: Carve-out financials for demerger (3 years) submitted to SEBI and publicly available under SKF India demerged accounts.
items.quote: As a part of our demerger requirement, we had to share the carve-out financials of the previous 3 years.

items.statement: Plan to hold separate investor call/meeting to explain demerger rationale and value creation roadmap; timing not yet fixed.
items.quote: We are planning to have some kind of a call to talk about more -- in detail about the demerger. But the timing is not right, right now.

items.statement: Medium-term goals include mid-teen EBITDA, 35% MHCV market share, substantial non-MHCV growth, alternate fuel leadership, subsidiary value unlocking, and ESG leadership
items.quote: Ashok Leyland is making good progress towards all its medium term goals, which are as follows. a) Achieve mid-teen EBITDA b) Achieve MHCV market share of 35% c) Substantial growth in our non-MHCV businesses d) Leadership in alternate fuel vehicles e) Value unlocking from subsidiaries

items.statement: Export target of 25,000 units in medium term, aiming for ~15,000 units in FY25
items.quote: So, exports also, in the long run, our target is to achieve 50,000. But in the medium run, we want to achieve a number of 25,000. This year we are hoping that we wil l end up close to 15

items.statement: Switch India expected to turn EBITDA positive by Q1 or latest Q2 FY26
items.quote: Switch India going forward should be EBITDA positive. Now it can happen Q1 or latest Q2.

items.statement: Hinduja Leyland Finance reverse merger with NDL Ventures on track for completion by end of Q1 FY26
items.quote: The reverse merger of Hinduja Leyland Finance with NDL Ventures is on track. As mentioned earlier, this is likely to be concluded by the end of Q1FY26.

items.statement: MHCV industry grew 10% sequentially in Q3 FY25; January already positive YoY; February and March looking better
items.quote: The MHCV industry, which had slowed down in Q2, gained strength in Q3, led by a pickup in consumption demand during festive season and better flow of government CAPEX in the second half of the quarter. As a result, Q3 FY25, domestic MHCV TIV was sequentially up by 10%.

items.statement: Bus demand slowdown is temporary; order book of ~4,000 buses to be supplied over 6-8 months; pent-up demand remains strong for at least 2 years
items.quote: This growth slowdown in bus demand is a temporary thing - overall, there is a huge pent up demand still available in the market. Whether it is STUs or MDVs or even ICV buses, we still believe that bus is a story which will continue to be favorable. Not just like next year, but probably for at least two years or so.

items.statement: Defense pipeline strong; expect 10,000-12,000 new truck orders over next 3-4 years from replacement demand
items.quote: And many of th ese are now beyond their productive age. And therefore we expect that in the next 3 to 4 years, and this is what we are also hearing from the ministry , that about 10,000 to 12,000 new trucks would be required

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin improved to 12.8% from 11.6% in Q2 FY25 and 12.0% in Q3 FY24; driven by cost reductions, commodity prices, and favorable mix
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin improved to 12.8% from 11.6% in Q2 of the current fiscal, and from 12.0% in the same period last year.

items.statement: Material cost at 71.5% of revenue in Q3 FY25 vs 72.2% in Q3 FY24; achieved through continued cost savings
items.quote: Material cost as a percentage of revenue was at 71.5%, lower than 72.2% in Q3 last year. This was achieved by our continued focus on material cost savings.

items.statement: Cost reduction of Rs. 650+ crores annually sustained over last two years; continuing in current year
items.quote: Last two years, we have also shared this in the previous calls, last two years has been quite good. Now we have, we ended up with a good Rs. 650 plus crores of cost reduction each year and this year also we are continuing on the cost reduction measures.

items.statement: Monthly breakeven volume reduced by more than half over last couple of years
items.quote: I am very happy to say that our breakeven volume, monthly breakeven volume, has reduced to more than half in the last couple of years.

items.statement: Export order book for Q4 is very robust
items.quote: Our export order book for Q4 is also very robust.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 capex Rs. 179 crores; cumulative 9M FY25 capex Rs. 486 crores
items.quote: CAPEX for the quarter was Rs. 179 crores and cumulative for the year is at Rs. 486 crores.

items.statement: Board approved Rs. 200 crores investment in Hinduja Leyland Finance and Rs. 500 crores in Optare (Switch holding company)
items.quote: Ashok Leland Board of Directors has approved further investments of Rs. 200 crores in Hinduja Leland Finance and of Rs. 500 crores in Optare, the holding company of Switch.

items.statement: Crossed 1,000 MHCV touch points and 800 LCV touch points in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Q3 also proved to be a milestone quarter for us as we crossed 1,000 MHCV touch points and 800 LCV touch points.

items.statement: Favorable mix in Q3 with higher multi-axle and tipper volumes; bus ASP increased; Power Solutions, Defense, spare parts grew strongly
items.quote: This quarter has witnessed quite a good mix both in the truck side as well as on the bus side. That has only resulted in a higher ASP as you are observing. The mix has been quite good especially with good pick up on the multi-axle vehicles and the tipper segment volumes.

items.statement: Tipper market share fell from ~29-30% to 23%; 7% headroom to regain; volumes growing after product gaps addressed
items.quote: Roughly we were close to 29%-30% about two years back. Now we are at 23% or so. So, we have this 7% headroom on market share in tippers.

items.statement: Net price realization flat in Q3 FY25; price increase attempted in one month but not sustained in subsequent two months
items.quote: It has almost been flat. We tried to increase the prices, in one month we succeeded, but subsequent two months we could not succeed. But overall if you look at we would have remained flat as far as the trucks and buses are concerned.

items.statement: Rubber price increase partially offset material cost savings in Q3
items.quote: Actually, a portion of the material cost reduction was taken away as we have also witnessed an increase in the prices of rubber. We had to concede a bit of the increase on the rubber side.

items.statement: Export volumes grew 33% YoY in Q3 FY25; 9M FY25 exports up 19% YoY; strong presence in GCC, SAARC, Africa
items.quote: The export volumes registered a growth of 33% in Q3 on a YOY basis. Our export business is driven by our continued focus on export-specific products and our strong local presence in GCC, SAARC, and African markets.

items.statement: Net cash position of Rs. 958 crores at end of Q3 FY25 vs net debt of Rs. 1,747 crores at end of Q3 FY24; before Rs. 700 crore subsidiary investments
items.quote: At the end of last quarter, we were cash positive at Rs. 958 crore. As compared to a net debt of Rs. 1,747 crore at the end of Q3 last year, this is a major posit ive swing in our cash position

items.statement: Rs. 500 crore investment in Optare partly to pare down Switch UK debt; Switch UK evaluating options due to weak EV market
items.quote: We have some debt in Switch UK, so we want to pare down. We are trying to reduce all the costs there including the interest burden on Switch UK.

items.statement: MHCV market share retained at 30%+; 9M FY25 share at 30.4%; medium-term target 35%
items.quote: Ashok Leyland continues to retain 30% plus market share in domestic MHCV market. Our nine-month ended December 24 market share stood at 30.4%. We remain committed to achieving our MHCV market share goal of 35% in the medium term.

items.statement: LCV market share in 2-4T segment at 18.5%; target 20% short term, 25% medium term
items.quote: In the addressable 2 to 4 ton market, AL market share was 18.5%. With the launch of Saathi, we are committed to improve our market share to 20% in the short term and 25% in the medium term.

items.statement: Switch UK outlook uncertain; EV market subdued; evaluating options including rationalization and debt reduction
items.quote: However, the outlook for the electrical bus market in UK continues to be uncertain. In view of these trends, we are providing due focus to the India market and concurrently evaluating available options for the UK.

items.statement: Dedicated Freight Corridor impact on CV demand will be small, gradual, and long-term due to implementation challenges
items.quote: There would be some impact like we spoke last time also, but it would take a long, long time and the impact would be like gradual. As there are a lot of challenges in setting up DFCs, in making the right proposition for the customers.

items.statement: International order book at INR5,482 million; domestic project order book at INR25,900 million; domestic products order book at INR3,988 million as of Dec 31, 2024
items.value: INR5,482m intl; INR25,900m domestic project; INR3,988m domestic products
items.quote: As of December 31, 2024, our international order book stood at INR5,482 million while the domestic order book for the project business was at INR25,900 million and domestic products order book was INR3,988 million.

items.statement: Pump division outlook positive with robust inquiry pipeline, especially drainage pump orders from Thailand in advanced stage
items.quote: On the operational front, the pump division maintains a positive outlook supported by a robust inquiry pipeline, particularly for drainage pump orders from Thailand, which are in advanced stage.

items.statement: Project division revenues rose to INR5,720 million in 9M FY25 vs INR4,740 million in 9M FY24; execution slowed in Q3 due to receivables but construction on schedule with recovery expected next fiscal
items.quote: Meanwhile, the project division saw revenues rise to INR5,720 million in 9 months FY25 compared to INR4,740 million in 9 months

items.statement: Expect revenue recovery in next fiscal year following Budget 2025; pace of new tenders to pick up; good growth expected in project segment next fiscal onwards
items.quote: Project execution momentum slowed down in the quarter as outstandings drastically increased. Despite these challenges, project construction remained on schedule with expectations of revenue recovery in the next fiscal year, following key announcements in Budget 2025. We also expect the pace of new tenders to pick up going forward and we expect to see good growth in this segment next fiscal onwards

items.statement: WPL international revenues increased to INR4,540 million in 9M FY25 vs INR4,310 million in 9M FY24; Gruppo Aturia seeing strong traction in MENA from revival of postponed contracts
items.quote: On the international front, WPL's revenues increased to INR4,540 million in 9 months FY25 compared to INR4,310 million in 9 months FY24. Gruppo Aturia is witnessing strong traction in the MENA region, driven by revival of postponed contracts following geopolitical stabilization.

items.statement: Three strategic acquisitions in FY25 to build international turnkey project division: Eigenbau (South Africa, INR700m revenue), MISA-SRL (Italy, INR900m), Paterson Candy International (Africa, INR2,150m); combined revenue >INR3,750m
items.quote: As part of a long-term growth strategy, WPL has made three key strategic acquisitions in FY25 to develop an international turnkey project division. These include Eigenbau in South Africa, which focuses on water and wastewater solutions with an estimated revenue of INR700 million, MISA-SRL in Italy, a provider of pumping solutions across Europe and MENA, specializing in the irrigation and drainage

items.statement: Acquisitions to contribute over INR3,750 million revenue and significantly enhance WPL's turnkey project division (FY24 revenue INR8,000 million)
items.quote: These acquisitions would contribute over INR3,750 million in revenue and significantly enhance WPL's turnkey project division, which recorded FY24 revenues of INR8,000 million.

items.statement: Project execution slowed due to drastic increase in outstandings; Jal Jeevan Mission funds blocked for 6 months; receivables for JJM scheme close to INR400 crores
items.quote: Receivables is close to about INR400 crores.

items.statement: Budget allocation clarified with fresh allocation for this year; expect receivables to come down rapidly and execution to pick up similarly
items.quote: Now, the most important thing is that with the budget clarification and fresh allocation for this year, now these projects are expected to gain momentum. So, we are expecting our receivables to come down rapidly and execution to pick up in similar fashion.

items.statement: Expect improvement from Q3/Q4 onwards with better government payments; should exceed last year's execution of ~INR800 crores
items.quote: So, you will see, obviously, it will improve. It is -- we were doing very well in the second quarter. And in September, we were expecting funds. So, our outstandings were rising and we were expecting funds. But that has got postponed till this budget. So, we got affected one quarter. I think we will be back to normal. If not, in this quarter, it should be improved and next quarter onward, it shoul

items.statement: Jal Jeevan Mission extended to 2028 in Budget 2025; FY25 allocation ~INR67,000 crores; most will fill last year's gap, limited new awards going forward
items.quote: Now it is extended till FY28 and this year's allocation on FY28 is about INR67,000 crores. So now there is no ambiguity on that. The extension of the scheme, the Jal Jeevan was supposed to finish in 2024, so the funds could not be disbursed. Now it is extended till 2028, which allows clarity there.

items.statement: Water infrastructure opportunity in India >INR1 lakh crores, up to INR1.5 lakh crores; company executing ~INR800 crores with strong qualifications; sufficient business going forward
items.quote: We are working in the water infrastructure project. There are urban water, rural water, drainage, there is irrigation, there is industrial water also there. Now here there was an interim scheme where there was a big shortfall in rural water supply. So the government came out with Jal Jeevan. Jal Jeevan, please understand is a temporarily accelerated effect for rural water supply improvement. Now e

items.statement: Capex not significant; capability building is about recruiting and training personnel as volumes grow, not capital expenditure
items.quote: Capex is not significant. So, it's not a discussion subject. Very insignificant.

items.statement: 5 domestic projects in advanced stage, expected to be commissioned in next 3 months
items.quote: 5 projects are in advanced stage, in the next 3 months should be commissioned.

items.statement: Indian Navy project trials 80-90% completed; most gone into bulk production; project on schedule
items.quote: Majority have been done, 80%-90% trials have been completed and most have gone into bulk production already. So, the project is moving well and on schedule.

items.statement: Consolidated cash approximately INR550 crores; international cash reserves strong; well funded for acquisitions; will review only for very large acquisition
items.quote: On a consolidated level, the cash is approximately INR550 crores.

items.statement: Looking at more acquisitions in Europe for product expansion; advanced talks ongoing; will update on progress
items.quote: So, we are looking at more acquisitions in Europe. We are primarily looking to -- so this project was one idea which we are doing. Similarly, we are looking at product expansion and we are in advanced talks and we will keep updating on that.

items.statement: Target geographies for water infrastructure growth: India, Africa, MENA; now present in all three; Middle East/North Africa and Southern Africa even higher growth than India
items.quote: Sir, these are very, very promising geographies. As we had outlined in our business strategy, the three areas which have tremendous scope for water infrastructure growth were India, Africa and the MENA region, Middle East, North Africa. And now we are present in all three. So, we are moving as per our strategy and these are the most prospective regions for water infrastructure growth.

items.statement: Product business doing exceedingly well; order book good; steady demand in both government and non-government areas; no abnormal acceleration
items.quote: Actually, our product business is doing exceedingly well this year, as our numbers show. And order book is also good. So, it's a little bit of state elections and government budgets which have a little bit affected these investments but I don't see any effect even in government or non-government areas going forward. We see steady demand. I would not say it's accelerated or anything abnormal, but s

items.statement: No increase in material costs; steel prices have gone down, providing benefits
items.quote: I don't see any such increase in material cost. Actually, material costs have gone down. Steel prices have gone down. So, we are getting benefits in that respect.

items.statement: No significant Chinese competition in our business segments
items.quote: In our business, we don't see much Chinese presence.

items.statement: Expect pickup in new tenders in Q4 FY25 and next fiscal; pent-up work not yet tendered expected to come to market soon
items.quote: So as we had mentioned last quarter, we had expected a pickup in the new tenders in the third quarter, but now we expect it in this quarter and going forward, surely in next fiscal because there is a lot of pent up work which has not been tendered and we expect these to come to market very soon. So we are not concerned, exceedingly concerned.

items.statement: PCI acquisition (55% stake) to complete in Q1 FY26; Eigenbau and MISA numbers to be shared in year-end results; full color by mid next year
items.quote: MISA was acquired in January, so, you know, we will have one quarter of performance. And PCI, the transaction will take, as I have said, till first quarter of FY26. So, I think surely, as these companies' transactions are completed, you will see them. And surely by middle of next year, you will have full color of all these transactions, the order books and how the revenues are looking.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margins ~17% for 9M both years; target range 15-20%; international acquisitions have strong margins, better than Indian markets
items.quote: Our margins are consistent. We are having roughly, if you take 9 months, last year, we had 17% consolidated margins. This year, we have 17% consolidated margins. So, I think we have lots of different parts of our business. So, to look in, we should look at the overall figure where our target has always been between 15% and 20%.

items.statement: Thermal power sector seeing good demand for engineered large pumps; new product lines (Navy, sewage/drainage) driving growth
items.quote: But yes, I would highlight that one of the sector which is improving now is the thermal power sector. So we are seeing good demand for pumps in the thermal power sector, which is new.

items.statement: International product revenues ~INR453 crores in 9M; domestic product revenues ~INR215 crores; well diversified across geographies (Australia, India, South Africa, Thailand)
items.quote: Number one, our product cycle is linked between international -- most of our international business presently, which is to the tune of in 9 months approximately 453. And 215 is the domestic revenues. So about INR660 crores is product. And we've already got a good balance there between domestic and international, which allows us to diversify.

items.statement: Business model subject to scheduling shifts due to government budgets, elections, geopolitical events; projects postponed not cancelled; building international project business to diversify risk
items.quote: So it is dependent on, various factors and especially in because we are linked with government so, budgets and elections we are linked to that. Again in the Middle East, North Africa region we are affected by wars there. So our business is, the thing is, it can be postponed, it does not get cancelled.

items.statement: Guided for INR1,700-odd crores revenue by FY27
items.quote: So, we have guided for around INR1,700-odd crores by FY '27. And I mean, that's something that we have as a target internally, and we have built capacities for that.

items.statement: Domestic call-offs picked up rapidly in last week of December and continued into Q4
items.quote: The silver lining is tha t the rapid calls offs we started witnessing in the last week of December, which continued into the first month of Q4 as well

items.statement: Expect most domestic order backlog to come up to speed by Q4 FY25
items.quote: We are expecting most of the order backlog in the domestic markets to come up to speed by Q4 of FY '25.

items.statement: Early summer in 2025 expected to boost beverage consumption and domestic demand
items.quote: With anticipation of a good summer in 2025, we are expecting to a ctually see a good growth going forward

items.statement: More than doubled tomato processing capacity; new plant running at full utilization since December
items.quote: We have more than doubled our tomato processing capa city. And since December, our new tomato processing plant is running at full capacity utilization

items.statement: Pastry line doing well; two more lines starting commercial production this month doubling capacity
items.quote: Our new pastry line is doing very well. We will start the commercial production of two more lines in this vertical, which will result in doubling of capac ity by the end of this

items.statement: Export shipment backlog of Q1 and Q2 was called off resulting in export tonnage growth
items.quote: Export shipment backlog of Q1 and Q2 was called off which resulted in export tonnage growth.

items.statement: INR4.2 crores forex MTM losses impacted EBITDA margins and other expenses in Q3
items.quote: Only point of note that we would like to highlight is around INR4.2 crores of forex MTM losses impacted our EBITDA margins and the other expenses in this particular quarter.

items.statement: INR7.5 crores DDP shipments increased both top line and other expenses
items.quote: Around INR7.5 crores worth of DDP shipment was actually done. So that would have actually been added to our top line this quarter as well as the other expenses would have actually gone up because whatever we sell under DDP shipment basis in the top line is also a part of our cost.

items.statement: Targeting EBITDA margin improvement with scale; EBITDA improving over last few quarters
items.quote: You can see that the EBITDA improvement is always if you see last few q uarters, there's EBITDA improvement. So we are targeting that and we are quite positive tha t, that is going to improve

items.statement: Cost-plus business model; top line function of raw material price
items.quote: our business model is a cost-plus model. So the top line is a function of the raw material price. That's the only caveat to it

items.statement: Inventory at INR600 crores as of December end, flat vs September; buildup due to tomato and guava
items.quote: Correct. That's right. That's also because we have built up inventories in t he tomato business, right. As in our newer capacity in tomato is fully running at capa city since December. So, we have added to that and some bit of guava has also been added

items.statement: Low inventory holding period in tomato business expected to improve working capital position
items.quote: The low inventory holding period of the tomato business is expected to improve our wo rking capital position as a business

items.statement: Working capital debt INR360 crores; long-term debt INR70 crores
items.quote: Around INR360 crores of working capital debt is what we have and aro und INR70 crores of long-term debt

items.statement: INR2.5 crores extra capex-related interest cost hitting P&L from last couple of quarters
items.quote: So, around INR2.5 crores of extra capex-related interest cost has actually started hitting the P&L from the last couple of quarters.

items.statement: Plan to grow scale and margins to reduce debt; working capital intensive business
items.quote: Our plan is to increase the business and to increase our margin. That's our broad-based plan. So the debt -- I mean, this is a working capital-intensive business. So, that ne eds to be kept into context

items.statement: Preferential allotment proceeds used for PLI capex, tomato capacity doubling, and incremental working capital

items.statement: Digital & Data business (57% of revenue) grew 2.4% QoQ; ERP business declined 5.7% QoQ due to seasonal weakness.
items.quote: Among service lines, our Digital & Data business that contributes about 57% to overall revenues grew by 2.4% quarter-on-quarter. The ERP business witnessed a sequential decline of about 5.7%.

items.statement: Cash and balances at $240 million, up 8.2% QoQ and 18.3% YoY; operating cash flow $29.9 million (155% of EBITDA); DSO at 53 days.
items.quote: Our cash and balances at the end of the third quarter stood at $240 million, up 8.2% quarter-on-quarter and about 18.3% year-on-year.

items.statement: Roop (Americas head) departed; CEO stepping in to run Americas business while searching for replacement.
items.quote: Roop has decided to take up an opportunity outside of Birlasoft and we wish him well. So, for now, I am stepping in to run the Americas business as an additional responsibility while we look for a solid replacement.

items.statement: Added 3-4 new logos across verticals; targeting a new Manufacturing logo in Europe in Q4 to achieve goal of one major logo per vertical.
items.quote: We've actually added, I think about 3 or 4 new logos in the verticals that we serve. Now, how much will the logos scale, only time will tell.

items.statement: Top 6-10 accounts declined 5% QoQ and 14-15% YoY due to furloughs; management focused on mining top 10-15 clients to return to growth.
items.quote: Some of this decline is because of the furloughs that I spoke about. So, furloughs have impacted some of these clients, which was why they have shown a decline.

items.statement: Project ramp downs in healthcare and manufacturing, over and above furloughs, may impact Q4 revenue.
items.quote: In terms of project ramp downs, we have seen some amount of project ramp downs, not very large, but a little bit of project ramp downs in health care as well as in manufacturing.

items.statement: No formal guidance given; predictability suffered in FY25 due to unanticipated furloughs and client-specific issues; expect predictability to improve in FY26.
items.quote: We don't give a guidance usually. Our job will be to execute for the quarter.

items.statement: No plans to return cash to shareholders via buyback; conserving cash for potential M&A opportunities after delivering organic revenue growth.
items.quote: I would say, no, at this point of time. We're really looking at conserving cash for any potential opportunity that would come up in the future.

items.statement: Will consider M&A after delivering a couple of quarters of organic revenue growth; current focus on operational margin improvement and revenue growth.
items.quote: We will look at an M&A at some point in time. But right now, we want to deliver a couple of quart ers of revenue growth

items.statement: No client discount requests yet; pricing pressure possible in competitive medium-sized deals ($30-50M).
items.quote: Now, up to date, we have not heard from any of the clients asking for a discount. So that's a positive thing. But we don't know what happens in the future.

items.statement: Infrastructure business outperforming Applications business could create medium-term margin headwind.
items.quote: If our Infrastructure business continues to outperform our Applications business, then obviously in the medium term there could be a margin impact.

items.statement: Furlough impact shaved off at least 150 bps of QoQ growth in Q3.
items.quote: I would say it would be at least about 150 bps in terms of what has got shaved off because of this.

items.statement: Financial Services and E&U expected to lead growth over next year; Manufacturing soft for couple of quarters; Healthcare expected to recover in couple of quarters with new leadership hires.
items.quote: I think E&U and Financial Services will lead growth over the next one year. Now again, one quarter, you may see Financial Services also impacted. But I think over the next 4 quarters if you normalize, Financial Services and E&U will continue to grow.

items.statement: Targets Rs 6,000 crore revenue by FY28 with double-digit EBITDA growth
items.quote: This growth trajectory position s us well to achieve our target of growing our topline to Rs. 6,000 crores by FY28 with double digit EBITDA growth being an attainable goal

items.statement: Targets 10-12% EBITDA margin by FY28
items.quote: Our plan to reach a double-digit EBITDA remains intact. We are very clearly heading in that direction where double digit EBITDA will be there. What we have stated is that between 10%-12% by FY28 and that is our target remain is there and we are heading in that direction.

items.statement: Expects 20%+ volume and value growth in Indonesia next financial year
items.quote: This recovery is expected to drive a 20% plus growth in both volume and value in the coming financial year.

items.statement: Guatemala facility cash breakeven anticipated next year
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect a significant improvement in this Gautemala facility by next year with a cash breakeven point anticipated.

items.statement: India EBITDA target high single digit, then double digit in 3-4 quarters
items.quote: Our goal is to first work towards achieving high single digit EBITDA in India and we are making significant efforts to march towards the same.

items.statement: Committed Rs 35 crore capex for Bihar facility, Phase 1 Rs 22 crore capitalized by March-April
items.quote: In India, as we have highlighted in our earlier call as well, we are investing INR 35 crores approximately in total capital expenditure in Bihar with approximately INR 22 crores allocated to Phase-1 which will be capitalized by March-April.

items.statement: Committed Rs 21 crore for Indonesia acquisitions, expects 20%+ ROCE from FY26
items.quote: As communicated, we have already committed INR 21 crore for Indonesia acquisitions. This incremental investment is likely to yield ROCE of 20% plus from FY26 onward.

items.statement: Large part of capex to be committed in FY26 to reach 125-130 million pieces capacity
items.quote: As I mentioned, if you look at the installation, the capacity, how it is increasing, it is expected that large part of CAPEX will be committed in FY26 which will take us to 125-130 million pieces capacity.

items.statement: Installed capacity 90 million pieces by March 2025, 105-110 million by FY26, 125-130 million by FY27
items.quote: By the end of this year, we expect to reach around 90 million pieces of installed capacity. By FY26, we anticipate this figure will rise to 105-110 million pieces and by FY27, we expect to reach 125-130 million pieces.

items.statement: Capacity utilization around 78-80% adjusted to SAM by March 2025
items.quote: Our capacity utilization will hover as I mentioned adjusted to stand around 78%-80%.

items.statement: Order book crossing 74 million pieces for FY25 vs 56-57 million shipped last year
items.quote: So, this year we are seeing already like our order book is crossing, I think about 74 million odd numbers.

items.statement: Strong order book for spring/summer seasons in India, Q4 historically best quarter
items.quote: From India, we already have and we foresee good order book for upcoming spring and summer seasons products. Historically, Q4 is generally the best quarter for Indian operations. We again foresee this year.

items.statement: US apparel store sales $29.5B in Dec 2024, up 6% YoY; expects robust consumer spending
items.quote: The US apparel stores showed notable resilience in 2024 with estimated sales hitting $29.5 billion basis of 2024 December numbers, which is 6% higher on a year-on-year basis. We expect consumer spending to remain robust and steady throughout this year ahead.

items.statement: Bangladesh volumes grew high 30s% YoY in 9M FY25 despite country unrest
items.quote: In regards to Pearl, what we are seeing is we have grown significantly, like if I look at the numbers, it will be like high 30s that we are growing.

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin 9.1% in Q3 FY25, 8.9% in 9M FY25
items.quote: The adjusted EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at. 9.1%. We are also pleased to share that we crossed the INR 250 crore mark for consolidated adjusted EBITDA in 9-month period. Adjusted EBITDA increased by 25.5% year-on-year to INR 291.8 crore with an adjusted EBITDA margin of 8.9%.

items.statement: India adjusted EBITDA margin 3.7% in Q3 FY25, target high single digit then double digit
items.quote: Our adjusted EBITDA margin stood at 3.7% in Quarter 3 Financial Year '25. On the margin front in India, we still have large scope to grow significantly.

items.statement: Gross contribution fell from 56.68% to 50.50% due to product mix, but manufacturing cost also fell keeping EBITDA stable
items.quote: The gross contribution has come down from 56.68%-50.50%. The gross margin, which is after the manufacturing gross has remained the same because the manufacturing cost has come down because the product mix has changed the number of minutes are required to produce a style has really come down, hence the lesser manufacturing cost.

items.statement: Average realization ~Rs 600 per piece, function of product and customer mix
items.quote: Our average realization per piece continues to be around Rs. 600 per piece. Please note average realization is a function of product mix, customer mix.

items.statement: Rupee depreciation benefits topline and bottomline; hedges 20-30% of order book
items.quote: So, the depreciation of currency it only benefits us in improving the topline and the bottomline. We have a hedging strategy, but we are taking a hedging forward cover in a very calibrated manner and we take some 20%-30% of the order book get hedged.

items.statement: US vs non-US customer order book split trending 65-35 vs 85-15 three years ago
items.quote: As we expand, our market presence across these regions, our order book share from US based customers versus non-US based customers is trending towards 65-35. You may recall this was 85-15 three years back.

items.statement: Growing wallet share with existing customers and adding new financially sound growing customers
items.quote: Wherever we see that the customer is going strong, we are definitely trying to grab more and more wallet share of the customer. And at the same time, we are also finding out the new customers like who we think are the players for the future.

items.statement: Long-term credit rating upgraded to ICRA A stable from A-; short-term to ICRA A1 from A2+
items.quote: We are happy to share that our long-term credit rating has been upgraded to ICRA A stable from ICRA A- stable, whereas our short-term credit rating has been upgraded to ICRA A1 from ICRA A2+.

items.statement: Sales volume 53.8 million pieces in 9M FY25 vs 39.8 million in 9M FY24 (35% growth)
items.quote: For 9-months FY25, our sales volume has reached 53.8 million pieces compared to 39.8 million pieces in the same period of FY24.

items.statement: Bangladesh political unrest and financial irregularities made management cautious on acquiring ready assets; shifted to building own facilities
items.quote: Then what this turmoil taught us is that the links because in this kind of country, like, where the money came from and lot of financial irregularities that surfaced after this change of regime, so that made us much more cautious about going for a ready asset.

items.statement: India expanding beyond blouses/tops into new categories and Tier-2 cities to improve scale and margins
items.quote: We are expanding in other categories in India, building up those kind of manufacturing lines and marketing. Most of the customers that we are working with also knew that Pearl India does only blouse, so as we are acquiring the new customers and newer products so that is one strategy that we have worked upon.

items.statement: Bangladesh retains GSP benefits with EU, UK, Canada, Australia, China; logistics improving
items.quote: This country of Bangladesh still has advantages of lower cost, higher efficiency, productivity, availability of skilled workforce and a well experienced middle and lower-level management staff along with the favorable trade agreements with important markets that of European Union, UK, Canada, Australia and China.

items.statement: Management guided for 10-12% top-line growth and 15-20% bottom-line growth going forward
items.quote: We think that we c an grow at 10% to 12% at the top -line and 15% to 20% at the bottom -line

items.statement: Capex of INR30-40 crores per year planned for next 2-3 years for processing lines and warehouses
items.quote: But in terms of the capex, year-on-year, INR30 crores to INR40 crores should be at a very higher for the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Export revenue target of INR160 crores in 3-5 years, down from previous INR150-200 crore guidance
items.quote: 3 to 5 years, yes, definitely between close to INR160 crores we can see, 3 to 5 years.

items.statement: Maize volumes expected to grow 10-12% next year with acreages increasing
items.quote: We see very good growth in maize, like it is 10% to 12% growth in terms of the volumes for the next year.

items.statement: EBITDA margins declined due to higher production costs and employee costs; expected to recover as costs are passed to farmers
items.quote: As the revenue is flattish on a year-on-year basis, we see a slightly decline in EBITDA margins, which usually shouldn't be. But it should be corrected over the years.

items.statement: Cost of production increased 5-10% across most crops, some over 10%; company passing on increases in Rabi season and next year
items.quote: Usually, the cost of production is up by 5% to 10% in most of the crops. In some crops, it is more than 10%.

items.statement: New product contribution 30-40% in non-cotton crops, 10-15% in cotton; cotton new products expected to reach 30-40% in 2-3 years
items.quote: Contribution in most of the crops, except for cotton, all the other crops, like it remains in between 30% to 40%. Cotton contribution is slightly lower because most of the hybrids are pretty old hybrids. Cotton it should be like 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Cotton market share dropped to 8-10% from 13-14% last year; 20% share in Gujarat, 5-10% in other states
items.quote: We are in between that 8% to 10% market share now. So earlier, we were at 15%, but this year we lost.

items.statement: Seed production up 15-20% across all crops vs previous year; comfortable inventory position
items.quote: Across the board, across all crops, we have increased the production, both in terms o f the cotton and non -cotton segment. Production will be definitely higher like 25% to 30% more than the last year

items.statement: Cotton price increase of 1.5-2% last year vs 5-7% cost increase; government decision expected Feb-Mar; BG3 cotton trials complete, awaiting approval
items.quote: In terms of the absolute, it was like 1.5% or 2%. I don't remember that selling price is like INR857 now. It was from INR845 or INR840.

items.statement: Export sales down to INR18.23 crores from INR38.1 crores due to Bangladesh political unrest; expanded to new countries for future growth
items.quote: Export sales stand at INR18.23 crores as compared to INR38.1 crores in financial year '24. The decline is due to political unrest in Bangladesh.

items.statement: Employee cost up 16-17% in Q3 due to headcount increase across functions and 8-9% increments
items.quote: One, there are usual increments what we give. And the other thing is count also we have increased the count. We both will contribute for the employee cost.

items.statement: Cotton volumes down 35%, revenue down 27%; hybrid rice volumes up 14%, revenue up 27%; selection rice volumes up 18%, revenue up 34%; maize volumes up 8%, revenue up 25%
items.quote: Hybrid rice volumes increased by 14% and revenues by 27%. Selection rice volumes increased by 18% and revenue increased by 34%. Maize volumes increased by 8% and revenues increased by 25%. Volumes of cotton hybrid decreased by 35% and revenues decreased by 27%.

items.statement: Cotton margins under pressure if government price increase lower than cost increase; unseasonal weather events could impact paddy production
items.quote: Definitely, there will be pressure in the cotton margin, but the other crops will be doing well. So that's the reason as an overall basis, we will not be that much stressed.

items.statement: Cotton share loss due to old hybrids, competitive products, lower availability, and higher pricing vs competition
items.quote: It's a combination of all. One is that it was pretty old hybrids. There are some other competitive hybrids which are doing well. The other thing is the availability was also low and we were trying to realize more from the competition when compared to the competition.

items.statement: No M&A discussed; focus on organic growth through new product launches and export expansion
items.quote: But going forward, we see a very good market for exports. S o we have expanded to many other countries. That will eventually result in revenues in the next 2 to 3 years

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin above 20% for full FY25
items.quote: And I think we should be able to maintain this above 20% for the entire year of '24-'25.

items.statement: Prices bottomed out; uptrend expected by end of Q1 FY26
items.quote: Going forward, I think bottoming out '11. has already happened. We are not likely to see any further price reductions happening. There is only one way to go from here, which is up. Prices are only going to go on an uptrend in the coming quarters. And I think by end of Q1 of t he next financial year, we should see the turnaround happening, if not earlier

items.statement: Mill expansion of INR 735 crore on schedule, commissioning by March 2026
items.quote: We are also pleased to report that the mill expansion project, with an investment of INR 735 crores, is progressing as per schedule, with some project suppl ies and installations already having been completed. We expect the project to be fully commissioned by March 2026, further strengthening our operational capabilities and taking the production capacity up by 50

items.statement: Capacity to increase 50% after expansion commissioning
items.quote: We expect the project to be fully commissioned by March 2026, further strengthening our operational capabilities and taking the production capacity up by 50%.

items.statement: One machine upgrade in May (Q1), second in Q3, two in Q4 FY26; each shutdown 20-30 days
items.quote: So, we graded that into different time periods. One of the machines is probably going to go for renovation in the month of May. So, in Q1, there will be one machine which will be up for shutdown. In Q3, there will be a second one and in Q4, there will be two machines one by one. Not in the same month, in different months that will be up for a shutdown and upgrade.

items.statement: Demand expected to pick up with publishing season and government tenders; new education policy to drive textbook demand
items.quote: Lastly, we remain optimistic that the demand for writing and printing paper will pick up in the coming quarters, particularly with the upcoming publishing season and the anticipated release of government tenders.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin 18.66%; nine-month margin 22.02%
items.quote: For the quarter under review, operational income to date is INR 270 crores, reflecting a decline of 3% quarter-on-quarter. And EBITDA was INR 50 crores, which was 17% lower on a Q-on-Q basis. EBITDA margins stood at 18.66% and net profit for the quarter was INR 21 crores, which was down 30% Q-on-Q basis and PAT margins were reported at 7.77%.

items.statement: Cost optimization plan targets INR 40 crore annualized savings including INR 15 crore from AI-driven Project Nirmaan
items.quote: A comprehensive cost-optimization plan spanning 11 verticals was launched across the mill in November 2024, targeting annualized savings of INR 40 crores. This includes INR 15 crores in savings from Project Nirmaan, an AI-driven initiative.

items.statement: Q3 realization down ~6% QoQ; no price hike since start of year
items.quote: I would say this would be in the range of between Q2 and Q3, we would have reduced by about 6%.

items.statement: Wood prices rising due to MDF industry demand; sapling supply increased from 8 lakh to 40 lakh per year
items.quote: Yes. I believe so very clearly because prior to that, we were generating just about 8 lakh saplings a year. We have increased the supply of our saplings to a good phen omenal figure of 40 lakh saplings every year, and we are being able to sell all of that without any hesitation, without any effort around in the farming network that is attached and engaged with us

items.statement: Eucalyptus saplings take 3-4 years to mature; wood supply rising from past plantations
items.quote: So, essentially a good clonal variety of eucalyptus, which is generally the sapling that we grow, takes about three to four years to reach maturity.

items.statement: New Kuantum Korra variant with >90% agro-furnish developed; twin roll presses commissioned reducing chemical, effluent, water usage
items.quote: Additionally, a new variant of the Kuantum Korra product, made with over 90% agro-furnish, has been developed at our mill, offering exceptional smoothness and quality. These initiatives, apart from the various others undertaken in the past, have resulted in the company being able to withstand the market pressures of declining sales realization.

items.statement: Strong dealer network across India; 18+ paper varieties and many SKUs drive volume consistency
items.quote: We have a policy of being able to collect all our orders in advance and we produce to the orders that we collect. So, the volum e growth is largely depicted by the marketing strengths that we have and the fact that we are present in all corners of the country and are being able to dedicate our products and serve the market needs with dealers all across the country of ours. And we have a very large

items.statement: Imports rising, suppressing prices; exports hurt by Red Sea crisis; Kuantum insulated as 50% sales in North India
items.quote: Imports are increasing of the varieties that we are dealing with. And that is what is suppressing the market even further. And added to that, as a country, we were being able to export a fair bit of a volume to the European and Western markets. That, unfortunately, is not happening because of the Red Sea crisis and shipping volumes and costs coming up high.

items.statement: Industry requested anti-dumping duty; copier paper under consideration; hopeful post-elections
items.quote: Well, the association of which we are also a part, we have put in a request, we have put the government on to the stream to look at this very, very seriously. It has come in in parts, for instance, on copier paper, there is some kind of anti-dumping clauses that are in consideration. And we are hopeful that now with also the elections, the major elections getting over, the '11. government would be

items.statement: Tissue paper project put on hold to prioritize INR 735 crore machine renovation project
items.quote: We have put that project on hold for the time being. We postponed that because we saw a far better opportunity for ourselves in terms of renovating all our existing machines. And this project cost itself is to the tune of INR 735 crores, which we have set out and put out in public domain. I think this project per se is going to be more rewarding for us.

items.statement: Nine-month sales volume ~125,000 metric tonnes; quarterly run-rate 41,000-43,000 tonnes
items.quote: Despite these headwinds, we managed to achieve healthy volume growth, with paper sales volumes reaching almost 1,25,000 metric tonnes for the first nine months of this financial year.

items.statement: Geopolitical risks (wars, Red Sea crisis) impacting global trade; cycles shortened to 1-2 years
items.quote: But now that enough availability of wood is there, those kinds of trends have been reduced. And now it's largely a market dynamic that is happening and also impacted by geopolitical situations like wars happening, Russian-Ukrainian war, Red Sea crisis happening because of the West Asia crisis, things like that are impacting markets throughout the world.

items.statement: Barrier-coated paper technology for food packaging being evaluated with European suppliers; plastic packaging currently cheaper
items.quote: Even Kuantum as a company is engaging with the suppliers, chemical suppliers, machinery suppliers, all and most of them based out of Europe, who have got advanced technologies already in place to look at how to serve this application better than what they did or what we can do. '11. So, we are looking at this technology very, very seriously of how to create the rightful barrier coated papers, whic

items.statement: Power Gen demand in low and medium horsepower segments corrected by 40-45% due to CPCB IV transition and prebuy effect
items.quote: The overall market at th ese segments corrected by -- and by corrected, I mean, contracted by around 40

items.statement: High horsepower Power Gen market demand very strong with market share improvement
items.quote: On the high horsepower side, the market demand has been very strong, and we are slowly making progress. We have seen an improvement of our market share in this segment

items.statement: Industrial segment continues double-digit growth at 16% YoY driven by CEV BS-V emission norms and infrastructure demand
items.quote: On the industrial side, we continue to witness double-digit growth. Sales were INR268 crores for the quarter, registering a 16% growth year-on-year.

items.statement: Distribution and aftermarket business grew 15% YoY to INR208 crores
items.quote: Distribution and aftermarket business at INR208 crores registered a 15% growth for the quarter

items.statement: International B2B sales declined 17% YoY to INR112 crores due to absence of large one-time orders from previous year
items.quote: On the international side, the same quarter last year had some large onetime orders, which gave a significant upside to the numbers then. This quarter did not see a similar impact.

items.statement: Farm Mechanization sales nearly halved from INR19 crores to INR9 crores due to conscious pause to correct business model
items.quote: As a result, Farm Mechanization sales nearly halved from INR19 crores to INR9 crores this year.

items.statement: Power Gen demand expected to return to pre-emission norm levels in coming couple of quarters
items.quote: We see the demand levels coming back to the earlier levels in the coming couple of quarters.

items.statement: Expect better Q4 FY25 with industry volumes reaching 36,000-38,000 units from 32,000 in Q3
items.quote: And in Q4, our anticipation is we'll be closer to around 36,000 to 38,000. That's the anticipation.

items.statement: B2C margins expected to recover to pre-consolidation levels after plant transition completion
items.quote: I would say that now the fact that this consolidat ion has happened at the plant, we should see a recovery back to the pre-consolidation levels as far as the EBITDA profile is concerned

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin at 10.1% in Q3 FY25 vs 11.3% in Q3 FY24 due to operating leverage loss from lower sales
items.quote: EBITDA margin at 10.1% for quarter 3 FY '25 versus 11.3% for quarter 3 FY '24.

items.statement: Consolidated B2B segment PBIT margin ~14% decrease YoY; B2C segment loss before interest and tax of ~INR21 crores
items.quote: B2C segment revenue for the quarter was at INR224 crores, which is 14% degrowth year-on-year. The segment registered a loss before interest and tax of approximately INR21 crores.

items.statement: Arka Financial Services segment EBIT (ex-exceptional) at INR29 crores, down 23% YoY despite 43% revenue growth
items.quote: The segment EBIT, including -- excl uding exceptional item was at INR29 crores, that is 23% decrease year-on-year

items.statement: CPCB IV products priced 30-40% higher than CPCB II; pricing convergence seen across nodes
items.quote: if I just look at a thumb rule, I would say you can take 35% to 40% increase in scope of the product because the CPCB IV product is very different compared to what it was in CPCB II.

items.statement: CPCB IV pricing stable with node-by-node variations; some prices down, some revised up
items.quote: So, there's a process of price discovery that I'm sure each organization is doing. So, node by node, there are variations. In some cases, the prices have gone down. In some cases, they get revised upwards.

items.statement: Optiprime range (117 kVA to 3,000 kVA) seeing strong order book with confirmed orders up to 2,500 kVA
items.quote: We are getting not just a lot of interest, but also a lot of confirmed orders that we are executing. And those orders are honestly starting at about 117 kVA and today, we are executing orders of about 2,500 kVA also

items.statement: Ahmedabad plant consolidation completed; five units consolidated to single Sanand plant now fully operational
items.quote: We have completed our plant transition this quarter. As I had briefly mentioned in our earlier calls, it was a complex transition wherein we have consolidated five of our manufacturing units in Ahmedabad to a single plant at Sanand.

items.statement: Inventory at 77 days (higher due to CPCB norm changes and upcoming BSI upgradation); payables 70 days, receivables 43 days
items.quote: However, inventory level at 77 days is on the higher side due to CPCB norm changes and the upcoming BSI upgradation for the industrial engines.

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents net of debt at INR159 crores including treasury investments
items.quote: Cash and cash equivalents as at end of quarter 3 was INR159 crores. Please note, the cash and cash equivalent is net of debt and includes treasury investments.

items.statement: Board approved interim dividend of 125% (INR2.50 per share)
items.quote: I'm also happy to share that the Board of Directors has approved the interim dividend of 125%, that is INR2.50 per share.

items.statement: Arka Financial Services AUM at INR6,740 crores as of Dec 31, 2024
items.quote: As of December 31, 2024, the assets under management stood at INR6,740 crores.

items.statement: LGM year-to-date sales INR350 crores with EBITDA margin of 1.4%
items.quote: From year-to-date basis for LGM, we did a sales of INR350 crores with EBITDA of 1.4%.

items.statement: Exports nearly doubled since FY22; Middle East expected to pick up sooner than Americas
items.quote: if you look at where exports were when we started this journey, we have doubled our exports more or less, if you look at this year versus FY '22.

items.statement: Power Gen market share at ~30.3% excluding Telecom segment; HHP market share saw some deterioration
items.quote: So, what I was saying is that if you look at our market share for the last quarter in Q3, we were at roughly at about 30.3%, excluding Telecom segment.

items.statement: CPCB IV emission norms transition completed; CEV BS-V effective Jan 1, 2025 for industrial engines
items.quote: With CEV BS-V going live from January 1 of this year, we continue to see strong demand from the infrastructure sector.

items.statement: CPCB II inventory in larger industry ecosystem depleted over last 2 quarters; manufacturer inventory fully consumed
items.quote: As far as the entire -- I mean, the larger industry is concerned, we did see different players liquidating CPCB II in the last 2 quarters also. But all of that seems to have depleted now

items.statement: Power Gen portfolio heavily weighted to LHP/MHP; HHP contribution smaller but growing with Optiprime range up to 3,000 kVA
items.quote: the overall product mix that we have is largely on the LHP, MHP side in terms of the Power Gen revenue case. So even if I compare it to our industrial business, which is growing at double digits growth.

items.statement: Consolidated loan AUM grew 34% YoY to INR 1,11,308 crore as of 9M FY25
items.quote: We had a consolidated loan assets under management, which grew by 34% year-on-year to INR1,11,308 crores as of ninth month as against INR82,773 crores last year.

items.statement: Standalone gold loan portfolio grew 37% YoY adding INR 26,305 crore in Q3 FY25
items.quote: For Q3 financial year '25, our stand-alone assets under management witnessed a significant growth of INR26,305 crores driven by a robust 37% year-on-year growth on our core gold loan portfolio.

items.statement: Gold loans increased by INR 21,660 crore in 9M FY25 registering 29% growth
items.quote: During 9 months, the gold loans increased by INR21,660 crores, registering a growth of 29%.

items.statement: FY26 loan growth guidance set at 15% will be revisited after next quarter
items.quote: The guidance for 2026, as usual, we are giving only the usual 15% guidance for 2026 also. We will revisit it after next quarter.

items.statement: FY25 guidance revised from 15% to 25% but already achieved 29% in 9M; not raising further
items.quote: So last quarte r, we revised the guidance from 15% to 25 percentage for the whole year. But in the third quarter, we overachieved it. We have reached 29 percentage

items.statement: Incremental cost of borrowing roughly 9% with most bank loans MCLR linked annual reset
