items.quote: Further, close to Rs. 14 billion of new orders won since FY21 are expected to have the SOP by this financial year and further Rs. 10 billion are expected to have SOP in FY26.

items.statement: Sales to Bajaj growing at 10.8% CAGR FY22-FY25E; other OEMs at 13% CAGR; winning orders across all product verticals with other OEMs
items.quote: From FY22 to what is expected at the end of this financial year, our sales to Bajaj have been growing at a robust compounded annual growth rate of 10.8% in spite the high base and the high content per vehicle.

items.statement: Signed technical assistance agreement with leading Korean entity for 4W suspension (shock absorbers/struts); will be second source supplier initially
items.quote: We are happy to state that one such technical assistance agreement for 4W suspension has been signed last month with a leading Korean entity. This technical assistance agreement will give Endurance Technologies the complete capabilities to manufacture and sell shock absorbers and struts to a large range of four-wheelers.

items.statement: 4W braking technology partnership likely with BWI (existing 2W ABS partner); target SOP Q4 FY26
items.quote: The technology for the high-end braking systems will likely come from BWI, who is already a partner as you know for the 2W ABS. We are at a fairly advanced stage in talks with them.

items.statement: EV sales Rs. 722M in Q3 FY25 (3.5% of sales), ~2x Q1 FY25; net EV order wins Rs. 9,631M since FY22 (after removing Rs. 1,580M from distressed OEMs)
items.quote: Our sales to electric vehicles in Q3 FY25 was Rs. 722 million, which is about 3.5% of our sales. This is close to double our Q1 FY25 sales.

items.statement: 96% of product range (ex-clutch assemblies) is EV agnostic, usable in both EV and ICE models
items.quote: We have always maintained that our product range except clutch assemblies, which is almost 96% of our range, are EV agnostic and is used in both EV and internal combustion engine models.

items.statement: Suspension: Won Rs. 1,413M peak annual sales orders in FY25 (ex-Bajaj) from Hero, HMSI, Kawasaki, e-scooters; inverted front fork expansion
items.quote: In FY25, so far we have won orders to the tune of Rs. 1,413 million of peak annual sales. These are from various OEM customers and for their various platforms.

items.statement: Braking: Won Rs. 1,710M new orders in FY25 (ex-Bajaj) from Hero, HMSI, Mahindra, RE, TVS; now supplying to every prominent 2W OEM
items.quote: We have won Rs. 1,710 million of new orders till date in FY'25 from multiple OEMs. With these inroads, we would now be supplying to every prominent two-wheeler OEM in the country.

items.statement: Transmission: Won Hero and RE clutch orders adding 1M units/year and >Rs. 1,000M sales in FY26; Adler Assist/Slip clutch orders won
items.quote: A couple of significant new wins are the clutches from Hero MotoCorp and Royal Enfield, which will help us to increase the annual sales of 1 million more clutch assemblies and increase sales value by more than Rs. 1,000 million in the next financial year.

items.statement: Drive shaft: Won Rs. 450M new orders in FY25; expect ~Rs. 1,000M annual run rate including Bajaj; 4W drive shaft SOP FY26
items.quote: Despite this being a new vertical, with no 2W end use, we soon expect to hit an annual revenue run rate of close to Rs. 1,000 million per annum, including orders from Bajaj Auto. We expect to start SOP also for 4W drive shaft in FY26.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 consolidated revenue Rs. 28.8B (+11.3% YoY), PAT Rs. 1.84B (+21.1% YoY); margin expansion from lower material cost in India and lower other costs in Europe
items.quote: During this quarter, the company performed well and turned in revenues of Rs. 21.9 billion and Rs. 28.8 billion respectively for the standalone company and the consolidated company. This translates to a year-on-year growth of 9.2% and 11.3% respectively.

items.statement: European subsidiaries: Q3 revenue +21.2% YoY, EBITDA +26.7% YoY; grew despite flat market
items.quote: It is important to note that our European companies have defied many odds to post an impressive year-on-year growth of 21.2% in Q3 revenues, and a growth of 26.7% in Q3 EBITDA.

items.statement: European operations: past 3 quarters double-digit growth; Q3 closed with 21% turnover increase, 27% EBITDA increase, 17.5% net result increase
items.quote: I want to underline that we closed the previous quarter with 21% increase of turnover, 27% of EBITDA, and 17.5% of net result.

items.statement: Current capacities: 6M 2W braking systems, 8M 2W brake discs, 1.5M 3W tandem master cylinders, 1M 3W drum brake assemblies, 650K 2W ABS
items.quote: Just reminding you that our capacities at present are six million 2W braking systems, eight million 2W brake discs, 1.5 million 3W tandem master cylinders, one million 3W drum brake assemblies and 650,000 2W ABSs or the anti-lock braking systems.

items.statement: State incentives: Remaining Rs. 80M under 2013 scheme to be booked in FY26-FY27; 2019 scheme applications complete, awaiting eligibility certificate
items.quote: The remaining INR 80 million under the 2013 scheme will be booked in FY26 and FY27. For the 2019 scheme, we are at a stage where we have submitted our applications and our documentation is complete.

items.statement: European operations: YTD new car sales -0.4% but Endurance subsidiaries revenue +16.1%, EBITDA +22.1%; Q3 FY25 revenue +21.8%, EBITDA +27.4% YoY
items.quote: despite the difficult market, whe re the year-to-date new car sales have dropped by 0.4% compared to the same period of last year, our subsidiaries grew their revenues by 16.1% and EBITDA by 22.1

items.statement: Gender diversity at 20% of total hiring; Winning the Women program; Saksham capability building; wellness programs; right-sizing organization pyramid
items.quote: We have been actively right sizing our organization pyramid to ensure agility and accountability. On talent acquisition, we are focusing on strategic workforce planning at all levels with a focus on gender diversity, which is at 20% of our total hiring.

items.statement: German region facing inflationary pressures from high energy costs; management finding mitigation actions
items.quote: The German region experienced inflationary pressures due to high energy cost which the management is finding mitigation actions for.

items.statement: EV order numbers toned down for internal business plans due to market volatility and OEM financial status
items.quote: We also state here that given the volatility of the markets, particularly for electric vehicles and the status of some of the OEM clients, we further tone down these numbers down for our internal business plans.

items.statement: French authority audit of the drug product site in France completed successfully in January; official GMP certification expected by end of Q4 FY25.
items.quote: It was planned to be in December and unfortunately, because of the flu, the inspector postponed it to January, but it was done in January, and it was extremely successful. So now we are expecting the official GMP certification of that site coming by the end of this quarter.

items.statement: Chinese affiliate audited by local authority; Chinese certification expected to enable pursuit of Chinese pharmaceutical market.
items.quote: With our Chinese affiliates, same as France, we have been audited by the local authority. And same as France, we should get the local Chinese certification, which is going to allow us to chase for Chinese business.

items.statement: Development requests picking up after mid-year slowdown, enabling new project and customer bookings soon.
items.quote: Development activities, 2024 has been a bit more difficult on that side, especially by the middle of the year. But lately, we have seen that the number of requests from the market is picking up, and that's a very good news because that means that we will be able sooner rather than later to book new projects and new customers for sure.

items.statement: France booked important new customers and orders, giving high confidence to achieve forecast and ambitions for next year.
items.quote: Alongside with this, in France, we have also booked a number of important new customers and orders, which are placing us in a very high confidence that we will achieve the forecast as well as our ambitions for next year.

items.statement: Netherlands cholesterol orders coming in lately, likely to exceed target for that business unit.
items.quote: And especially on cholesterol, we have seen a number of orders coming in lately, which are going in the right directions and probably we will be able to go beyond the target for that business unit.

items.statement: Capex for first 9 months at USD 20.8 million; on track for full-year budget.
items.quote: The capital expenditure for the first 9 months stood at USD 20.8 million. So, we are very much on track as far as the budget is concerned for the capital expenditure for the end of the year.

items.statement: Expected annual capex of $20-25 million over next three years with no significant capex outlay planned.
items.quote: What we expect is that overall, the capex per year should be somewhere between $20 million to $25 million or somewhere around that.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin 20.6%; 9M FY25 margin 16%; full-year target 17-18% considering France losses and Netherlands subdued performance.
items.quote: For the full year we should be at about 17% to 18%. For the next year or 20% kind of margin is something which needs to be sustainable.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin progression: ~20% next year, ~22% FY27, ~24-25% by FY28 as India performance improves.
items.quote: I think it would still be at about 22, and then it will go to say 24, 25

items.statement: Revenue guidance for FY25: INR 2,700 crore plus; EBITDA guidance: INR 400 crore plus.
items.value: INR 2,700 crore+ revenue, INR 400 crore+ EBITDA
items.quote: I think we should end the year with about INR2700 crore plus kind of revenue. So that would be the idea. However, in terms of EBITDA we would be in excess of INR400 crores.

items.statement: 3-5 year revenue CAGR target of around 10% driven by Dishman-Carbogen integration and incremental Swiss orders.
items.quote: We expect that it would be safe to assume a CAGR of around 10% if you take a 3 to 5 year view.

items.statement: Net debt target: reduce net leverage to 1.5-2.0x in next 3 years; absolute net debt around CHF 120 million.
items.quote: So, if I have to give a figure just on the net debt, I would say that it should be somewhere around 120-odd million.

items.statement: Net debt at 31 Dec 2024: CHF 168 million, down CHF 5 million from 30 Sep 2024.
items.quote: As far as the net debt is concerned, as of 31st of December, this stood at CHF 168 million, which is a decrease by about CHF 5 million as compared to September 30, 2024.

items.statement: Interest cost increased 47% YoY in Q3 due to covenant breach step-up; expected to reduce by ~4% (2% from Jan, 2% by Mar) as covenants now met.
items.quote: However, now with the improved performance of Q2 and Q3, we are now meeting the financial covenants and that should reduce the interest cost by almost about 4%. So, there would be a reduction of 2% that would be visible from January of this year and another 2% by March of this year.

items.statement: Q3 CRAMS revenue split: ~60% commercial, 40% development; full-year norm ~50-50 but commercial share higher this year.
items.quote: So out of the total revenue in the quarter, roughly about -- so roughly about 60% of the revenue came from commercial and 40% came from development work. Usually, our split for the full year is roughly 50-50, but this year, the commercial revenue portion has been much higher as compared to development.

items.statement: ADC business currently only development revenue (~$15-20M); commercial production expected FY26-27 with potential $15-20M revenue per product.
items.quote: For the time being, it's only development because we are only working on the development project with our customers, with one of our main partners in that field. We are finishing the development work this year. That means that the next fiscal year will be kind of a pause because with the amount produced and the time they get their full market authorizations, the business is going to resume by comm

items.statement: ~17 ADC projects in late phase; historically ~10% Phase III attrition to commercial, implying 1-2 future commercial products.
items.quote: We should have right now about 17 products in late phase. So that means one to two products should go to commercial at some point.

items.statement: Both manufacturing lines in France operationalized; second line started January 2025; depreciation reflects one line for Q3, both for Q4.
items.quote: We have operationalized both the manufacturing lines in France. So, the current depreciation figure of INR71.9 crores for Q3 FY '25 takes into account the depreciation of one manufacturing line because the second one got operationalized in January of this year.

items.statement: Global sales meeting in India to reinforce Dishman-Carbogen collaboration and drive synergies for global strategy.
items.quote: Last but not least, this week and next week, we are organizing a global sales meeting here in India with our drug substance people at Carbogen Amcis to reinforce the collaborations between Dishman Carbogen Amcis and Carbogen Amcis and to drive the synergie s between the 2 companies with the objective to present a global strategy and enable more business for both companies

items.statement: France subsidiary Q3 revenue $3M, loss $1.1M; expected ~$9M revenue FY25, ~$18M FY26 with breakeven next financial year.
items.quote: As far as the French performance is concerned, the revenue was about $3 million in the quarter. And the loss was $1.1 million in the quarter. So, what we expect is by the end of the year, we should be close to $9 million of revenue. And in the next year, what we expect is we should be closer to about 18 million, and that would mean that we would be breaking even in the next financial year.

items.statement: India CRAMS 9M revenue up 61% YoY to INR 209 crore; India Quats & Generics up 31% YoY; FY26 expected as real turnaround year for India facilities.
items.quote: And for the 9 months, this number stood at INR209 crores as compared to INR130 crores of the 9 months of FY '24, which is an increase of 61%. The India Quats and Generic business, which is largely done out of the Naroda facility did a revenue of INR41.5 crores as compared to INR28.68 crores in the quarter, which is an increase by 31%. And for the full year, it did a revenue of about INR87 crores.

items.statement: Not a peptide producer; GLP-1/peptide drug conjugation not core business; would require significant capex and new capabilities.
items.quote: One thing that is for sure, we are not peptide producer per se on our side. So, we have questions around those kind of things, technology that are surrounding those concepts, but GLP-1 itself and the peptide production is not our core business. This is for sure. And if we have to go there, that would request a significant amount of capex to invest as well as another knowledge that is not core of o

items.statement: FY25 operating income growth guidance 12-13% with ~11% EBITDA margin; FY26 revenue target INR 2,000 crores with 13-14% EBITDA margin
items.quote: So this fiscal, we have a guidance of 12% to 13% kind of revenue growth with an EBITDA level of approximately 11%. And next year, as we have already also mentioned in our presentation, we have taken a vision of achieving INR2,000 crores revenue in FY '26 with an EBITDA level of somewhere between 13.5%, like from 13% to 14% kind of an EBITDA level.

items.statement: Project Lakshya distributor count rose to 315 from 290 in March 2024; 25 new distributors added in 9M FY25
items.quote: In the first nine months of FY '25, we welcomed 25 new distributors to the initiative, bringing our total distributor count to 315, up from 290 in March '24.

items.statement: Project Lakshya share of domestic sales increased from 26% in FY24 to 31% in 9M FY25; target 65-70% by FY26
items.quote: We are pleased to report that Project Lakshya's share of domestic sales has risen from 26% in FY '24 to 31% in nine months FY '25. Looking ahead, we expect that by FY '26, 65% to 70% of our revenue will be contributed by distributors under Project Lakshya.

items.statement: Announced capex for factory and spinning plant completed; only 2-3 MW solar capacity pending over next 6-12 months
items.quote: Yes. Mostly our capex, which we announced earlier in '21-'22 with regard to our factory and the spinning plant, we already completed. And we also capitalized in the month of December only. So almost our announced capex plan is already almost completed. Now there is only a pending 2, 3 megawatt solar capacity we have to add in the coming 6 to 12 months.

items.statement: Renewable power generation capacity reached 8 MW as of December 2024, up 2 MW in H1 FY25
items.quote: As of December '24, our total power generation capacity reached 8 megawatts, marking an increase of 2 megawatts in the first half of the fiscal year '24-'25.

items.statement: South region target to grow from 8-9% to 13-15% of revenue in 2-3 years; Mahesh Babu onboarded as brand ambassador for Dollar Bigboss in South
items.quote: So in two to three years' time period, we really want to see South India's contribution coming up from 8% to 9% to 13% to 15% kind of a contribution level. And apart from that, North India is heavy because we count Rajasthan and UP two big states as part of North India itself.

items.statement: QIP fundraising plan deferred due to prevailing market conditions; will reassess future fundraising needs
items.quote: Now in view of the prevailing marketing condition, the company has decided to defer its plan to raise funds through the qualified QIP. We believe this decision will allow us to better assess our requirement and ensure that any further -- any future fundraising efforts are in the best interest of our shareholder and the company.

items.statement: JV Pepe Innerfashion Private Limited revenue doubled to INR 26 crores in 9M FY25 from ~INR 10-11 crores in 9M FY24; first profitable year with ~INR 5 crores EBITDA
items.value: INR 26 cr revenue, INR 5 cr EBITDA
items.quote: Last year, for nine months ended, we had a revenue of somewhere around INR10 crores to INR11-point-something crores. But this year, nine months ended, we have doubled our sales. Currently, we are standing at around INR26 crores. And for the first time, this is a first time -- first fiscal year where we are seeing good profitability also coming in with an overall EBITDA of around INR5 crores in INR

items.statement: Total volume grew 8.2% YoY in Q3 FY25; 9M FY25 operating income INR 1,161 crores (+8.3% YoY); PAT INR 20 crores in Q3 (+12.8% YoY) and INR 62 crores in 9M (+8.2% YoY)
items.quote: Our operating income in Q3 FY '25 stood at INR 381 crores, marking a 14.8% year-on-year growth. Over the first nine months, operating income stood at INR 1,161 crores, reflecting an 8.3% year-on-year growth. Additionally, total volume grew by 8.2% in Q3 FY '25 over the same quarter of the previous year. Profit after tax for the quarter grew by 12.8% year-on-year to around INR20 crores. For the fir

items.statement: ASP increased ~7% on 9M basis; gross margins improving due to product mix change and premiumization
items.quote: And plus if you see with the product mix change, this year, our ASP has gone up by 7%, like there's a value growth of 7% overall on a nine months basis as well. So our gross margins are also improving.

items.statement: Athleisure segment contributing 12-13% of total sales and growing well from a low base; Thermal and Force NXT showing strong growth
items.quote: Athleisure. So athleisure segment is doing well. Like if you compare it with the COVID times, it's not like that. But yes, since the base is low, then we are seeing good growth coming in from athleisure as well. But overall, it is contributing around 12% to 13% to our total sales, athleisure as a category.

items.statement: Quick commerce presence: enrolled in Swiggy Instamart and Zepto; agreement with Blinkit near completion; also on Flipkart Minutes and Myntra quick commerce
items.quote: Yes. So for quick commerce, we have already enrolled ourselves in Swiggy Instamart. We are present in Zepto also. And we are on the verge of completing our agreement with Blinkit. And plus with the marketplaces like Flipkart, Amazon and Myntra coming up with their own quick commerce department and channels, we are already doing business with Flipkart, which is by the name of Minutes, and Myntra al

items.statement: Working capital days elevated at 171 in Q3 due to seasonal inventory build for Q4; inventory days typically 95-97 days as industry standard
items.quote: So the overall increase in the net working capital days is because -- mostly because of the inventory days. There is not much movement in the debtor days, I would say. And inventory, we had to stock up like the -- for the Q2 and Q3, it was mostly the summers, which was stocked up. And since our Q4 is quite heavy, we have to build inventory in advance. So it's just seasonality thing.

items.statement: Rainwear segment (Dollar Protect Rainguard) grew 90% in 9M FY25 to INR 22 crores revenue at ~23-24% EBITDA margin
items.quote: Like we have launched raincoat very recently. And this year, nine months ended, we are seeing a 90% kind of growth and with a revenue of INR22 crores in nine months and at an EBITDA level which is around 23%, 24%.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA margin of 10%-12% in near future
items.quote: We are aiming for around 10%-12% in the near future.

items.statement: Expects normalized revenue growth of 10%-15% and aims to do better
items.quote: But we expect to get back to some sort of normalized growth of between 10%-15%, and we expect to do better than that.

items.statement: Gross margin stable at 77%-80%, best in class among Indian winemakers
items.quote: I can tell you to the best of our knowledge, our gross margins are probably the best in class amongst the winemakers in the country and we are at around 77%-80% gross margin today and that has been very stable over the last many quarters.

items.statement: EBITDA margin dropped to 4.88% for 9M FY25 from 13.2% due to higher brand investments
items.quote: On EBITDA, our EBITDA margin has dropped from about 13.2% to about 4.88% for the current 9 months and that is largely because the company has increased its brand investments and generally expenses in line with some new product launches, new initiatives, and many of those things will o nly begin to show its rewards in the coming quarters

items.statement: Adding 40 acres vineyards by H2 FY25 and 60 acres before Q2 FY26; new 50,000 sq ft winery operational
items.quote: To strengthen our world -class wine making business, we are scaling up our production by adding 40 acres of vineyards by H2 FY25 with another 60 acres planned to be planted before Q2 FY26, ensuring the higher quality grape supply for our most premium wines. Additionally, we have commenced operations at our new 50,000 sq. ft. winery building.

items.statement: New winery and solar investments to save over Rs. 10 million annually
items.quote: The new winery building and the investments made in solar energy will result in savings of over Rs. 10 million in costs annually.

items.statement: Total vineyard area to reach 400 acres with current additions
items.quote: We will have 400 acres.

items.statement: Over 70% of sales from premium and luxury wines
items.quote: Over 70% of our sales come from premium and luxury wines, and we remain geared to sustain our position here as the category further develops within AlcoBev.

items.statement: Canned wine portfolio grew 20% in FY24, continues as focus area
items.quote: We have grown 20% in FY24, and it continues to be a good focus area.

items.statement: Launched 'Pour Room' wine and coffee bars with Blue Tokai in Bangalore; plans expansion
items.quote: During the quarter, we launched 'Pour Room', which is our brand for wine and coffee bars in collaboration with Blue Tokai . The very first 'Pour Room' has opened at Koramangala in Bangalore to an encouraging response. This venture is set to expand across Bangalore and other major cities, offering consumers an experiential setting to enjoy our wines.

items.statement: Soft launched RTD 'Shotgun' as category broadening initiative
items.quote: I am glad to share that our RTD offering, 'Shotgun', has been soft launched in the current quarter. 'Shotgun' is an accessible, all occasion wine-based drink and we see vast potential in it as category broadening initiative.

items.statement: HoReCa channel increased listings YoY across prestigious restaurants and hotels
items.quote: HoReCa remains a strong growth channel for us, which increased listings YoY across prestigious restaurants and hotels.

items.statement: Industry grew only ~2% this year; company calls it an aberration
items.quote: Overall, the entire AlcoBev industry has grown only about 2%. This is as per some even newspaper article which came just day before yesterday. This year has been a flat year for more or less the entire AlcoBev industry.

items.statement: Inventory cycle typically 5-6 months including 90 days winemaking process
items.quote: In terms of inventory, I mean, wine as a process takes at least 90 odd days to make in tanks. You've got 3 months there just in the process of wine making. And then after that, it is carrying at least a couple of months of sale inventory. Our business inventory turnover ratio by nature of the business is fairly long, that is one part

items.statement: Alcohol regulations are state subjects; price increases require state-by-state approval
items.quote: It is absolutely like any other AlcoBev, we have to go to each state, alcohol regulations are state subjects, any price increase, etc. has to be discussed with each state individually.

items.statement: Sustained brand investments needed for 1-1.5 years for category development
items.quote: I think wine, for it to be better understood and communicated, I think it will require a sustained form of investments and brand initiatives. I believe we see this at least for another 1-1.5 years.

items.statement: Brand investment spend at 8%-9% of top-line
items.quote: But we continue to spend about 8%-9% of our top-line on brand investment.

items.statement: Canned wine gross margin comparable to bottles, a few percentage points lower
items.quote: we have grown 20% in FY24, and it continues to be a good focus area. On the cost side see aluminum cans are also more sustainable form of packaging. This whole concept is also very close to our heart that we wish to be as sustainable as possible. Aluminum is recycled N number of times and yes it's a more economical form of packaging. But in terms of gross margins, packaging is only one part. There

items.statement: Present pan-India except Chhattisgarh, Bihar, and 1-2 northeastern states
items.quote: We are present pan India. The only states we are not present are Chhattisgarh, the dry states like Bihar and 1-2 states in the northeast.

items.statement: Historical wine business revenue grew from Rs. 92 crore in FY21 to ~Rs. 200 crore in FY24 (>20% CAGR)
items.quote: But if you see our historical performance in FY21, our wine business falls about Rs. 92 crore. And now in FY24, we are almost Rs. 200 crore. That shows the growth of more than 20%.

items.statement: Performance moderated due to higher dry days, RTM transitions, and lower urban consumption
items.quote: The year thus far has seen moderated performance, owing to a few factors, including a higher number of dry days during the period coupled with transition to new RTMs in key states. The country has also encountered lower urban consumption that has had impact on our category as well.

items.statement: Developing exclusive vineyard resort at Akluj, Maharashtra; expects opening in FY27
items.quote: As you may know , we are developing an exclusive vineyard resort at Akluj, Maharashtra. The work on this is in advanced stages of planning and we expect to open in FY27, as a first of its kind property in India with multiple experiences besides vineyard tourism and luxury stays are being planned.

items.statement: Investing in backend processes and sales technology to enhance efficiency and margins
items.quote: As we gear up for the next phase of business expansion, we are also investing in backend processes and updating technology in sales and distribution to enhance efficiency and operational control. While making us more agile, these programs are designed to make us leaner and contribute towards better margin.

items.statement: Management says blended PAT margins will be maintained as IPP share grows from ~13% to 21-22%
items.quote: PAT margin -- we'll be able to maintain the PAT margin because our business is a combination of CPP and IPP. I can tell you that going forward, our IPP component, which at present, I think, is 13% i.e. 13% is IPP this quarter and 87% is the CPP, which we plan to take it to the level of 22% to 21% kind of going forward.

items.statement: Order book stands at approximately 2.86 GW as of Jan 15
items.quote: But I can give you a megawatt that we had shown in the presentation, we have approximately 2.86 gigawatt of as on Jan 15.

items.statement: IPP capex: wind INR 6-8 cr/MW, solar INR 3-3.85 cr/MW depending on land and evacuation
items.quote: See, hybrid, I mean, if I say, around INR 6 crores to INR 8 crores for the wind portion, you can say, INR 6 crores to INR 8 crores per megawatt for the wind portion. And when it comes to the solar portion, it ranges from INR 3 crores to INR 3.75 crores, INR 3.85 crores depending upon the land and everything.

items.statement: Demand for renewables is increasing due to government push and national targets
items.quote: No, I see the demand rather increasing in this space because a lot of players are entering into it. A lot of benefit. Government's push is more important. You see light of government has started on the renewable. They are also thinking of going into offshore windmill and everything.

items.statement: Execution timeline: pure solar 100 MW can be done in 6-8 months; IPP projects targeted within 12-15 months vs 2-year PPA allowance
items.quote: See, executing, if we go full fledge and we put all our resources, we can do within -- if it is pure solar, it can be done within 6 to 8 months also. This is very short period depending upon all other factors.

items.statement: Module prices ~60% of capex/MW; procured from Tier 1 suppliers like Waaree, Emmvee; exact pricing confidential
items.quote: It depends. I mean around 60%,would be the module price.

items.statement: Milestone billing causes quarterly EBITDA cyclicality: Q2 higher (service component), Q3/Q4 lower (material component); pattern repeats yearly
items.quote: No. I explained this particular question that you need to understand that we do billing on the milestone basis. And some milestones are there where the service component is built. mostly, these components are built in the middle where there is a slack flat period where the materials or anything take a slack.

items.statement: Pledged shares ~45% of promoter Faruk Patel's holding (~21-22% of total equity); collateral for old SBI loan (INR 400-500 cr for Khavda), not for fund raise; SBI to release pledge
items.quote: So at present, the pledge that is there, I think it's 45% of what Faruk sir's total share is. So it would be around -- on the total pledge, it would be around 21% to 22%.

items.quote: I can tell you that going forward, our IPP component, which at present, I think, is 13% i.e. 13% is IPP this quarter and 87% is the CPP, which we plan to take it to the level of 22% to 21% kind of going forward.

items.statement: Revenue growth minimum 60% YoY; will surely surpass

items.statement: International opportunities at nascent stage; approached by foreign players; will not disclose until constructive roadmap ready

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY25 guidance with year-on-year growth on pro forma combined basis and accelerated growth trajectory in FY26
items.quote: We reaffirm our FY'25 guidance with year-on-year growth on a pro forma combined basis for the full year and with an accelerated growth trajectory in FY'26.

items.statement: RFQs doubled year-on-year in 9 months FY25 reflecting strong inbound inquiries from global pharma and biotech

items.statement: Q3 FY25 adjusted EBITDA margin at 38.7%; 9 months FY25 at 34.8%

For the 9 months of FY'25, our revenue growth is 5% year-on-year, reinforcing our resilience and long-term scalability with adjusted EBITDA margins at 34.8%.

items.statement: Phase-3 pipeline expanded to 15 projects with 9 active molecules, up from 12 projects and 7 molecules last quarter

items.statement: Rs 2.3 billion capex invested in 9 months FY25 for capacity expansion; growth capex of Rs 400 crore added via inorganic acquisitions

items.quote: Capacity side, as you understand when the cyclical nature was slightly hitting us, we don't have any capacity challenge right now and we have enough invested in the existing site and also in additional site of Suryapet and these molecules are predominantly manufacturing at our Pashamylaram.

items.statement: Onboarded one of top 5 global pharma leaders for early to mid-phase projects; expanding commercial presence across US, EU, Japan

items.statement: NJ Bio acquisition provides onshore US capabilities for ADC manufacturing; expanding commercial presence in US, EU, Japan

items.quote: Investment in injectables about INR75 crores.

items.statement: No break-even guidance for injectables; management refuses to disclose injectable opex due to cost-plus competitive sensitivity
items.quote: So we have not given any kind of guidance. Of course the goal of the entire management is to achieve the break-even milestone as soon as possible. But we have not given any guidance and we would request you to let us stay in that.

items.statement: Working capital days and net cash not disclosed; stated to be within typical range
items.quote: So again Neelam, since those are not part of LR, we are not sort of disclosing those numbers. But we are still within range of what we have been typically.

items.statement: Targeting KFC brand contribution margin of 19-20% at about 100,000 ADS over a few quarters
items.quote: we are targeting KFC to get to 19 to 20% margin at about 100,000 ADS , and we are tracking on that . It will take us a few quarters to be able to get there

items.statement: Plan to add 20-25 stores in Thailand (8-9% growth) and target 3-4% SSSG for 11-12% revenue growth in FY26
items.quote: We plan to add about 20 to 25 stores, which is 8 to 9% of the stores that we have. And then on top , we are targeting a SSSG of about 3 to 4% which should give us about 11 to 12% revenue growth.

items.statement: Will moderate Pizza Hut expansion further versus current pace; expansion dependent on brand performance
items.quote: Going forward, as we have spoken in the past, we will be moderating Pizza Hut expansion, and you will see even further lower numbers versus what we have done so far.

items.statement: Three new QSR brands planned for launch from Q1 FY26 (April onwards)
items.quote: Yes, we are on track from Quarter 1 of the next financial year.

items.statement: Focus on small format stores which are highly capital efficient and offer stronger payback potential
items.quote: A key driver of this has been our focus on small format stores over the past few years which are highly capital efficient and offer stronger payback potential.

items.statement: Added 111 net new stores in Q3 FY25, total store count 2,032 as of Dec 31, 2024
items.quote: In Quarter 3, we added 111 net new stores, bringing our total store count to 2 ,032 as of December 31st, 2024.

items.statement: Core brands KFC, Pizza Hut, Costa added 107 stores in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Our core brands KFC, Pizza Hut and Costa added 107 stores in Quarter 3, thereby further strengthening our brand performance.

items.statement: KFC India added 44 stores in Q3 FY25, total 689 stores
items.quote: KFC in India added 44 new stores in Q3 FY25. With this, the total store count for KFC in India stands at 689 stores at the end of Q3 FY25.

items.statement: Pizza Hut India added 51 stores in Q3 FY25, total 644 stores
items.quote: During the quarter, Pizza Hut added 51 new stores, reaching a total count of 644 stores in India.

items.statement: Costa Coffee added 2 stores in Q3 FY25, total 209 stores
items.quote: Costa Coffee added two new stores during the quarter, reaching a cumulative store count of 209 stores.

items.statement: International stores total 374 with 9 KFC stores added in Thailand and 1 Pizza Hut store in Nepal in Q3
items.quote: Total number of international stores was 374 with the addition of 9 new KFC stores in Thailand and 1 Pizza Hut store in Nepal in Quarter 3.

items.statement: Consumer sentiment remained subdued but green shoots of recovery seen in metro and large cities during festive season
items.quote: While the overall consumer sentiment remained a little subdued , during the festive season our QSR in general and DIL witnessed some green shoots of recovery in the metro and large cities.

items.statement: KFC and Pizza Hut clocked highest-ever sales on big festival days driven by value menu items and discounts
items.quote: With both brands experiencing recovery in demand by clocking highest -ever sales of big festival days.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin 68.7%, down 60 bps QoQ due to food inflation in oil, chicken, cheese, coffee beans
items.quote: The gross margin for the consolidated business was 68.7%, a drop of 60 basis points versus the previous quarter. The impact on gross margins was primarily due to food inflation that we have seen in core brands, driven by rising oil, chicken, cheese and coffee bean pricing.

items.statement: Consolidated brand contribution 14.3%, up 70 bps QoQ on sales leverage and cost optimization in India and Nigeria
items.quote: The brand contribution for Q3 FY25 stood at 14.3%, higher by 70 basis points versus the previous quarter. Improvement in brand contribution was mainly on account of sales leverage and fresh measures on cost optimization in the Indian and Nigerian operations.

items.statement: KFC brand contribution 17.2%, up 60 bps QoQ on better sales leverage and cost optimization
items.quote: The brand contribution margin at 17.2% for the current quarter saw an improvement of 60 basis points because of better sales leverage and cost optimization measures.

items.statement: Pizza Hut brand contribution 2.1% (Rs 4 crore); margins lower but expected to improve from next quarter on marketing cost optimization
items.quote: The gross margin for the quarter was 76.2%, and brand contribution for the quarter was Rs. 4 crore with the margin at 2.1%.

items.statement: Costa Coffee brand contribution 16.9%, gross margin 75.5% up 50 bps QoQ
items.quote: The gross margin for the quarter was 75.5%, an improvement of 50 basis points over the previous quarter. Brand contribution in Q3 saw an improvement and stood at 16.9%.

items.statement: International brand contribution 16.6%, up 60 bps QoQ; reported EBITDA 14.9% vs 13.4% in Q2
items.quote: Brand contribution margin at 16.6% saw an improvement of 60 basis points versus Q2 FY25. The reported EBITDA was 14.9% during the quarter versus 13.4% in Q2 FY25.

items.statement: Expect Pizza Hut margin improvement from next quarter due to marketing cost optimization and fresh cost measures
items.quote: we will see margin improvement coming from next quarter because we are optimizing the marketing cost in Pizza Hut versus what we have done in the last 6 to 9 months.

items.statement: Fresh cost optimization measures in KFC and Pizza Hut (labor, electricity) to yield results from January
items.quote: At the same time, we have taken some fresh cost optimization measures also in Pizza Hut as well as KFC, which will start to yield the results from January onwards.

items.statement: Food inflation driven by rising oil, chicken, cheese and coffee bean pricing impacted gross margins
items.quote: The impact on gross margins was primarily due to food inflation that we have seen in core brands, driven by rising oil, chicken, cheese and coffee bean pricing.

items.statement: Value menu items (KFC Roll Variants, Snackers, Epic Savers) and Pizza Hut discounts drove volumes during festive season
items.quote: For the budget conscious consumers, Value Menu Items such as KFC Roll Variants and Snackers were major attractions during the festive season. KFC Epic Savers and Pizza Hut discounts offered help in driving volumes.

items.statement: Vaango SSSG strong due to older airport locations; new stores in food courts/high streets start lower and mature over time
items.quote: Vaango is doing well on SSSG because of the older locations, because that is how the SSSG gets calculated , the formula is one -year-old stores . During the period ended 9 months we have added 31 new stores in Vaango. The new stores typically start the journey at a lower rate and then they mature over a period of time .

items.statement: KFC performance impacted in Kerala, Assam, West Bengal due to geopolitical situation; improvement seen as situation stabilizes
items.quote: We have primarily seen the KFC numbers getting impacted in Kerala, Assam and West Bengal, which are very highly concentrated because of geopolitical situation. However there also we have seen an improvement and a turnaround happening.

items.statement: Sister franchise partner has higher metro share where recovery is better; DIL sees similar trends in metros but not big divergence
items.quote: As you know, our sister franchise partner is predominantly present in the large metros because if you look at the country, they have a higher share of metro cities. And we have seen a better recovery in metros versus smaller ones.

items.statement: Union Budget 2025 new personal tax regime expected to enhance purchasing power and improve consumer spending for QSR industry
items.quote: We are optimistic that the recently presented Union Budget 2025, particularly the new personal tax regime, will bring much needed cheer for the middle class in the country. In our view , the Budget should enhance purchasing power leading to improved consumer spending.

items.statement: Nigerian currency showing signs of stabilization, broke continuous weakening trend in Q3
items.quote: The Nigerian currency is showing signs of stabilization and broke its continuous weakening trend in Quarter 3.

items.statement: Thailand currency impact caused 100 bps drop in international gross margin due to closing inventory valuation
items.quote: The gross margin was 64.1%, a drop of 100 basis points versus the previous quarter because of Thailand currency impact on closing inventory valuation.

items.statement: Rupee depreciation impact minimal on operations; only key equipment capex affected; international consolidation is translation effect
items.quote: we don't have a lot of imports except for, we only get a little bit impacted by, key equipments on the capex side. But as far as operations are concerned, the impact will eventually come in depreciation. But otherwise, on the raw material side, packing material side, our import structure is very small.

items.statement: No change in aggregator agreements yet; discussions ongoing but managed to hold against pressure
items.quote: No, not yet. So the discussions are on, because there has been a pressure from the aggregators, but so far we have managed to hold.

items.statement: PBT improved to Rs 9 crore from loss of Rs 4 crore QoQ on better EBITDA
items.quote: The PBT for Q3 FY25 on a consolidated basis was Rs . 9 crore versus a loss of Rs. 4 crore for the previous quarter. The improvement in PBT is primarily on account of better EBITDA.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue Rs 1,294 crore, up 53.5% YoY (includes Thailand acquired Jan 2024)
items.quote: DIL's consolidated revenue for the quarter stood at Rs. 1,294 crore, reflecting a 53.5% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: India business revenue Rs 873 crore, up 9.6% YoY mainly due to store expansion; up 4.4% QoQ
items.quote: The Indian business witnessed a growth of 9.6% year-on-year mainly due to store expansion. Revenue was Rs . 873 crore with growth of 4.4% versus the previous quarter.

items.statement: International revenue Rs 430 crore, up 9% QoQ
items.quote: The international revenue for the quarter was Rs. 430 crore with growth of 9% versus Q2 FY25.

items.statement: Consolidated pre-IndAS EBITDA Rs 131 crore (10.1% margin) vs Rs 114 crore previous quarter; post-IndAS EBITDA margin 16.9% vs 16.3%

The pre-IndAS margins for the quarter for the consolidated business were 10.1% , an improvement of 70 basis points versus the previous quarter. The Consolidated reported EBITDA on a post -IndAS basis was 16.9% versus 16.3% in Q2 FY25.

items.statement: Aggressive expansion during downturn is conscious strategy; missing real estate opportunities is irreversible; cannot open 400 stores in one year later

items.statement: Pizza Hut expansion moderated due to brand performance; DA commitments forced some openings but flexibility exists
items.quote: If you look at our openings on Pizza Hut this year are lower versus the previous year. And therefore, there is flexibility available. But again, at the same time, we are very cautious that we should not be defaulting on our agreements, and the DA works from January to December period. So, therefore, we will be recalibrating Pizza Hut as we go along.

items.statement: Opened first food court under JV with PVR INOX at Kota (51% economic interest); entity to be consolidated per AS-28
items.quote: We opened our first food court under the strategic tie-up with PVR INOX at Kota. DIL has an economic interest of 51% in the new Company. Please note that this entity shall be consolidated in accordance with Accounting Standards 28.

items.statement: Experimenting with KFC Coffee in some outlets but strategy focuses on smaller formats for payback efficiency, not large formats like McCafe
items.quote: we have introduced, and we have experimented with KFC Coffee in some of the outlets. Now, this is a different strategy versus what McDonald's is doing by way of McCafe or what Burger King is doing by way of BK Café because they operate large stores, and whereas our strategy is to bring the formats down to focus on the core, to make it more efficient on the paybacks and the margins.

items.statement: In discussions with aggregators on 10-minute delivery; KFC ready-to-eat model can participate; Pizza Hut preparation time 7-9 minutes
items.quote: we are also in discussions with one or two players in terms of how we can participate and experiment. items.quote: Based on our sustainable sales expectation for Q4 and contribution from the 2 launches that are expected this quarter, we are constrained to trim our full year number to about 4.6 - 4.8 million square feet. Sales values go down to some extent.

items.quote: We are setting ourselves with a targeted Q4 handovers of about 1,500 units as compared to 1,300 units that we did last year.

items.quote: We believe EBITDA without other income can reasonably stabilize between 22% - 25% at any point of time on an annual basis. Quarter-to-quarter fluctuations will always be there because of base effect.

items.quote: On a medium-term basis, as we have said, we are looking at more than nearly tripling our revenues on an annual revenue recognition by FY '28, which is a 3 years plan that we have articulated publicly.

items.statement: Robust demand with customer activity reviving post festive season from late October 2024
items.quote: Customer activities have revived post the beginning of festive season, midway through October-November 2024. We have seen a remarkable bounce back in customer activity; therefore, we remain positive about the underlying market conditions.

items.statement: Q3 sales volume 1.26 msf (+22% QoQ, +14% YoY); sales value INR 670 cr (+18% QoQ, +14% YoY)

items.quote: As we have set out to achieve our medium-term aspiration, we need to nearly double our pipeline from 17 million square fee t launch pipeline to over 30 million square feet in the next 12 to 18 months, max 24 months

items.quote: Overall, margins remained healthy, that clearly shows that the projects that are getting recognized have a healthy margin profile. Gross margins are about 31%. EBITDA margins were about 24%, 8% PBT margins.

items.quote: Overall, price remains stable. Our portfolio price hike is in the range of about 5% during the year so far, appreciable modesty in price hikes because we have had very robust price hikes over the last 2 years, 20% growth in our portfolio price averages between FY '23 and '24.

items.statement: 3 definitive launches planned for Q4 (Pune, Bangalore Electronic City, Kolkata contingent); 2 launches high confidence
items.quote: These 3 appear to be the definitive launches for current year. Two of them surely on track. Third one is still contingent on the West Bengal. Final clearances are still awaited.

items.statement: Pune launch delayed ~3 quarters due to elections/regulatory delays; now weeks away from RERA
items.quote: Pune, we have spoken about it a couple of quarters now. I think it's about delayed by almost 3 quarters. Variety of factors beyond our control, central elections, state elections, post-election delay in appointing the regulatory authorities.

items.statement: Gross collections stable at INR 346 cr in Q3 and INR 1,030 cr for 9M FY25; growth impacted by deferred handovers/launches
items.quote: Gross collections remained stable at INR 346 crores for Q3 and INR 1,030 crores for 9 months for FY '25. However, growth was impacted by deferred collections from handovers and new launches.

items.quote: These 2 projects alone held revenue recognition potential of about INR500 crores, most of it should come through in Q4.

items.statement: Full-year effective tax rate guided at 16.5%-17% for FY25.

items.statement: International hotels & ancillaries GTV grew 48% YoY in Q3, led by Europe (+90% YoY, 60%+ organic), LATAM (+34%), and Middle East (+31%).
items.quote: You would see that for this quarter, the YoY growth is very impressive 48%; both India and international operations are growing at a fast clip. The leading contribution this quarter has been from Europe, which has grown 90% YoY.

items.statement: India hotels & ancillaries GTV grew 18% YoY in Q3, accelerating from 9% in Q2.
items.quote: Manish, just to add to the India growth we grew actually from 9% in Q2 we actually grew at 18% in Q3.

items.statement: Monthly transacting buyers grew 9% YoY in Q3; active agents up 10% YoY (international +24%).
items.quote: If you look at the numbers for Q3 & 9M, there is a 9% increase in the monthly transacting buyers compared to same period last year.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA as % of GTV held at 1.05% in Q3 despite revenue margin pressure.
items.quote: But if we see adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of GTV, we have maintained a similar margin at 1.05% this quarter versus last quarter, same year.

items.statement: Working capital remains negative; cash & bank balances Rs 1,335.5 Cr as of Dec 31, 2024.
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains robust, with the net worth of Rs. 1,115.5 Cr as at 31 st of December 2024, notably our working capital continues to remain negative. Our cash and bank balances are also strong, standing at Rs. 1,335.5 Cr as at 31st December, 2024.

items.statement: Union Budget 2025 increased TCS threshold to Rs 10 lakh from Rs 7 lakh; 120 new airports under UDAN scheme to boost India outbound travel.
items.quote: We are also infused by multiple initiatives announced by the Union Budget 2025 like the increase in TCS threshold to Rs. 10 lakhs from Rs. 7 lakhs. With Noida and Navi Mumbai airports kicking off very soon. 120 new airports connectivity in the pipeline under the UDAN Scheme, as per Budget 2025.

items.statement: Actively exploring M&A opportunities globally but nothing close to fruition in next few weeks or months.
items.quote: Swapnil, we continue to explore opportunities and like we have said in the past, we are very cautious in committing to something. All I can say at this point is, we are exploring across the globe, in multiple geographies, but nothing at this point in time which looks close to coming to fruition in the next few weeks or months. So, no further comments on that.

items.statement: India hotel focus remains outbound premium (4-5 star); domestic 2-3 star segment not a priority.
items.quote: For us, our focus still remains is the outbound story and that's our key focus for India outbound and for people traveling overseas. From a domestic hotel point of view, our business is relatively small, right. So, I don't think that kind of bothers us but yes, we are focusing on organized chains, the typical five stars and structure chains which we will continue to get the supply on our side. But

items.statement: International NPS score of 70 in Dec 2024 via external tool, reflecting low churn.
items.quote: Finally, we also launched NPS on international business via an external tool. The overall NPS stood at 70 in December of 2024 which we believe is a very industry leading score, which is also a reflection of the low churn on the platform.

items.statement: Take rates guided to remain range-bound 7.2%-7.6% for hotels; focus on profitable top-line growth not take-rate expansion.
items.quote: Our view remains that they'll remain fairly range bound, we have been guiding around between 7.2% to 7.6% because right now the company is not really focused on improving the take rate. We do want to maintain them because that is an important metric, so we don't want to buy business by reducing take rates, but we are also not focused on increasing take rates at this point in time because again the

items.statement: Organic GTV growth ~20% YoY in Q3 (ex-Jumbonline); hotels organic GTV growth ~36% YoY.
items.quote: The organic growth in terms of the GTV without including the Jumbonline numbers basically, we have grown overall at around 20% YoY in this quarter. Karan Uppal: 36% organic in the hotel business

items.statement: Gross profit as % of GTV improved to 4.14% in Q3 from 3.89% YoY due to higher hotels share (60% vs 51%).
items.quote: Gross profit as a percentage of GTV for Q3 improved from 3.89% to 4.14% on YoY basis. This enhancement was largely driven by an increased share of hotels and ancillary services within our GTV which rose from 51% to 60% YoY.

items.statement: Net worth Rs 1,115.5 Cr as of Dec 31, 2024; balance sheet robust with negative working capital.
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains robust, with the net worth of Rs. 1,115.5 Cr as at 31 st of December 2024, notably our working capital continues to remain negative.

items.statement: FY25 operational seats target 135,000 by March 2025
items.quote: Our guidance for this full year was 135,000 seats.

items.statement: FY25 blended occupancy guidance 70-73%, mature centers 83-85%
items.quote: At the beginning of the year, we gave the original guidance that the blended occupancy at the whole portfolio level was expected to be about 70% to 73%. The greater than 12-month center vintage occupancy is expected to be between 83% to 85%.

items.statement: Construction fit-out revenue growth guidance roughly 30% YoY
items.quote: So our construction and fit-out business is in line with our guidance that we have given, which is roughly about 30%-odd growth.

items.statement: Capex cost per seat blended range around INR 54,000
items.quote: So the capex cost what we are incurring at this point of time is in the range what we gave in the prospectus. It is in the range of around 54,000 per seat kind of a thing.

items.statement: Operational seats 120,000+ across 193 centers as of Dec 2024
items.quote: I'm pleased to share that we have surpassed 120,000 operational seats across 193 centers nationwide.

items.statement: Total capacity including fit-out and LOI exceeds 160,000 seats across 237 centers, 8.0 million sq ft
items.quote: Including centers under fit-out and Letter Of Intent (LOI) stages, our total capacity now exceeds 160,000 seats across 237 centers, spanning an extensive 8.0 million square feet.

items.statement: Surpassed 200 operational centers milestone as of call date
items.quote: I'm excited to announce that as of today, we have surpassed the milestone of 200 operational centers.

items.statement: Signed LOIs for 23 new centers adding 18,000 seats and 0.8 million sq ft
items.quote: We have a strong expansion pipeline with signed LOIs for 23 new centers, adding 18,000 seats and approximately 0.8 million square feet of chargeable area.

items.statement: Signed demand contracts for 15,000 new seats in Q3 FY25 and 40,000 in 9M FY25
items.quote: On the demand side, we have signed demand contracts for 15,000 new seats in Q3 FY '25 and 40,000 new seats in 9 months of FY '25.

items.statement: Sector expected to grow 20-25% annually barring macro challenges
items.quote: Barring any unexpected macroeconomic challenges, we foresee the sector growing at an annual rate of about 20% to 25%.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin 33.8%, up 320 bps YoY
items.quote: Our EBITDA registered strong growth, increasing by 59% YoY to INR107 crores with a margin of 33.8%, an improvement of 320 basis points over the same quarter last year.

items.statement: IGAAP EBITDA margin Q3 FY25 14.7% vs 9.9% YoY, up 480 bps
items.quote: The margins stood at 14.7% as against 9.9% in Q3 of FY '24, which is a growth of 480 basis points.

items.statement: Construction fit-out revenue 50-50 split between landlord partners and third-party clients
items.quote: In terms of the revenue, it's almost a 50-50 split. 50% of the revenue comes from what the -- our landlord partners are giving to fit out the center and about 50% comes from third-party clients.

items.statement: Construction fit-out segment contribution margin blended 16-17%
items.quote: At a contribution margin level, this business is some where in the -- about blended between 16% to 17% margin

items.statement: Seat pricing escalations: small cohorts 5-8%, large cohorts 4-6%; new customers reflect current rental trends
items.quote: In the existing client contracts for smaller cohorts, the general escalations, which we have tied in ranges from 5% to 8% in terms of the larger cohorts, the price escalations are usually between 4% to 6-odd percent.

items.statement: 66% occupied seats by large corporates/MNCs, 20% SMEs, 13% startups; 39% clients multi-center
items.quote: Approximately 66% of our occupied seats are taken by large corporates and MNCs, while around 20% are occupied by SMEs and another 13% by start-ups with the remaining share attributed to freelancers. Additionally, 39% of our clients operate across multiple centers within our portfolio.

items.statement: Managed aggregation model (65% portfolio) with profit-share and ~50% min guarantee mitigates risk and drives high ROCE ~75%
items.quote: On our supply side, we have talked about the managed aggregation model which makes us risk mitigated when it comes to our occupancy build-up because in majority of our portfolios, almost 65% today, we are partnered with our landlord, which is in a profit share model and the minimum guarantee is typically about 50% of the market rental.

items.statement: Construction fit-out working capital consumed until milestone billing or completion billing
items.quote: The working capital requirement normally arises from that side. So until the time we bill to the customer, it consumes our working capital.

items.statement: Net debt-free; net debt-to-equity -0.29 as of Dec 2024
items.quote: The company continues to have a comfortable liquidity position, remaining debt-free at the net level. Our debt-to-equity ratio at the net level has improved to (0.29) as of December '24 from a (0.28) as of December '23.

items.statement: No fund raise planned for Q4 FY25; FY26 funding needs to be commented later
items.quote: If you're talking Q4, obviously, no, we are not going anywhere for a fund raise. Next year, I'll not be able to comment at this point of time.

items.statement: Blended exit occupancy 73%; centers >12 months at 84% as of Dec 2024
items.quote: As of December 2024, exit month occupancy stood at 73%, while centers operational for over 12 months reached 84%.

items.statement: Ancillary services revenue Q3 FY25 INR 31.5 cr, up 110% YoY
items.quote: ASR revenue for Q3 is INR31.5 crores, which in last year was INR15 crores for the quarter 3 of last year, which is a growth of 110%.

items.statement: Landlord payback on capex 4-5 years; return on capex ~10-11%
items.quote: On an overall basis, from a landlord perspective, their usual payback ranges between 4 years to 5 years for the capex or a bit lower than that.

items.statement: Targets INR 1,000 crore revenue with 15% PAT margin in next 900-1,000 days
items.quote: And our target remains very clear that we would like to be a INR 1,000 crores company with a 15% PAT in the next 900 to 1,000 days. That's our target.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded to 58.1% in Q3 FY25 from 54.7% in Q3 FY24 driven by localization and dollar mitigation
items.quote: The gross margin expanded to 58.1% in Q3 FY '25 compared to 54.7% in Q3 FY '24.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 20-22% expected by mid next year as new stores mature
items.quote: I think the EBITDA margin of somewhere about 20% - 22% is what we should be aiming at. But because new stores are taking a little longer to breakeven and it takes a little longer gestation period, it's a little subdued now.

items.statement: Manufacturing capex of INR 5-7 crore planned for next year funded from internal accruals
items.quote: Say max INR 5 crores to INR 7 crores for next year, manufacturing capex.

items.statement: Manufacturing facilities at Jigani and Electronic City operating at 70% utilization on single shift basis
items.quote: Currently, it's at about 70% utilization.

items.statement: Capacity can scale to INR 800 crore revenue by adding second shift without major capex
items.quote: I think we are qu ite comfortable till at least about INR 800 crores as we see it in today's run rate

items.statement: B2B order book flat; Williams-Sonoma orders on hold pending US tariff clarity, expected by April
items.quote: So the B2B order book has remained flattish throughout the year. While we have ongoing discussions with Williams-Sonoma from America, nothing has materialized yet because they are waiting and watching the tariff issues that are happening in America currently.

items.statement: Luxury housing sales (INR 1-10 cr) grew 46% in 2024 and 500% over 5 years, driving furniture demand
items.quote: Sales of apartments priced between INR 1 crores to INR 10 crores increased by 46% in 2024 and have grown nearly 500% for the past 5 years.

items.statement: Inventory handover delays from developers continue; expecting major chunk from Q1 FY26
items.quote: We are hoping starting from Q1, we are going to see a lot more inventory coming into the market.

items.statement: Case goods contribution increased from 11% to 16% in 9M FY25; bedroom furniture at 4%, targeting growth
items.quote: It has jumped from 11% to 16%. Bed and bedroom furniture also now we are actually innovating and coming up with a new catalog.

items.statement: Leather localization at 33%, targeting 35% this year and 45% by end of next year; import duty on crust removed
items.quote: We had targeted close to 35% of our leather purchase to be localized this year, and we are on track. Also, we have mitigated the risk of expensive dollar, which has played out good for us.

items.statement: Long-term vision to reach 80% leather localization in 24-36 months as tanners invest in machinery post duty removal
items.quote: In the long term, I think, our vision will be to get to almost 80% localization probably in 24 to 36 months.

items.statement: B2B2C segment degrew 27% in Q3 and 15% in 9M FY25 after shift to cash-and-carry; credit overdues reduced from INR 3 cr to INR 60 lakh
items.quote: Post transition, segment degrown by 15%.

items.statement: B2B2C recovery expected by Q2 FY26 after credit grading and agency rating
items.quote: We are getting a credit agency to rate these customers, and we will come back to the market, and we are hoping to get this business probably by Q2 of next year.

items.statement: Revenue mix: COCO retail 60%, B2B2C 20%, B2B 20% of total revenue
items.quote: So COCO is 60%, then we have B2B2C, which is 20% and then we have B2B, which is 20%. So it adds up to 100.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth negative in low single digits for Q3 FY25 due to cannibalization from new store expansion
items.quote: Our SSG is same-store sales growth is negative for the quarter. We have expanded the retail square feet. And quarter 2, quarter 3, we really saw subdued demand that led to my SSSG being negative.

items.statement: Pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin 9.4% in Q3 FY25 vs 13% in FY23 and 12% in FY24
items.quote: Pre-Ind AS for the quarter is 9.4%.

items.statement: B2B2C overdues reduced from INR 3-4 crore to INR 50 lakh; overall receivables now minimal under cash-and-carry
items.quote: So I think for this 1 segment, we had almost INR 3 crores to INR 4 crores of overdues, which has now come down to almost like INR 50 lakhs.

items.statement: BIS certification on fabrics and boards implemented from 11 Feb; QCO on full furniture likely, benefiting domestic integrated manufacturers
items.quote: We have already moved far ahead in terms of BIS certification and already BIS certification on certain parts and components of furniture has come into play from 11th of February.

items.statement: Pilot export shipment of one container to Germany starting March; US exports on hold pending tariff clarity
items.quote: In March, we have just started our pilot shipment and one container of furniture is being exported to Germany.

items.statement: Small price increase taken in Q2 to offset cost inflation; major margin improvement from localization and dollar savings
items.quote: There was a small price increase, but that was again to offset the cost inflation, which happened. But then that really gets passed on. But the major portion is the localization of critical raw materials that has happened, and that has really getting translated into the bottom line.

items.statement: Marketing spend maintained at 7-9% of revenue; reduced this year due to store launch delays, may increase if market sluggish
items.quote: We have always ensured that our marketing spends are always within 8% to 9%, and that is the trend we will continue to follow.

items.statement: FOFO franchisees trained via bi-annual 2-day events at factory; strict controls via Salesforce and warranty linkage
items.quote: Every year, we conduct two events in the factory. We conduct events for almost 2 days each time, all the new products, so all the franchisees will be here in Bangalore, and we completely train them with our products.

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty delaying B2B export discussions with Williams-Sonoma and other US buyers
items.quote: Because of the uncertainty today due to Trump and the tariff, it is on hold. Once we get some amount of clarity, we can restart that exercise.

items.statement: Store count at 68 (41 COCO, 27 FOFO); added 4 stores in Q3 FY25 (2 Level Next, 2 Sofas & More)
items.quote: Continuing the expansion strategy, the company added 4 new stores in Q3 FY '25, 2 under the Stanley Level Next brand and 2 under Stanley Sofas & More brand. With this, our total store count is 68 stores, comprising 41 COCO stores and 27 FOFO stores.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guidance of 16-17% and EBITDA margin guidance of 13-15%
items.quote: So, we expect to achieve a top-line growth of around 16% to 17% this year, with margins in the range of 13% to 15% as per our estimates currently.

items.statement: 9M FY25 EBITDA margin at 13.83%, down 289 bps YoY due to pricing pressure and one-off costs
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin for 9 months FY25 stood at 13.83%, down by 289 basis points from 16.72% in the period of 9 months FY24.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin at 12.85% vs 15.42% in Q3 FY24, down 257 bps
items.quote: So, the EBITDA in Q3 of FY24 it was 15.42% and this Q3 it is 12.85%. So, it's by 257 basis points not 500 basis points.

items.statement: Gross margins declined due to increased competition and pricing pressure across both CCR and ETS segments
items.quote: Yes, it is the last few months we have seen an increased competition which has put a pricing pressure which has also led to a decrease in our gross margins.

items.statement: One-off expenses of ~Rs 2 crore in Q3 from events, festivals, GST input reversals, and server hosting charges
items.quote: Also, certain excess charges in terms of we had to pay off for the server hosting. So, this added to the extra approximately Rs. 2 crores of costing.

items.statement: Added 130 new clients in 9M FY25 including large IT MNCs, port logistics, global consultants, financial services, PE firms, and consumer goods companies
items.quote: This year we have added over 130 clients, which we consider the clients are our strongest asset we believe.

items.statement: Existing customers grew 23% YoY in 9M FY25
items.quote: So, we have from the last financial year one number I do have handy is that in our existing customers, we saw growth of around 23%.

items.statement: 9M FY25 revenue mix: 42% CCR, 58% ETS; Q3 FY25 mix: 43% CCR, 57% ETS; similar mix expected next year
items.quote: So, this last quarter, we did around 43% was CCR and 57% was ETS. And for the whole year, I think we will end up with around 42% for CCR and around 58% for ETS.

items.statement: International revenue crossed Rs 8 crore in 9M FY25 vs Rs 5 crore in full FY24; EBITDA positive, asset-light model managed from India
items.quote: In this 9 months, we've already crossed around Rs. 8 crores of business for our international operations.

items.statement: Higher depreciation from new fleet additions impacted PAT margin in 9M FY25
items.quote: This was due to increased depreciation costs from new fleet addition, higher direct and indirect expenses and slightly reduction in the unrealized gain on the investment which we have in the mutual funds and equities.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity ratio at 0.04%, negligible debt, no plans to increase leverage
items.quote: So, we are almost at a very negligible debt. If you see our debt ratio, it has consistently gone down and is now I think only 0.2% sorry 0.04% is our debt-to-equity ratio currently.

items.statement: Healthy cash position; evaluating acquisition targets and planning good dividend for end of year
items.quote: We have a healthy cash position. We are still looking at targets for acquisition. At the same time, we would be looking to utilize that for giving out a good dividend also end of this year.

items.statement: Heightened competition from both organized and unorganized players; IPO may have attracted new entrants who compete on price
items.quote: It is from both; it is a mix.

items.statement: Management expects competitive intensity to peak and normalize as new entrants face service delivery challenges
items.quote: I don't think so. I think we're seeing a peak of the competition that is coming in, but I cannot say, but I don't think so with our experience and our brand in the corporate mobility sector, we think we should be able to come out a winner as compared to all the others.

items.statement: Working capital cycle unchanged despite pricing pressure
items.quote: It's the same. There's no change.

items.statement: New client additions across both segments: 9 in ETS, balance in CCR; acquisitions across all major cities including Bangalore, Gurgaon, Mumbai, Pune, Hyderabad, Chennai, Kolkata
items.quote: We have added I think almost nine clients in ETS and the balance in CCR.

items.statement: Revenue from operations grew 17.5% YoY to Rs 4,767 million in 9M FY25
items.quote: In the first 9 months of FY25, our revenue from operations stood at Rs. 4,767 million as compared to Rs. 4,054 million in 9 months FY24, reflecting a year-on-year growth of nearly 17.5%.

items.statement: Global outlook uncertain due to Trump tariff impact on international travel; domestic outlook positive
items.quote: I'm not sure about the global scenario with a lot of volatility being seen with the Trump tariff, how that may affect international travel. But domestically, I think the business scenario and the travel scenario in India looks very, very positive.

items.statement: Increased sales team; AOP for next year being finalized
items.quote: Like I mentioned, we have increased our sales team, and we are currently in the process of drawing up our AOP for the next year.

items.statement: Evaluating acquisition targets using healthy cash position
items.quote: We are still looking at targets for acquisition.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 expected to maintain Q3 profitability momentum with neutral gold price impact due to hedging
items.quote: we are hopeful that we will continue the momentum on the same way. Main reason is that now we are focusing more on hedging part, so there should not be any impact whether gold prices will be go up or go down.

items.statement: Plan to add 25 stores in FY26: 8 COCO PNG stores, 7-8 franchisee PNG stores, ~10 litestyle stores (half COCO/half FOCO), plus 1-2 US stores
items.quote: Next financial year, the plan is that considering a company-owned store and a franchisee store, along with our litestyle format what we have envisaged, the store with lighter weight jewellery, we would be adding 25 stores in the next financial year, which will be a mix of franchisee and company-owned stores.

items.statement: Reached 50 stores in January 2025, targeting 53 stores by March 2025 end (3 more in March)
items.quote: Yes. So we have already added two stores in January. So right now we are at 50 stores. And in the month of March, we will be adding three more stores. So we will be at 53 stores as of March end.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin 5.3% (+50 bps YoY), PAT margin 3.5% (+60 bps YoY)
items.quote: We achieved EBITDA of INR 129 crores, making 37.2% growth year-on-year with EBITDA margin of 5.3 up from 50 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 revenue INR 2,435 cr (+23.5% YoY) driven by festive/wedding demand, consumer sentiment, product portfolio enhancement
items.quote: For the entire Q3 FY25, our total revenues stood at INR 2,435 crores, registering a 23.5% growth year-on-year compared to INR 1,972 crores in Q3 FY 24. This performance was largely driven by a strong demand during the festive and wedding season.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 same-store sales growth: gold value +44% YoY, gold volume +14% YoY
items.quote: Q3 same store sales growth we have in terms of gold is 44%, wherein the value growth 44% and volume growth we have observed 14% year-on-year.

items.statement: Studded ratio rose 39% YoY to 7.4% in Q3 FY25; targeting 12-13% in 2-3 years via Polki/jadau (Polmi), precious stones, natural diamonds
items.quote: Additionally, an important point we observed is a 39% year-over-year increase in our studded ratio, which now stands at 7.4% highlighting our evolving consumer preference towards more premium jewellery offerings.

items.statement: Hedging coverage increased from 12% to >45% via GML in Q3; as of January 2025 fully hedged (100%) for total gold business
items.quote: the proportion of hedged gold through GML increased from 12% last quarter to over 45% this quarter, which showcases our effective risk management strategy and the ability to navigate further.

items.statement: Inventory INR 1,800 cr and GML 558 kg as of Dec 2024; total inventory hedging ~60-70%, profitability fully hedged
items.quote: Closing inventory on December is 1,800 crores. And my GML is almost 558 kgs.

items.statement: Nearly debt-free as of Dec 2024 (INR 50-60 cr term loan remaining); IPO proceeds used to repay INR 300 cr bank debt
items.quote: From the IPO proceeds, we have also repaid the entire bank debt. So if you have seen the IPO objectives, INR 300 crores was to repay the term loan, the bank debt and then the balance was primarily used for stock infusion.

items.statement: FY26 expansion funded via internal accruals; no heavy debt planned; ~10 franchisee stores require no capital
items.quote: Our internal accruals are strong. And we will not be looking at raising heavy debt to fund the expansion. It will be managed through our internal accruals. And around 10 stores out of this would also be franchisees, which will not be draining our capital.

items.statement: Transaction volume +21% YoY, ATV +22% to INR 86,000, footfalls +36%, conversion 93% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Moreover, we recorded a 36% increase in footfalls and supported by a strong conversion ratio of 93%.

items.statement: Gold price ~INR 80,000 (vs INR 72,000 YoY) but demand still +5%; consumers exchanging old gold for wedding jewellery
