items.statement: Q4 FY25 aluminum hedged 35% at $2,600/t, 15% zero collar $2,262-$2,558, currency 16% at Rs. 88
items.quote: So the hedge bit, this current Q4 FY '25, we have 35% of the commodity hedged at $2,600 per ton. And we had ongoing 15% zero collar with the bottom at $2,262 and a ceiling at $2,558.

items.statement: FY26 aluminum hedged 12% at $2,700/t, currency 13% at Rs. 87.33
items.quote: And just to round it off, for next year we have 12% of the commodity hedge that $2,700 per ton and 13% of the currency at Rs. 87.33 per dollar.

items.statement: Novelis targets long-term EBITDA per ton of $600 over next several years
items.quote: We are not in a place to talk specifically about the total impact of all those projects and the timing, but in the early April time frame we will be able to la y out in a bit more detail what some of those are, so that you can better understand how we progress back towards our longer term EBITDA per ton of $600 per ton over the next several

items.statement: US tariff exemption uncertainty for Novelis, but higher Midwest premiums may offset impact
items.quote: We simply do not see a scenario where either between the countries; Canada, US, Mexico, Korea, we simply do not see a scenario that there will not be a settlement soon around reciprocal tariffs.

items.statement: Scrap prices peaking but expected to remain at structurally higher levels long-term
items.quote: We do think that the overall scrap pricing in the market is starting to peak out. Now, how much it moderates back in the short term, medium term is hard for us to predict. We do think that we will be at new levels, higher levels of scrap pricing on a longer term basis.

items.statement: Expect operating performance to improve on demand recovery, internal profitability initiatives, and reduced RM inflation
items.quote: We expect our operating performance to improve going forward on the back of , (a) recovery in the overall demand momentum , s econdly, initiatives being taken internally to significantly uplift profitability , a nd lastly, due to reduced RM inflation

items.statement: Expect healthy replacement demand momentum to continue in Q4 with signs of further strong pickup beyond current levels
items.quote: In terms of the demand outlook, we expect the replacement demand momentum to continue to be healthy in Q4. And, in fact, we are seeing signs of a further strong pickup even beyond the current levels.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 13.7% in Q3 FY25, flat sequentially despite raw material cost pressure
items.quote: The consolidated EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 9.5 billion, a margin of 13.7% compared to 13.6% in the last quarter.

items.statement: India EBITDA margin declined to 11.1% in Q3 FY25 from 12.1% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 5 billion, a margin of 11.1% compared to 12.1% in the last quarter.

items.statement: Europe EBITDA margin improved to 17.7% in Q3 FY25 from under 15% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter stood at EUR 32 million, with an EBITDA margin of 17.7% compared to under 15% for the last quarter.

items.statement: RM cost expected to be range-bound in Q4 at similar levels to Q3, indicating plateauing
items.quote: Moving to the RM outlook, we expect the RM cost to be range bound in Q4, almost around similar levels as Q3, which indicates a certain plateauing out.

items.statement: No near-term price increases planned due to market situation and competitive intensity
items.quote: Currently, given the market situation, etc., and the overall scenario, absolute near-term, no price increases planned. We'll continue to assess that situation and then take a call.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 RM basket at INR 175/kg, up 15% YoY and 2% QoQ; natural rubber INR 215/kg, synthetic rubber INR 195/kg, carbon black INR 120/kg
items.quote: current year, Q3, the RM was roughly about INR 175 a kg, up 15% vis -à-vis the same quarter last year, but sequentially up 2%. Mumuksh Mandlesha: And can you give the natural rubber and other sub- component prices? Gaurav Kumar: Natural rubber was around INR 215 a kg, synthetic rubber at INR 195, and carbon black at INR 120 rupees

items.statement: Europe UUHP segment accounted for 48% of PCLT replacement volumes in Q3 FY25, up from 43% earlier, a 400 bps improvement
items.quote: More importantly, w e registered more than 400 basis points improvement in our product mix with UUHP segment accounting for 48% of PCLT replacement volumes in the quarter. Earlier it was 43%.

items.statement: Securing additional model wins from marquee German PV manufacturers, revalidating product capabilities
items.quote: Starting with R&D, we continue to secure additional model wins from marquee German PV manufacturers, thereby revalidating our product capabilities.

items.statement: US identified as next growth market with PCR Vredestein and Apollo TBR growing; Middle East, specifically Saudi Arabia, also targeted
items.quote: So, clearly, Siddhartha, we are looking at the US as our next growth market, and you'll see, we will be growing slow and steady. As I mentioned, PCR Vredestein is doing good in the US market. Apollo TBR has also started growing. So, the US is a clear growth market. The next market that we are also looking at is the Middle East, specifically in Saudi Arabia.

items.statement: FY26 capex to increase with growth capex for PCR capacity; maintenance capex ~INR 700-750 crores plus ~INR 800 crores growth capex, total ~INR 1,500-1,550 crores
items.quote: So, if we take a normal maintenance Capex around INR 700 crores - INR 750 crores mark that we talked about earlier, on top of that , very much at the top of the numbers, maybe add around INR 800 crores more.

items.statement: India PCR utilisation high 80%, Europe PCR utilisation in 90%; TBR utilisation ~80% with sufficient headroom
items.quote: TBR is around 80%, Basudeb, so we have sufficient headroom. But PCR, currently in India, we are high 80% and, in fact, in Europe, in the 90%.

items.statement: FY26 capacity addition ~10% overall: India PCR +7-8%, Europe slightly more via Hungary brownfield expansion
items.quote: about 7% - 8%, Europe, slightly more. So, overall we are looking at capacity addition just about 10% or a little less. Basudeb Banerjee: And Europe it will be through Hungary? Gaurav Kumar: That's correct, we don't need any greenfield. We have enough brownfield

items.statement: Gross debt: India INR 3,200 crores, consolidated INR 3,500 crores as of nine months FY25
items.quote: The gross debt number is INR 3,200 crores for India. At a consol level, the total Capex for the nine months is about INR 500 crores, and the gross debt number is about INR 3,500 crores.

items.statement: India interest cost increased due to working capital borrowings from profitability challenges and weaker market; temporary measure
items.quote: The India interest cost has gone up mainly on account of working capital borrowings, which is largely a combination of the profitability challenges and a slightly weaker market, and the Europe interest cost has come down. Moving up on the working capital borrowings, etc., is fairly a temporary measure.

items.statement: India replacement volume growth 5% in Q3 FY25; OE volume declined ~10%; exports flattish
items.quote: the volume growth overall for replacement this quarter was 5%, and OE was almost minus 10%. Siddhartha Bera: And, sir, exports? Gaurav Kumar: Exports was

items.statement: Europe demand recovery continuing with strong passenger car and truck tyre replacement demand; UHP/UUHP growing faster, mix improving
items.quote: Europe, in fact, for the last quarter or so, and even going into the current quarter, the demand on both the passenger car and truck tyres replacement is very strong. As of now, no signs as to why that growth should taper off, and the good thing for generally tyre makers, even for us, is that within that, the UHP and the UUHP segment is growing even faster. So the mix continues to improve.

items.statement: Peers outperformed on revenue growth; Apollo prioritising profitability over market share but addressing growth gap sequentially
items.quote: It has to be chosen as a prudent strategy of market share or growth vis -à-vis margins. The priority to profitability margins will continue to be there, and yes, a couple of our peers have definitely done better than us. But if you see sequentially vis -à-vis Q2 to Q3, our numbers are coming in line with some of our peers and ahead of some of our peers, so we are addressing that issue in terms of

items.statement: India strategy shifting from 12-13 inch OEM to 14-17 inch premium segments for higher profitability; volume lower but margins better
items.quote: Primarily in India, to give you an example, we are trying to vacate the 12-inch, 13-inch market, especially with the OEMs, and then going up-sizing of 14, 15, 16, 17, which is where more profitability is concerned. Volume is less, but profitability is there.

items.statement: Other expenses reduced sequentially due to A&P and administrative cost cuts; expected to normalize toward prior levels as revenue grows
items.quote: So some bit of it, Amar, is immediately cutting down on A &P and some of the easy administrative expenses, which was coming down hard given the overall cost pressures. I would say the prior levels are more normalized levels, and one would tend towards that.

items.statement: Rupee depreciation and logistics costs impacting imported natural rubber costs; RM basket flattish in Q4 as natural rubber taper offset by crude derivative increases
items.quote: I don't have an outlook for each raw material, but overall, as I said, flattish. So, some bit of it coming down on natural rubber would then be negated by some bit of it up on the crude side. So, the rupee devaluation doesn't really work in our favor on the raw material basket

items.statement: Reifencom Q3 FY25 revenue EUR 88 million with 7%+ EBITDA margin
items.quote: For the quarter, the Reifencom operations did EUR 88 million in revenue, with a 7% plus in EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Targeting specialty films volume share of 80% in medium term, excluding new BOPP/CPP capacity
items.quote: While 71% is the YTD number for December 24, we are targeting the medium term to reach to 80% but this obviously will be excluding new capacity for the BOPP and CPP, which will take little time actually to expand specialty further on the new line.

items.statement: Expect incremental cost rationalization of close to Rs 25 crore in FY26
items.quote: Number two, cost rationalization, we expect incremental cost rationalization of close to Rs.25 crore in FY26.

items.statement: New BOPP, CPP and sun control film capacity to add to top line and bottom line from FY26
items.quote: Number three, the new capacity kickoff for the BOPP, CPP and sun control film, which will add to top line and bottom line from FY26.

items.statement: All new packaging verticals except B2C to be EBITDA positive in FY26; sun control EBITDA positive from FY27
items.quote: All other new business verticals related to packaging should be EBITDA positive in FY26 except B2C business, which may take some time. Even among B2C business, we expect sun control to be EBITDA positive from FY27.

items.statement: Specialty chemicals to achieve high yield EBITDA and more than 30% ROCE in FY25
items.quote: The specialty chemical subsidy is advancing well to achieve high yield EBITDA and more than 30% return on capital employed in FY25.

items.statement: Rigid packaging expected to exceed Rs 120 crore top line with positive EBITDA in FY26
items.quote: The vertical is moving in line with the plan and we expect more than Rs.120 crore of top line with positive EBITDA in FY26 from rigid packaging.

items.statement: Top line CAGR of 20% for next three years; may grow faster due to new BOPP line commissioning in Q1/Q2 FY26
items.quote: Yes, or maybe a little more actually, because we are going to commission the world's largest BOPP line, and we expect this to get commission in either first quarter or second quarter of FY26. So, this should add close to 40% to the existing capacity. So the answer is yes, top line may grow little even faster.

items.statement: US and Japan run rate currently touching $5 million per month combined; expect to reach $6 million within 3-6 months
items.quote: So our current run rate has already started touching close to $5 million for both these countries put together, and we expect that they should start touching $6 million within next three to six months.

items.statement: FY25 capex estimated at Rs 430-450 crore, majority already done by Dec 2024
items.quote: The Company's capex in FY25 is estimated to be about Rs 430-450 cr majority of which is already done at Dec 2024.

items.statement: New BOPP and CPP lines will be world's largest production capacity lines, increasing company production capability by 45-50%
items.quote: Both BOPP and CPP lines will be the world's largest production capacity lines and will increase company production capability by close to 45% to 50%.

items.statement: New BOPP line nameplate capacity close to 70,000 tons; expect around 60,000 tons additional actual production
items.quote: We expect to produce, the name plate capacity is close to 70,000 tons. But from actual production perspective, we expect around 60,000 tons additional production from this line.

items.statement: BOPET film capacity to grow by close to 40% in coming year
items.quote: Our BOPET film capacity is going to grow by close to 40% in the coming year.

items.statement: BOPP margin running close to Rs 21 per kg in Dec 2024 quarter vs Rs 25 in Sep 2024 and Rs 9 in Dec 2023
items.quote: BOPP margin has been running close to Rs.21 per kg during December '24 quarter, which was Rs.25 per kg in September '24 quarter and Rs.9 per kg in December '23 quarter.

items.statement: BOPET vertical posted EBITDA in mid-teens during Q3 FY25
items.quote: BOPET vertical (about 15% of Company's sales for Q3, FY25) has witnessed better margins and posted EBITDA in mid-teens during Q3, FY25.

items.statement: Specialty chemicals expected to close FY25 at close to Rs 190 crore revenue with close to 20% EBITDA margin
items.quote: Cosmos Specialty Chemicals is doing quite well, as Neeraj mentioned earlier. We should be closing the year close to 190 crores at a very healthy, close to 20% kind of an EBITDA numbers.

items.statement: Strong demand helped BOPP margins recover fast after temporary pressure from domestic capacity commissioning
items.quote: The BOPP margin has also witnessed pressure for a few weeks in December‘24 quarter with some capacity commissioning in the domestic industry, though it recovered fairly fast due Cosmo First Limited February 12th ,2025 to strong demand

items.statement: Export growth close to 20% this year; domestic market share small with customers being refused regularly
items.quote: We are growing very nicely in the export market this year we have grown close to, a bit lower than 20% in this year. And the second thing is that, right now our market share in the domestic market is very small. We have to kind of keep refusing to many, many customers on an ongoing basis in the domestic market.

items.statement: Specialty films reached 73% of total volume in Q3 FY25 and 71% YTD vs 64% in FY24; 14% higher specialty sales volume YTD
items.quote: The Company has reached speciality sales of 73% of total volume in Q3, FY25 and 71% on Dec 2024 YTD basis as against 64% in FY24. You will notice, step by step, the Company is improving on speciality sales. On Dec 24 YTD basis, we are running 14% higher speciality sales in volume terms.

items.statement: Specialty films split broadly 50:50 between specialty and semi-specialty
items.quote: So with respect to bifurcation into specialty and semi specialty, broadly it's 50:50, peer-to-peer or quarter-to-quarter there may be some minor changes in this ratio.

items.statement: Five new BOPP lines expected in FY26 (three large, two small); Dhanashree planning lines in FY27-28
items.quote: In the next financial year, there are five new lines, including our expected to commission out of which three lines actually are bigger lines and two are relatively smaller lines. And then, as you rightly pointed out, Dhanashree is planning in FY27 and FY28 as per the news that is available with us.

items.statement: EPR regulations from April; Cosmo uses significant recycled content in flexible and rigid packaging
items.quote: See, as far as the EPR is concerned, good thing is that we use lot of recycled both in flexible and rigid. And in any case, we are continuously in touch with the government to explain them what is realistic and what is not realistic.

items.statement: Net debt close to Rs 900 crore; 2.6x EBITDA and 0.6x equity
items.quote: The financials remain strong, the company's net debt position is close to Rs.900 crore which is 2.6 times to EBITDA and 0.6 times to equity.

items.statement: Ms Yamini Kumar appointed as Whole-time Director (Corporate Strategy, ESG & CSR) for 5 years
items.quote: Ms Yamini Kumar (Jaipuria) has been appointed as Whole time Director (Corporate Strategy, ESG & CSR) for a period of 5 years.

items.statement: BOPP base film margins expected to remain subdued in FY26 due to domestic capacity additions
items.quote: Moving into outlook, though the BOPP base film margins are expected to remain little subdued in FY26 due to expected capacity addition in the domestic industry.

items.statement: US import duties >30-40% could create business case for US plant, but not basis for long-term decisions
items.quote: But if these duties exceed 30%, 40% then there could be a business case. But we have to see lot of things, what duties are levied on Mexico, what are levied on India, if at all and so on, so forth. And again duties should never be a rational for starting up a plant, because if next US regime, they remove these duties, then all these investments can have a very detrimental impact.

items.statement: Zigly demerger evaluation ongoing; timeline now 2-3 years depending on growth pace
items.quote: We are continuously evaluating this, as we said earlier it will take us last time we said three to four years and obviously since then sometime has elapsed. So, I would say that now we should be looking at anywhere between two to three years before we demerge.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 capex expected at INR200-225 crores
items.quote: For the full year, we expect the capex to be at around INR200 crores to INR225 crores.

items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance of INR3,200-3,500 crores with 25-30% growth
items.quote: I would still expect anywhere between INR 3,200 crores to INR3,500 crores of top line, registering maybe anywhere between 25% to 30% of top line growth.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth of 15-20% with 100-150 bps EBITDA margin expansion
items.quote: I would still say that we should be looking at anywhere between a 15% to 20% of top line growth, and again, expansion on the margins, especially at the EBITDA level. We definitely should see at least 100, 150 bps expansion on the EBITDA margin.

items.statement: FY26 capex to be much lower than FY25 due to completed capacity additions
items.quote: I would expect that in FY '26, the capex number would be much lower than that of FY '25.

items.statement: Order book of INR2,600 crores with 33% EV and 78% PV allocation
items.quote: Looking ahead, I am pleased to report that we have a strong and healthy order book of INR2,600 crores, of this, a significant 33% is dedicated to electric vehicles, reflecting our growing commitment to the EV sector and 78% is allocated to passenger vehicles.

items.statement: Order book expected to sustain between INR2,500-3,000 crores
items.quote: I think anywhere between INR 2,500 crores to INR3,000 crores order book which we would like to sustain going forward as well.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin at 8%, 9M at 8.2% due to antidumping duty, raw material costs, FX impact
items.quote: Despite this growth, we observed a slight dip in our EBITDA margins, which stood at 8% for quarter 3 and 8.2% for 9 months FY '25.

items.statement: Antidumping duty on PCBs increased cost by 50-60 bps, raw material prices up, USD-INR impact 10-20 bps
items.quote: The decline in margin was due to the following reasons: the antidumping duty imposed on PCBs has resulted in a 50 to 60 basis point increase in cost; the upward trend in prices of certain essential raw materials, which had an impact on overall cost structure, USD-INR effect changes has impacted by 10 to 20 basis points.

items.statement: Tooling margin declined from 24% to 7% in 9M FY25, sustainable long-term at 10-15%
items.quote: On a 9-month basis, the margin on tooling used to be last year at about 24%, which has declined to 7% in the current 9 months.

items.statement: Raw material consumption increased from 63.3% to 65% in Q3 FY25 due to escalations
items.quote: There has been a significant increase in the raw material consumption for quarter 3, specifically, where if you look at quarter 3 FY24 to quarter 3 FY25, it's actually gone up from 63.3% to 65%.

items.statement: LED lighting share at 52% of 9M FY25 revenue vs 36% last year, 86% of order book
items.quote: For 9 months FY '25, LED lighting now constitutes 52% of our total revenue, compared to just 36% during the same period last year.

items.statement: LED share expected to reach 60-65% in FY26 as 90% of order book is LED
items.quote: I would not have an exact number, but definitely, we do expect the LED share next year to be around between 60% to 65% or so.

items.statement: Regained Maruti Suzuki revenue share with 60% of INR2,600 crore order book from Maruti
items.quote: Out of the INR2,600 crores order book the company is sitting on, 60% of that is Maruti Suzuki alone.

items.statement: Launched lighting for Mahindra BE 6, XEV 9, Maruti Swift Dzire, Tata Tiago/Tigor refresh
items.quote: We successfully launched lighting systems for the latest Mahindra & Mahindra best platforms, BE 6 and XEV 9, Swift Dzire new for Maruti Suzuki and Tiago, Tigor refresh for Tata Motors.

items.statement: PV industry grew 4.7% YoY to 4.3M units, SUV share 55%, 2W premiumization strong
items.quote: In the PV segment, industry data from SIAM shows that the domestic PV wholesales reached 4.3 million units, reflecting a 4.7% year-on-year growth. The demand for SUVs continue to rise, with their share in total PV sales increasing to 55% in 2024, less than 50% last year.

items.statement: CV segment slowdown due to elections and reduced capex, but only mid-single-digit revenue share
items.quote: The commercial vehicle, or the CV segment, faced a slowdown due to the government elections and reduced private sector capital expenditure. However, since CVs contribute only a mid-single-digit share of our revenues, the overall impact remained limited for the company.

items.statement: Antidumping duty on PCBs to be largely localized by FY26, eliminating impact
items.quote: However, internally, we have already kick-started actions and in FY '26, we do expect a large part of this imported PCB will be localized. So in reducing or eliminating the antidumping duty impact, we do not expect this impact to continue for the most part of FY '26.

items.statement: Raw material cost pass-through to OEMs with 3-6 month lag, compensation expected late Q4 or Q1 FY26
items.quote: The raw material costs, we definitely pass on, and there is a lag of anywhere between 3 to 6 months when they compensate us back.

items.statement: Chakan plant reached 70% capacity utilization, contributing to bottom line
items.quote: But answering your question, the Chakan plant has now reached a capacity utilization of 70%. And standalone as a plant, it definitely has contributed to the bottom line.

items.statement: No new long-term debt planned, will repay per schedule showing reduction next year
items.quote: We are not looking for as such any new long-term debt. So we will continue to repay as per schedule and will show a reduction in next year.

items.statement: Selected under PLI scheme for whitegoods and automotive components
items.quote: Lumax Industries has also been selected under the PLI scheme for whitegoods and automotive components.

items.statement: Employee cost flat YoY at INR88 crores in Q3 FY25, sequential drop due to INR4 crore variable pay reversal
items.quote: So the manpower cost, if I look at on a quarter-to-quarter basis, was similar. It was about INR84 crores in Q3 FY '24 and INR88 crores in FY '25 quarter 3.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 margin pressure expected from raw material costs, antidumping duty, FX impact
items.quote: The current biggest challenge for quarter 4, which I foresee, is again on the raw material consumption. The raw material consumption, both because of the antidumping duty being imposed as well as the recent escalations on basic raw materials. Also, the foreign exchange has got a direct impact on our raw material consumption because a lot of the material is still imported.

items.statement: Revenue grew 40% YoY to INR887 crores in Q3 FY25, 31% to INR2,477 crores in 9M FY25
items.quote: On the revenue front, we have recorded a strong year-on-year growth of 40%, with revenues reaching all-time high of INR887 crores for the quarter. For the 9-month period, revenues also grew by 31%, totaling INR2,477 crores compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: PAT grew 31% YoY to INR33 crores in Q3 FY25, 28% to INR96 crores in 9M FY25
items.quote: profit after tax for Q3 FY '25 stood at INR33 crores as compared to INR26 crores in Q3 FY '24, a growth of 31%. PAT margin for Q3 FY '25 stood at 3.8%. PAT for 9 months FY '25 stood at INR96 crores, registering a growth of 28% on Y-o-Y basis with a margin at 3.9

items.statement: No immediate asset monetization plans, but open if real value achievable
items.quote: Well, as of now, we do not have any immediate plans of any asset monetization. However, if we do feel that there is something which will fetch us the real value, we will look at monetizing our assets as well.

items.statement: Targets 17% EBITDA margin within next two years from current ~12.5%
items.quote: See our goal is to get to 17% within the next two years. That's the target that we are setting ourselves internally, to achieve a 17% EBITDA margin that we want to achieve and today we are around 12.5%.

items.statement: Targets $200 million revenue in next two years
items.quote: Our target is the 200 million that we want to achieve in the next two years, is where the target that we have setup.

items.statement: Preferential issue and FCCB fundraise nearing completion; expects money before March end
items.quote: Today, we are in the fag-end of the process. It's a long, drawn out process, not just limiting to what approvals we need from the SEBI, MSE, BSE, it is also the banking requirements because there is a foreign currency involved.

items.statement: Expects to close FCCB round in one to two weeks; preferential issue on similar timeline
items.quote: I am thinking like one week, maybe max two weeks is when we will be able to close the FCCP round and similar timelines for the preferential bonds too.

items.statement: Margin improvement driven by operational efficiencies and AI tool productivity gains
items.quote: The margin improvement is primarily driven by efficiencies that we are able to squeeze out of the system itself, we found some inefficiencies, and we squeezed that out. The second thing that I told you earlier also is, we are able to get more performance improvement using some of these AI tools that we are actively using in our day-to-day outrange.

items.statement: No impact from Trump tariffs on IT services; expects deregulation to improve US IT services business
items.quote: But from a services side, there is no impact so far there is no focus on services except, the outlook is that there will be deregulation, specifically on the AI side and the cloud side and so on and so forth. Which will improve IT services business in the US.

items.statement: Growth driven by AI-enabled services, account mining existing customers, and large partnerships
items.quote: We are targeting growth in the AI and AI enabled services. That is one area of target that we are going after, and we are seeing a lot of traction in that. And also, the second thing that we have been doing is we are doing a lot of account mining, so I have given a target to our senior management team that we need to start getting more revenue from existing customers.

items.statement: Next LIC milestone payment expected within next three months on seven-year contract
items.quote: The next milestone is probably within the next three months we should get a large chunk of the money coming in.

items.statement: Global headcount ~1,750; hiring for challenging work and offering stock options to attract and retain talent
items.quote: To answer your question we are around 1600 employees globally, and that is where we have been constant around that time. And are we looking to hire people, absolutely we are looking to hire people.

items.statement: Corrected headcount to little over 1,750 employees globally
items.quote: I was corrected by the number of employees; it's actually 1750, little over 1750.

items.statement: LIC contract requires higher upfront investment recouped within three years
items.quote: Initially the amount of money we get is low, and as we get on with my multiple year contract it's a seven year contract, as you get the yearly payments will increase our outflow initially when it comes to our investment is higher from a cash flow perspective, but we recoup that probably within three years.

items.statement: 9M FY25 revenue Rs 812 crore, EBITDA Rs 99.5 crore at 12.2% margin, PAT Rs 60.5 crore at 7.4% margin
items.quote: Now, comparing that with the nine months, the nine month number is around 812 crores, with the 99.5 crores as EBITDA and a net profit of 60.5 crores.EBITDA margin is around 12.2% with a PAT margin of 7.4% for the nine months.

items.statement: Three significant client wins: advanced intelligence platform for sustainable landscape management, finops-driven digital ecosystem for large customer, AI-powered coal tracking for large power group
items.quote: So this quarter, we have had three significant client wins, just to give a little bit of a color on those three. So there is one where we are basically working, we are working with the client to revolutionize and build an advanced intelligence platform that enables them to seamlessly track funding and geospatial insights and marry that with their operational workflows.

items.statement: Operational highlights: SAP HANA rollout across 21 countries for global HPC/AI infrastructure leader; OTT content management system launch serving 33 million users recognized by MongoDB; Forbes spotlight on UN financial aid digital solution
items.quote: The first one in this quarter that was significant was the successful implementation of a SAP HANA system, which is helping them drive seamless business integration and operational efficiency across 21 countries. This is done for a global leader that provides high performance computing and AI infrastructure.

items.statement: Differentiates via nimble, agile delivery; wins deals where large IT firms failed or lack flexibility
items.quote: Sometimes it also happens that the larger IT companies are unable to provide the services, and the customers have called us basically and said, hi I am not going to name these large companies are unable to provide. They failed in their delivery. Can you now recover from it and we have done that successfully.

items.statement: No plans to enter new geographies; addressing challenges in existing geographies
items.quote: We don't want to enter new geographies, we already have enough geographies that we have, there are some challenges with some of the geographies that we are facing, and we have been addressing that, but at this point, no.

items.statement: Working capital fluctuations cause month-to-month variation; long-term debt decreasing
items.quote: But again, there will be some slight fluctuations there and the working capital will go up, whereas the long term debt is going to be lower. So based on where we are within the cycle of our usage of funds it varies from month-to-month based on the working capital.

items.statement: Working capital needs increase with growth; funded by current fundraise
items.quote: But again, there will be some slight fluctuations there and the working capital will go up, whereas the long term debt is going to be lower.
