items.quote: So, we continue to drive ADR, and we're confident that we will be able to drive ADR like we've done in the past, and there's no reason for that to change. That position still remains unchanged from previous questions that I've answered along these lines.

items.statement: Willing to sacrifice occupancy for equal or better RevPAR and higher profitability; 10-year data suggests price inelasticity
items.quote: Provided we can increase RevPAR, we will focus on and actually not only just RevPAR but RevPAR plus driving bottom line, we will be happy to sacrifice occupancy for either equal or better RevPAR or increase profitability.

items.statement: International hotels RevPAR +20% YoY; Bali and Marrakech have considerable upside; Middle East crisis stabilizing
items.quote: Our international hotels also have done considerably well versus last year. We have seen a 20% growth in terms of RevPAR, driven by the fact that last year we got badly impacted by the Israel conflict, which is now stabilizing, at least from tourism and travelers' perspective.

items.statement: Flight catering business performed incredibly well with strong topline and EBITDA growth; optimistic due to airline capacity additions
items.quote: All I can say, Yagnam, is that the business has really, really performed incredibly well and we are so happy with the performance of our flight business. We've seen strong growth in topline, we've seen strong growth in EBITDA.

items.statement: Direct booking segment driving revenue growth faster than Leisure and MICE segments
items.quote: If you look at Q3 performance, on a standalone basis, our Q3 was the highest performance, in terms of Revenue, EBITDA and PAT, driven by occupancy, as well as healthier ARR growth, which is helping the overall financials.

items.statement: No correlation analysis done between stock market declines and hotel demand; last 6 months of market decline hasn't impacted RevPAR growth
items.quote: So my.... first of all, we haven't done that analysis to correlate the stock market movements with our business. But what I can say which is reflected in the numbers is that we have strong RevPAR growth at high occupancy levels. So if that is anything to go by, then the last six months where we've seen a decline hasn't impacted us would be a reasonable assumption to make.

items.statement: Company does not provide revenue guidance; shied away from it historically
items.quote: We don't do guidance. Maybe we should but I don't know, Navin, and maybe we can have a chat separately but we've shied away from guidance.

items.statement: Vineet Kapur joined as new CFO, replacing Kallol
items.quote: Many of you will be meeting Vineet for the first time. So, Vineet joined us as CFO, and it's great to have him on board. Taking on the roles from Kallol, who all of you know.

items.statement: EIH maintains >100% MPI and ARI index vs competition, resulting in sustained RGI >100% except during COVID
items.quote: If you look at both on MPI as well as ARI, we have been able to maintain more than 100% index versus the competition. And that's resulted in a good RGI over a good sustained period of time, except for the blips, which we saw during the COVID era.

items.statement: Strong cash position maintained to support announced and planned expansion
items.quote: This is the cash flow situation. So pretty strong funds position we've been able to maintain. This will help us to support all the expansion plans which we have already announced and are planning to announce in the coming future.

items.statement: Wildflower Hall lease matter - management declines to comment beyond public domain information
items.quote: I really don't want to comment on Wildflower Hall. I think what is available in the public domain is all I would like to restrict my answer to.

items.statement: No fixed occupancy target; pricing strategy varies by hotel, segment, seasonality and competitive set to maximize RevPAR
items.quote: So, I don't, you know, and I take the direct segment. Direct segment; you have great flexibility and a large part of our business, as you can see from the slide, comes from that segment. And that's why we look at our pricing. We're just pricing based on business on books, pick up etc. So, you have the ability to yield either upwards or downwards based on demand.

items.statement: Q4 CY24 EBITDA INR320m vs INR618m YoY; full year EBITDA INR1.5bn vs INR2.1bn (-28%)
items.quote: Full year EBITDA stands at INR1.5 billion compared to INR2.1 billion in 2023, it reflects a decrease of almost 28%.

items.statement: Margin pressure from raw material inflation, adverse sales mix, high freight costs, and one-off items
items.quote: The pressure on margin has arisen due to the cost inflation, which include raw material inflation, sales and unfavorable product mix, high freight costs due to Sea crisis and a couple of one-off items.

items.statement: FMCG demand under inflationary pressure across most segments, impacting consumer spending
items.quote: In the overall ecosystem FMCG sector from which HIL derives bulk of our demand, inflationary pressures are impacting demand across most of the segments, barring a few, and it's affecting consumer spending.

items.statement: Blueloop contribution increased from 25% to 27.5% in CY24 but mainly low-end structures; high-end adoption slower
items.quote: We moved our blueloop contribution from -- sales contribution from 25% to 27% to 27.5% in last year.

items.statement: High-end blueloop structures needed for margin improvement; current low-end structures offer limited differentiation
items.quote: So that's something which is, I would say, work in progress. We have been engaging with a lot many category of our customers. And there is some kind of activation. At the same time, the adaptability -- rate of adaptability is still lower.

items.statement: No major capex planned for CY25; only maintenance capex across 10 plants
items.quote: In 2025, we are not planning for any big capex per se. But obviously, when you have managing 10 plants and always there will be one another capex will be there.

items.statement: Capacity utilization has 15-20% headroom for more production with current capacity
items.quote: But by and far, if you look at, I think we can do more production with the similar capacity. So we do have a room of somewhere between 15% to 20% more production.

items.statement: ECB of ~INR1bn outstanding; 50% repaid in Q3 CY24; no repayment scheduled in CY25, next in CY27
items.quote: End of December 2024, we have only ECB, which is reflected into our books of accounts, and that's approx INR1 billion.

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio at 0.1 post ECB repayment; strong liquidity with sizable undrawn credit lines
items.quote: Debt equity ratio now continues at 0.1 post ECB repayment in September quarter. Overall liquidity remains strong as we do have sizable credit lines, which are open with minimal utilization.

items.statement: Working capital improved YoY and QoQ; position remains comfortable
items.quote: Working capital has improved on a Y-o-Y basis as well as on a quarter-on-quarter basis on account of monitoring of the various levers and acting accordingly. The overall working capital position continues to be comfortable.

items.statement: Exports stable in CY24 despite Red Sea freight challenges; targeting higher share via tariff shifts, forex, and global coordination
items.quote: In 2024, I would say export remained stable in spite of having Red Sea influenced challenges on vessel availabilities or the sea freight and so on.

items.statement: Export contribution ~30% in CY24; management sees trajectory toward higher proportion but no specific target
items.quote: So it is definitely a very good question, I would say. Yes, there would be trend which will be improvement. I can't say whether it will be 45% or so, but there is -- as I said, 3 things: external positive environment; second, the forex; and then third, our own push.

items.statement: Centralized services and IT charges from parent rose to ~55% of EBITDA in CY24; management says arm's length benchmarked
items.quote: And in the past also, I mean, whatever the tax assessments which we have and all, we are able to justify that all transactions what we have at arm's length.

items.statement: Regulatory changes in EU and Southeast Asia driving sustainable packaging adoption; India adoption slower
items.quote: And we are also seeing that in the regulatory environment across the globe, certain countries are making changes in the regulatory requirements. I mean I don't want to go into the specifics, but at this moment, countries in some countries in European Union or in certain Southeast Asia are clearly ahead of the curve.

items.statement: Customer adoption barriers: testing protocols, global rollout timelines, cost-plus mindset, waiting for regulatory push, need for own investment
items.quote: So one is a technical or protocol-related challenge. The second one, sometimes some customers know that it is the right thing to do, but then they are waiting for some regulation to push because some of these solutions are cost plus.

items.statement: Heightened competition from small players in domestic packaging market impacting mix
items.quote: Heightened competition in the domestic market with the small time players entering into the packaging market is also impacting the mix.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR2 per share for CY24, subject to AGM approval
items.quote: For full year 2024, the Board of Directors have recommended a dividend of INR2 per share, which is subject to approval of the shareholders at the AGM of the company.

items.statement: Focus on safety performance as key tool for employee engagement and improving safety standards
items.quote: Focus area will continue to be improve upon our safety performance, which is clearly an important tool, which we use for employee engagement and improving the safety standards across the area of our businesses.

items.statement: Geopolitical impact on exports seen as temporary blip; inflation may continue to impact margins even if demand improves
items.quote: We are also noticing an impact of global geopolitical on the export side. However, we believe this is a one-off temporary blip and our strategy to focus on medium- to long-term growth initiatives and our resilience will help to see us through the same.

items.statement: Revenue CY24 INR24.5bn vs INR24.8bn (-1.2%); Q4 revenue INR6bn (+2.7% YoY, -5.3% QoQ)
items.quote: For the 12 months period ended on December '24, the top line stands at INR24.5 billion versus INR24.8 billion in 2023, a slight decrease in overall top line by 1.2%.

items.statement: Volumes flat YoY for full year CY24; Q4 volumes slightly up YoY but down QoQ
items.quote: The 12 months volume is almost flat if you compare with 2023.

items.statement: Backward integration equipment used for alternate structures; not yet accretive to margins until high-end blueloop scales
items.quote: So right now, yes, equipments are not idle, but they are used for alternate structures where we have a capability to buy in the marketplace and produce in-house. So when we compare, at this moment, it is not really helping us in terms of any accretive margin improvement.

items.statement: Cash balance ~INR300cr; no concrete deployment plan yet
items.quote: As of now, we'll continue with that. And in due course of time, we'll decide how we are going to deploy that. So no concrete action plan at this point of time.

items.statement: Tube laminates a key focus for blueloop adoption; currently domestic-focused with export expansion planned
items.quote: And maybe I would say this business and this type of customers are one of the forefront to adopt our blueloop structures. And so that is going in the right direction.

items.statement: Rural consumption showing promising improvement; urban recovery expected but timing uncertain
items.quote: But other side, if you look at rural economy is showing some promising improvement. However, urban is taking time. So expectation is that when we read the articles and something is there really expected that urban is also going to come back.

items.statement: Margin recovery expected as demand improves and blueloop high-end scales; no specific timeline given
items.quote: We shall see that in future quarters. We should see some revival.

items.statement: Revised FY25 consolidated EBITDA target to INR100 crores from earlier INR130 crores due to subsidiary underperformance
items.quote: So in the light of this, I would say that considering the good performance of standalone in Q4, we should be doing about INR100 crores of EBITDA for the full year.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin target 13-14% for FY26; consolidated subsidiary EBITDA margin target 6-7% for FY26
items.quote: At a standalone level, we should be able to achieve around 13% to 14%. And at a subsidiary level, including Canada, we should be between 6% to 7% of EBITDA.

items.statement: Revised FY25 consolidated revenue growth guidance to 13% on gross accounting basis from earlier 18% due to Canadian subsidiary drag
items.quote: We expect to close the year with gross accounting 13% of revenue growth as against the 18%, and mainly because of the drop in the subsidiary.

items.statement: No consolidated FY26 guidance given due to pending strategic decisions on Canadian subsidiary
items.quote: At this point of time, I wouldn't guide anything. Let us -- because we have certain actions to take in the Canadian subsidiary, perhaps we can see it in the next concall.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin 6.9%, standalone 11.8%; margins impacted by Canadian subsidiary losses and France utilization delays
items.quote: The Q3 FY25 our consolidated EBITDA margins stood at 6.9% and standalone EBITDA margin stood at 11.8%. Our margins were impacted mainly due to the losses in the Canadian subsidiary and lower utilization due to delays in new project starts in France.

items.statement: Target to improve subsidiary margins to 7% in short term and 11-12% in subsequent years
items.quote: Our objective is to try to move that margin up to a 7% level or so in the short-term in the coming year, and then push it up further as growth comes in to 11% to 12% range in the subsequent years.

items.statement: Standalone BTS EBITDA margin 18-20%, EMS 11-13% on yearly basis; French engineering services ~4% but pulled down by Canadian losses
items.quote: BTS generally is about 18% to 20%, and EMS, it is between 11% to 13%. And that is what we are targeting and we are achieving on a yearly basis.

items.statement: Consolidated order book INR1,675 crores as of 31 Dec 2024; domestic BTS order book grew from INR376 crores (FY23) to INR563 crores (9M FY25)
items.quote: Our order book position stands at INR1,675 crores as on 31st December, 2024. Our pipeline continues t o remain strong for both Build t o Spec and EMS customers in our standalone

items.statement: Domestic BTS order book expected to further improve by end of FY25 with additional Q4 orders
items.quote: We expect this to further improve by the end of this financial year with some additional orders that we're expecting in Q4 as well.

items.statement: Recognized as platinum and panel supplier for engineering services by Airbus and Thales; strong engagement with multiple customers in France
items.quote: We have actually a very good feedback and engagement with multiple cust omers, including with Airbus, with Thales. In fact, just in the last few weeks we have been recognized as a platinum and panel supplier for their engineering services business

items.statement: Won over INR300 crores contract for satellite-based payloads for Electronic Warfare Applications; expecting substantial Q4 orders from radar domain for naval programs
items.quote: We've, just in the last year, won over INR300 crore s contract for satellite-based payloads for Electronic Warfare Applications. In Q4, we are also expecting some substantial orders, and we will receive them from the radar domain, and these are for naval programs

items.statement: Board approved fundraising via QIP or other means for growth capital to support standalone business opportunities
items.quote: We sought and got approval from our Board to be able to raise some funds through either a QIP or other means. And so we are pursuing those options, but we will be able to share that information maybe a bit later on.

items.statement: Fundraise approved by Board is growth capital for standalone business expansion opportunities
items.quote: The fund raise, which actually we've got the approval, but the timing-wise we need to get back, is essentially a growth capital. So that's what I wanted to add.

items.statement: France engineering services onshore/offshore split ~65% onshore, 35% offshore; shifting work from Canada to India for cost advantage
items.quote: So in terms of headcount, we are roughly about 60% -- you can say 2/3, so 65% or so in onshore and 35% offshore. That's a rough breakup.

items.statement: Created India team over last 12-18 months to execute Canadian work; majority of new contract execution now from India
items.quote: in the meanwhile what we've also been doing is, in the last 12 to 18 months, have created a team in India that is able to execute the similar kind of work. So we have been shifting a lot of the work from Canada to India, especially on some of the new c ontracts that we've won

items.statement: Canadian subsidiary losses dragging consolidated P&L; strategic decisions on Canadian operations expected in next couple of quarters
items.quote: We will be basically making some strategic decisions with regard to the Canadian operations in the next couple of quarters to ensure that it doesn't continue to drag the overall P&L.

items.statement: Canadian subsidiary turnaround targeted by June 2025 best case, September 2025 worst case; may involve exceptional costs
items.quote: I would say June is a good estimate. The worst case before September we should be able to ensure that Canada is no longer a dragger.

items.statement: Exceptional provision for entire exposure in Ausar Energy (30% associate) referred to French court redressement judiciaire; four interested bidders, partial recovery hoped
items.quote: As a matter of abundant caution and prudence, we have provided for the entire exposure. But as it evolves, perhaps in the next month or so, we should be able to get a better clarity.

items.statement: Space sector: delivering full satellite payloads, won largest ever order for 3-satellite constellation; expect repeat constellations and ISRO opportunities
items.quote: this year marked -- or basically 2024 marked the biggest order that we've received in the space sector so far, wh ich was for a constellation of three satellites, payloads for that

items.statement: Domestic BTS order book grew from INR376 crores (FY23) to INR427 crores (FY24) to INR563 crores (9M FY25)
items.quote: Our domestic or standalone BTS order book, which has increased quite well from where it was at around INR376 crores at the end of FY '23 to INR427 crores at the end of FY '24 to INR563 crores at the end of 9 months.

items.statement: Gross value of net-accounted contracts INR32 crores in Q3 FY25 and INR71 crores for 9M FY25; adjusting for gross, Q3 revenue grew 13% QoQ and 9M grew 6% YoY
items.quote: The gross value of such contracts was INR32 crores in Q3 FY25 and INR71 crores for 9 months FY25. So adjusting for gross value, the revenue for Q3 FY '25 has grown by 13% quarter-on-quarter and for the 9 months FY25 by 6% year-on-year.

items.statement: Standalone business heavily skewed to Q4 for Build-to-Spec defense/space revenue; EMS new customers in ramp-up phase
items.quote: a la rge part of the revenue for the Build To Spec business in the standalone entity is expected in Q4 of the financial year, and that should help improve the revenue and the margins

items.statement: Ausar Energy associate under French court redressement judiciaire process; provision made for full exposure
items.quote: This company has now been referred to redressement judiciaire which is a process by which the French court tries to revive the company towards its sustenance and growth.

items.statement: Board-level discussions ongoing on subsidiary strategy given shareholder feedback on time/resources spent; serious deliberation on Canadian operations
items.quote: These discussions are being deliberated very, very seriously at our Board level also. And as I mentioned, some of the decisions or discussions that we are having with regard to the Canadian operations as a first, but more generally, the subsidiary are being discussed and considered.

items.statement: Received STPI Export Award for FY23-24 for Best Performing Electronic Hardware Exports from Karnataka
items.quote: Centum also received an Export Award for FY'23-'24 recognizing the Best Performing Electronic Hardware Exports from STPI in Karnataka.

items.statement: Gross accounting difference between net and gross revenue expected to normalize from FY26
items.quote: Yes. FY '26, it should get normalized.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to improve from next financial year as annual procurement contracts expire on 31st March 2025
items.quote: See, the EBITDA margins should certainly improve going forward from coming year because our procurement contracts are for -- on an annual basis, which will expire by 31st of March this year.

items.statement: Top line growth expected at 8% to 10% for the industry overall
items.quote: Top line growth, we are certainly looking, as I was telling earlier to replying to a question that we expect made me to grow much faster than what we have shown so far. We have also said that agriculture business is definitely growing in India at a reasonable rate and we would be seeing a growth overall at 8% to 10% for the industry as a whole.

items.statement: Building Products segment to grow faster than current rates, targeting to double the rate of growth next year
items.quote: Building Products segment will grow faster than what we have grown so far. Thinking that the growth rates will be faster than what we have today.

items.statement: Agriculture segment to continue growing at regular 8% to 10% annual growth rate
items.quote: Agriculture will continue to grow as per the regular 8% to 10% annual growth rate.

items.statement: Industrial segment to remain limited and cautious, not pursuing aggressive growth
items.quote: As far as Industrial is concerned, I mean, after election is, almost new budget has also come, money allocation has been made. So there will be better demand in institutional business or supplies. But as I have been maintaining, we'll be careful. We will not go very aggressive on this.

items.statement: INR20 crores capex already spent in current year, expansion plans nearing finalization before end of financial year
items.quote: Already during this current year, INR20 crores capex has been -- payout has been already made, and we are further going ahead with our plans. Our plans are almost towards conclusion before end of this financial year before we make annual operating plan for the coming year.

items.statement: Fungible extrusion capacity exists; moulding capacity being augmented for Building Products
items.quote: There is a fungible capacity. Not everything, but quite a substantial portion of the extrusion is possible, but molding is specific to our business because molds are specific.

items.statement: Extrusion side has adequate capacity; moulding side needs further augmentation
items.quote: Extrusion side, we have adequate capacity. But moulding side, we still have to catch up with the requirement, which we have built up in last some time with this capex we have done. And we'll be further augmenting our moulding capacities.

items.statement: Building materials demand consistent across all regions, temporary impact of 10-15 days from unseasonal rains
items.quote: See, as far as building materials are concerned, the demand is consistent and across all segments across India. It is not affected by sudden rains or short rain cycles. There can be a temporary impact of 10 days, 15 days, nothing more.

items.statement: Industrial segment demand improving post-elections with new budget allocations
items.quote: The industrial segment is looking up now because now after elections, I think the new finances are getting cleared and those monies will flow.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA loss of INR1.4 crores and net loss of INR11 crores; 9M FY25 EBITDA margin at 4.83%
items.quote: There was an EBITDA loss of INR1.4 crores and a net loss of INR11 crores for this quarter. For the 9 months ended financial year 2025, our revenues were around INR584 crores, which declined by around 13% on Y-o-Y basis. EBITDA declined by 38% on Y-o-Y basis to INR28 crores with EBITDA margin reported at 4.83%.

items.statement: Building Products segment offers better EBITDA margins than Agri; industry EBITDA margins typically 16-20%
items.quote: I certainly feel that the building segment has offered much better EBITDA margins than Agri, and that's where our focus is. And if material price is correct, the EBITDA margin should be in line with the industry. And you will see generally industry is showing between 16% to 20% EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Raw material procurement prices 7-9% above open market prices due to annual contracts linked to international benchmarks
items.quote: I mean, the difference between local market and the raw material manufacturers or landed prices were to the significant extent of 8%, 7%, 9% with month-to-month, they will be even higher than that.

items.statement: Local raw material manufacturers have started correcting prices in current month
items.quote: But now for the first time, you can see that even local manufacturers are correcting their prices.

items.statement: PVC raw material prices declining globally; India imports 60% of PVC demand; local market prices suppressed by high import volumes
items.quote: You see, the question is that you see when prices are on a declining trend, your imports normally arrive on Indian shore after 40 days or 45 days of shipments. So, there is a time lag between the price contracted to the material delivered. Number two, the local prices of local manufacturers generally are aligned with -- and the local market prices are aligned with a marginal difference maybe here

items.statement: Annual procurement contracts linked to Platt's international prices; contracts expire March 2025
items.quote: Prices are linked to Platt. This is an international exchange, which determines the prices. They are linked. So prices are linked and the local market operates on a buying selling. So there is a definite difference between two.

items.statement: Government has circulated country-wise manufacturer-wise anti-dumping duty on PVC; final notification awaited
items.quote: Government has already issued and circulated country-wise manufacture-wise ADD, which they would like to apply. The only notification is awaited, which we are still not…

items.statement: Major dumping of PVC identified from a neighboring country (China implied)
items.quote: I can't give you the exact numbers, but generally, what people discuss and industry talks is the major dumping is coming from a country next to us.

items.statement: Focus shifting to higher-margin Building Products; Agri at 78% of revenue; Industrial segment reduced 73%
items.quote: We will certainly look towards higher-margin products. And we will also look at the opportunities around which we would like to cash.

items.statement: Building Products volumes grew 30% YoY to 2,262 MT; Agri volumes grew 2% YoY to 16,511 MT; Industrial volumes declined 73% YoY to 931 MT
items.quote: The Agri segment volumes grew marginally by 2% year-on-year basis to 16,511 metric tons as compared to 16,230 metric tons in Q3 financial year '24. The Building Products segment total volumes grew by 30% year-on-year to 2,262 metric tons as compared to 1,753 metric tons in Q3 financial year '24. While the Industrial segment volumes declined significantly from 3,496 metric tons in Q3 financial year

items.statement: Institutional sales to EPC contractors reduced significantly due to payment cycle concerns; dealer network has firm payment cycles with minimal receivables
items.quote: We don't have outstanding receivables Saket because our policies are of very firm payment cycle from all the dealers. And we are mostly engaged with our own dealers. And as far as institutional sales are concerned, as you are saying, our sales have come down significantly. So I mean, there are hardly any outstanding as far as institutions are concerned because you would see that from a level of --

items.statement: Promoters converted INR17 crores of warrants into equity; remaining 50% conversion planned next financial year; company comfortably placed on debt
items.quote: Only promoters have converted about 17 crores worth of warrants into equity. And the reason I always explain, you see in the current stock exchange rules, if you are having acquisition of more than 5% on a basis, it triggers certain other rules. So we wanted to be very careful. That's why we want to divide into two financial years. So 50% conversion was done here and 50% will be done in the next f

items.statement: Net debt increased from INR105 crores to INR112 crores; company conservative on additional debt
items.quote: No. I mean as far as company's financial placement is concerned, we are comfortably placed. We don't have much debt on book. And we are working on a business plan where we will be conservative towards additional debt.

items.statement: Warrant funds to be drawn only when capex cycle starts; prudent financial management
items.quote: Because we will take funds only when we are starting our capex cycle. We don't want to take any money upfront and pass the money here. We must be very prudent in our financials.

items.statement: Worst of raw material price impact may be behind; Q4 FY25 still challenging; improvement expected from Q1 FY26
items.quote: I think the things have started getting on a correction side. I would say that this Q4 may be still not that great. But from Q1 next year, we hope to be doing much better and what we expect because we'll be able to put all things behind us by then.

items.statement: Similar raw material price collapse experienced during 2008 global financial crisis
items.quote: I had experienced similar situation in 2008 at the time of world crisis financial crisis. Sivaramakrishna Kodali: In the global financial crisis. Shiv Singh Mehta: Financial crisis. At that time also, the prices dropped like nine pin almost. And this is, again, we are experiencing this year in the international market

items.statement: CPVC revenue target of INR170 crores being worked towards for next year
items.quote: Yes, we are definitely working towards that number. And I think you will see coming next year, our numbers would be far, far better than what probably we have so far achieved because our all efforts are to development of market and business in the building materials segment.

items.statement: SCD achieved 11.8% EBITDA margin in Q3 FY25, first time in double digits
items.quote: For the first time, it has declared a double-digit EBITDA margin of 12%, 11.8%.

items.statement: Chairman believes SCD margin improvement is sustainable due to operational excellence across plants
items.quote: Is it sustainable? I would believe so that it is sustainable. I think the operations continues to be pretty good going forward.

items.statement: SED installed a new SMT production line now fully operational to fill capacity
items.quote: To cater to the growing needs of our customers, we also inst alled a new SMT production line, which is now fully operational and will help us fill capacity and manage capacity going forward

items.statement: Morocco plant moved from 3-shift to 1-shift operation showing productivity gains
items.quote: we have, for example, moved from a 3-shift operation, we are moving to just about a 1-shift operation, which shows the kind of productivity improvements that we could have done on the same revenue and sales.

items.statement: SCD winning new electronic product contracts from major off-highway OEMs
items.quote: in the last quarter, we saw them winning business for the electronic products, at least for our electric EV division, like various sensors, starters from 2 of the major off-highway OEMs.

items.statement: SED margins impacted by product mix changes due to EV volume shifts
items.quote: This meant that revenue grew, but some of the margins were impacted by product mix changes.

items.statement: SED won throttle project from leading EV 2-wheeler customer and global off-highway electronics projects
items.quote: we won a very good throttle project from a key leading EV 2-wheeler customer. And we also secured global off-highway projects in electronics from these off-highway customers

items.statement: Shifting motor sourcing for Matamoros from France/China to India to reduce cost and supply chain pain
items.quote: we are also doing our part of the job to try to develop alternate motor source to avoid the motor duty issue and that would be from India.

items.statement: In-sourced electronic board production from external supplier to SCD India for Matamoros plant
items.quote: we used to buy these populated boards and PCBs for our Matamoros plant. And that we switched the source to India, that is SCD. Therefore, we in-sourced it within the group.

items.statement: Matamoros tariff case pending in court; engaging customers for cost recovery
items.quote: On the tariff front, we have gone to the court, as you know, and like any courts in any part of the world, justice moves very slowly. So having said that, we have not kept quiet. We have been engaging the customers, customer and also and trying to claw back and have some sort of a compensation.

items.statement: SCS second tranche (China and Canada) expected to close in Q4 FY25 or early Q1 FY26
items.period: Q4 FY25 or early Q1 FY26
items.quote: the second tranche was China and Canada, and that is under discussion. As you know, we've set up the entities to make these acquisitions in both Canada and China. But this is expected to close in Q4 or early Q1 of next year.

items.statement: SCS China and Canada business is profitable and will improve consolidated SCS performance from April 2025
items.quote: when the second tranche closes, the China and Canada part, that is actually a profitable part of that business. So, when you look at together as SCS, let's say, from 1st of April onwards, I think the numbers should look slightly better.

items.statement: Morocco plant strategically located for US/Europe supply; 4-5 days to US East Coast
items.quote: Morocco is very strategically located. And Tangier, where we have our plant is the sixth largest, I think, port in the world with just a few hours to Europe and probably less than a week, maybe 4, 5 days to U.S. to East Coast of U.S.

items.statement: Wescon non-auto business at bottom; margins improved via operational excellence despite volume decline
items.quote: I think we are in the bottom of the pit. I think in the next 1, 2 quarters, it should stabilize and start improving. The important point is that we have tightened our belt so much despite these low volumes, Wescon is turning out good margins.

items.statement: Poland plant closing in next 2 quarters; Germany warehouse moving near Hungary plant
items.quote: Poland plant will soon be closed. It's already dwindled down to a few team members only in the Poland plant, but now will be completely closed in the coming 2 quarters. And the Germany warehouse will be shifted to a location very close to Suprajit Hungary

items.statement: Total debt INR 627 crores; cash surplus INR 276 crores in mutual funds and bonds as of Dec 31, 2024
items.quote: The total debt level was INR627 crores as on 31st December 2024. The cash surplus invested in the mutual funds and bonds was INR276 crores as on 31st December 2024.

items.statement: Indian cable exports grew 35% in 9M FY25 showing global strategy strength
items.quote: Our Indian cable exports saw a fantastic 35% growth. This shows the underlying strength in our global strategy as to how we have moved literally almost, I would say, conquered the Western world.

items.statement: Forex gain in Q3 FY25; Q2 forex impact to be confirmed later
items.quote: Overall gain, Mumuksh.

items.statement: Deployed operational excellence team from India including MD to Morocco for SCS turnaround
items.quote: we have deployed our operational excellence team from India, including Mohan, as you know, who is now talking from Morocco, who is leading this effort as well.

items.statement: SED second SMT line installed but EV customer volumes collapsed causing underutilization
items.quote: We have set up another top line, SMT line, which went into production recently I mean, in that quarter. But the point is we also set up the overheads to set it up as well. But the volumes have not picked up because some of these EV players whose volumes have been projected and we have been pushing us to set up the second line, suddenly, the volumes have all collapsed.

items.statement: New SCD contracts at better margins replacing legacy low-priced contracts from LDC acquisition
items.quote: The legacy old products where we have bad pricing when we acquired, let's say, LDC, they are slowly going away and the newer contracts are getting in.

items.statement: No pre-buying by customers ahead of potential tariffs
items.quote: No. Answer is no. Nobody stocks up these things.

items.statement: Effective tax rate ~26-27% for year; Q3 spike due to mutual fund/bond redemption tax
items.quote: Around 26%, 27% only. That will continue. There is no change in that. But in the quarter, this was an exceptional item actually.

items.statement: Products & Solutions revenue grew 10% YoY in Q3 FY25 driven by government and BFSI customers; retail expansion also contributed
items.quote: The increase in revenue in the Products and Solutions vertical attributed to the increase in businesses with the government and BFSI customers. For the retail segment, where we are expanding our reach as a single point solution provider also contributed to an increase in revenue.

items.statement: Customer Support Services revenue grew 28% YoY in Q3 FY25 from higher volumes from existing customers and new business additions
items.quote: The increase in revenue in the customer support vertical is attributable to an increase in the volume from existing customers and addition of few new businesses.

items.statement: EBITDA was Rs 3 crore in Q3 FY25, up significantly YoY; net loss narrowed to Rs 70 lakh YoY and QoQ
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was around 3 crores, representing a significant increase year-on-year, and net loss was reported at approximately 70 lakhs, which has also reduced on both year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: 9M FY25 EBITDA grew 27% YoY to Rs 9 crore; net loss was Rs 3 crore
items.quote: EBITDA for the 9 months was around 9 crores, representing a growth of 27% year-on-year, and the net loss was reported at approximately 3 crores.

items.statement: Captive SMT line usage may improve EBITDA by 1-2% over time; short-term impact minimal due to cost recovery
items.quote: From EBITDA perspective, we expect in the short run it may not have much impact as it is all newly started and there will be another recovery of cost. But over a period of time, we expect at least 1% to 2% improvement in EBITDA through these initiatives for the internal consumption, captive consumption.

items.statement: IATF certification for automotive EMS expected in a couple of quarters; SMT line currently used for captive consumption
items.quote: Work on that is going on, and we should be certified in a couple of quarters max because that needs some kind of preparation.

items.statement: Additional SMT lines will be added as EMS business grows; timeline depends on order inflow and could be a few quarters to several years
items.quote: The line can be set up really quickly. If the business grows really fast, those number of lines can come fast. If the business does not come in, those lines in 3 years also will not make any meaning.

items.statement: Solar O&M megawatts under management expected to reach 800-900 MW by year-end; revenue remains small relative to capacity
items.quote: Yes, we have added a few more megawatts, and I think we hope to end the year with about 800 to 900 megawatts under management, and it will consistently grow on that side.

items.statement: Infra Managed Services yet to win large customers; will announce when deals are closed
items.quote: On the IMF side, we are yet to crack any big customers, and when that happens, you will definitely hear from us.

items.statement: Mobile printers gaining traction in government last-mile digitisation projects, led by Department of Post
items.quote: Yes, that is where the traction is, because if you notice the Department of Post was one big customer, a couple of others who are looking at taking the print or the business to the last mile into much more of the heart of India, that is where the mobile printers are being used and commissioned and that is where the use case has increased.

items.statement: AIDC (barcode) products are a new initiative facing entry barriers; traction building gradually
items.quote: AIDC has been a new entrant. We have been a new entrant to AIDC. That is why we are concerned that's a new initiative, and it has to sort of as a new entrant all the entry barriers which we face, we continue to face. So we are working on that, and hopefully you will see how the traction transforms.

items.statement: Addressable market for Products & Solutions assessed at Rs 2,000 crore with 18-20% market share; market growing at 8-10% annually
items.quote: My understanding is the market is growing at about 8 to 10 percent. Last year and year before were particularly different, difficult market years. But I think overall it is about 8 to 10 percent of the growth that has been attributed to the segment, Mr. Patel.

items.statement: Make in India and PLI schemes evolving; industry and government need to collaborate further to curb cheap imports
items.quote: I think the government has done a lot for Make in India initiative. A lot more needs to be done. The scenarios are slowly evolving, and we do certainly, like you rightly pointed out, see a lot of imports, finished goods from overseas, which are disrupting the market. So I think the industry as a whole and the government needs to work together to see how to further ensure that the PLI or the Make i

items.statement: Employee costs ~Rs 19 crore/quarter; will rise faster than revenue initially as business development and operations teams expand, then stabilise
items.quote: Initially it will increase a little faster, but I think it will stabilize as the revenue grows a little faster than for the revenue growth of all the new initiatives.

items.statement: Government project rollouts (e.g., mobile printers) face delays due to elections and policy uncertainty; no real-time visibility on timing
items.quote: Without commenting on the way the government works, the hope that they will digitize soon and quickly. But every time there is an election, if there is something, these projects keep getting delayed. So we really do not have a real-time understanding of how these things work at this point.

items.statement: Management acknowledges investor frustration over limited forward guidance; commits to more structured communication at the right time
items.quote: I know the investor community is frustrated. I know the investor community thinks we are keeping them in the dark. Maybe not on purpose, but that is a policy which the company is following. We will find the right time and engage a little more if that makes sense at the right time.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM target to reach 22,000-23,000 by FY25 end, closer to pre-ban 24,000-25,000 level
items.quote: I think the year we should end at around 22, 23 and it will take maybe some more time to get to 25.

items.statement: Gold loan yields expected to normalize in FY26, with at least 1% recovery in Q1 FY26
items.quote: This year is -- so next financial year, maybe from first quarter itself, we'll see that the yield coming back to the normal levels. The whole year will be normal.

items.statement: MFI credit cost guidance of 8% to 8.5% for the current period
items.quote: On an average, we will be looking at a credit cost of around, for this, around 8% to 8.5% kind of a thing.

items.statement: Expect worst of provisions behind, improvement from Q4 FY25 onwards
items.quote: I believe that we have taken, in case of MSME, our insurance cover starts from the loans, I think from September or October. In microfinance, I think some pain is still there, but it may not be as bad as the third quarter, which was the worst ever quarter.

items.statement: Gold loan volume growth strong, demand sufficient to approach pre-ban levels
items.quote: So for the time being, it looks like that our volume growth will be stronger. So we -- at the time of ban, we had 10,000, then we went up to 11,000 in the 10 days after the ban in September then 15,000.

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio yield down ~2% due to competitive pricing to regain customers
items.quote: Gold loan volume growth is there, but the portfolio yield is down by almost 2%.

items.statement: Spread normalization expected in FY26 as cost of funds peaks and yields recover
items.quote: I think next financial year as a whole and, of course, the trend will be evident from the first quarter itself.

items.statement: Consolidated loan AUM at INR 71,410 crores, down 8% YoY, up 7% QoQ
items.quote: For the quarter, our consolidated loan AUM fell by 8% year-on-year and was up 7% quarter-on-quarter. It is now INR 71,410 crores.

items.statement: Assigned loan book at INR 12,472 crores, down 33% YoY and 11% QoQ due to RBI embargo limiting seasoned assets
items.quote: The assigned loan book stands at INR 12,472 crores, which is down 33% year-on-year and 11% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Co-lending assets at INR 9,236 crores, down 20% YoY but up 9% QoQ
items.quote: We also have co-lending assets of INR 9,236 crores, which is down 20% year-on-year and up 9% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Gross NPA 2.4%, Net NPA 1%, up 70bps and 14bps YoY due to MFI, unsecured, small ticket LAP stress
items.quote: Our gross NPA stood at 2.4% and net NPA was at 1%, which is up 70 basis points and 14 basis points, respectively, when compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: MFI zero-day bucket forward flow declining, collections improving across most states
items.quote: I think the forward flow in the zero -day bucket is slowly coming down. So that was the initial thing. So yes, thing s -- I mean, the things have improved in the last 3, 4 months

items.statement: Quarterly average cost of borrowing at 9.16%, up 9bps YoY and 1bp QoQ
items.quote: Our quarterly average cost of borrowing increased 9 basis points year-on-year and 1 basis point quarter-on-quarter to hit 9.16%.

items.statement: Dollar bond issued in January at near double-digit fully hedged cost, will impact Q4 weighted average cost
items.quote: The dollar bond that we have raised in the month of January with full hedging, the cost is significantly higher. It's almost kind of double digit, and that will impact the weighted average cost of fund going forward.

items.statement: Cost of funds appears to have peaked, incremental moderation expected post Q4
items.quote: I think that the cost of funds also seem to have peaked out. But the impact of -- okay, what happens is that, as I said that we raised high-cost money in the month of January. So your March quarter impact will be there of the cost of fund. But beyond that, I think the incrementally we see cost of funds moderating.

items.statement: Raised INR 9,964 crores via term loans, bonds, CP and INR 1,477 crores via assignment in Q3
items.quote: During the quarter, we raised INR 9,964 crores through term loans, bonds, and commercial paper and INR 1,477 crores was raised from assignment.

items.statement: Cash and committed credit lines at INR 5,656 crores as of Dec 31, adequate for 6 months maturities of INR 5,297 crores
items.quote: Our cash and cash equivalent and committed credit lines from banks and institutions stood at INR5,656 crores. This is adequate to meet near-term liabilities, but also fund growth.

items.statement: Dollar bond proceeds received Jan 24, liquidity now back to normal levels above 6-month coverage
items.quote: The dollar bond issue money came on the 14th -- sorry, 24th of January in this quarter. So the liquidity as we speak is back to the normal level, but you don't see them in these results, you see them in the next quarter.

items.statement: Net gearing at 3.1x, positive ALM in all buckets
items.quote: We have a positive ALM in all buckets and our net gearing is at about 3.1x.

items.statement: Karnataka MFI ordinance causing temporary repayment disturbances despite exemption for regulated entities
items.quote: The Karnataka government's regulation on MFI, although targeted at unregulated entities, is affecting the borrower sentiment and the repayment culture.

items.statement: RBI guardrails reducing MFI loan limits to INR 2 lakh and lender count to 3-4, structurally limiting MFI growth
items.quote: Because the new guardrails, which restrict the loan amount to broadly say INR2 lakh instead of INR3 lakh, number of lenders from unlimited to 4 or maybe 3 going forward.

items.statement: Target portfolio mix: Home loan ~33%, Gold loan ~33%, MFI 8-10%, MSME 20-25% (70% secured), Unsecured <15%
items.quote: So both these will be around, say, 1/3, 1/3 of our total portfolio. And microfinance may be around 8% to 10%. And then another 20%, 25% will be MSME loan, 25% or so, which will have 2/3 or 70% will be secured and the remaining will be unsecured. Broadly speaking, our unsecured -- our target is to bring it to 15% or lower of the total portfolio.

items.statement: Capital adequacy: NBFC 22%, HFC 46.2%, Samasta 32.2%, all well above 15% minimum
items.quote: Our capital adequacy for the NBFC is at 22%, HFC at about 46.2%, and for Samasta Microfinance is 32.2%, which is well above the minimum threshold of 15%.

items.statement: MFI borrower sentiment impacted by credit restrictions, leading to voluntary defaults despite repayment capacity
items.quote: The borrowers as they know that they are not going to get new loan because of the restrictions on the number of loans or the amount of loan or also many microfinance companies pulling back, then they stop repaying the earlier loan and/or whatever they have because they say that, okay, we are not going to get new loans.

items.statement: ADIA invested for 7+ year horizon, no push for HFC demerger, will be done strategically when appropriate
items.quote: ADIA is a long-term investor. So I think there is some understanding that they are invested for at least 7 years in terms of their own investment horizon. So it will be done strategically whenever it's appropriate time.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guided at 15-20% and EBITDA margin at 14.5-15%
items.quote: anywhere close to between 15% to 20% would be our estimate in terms of the top line growth. I think our endeavour is to continue to sustain and further expand these EBITDA margins in FY '26 as well

items.statement: FY25 full-year revenue expected around INR 3,500 crores with EBITDA margin similar to 9M
items.quote: we should be looking – to similar a 9 -monthFY25 growth, anywhere between 20% to 25%, which should ideally get the total consolidated revenues closer to around INR 3,500 crores, and we should be able to sustain a similar EBITDA margin in quarter 4 as well.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY25 maintained at INR 130-140 crores
items.quote: The guidance for the full year remains at INR 130 crores to INR140 crores.

items.statement: Total order book INR 1,350 crores; 90% new business; 30% maturing FY26, 40% FY27, 30% FY28; ~40% EV
items.quote: The total order book, considering the value of all product categories, are INR 1,350 crores, out of which 90% is new business. 30% order book value will mature in FY '26, 40% in FY '27 and remaining 30% in FY '28. EV contribution is approximately 40% of the total order book.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 14% in Q3 and 9M FY25; absolute EBITDA INR 127 cr (Q3) and INR 350 cr (9M)
items.quote: EBITDA margin stands at 14% for Q3. Absolute EBITDA for Q3 is at INR127 crores, a growth of 9% on a year -on-year basis. 9 months '25 margins stood at 14% with EBITDA growing by 15% at INR350 crores on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin ~10.5% for 9M FY25, up 60-70 bps YoY excluding other income
items.quote: the EBITDA margin, if we exclude the other income part, yes, it has grown by almost 60 to 70 basis points, which you said at closer to 10.5% for the 9 months.

items.statement: Aftermarket Q4 FY25 expected double-digit growth YoY; FY26 double-digit growth to continue; target to double Aftermarket revenue in 3 years driven by exports
items.quote: for quarter 4 stand alone, we should be looking at a good double-digit growth rate, which is pretty similar to what the Aftermarket division used to do up until FY '24. Giving you a horizon, I think this growth momentum in FY '26 will continue very healthy into a double-digit territory. And yes, our endeavor is still to double the Aftermarket revenues in the next 3-year time frame, given the fact

items.statement: PV share rose to 50% of 9M FY25 revenue from 47% YoY; 2/3W 25%, Aftermarket 12%, CV 8%, others 5%
items.quote: With increased focus on passenger vehicle segment and integration of IAC, our share of passenger vehicle stood at 50% in 9 months FY '25 as compared to 47% in last year. In 9 months, FY '25, 2/3-wheeler contribution to overall revenue is at 25%, Aftermarket at 12%, our CV at 8% and balance 5% was contributed by other categories.

items.statement: EV agnostic products contribute >90% of value; expected to remain so for 24-36 months
items.quote: more than 90% of the value contribution continues to come from EV agnostic products, and we don't see this trend changing at least over the next 24 to 36 months.

items.statement: 9M FY25 capex INR 83 crores mainly for IAC and Lumax Alps new product SOPs; full year guidance INR 130-140 crores
items.quote: The capex outlay during 9 months has been at INR83 crores, majorly on account of new products SOPs in IAC and Lumax Alps. The guidance for the full year remains at INR 130 crores to INR140 crores.

items.statement: Lumax FAE oxygen sensor capacity utilization to rise from ~10% to 45% in FY26 with OBD2 implementation; targeting 70% in FY27 with second OEM
items.quote: This will take care for a full year capacity utilization of about 45%, which was earlier hovering around 10% because of the non- implementation of OBD2. We are aggressively pursuing the second OEM then to fill up the remaining capacity and that's the reason FY '27 would be the e date of the second OEM.

items.statement: Raw material price increases seen but recoverable from OEMs in 3-6 months lag
items.quote: There are certain signs of raw material pricing going up. But again, that is a lag. We should be able to recover them from the OEMs in 3 to 6 months' time frame.

items.statement: OBD2 implementation from April 2025 to add INR 60-70 crores full-year revenue for Lumax FAE via secondary oxygen sensor
items.quote: We are anticipating almost INR 60 crores to INR70 crores increase in our top line revenues with the implementation of the secondary oxygen sensor, which now becomes mandatory from 1st April 2025.

items.statement: Long-term debt INR 462 crores as of 31 Dec 2024, up due to Greenfuel acquisition; debt/equity 0.53; free cash INR 315 crores
items.value: INR 462 crores debt; 0.53 D/E; INR 315 crores free cash
items.quote: The company is sitting on a healthy free cash of INR 315 crores as on 31st December, whereas the long-term debt is at INR462 crores, which has increased from previous quarter due to acquisition for the purchase consideration of Greenfuel Energy. The long-term debt equity ratio stands at 0.53 as on 31st December.

items.statement: Aftermarket exported ~2,000 CNG kits to Africa (PV and buses); exploring more geographies for conversion kits
items.quote: On the Aftermarket, yes, we have already supplied about 2,000 CNG kits to the African market. We do believe that there is a tremendous export potential of converting CNG kits in Africa. We've done this for passenger vehicles as well as buses, and we contin ue to explore further geographies and territories for penetrating this conversion

items.statement: Lumax Ituran Telematics received Hall of Fame Award from Daimler India Commercial Vehicles for 100% delivery and quality
items.quote: The subsidiary company, Lumax Ituran Telematics, received a prestigious Hall of Fame Award from Daimler India Commercial Vehicles for its role as a reliable telematics partner, achieving 100% delivery and quality performance.

items.statement: Mechatronics segment revenue expected to nearly double in FY26; all JVs (Telematics, Yokowo, Oxygen Sensor, Alps Alpine) firing with significant run-rate
items.quote: for the next year onwards, we do expect to almost double our revenue within the Mechatronics vertical. All the joint ventures which sit under the Mechatronics are expected to report a very handsome growth, although it was of a small base, but we have gained significant traction on all of them.

name: Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Ltd

items.statement: ABLBL to start FY26 with INR700 cr debt; demerged ABFRL to have INR1,300-1,500 cr cash
items.quote: We expect ABLBL to start the next year with opening debt of INR700 crores, whereas demerged ABFRL will have a likely cash balance of approximately INR1,300 crores.

items.statement: ABLBL to become debt-free in 2-2.5 years
items.quote: Over next 2, 2.5 years, we expect this to become a debt-free company.

items.statement: Demerged ABFRL to be free cash flow generating in 3 years
items.quote: Over the next 3 years, we should be able to accelerate the growth of these new businesses to a point that at the end of that cycle, the company as a whole, which is the demerged ABFRL, will be free cash flow generating company.

items.statement: TMRW fundraise planned in next 9-12 months
items.quote: In terms of time line, we'll look at, when markets are right in the next 9 to 12 months, to raise this capital.

items.statement: ABLBL plans 300+ new stores in next 12 months
items.quote: Over the next 12 months, the brands are poised for an aggressive expansion with a significant rollout of 300 -plus new stores across the portfolio.

items.statement: Tasva to add 40-50 stores in FY26 from ~70 currently
items.quote: I think it would be in the range of 40 to 50 stores from the current level of about -- we end this year at about 70-odd stores, and we should be able to probably add closer to 50 stores next year.

items.statement: Style Up to end FY25 with 48-50 stores; plans to add ~50 stores in FY26
items.quote: We expect this year to end with a network between 45 to 50 stores -- 48 to 50 stores. Next year, we'll definitely, at the minimum level, double it.

items.statement: Pantaloons opened 13-15 stores in FY25, shut ~20; plans 15-20 new stores in FY26
items.quote: Next year, we are looking at, again, opening about 15 to 20 stores.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 15.9% in Q3 FY25 vs 14.5% YoY
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA stood at INR683 crores, growing 13% Y -o-Y in absolute terms, with 15.9% margin as against 14.5% margin in Q3 last year.

items.statement: ABLBL EBITDA margin 16.5% in Q3 FY25, up 90 bps YoY
items.quote: ABLBL posted revenue of INR2,151 crores with EBITDA of INR355 crores in Q3 FY '25 and an EBITDA margin of 16.5%, 90 basis point expansion versus last year.

items.statement: Lifestyle Brands EBITDA margin 19.6% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Brands posted revenue of INR1,817 crores with EBITDA of INR357 crores in Q3 FY '25 w ith EBITDA margin of 19.6%.

items.statement: Pantaloons EBITDA margin 19.3% in Q3 FY25, up 170+ bps YoY
items.quote: On profitability front, the segment reported an EBITDA margin of 19.3%, reflecting an improvement of over 170 basis points Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Ethnic portfolio EBITDA margin 19.2% in Q3 FY25, up 1,160 bps YoY
items.quote: Profitability for the overall portfolio also improved sharply with EBITDA margins reaching 19.2%, a remarkable 1,160 basis point Y-o-Y expansion.

items.statement: Tasva delivered first positive EBITDA in Q3 FY25
items.quote: The brand for the first time delivered a positive EBITDA this quarter, showcasing intrinsic potential of its business model.

items.statement: TCNS recorded second consecutive quarter of positive EBITDA despite revenue decline
items.quote: Meanwhile, TCNS recorded its second consecutive quarter of positive EBITDA despite a revenue decline of over 20% due to ongoing distribution optimization aimed at establishing profitable distribution.

items.statement: Overall consumption subdued; festive/wedding season robust but other periods inconsistent
items.quote: The overall consumption remains subdued this quarter as well with periods of high to moderate consumption. While the festive and wedding season witnessed robust demand, other periods experienced inconsistent footfalls.

items.statement: Lifestyle Brands retail LTL growth 12% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Lifestyle Brands, the brands have seen a retail LTL growth of 12% across brands on a network of more than 2,500 stores.

items.statement: Pantaloons LTL negative 2.5% overall; positive 2.5% excluding East zone
items.quote: Excluding the East zone, Pantaloons recorded a positive LTL growth of 2.5%. At an overall level, the LTL was negative 2.5%.

items.statement: Ethnic portfolio (ex-TCNS) grew 39% YoY in Q3 FY25
items.quote: While TCNS is still going through a distribution rationalization to focus on profitable channels, which led to its degrowth for rest of the portfolio, excluding TCNS, the growth has been 39%.

items.statement: Tasva sales grew >50% YoY in Q3 FY25 with 18% LTL
items.quote: Tasva, ably leveraged the festive and wedding season this quarter with sales growing by more than 50% versus last year. Tasva delivered an 18% LTL growth.

items.statement: TMRW sales grew 26% YoY in Q3 FY25 with margin improvement
items.quote: Our digital brand portfolios under TMRW posted a growth of 26% in sales year -on-year with an improvement in margin.

items.statement: Luxury Retail (Collective & Mono) grew 13% YoY with 10% LTL
items.quote: Luxury Retail, the Collective & Mono brands grew by 13% in Q3 FY '25, led by a strong LTL of 10% and robust e -commerce performance.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue INR4,305 cr in Q3 FY25, up 3% YoY
items.quote: The company delivered consolidated revenue of INR4,305 crores, a growth of 3% over same quarter last year.

items.statement: YTD revenue INR11,376 cr, up 7% YoY
items.quote: At YTD level, company recorded a revenue of INR11,376 crores, which is growth of 7% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt ~INR1,800 cr after QIP; to reduce further after preferential issue
items.quote: The total net debt of consolidated ABFRL at the end of Janu ary 2025 stood at approximately INR1,800 crores after receiving INR1,860 crores of QIP money. This will further come down post receipt of preferential issue of INR2,379 crores

items.statement: Raised USD 490 mn via QIP and preferential issue
items.quote: The company has successfully secured USD 490 mil lion equity capital through a mix of QIP and preferential issue.

items.statement: Demerger of western wear into ABLBL progressing; NCLT hearing in third week of March 2025
items.quote: First, the demerger of western wear brands business into a separate entity, that is Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited, or ABLBL, is progressing well and set for completion within the next 2, 3 months. The NCLT hearing is scheduled in third week of March 2025.

items.statement: Pantaloons focusing on private label; share improved slightly
items.quote: Our emphasis on private label has been there. Over the last few years, our share of private label has improved a little bit.

items.statement: Style Up is 100% private label; Pantaloons mixes private and external brands
items.quote: Style Up is a completely private label space with everything that is sold in the store is designed by us in -house. Pantaloons, as you know, has external brands.

items.statement: Style Up exit price points INR1,200-1,300; bulk below INR1,000; Pantaloons exit price ~2x
items.value: INR1,200-1,300 exit price for Style Up
items.quote: In case of Style Up, our exit price points are about INR1,200 to INR1,300, with bulk of our merchandise being below INR1,000. In case of Pantaloons, the exit price point is much higher, would be probably twice of that.

items.statement: Innerwear at ~INR500 cr revenue; needs 40-50% growth to reach single-digit EBITDA margin
items.quote: So we are closer right now to about INR500 crores. I think we'll have to grow by another 40% to 50% from this level to get to that kind of margin structure.

items.statement: Forever 21 offline operations being phased out; positive EBITDA impact expected
items.quote: So it will be positive because we were not making money in that business. But obviously, we don't reveal details at the brand level. It wouldn't be right to give you the exact number. There will be a positive impact on EBITDA.

items.statement: Management says FY25 revenue will not reach Rs 2,000 crore target due to weak institutional sales and poor southern crop season
items.quote: So, 2000 plus looks may not be able to achieve that in this year because of the factor that the technical sales were little lower and also few of the important crops where we have very strong presence, especially in the south, did not pan out the way we thought.

items.statement: Management expects FY26 performance to be much better across all parameters with lower OPEX, full potential of patented products, and reduced inventory

items.statement: 9M FY25 stud ratio 10.5% vs 11.6% YoY; Q3 stud ratio ~11%
items.quote: So, our 9-month stud ratio was 10.5%. And our Q3 stud ratio has been about 11.0%.

items.statement: Diamond jewellery sales flat in absolute terms (Rs 142 cr vs Rs 143 cr 9M)
items.quote: So, our sale of diamonds, just to reiterate, last 9 months was Rs.142 Cr and this particular 9 months is around Rs.143 Cr.

items.quote: In gold jewellery, the growth is 21%. In the diamond jewellery, it has grown by 9%. items.statement: Invoice count up 4.5%, ATV up 14.5%, ASP up 15.5% YTD
items.quote: We have seen that the ATV has gone up by 14.5%. We have seen the ASP has gone up by 15.5%. So, there have been positive signals in terms of the growth of the sales even though there has been an increase in prices.

items.statement: Expansion focused 60-70% East India, 20% North, 10% West/South
items.quote: Therefore, 60% to 70% of our new stores, we will continue to focus on growing in East India 20% odd we will grow in North India and remaining 10% in West and South.

items.statement: Customs duty cut impact Rs 57-60 cr on 9M EBITDA/PAT
items.quote: In terms of the adjusted EBITDA and adjusted PAT, what we have seen is that we have taken into account Rs.58-60 Cr duty cut impact on the overall numbers.

items.statement: Gold loan rate hike may persist or normalize; monitoring quarterly

items.statement: Making charge income ~10-11% of revenue, stable over 11 quarters
items.quote: So, when we talk about the balance of, let's say, 4.5% to 5%, that comes from diamond, platinum, silver, and so on. Your point was that it has been volatile. items.quote: We have already launched the Sennes brand. We had opened 4 stores also in Calcutta.

items.statement: No specific guidance given for Q4 FY25 profitability and asset quality; outlook and guidance for FY26 to be shared with Q4 results
items.quote: We are not giving any specific guidance on profitability and asset quality in current environment for Quarter 4 FY25, will share outlook as well as guidance on both for FY26 at the time of our Quarter 4 FY25 numbers.

items.statement: JLG disbursements expected to normalize by Q2 FY26; non-microbanking portfolio to continue healthy growth in Q4 FY25 and FY26
items.quote: We expect JLG disbursements to normalize sometime around Quarter 2 FY26. Expect good growth in MBBL portfolio that is individual loan. Our CASA deposit ratio was 19.7% as on December 24, largely at the same level of 19.6% as on September 24. And CASA plus retail term deposit ratio improved from 68.4% as on September 24 to 70.1% as on December 24.

items.statement: Opened 61 new branches in Q3 FY25, 140 in 9M FY25; total branches 1,028; may not need much branch expansion in FY26
items.quote: We continue to build our banking franchise and opened 61 new branches in Quarter 3 FY25, overall 140 new branches in 9 months of FY25 taking total branch network to 1,028 branches as on December 24. With current year expansion, we have significant large franchise which is adequate for our growth target and hence we may not need much expansion of our branch network in FY26.

items.quote: We have added around 350 more people in our micro banking team in Quarter 3 FY25 and almost around 2,000 people in nine months of FY25. We're reducing case load per staff as well as we have collection team of micro banking of more than 800 people.

items.statement: Cost of funds expected to decline; CD ratio fell to 92% from 99% YoY; net of refinance borrowing CD ratio 86%; surplus liquidity >Rs 2,500 crore
items.quote: In line with our strategy, we have been reducing our CD ratio, which declined to 92% as on December 24, from 99% as on December 23. And if we net off refinance borrowing from advances, CD ratio declines to 86%. We don't have any short-term borrowing on our balance sheet. We expect our CD ratio to decline further.

items.statement: No short-term borrowings; CD ratio 92% (86% net of refinance); expect further CD ratio decline
items.quote: We don't have any short-term borrowing on our balance sheet. We expect our CD ratio to decline further.

items.statement: Revenue growth expected ~20% over next 2-3 years from mature facilities and new additions; EBITDA margins to sustain at current levels despite opening 45-50 facilities this year
items.quote: In terms of revenue, the revenue from our mature facilities and the newer facility additions over the next 2-3 year perspective, should be close to about 20%. items.statement: Chennai flagship centre expected operational early FY26 (9-10 months); construction underway

items.quote: these 3 will give us anywhere between INR2,200 crores to INR2,500 crores of the top line at a full capacity utilization basis.

items.quote: We are running at a production rate of about 950 tons against our 1,000 ton capacity, and we are trying to ramp up production even more.

items.quote: As a corporate policy, would not go to more than 2.5x of the debt to EBITDA. Yes, debt to EBITDA.

items.statement: FY25 capex expected 5-6% of turnover due to new order book requirements
items.quote: But for 2025, we will, for sure, have to spend much more money in CAPEX, because of the new order books are required in this additional CAPEX. So, we talk more or less about 5% to 6% of our turnover in CAPEX every year.

items.statement: Average ~20% free capacity across verticals; aluminium fully booked working weekends; adding new machinery
items.quote: Approximately, we can say that we can have around 20% of average free capacity, but in certain verticals like aluminium, we are fully booked. In this moment, we are working even Saturdays, Sundays. So, we are adding a new machinery.

items.statement: Europe: MHCV down 35% in Q4, Off-highway weak, Passenger Cars flat; expect weak H1, potential H2 recovery from US infrastructure/oil&gas policies
items.quote: We started with minus 10% in the first quarter, minus 21% in the second, minus 28% in the third, and finally, the last quarter was minus 35%. So, that is the drop of the Commercial Vehicles marketing in Europe.

items.statement: India: Q4 Light Vehicle +3.2%, 2W +8%, Tractors +12%; FY24 Light Vehicle +3.8%, 2W +16%, Tractors and Trucks declined
items.quote: The Light Vehicle segment, which is our largest, slowed to a growth of 3.2% in this quarter, while Trucks were massively negative in terms of growth, Tractors and 2-wheelers grew 12% and 8%, respectively.

items.statement: India Q4 EBITDA 17% vs 16.5% YoY, 17.7% QoQ; FY24 17.9% vs 16.7% (incl 0.7% non-recurring subsidy); Europe Q4 15% vs 16.9% YoY; Consolidated FY24 17.3% vs 17.1%
items.quote: The India operations achieved an EBITDA margin of 17% in Q4 C '24 versus 16.5% in Q4 C '23 and 17.7% in Q3 C '24.

items.statement: India margins have scope to improve but at slower pace; Europe margins range-bound ~15-16% unless sales collapse; expect Trucks/Off-highway recovery in 2-3 quarters
items.quote: In Europe, it all depends on the sales. Like if the sales decline is arrested, like we had big drops in both the quarters, last quarters. So, in spite of that, we are still at around 15% and overall, for the year around 16%.

items.statement: Commodity prices largely stable/trending down; <1% impact on sales; no margin impact from pass-through
items.quote: No, there has not been almost any relevant change, less than 1% of impact on the sales, so very minimal impact.

items.statement: India has 12-15 strong clients beyond anchors; order delays at some EV and Hosur customers being resolved; competitive pressures exist but managed via reliability/efficiency
items.quote: I think we have at least 12 to 15 strong clients in India, and we regularly interact with them. We had talked about order delays at so me of the other clients, that's the reason why we have increased our focus on anchor customers

items.statement: Actively looking at plastics and other strategic gaps; no acquisition since 2019; only customer-driven inorganic to address strategic gaps
items.quote: We wanted to do plastics. There are other areas that we are actively looking at. We will continue to look at that. Of course, we are not going to do acquisitions just for growth, we will only do it when some of our strategic gaps are addressed.

items.statement: India ~12,600 employees, no headcount growth expected (growth via efficiency); Europe ~900 employees, reduced from prior year adapting to lower volumes
items.quote: In India, we are about 12,600 employees, that is the total amount of Indian employees, and we don't expect to grow this figure as we expect to grow the business with increasing our internal efficiency. And in Europe, we are a little bit more than 900 people, okay. That's the amount of people that we have in Forgings plus Metalcastello. We have reduced all these figures from the previous year, adap
