items.statement: Board recommended dividend INR 7/share vs INR 5/share prior year (itself double previous 2 years); pending AGM approval
items.quote: Given the strong cash generation, the Board of the Company has recommended an enhanced dividend payout of INR 7 per share versus INR 5 per share made last year.

items.statement: Europe EV penetration stagnated at 13% in 2024; forecast 43% by 2029 (down from earlier 56%); managing transition via aluminium/steel forge substitution for crankshafts
items.quote: After an initial spurt in the last few years, the European light vehicle market witnessed a stagnation in EV penetration in 2024 at 13%. Current forecast suggests that this ratio will move up to 43% in 2029, which is down from earlier estimates of 56%.

items.statement: No formal guidance given; management expects India growth to offset Europe decline over next years; mid-single digit revenue growth considered reasonable but not committed
items.quote: We don't give guidance, because... Vikas Sinha: No, these are forward-looking statements. But like what you are asking for is something that is reasonable. Let's leave it at

items.statement: Automotive industry uncertainty, volatile markets, EV transition slower than predicted, supply chain transformation via digitization/Industry 4.0
items.quote: The automotive industry is faced with significant uncertainty, both in the immediate and long term. Markets are volatile. The transition to EVs is not happening as smoothly as predicted.

items.statement: EV order book diversified across aluminium/steel castings, forgings, gears, stampings, composites for e-2W, e-3W, e-4W in India; Metalcastello has healthy EV transmission order book in Europe (some delayed)
items.quote: Our EV order book in India is spread across aluminium and steel castings, steel forgings, gears, stampings and composite parts for e-2-wheeler, e-3-wheeler and e-4-wheeler segment.

items.statement: India plants 68% of sales (incl ~INR 3B Mexico), Europe 32%; Mexico subsidiary of CIE Galfor Europe, sales ~INR 3B at 12-13% EBITDA margin
items.quote: Plants in India accounted for 68% of CIE India's sales with 32% coming from Europe. This 68% includes that INR 3 billion from Mexico, please note.

items.statement: Operating cash flow 66% of consolidated EBITDA; no specific debtor/inventory days disclosed
items.quote: The Company generated operating cash flows to the extent of 66% of consolidated EBITDA.

items.statement: Media business expects to break even at PBT level within 24-28 months
items.quote: we are on a clear path to break even at the PBT level, and while I won't put an exact date on it, we expect to achieve this within the next 24 to 28 months.

items.statement: South Africa demand exceeded expectations, expanding from 2 to 4 floors with 360 seats
items.quote: demand has exceeded expectations. Initially, we secured two floors, but based on current demand, we have signed up for two additional floors, bringing the total capacity to four floors with approximately 360 seats.

items.statement: Q3 and Q4 margins may be lower due to startup costs for new deals, revenue impact from Q1 FY2026
items.quote: As a result, Quarter 3 and Quarter 4 margins may be lower, as most startup costs will be incurred in Quarter 4, while revenues will begin to flow in Quarter 1 of FY2026.

items.statement: Transitioning onshore to offshore operations expected to improve margins despite revenue decline
items.quote: While this shift may result in a revenue decline due to lower offshore rates, we expect improved margins from our offshore centers.

items.statement: Won largest core IT services engagement with a banking company in Americas, ramping in Q4, revenue from Q1 FY2026
items.quote: The largest among them is a core IT services engagement with a banking company in the Americas. This is a significant contract that we won toward the end of last year. We have begun ramping up in Quarter 4, but the revenue impact will start reflecting in our books in Quarter 1 of the next fiscal year.

items.statement: Deployed HGS Agent X for new public sector client in Canada for complete contact center transformation
items.quote: Additionally, we have successfully deployed HGS Agent X for a new public sector client in Canada as part of a complete contact center transformation project.

items.statement: Signed six-year contract with Ontario public sector agency for cloud contact center, cybersecurity, and AI-assisted agent services
items.quote: We have signed a six-year contract with them to provide technology services, including cloud contact center deployment, cybersecurity services, and AI-assisted agent services.

items.statement: Net free cash flow of Rs. 205 crore for 9M FY2025 after capex of Rs. 67 crore
items.quote: Even after netting off CAPEX of Rs. 67 crore, our net free cash flow stands at Rs. 205 crore.

items.statement: Expanded Bangalore footprint adding 10th floor for AI Hub and banking client support center
items.quote: We have also expanded our footprint in Bangalore, adding an additional floor—the 10th floor—on top of our existing corporate office. This new space will house our AI Hub and support center for the banking client whose business we recently won.

items.statement: Will inaugurate first center in Waterloo, Ontario, Canada in April 2025 for Government of Ontario public sector client
items.quote: I am pleased to announce that in April 2025, we will inaugurate our first center in Waterloo, Ontario, Canada. This center will serve a public sector client for the Government of Ontario.

items.statement: Transitioning contracts from FTE model to transaction-based pricing for automation upside
items.quote: Additionally, most contracts that were previously structured on a full-time equivalent (FTE) model, we're trying to transition to transaction-based pricing, that gives us an upside if we're able to deliver more through automation.

items.statement: ISG rated HGS as Leader in Leaders Quadrant alongside Sutherland, Foundever, Teleperformance, WNS, Genpact
items.quote: ISG, one of the top analyst firms, has rated HGS as a leader. We are positioned in the Leaders Quadrant, alongside billion-dollar firms such as Sutherland, Foundever, Teleperformance, WNS, and Genpact.

items.statement: Customs duty cut on ethernet switches in Budget 2025 will help rural telecom infrastructure
items.quote: one notable highlight is the customs duty cut on ethernet switches, which will help establish telecom infrastructure in rural markets.

items.statement: FX swing of Rs. 40 crore from loss of Rs. 8.85 crore in Q2 to gain of Rs. 31 crore in Q3
items.quote: For the quarter ending September, we reported an FX loss of Rs. 8.85 crore, whereas this quarter, we recorded an FX gain of Rs. 31 crore. That represents a Rs. 40 crore swing.

items.statement: DSO improved from 65 days peak to 61 days, positively impacting operating cash flow
items.quote: Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) improved, moving from 60 days at the beginning of the year to 65 days during peak ramp-ups, and now back down to 61 days, positively impacting cash flow from operations.

items.statement: Total borrowings reduced by Rs. 93 crore from Rs. 1,305 crore (Mar 2024) to Rs. 1,212 crore (Dec 2024)
items.quote: Total borrowings stood at Rs. 1,212 crore as of December 2024, down from Rs. 1,305 crore in March 2024 - a Rs. 93 crore reduction during the year.

items.statement: Borrowings declined Rs. 44.5 crore sequentially from Rs. 1,257 crore (Sep) to Rs. 1,212 crore (Dec)
items.quote: Borrowings declined by Rs. 44.5 crore during Q3, reducing from Rs. 1,257 crore in September to Rs. 1,212 crore in December.

items.statement: Merged five US wholly owned subsidiaries into HGS CX Technology completed Feb 14, 2025, reducing administrative overhead
items.quote: To streamline operations, we have merged five U.S. wholly owned subsidiaries into HGS CX Technology, a step-down wholly owned subsidiary of HGS. This merger was completed on February 14, 2025, at 6 p.m. Eastern Standard Time.

items.statement: Actively looking for acquisitions in digital, AI, automation space for business synergy
items.quote: So, we continue to look for opportunities where there is business synergy, and we expect these to be primarily in the space of digital, AI, automation. That's the broad direction in which we aim to acquire new capabilities or technologies for our growth.

items.statement: Completed buyback of Rs. 1,020 crore in June 2023; further buybacks tax inefficient as funds are abroad
items.quote: As you know, we already completed one buyback in June 2023, returning about Rs. 1,020 crore of cash to shareholders. Most of the funds we now have are abroad, and conducting another buyback would require bringing the money to India, making it tax inefficient.

items.statement: Great Place to Work certified in Canada and Philippines
items.quote: One award that I am particularly proud of is the Great Place to Work certification. As you know, talent is key to success in our business, and we have been certified in Canada and the Philippines.

items.statement: Broadband subscribers 1.2 million, DTV subscribers 4.43 million across 4,500 pin codes
items.quote: We also have a significant broadband and DTV business, covering 4,500 pin codes across India, with 1.2 million broadband subscribers and 4.43 million DTV subscribers.

items.statement: Management expects conservative revenue growth of 25-30% for FY26, with clearer guidance by end of Q4 FY25.
items.quote: From a conservative perspective, growth could be around 25–30%, and by the end of the fourth quarter, we will be able to give a clearer outlook.

items.statement: Order book stands at over INR 3,400 crores as of February 10, 2025, with 95% metering and 99% of that smart meters.
items.quote: As of February 10, 2025, our order book stands at over INR 3,400 crores, with more than 95% linked to metering and 99% of that specific to smart meters.

items.statement: Strong demand for smart meters expected for next couple of years; AMISP execution ramp-up will drive growth.
items.quote: Overall, there should be strong demand for meters for the next couple of years.

items.statement: Overall gross margin near 35% this year; 35-40% jump unlikely without significant mix shift or service offerings.
items.quote: Overall, our gross margin this year stands near 35%, influenced by a product mix of meters plus consumer and industrial segments.

items.statement: CapEx for smart meter automation funded via internal accruals; fourth automated line inaugurated, another for subsidiary Himachal Energy.
items.quote: Most of this CapEx is funded via internal accruals rather than new debt.

items.statement: Annual smart meter capacity ~1.1 crore meters at 70-80% utilization; can reach 100% with extra shifts; sufficient for next 12-15 months.
items.quote: Our annual capacity is around 1.1 crore meters, currently at 70–80% utilization. This can be increased to 100% by running extra shifts or streamlining operations further.

items.statement: Wires & cables revenue +25%, domestic switchgear +21% in nine months FY25; fan segment launched in 3 regions, targeting 40% India coverage by July.
items.quote: Wires & Cables revenue: +25% Domestic switchgear revenue: +21%

items.statement: Net working capital and interest costs declined last two quarters; debtor days reduced ~30 days due to faster-paying AMISPs.
items.quote: Over the last two quarters, our net working capital and interest costs have declined. Our debtor days have reduced by ~30 days, partly because we're now dealing with AMISPs (faster payers) rather than direct utilities.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity at 0.69; absolute debt stable or slightly decreased, ratios to improve further with revenue growth.
items.quote: Debt-to-equity is now at 0.69. With higher revenues, absolute debt may remain stable or slightly reduce, but overall ratios should improve further.

items.statement: No direct sourcing from China; imports from global suppliers (Singapore, US); moving to in-house component manufacturing to reduce currency exposure.
items.quote: We do not source anything directly from China. India lacks certain raw materials (e.g., polycarbonate and electronic ICs), so we import from global suppliers (Singapore, US, etc.).

items.statement: Export certifications take 18-24 months; background work ongoing; focus remains on domestic demand for next couple of years.
items.quote: We do have background work ongoing for exports- certifications alone take 18–24 months. As I was in Dubai last week for some inquiries, we do see ourselves expand internationally and gradually while focusing on execution.

items.statement: Supplying to most leading AMISPs; 900+ authorized dealers and 83,000 retailers nationwide, targeting 100,000 retail outlets by June 2025.
items.quote: We now have over 900 authorized dealers and 83,000 retailers nationwide, aiming to surpass 100,000 retail outlets by June 2025.

items.statement: Not just a contractor; meter is critical technology in AMI solutions; reliability and scale provide strong position despite renegotiations.
items.quote: We're not just a contractor; the meter is the critical technology in AMI solutions. AMISPs face steep penalties for SLA breaches. Using unproven or cheaper sources risks bigger losses if meters fail.

items.statement: BLDC and star-rating compliances raising quality standards, reducing unorganized segment in fan market.
items.quote: BLDC (Brushless DC) and star-rating compliances are raising quality standards across the industry, reducing the unorganized segment.

items.statement: Employee costs risen due to increased production and strategic hiring in R&D; automation reducing labor needs; no big headcount surge expected.
items.quote: To clarify, employee costs overall have risen this year due to increased production and strategic hiring, particularly in R&D. However, automation is helping us reduce labor requirements in production lines.

items.statement: Borrowing costs decreased due to rating enhancements; further rating improvement targeted; possible macro rate decrease in next 18 months.
items.quote: Yes, we've already seen a decrease in borrowing costs thanks to rating enhancements. We aim to improve our rating further. Additionally, there are indications of a possible macro-level decrease in interest rates in the next 18 months.

items.statement: Reviewing expansions in LT power and control cables given strong 25% growth in wires/cables; robust demand from retail, building, infra, telecom.
items.quote: Now we're reviewing expansions in LT power and control cables, given strong growth (25% so far this fiscal in wires/cables). We see robust demand from retail, building, infra, telecom, etc.

items.statement: AMISP on-ground challenges (local policy, utility coordination, logistics) caused INR 40-50 crore revenue shift from Q3 to Q4.
items.quote: Although the orders are there, certain AMISPs delayed or postponed some shipments, leading to about INR 40–50 crores of potential revenue shifting out of Q3.

items.statement: PCB population and assembly done in-house since 1996; bare PCBs purchased, electronic components imported, all mounting and final assembly in-house.
items.quote: We have done PCB population and assembly in-house since 1996. We purchase bare PCBs and import electronic components (since India does not manufacture them), but all mounting and final assembly is done in our facilities.

items.statement: NABL accreditation under ISO/IEC received for laboratory, reinforcing commitment to high-quality R&D and testing for wires and cables.
items.quote: I am also pleased to highlight our recent NABL accreditation under ISO/IEC for our laboratory, reinforcing our commitment to high-quality R&D and rigorous testing capabilities for wires and cables.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth expected around 10% with margins maintained at current levels
items.quote: We should be largely in the same range as we are this year, maybe about 10% growth. Nothing significant as we see today.

items.statement: NSE listing expected to be completed by end of April
items.quote: We believe that it should be done by April end

items.quote: But it is largely due to little better demand that we are seeing in specific couple of products. And basically, the end-use application of the customer is seeing also higher demand.

items.statement: Overall demand structure expected to remain similar with no major dip or phenomenal growth
items.quote: Overall, our structure, the demand structure is expected to remain very similar. At least we may not see any phenomenal growth, but we are not also expecting any major dip or reduction or anything like that.

items.quote: in case of polymers, as you are already aware, there are certain products where we have a formula-driven pricing. So margin remains constant

items.quote: It would be around EBITDA margins of 20% roughly.

items.statement: Current EBITDA margins expected to be maintained in FY26

items.quote: Currently, their demand is steady, nothing significant in terms of drop or increase. items.quote: I feel that, or I believe that it is going to be next year when we will see some pick up in this couple of acid chlorides.

items.quote: With one customer, we believe, because their end user or end customer is expected to approve their product by end of March. So we believe that that product will start to gradually go on stream for us around April or May and it will be a very small quantity to start with.

items.statement: 3-4 new products combined could generate Rs. 150-200 crores annually in 2 years
items.quote: If everything goes right, then about 3-4 products when you put together in another 2 years' time, at the completion of 2 years, it would be annually anywhere between Rs. 150 crores-Rs. 200 crores.

items.statement: Capacity expansion to be considered after new products reach critical mass in 1.5-2 years
items.quote: At that time, we should be starting to look for new capacities, whether within the factory if we get permission or outside of the factory.

items.statement: New products will use mix of converted existing facilities and new capacity; job work options available
items.quote: It is a combination of both. Some of the current facilities can be converted and utilized to take those products and that would help us in the initial period when initial volumes the ramp up is slowly happening and initial volumes are not very large.

items.quote: For example there is one product which requires nitration chemistry. Okay so when we say diversification, we are largely talking about non-acid, non-alkyl chloride.

items.quote: So, two acid chlorides have come into manufacturing. One is right now gradually ramping up. That's going to US customer and I think they have taken two lots.

items.statement: Added 6-7 new customers across Eurasia, South America, Japan and domestic market
items.quote: So right now, see, what we are doing is that we added a couple of customers in Eurasia, two customers in South America. Of course, some of them are existing products. We are working with almost 4-5 customers in Japan, talking to one more customer again in one of the South American country and at the same time working with couple of domestic customers for some more products.

items.statement: Two new Indian customers added recently
items.quote: So yes, we have two more, two new Indian customers.

items.statement: US customers source 90-95% from Transpek; limited benefit expected from potential tariffs on Chinese competitors
items.quote: Not significantly because for example, two of our important customers in the US are buying almost 90%-95% of their requirement from us. So whatever is left in terms of buying from possibly Chinese companies, it is very small, very small.

items.statement: Customers keen to shift from Chinese suppliers; Transpek exporting to China competing with local suppliers
items.quote: See, actually what some of our customers that we have been interacting with are already buying from Chinese suppliers and they are very keen to get out of that.

items.statement: No significant US tariff impact expected on exported products; scenarios run show manageable impact
items.quote: So far as our products are concerned, we have no, I mean to the best of our knowledge, there is no significant producer of the products that we are exporting to US. items.quote: Some of them were good but highly overpriced because when we were looking, at that time the multiplier was generally very high in industry and some of them were that we looked at were not fitting into our ethos or in our value system in terms of environment management and sustainability practices and all that. So, far we have not yet zeroed onto any anything which would appeal to us from all aspec

items.statement: Company remains very low debt with strong balance sheet
items.quote: We remain a very low debt company with a strong balance sheet.

items.statement: Customers cautious on inventory building causing timing delays despite stable order quantities
items.quote: Most of the customers are very cautious in building up inventories. So even though they may have indicated that, okay, this is going to be the order sequence or order pipeline, the quantity remains same, but the timing kind of increases because sometimes they don't want to build inventory if their products and schedule gets changed.

items.statement: Target EBIT margins of 8-10% in coming years as recovery continues
items.quote: We do hope to achieve EBIT margins of 8-10% in the coming years.

items.statement: Maintenance capex around ₹10-15 crore per year
items.quote: Maintenance capex is around ₹10 to ₹15 crore generally for a year.

items.statement: Grain processing plants running at ~80% capacity utilization; no capacity increase planned
items.quote: Yes, as I mentioned, the plants are running at almost 80% capacity utilization.

items.statement: C1 tender allocation of 15 crore liters worth ~₹1,000 crore; C3 tender opened after FCI rice release
items.quote: From that, we had taken an allocation of about 15 crore liters, which is worth approximately ₹1,000 crores.

items.statement: Three ethanol pricing points: maize ₹71.86/liter, damaged food grains rice ₹64/liter, FCI rice ₹58.50/liter
items.quote: One is ₹72, ₹71.86, which is when we produce ethanol from maize. The second pricing point is ₹64, which is when we produce ethanol from rice, specifically damaged food grains. The third pricing point is ₹58.50, when we produce ethanol from FCI rice.

items.statement: Maize prices softened from ₹26-27/kg to ₹23.50-24.50/kg after FCI rice release announcement
items.quote: After the news of FCI rice being released for the ethanol industry, we were able to buy maize anywhere between ₹23.50 and ₹24.50.

items.statement: FCI rice supply restarted at ₹22.50/kg (was ₹20-21 earlier); 70+ lakh metric tons stocked at FCI
items.quote: The government has announced a paradigm shift to support the grain-based ethanol players with its commitment to the Ethanol Blending Program, and this is by reducing the FCI broken rice price from ₹28 to ₹22.50.

items.statement: Government ethanol blending at 16% and policy irreversible; OMC tenders increasing (C1 910 crore liters, then C2, C3)
items.quote: And you see, the government is already blending 16% ethanol in petrol, which means they are already substituting 16% of crude oil with a domestically produced product. So, there is no way the government will reverse this policy.

items.statement: Bumper maize crop expected due to increased sowing; positive for price stability
items.quote: I hear that there's a bumper maize crop, so I'm hopeful that will have a positive impact on the industry.

items.statement: Grain processing customers include Asian Paints, Dabur, Patanjali, Unilever; pricing limited by import parity and substitutes (glycerine for starch)
items.quote: Our customer base includes companies like Asian Paints, Dabur, Patanjali, Unilever. So, if I talk about a product like sorbitol, beyond a certain price, the product becomes unviable for our end customer, and they will start importing.

items.statement: Ethanol working capital cycle 25-30 days (OMC payment 21-25 days); grain processing 30-45 days
items.quote: The working capital in the case of ethanol is basically with OMCs (Oil Marketing Companies). We receive payment in 21 to 25 days, so there is hardly any requirement. It's an assured return, with a 25-30 day cycle for ethanol. In other cases, it's 30 to 45 days for the working capital cycle.

items.statement: Net debt ~₹5.25 crore including working capital and term loans as of December end
items.quote: Net debt is around ₹5.25 crore, which includes working capital as well as term loans.

items.statement: Assam plant receives ₹3.5/liter combined incentives (₹2 PLI + state incentives)
items.quote: All put together—from both the state and central government—we have about ₹3.5 per liter in incentives. This includes ₹2 PLI and other state incentives.

items.statement: Sorbitol exports to 40+ countries stable at ~₹100 crore revenue; no significant deviation expected
items.quote: See, we export sorbitol to over 40 countries, and we have revenue of about ₹100 crore coming from it. So, the revenue from exports will remain stable, with not much deviation on either the upper or lower side.

items.statement: Ethanol yield: 2.6 kg maize per liter, 2.2 kg rice per liter
